title: F32.show rounds decimal ties differently on native (20713.812) and JS (20713.813)
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend floattie.bend              # default run
bend floattie.bend -o tie && ./tie
bend floattie.bend -o tie.js && node tie.js
```

### What happened

| Value | default run | native binary | JS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `20713.8125` | `20713.813` | `20713.812` | `20713.813` |
| `3764828.25` | `3764828.3` | `3764828.2` | `3764828.3` |
| `0.0 - 3056512.25` | `-3056512.3` | `-3056512.2` | `-3056512.3` |

All exit 0. The inputs are exact binary32 values that sit on a decimal tie at the shortest round-tripping precision. Both spellings parse back to the same `f32`, so no value is lost, but `F32.show` gives different text on native than on the other two paths.

The cause is the rounding rule of the two formatters in `bend2/comp.ts`:

- C `f32_text` (around line 450) uses `snprintf("%.*e")`, which rounds the exact binary value half-to-even: `printf '%.7e' 20713.8125` prints `2.0713812e+04`.
- JS (around line 534) uses `Number.prototype.toExponential`, which rounds halfway cases away from zero: `(20713.8125).toExponential(7)` is `2.0713813e+4`.

Programs that print floats (or compare printed output across backends, for example golden tests) see this as a C/JS divergence.

Suggested fix: pick one rule for `F32.show` and implement it in both lanes, for example half-to-even in JS by checking the tie with exact arithmetic, or produce the digits from the shortest round-trip algorithm in both. A regression test with these three values would pin it.

### The file

```bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(F32.show(20713.8125))
    IO.print(F32.show(3764828.25))
    IO.print(F32.show(F32.sub(0.0, 3056512.25)))
```

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.28 (main at 11c65a2, run from source with bun). Also seen on 2.0.13 and 2.0.16.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.4.4.1)

title: Char.from_u32 of a surrogate fails in JS and the interpreter but prints invalid UTF-8 natively
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend surrogate.bend              # default run
bend surrogate.bend -o s && ./s
bend surrogate.bend -o s.js && node s.js
```

### What happened

| Path | Output | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default run | `max scalar = …`, then `bend: 55296 is not a Unicode scalar value` | 1 |
| JS | same as the default run | 1 |
| native binary | `max scalar = …`, then `surrogate = ` followed by bytes `ED A0 80`, then `unreachable` | 0 |

`Char.from_u32(55296)` (U+D800, a surrogate) is accepted by the checker, since `Char.from_u32` in `base.bend` is just `Chr{x}`. The JS runtime's `char_new` (`bend2/comp.ts`, around line 553) rejects surrogates and values above 0x10FFFF, while the C runtime prints the code point encoded as 3 bytes, which is not valid UTF-8, and carries on. `Char.to_u32(Char.from_u32(55296))` likewise returns `55296` natively and fails in JS.

So the same program fails on one backend and succeeds with invalid output on the other. #809 fixed the related input side (invalid UTF-8 read by `io_str`); this is the output and construction side.

Suggested fix: decide what a `Char` outside the Unicode scalar range means and apply it in both runtimes, for example fail in C the way JS does, or have both print U+FFFD. Boundary tests at 0xD7FF, 0xD800, 0xDFFF, 0xE000, 0x10FFFF and 0x110000 would pin it.

### The file

```bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print("max scalar = " ++ Char.show(Char.from_u32(1114111)))
    IO.print("surrogate = " ++ Char.show(Char.from_u32(55296)))
    IO.print("unreachable")
```

title: evals/hard.factor_power_reduce.bend does not check: it redeclares Base's Nat.pow
body:
### What you did

```sh
for f in evals/*.bend; do bend "$f" --check-only; done
```

### What happened

19 of the 20 evals print `All terms check.` `evals/hard.factor_power_reduce.bend` fails:

```
- observed : 'Nat.pow'
Location:
20 |

   |     ^^^^^^^
22 |   match n:
```

The eval imports Base, which already defines `Nat.pow`, and then defines its own `Nat.pow` at line 21. On 2.0.13 and 2.0.16, importing the unchanged file from a wrapper under an alias (`import ./factor.bend as Factor`) checked cleanly, so the proofs themselves are fine and only the name collides. `gates/repo.ts` skips `evals/`, so no gate checks the evals on their own.

Suggested fix: rename the local definition (for example `Frac.pow_nat` or `pow`) or use Base's `Nat.pow`, and add a gate step that runs `--check-only` on every eval.

body:
### What you did

### What happened

```text
Error excerpt from the original project:


Error:
- expected : an unambiguous name (the alias Main shadows Main.Pong)


I expect `import ./Main.bend as Main` to let me refer to definitions as `Main.Pong`, etc. The alias identifies the same module, so there should be no ambiguity.

import ./Main.bend as Main
import ./Game.bend as Game


Changing the alias to a different name and updating its references makes the original project pass.
```

### The file

```python
Reduced example, with both files in the same directory:

`Main.bend`:


type Pong is Data:
  Pong{}


`Proof.bend`:


import ./Main.bend as Main

def keep(x: Main.Pong) -> Main.Pong:
  x


Possible cause: in `parse_reso`, the shadowing check tests whether both the resolved name `q` and the original name `k` exist. It does not exclude `q === k`. For a sibling import named `Main`, both names are `Main.Pong`, so the check reports a conflict with the same definition.
```

title: fix(compiler): register pure result constructors
body:
## Why

the pure `main` in #1067 checks and runs in the interpreter and JS, but its native build fails with an undeclared `CID_INNER`. The field's type becomes concrete at a generic instantiation, so `show_main` finds constructors that the earlier reachability pass missed.

i'm evaluating Bend alongside our TypeScript monorepo and reproduced this while comparing native and JS behavior.

Fixes #1067.

## Scope

Register `show_main`'s constructor names in the existing `fl.cids` map, using the same arity calculation as the surrounding code. Three compiler lines, no new helpers, and 31 added compiler tokens within the current cap.

Two new regressions cover an unused sum alternative and a recursive value shared across a pair. Existing tests stay intact.

## Blast radius

The C emitter's constructor metadata for pure-main result types. IO mains have no display descriptor, so their registration stays the same.

## Verification

On macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11 and clang 23.1.2:

- Both regressions and the original repro fail to build natively on `11c65a2`. With the fix, checking, interpreter, emitted JS and native execution pass.
- Twelve existing native fixtures pass. Their generated C is byte-identical before and after the fix, covering arrays, wide records, static data, sharing, borrowing and intrinsic arguments.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 46/46. `git diff --check` passes.

Cluster, GPU and benchmark gates were not run.

title: A spin reads a shared Array's redirect once, atomically: blk_loc no longer races its count
body:
Fixes #975.

## Why

A fork's shared Array handle is a redirect: one heap cell holding the array's loc in bits 24..63 and a reference count in bits 0..23. Two things are wrong with how `blk_loc` reads it.

- **It's a data race (#975).** `blk_loc` reads the whole cell with a plain 64-bit load, while `rfc_bump` and `term_drop` move the count with 32-bit atomics on the cell's low half. ThreadSanitizer reports it on the issue's repro. No Bend result was wrong: the loc bits never change while the reader holds its count. But in C the compiler is free to assume otherwise.
- **It's read on every access.** A spin (a flat def's self-jumping loop) re-reads the cell on each `Array.get`/`set`/atomic of an array parameter, although the loc can't change during the loop. bend-parallel's counting sort spends most of its b=0 time on those reads.

## What changes (`bend2/comp.ts`, +40 / −4; one new test)

Two commits. They review better apart, and the squash lands them together.

1. **`blk_loc` reads the cell atomically.**
   - **Host:** one relaxed 64-bit atomic load (`__atomic_load_n`).
   - **Device (`#if DEVICE`, CUDA and Metal):** the two halves, each through the file's `a32_load`, recombined as `hi << 8 | lo >> 24`. `rfc_view` already reads the same cell this way on every lane. Metal has no general 64-bit atomic load, which is why the device can't take the host's path.
   - **No acquire.** The old read had none, and a fork's writes reach its join through the task counter, not through this cell.
   - A program whose Arrays are never shared (`BLK_SHR 0`, which is all 16 `bench/runtime` programs) has this branch compiled out.
2. **A spin reads a passed-back array's redirect once, before its loop.**
   - **What counts as "passed back as is":** the emitter records which params it reassigns in a new `Seg.moved`.
     - `emit_jump` adds a param when the self-jump's argument for it is not the param itself (`args[i] !== p`).
     - `bind_pop` adds any local it re-binds through `term_keep`.
   - **The hoist:** after the body is emitted, `spin_hold` checks each param of a looping spin (`seg.spin`) that is not in `moved` and whose loc the body reads. It declares `Loc _bl_N = blk_loc(e.mem, p);` before `WL_SPIN` and uses that local for the reads.
   - **Why the reads are rewritten by text.** The reads come from three emitters (`arr_op`, `arr_leaf` and the `array_atomic_*` templates), and all three run before the spin's jumps are known. `spin_hold` therefore replaces that one exact spelling in the spin's own lines. The decision to hoist comes from the emitter's data, not from the text: there is no pattern-matching on assignments or `&p`.

## Why the hoist is safe

- **The cell's loc bits never move.** They are written once, in `rfc_wrap`. Afterwards only the count, in bits 0..23, changes, by 32-bit atomics. A count that would carry into bit 24 has already posted `ERR_RFCS` in `rfc_bump`, so that run has failed anyway.
- **The cell can't be freed or reused during the loop.** The looping param holds a count, or its caller does for a borrowed param, and it passes the same handle back on every jump.
- **Nothing else changes the param inside a spin.**
  - Array writes (`array_set`, `swap`, the atomics) happen in place and return the same handle. An Array is affine, so no copy-on-write produces a new one.
  - No emitter site takes a local's address. The only `&` is `&wpoll` inside `WL_SPIN`.
  - A spin is a flat def, and a flat def neither forks nor bangs (`carb_book`), so it has no fork or task that could hand the param elsewhere.
- **A handle that isn't a redirect costs nothing.** `blk_loc` of it is just its own loc bits, so hoisting it reads no memory.
- **Where the hoist doesn't run.** A spin compiled as a host segment's tail call (`WL_AGAIN` as `musttail`) isn't affected. Native spins always compile as a `for` loop.

## Endianness

The host path reads the whole word, so it has no endianness assumption. The device path takes `w` as the low half and `w + 1` as the high half, as `rfc_view` and `rfc_bump` (which adds to `a32_at(r)` as the count) already do. Every target Bend builds for is little-endian: x86-64 and arm64 hosts, NVIDIA GPUs and Apple GPUs.

## Mixed-size access

On the host, a 64-bit atomic load overlaps the 32-bit atomic RMWs on its low half. ISO C11 doesn't define mixed-size atomics. The runtime already mixes sizes on these `u64` cells through `a32_at`, though, and on x86-64 and arm64 an aligned 8-byte load is single-copy atomic. ThreadSanitizer treats both accesses as atomic and reports nothing. The plain read it replaces was an outright data race. I tried the device's two 32-bit halves on the host first (numbers below). It was race-free too, but 2–3x slower on histogram, because the compiler can't merge or hoist the atomic loads.

## Measurements

The machine is an AMD Ryzen 7 5800XT (8 cores / 16 threads) under WSL2 (kernel 6.18), with AMD clang 22 (ROCm 7.2.1) at `-O3`. All runs are CPU-only (`--gpu off`): the machine's GPU is an AMD Radeon, which upstream has no lane for. It's a shared machine. I give the 1-minute load average with each table; the c16 runs themselves push it up. Builds were interleaved, with the order rotated each round, and every value is a median.

### bend-parallel benches (sort, histogram, scan; ms per call; 5 rounds; load 0.6 → 4.4)

"fix" is commit 1 alone; "both" is this PR. The d=22 rows are single calls with 1 ms resolution.

| case | main | fix | both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sort d22 b0 c1 | 30 | 26 | 17 |
| sort d22 b0 c16 | 30 | 25 | 18 |
| sort d22 b6 c1 | 32 | 26 | 19 |
| sort d22 b6 c16 | 10 | 9 | 8 |
| sort d22 b12 c1 | 36 | 32 | 24 |
| sort d22 b12 c16 | 18 | 18 | 14 |
| sort d17 b0 c1 (8 calls) | 0.75 | 0.63 | 0.38 |
| sort d14 b0 c1 (64 calls) | 0.109 | 0.078 | 0.031 |
| hist d14 b12 c16 (64 calls) | 4.16 | 4.94 | 4.08 |
| hist d17 b12 c16 (8 calls) | 4.38 | 5.25 | 4.25 |
| hist d22 b0 c1 | 3 | 5 | 4 |
| scan d22 b0 c1 | 3 | 4 | 2 |

- The other scan and histogram rows are within 5% of main in both builds.
- Checksums match across all builds and lanes.
- **The fix costs something on its own:** the histogram rows above get slower. The hoist more than recovers it, and the PR lands as one squashed commit.
- **What's left:** histogram at d=22 b=0 c1 is still about 1 ms over main (single-call rows). The reads are likely in spins that don't loop themselves and are called from another spin's loop, so the hoist doesn't reach them. The multi-call histogram rows at d=14 and d=17 are flat.

Host read variants (histogram d22 b0 c1, 5 runs, ms):

| read | ms |
|---|---|
| main (plain) | 3–4 |
| two 32-bit halves | 9–11 |
| one relaxed 64-bit load | 4–6 |

With the hoist, sort d22 b0 c1 is 22–23 ms with halves and 17 ms with the 64-bit load.

### `bench/runtime` (16 programs, `--threads 1` and `--threads 16`, `--gpu off`; 5 rounds; load 2.1 → 3.3)

- All 16 are `BLK_SHR 0`, so the new `blk_loc` branch is compiled out. The hoist fires only in bfs (2 spins), editdist (2) and terrain (3). The other 13 emit the same C as the fix alone.
- **29 of 32 rows are within ±2% of main.** raytrace c16 is −2.2% and tree-radix c16 −3.0%. All outputs are identical.
- **tree-bitonic c16 read +6% (2.152 → 2.275 s), which is noise.** Its C under this PR differs from main only in `blk_loc`'s dead branch, and the two binaries' `.text` sections are byte-identical. An isolated rerun (10–12 alternating runs each, load up to 10 from the runs themselves) gave:
  - main 2.168 s vs this PR 2.209 s (+1.9%);
  - then main 2.177 s, a byte copy of main 2.203 s, and this PR 2.137 s (−1.8%).

## Verification

- **ThreadSanitizer** (AMD clang 22, `-O1 -g -fsanitize=thread`, `TSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=0 exitcode=0'`, `--gpu off`):
  - **#975's repro, verbatim, `--threads 2`, 3 runs each:** main reports 1 race each run (`blk_loc` against `rfc_bump`). Fix alone and this PR report none. All runs print `4`.
  - **Larger variant:** 1024 leaves, each a 40-turn atomic-add spin over the shared handle (hoisted), then one more add.
    - main reports 1, 2 and 3 races at `--threads 2`, `4` and `16`.
    - Fix alone and this PR report none at all three.
    - Every run prints `11264`.
- **`tests/reg/spin_array_hold`** (new) passes on check, interp, JS and C.
  - `swap` trades its two arrays each turn, so neither param is held and the reads stay per turn.
  - `tot.go` holds its array, and so does `bump`, which runs on a fork's shared handle (`BLK_SHR 1`) inside `fan!`.
  - **The test catches the bug.** With the `moved` check removed, C prints `1234` / `0` instead of `1030` / `204`.
  - The turn counts come from an array's size, so the compiler can't unroll the loops.
- **Local gate** (`gates/test.ts`'s rules on one machine, CPU lanes only, `io_tcp_send_slow_peer` excluded): 1469 / 1473 on this branch against 1468 / 1472 on `main`; the one extra test is `spin_array_hold`, which passes. The same 4 tests fail on both, for reasons outside this change: `io_audio_only_{open,write,close}` (this machine has no ALSA headers) and `io_process_run` on interp and JS (its "inherited pipe" case).
- **bend-parallel's `run_tests.sh`** (the package code unchanged, this compiler): 9 tests × check, JS, c1 and c16, plus the proof: 37 / 37.
- **The structural rule makes the same decisions as a text rule.** I also built an oracle with an earlier version of the hoist, which decided by string-matching the generated lines (`p = rI;`, `rI = p;`, `&p`). Over 336 programs (tests/reg, tests/run, tests/io, bench/runtime and bend-parallel), it generates byte-identical C to this PR's rule; 22 of those programs have at least one hoist.
- **`bun gates/repo.ts`:** 46/46. `comp.ts` goes from 63,523 to 63,650 ttok (+127) with the fix and to 63,900 (+250) with the hoist, against a 64,000 cap.

## Not run

- **CUDA and Metal were not compiled or run here** (no NVIDIA or Apple GPU).
  - Neither lane gets a new construct: the device branch is `rfc_view`'s read, `a32_at` plus two `a32_load`s in one expression. Metal's `a32_load` is a statement expression through a volatile local; CUDA's is a volatile 32-bit load.
  - The hoist adds one `Loc` local before the spin's `for (;;)`, and spins are already device code.
  - On Metal, the new test's `fan!` runs its leaves on the GPU. That is new coverage of the halves read there, and also where a Metal problem would show.
- **The cluster, perf and GPU gates:** not run.

title: F32.read rounds once and F32.show rounds ties to even on JS, as on C
body:
#1055 and #1079 are two of four places where `F32.read` and `F32.show` differ between JS and C:

- `F32.read` did `Math.fround(Number(s))`, which rounds twice. On an exact f32 midpoint the second rounding can go the wrong way. `strtof` rounds once.
- `F32.read` skipped any Unicode space with `\s`. `strtof` skips ASCII whitespace only.
- `F32.show` used `toExponential`, which rounds a tie away from zero. `printf` rounds it to even.
- `F32.show` kept the shortest text for which `Math.fround(Number(t))` gave back `x`. That rounds twice as well, so `strtof` can read the text as the neighbouring f32.

```
                                          C              JS on main
F32.read("16777217.00000000001")          1266679809     1266679808
F32.read("340282356779733661637539395458142568447")
                                          2139095039     2139095040    (#1055)
F32.read("-7.0064923216240854e-46")       2147483649     2147483648
F32.read("\u{a0}1")                       None           1065353216
F32.show(23577.5625)                      23577.562      23577.563     (#1079)
F32.show(7.0385313e-26)                   7.0385313e-26  7.038531e-26
```

`F32.read` spots a midpoint with float ops, since `h = 2v - g` is an exact f32 only when `v` sits halfway between `g` and `h`. Only then does it compare the decimal exactly in BigInt. `F32.show` rounds a tie to even and checks each candidate with the same reader. For an integer `x` every candidate parses to a double exactly, so there it keeps the plain `Math.fround` check. `comp.ts` grows by 406 ttok, to 62,990.

Test plan
- [x] `tests/run/float_text_lanes.bend` prints the same line on the interpreter, C, bun and node
- [x] `F32.show` matches C on about 120M f32 values and `F32.read` matches `strtof` on 3.2M edge-case strings
- [x] On random f32, `F32.show` is about 8% faster than main on bun and 40% faster on node

Closes #1055, closes #1079.

title: JS lane: a long do block emits JS that node cannot load (parser stack overflow from ~300 steps)
body:
### What you did

`bend t.bend -o t.js && node t.js`, where `t.bend` is one `do IO<Unit>:` block of N sequential `IO.print` steps (generator below).

### What happened

```text
$ node t.js        # N = 300
node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1866
  const result = compileFunctionForCJSLoader(content, filename, false /* is_sea_main */, shouldDetectModule);
                 ^

RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at wrapSafe (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1866:18)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1908:20)
```

By N:

- 200: runs
- 250: runs, then `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)`
- 300, 400: the `RangeError` above, raised while node loads the file, before any code runs

The native build (`bend t.bend -o t`) prints all 400 lines.

The 250 failure looks like the SOON "Continuation passing for non-tail calls on the JS lane" entry in WONTFIX.txt. The 300+ one happens in V8's parser on the emitted source, so it may need flatter codegen for long `do` blocks rather than CPS. Workaround: split the block into defs of ~20 steps each.

### The file

```python
# generated by:
# python3 -c "print('import Base\n\ndef main() -> IO(Unit):\n  do IO<Unit>:'); [print(f'    IO.print(\"{i}\")') for i in range(300)]" > t.bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print("0")
    IO.print("1")
    # ... one IO.print per line, 300 in total
    IO.print("299")
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.28

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101); node v26.7.0

title: Two aliases of one file disagree when one import path leaves the entry's directory and comes back
body:
### What you did

bend d1/X.bend --check-only

### What happened

```text
Error:
- expected : a defined name
- observed : ../d1/Y.y_val
Location: ../d2/Z.z_val
4 | def z_val() -> U32:
5>|   Y2.y_val()
6 |
```

### The file

Three files: `d1/X.bend` is the entry, and `d1/Y.bend` is imported along two paths, as `./Y.bend` from the entry and as `../d1/Y.bend` from `d2/Z.bend`.

```python
# d1/X.bend
import Base
import ./Y.bend as Y2
import ../d2/Z.bend as Z

def x_val() -> U32:
  Y2.y_val()

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(U32.show(U32.add(x_val(), Z.z_val())))
```

```python
# d1/Y.bend
import Base

def y_val() -> U32:
  1
```

```python
# d2/Z.bend
import Base
import ../d1/Y.bend as Y2

def z_val() -> U32:
  Y2.y_val()
```

The header comment of `bend2/bend.ts` says two aliases of one file agree ("Name.x resolves to the file's canonical name, so two aliases of one file agree"). Here they don't. The entry loads `Y.bend` as `Y`. `Z`'s alias is computed as `path.posix.join(dirname("../d2/Z"), "../d1/Y.bend")`, that is `../d1/Y`, which no file was loaded under. `book_load` then returns early for the second import, since that real path is already in `seen`, so `Z`'s `Y2.y_val()` finds nothing. It shows up whenever two sibling directories import each other's files and the entry sits in one of them.

On 2.0.27 the same files were refused at the import instead: `one namespace per file (d1/../d2/../d1/Y.bend is both 'Y' and '../d1/Y')`. Since #1042 the refusal is gone, and the error moves to the first use of the alias.

A pointer, in case it helps: in a scratch copy, `al[m[2]] = seen.get(got) ?? sub;` (the alias takes the name the file was already loaded under) makes these files check and run (`2`). I only tried it on this example, not on the test suite, and I know `bend.ts` is yours to write.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.28 (and main at 11c65a25, same error)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8

title: TCP.listen and UDP.bind take the address to bind: today every server listens on all interfaces
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# today: 0.0.0.0, every interface of the machine
l : Listener <- IO.try(Listener, TCP.listen(8080))

# asked: the address, as TCP.connect already takes its host
l : Listener <- IO.try(Listener, TCP.listen("127.0.0.1", 8080))
s : Socket   <- IO.try(Socket, UDP.bind("127.0.0.1", 9000))
```

### Why

`TCP.listen(port)` and `UDP.bind(port)` always bind `0.0.0.0` (`io_sys_addr("0.0.0.0", ...)` in `effs/tcp_listen.c` and `effs/udp_bind.c`, `io_addr("0.0.0.0", ...)` in the JS twins), so every Bend server is reachable on every interface of the machine it runs on. A process meant only for that machine, like a worker behind a proxy on the same host, a dev server or an admin port, has no way to say so. What keeps the network out then lives outside the program, in a firewall rule.

Bend already has the other half: `TCP.connect(host, port)` reads an IPv4 literal through the same `io_sys_addr` / `io_addr`, so the change is mostly passing the string through, in both lanes.

Two shapes I can see, whichever you prefer:

1. `TCP.listen(host, port)` and `UDP.bind(host, port)`, like `TCP.connect(host, port)`. One signature, and a caller that wants every interface writes `"0.0.0.0"`; the tests and demos that listen would change with it.
2. A second def next to each that takes the address, leaving `TCP.listen(port)` and `UDP.bind(port)` as they are.

I'd be glad to write it as a PR, with a test, in whichever shape you choose.

title: Propositional mismatch: weight_ok inside weight_balanced hypothesis vs explicit call
body:
## Bend version
$(bend version)

## Minimal file
In paymog/bend-kit branch `issue-88-omap-balance`, file `collections/weight_proj_min.bend`.

## Command
`bend collections/weight_proj_min.bend`

## Expected
`proj_ok` should check: from a hypothesis `{weight_balanced(K,V, OBin{...}) == True}`, derive `{weight_ok(omap_weight lo, omap_weight hi) == True}` via `Bool.and` projection (same pattern as `c4`/`bn` for search-tree laws).

## Actual
Checker rejects `and_l` because the first conjunct in the hypothesis (expanded `weight_ok` with `Nat.mul(3n, wl)` reduced to nested `Nat.add`) is not considered the same `Bool` as the explicit `Laws.weight_ok(Laws.omap_weight(...), ...)` in the projection, even though they are the same definition.

This blocks universal inductive proofs over `weight_balanced` for #88 (ghost weight balance for `OMap.put`/`del`).

## Workaround sought
Either definitional equality on `Bool`/`Nat.mul` for ghost proofs, or a built-in way to project nested `&&` hypotheses without syntactic identity of duplicated subexpressions.

title: io: refuse a non-scalar Char in the C lane's UTF-8 writer
body:
Fixes #1080.

## The divergence

`Char.from_u32(55296)` (U+D800, a surrogate) is accepted by the checker, since `Char.from_u32` in `base.bend` is just `Chr{x}`. The issue's table, reproduced here on `main` at 574b6d3:

| Path | Output | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default run | `max scalar = …`, then `bend: 55296 is not a Unicode scalar value` | 1 |
| JS | same as the default run | 1 |
| native binary | `max scalar = …`, then `surrogate = ` + `ED A0 80`, then `unreachable` | 0 |

`Chr{55296}` is a literal code, so `Char.Chr`'s `intr` cannot fold it to a
JS string literal and emits `char_new(55296)`. The JS lane has `char_new` in
its prelude. The C lane has no such call: the whole String constant-folds
into `STAT_IMG` as a raw `55296ull` word on the `SCon` chain, and
`io_cstr` hands each word to `io_utf8`, which encoded the code point
mechanically and wrote `ED A0 80` — not UTF-8, since a surrogate has no
UTF-8 form. The program then carried on and exited 0.

So the same program failed on two lanes and "succeeded" on the third with
output no reader can decode.

## The fix

A `String` is a chain of Unicode scalar values — `lit_of` says so, and folds
a literal that spells a surrogate into its chain for exactly that reason.
So a non-scalar code is a value no lane should print, and the C lane already
had the refusal available to copy: `char_new` spells it
`bend: <code> is not a Unicode scalar value`. `io_utf8` now makes the same
refusal, on stderr, with `_exit(1)`, matching `err_fail`'s shape.

`io_utf8` is the tight point: its only two callers are `io_cstr` (the
printed String) and `show_chr`, and `show_chr` already escapes
`c < 32 || c == 127 || (c >= 0xD800 && c <= 0xDFFF) || c > 0x10FFFF` as
`\u{hex}` before calling it, so a `term_show`d value is unaffected and
`tests/show/string_escape.bend` keeps its law.

I took the refusal over substituting U+FFFD because the interpreter and the
JS lane already refuse, so matching them changes no existing lane and only
closes the one that diverged.

## Why no existing test caught it

`tests/io/marshal_char_scalar.bend` already pins this law:

```
#|bend: 55296 is not a Unicode scalar value
#|exit 1
```

but it pins it at the FFI seam, through `marshal_char_scalar.js`. Under
`gates/test.ts`, a test that imports a foreign file runs only the lanes that
file has — so that golden's compiled leg is JS alone and the C lane was
never asked. `Char` built in Bend and printed is the leg it leaves open,
and it is where the divergence actually lived.

`tests/io/char_scalar_print.bend` is that leg. It has no foreign import, so
`test_read` gives it `["js", "c"]` and it runs compiled in both. The three
boundary scalars (55295, 57344, 1114111) cross first, as they do in
`marshal_char_scalar`, so a guard misfiring on any of them would name that
code in the refusal instead of 55296. It is the same writer as
`halt_utf8_law`, with scalars only.

## Verification

All three lanes byte-identical, checked against the `#|` block with the
`gates/test.ts` `tidy` + `exit N` rule:

```
bend main tests/io/char_scalar_print.bend                                  # interp, exit 1
bend main tests/io/char_scalar_print.bend -o out.js && bun out.js          # js,     exit 1
bend main tests/io/char_scalar_print.bend -o out    && ./out               # c,      exit 1
```

Reverted, the C lane fails the golden — it prints `ED A0 80` and
`unreachable` and exits 0:

```
ed 9f bf ee 80 80 f4 8f bf bf 0a ed a0 80 0a 75 6e 72 65 61 63 68 61 62 6c 65 0a
```

Ran every existing test that touches a `Char` or a `String`
(`grep -rln 'Chr{\|Char\.' tests/*/*.bend`, 33 files) across its lanes
under that same rule: 58 lane-runs, 0 failures. `halt_utf8_law`,
`print_utf8_law`, `text_utf8`, `marshal_char_scalar`,
`marshal_string_scalar`, `show/char_unicode` and `show/string_escape` are
among them.

`bend2/comp.ts` is 62873 o200k tokens against `gates/repo.ts`'s 64000 cap
(62808 before), so the +65 does not need a cap bump.

## Note on scope

This is the output/construction side only, as the issue separates it from
#809's input side. `Char.from_u32` still typechecks to a `Char` for a
non-scalar code, so the guard is at the writer, not the constructor — a
program that builds one and never prints it is still accepted, exactly as
before. If the maintainers would rather have `Char.from_u32` itself fail, or
`Chr` be rejected by the checker, say so and I will move the guard; the test
covers the writer and would need to follow the value to wherever the
refusal lands.

title: Checker rejects a reachable fallback after a nested constructor pattern
body:
### What you did

Checked the self-contained file below on Bend 2.0.29, using a local wrapper that runs the unmodified checkout with Bun:

```sh
bun /path/to/bend/bend2/main.ts repro.bend
```

This only checks the file; it does not emit or run compiled code. I checked `WONTFIX.txt` and searched existing issues and pull requests before reporting this case.

### What happened

The checker exits with status 1:

```text
Error:
- expected : Witness(With{_5})
- observed : Unit
Context:
- _5 : Single<> - Only{}
Location: witness
17 |     case With{Only{}}: Unit{}
18>|     case rest: Unit{}
   |                ^^^^^^
```

### The file

```bend
import Base

type Single is Data:
  Only{}

type Choice is Data:
  With{item: Single}
  Other{}

def Witness(x: Choice) -> Type:
  match x:
    case With{Only{}}: Unit
    case rest: Unit

def witness(x: Choice) -> Witness(x):
  match x:
    case With{Only{}}: Unit{}
    case rest: Unit{}
```

### bend --version

```text
bend 2.0.29
```

Checkout revision: `c8691aa93b0b1bb2fda277d9fc88c5aa797e88de`. Bun: `1.3.14`.

### uname -sm

```text
Darwin arm64
```

### clang --version (the first line)

```text
Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)
```

Clang is not invoked by this reproduction.

### Expected result and control

Expected: `All terms check.`

`Only{}` is the only constructor of `Single`, so after `With{Only{}}` the fallback is needed for `Other{}`. The reported context instead contains the empty residual `Single<> - Only{}`.

Replacing **only the last line** with `case Other{}: Unit{}` makes the file pass with `All terms check.` and exit status 0. The definition of `Witness` and the proof's return type remain unchanged. Both variants were rerun with the same outcomes.

### Related cases

The original occurrence was a character pattern followed by a fallback, rejected with `Word.Nil<> - WNil{}`. The file above removes characters, literals, and application code. Explicitly enumerating the remaining patterns works around it, but is bulky for `Char`.

I did not find an exact duplicate. #892 concerns C emission for string patterns; the residual-type discussion in #1004 concerns literal checking. This reproduction involves neither C emission nor literals. I have not established the checker's internal cause.

title: A forking call no longer pays a condvar wake per pool turn: turns count rows, the main thread takes rows, and a turn visits only the rows that can hold a task
body:
On 2.0.29 (`574b6d39`). Three commits; the third (a yield before sleeping) is optional and last, so it can be dropped on its own.

## Why

Once a program forks, `corpus_eval` hands it to the pool (`task_deal`, `pool_open`, `cube_run(H, false)`) until the root is done. Each fork tree is one `cube_run` iteration: a grow turn (`pool_turn(true)`) and a drain turn (`pool_turn(false)`), each a full barrier. A call that forks pays at least two barriers per tree, however little work the tree holds. bend-parallel's scan forks two trees per call, its histogram two, its sort six.

On 2.0.28 I timed the pool with counters in the generated C: a 1K-key scan at fork depth 6, 2,000 calls in one `corpus_eval`. 2.0.29's pool is the same design, and costs the same (the main column below).

| --threads | per call | per turn | where a turn goes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 16 | 1.79 ms | 450 us | workers wake 138 us after the tick on average, the slowest over 500 us; the main thread wakes 250 us after the last one is done; the work itself is 2.7 us per worker |
| 1 | 0.33 ms | 80 us | wake 25 us, join 25 us, work 31 us |

Three things cost that, each in `bend2/comp.ts`:

1. **Every turn waits for every worker.** `pool_turn` sets `pool_done` to `pool_size` and sleeps on `pool_wake` until it reaches 0. Each worker must wake from the condvar, find no rows left and check in, and the last one's `pthread_cond_broadcast(&pool_wake)` also wakes the sleeping workers again, since both directions share one condvar. The main thread sleeps meanwhile.
2. **Workers sleep between turns** (`pool_work`'s `pthread_cond_wait`). The next turn is often a few microseconds away, but a condvar wake costs over 100 us on this machine.
3. **A turn walks the whole bag.** The grow turn runs `row_grow` over all 128 rows (`CUBE_G`) and the drain turn walks all 1024 units (`LANES / LINE`), reading every ring's head, however small the frontier is. For a 64-leaf tree that walk is most of a turn: on one thread, 48 of the grow turn's 60 us.

## What changes (`bend2/comp.ts` only; ttok 62,584 → 63,019 with commits 1–2 below, 63,085 with the third, against 64,000)

The pool keeps 2.0.29's atomics: `a32_*` on plain `u32`, no `_Atomic` or `atomic_*_explicit`.

1. **A pool turn ends when its rows are done, not when every worker has woken; the main thread takes rows too** (+219).
   - A claim is one relaxed `a32_add` on `pool_row`, a `u32` that carries the turn, the grow flag and the row.
   - `pool_done` counts down the turn's rows. Each worker subtracts its count once (`a32_sub_rel`), when a claim comes back past the last row. The worker that brings it to 0 signals the main thread on its own condvar, `pool_join`. The main thread waits with `a32_load_acq(&pool_done) != 0`, as before.
   - The main thread is worker 0: after it opens a turn, it claims rows like the others. `--threads N` now runs N − 1 pool threads.
   - A worker that wakes late for a turn claims from whatever turn is open. It gets that turn's rows, or none, and no one waits for its wake.
   - `pool_tick` and `pool_grow` go away; the worker's body moves into `pool_rows`, unchanged.
2. **A pool turn visits only the rows that can hold a task, not all 128 rows and 1024 units** (+216).
   - Frontier deal i goes to `ring_flip(i)`, whose row is at most i, and a grow turn pushes only within its own row (`ring_pick(base, 1, cur)`).
   - So the grow turn visits the rows below `min(f, CUBE_G)`, and the drain turn the rows below the deals made so far (the frontier, plus any continuation that forked while growing). The main thread's column grow can reach any row, so a turn after it visits all of them.
   - The bound rides in the claim word.
   - The invariant is written at the deal site (above `ring_flip`) and checked where breaking it would show: a task dealt past a turn's rows would sit in its ring until the frontier drained, so `cube_run`, on that failure path only, walks the rings and fails with "a task left past its pool turn's rows" rather than "frontier drained without a result". A run that succeeds never reaches the walk.
3. **A pool wait yields a while before it sleeps** (+66, optional, last so it can be dropped). `POOL_WAIT` calls `sched_yield()` up to 128 times while its condition holds (about 80 us here), then blocks on the condvar as before. It serves both waits: a worker's for the next turn, and the main thread's for the last row. See "The third commit" below.

### The claim word

`turn << 20 | rows << 12 | grow << 11 | counter` (commit 1 alone has no rows field: `turn << 12 | grow << 11 | counter`).

- **counter, 11 bits.** A turn has at most `LANES / LINE` units: `CUBE_T` (128) × `CUBE_G` / `LINE` (16), with `CUBE_G` at most 128 (`CUBE_LOG` is 7 on the host; CUDA's `gpu_shape` clamps it to 4..7), so 1024. Past them, each thread makes at most one claim per opening: it leaves `pool_rows` on its first claim past the end and then waits for a turn value different from that claim's. `pool_size` is at most `CUBE_T`, so the counter stays below 1024 + 128 = 1152 < 2048 and never carries into `grow`.
- **rows, 8 bits.** 1..128.
- **turn, 12 bits.** It wraps every 4096 turns, routinely in a long run. A worker compares the turn in the word with the last one it saw. If it sleeps through exactly a multiple of 4096 turns, it sees its old value and keeps sleeping through that turn. That costs nothing: a turn completes when its rows are done, not when its workers check in, and the main thread takes rows itself, so no turn needs any particular worker.

### Why it's safe

- **Every row of a turn is processed exactly once.** A row index comes from one `a32_add` on the word that names the turn. Two threads can't get the same (turn, row).
- **No row is processed with the wrong mode or bound.** The grow flag and the bound come from the same atomic read as the row.
- **A turn can't end early.** A worker subtracts its rows from `pool_done` only when it leaves the loop, so while it holds an unfinished row of turn T, `pool_done` isn't 0 and the main thread can't open T + 1. That also means every claim a worker makes before leaving is still in T.
- **Ordering.** The main thread stores `pool_done` (relaxed) and then opens the turn with `a32_store_rel(&pool_row, ...)`. A worker claims with a relaxed `a32_add`, then calls `a32_acq(&pool_row)` before it touches a claimed row. That is the shape `task_deliver` already uses (`a32_sub_rel`, then `a32_acq`). The acquire load reads the opening store or a later claim in its release sequence. It can't read the next opening's store, because this worker holds an unfinished row. So the worker sees the rings, the grow's pushes and the `pool_done` reset. The main thread's `a32_load_acq(&pool_done) == 0` reads the last of the release subtractions, so it sees every row's writes.
- **No lost wakeup.** A worker checks the turn under `pool_lock` before `pthread_cond_wait`, and the main thread opens the turn and broadcasts under the same lock. The join is symmetric: the last row's worker signals `pool_join` under the lock.
- **The rows bound** (commit 2):
  - At the top of each `cube_run` iteration, every ring that holds a task is in a row below the bound. After a drain, only `task_deal` with stride 0 pushes, to `ring_flip(g)` for g below the cursor.
  - A grow turn pushes only within its own row.
  - The one push that can reach any row, the main thread's column `row_grow` (stride `CUBE_G`), sets the bound to `CUBE_G`.
  - `ring_flip(i)`'s row is `i % CUBE_T` (at `CUBE_LOG` 7) or below (at smaller `CUBE_LOG`), so at most i.
  - These are all the host's ring pushes on 2.0.29: `task_deal`, `monk_step`'s push of a fork-free continuation (stride ≠ 0 only, so within its row), `row_grow`, and `corpus_eval`'s first deal. The GPU seam's `ring_push(H, 0, t)` runs `cube_run(H, true)`, not the pool.
  - **Liveness: a task dealt during a drain, past that drain's bound, isn't lost.** It lands in `ring_flip(g)`, where g is below the cursor at the end of the drain. The next iteration reads that cursor as its f before resetting it, so f > g >= the task's row, f > 0, and the next bound, `min(f, CUBE_G)`, covers the task's row. Such a task waits one iteration, where the full walk on one thread could have reached it in the same turn. That changes the one-thread schedule of tree-bitonic, not its result.

## The third commit: optional

What commit 3 gives on this machine, on top of 1+2 (bend-parallel, c16, 5 rounds, rounds don't overlap):

| case | main | 1+2 | 1+2+3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| scan d10 b6 c16, ms per call | 1.830 | 0.111 | 0.0435 |
| sort d17 b6 c16 | 3.63 | 0.92 | 0.375 |
| sort d17 b12 c16 | 10.39 | 7.84 | 7.39 |
| hist d17 b12 c16 | 4.34 | 2.70 | 2.42 |
| hist d20 b6 c16 | 1.88 | 0.63 | 0.25 |

Before timing, I set the bar for keeping it: at least 25% off scan d10 b6 c16 and at least 3% off sort d17 b12 c16. It clears both: −61% (67 us per call) and −5.8%. At c1 it does nothing: one thread finishes every row before it waits, so there's nothing to yield for.

It's last so it can be dropped. It is tuned to this host, where a futex wake costs about 140 us. Upstream's runtime has no yield-spin anywhere else, and its perf gate runs on Mac minis, where a condvar wake is likely cheaper and 128 `sched_yield`s take an unmeasured time. What it costs:
- up to about 80 us of yielding per wait, on a pool that is between turns;
- about 2% more CPU on kmeans c16 at matched layout (below).

Without it, the branch still takes scan d10 b6 c16 from 1.83 ms to 0.11 ms per call.

## Measurements

The machine is an AMD Ryzen 7 5800XT (8 cores / 16 threads) under WSL2 (kernel 6.18), with AMD clang 22 (ROCm 7.2.1) at `-O3` and no GPU. It's a shared machine. I give the 1-minute load average with each table; the c16 runs themselves push it up. Every value is a median.

### bend-parallel benches (ms per call; 5 interleaved rounds, order rotated each round; load 0.8 → 3.8)

bend-parallel 7fb04de. "1+2" is the first two commits, "all" this PR. scan d10 is 2,000 calls in one run; the precise drivers run d=17 64 calls and d=20 and d=22 16 calls each. Checksums match across all builds, lanes and rows.

| case | main | 1+2 | all |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| scan d10 b6 c16 | 1.830 | 0.111 | 0.0435 |
| scan d10 b6 c1 | 0.3185 | 0.0155 | 0.0155 |
| sort d17 b6 c16 | 3.625 | 0.922 | 0.375 |

| hist d17 b6 c16 | 1.797 | 0.328 | 0.109 |
| hist d17 b12 c16 | 4.34 | 2.70 | 2.42 |

- The fixed cost of a forking call drops from about 1.8 ms to about 0.04 ms at c16, and from 0.32 ms to 0.016 ms at c1.
- The b=0 rows don't fork. They are within 2% of main at c16. At c1 the largest gap is sort d20 b0, where main is 6.88 ms, 1+2 is 7.25 (+5.5%) and all is 7.13 (+3.6%). The other c1 b=0 rows are within 2%.

### bench/runtime (seconds; 16 programs, c1 and c16, `--gpu off`; 5 interleaved rounds, order rotated; load 2.3 → 4.1)

All 16 programs print the same output on every build. Rows not shown are within 2.5% of main on both builds.

| bench | lane | main | 1+2 | all | 1+2 / main | all / main |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| tree-radix | c16 | 0.985 | 0.890 | 0.872 | 0.904 | 0.886 |
| kmeans | c16 | 0.776 | 0.753 | 0.736 | 0.971 | 0.949 |
| hashmap | c16 | 0.453 | 0.432 | 0.433 | 0.955 | 0.957 |
| lexer | c16 | 0.403 | 0.420 | 0.405 | 1.043 | 1.005 |
| bfs | c16 | 0.472 | 0.478 | 0.486 | 1.012 | 1.029 |

| tree-bitonic | c1 | 11.932 | 12.207 | 12.103 | 1.023 | 1.014 |

**Rows that move by more than about 3% are checked at matched layout before they're attributed.**

The PR adds libc imports (`pthread_cond_signal`, and `sched_yield` in commit 3) and a function, `pool_rows`, with its `.eh_frame` entry. That moves `.text`, and with it the program's hot code (`WL_FID_*`, `monk_step`), by 16–48 bytes mod 64. On 2.0.28 that shift alone moved CPU time by up to 11% on this Zen 3 host, in a direction that depends on the program and lane. It produced that version's editdist, symreg and tree-matmul c16 slowdowns (+4–10%). On 2.0.29 the layout has moved again, and those three are within 3% of main.

The check: `pad.py` puts a 64-aligned pad at the start of `.text`, so at each pad N (0, 16, 32, 48) main and both branches put `monk_step` and `main` at the same address mod 64 (checked with `nm`). c16, 9 rounds, load 1.0 → 14.6 from the runs themselves; the geometric mean over the four pads, against main:

| bench | lane | 1+2 wall | 1+2 CPU | all wall | all CPU | reading |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| tree-radix | c16 | 0.923 | 0.942 | 0.912 | 0.931 | real gain (0.90–0.95 at every pad) |
| kmeans | c16 | 0.953 | 0.994 | 0.956 | 1.019 | real wall gain; the yields cost about 2% CPU |
| hashmap | c16 | 1.007 | 1.003 | 0.997 | 1.000 | layout |
| lexer | c16 | 0.989 | 0.998 | 0.987 | 0.996 | layout |
| bfs | c16 | 1.002 | 0.999 | 1.005 | 1.000 | layout |
| tree-matmul | c16 | 1.002 | 1.002 | 1.002 | 1.001 | layout |
| tree-matmul | c1 (5 rounds) | 1.003 | 1.002 | 1.004 | 1.004 | layout |

- Unpadded, the layout-attributed rows are the ones whose hot code moved: `monk_step` mod 64 for main / 1+2 / all is hashmap 0/0/16, lexer 32/16/32, bfs 32/32/48 and tree-matmul 48/48/0. tree-radix (16/16/16) and kmeans (0/0/0) didn't move.
- No alignment is best for every program, so there's nothing to fix in the pool code. A different compiler, CPU or later commit will reshuffle these rows again, and upstream's perf gate may see a different set on its hardware.
- tree-bitonic c1 (+1.4–2.3%, under the 3% bar) wasn't padded. On 2.0.28, about +2% of it was real, from commit 2's schedule: at `--threads 1`, a drain turn visits the rows below the deals made before it started, so tree-bitonic runs half as many `cube_run` iterations (258 → 121 there), with the same output.

## Verification

- **The row bound, as a runtime check** (a patched copy of the emitted C, not committed). A debug build aborts in `pool_turn` if any ring at or past the bound holds a task. It sleeps 0–50 us before one claim in eight and before each final subtraction, to force late workers. It aborts if a claim's counter reaches all + `pool_size`, and it can cut the turn field to k bits (`DBG_WRAP`), so sleepers constantly meet wrapped turns.
  - All 50 tests that fork (`tests/*`), at `--threads 1, 2, 3, 7, 16, 32`: every output right, no abort. The first two commits alone: the same at 1, 2, 16, 32.
  - With a 1-bit turn at 2, 4, 16, 32, and a 2-bit turn at 2, 16, 32: every output right.
  - bend-parallel's 10 tests and the 16 `bench/runtime` programs at 1 to 32 threads: every output right. bend-parallel's tests with a 1-bit turn: right.
  - scan d10 b6 (8,000 turns) with a 1-bit turn: right at 2, 4, 16, 32 threads, with 334, 970, 3,019 and 3,445 workers late for their turn.
  - Past a turn's end, a turn never took more claims than there were threads, well inside the 1152 the word allows for.
  - **Positive control.** Halving the grow bound (`(f + 1) / 2`) makes the debug check fire (`ring 128 holds a task past grow bound 1`). On the committed code, without hooks, the same mutant fails with the new message: `bend: a task left past its pool turn's rows`.
- **ThreadSanitizer** (AMD clang 22, `-O1 -g -fsanitize=thread`, the plain runtime, no hooks; the 50 forking tests at `--threads 2, 4, 16`):
  - This branch alone: outputs all right. 4, 8 and 13 reports in 3 programs, every one a `blk_loc` 8-byte read against a 4-byte atomic write in `rfc_bump` or `term_drop`. That is #975, fixed by #1084. None are in pool code.
  - Stacked on #1084: 0 reports at 2, 4 and 16 threads (51 programs with #1084's new test).
- **`bun gates/repo.ts`:** 46/46.
- **Local gate** (`gates/test.ts`'s rules on one machine, no GPU lane, `io_tcp_send_slow_peer` excluded): 1473 / 1477, the same four failures as main (`io_audio_only_{open,write,close}`: no ALSA headers here; `io_process_run` on interp and JS).
- **bend-parallel's `run_tests.sh`** (check, proof, JS, c1, c16), stacked on #1084: 41/41.

## With #1084

- **The two branches merge cleanly** (git's ort merge, no conflict). Stacked, `comp.ts` is 63,463 ttok, or 63,397 without the third commit, under the 64,000 cap.
- **The gains stack.** In ms per call, main / #1084 / this PR / both:
  - sort d17 b12 c16: 10.39 / 8.06 / 7.39 / 5.03;
  - sort d22 b12 c16: 15.94 / 12.19 / 13.19 / 9.25;
  - hist d22 b12 c16: 5.69 / 5.25 / 3.75 / 3.31.

## Not run

- **CUDA and Metal.** The device loop doesn't use the pool. On a GPU build, the CPU pool runs only for forks outside `!` calls, through this same code.
- **macOS.** `sched_yield` is POSIX and `<sched.h>` is included on every host. How long 128 yields take there, and what commit 3 gains there, wasn't measured.
- **The cluster, perf and GPU gates.**
- **One machine.** WSL2 on 16 vCPUs.

title: Native compiler: Bool.or(U32.is_eq(x, K()), y) is always True when K is a nullary def
body:
### What you did

Bool.or()

### What happened

```text
Native: `Bool.or`/`Bool.xor` read a comparison against a nullary def as always True (regression from #1038)

On 2.0.29 (Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, clang 18.1.3), the native build prints `True` but `bend file.bend` and the JS lane print `False`:

The same happens with `Bool.xor` and with the comparison on either side. 

Workarounds: a literal (`U32.is_eq(0, 1)`), a def with arguments, binding `+k = K()` first, and `&&`/`Bool.not`/`match` works fine.
```

### The file

```python
import Base

def K() -> U32: 1

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(Bool.show(U32.is_eq(0, K()) || False{}))   # native: True
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.29

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1)

title: An intrinsic's result takes its def's return layout when no type is asked, so U32.is_eq on a nullary def reaches Bool.or as a flat tag (#1093)
body:
Fixes #1093.

`emit_intr` took the layout of a string-template intrinsic's result from the asked type only. When `U32.is_eq`'s argument is a call to a nullary def, the comparison gets emitted with no asked type, so `lay_of(null)` returns `BOX`. `Bool.or`/`Bool.xor` then read the raw `U32_BIN` word as a boxed Bool, and `U32.is_eq(0, K()) || False{}` prints `True` on C (the interpreter and JS print `False`).

The fix falls back to the def's declared return type. The `Array.isArray(it.C)` branch just above already does this. With the fix, the repro's C is the same as for a literal argument: `spin_0(e, _o_0, ((U32_BIN(0ull, ==, 1ull)) | (0)))`.

`tests/reg/intrinsic_nullary_arg.bend` covers `Bool.or` and `Bool.xor` with the comparison on either side.

Validation (Linux x86_64, bun 1.4.2, clang 21.1):
- New test on C before the fix: `True True True False False`. After the fix: `False False True True False`. The fixed output matches the interpreter and the JS lane.
- `tests/reg/intrinsic_arg_layout.bend` (#1038) still prints its expected lines on C.
- Built `-o x.c` for every test with `import Base` and a `main`, with and without the fix: 660 built on both, and all 660 emitted C files are byte-identical. The only new file is the new test.
- Not run: `gates/test.ts` (needs the mini cluster) and `gates/repo.ts` (`ttok` isn't installed here). comp.ts grows by one line.

title: Foreign effect IDs resolve only in the owner's import scope (#1045)
body:
Closes #1045.

A later entry declaration could take a sibling foreign file’s `CID(None)` or `CID(Con)` by spelling the sibling’s canonical namespace. The C lane could then treat the returned tag as a value of the wrong allocation size. Foreign `CID`/`FID` substitution now accepts local names only from the effect owner’s source and fallback names only from files loaded before that owner (its imports). The generated runtime’s own IDs are unchanged. Unknown names fail rather than bind to later entry declarations.

`tests/io/cid_capture.bend` imports a trusted sibling under another alias, forges both `None` and a three-field `Con`, consumes the `Maybe` result, and drops the `List` result. Before the fix interpreted JS printed `Some ` instead of `None`; after it, interpreted JS, emitted JS and native C print `None` / `6`. The native regression also ran under AddressSanitizer without a report. An existing imported effect with module-local constructors (`marshal_imported_nullary`) still runs on JS and C. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 46/46. Cluster and macOS not run.

title: Lift deep JS continuations so long do blocks load (#1086)
body:
Closes #1086.

A single long `do` emitted hundreds of nested `run_clo` arrows; Node 22 raises `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` while loading a 400-step program, and Bun also hits its parser stack. The JS compiler now lifts every 33rd nested continuation into a top-level function and explicitly passes its captured local values. Ordinary shallow closures keep their existing shape. Hoisted function bodies undergo the same non-tail-call/trampoline substitution as other emitted functions.

`tests/io/do_long_js.bend` has 400 sequential effects, carries a string across them and calls a pure def in the final effect; expected output is `[value]`. Interpreted checkup, emitted Node, emitted Bun and native C complete. A separate 1000-step program also completes on Node, and a long `match` branch retaining a constructor field completes. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 46/46. Cluster gate and macOS not run.

title: Build self-contained ES modules and TS declarations with --lib (#1029)
body:
Closes #1029.

`bend core.bend --lib -o dist/core.mjs` checks the file and emits a self-contained ES module plus `dist/core.d.mts` (`.js` produces `.d.ts`). A failed check writes neither file. Exports are exactly the loader’s filled non-Base, non-IO defs: default object keys preserve dotted names, and valid identifier names are exported individually. Synthetic local bindings keep named exports apart from runtime helpers, and computed object keys preserve `__proto__`.

TypeScript declarations follow the JS boundary: `Nat` is bigint, U32/F32 number, Bool boolean, String/Char string, Array a JS array, and user datatypes are discriminated constructor unions with transitive generic types. Erased parameters do not appear. Unrepresentable dependent or higher-order types are `unknown`, rather than an inaccurate promise. Repeated Bend parameter names receive distinct TS names. The declaration emitter is separate from the C/JS compiler to retain its ttok cap.

Verification: built and imported `.mjs` under Node and `.js` in a Node ESM package; a strict TypeScript 7 consumer imported `slots`, `Job`, `Iv`, nested `List`, and a dotted default method, with `@ts-expect-error` confirming nonexistent fields are rejected. Generic `Box<T>`, erased parameters, JS-runtime name collisions, prototype-safe keys and duplicate binders were exercised. Incomplete source produced no outputs; ordinary JS CLI emission and the Bun `.bend` loader still run. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 47/47. Full repository `tsc` retains four diagnostics in untouched `bend2/bend.ts` and optional canvas docs; none in changed files. Cluster/macOS gates not run.

title: Bind TCP and UDP servers to an explicit IPv4 address (#1088)
body:
Closes #1088. This takes the single-signature option: `TCP.listen(host, port)` and `UDP.bind(host, port)`, without an implicit wildcard overload.

Both C and JS effects now parse the requested IPv4 literal with the same strict helpers as `TCP.connect`. Native code rejects embedded NULs and releases the copied host before opening the socket; malformed addresses or ports past 65535 return `Fail(EINVAL)`. Every caller in tests and demos was migrated. Local HTTP/echo servers and loopback fixtures now explicitly bind `127.0.0.1`; the rollback client and relay deliberately retain `0.0.0.0` for remote peers. The guide documents the exposure choice.

`tests/io/server_bind_host.bend` checks invalid addresses in both effects, valid loopback/wildcard binds, and handle cleanup. Interpreted JS, emitted JS and native C all produced `22 / 22 / bound`. An OS-level localhost smoke observed `ss` reporting TCP and UDP on `127.0.0.1` in all three lanes: TCP connections to `127.0.0.1` succeeded and to `127.0.0.2` were refused. Migrated TCP/UDP loopback, TCP/UDP poll and port-boundary fixtures passed on JS and C; all three affected demos passed checking. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 46/46. Cluster and macOS gates not run.

title: Restore locality in recycled CPU heap generations (#1007)
body:
Closes #1007. A HOT free chain interleaves short-lived temporaries with long-lived string/tree cells; parking it as a COLD generation and passing it through the bank perpetuates the scrambled address order. On the host, every fourth handoff of the small (1–128 word) classes now restores full address order with an in-place, byte-wise radix distribution over free-list links. This is linear in the generation size, uses only 256 small head/tail buckets on the call stack, and does no extra work on ordinary allocation/free; classes larger than a page and the GPU path are unchanged. The guide documents the reuse behavior.

On this Linux/clang 22 host, the issues exact 3,004,928-character/round workload, four threads: before, round 1 was 68 ms and round 24 was 1035 ms; after, round 1 was 81 ms, round 24 about 120–140 ms, and round 48 153 ms. At one thread the 48-round treatment ran 134→156 ms. This trades a little first-round work for much lower and steadier cost in a long-running process. Interleaved unchanged-vs-treatment measurements of queens, hashmap and lexer at one and four threads gave identical outputs and timing ratios from 0.99x to 1.02x.

Added deterministic multi-round forked string-recycling regression, exercised through interpreter, emitted JS and native with 1 and 4 threads; native 4-thread run also passed clang AddressSanitizer. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 46/46. Cluster/Metal/CUDA gates not available here.

title: A Word(64n) produced by matching a pair whose first element is a datatype fails to emit with "a constructor outside a datatype"
body:
## Reproduction

    # repro.bend
    import Base
    import ./df.bend as D          # declares datatype Df<T>
    import ./f64.bend as F         # from_bits, to_hex, Bits.of_word, Bits.hex

    def second(p: D.Df<Array<U32>> & Word(64n)) -> Word(64n):
      match p:
        case (df, v):
          v

    def main() -> IO(Unit):
      df = D.df_new(1)
      begun = D.chunk_begin(df, 0, 0)
      p = D.eval_chunk(begun, 0, 0, 0, 0, 64, 0)
      w = second(p)
      do IO<Unit>:
        IO.print(F.to_hex(F.from_bits(w)))

`df_new`, `chunk_begin` and `eval_chunk` are three functions of an evaluator and can be
any three that return a datatype; the only thing the repro needs is a datatype in the
first element of a pair.

## What is not the cause

Each of these is fine alone, and each was measured in a file that emits and runs:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| a `U32 & U32` pair, returned and matched | emits |
| the `Df & Word` pair, matched, with the word printed as a literal | emits |
| `F.from_bits` and `F.to_hex` on a `Word(64n)` from `R.join32` | emits |
| `F32` as a constructor, a namespace and a scrutinee | emits |
| `Word.zero`, `List` on `&2`, `F.Bits`, `+` markers, `Nat` arithmetic | emits |

## What does not change the outcome

Five shapes were tried. The first four leave the `Word` in scope near the failing call;
the fifth removes the `F64` entirely, since `to_hex` is defined as
`Bits.hex(Bits.of_word(64n, to_bits(f)))`.

    (df, v) = p                                  still fails
    match p: case (df, v): v                     still fails
    w = bits(p), then print                      still fails
    the match in one def, from_bits in another   still fails
    Bits.hex(Bits.of_word(64n, w))               still fails

**So it is not the expression, not the helper, and not the scope: a `Word(64n)` produced
by matching a pair whose first element is a datatype cannot be passed to any function
in f64.bend.**

## The guess, offered as a guess

It looks like the datatype's constructor cannot be placed after travelling into a
tuple and back out. `U32 & U32` does not trigger it, which fits - two words need no
constructor - and a pair holding a datatype does, which also fits. If `Df<Array<U32>>`
were wrapped once more on the way out of the match, or if the word were read from a
field rather than from a tuple element, it would presumably compile, and that is the
kind of check that would confirm or kill the theory quickly.

title: [minor] Native IO.die adds extra blank lines to stderr for empty Halt messages
body:
### Bend version/backend
Bend 2.0.29, native backend (the default `bend <file.bend>` execution).

### Minimal reproducer
```bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print_err("Usage\n")
    IO.die(Unit, 2, "")
```

### Command
```sh
bend repro.bend >stdout.txt 2>stderr.txt
printf "exit=%s\n" "$?"
od -An -tx1c stderr.txt
```

### Observed
Exit code 2. The stderr bytes are `Usage\n\n\n` (three line feeds): the explicit error line followed by two additional newlines despite the empty `IO.die` message.

### Expected
Exit code 2 and exactly `Usage\n` on stderr, so callers can print one user-facing error and use `IO.die(..., "")` without duplicate blank lines.

title: A native is a call on the device when it loops and is long
body:
I found this with [bend-bench](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench), comparing 2.0.3 against 2.0.26 in alternating runs: ray tracing on the GPU got 38% slower.

The cause was the inline rule. Natives were FAR (noinline) when their body reached SPIN_FAR (256) lines, else INLINE. 6e16f4e4 folded a let into constants and raytrace's bounce loop fell from 357 to 258 lines, under the bar. It became INLINE, and since its only call site sits in the per-sample shader, which is itself inlined at four sites, the device program carried four copies of the loop. Raytrace on CUDA went from 0.94 s to 1.33 s.

Now a native is FAR only when it loops (`seg.spin`, which `emit_jump` already sets) and has SPIN_FAR lines, with SPIN_FAR 200. A loop-free native inlines at any size. FAR is noinline on the devices and plain `static` on the host, where clang decides (the old noinline on raytrace's per-cell loops cost 23-31% on the CPU, which the header note recorded).

I tried making every loop FAR first, which is shorter and gets raytrace to 1.9x, but a noinline call raises the kernel's register count (editdist's bend_dev 62 -> 80, with 96 bytes of stack) and cuts occupancy: editdist lost 9% and merkle 5%. Capping registers at 64 fixed both but cost queens 30%. Keeping short loops inline avoids all of that.

comp.ts 62584 -> 62579 ttok, +8 -7 lines, on 2.0.29.

Measured with bend-bench `gpu fast` (profile fast-gpu-v2) on an RTX 3090, CUDA 13.1, 4GB heap, 3 measured runs per workload after a correctness check and warmup, 574b6d39 and this branch alternating three times:

title: One file is one module however an import spells its path
body:
`book_load` loads each file once, keyed by its real path, but binds the import's alias to the namespace this particular path spells (the importer's namespace joined with the relative path). When an import chain climbs out of a directory and back into it, relative to the checked file, the same loaded file gets a second spelling: from `a/p/main.bend`, `a/q/x.bend` is `../q/x` when imported directly but `../../a/q/x` when reached through a module outside `a/`. The file is not loaded again, so the second alias names a namespace with no definitions and every use fails:

```
Error:
- expected : a defined name
- observed : ../import/respelled/core.seven
```

The fix binds the alias after loading, to the namespace the file was actually loaded under (`seen.get(got) ?? sub`).

This shows up in any project that groups code by feature, where a shared library imports back into a feature that also imports it directly (found in a feature-first layout of bend-collections: 95 entry files failed).

**Tests**: `tests/import/respelled_first` and `respelled_second` reach one module both ways, in each import order, through `tests/reg/respelled/facts.bend` (the helper must live outside `tests/import` to climb out and back in). Both fail on `main` with the error above and print `14` with the fix on the interpreter, JS and C lanes (Linux). The 31 other tests that import files give identical `--check-only` output with and without the change; `gates/repo.ts` passes.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UNs7cW2qitQ3PToFFqqZeD

title: A file reached through two relative import paths gets a second, empty alias (fixed by #1103)
body:
One file reached through two relative import paths loads once but gets two aliases, and the second alias has no definitions.

This is the case #1103 fixes. I'm filing it separately because the reproducer below is smaller than the PR's tests, and it gives the PR a second, independent confirmation.

### Reproducer

Three files, with no import cycle:

`nested/types.bend`
```
import Base

type Side is Data:
  Long{}
```

`use.bend`
```
import Base
import ./nested/types.bend as T

def side(x: T.Side) -> Bool:
  match x:
    case T.Long{}: True{}
```

`nested/check.bend`
```
import Base
import ./types.bend as T
import ../use.bend as U

def check() -> Bool:
  U.side(T.Long{})
```

Run `bun bend2/main.ts nested/check.bend`.

On 2.0.29 (574b6d39) the check fails on the `case T.Long{}` line in `use.bend`. Checking out the head of #1103 (5331654e) against the same three files prints `All terms check.`

### Cause

`book_load` keys loaded files by real path (bend.ts:953). The alias uses the namespace this particular path spells, which is the importer's namespace joined with the relative path (bend.ts:1003). `check.bend` loads `nested/types.bend` first as `types`. When `use.bend` imports the same file, the joined path gives it a second namespace. The real path is already in `seen`, so the loader returns early, and the second namespace never gets definitions.

#1103 binds the alias to the namespace the file was loaded under (`seen.get(got) ?? sub`).

### Where it came up

We hit this in a project that keeps shared types in a subdirectory that files at the root also import. Our workaround moves the shared files to the root, so every importer spells the same path.

title: JS lane: a Nat inside a value passed between two loaded .bend libraries stays a BigInt (constructor tags depend on the importing root), since 2.0.29 (still in 2.0.30)
body:
Bend 2.0.29 (c8691aa9) and 2.0.30 (56330b24), bun loader (`bun --preload bend2/main.ts`), macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.14.

a.bend
    import Base
    type Counter is Data:
      Counter{count: Nat}
    def Counter.make() -> Counter:
      Counter{5n}

b.bend
    import Base
    import ./a.bend as A
    def dec(c: A.Counter) -> Nat:
      A.Counter{count} = c
      Nat.sub(count, 1n)

t.ts
    import A from './a.bend';
    import B from './b.bend';
    const c = A['Counter.make']();            // c.$ === "Counter", c.count === 5n
    B['dec'](c);                              // 2.0.29: TypeError: Invalid mix of BigInt and other type in subtraction
    B['dec']({$: 'Counter', count: 5n});      // same TypeError
    B['dec']({$: 'a.Counter', count: 5n});    // 4n

Results:
- 2.0.27: all three calls return 4n.
- 2.0.28: all three return 4n, but a.bend's library tags the value "Counter" while b.bend's library names the same constructor "a.Counter" (#1042 made a tag the namespaced key, and the root file's namespace is empty).
- 2.0.29 and 2.0.30: the first two throw. The host wrapper's in-marshal (js_marshal) dispatches on the tag string: `case "a.Counter": ... count: nat_host(v.count)`, and `default: at[key] = v` passes a value with any other tag through unconverted. The BigInt then reaches code that now treats a Nat as a JS number (#1061 / 87a1e9c9), and fails far from the boundary, or silently compares unequal (BigInt vs number with ===) instead of throwing.

The cross-library case has no host-side fix: two libraries compiled from the same source disagree on one constructor's tag, so a value one library returns is not recognised by the other. Either the tag should not depend on which file is the root of the book (a file's namespace being its real path, as #1042 says, for the root too), or the in-marshal should convert by type rather than by tag for a single-constructor type, and an unrecognised tag should fail at the boundary instead of passing through.

Seen in a real program: a record built by one module (a jitter buffer inside a bridge) returned to TS and passed into a function of another module throws in `Jitter.emit_ready` on `count - 1`; another returns false from a validity check because a BigInt count compares unequal to a number.

title: File.open_under opens a file below a directory and never through a symbolic link
body:
A server that maps a request's path onto a directory has to refuse "..", a symbolic link that leads out, or anything that is not a regular file — and `File.open` follows whatever the path names. This adds the open that does not.

`File.open_under(root, path)` opens `path` read-only below `root`:

- One `openat` with `O_NOFOLLOW` per component: a symbolic link anywhere under root — to a file or to a directory, dangling or looping — fails `ELOOP` at the kernel, not from a prior check.
- An empty, "." or ".." component fails `EACCES`: a climb out of root is simply not a name you can say.
- An intermediate that is not a directory fails `ENOTDIR` and is never opened; a link there is re-read with `fstatat` and still answers `ELOOP`.
- The end must be a regular file (`EISDIR` for a directory), so a directory name cannot be used to probe inside.
- `root` itself is opened as given: it is the operator's choice, not the peer's.

The JS twin `lstat`s each component and opens the end with `O_NOFOLLOW`. Unlike the C walk it is best-effort against a concurrent writer under root — its comment says so.

The test (`tests/io/file_open_under.bend`) builds its fixtures in `/tmp` and pins every refusal to its exact code (`ELOOP` 62/40, `EILSEQ` 92/84): 20 cases, green on the check, interpreted, C and JS lanes; `gates/repo.ts` 47/47.

title: Open resizable windows and deliver drawable-size events (#1021)
body:
Closes #1021. Adds `Window.open_resizable` and `App.run_resizable` while preserving existing fixed-size `Window.open` / `App.run`. `Resize{width, height}` reports drawable **pixels** in `Window.frame` events, so an App tick can choose the next view size.

On macOS, the resizable style and auto-sizing view track content bounds; the backing scale drives Metal `drawableSize`, mouse coordinates and size-change notifications (including a screen-scale change). The frame pumps events before reading the drawable dimensions. On X11, WM size hints allow 1..16384 pixels, `ConfigureNotify` delivers actual dimensions, and the existing 32-bit `XImage` buffer is resized once per event batch before the next frame. The JS lane remains explicitly display-unsupported with an accurate error for the new API. The exhaustive Slash Boss proof covers the new event case.

Verified on a live Linux Xwayland display: an optimized native `App.run_resizable` window was initially 64x48 (pixel 255), grew to 96x64, shrank to 48x40, and painted pixel 65280 at the new bottom-right corner after each resize; its tick printed `48x40`. The same grow/shrink scenario passed under clang AddressSanitizer. The scripted event/close transition passed in interpreter, emitted JS and native C. Existing fixed-size gfx fixture and both no-display errors passed; affected examples and proof check. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 46/46. macOS/Metal and cluster gates not available on this Linux workstation.

Removed the GUIDE.md changes as requested in #1644.

title: Normalize typed JS constructor tags across loaded books (#1105)
body:
Closes #1105. A file compiled as the root exports `{$: "Counter", count: 5n}`, while a second book importing it expects `{$: "a.Counter", count: 5n}`. The existing `js_marshal` skipped that tag, left `Nat` as a BigInt, and let the JS lane fail later (or silently compare different number kinds).

At the typed JS boundary, a qualified constructor now accepts the short root spelling; a root constructor also accepts a qualified spelling when values return from another library. The input is copied with the constructor tag normalized to the receiving book before its nested `Nat` fields are converted. This applies to single- and multi-constructor ADTs, recursive fields, and variants without a `Nat` field. Unknown constructor tags fail immediately with a `TypeError` instead of bypassing conversion. The already-matching constructor path keeps its original one-copy behavior; no extra work is added to ordinary C or interpreter evaluation. The guide documents the bridge.

Failing-before: two independently loaded `.bend` libraries, `B.dec(A.make())`, raised `TypeError: Invalid mix of BigInt and other type in subtraction`. After: Bun loader passes that case (`4n`), a two-constructor variant (`8n`), recursive Nat-bearing values (`8n`), both directions of library handoff, plain JS objects using short/qualified tags, and boundary rejection of wrong tags including nested wrong variants. Separately emitted self-contained ES modules pass the same counter/variant/recursive handoff under Node. Existing `marshal_native_forms` interpreter and emitted JS, and `js_group_args` emitted JS, pass unchanged. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 47/47. The repository test gate executes one Bend book at a time; the two-book loader scenario was exercised with an external smoke program, not as a single-book golden. Cluster/macOS gates not run.

```text
Location: main
20 | def main() -> U32:
21>|   twice(~sq, 3)
```

### The file

```python
import Base

def sq(+x: U32) -> U32:
  (x * x : U32)

def twice(~f: U32 -> U32, x: U32) -> U32:
  f(f(x))

def main() -> U32:
  twice(~sq, 3)
```

I expected `sq` to be accepted as a `U32 -> U32`. As I understand it, a `+` parameter only asks more of the caller's argument (it must be `Data`), and every `U32` is `Data`, so `sq` can be used wherever a plain `U32 -> U32` is expected.

I don't know whether rejecting it is deliberate. Templates have had soundness bugs before (#902, #905), so there may be a reason the two function types must match exactly. If so, an error that says a `+` parameter can't be passed where a plain one is expected would help. The workaround is to take `x` plainly and rebind it inside the body with `+x = x0`.

title: F32 on the JS lane answers differently from C: pow's specials, a last-digit tie in F32.show, and F32.read just past a float midpoint
body:
### What you did

`bend t.bend` (interpreted), then `bend t.bend -o t.js -o t` and ran both, with the file below.

### What happened

The same program prints different numbers on C than on JS and the interpreter:

```text
C:      1 1 1 1.4414062 1.0000001 1
JS:     nan nan nan 1.4414063 1 1
interp: nan nan nan 1.4414063 1 1
```

Three separate causes, each where a JS built-in parts from C:

- **`F32.pow` specials.** C99's `pow(1, y)` is 1 for every `y`, NaN too, and `pow(-1, ±inf)` is 1. `Math.pow` answers NaN for all three.
- **`F32.show` on a last-digit tie.** C prints through `printf`, which rounds an exact tie to even. JS's `toExponential` rounds it up, so `1.44140625` shows as `1.4414062` on C and `1.4414063` on JS. This affected 0.45% of 200k sampled floats.
- **`F32.read` just past a float midpoint.** JS parses to a double, then `Math.fround`, so it rounds twice. A decimal just past the midpoint of two floats parses to the midpoint itself, which then ties to even. `F32.read("1.0000000596046447753906250001")` is `1.0000001` on C (`strtof`, one rounding) and `1` on JS. Just under the midpoint (`…249999`), both give `1`.

These matter for the "develop on JS, ship native" workflow the README suggests: the same program can print different numbers on the two targets.

### The file

```python
import Base

law val:
  for m: Maybe<&2, F32>
  F32

def val(m):
  match m:
    case None{}:
      0.0
    case Some{v}:
      v

law num:
  for s: String
  F32

def num(s):
  val(F32.read(s))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  nan = num("nan")
  inf = num("inf")
  a = F32.show(F32.pow(1.0, nan))
  b = F32.show(F32.pow(F32.neg(1.0), inf))
  c = F32.show(F32.pow(F32.neg(1.0), num("-inf")))
  d = F32.show(1.44140625)
  e = F32.show(num("1.0000000596046447753906250001"))
  f = F32.show(num("1.0000000596046447753906249999"))
  IO.print(a ++ " " ++ b ++ " " ++ c ++ " " ++ d ++ " " ++ e ++ " " ++ f)
```

I have a fix for all three on the JS side only, and will open it as a PR.

### bend --version

main at af569d48 (2.0.31); also 2.0.29 (574b6d39). JS lane on bun 1.4.2 and node

Linux x86_64 (WSL2)
