title: A Kind-spliced lambda can make the all-green emitted book compute the unused column's value (kernel-certified 7n vs source 3n)
body:
### What you did

BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bend drift.bend --check-only, --verdict, and -o + kernel on the emitted book, with an oracle equality appended to the emitted book to certify what it actually computes.

(Corrected the file below to the exact reproducer; an earlier edit of this issue carried a hand-simplified variant that does not parse-check. This one is verified as-is.)

### What happened

All three gates are green, but the emitted book computes a different value than the source: the source's `use()` evaluates to `3n`, while the kernel-certified emitted book's `use` evaluates to `7n` (an appended oracle def `ora7 : {use == 7n : Nat}` is ACCEPTED by the kernel on the emitted book, `ora3 : {use == 3n : Nat}` is rejected). The drift is deterministic and flips with the two columns' values (swapping 7n/3n flips the certified value), and propagates downstream (`Nat.add(use(), 10n)` certifies 17, not 13). Mechanism: the Kind-specialized parameter splices the inline identity lambda into the instance body; the splice is scope-moved onto the convoyed match parameters and routes to the UNUSED column's `Mk{(z => 7n)}` instead of the used `Mk{(w => 3n)`. Ordinary's own reflexivity accepts `{use() == 3n}` at the source level — the two worlds disagree on the same definition's value (and if you assert it in the source, `--verdict` then fails, so the divergence is only visible through the emitted book).

The same shape at the type level (type-valued specialized lambda column convoyed through a match) is sharper: the kernel proves `obs == MkT{Nat}` while the source computes `MkT{Bool}`, again with all gates green — available on request.

This looks like the #1168 scope_move capture family reaching the value level while all gates stay green.

### The file

```python
import Base

type Box is Type:
  Mk{fn: Nat -> Nat}

def qof2(f: Box -> Box) -> Quant:
  &1

def Unit2(f: Box -> Box) -> Type:
  Unit

def get(b: Box) -> Nat:
  match b:
    case Mk{fn}: fn(0n)

def looseK(f: Box -> Box, g: Box, h: Box, -A: Kind(qof2(f)), -w: Unit2(f), b: Bool) -> Nat:
  match b:
    case True{}:  get(f(h))
    case False{}: get(f(h))

def use() -> Nat:
  looseK((y => y), Mk{(z => 7n)}, Mk{(w => 3n)}, Unit, Unit{}, True{})
```

title: --verdict depends on declaration order: swapping two type declarations turns SOME PROOFS FAIL into ALL PROOFS CHECK
body:
### What you did

bend ab.bend --verdict (then the same with ba.bend, the file with the two types swapped)

### What happened

```text
$ bend ab.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend ab.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.
$ bend ab.bend -o ab.bendtt
BendTT: out of scope, so not in ab.bendtt:
- A: names A.qv.arms, out of scope: names B, out of scope: a kind that depends on a run-time value
- B: a kind that depends on a run-time value
$ bend ba.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK

A self-recursive type (self.bend, the second file below) fails in every order:
$ bend self.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend self.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. [...]
$ bend self.bend -o self.bendtt
BendTT: out of scope, so not in self.bendtt:
- A: a kind that depends on a run-time value
```

### The file

```python
# ab.bend (ba.bend is the same file with `type B` declared before `type A`)
def qof(n: Type) -> Quant:
  &1

type A<n: Type> is Kind(qof(n)):
  A1{b: B<n>}

type B<m: Type> is Type:
  B1{a: A<m>}

# ---- self.bend (a separate file) ----
def qof(n: Type) -> Quant:
  &1

type A<n: Type, m: Type> is Kind(qof(n)):
  A1{a: A<m, n>}
```



**Cause.** `spec_of`
([safe.ts#L347-L373](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L347-L373))
caches one result per name:

* its cycle guard
  ([L350](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L350))
  answers `[]` ("nothing specialized") for a name whose computation is still in progress;
* [L362](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L362)
  reads that placeholder when the DFS reaches a name on the stack;
* [L370](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L370)
  caches every answer permanently, including answers derived from the placeholder.

The rule is monotone, so the intended answer is its least fixpoint. The code runs one DFS pass seeded
with bottom, which under-approximates the fixpoint on any cycle. Roots are visited in declaration
order. So with A first, B caches `[false]` and keeps `m` live, and `A<m>` then puts a run-time value
at A's specialized parameter, which is out of scope (`spec_val`,
[L376-L384](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L376-L384)).
With B first, B reads A's finished answer and everything is specialized consistently. On the
self-cycle, A reads its own placeholder and answers `[true, false]` instead of `[true, true]`, so it
fails in every order.

**Fix direction (tested).** Compute `spec_of` as a least fixpoint. Re-run the DFS pass while any
in-progress read came out lower than that name's final answer in the pass, and cache only the answers of
a consistent pass. It terminates, since answers only grow and are bounded by the parameter count. It
costs one pass when no read comes out low. It fixes all three files, and the kernel accepts the output.
It is about 35 lines, and `-o` output is byte-identical on every `tests/**` and `demos/**` file whose `.bendtt` the kernel
already accepts (1057 of the 1558).

The simpler alternative, "don't cache a result that read an in-progress entry", fixes `ab.bend` but
**not** `self.bend`, so I'd avoid it.

**Impact.** A false FAIL, and it fails closed: the defect only removes specializations, and any kind
that depends on a parameter left live goes out of scope. None of the files under `tests/` or
`demos/` hits it, but a verdict that flips when two declarations are swapped is a real usability bug.




### bend --version

2.0.32

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

_No response_

title: --verdict: a binder inside one parameter's type can mark a later, live parameter as specialized ("a kind that depends on a run-time value")
body:
### What you did

bend alias.bend --verdict

### What happened

```text
$ bend alias.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend alias.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.
$ bend alias.bend -o alias.bendtt
BendTT: out of scope, so not in alias.bendtt:
- use: a kind that depends on a run-time value
$ grep -A1 '^h.qv' alias.bendtt
h.qv : ∀-x0 : ∀x0 : Nat -> ∀x1 : Nat -> *1 -> Nat =
  λ-x0 => h_7e_m
$ ~/.bend/bendtt/7f6ef51c9f75d7de/bendtt alias.bendtt
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In h.qv:
affine live code, calls that descend
```

### The file

```python
import Base

def qof(n: Nat) -> Quant:
  &1

def h(-P: @a: Nat -> @k: Nat -> Kind(qof(k)), m: Nat) -> Nat:
  m

def use(y: Nat) -> Nat:
  h(a => k => Nat, y)
```

`m` is an ordinary live `Nat`, and no kind depends on it, so I'd expect `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

**Cause.** `spec_of` lowers each type at depth 0
([safe.ts#L368](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L368)),
so the binders inside parameter `j`'s domain get levels `j, j+1, …`. Those collide with the parameter
levels, and `go` records raw levels
([L358-L359](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L358-L359)).
In `h`, `P`'s domain puts `k` at level 1, which is also `m`'s level. So `k` occurring in a kind marks
`m` as specialized, and `spec_of(h) = [false, true]`. Two failures follow:

* `use` passes a run-time `y` at the "specialized" `m`, so it goes out of scope (`spec_val`,
  [L376-L384](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L376-L384));
* the root instance `h.qv = λ-x0 => h_7e_m` calls the root constant `h~m` before it is emitted, so the
  kernel rejects it too.

The same aliasing lets an inner binder at level `j` mark parameter `j` itself: with `Kind(qof(a))`,
`P` is specialized.

**It can also drop a def silently.** Give the aliased parameter an empty type, and the def gets no
root, so `--verdict` PASSes while `h` never reaches the kernel:

```python
import Base

def qof(n: Nat) -> Quant:
  &1

type Emp is Data:

def h(-P: @a: Nat -> @k: Nat -> Kind(qof(k)), e: Emp) -> Emp:
  e
```

```text
$ bend alias_emp.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend alias_emp.bend -o alias_emp.bendtt      # no "out of scope" line
$ grep -c '^h' alias_emp.bendtt
0
```

This is #1135's mechanism, reached from a live, non-`~` parameter. It is sound for the same reason,
since `h`'s type is vacuously true, but `h`'s body is never rechecked.

**Fix direction (tested).** Walk the telescope, and lower each parameter's domain, and whatever follows
the parameters, at depth `tld.n`, so genuine parameter references keep levels `< tld.n`:

```ts
const walk = (T: HTerm, j: number): void => {
  const F = B.term_force(T);
  if (F.$ === "All" && j < tld.n) {
    go(B.term_lower(F.A, tld.n), false);
    walk(F.B(B.Var(F.k, j)), j + 1);
  } else {
    go(B.term_lower(F, tld.n), false);
  }
};
[tld.T, ...(tld.$ === "ADT" ? tld.c.map((c) => c.T) : [])].forEach((T) => walk(T, 0));
```

Every variant passes with it, and `-o` stays byte-identical.

**Impact.** A false FAIL on a rare shape: a Π-typed parameter with at least two binders, whose kind
depends on a non-first inner binder, followed by a live parameter. There is also the vacuous silent drop
above.

bend 2.0.32

Linux x86_64

_No response_

title: --verdict overflows the stack on a ~ parameter of some datatypes: model_at's cycle check misses cycles through ∀-typed fields
body:
### What you did

bend model.bend --verdict

### What happened

```text
$ bend model.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend model.bend --verdict
Error: the machine stack overflowed (a deep recursion, or a literal too large to expand)
```

### The file

```python
import Base

type W<-F: Nat -> Type> is Type:
  C{g: Nat -> W<F>}

def f(~w: W<(n => Nat)>, y: Nat) -> Nat:
  y
```

A root with a `~` parameter needs a model of the parameter's type. `model_at`
([safe.ts#L431](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L431))
builds one by walking constructors, and stops cycles with a path of datatype keys
([L446](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L446)).
The key is `term_key(term_lower(F, d))`
([L443](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L443)).
It includes the levels of binders inside `F`'s arguments, so the same datatype gets a different key at
depth `d` and at `d+1`. The ∀-typed field `g: Nat -> W<F>` bumps `d`
([L439](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L439)),
so the path never repeats. This isn't a deep-but-finite recursion like #993: the walk never ends.

Control: with `W<-F: Type>` at `W<Nat>` (no binder in the argument), the same program gets
`ALL PROOFS CHECK` from `--verdict`.

**A second shape grows memory instead.** In a nested datatype, the keys grow without bound, and
constructor-first order tries `NCons` forever:

```python
import Base

type Nest<-A: Type> is Type:
  NCons{x: A, rest: Nest<Pair(A, A)>}
  NNil{}

def f(~n: Nest<Nat>, y: Nat) -> Nat:
  y
```

`--verdict` on this passed 32 GB before it was killed. Run it only under a memory cap.

**Fix direction.** Key a datatype without its binder levels (or lower it at a fixed depth), and bound
the walk, treating exhaustion as "no model" (out of scope) instead of crashing.

**Impact.** A crash, or unbounded memory, on programs bend2 accepts. It fails closed: no verdict is
printed. Like any unbounded run, it is a resource-exhaustion risk for tools that run `--verdict` on
untrusted files without a cap.

title: BendTT mismatch for opaque higher-order template with dependent equality result
body:
## Bug description

Bend 2.0.32's ordinary checker accepts a closed definition containing an opaque higher-order template parameter whose result type contains dependent equality, but `--verdict` cannot validate the same definition and reports a TypeScript/BendTT mismatch.

This is not being claimed as a soundness exploit or bounty submission. The kernel rejects it; the report is for the reproducible checker/formalization synchronization failure.

## Environment

- Bend: 2.0.32
- Source revision tested: `v2.0.32`, commit `573002f01ec6c52416d44489543f69a9625facf8`
- macOS arm64

## Minimal reproducer

```bend
import Base

type N is Data:
  Z{}
  S{p: N}

def pred(n: N) -> N:
  match n:
    case Z{}: Z{}
    case S{p}: p

def inj(a: N, b: N, e: {S{a} == S{b} : N}) -> {a == b : N}:
  %x@e : {pred(S{a}) == pred(_) : N}
  {==}

def use(~F: @a: N -> @b: N -> {S{a} == S{b} : N} -> {a == b : N}, a: N, b: N, e: {S{a} == S{b} : N}) -> {a == b : N}:
  F(a, b, e)

def main() -> N:
  Z{}
```

Save as `higher_evidence_base.bend` and run:

```sh
bend higher_evidence_base.bend --check-only
bend higher_evidence_base.bend --verdict
```

## Observed behavior

`--check-only`:

```text
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
```

`--verdict`:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.
```

## Minimization results

The mismatch disappears when any of these changes are made:

- Remove the `~` from `F` and make it an ordinary affine function parameter.
- Remove dependent equality from the result type while retaining equality as an input.
- Use the standalone `inj` proof without the higher-order opaque template parameter.

Equality only as an input passes both checker and verdict. Equality in the result of an opaque `~F` reproduces the mismatch.

I also tested direct, curried, let-bound, eta-expanded, and explicitly annotated applications. They all preserve the same mismatch. Making the result family reduce to an `Empty` branch does not produce an accepted proof: `--verdict` still rejects the definition.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. the ordinary checker rejects this unsupported form before reporting `ALL PROOFS CHECK`, or
2. BendTT accepts and validates the emitted term.

The current result is an explicit synchronization failure between the ordinary TypeScript checker and the formalized kernel.

title: Claim.consistent rules out Enu [], but an emptied datatype elaborates to Σ1 t:<> -> D.arms t: the missing corollary, proved against bendtt.lean
body:
### What you did

Compared Claim.consistent (bend2/bendtt.lean) with what safe.ts emits for Empty (bend empty.bend -o empty.bendtt)

### What happened

```text
Claim.consistent (bendtt.lean L1529-1531) states that no checked def's type converts to Enu []:
  ∀ bk k d, Book.check bk = .ok () → Book.get bk k = some d → ¬ Conv bk d.T (Enu [])

But safe.ts never emits Enu [] for Empty. It emits every datatype, Empty included, as a Σ over its
constructor labels:

$ bend empty.bend -o empty.bendtt
$ grep -A1 '^Empty' empty.bendtt
Empty.arms : ∀x0 : <> -> *2 =
  λ{}
--
Empty : *2 =
  Σx0 : <> -> (Empty.arms x0)

So "no def the kernel accepts has type Empty" (GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md) doesn't follow from
Claim.consistent as stated. It is true, but it needs a corollary that isn't in bendtt.lean. The
corollary is proved in the first comment, against an unmodified bendtt.lean.
```

### The file

```python
import Base

def id_empty(x: Empty) -> Empty:
  x
```

[`Claim.consistent`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bendtt.lean#L1529-L1531)
says that no checked def's type converts to `Enu []`. But `adt_emit`
([safe.ts#L316](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L316))
emits every datatype, `Empty` included, as `Σ1 t:<Ctrs> -> D.arms t`, which is a different type former.
GUIDE.md
([L658-L659](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/guide/GUIDE.md#L658-L659)),
CHANGELOG.md
([L57-L58](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/CHANGELOG.md#L57-L58))
and AGENTS.md
([L16-L17](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/AGENTS.md#L16-L17))
say that no def the kernel accepts has type `Empty`. That's true, but it takes a corollary of the same
argument `consistent` uses (`halts`, `progress`, `canon_pair`, `empty`). Here it is. Appended to an
unmodified `bendtt.lean` (2.0.32), `lean bendtt.lean` succeeds, and
`#print axioms consistent_empty_adt` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`:

```lean
-- A live Σ over the empty enumeration is uninhabited: `consistent`'s argument (halts, progress,
-- canon_pair, empty) for the type every emptied datatype elaborates to, `Σ1 t:<> -> D.arms t`.
theorem consistent_sig (bk : Book) (k : String) (d : Def) (q : Quan) (B : Term)
    (ok : Book.check bk = .ok ()) (get : Book.get bk k = some d) (hq : q.live = true) :
    ¬ Conv bk d.T (.Sig q (.Enu []) B) := by
  intro c
  have ⟨wt, lv⟩ := book_check bk ok
  have ⟨i, hi⟩ := index_of_get get
  have hl : Term.Live bk (.Ref k) := by
    simp [Term.Live, Term.live, Term.called, Term.unspine, hi,
      (List.findIdx?_eq_some_iff_findIdx_eq.1 hi).1]
  have hr : Typed bk [] (.Ref k) d.T := by
    have := Typed.ref (Γ := []) (σ := Term.Var) get; rwa [sub_var] at this
  have ht : Typed bk [] (.Ref k) (.Sig q (.Enu []) B) := .conv hr (.inl c)
  suffices ∀ t, Acc (fun u t => Eval bk t u) t → ¬ Typed bk [] t (.Sig q (.Enu []) B) from
    this _ (halts bk _ lv (fun _ => rfl) hl) ht
  intro t a; induction a with
  | intro t _ ih =>
    intro ht; rcases progress bk t _ wt lv ht with v | ⟨u, e⟩
    · obtain ⟨a, b, rfl⟩ := (canon_pair (r := q) (ks := []) (a := .Rfl) (b := .Rfl) wt v ht).1 ⟨_, .refl, .refl⟩
      obtain ⟨_, ⟨A, B', rfl, ha, _⟩, f, _⟩ := gen ht
      exact empty bk a wt ((value_tup v).1 hq) (.conv ha (.inl (conv_sig (fits_conv f)).2.1))
    · exact ih u e (pars_sr wt ht (eval_pars lv.1 e))

-- The datatype itself: no checked def's type converts to a `Ref` whose body is `Σ1 <> -> X`
-- (safe.ts's adt_emit shape), so no def has type `Empty`, or any other emptied datatype.
theorem consistent_empty_adt (bk : Book) (n k : String) (dn d : Def) (X : Term)
    (ok : Book.check bk = .ok ()) (gn : Book.get bk n = some dn) (hv : dn.v = .Sig .Q1 (.Enu []) X)
    (get : Book.get bk k = some d) : ¬ Conv bk d.T (.Ref n) := by
  intro c
  have ⟨_, lv⟩ := book_check bk ok
  have hd : Conv bk (.Ref n) (.Sig .Q1 (.Enu []) X) := hv ▸ pconv (.delta gn (lv.1 n dn gn))
  exact consistent_sig bk k d .Q1 X ok get rfl (conv_trans c hd)
```

The Σ has to be live (`q.live`). A dead Σ over `<>` isn't empty in the kernel, by design, since nothing
dead counts as live evidence: the kernel accepts `bad : Σ-x0 : <> -> <()>` with the dead field filled by
an erased self-reference. `adt_emit` always uses `Σ1`, so the corollary covers what safe.ts emits.

**Suggestion.** Add these two theorems (or an equivalent `Claim`) to `bendtt.lean`, so that the claim
the docs make is the one the kernel states.

This isn't a soundness report. Nothing here inhabits `Empty`. It is a gap between what the docs promise
and what the shipped theorem states, and the corollary closes it for `Empty` and every other emptied
datatype.

title: Imported files answer to their file name as well as to their alias, so one prefix can point at two files
body:
### What you did

`BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bend main.bend --verdict` on the two-file layout below, then on the four-file layout.

### What happened

Two files. `main.bend` imports `./X.bend` under the alias `Z`, and never declares an alias `X`. Still, `X.f` resolves:

```text
$ bend main.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
```

Renaming `X.bend` to `real.bend` (keeping `as Z`) gives the expected `expected : a defined name / observed : X.f`. So the file name is acting as a namespace prefix, independently of the alias.

Four files. `main.bend` aliases `./q.bend as X`. Another import (`y.bend`) loads `./X.bend` under `as Z`. In `main.bend`, `X.M` names `q.bend`'s def and `X.f` names `X.bend`'s def at the same time: the file-name namespace and the user alias merge. A reader of `main.bend` sees `import ./q.bend as X` and a claim about `X.f`, and assumes the wrong file.

The guide says "The alias is local to the importing file" (`guide/GUIDE.md`, imports section), which this contradicts. The emitted BendTT carries the real `X.f` with its real body, so the kernel checks the right thing; this is a name-resolution issue, not a soundness one.

Same result on 2.0.32 and on main at 777ee0b (2.0.34), run as `bun bend2/main.ts`.

### The file

Two-file case:

```python
# X.bend
import Base

def f(a: Nat) -> Nat:
  0n
```

```python
# main.bend
import Base
import ./X.bend as Z

def go() -> {X.f(1n) == 0n: Nat}: {==}

def main() -> Nat:
  0n
```

```python

def M() -> Nat:
  9n
```

title: The kernel walks a bound value only when the body copies it
body:
## The bug

`--verdict` refuses a file that `bend f.bend` checks and `bend f.bend -o f.bendtt`
translates. The kernel's own message, which `cli_verdict` does not print, is:

```
In all_ones_2048:
out of fuel
```

The boundary is sharp and deterministic: **850 list cells check, 851 does not.**
The same file with the `idl` wrapper dropped — so the stated type and the proof's
are syntactically equal and nothing converts — is accepted at **8192**.

Found against 2.0.32 on a real 4096-cell leaf enumeration. First commit here is
its minimal form, over `Base` alone. Reproduces unchanged on `main`.

## What it costs, measured

Rebuilding the kernel at a sixteenth of `FUEL` moves the boundary from 851 to
**207**. That is 851/4, not 851/16 — the cost is **quadratic in the size of the
data**, and 851 cells is where n² crosses 400,000,000.

## Why

`Term.val` took a closed q=2 let value or argument to normal form at **every**
binding. A recursion over data binds its own tail at each step, and that tail is
already in normal form — so the walk ran again per step.

## The fix

The two call sites of `Term.val` ask first:

```lean
def Term.copies (cl : Bool) (q : Quan) (f : Term) : Bool :=
  cl && q == Q2 && 1 < Term.uses f 0
```

At one live use the walk buys nothing. A value substituted once is evaluated once
whether it is bound eagerly or lazily, so taking it to normal form early can only
pay for parts the body never demands — it is not a trade, it is work with no
beneficiary. Above one use, val runs exactly as before.

`Term.uses` is the affine check's own counter, unchanged; it moves above the
evaluator that now reads it. It **adds** a match's arms rather than taking their
max, so the test is conservative: val still runs on any binder whose copies could
be on one path.

The only new work is the `Term.uses` call. It reads the binder's body — a static
term, the def's source, never the data — and `run` already walks that body once
per call, as `inst` does once per let. Nothing is cached and no limit is added.

val doing less is a `Pars` step either way (`Par.beta` carries no `Data` side
condition), so `wnf_pars` gains one case that closes the new branch by `.refl`.
Every other proof in the file is untouched; `lean bendtt.lean` is clean.

## Evidence

**The bug is gone, and the cost is linear:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/check/conversion_data_bound_once.bend` | out of fuel | checks |
| the same file at 8192 / 16384 / 49152 cells | out of fuel | checks |
| last size the kernel accepts | 851 | ~55000 |
| the same boundary at a sixteenth of `FUEL` | 207 — that is /4 | ~3500 — that is /16 |

**Nothing else changed class.** `--verdict` over all 1521 files of `tests/`: every
file keeps its verdict. 969 agree → 970 with the new test, 65 unsafe, 486 bend2
rejects, and `conversion_shared_cells_once` is still the one false reject, out of
fuel in 7.5 s before and after.

**It does not slow proofs.** `bench/checker` emitted and read by the kernel,
median of five interleaved runs:

| bench | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| compute_1600 | 962 ms | 961 ms | −0.1% |
| defs_12800 | 5191 ms | 5204 ms | +0.2% |
| generics_3200 | 4526 ms | 4296 ms | **−5.0%** |
| proofs_3200 | 6401 ms | 6395 ms | +0.0% |
| trees_400 | 1507 ms | 1540 ms | **+2.1%** |

`trees_400` is the one consistent regression — nine runs, no overlap between the
two sets. Everything else is flat or better.

The kernel over all 969 agreeing corpus files: 6.94 s either way. A 12.5 MB book
of 181 laws: **28.0 s → 21.9 s**, same verdict.

`bendtt.lean` +921 bytes. Gates run locally, not on the minis; `tests` and `repo`
not run.

title: `--verdict` passes a def that the kernel never checks
body:
### What you did

bend root_cols_repro.bend --verdict && bend root_cols_repro.bend - root_cols_repro.bendtt

### What happened

```text
## Repro


bend root_cols_repro.bend --verdict
bend root_cols_repro.bend - root_cols_repro.bendtt


## Result


ALL PROOFS CHECK


The verdict passes, but the def `skipped` is missing from the kernel text.
The `.bendtt` output holds these defs only:


Void.arms
Void
seen
Nat.arms
Nat


`skipped` is not there, and it is not reported as out of scope either.

## Expectation

One of these:

1. `skipped` goes to the kernel, or
2. `--verdict` fails and names `skipped` as out of scope.

`safe.ts` states the rule itself: "What the kernel cannot express is out of
scope: it goes, with every def that names it, and --verdict fails."

## Cause

The cause is in `root_cols` in `bend2/safe.ts`.

1. `v` is a `~` parameter, so `spec_of` marks it as specialized.
2. Its type `Void` is a datatype with no parameters, and every constructor
   has no fields. With zero constructors, that test is true by default.
3. So `vs` is the empty list: `adt.c.map(...)` over zero constructors.
4. `vs !== null`, so the function returns `vs.flatMap(at)`, which is `[]`.
5. `safe_book` pushes one root per entry. Zero entries give zero roots.
6. With no root, the def is never emitted, and `oos` never lists it.

The relevant lines:


const vs = A.$ === "Qnt" ? [B.None(), B.Lone(), B.Many()].map((q) => B.Qua(q))
  : adt !== null && adt.c.every((c) => B.term_wnf(e.book, c.T).$ !== "All") ? adt.c.map((c) => B.Ctr(c.k, [])) : null;
if (vs !== null) {
  return vs.flatMap(at);
}


## Impact

- The claim itself is sound. A def that takes a value of an empty type holds
  for every argument, because there are none.
- The problem is the guarantee. `--verdict` reports that the kernel checked
  every def, and here it checked none of the body of `skipped`. Only bend2
  checked it.
- So any bend2 checker bug that sits inside such a def would pass
  `--verdict` without the kernel seeing it.
- I did not find a way to turn this into a proof of `Empty`. A caller must
  pass a closed value of the empty type, and none exists.

## Suggested fix

Treat an empty enumeration as out of scope, so the verdict fails loudly:


if (vs !== null) {
  if (vs.length === 0) {
    oos("a specialized parameter of an empty type");
  }
  return vs.flatMap(at);
}


An alternative is to emit the def once at an opaque constant, as the code
already does for a specialized parameter of any other type.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `bend version` | bend 2.0.32 |
| Commit | 3378e623 |
| `uname -sm` | Darwin arm64 |
| `clang --version` | Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) |
| Lean | v4.34.0 |
```

### The file

```python
# root_cols_repro.bend
import Base

type Void is Data:

law skipped:
  for ~v: Void
  for n: Nat
  Nat

def skipped(v, n):
  n

def seen(n: Nat) -> Nat:
  n
```

title: Constructing Empty via descending recursive Bad data
body:
### What you did

bend --verdict no-base.bend

### What happened

```text
~/.bend/bin/bend no-base.bend  --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK

~/.bend/bin/bend no-base.bend -o no-base.bendtt

cat no-base.bendtt
Bad.arms : ∀x0 : <Step> -> *2 =
  λ{.Step: Σx0 : Bad -> <()>; λ{}}

Bad : *2 =
  Σx0 : <Step> -> (Bad.arms x0)

drain : ∀x0 : Bad -> Empty =
  λ{(,): λ{.Step: λ{(,): λx0 => λ{(): (drain x0); λ{}}}; λ{}}}

Empty.arms : ∀x0 : <> -> *2 =
  λ{}

Empty : *2 =
  Σx0 : <> -> (Empty.arms x0)
```

### The file

```python
import Base

# No base case: only a step. Every value needs a smaller Bad inside, forever.
# This type should be EMPTY (no closed value). Is it accepted as a declaration?
type Bad is Data:
  Step{p: Bad}

# If Bad is empty, we can eliminate it into anything -- INCLUDING Empty --
# but only given a Bad value, which we cannot build. So this takes a param
# (sound negation) OR we try to descend to produce Empty.
# Try: recurse on Bad, "reaching" the nonexistent base as Empty.
def drain(b: Bad) -> Empty:
  match b:
    case Step{p}:
      drain(p)
```

title: A published file goes without a leading byte order mark, so a package whose LICENSE was saved with one imports
body:
Some editors (Notepad, some Visual Studio setups) put a byte order mark (the three bytes `EF BB BF`) at the start of a text file. `bend --publish` read each file with `readFileSync(…, "utf8")`, which keeps the mark, so the hub stored and hashed the file with it. `bend.ts` fetches a package's files with `res.text()`, and UTF-8 decoding drops a leading mark, so the importer hashed different text and refused the file:

```
a file at …/0x…/LICENSE hashing to 3d61d9…
```

The publish reported success; nobody could import the package.

A `.bend` file with a mark already fails the checker before it is published, so today only a LICENSE (or a foreign `.c`/`.js` file) gets through. The fix is in `pkg_files` (`main.ts`): each file it sends drops a leading mark. The mark says nothing about the text, so the author sees no difference. `bend.ts` is left alone.

A companion change on the site repo makes the hub refuse a file that opens with a mark, so a `bend` released before this one gets a clear refusal instead of a package nobody can import.

## Tests

- `gates/ping.ts` gains a check: a package whose LICENSE opens with a mark publishes under the hash of the files without it, and an import of it runs. 34 / 34 against a local hub, with and without the hub change; without the `main.ts` change the new check fails on the hash mismatch above.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 49 / 49.

title: --verdict: a lambda whose variable is used twice does not convert to the same lambda passed for an abstract function, under a stuck call
body:
### What you did

```
bend twice.bend && bend twice.bend --verdict
```

### What happened

```text
$ bend twice.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend twice.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. [...]

$ bend twice.bend -o twice.bendtt && bendtt twice.bendtt   # kernel built by --verdict for 2.0.34
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In t:
expected: ((apply x0) λx1 => ({λ+x2 => ((Nat.add x2) x2) : ∀x2 : Nat -> Nat} x1))
observed: (code x0)
```

With `a => Nat.add(a, 1n)` in both places (the variable used once), both
commands print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

### The file

```python
import Base

def apply(m: Maybe<&2, Nat>, f: Nat -> Nat) -> Nat:
  match m:
    case None{}: 0n
    case Some{n}: f(n)

def code(m: Maybe<&2, Nat>) -> Nat:
  apply(m, +a => Nat.add(a, a))

def same(m: Maybe<&2, Nat>, -f: Nat -> Nat, e: {apply(m, f) == code(m) : Nat}) -> Unit:
  Unit{}

def t(+m: Maybe<&2, Nat>) -> Unit:
  same(m, +a => Nat.add(a, a), {==})
```

`apply(m, _)` is stuck on the abstract `m`, so the conversion compares the
two function arguments. In the emitted book, `same` states
`(apply x0 λx2 => (x1 x2)) == (code x0)`: its `f` is eta-expanded as a plain
`λx => f x`, while `code` has `λ+x1 => (Nat.add x1 x1)` (the variable is used
twice). Instantiated at `t`, the kernel's expected side keeps the redex
`({λ+x2 => … : ∀x2 : Nat -> Nat} x1)` under the plain λ, and does not identify
it with `code`'s `λ+`. bend2 does.

We met it proving that a `do` chain over `Result` returns only what it
checked: the continuation of a `+x : A <- m` binding is such a `λ+`, and an
inversion lemma for `Result.bind` takes the continuation as an abstract
`f`. We worked around it with one inversion lemma per binding, stating the
continuation literally.

title: 2.0.34: checking an inline equality mutates a shared partial head and changes acceptance
body:
## What I did

On `v2.0.34` (`7d8a3eb`), I checked this Base-free file:

```bend
type U is Data:
  U{}

def l(A: Type, B: Type) -> Type:
  A

def r(A: Type, B: Type) -> Type:
  A

type Box<-h: Type -> Type> is Type:
  Box{}

def G(-f: Type -> Type -> Type, -g: Type -> Type -> Type) -> Type:
  {f == g : Type -> Type -> Type} -> Box<g(U)>

def make() -> G(l, r):
  e => Box{}

def delta() -> Box<l(U)>:
  make()({==})
```

```console
$ bun bend2/main.ts --check-only repro.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bun bend2/main.ts --verdict repro.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
```

## What happened

Acceptance depends on whether the same equality proof is inline. Replacing the last definition with these two definitions makes 2.0.34 reject the file:

```bend
def proof() -> {l == r : Type -> Type -> Type}:
  {==}

def control() -> Box<l(U)>:
  make()(proof())
```

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : Box<l(U)>
- observed : Box<r(U)>
Location: control
```

The inline reproducer is also a regression from `v2.0.33`, which rejects it at `delta` with the same `expected Box<l(U)> / observed Box<r(U)>` error.

## Expected behavior

Checking the inline `{==}` argument should not mutate the result type used by the surrounding application. Inlining a proof or moving it into a named definition should not change whether this program type-checks.

## Notes

This appears to exercise the filled share-cell merge added in 2.0.34. While checking the inline equality, the bare references `l` and `r` compare equal by eta expansion. The comparison then aliases/replaces the cached cell for `r`. The codomain reuses that cell under a partial application, so `Box<r(U)>` is subsequently observed as `Box<l(U)>`. With the named proof, that mutation does not occur in the surrounding application and the nominal partial heads remain distinct.

This report is about stateful checker behavior, not a proof of falsehood: `l` and `r` are extensionally equal here, which is why the emitted BendTT is accepted by `--verdict`.

## Environment

- Bend: `v2.0.34` (`7d8a3eb`)
- System: `Darwin arm64`
- Clang: `Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)`

title: --verdict --publish silently discards --verdict and publishes unverified — the two flag guards omit each other
body:
### What you did

Ran bend <file>.bend --verdict --publish, expecting the CLI to reject the pair the way it rejects --verdict -o and --verdict --check-only

### What happened

```text
The book was published to BendHub ("public and permanent") and no verdict was computed or printed. Exit 0. Confirmed on a file that fails --verdict at the kernel gate: it published anyway.
```

### The file

```python
any
```


**Analysis.** Two adjacent guards each omit the other's flag:

* [main.ts#L276](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/main.ts#L276) — `if (publish && (outs.length !== 0 || only || checkup))`: no `verdict`.
* [main.ts#L279](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/main.ts#L279) — `if ((only || verdict) && (outs.length !== 0 || checkup || (only && verdict)))`: no `publish`.

So `--verdict --publish` passes both. `cli_publish` is then reached first and **returns**
([main.ts#L293](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/main.ts#L293)), before `cli_verdict`
([main.ts#L301](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/main.ts#L301)) is ever evaluated.

A user who writes `bend f.bend --verdict --publish` meaning "verify, then publish" gets "publish,
unverified, permanently". The discarded flag is never named, and the action is irreversible.

**Expected.** Either `--publish takes no other option` (the message the guard already exists to
print), or publish only after a PASS.

title: The kernel's proofs say the same in fewer tokens, and check a little faster
body:
`bendtt.lean` sat 114 ttok under its 64k cap, which leaves no room for kernel changes such as #1173. This PR only shortens proof bodies: no def, no theorem statement and no kernel behavior changes.

### Numbers (macOS arm64, Lean 4.34.1)

| | tokens | `lean bendtt.lean` | `--verdict` kernel build |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 63,886 | 6.41 s | 9.5 s |
| first commit | 61,190 | 6.40 s | 9.5 s |
| this PR | **58,839** (−5,047) | **6.32 s** | 9.3 s |

(best of 5 runs; the build is `lean -c` + `leanc`, what `--verdict` runs once per kernel version)

### What changed

- **Only proof bodies.** All 233 theorem statements on main are unchanged, checked mechanically, and no `def`, `structure`, `inductive` or `macro` line changed. Two lemmas are new: `le_rfl` (for the 24 inline `.inl (.refl _)`), and `strip`, lifted out of `confluent`. A few lemmas moved up so later ones can reuse them (`live_call` above `live_ok`, `ok_app`, `dm_repl`, `hd_ext`, `csym`, `enu_inj`).
- **Common rewrites:** `simp only …; exact` became `simpa`/`rwa`, `have … ; subst` became `obtain … rfl`, tactic blocks that only built a term became terms, and several `by_cases` became `split`. Repeated steps in `wnf_pars`, `chk`, `tp`, `ev`, `sr`, `live_sub`, `gsl`, `cmp_size` and the smaller lemmas are merged.
- **Check time.** The second commit keeps a change only if that proof checks no slower, profiled per declaration with `trace.profiler`. Some proofs got faster:
  - `strip` now uses `induction`; its pattern-matching recursion used to wait for `triangle`.
  - `triangle` reads `Term.dev` without building its equation lemmas.
  - `pars_former` no longer runs `simp_all` over `Term.former`.
  - `wnf_pars`, `eval_pars` and `eval_value` are shorter as well as quicker.
  - A first golfing pass had put `triangle` on the critical path of Lean's parallel check (+0.8 s); it is off it now.

### Checks

- `lean bendtt.lean` prints nothing: no errors, warnings or `sorry`. `consistent`, `halts`, `book_check`, `sr`, `progress`, `empty` and `confluent` depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- A kernel binary built from this file gives the same verdict as main's on all 1,109 `.bendtt` files the repo's tests, demos and benches emit, and on 7,000 fuzzed recursive defs fed to the kernel directly.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 49 / 49. Lines over 120 characters went from 17 to 8.

Not run: `gates/test.ts` and `gates/safe.ts` on the cluster (the kernel's behavior is unchanged, so they should not move).

#1173 (the descent change for #1167) will be rebased on top of this.

title: --verdict: the kernel runs out of fuel on conversion_shared_cells_once.bend, which bend2 checks by sharing (2.0.34)
body:
### What you did

```
cd tests/check
bun ../../bend2/main.ts conversion_shared_cells_once.bend --verdict
```

On `main` (`eb8f58b1`, Bend 2.0.34).

### What happened

bend2 checks the file, but the kernel rejects it:

```text
$ bun ../../bend2/main.ts conversion_shared_cells_once.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bun ../../bend2/main.ts conversion_shared_cells_once.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. ...
```

Running the kernel directly on the emitted book (9.8 KB) shows why:

```text
$ bun ../../bend2/main.ts conversion_shared_cells_once.bend -o csc.bendtt
$ ~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt csc.bendtt
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In agree_32:
out of fuel
```

It takes about 7 s to give up.

The test came in with 2.0.34 (#1071, PR #1151, `7d8a3eb0`), which made bend2's conversion compare a shared graph once. As the test's own comment says, each of the 32 levels of both roots uses the level below twice, so comparing them as a tree takes about 2^32 steps. bend2 now avoids that blowup; the kernel in `bend2/bendtt.lean` doesn't, so it runs out of fuel on `agree_32`.

This wasn't caught because the normal gates don't run `--verdict`: `gates/test.ts` checks each test with `--checkup`, and `gates/_run.ts` runs repo, test, perf and ping. Only `gates/safe.ts tests` runs the kernel over the corpus. In a local `--verdict` sweep of all 1,522 files in `tests/`, this is the only kernel mismatch.

### Expected

Either the kernel's conversion shares equal subterms the way bend2's now does (so `agree_32` checks within its fuel), or the mismatch is recorded as a known limit of the kernel. Sharing in the kernel means `bendtt.lean`'s proofs have to cover it.

### The file

`tests/check/conversion_shared_cells_once.bend`:

```python
import Base

def mix(a: U32, b: U32) -> U32:
  (a * 31 + b : U32)

def root_loop(d: Nat, +h: U32) -> U32:
  match d:
    case 0n: h
    case 1n+p: root_loop(p, mix(h, h))

def sq(+h: U32) -> U32:
  mix(h, h)

def root_rec(d: Nat, +x: U32) -> U32:
  match d:
    case 0n: x
    case 1n+p: sq(root_rec(p, x))

def agree_32(+x: U32) -> {root_loop(32n, x) == root_rec(32n, x) : U32}:
  {==}
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.34 (`main` at `eb8f58b1`)

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.6.4.2)

title: --verdict: two mutually recursive type-level defs that pass a kept parameter are rejected as "calls that descend"
body:
### What you did

```
bend kept.bend && bend kept.bend --verdict
```

### What happened

```text
$ bend kept.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bend kept.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. [...]

$ bend kept.bend -o kept.bendtt && bendtt kept.bendtt   # kernel built by --verdict for 2.0.34
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In A.group:
affine live code, calls that descend
```

With `-c` instead of `+c` in both defs (the parameter erased), both commands
print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. With `+c` kept but moved to the last position
(`B(f: Nat, +c: Nat)`, `A(e: Nat, f: Nat, +c: Nat)`), both commands also print
`ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The kernel built from PR #1173 (the fix for #1167) still
rejects `kept.bend`.

### The file

```python
import Base

def B(+c: Nat, f: Nat) -> Type:
  match f:
    case 0n: Empty
    case 1n+g: {c == c : Nat} & A(c, 1n, g)

def A(+c: Nat, e: Nat, f: Nat) -> Type:
  match e:
    case 0n: Unit
    case 1n+p: B(c, f)
```

`A` matches `e` and passes `f` unchanged to `B`; `B` matches `f` and calls
`A` back on its smaller part `g`. Every cycle descends on `f`. The kept
parameter `c` is passed unchanged in both calls.

WONTFIX.txt says the termination check reads arguments left to right (#770):
an argument before the decreasing one must pass through unchanged. Here `c`
does pass through unchanged, and the same group is accepted when `c` is
erased or moved after `f`, so the rejection seems to come from the kept
leading parameter alone.

We met it on a relation that states that an unfolding of an expression is
faithful: ten mutually recursive `-> Type` defs that carry the catalogue
they read (`+catalogue`). Erasing that parameter lets the kernel accept them.

title: A generic def over a Data record boxes it on the device heap: a Bool.pick of two records took Metal's compile from 8 s to over 11 minutes
body:
A generic def over a Data record, `Bool.pick` included, boxes the record on the device heap in flat code. Every call site then inlines the heap's allocation, `term_drop`'s walk and `ctr_take`. In a large kernel this took Metal's compiler from 8 seconds to more than 11 minutes.

Bend 2.0.34 (`777ee0b5`), macOS 26.6.2, Apple M5.

## Repro

```python
import Base

type Tint is Data:
  Tint{r: F32, g: F32, b: F32}

def mixed(a: Tint, b: Tint, +f: F32) -> Tint:
  Tint{+ar, +ag, +ab} = a
  Tint{+br, +bg, +bb} = b
  Tint{(ar + (br - ar) * f : F32), (ag + (bg - ag) * f : F32), (ab + (bb - ab) * f : F32)}

def light(+x: F32) -> Tint:
  Bool.pick(Tint, (x < 0.0 : F32), Tint{0.84, 0.95, 1.2}, mixed(Tint{1.3, 1.06, 0.72}, Tint{1.05, 1.0, 0.93}, x))

def red(t: Tint) -> U32:
  Tint{+r, g, b} = t
  F32.to_u32((r * 100.0 : F32))

def leaf(+i: U32) -> U32:
  red(light((U32.to_f32((i % 1000 : U32)) * 0.001 - 0.5 : F32)))

def tree(+k: Nat, +i: U32) -> U32:
  match k:
    case 0n:
      leaf(i)
    case 1n+e:
      a b = tree(e, (i * 2 : U32)) tree(e, (i * 2 + 1 : U32))
      (a + b : U32)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(U32.show(tree!(14n, 0)))
```

In the emitted C, `light`'s spin builds the computed `Tint` on the heap with `heap_alloc(e, cls_fit(3))` and three stores. It builds the literal one as a static term. It then calls the pick's spin with two `Term`s. That spin drops the unchosen record through `term_sink`, which inlines `term_drop`'s heap walk. Last, it unpacks the chosen record with `ctr_take` and `spare_free`.

Two variants of `light` for comparison:

- **match**: the same choice as a `match` in a non-generic def keeps the three fields in registers, as flat records are everywhere else.

  ```python
  def chosen(c: Bool, +x: F32) -> Tint:
    match c:
      case True{}:
        Tint{0.84, 0.95, 1.2}
      case False{}:
        mixed(Tint{1.3, 1.06, 0.72}, Tint{1.05, 1.0, 0.93}, x)

  def light(+x: F32) -> Tint:
    chosen((x < 0.0 : F32), x)
  ```

- **generic**: a generic def of one's own boxes just as `Bool.pick` does:

  ```python
  def choose(-A: Type, c: Bool, a: A, b: A) -> A:
    match c:
      case False{}:
        b
      case True{}:
        a
  ```

So the type parameter is what boxes the record, not `Bool.pick` itself.

The three variants were built to C and to a GPU program. Each ran with `--gpu off`, and nothing ran on the GPU:

| `light` | `heap_alloc` of a `Tint` | GPU program | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bool.pick(Tint, ..)` | 1 | 96,848 bytes | 1690288 |
| generic `choose(Tint, ..)` | 1 | 96,848 bytes | 1690288 |
| non-generic `match` | 0 | 73,824 bytes | 1690288 |

One pick site adds 23 KB to the GPU program. With the pick inside a flat 60-step loop that `leaf` calls from eight places, the program is 687 KB against 184 KB.

## Where it bit

[Bendcraft](https://github.com/AdrielSantana/bendcraft) is a voxel ray caster whose Metal program is 2.2 MB. One change made the light's colour a `Bool.pick` between two `Tint`s: the sun's, or the moon's once the sun has set. Before, it was a blend by a factor. That def is reached from four sites in a pixel's shading.

With the pick, `--gpu-build` did not finish. `MTLCompilerService` was at 99% CPU and 1.2 GB after 11 minutes, when I killed it. The same program with the choice written as a blend by a `Bool.pick(F32, ..)` builds in 8 seconds.

The tiny repro above still builds in a second or two. The compile time only blows up at the kernel's full size, so it is not a repro of the hang itself. It does show the code that caused it. Had it compiled, that code would also have allocated on the heap once a pixel, a call.

## Expected

A pick between two flat records should stay in registers, as a select per field, the way a non-generic `match` already does. One way would be to specialize a generic def at a flat Data type in flat code. Failing that, the drop of the unchosen value should not inline `term_drop`'s walk at every site.

The workaround is to choose the record in a non-generic def that matches on the `Bool`, or to pick its scalars.

title: fix(compiler): avoid expanding shared display layouts
body:
## Why

the JSON cache key from #1166 copies shared child layouts into a tree. That can turn a small type into a huge string before the compiler even checks the cache.

The regression below just returns `Ready{42}`, but compiling it exceeds 800 MiB because another alternative in its result type contains nested sums.

## Scope

Use layout identity and the normalized type as `show_main`'s cache key, through the existing `memo` helper. One net compiler line and a 16-line regression. The layout distinction from #1166 stays intact.

## Tradeoffs

Separate layout objects with equal structure may get separate descriptors. This avoids expanding the graph or adding a structural interner.

## Blast radius

Display descriptors for pure-main results in JS and native builds. IO mains bypass this cache.

## Verification

On macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11 and clang 23.1.2. The reproduction command is:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/reg/show_shared_layout.bend -o /tmp/show_shared_layout.js
```

- Compiling the new regression to JS on `eb8f58b` crossed an 800 MiB sampled-RSS limit and the watchdog stopped it. With this fix, the same command completed in 0.10 s at 113 MiB sampled RSS.
- The regression passes checking, interpreter, emitted JS and native execution, printing `Ready{42}`.
- Ten existing tests and one mixed-type control pass, including all three #1166 regressions. Their emitted C and JS are byte-identical to main. The unprintable-main diagnostic also matches.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 49/49. `git diff --check` passes. Compiler size is 63,778/64,000 tokens, 13 more than main.

Cluster, GPU and benchmark gates were not run.

title: Add a way to unlink / release a BendHub package name
body:
`bend link <name>@<version> 0x<hash>` can register and attach a name to a published package, but there is no matching command (or documented Bender UI) to drop a name an owner no longer wants.

Names ≥12 characters register immediately; short names go to auction. Once linked, leftover names from experiments stay claimed with no owner-side release path.

## Ask
- A documented owner-only way to release a name (e.g. `bend unlink <name>@<version>` or Bender UI), with clear rules when a name still has dependents / is the package’s display name.

## Not asking for
- Support cleanup of specific existing names in this issue (can open separately if you want that).

title: The kernel checks a self-call's descent against the column's pattern, as bend2's term_descend does, so a constructor rebuilt around a smaller part of its input descends (#1167)
body:
Fixes #1167. An alternative to #1173: the same rule, with the kernel's check written to read like bend2's `term_descend` rather than as path arithmetic.

### What fails

bend2 accepts a self-call whose argument rebuilds a constructor around smaller parts of the input (`term_descend`: same constructor, each field no bigger, one smaller; or no bigger than some field of the pattern). The kernel on main only accepts a rebuild of the input itself or of one of its pieces. So `height(Node{rest})` under `Node{Cons{x, rest}}` fails `--verdict` with `affine live code, calls that descend`.

### The change

bend2 compares an argument with the def's own pattern (`lhs.t`). The kernel now builds that pattern too, and compares against it the same way.

- **`Guard.pat`** builds each column's pattern from the case tree's tags and hits: every piece the tree split open is a `Pat.pair`, and the rest are `Pat.hole`s.
- **`Guard.at`**: the argument is the piece itself when it is the variable the tree bound there, or the label a match hit there.
- **`Pat.cmp`** is `term_descend`: the piece itself is eq; a constructor compares its fields in turn (`Pat.fields`); and when a field may be bigger, the argument is lt if it is no bigger than another field of that constructor (`Pat.visit`). As in bend2, only the fields are tried, minus the one that failed: not the tag, and not the pairs that chain the fields.
- **Erased fields** (review): a field that is dead at runtime counts as eq when it is the variable the case tree bound at that position, as `term_descend` compares it. So a constructor with erased fields (`KNode{k, e, rest, m}`) can be rebuilt around a smaller live field.
- Each function recurses on a smaller pattern, so the weighted pattern size proves termination with no `decreasing_by`.

- **Field chains.** A constructor is `(tag, (f1, (f2, ())))` in BendTT, so its fields are read down that right-hand chain. A tail that is the variable the case tree bound there is eq, so a pair rebuilt around a piece that was split further still rebuilds it, as on main.
- **Group selectors (`safe.ts`).** A helper's selector was `(.h, (.k, ()))`, so its call back passed `(.k, ())`, a pair on the chain, which the search no longer tries. It is now `(.h, ((.k, ()), ()))`: the call back passes a field of the selector. Base's `Word.adc.group` and the other law-and-helper groups need this.

### Proofs

- **`pat_below`:** a result other than gt makes the argument, under σ, a closed value no bigger than the piece; lt makes it smaller. It is proved by strong induction on the same size measure.
- **Supporting lemmas:** `below_up`, `below_le` and `below_tup`. `Frame.tags` now says a tagged variable is closed (its env entries already are), which gives the dead field's closure in `pat_below`; `below_up` reads the parent piece off `Term.get` directly, so `get_drop` and part of `get_val` are gone. `cmp_size` reads the result, and `desc_lex`, `hcl` and the measure are unchanged.
- `lean bendtt.lean` prints nothing, and `consistent`, `halts`, `book_check`, `sr`, `progress`, `empty` and `confluent` depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

### Size

`bendtt.lean` is at **63,463 ttok** of its 64,000 cap (main 61,325), so the next kernel change will need cuts. The diff is `bendtt.lean`, the group selector in `safe.ts` (BendTT output only, 22,470 of its 24,000 cap), the paper and the new test; `comp.ts` and `main.ts` are unchanged, so compiled C/JS is the same as main.

When first opened, against an older main, this PR was 60,901 ttok against #1173's 59,402; both accepted exactly the same calls on everything below. This one follows bend2's structure and is faster on literal patterns; #1173 is smaller.

### Checks (head f2b7d278, rebased on main 4ff8545f, macOS arm64, Lean 4.34.1)

- **Head 2838bd25 (fields only, new selectors), local:** `lean bendtt.lean` prints nothing, and the seven theorems still depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`; repo gate 54/54; the new test passes `--verdict`. All 1,128 test files that emit BendTT, re-emitted with the new `safe.ts`, get the same verdicts as on f2b7d278. A deep nested pattern (k=22) checks in 0.42 s against 1.5 s; k=30 is still exponential (#1543). Not rerun at this head: the cluster gates and the fuzzer. The checks below are from f2b7d278.

- **New test:** `tests/proof/descent_rebuilt_shell.bend` covers `height` (#1167), `kheight` (erased fields, from the review), `flat` over lists of lists, `drop2` (a deeper piece rebuilt whole), `skip` (a shell around such a piece) and `dig` (fields found in two pieces below). bend2 accepts all six; the kernel on main accepts only `drop2`. `kheight` also fails on the previous head (35d534a6). Here all six pass, and all four backends print the same result.
- **Gates:** repo 54/54, ping 55/55, test 1607/1607, perf 124/124.
- **Verdict sweep:** `gates/safe.ts tests` on the cluster matches main on every file, plus one new pass for the new test. The one false reject (`conversion_shared_cells_once.bend`, out of fuel) fails on main too. `gates/test.ts` doesn't run `--verdict`, so this sweep is what guards the new test.
- **Lean check:** `lean bendtt.lean` takes 8.0 s against main's 8.1 s.
- **Fuzz:** on the first head, 7,000 random recursive defs, with each call fed to the kernel directly so bend2 does not filter it: the kernel accepted exactly the calls bend2 accepts, and none of the 3,228 calls that loop. That fuzzer isn't in the repo and wasn't rerun after the erased-field change; a smaller run of 99 erased-field calls reached 3 that bend2 accepts, and the kernel accepted all 3.
- **Kernel time** (first head; the 1,109 real files take as long as on main):

  | pattern | main | #1173 | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | list of 400 `Zero{}` against 399 | 17.5 s | 0.62 s | 0.65 s |
  | 32-character string against its tail | 34.7 s | 6.6 s | 0.21 s |
  | `400n` called on `401n` | 0.32 s | 0.49 s | 0.24 s |

### Not changed (review)

- `Arg.cmp` rebuilds the pattern on every self-call: it costs about as much as the comparison right after it, and caching it would add a field to every guard the proofs build.
- `Guard.at`'s label lookup is quadratic: fine at today's sizes, and fixing it means proof changes with little token room left.

title: --verdict: split a root stuck on a constant at the constructors it reads (#1175)
body:
Closes #1175.

## Problem

A parameter that a kind reads (`-A: Kind(q1(f))`) is specialized, and its generic root was checked at one opaque constant `run3~f`. When the kind matched on it, `q1(run3~f)` was stuck, so it wasn't a Quant literal (the kernel only has literal quantities). A match on it in the body had no constructor either (`pick`). Either way the root was out of scope, and `--verdict` failed on programs bend2 accepts.

## Fix (`bend2/safe.ts`)

A root that gets stuck on one of its constants is split, and each piece is checked again (`root_at`):

- A root is a set of decisions: which constructor (or Quant literal) each path into its specialized arguments takes. `root_cols` and `value` build the arguments from them, with a fresh opaque constant wherever nothing is decided yet. A split adds a decision and builds the root again from scratch.
  - A field's constant takes its type from the fields before it. In `Tag{mode, val: Sel(mode)}`, splitting `mode` to `Shared` gives `val` the type `Sel(Shared)`.
  - Sibling roots share no constant, so a failure cached at one can't block a split in another.
- A root drains the items it names, dead ones too, before it is done. An item named only in a type that gets stuck on a constant (a datatype whose kind reads it) splits it like a live one.
- Each attempt splits only its own constants (`Safe.splits`, cleared per attempt). Items a failed attempt left pending still go out, as ordinary items.
- A split takes the first constant in the stuck term that can split. A term is stuck on a constant where a kind needs a literal (`quant_eval`, and `kind`, which no longer swallows the failure), where a match needs a constructor (`pick`), or where a constant with no model must go out (`def_emit`).
  - A Quant constant splits into its three literals, and only when read: a Quant parameter nothing reads goes out once.
  - A datatype constant splits into the constructors left; a datatype with none left doesn't split, so its root is out of scope rather than gone.
- A field doesn't split when its declared type reaches its own datatype, through the defs and datatypes it names (`reaches`, memoized per field in `Safe.rec`). Where the declared type applies a datatype parameter or hands it to a def, the walk follows that parameter's argument too (`Ap{v: F(X)}` at `F = G`, which is `Ap` again); where it holds it as data (`a: A`, `List<A>`), it doesn't.
  - So splitting always stops, with no depth cap: a kind that recurses through a `List`, through a `Tree` and its `Forest`, through a datatype nested at ever larger arguments, or through a type-function parameter is out of scope at once.
  - A datatype nested in itself at other arguments still splits (`Two<Two<Mode, Mode>, Mode>`), since its fields hold their parameters as data.
- Only the items the roots reach go out, so a failed attempt's items are not checked.
- Each root keeps the value it read, so a branch can rely on its kind (e.g. copying `x` only in the branch where `A` is Data).
- Kernel names count up on a clash (`f.qv_7`), so a def with many roots doesn't get ever longer names.

A root that no kind or match reads stays a single root. The old up-front enumeration of Quant parameters, and of datatypes whose constructors have no fields, is gone, since splitting covers both.

## Tests

- New test `tests/check/spec_root_split.bend`, with a law on `main`'s value:
  - #1175's `run3`: the kind matches `f`.
  - `run4`: the kind ignores `f`, but the body matches it.
  - `dup`: a kind that matches a nested enum field of a record, and a branch that relies on its kind.
  - `two_split`: two specialized parameters; a callee gets stuck on the second in one sibling root, and then in the other.
  - `tag_id`: a field whose type reads the field split before it.
  - `res_root`: a datatype whose kind reads the constant, named only in a type.
  - `res_pt`: an instance named only in a type, next to a split; a failed attempt's pending items still go out.
  - `nest`: a datatype nested in itself at other arguments.
  - `q_unread`: a Quant parameter nothing reads, which goes out once.

  It passes `--verdict` with this change and fails on `main`. `two_split`, `tag_id`, `res_root`, `res_pt` and `nest` also fail on this PR's first commit.
- New test `tests/check/spec_root_split_out.bend`: `ap_f` (a kind recursing through a type-function parameter) and `void_f` (a kind matching an empty datatype) go out of scope at once. Before, `--verdict` hung on `ap_f` and silently dropped `void_f`. The gate classifies the file as out of scope; a hang would show as a timeout.
- Full local `--verdict` sweep over all 1,525 pre-existing files in `tests/`: the same verdicts as the first commit, whose only change from `main` is the new test.
- The BendTT of the 1,039 files that elaborate: 1,028 emit as many defs as the first commit's.
  - The new test emits more.
  - `parse/fill_quant_block` emits 5 defs instead of 19: its datatype's two unread Quant parameters no longer go out at all 9 values. It still passes.
  - The 9 others drop items that only out-of-scope roots reached, and all of them already fail `--verdict`.
- `tsc`: 11 errors, the same as before this change.
- Cluster gates, on this branch rebased onto `main` (`d0fda2f7`), next to `main` itself:

  | Gate | This PR | `main` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test` | 1530 / 1530 | 1528 / 1528 |
  | `repo` | 48 / 49 | 48 / 49 |
  | `perf` | 106–116 / 117 | 116–117 / 117 |
  | `ping` | skipped | skipped |

  - `repo` fails on `main` too: `bend2/comp.ts` is at 64,274 ttok, over its 64,000 cap. This PR doesn't touch `comp.ts`, and `safe.ts` is under its cap.
  - `perf`'s failing cells were all GPU runtimes of about 0.08 s, 5–13 ms off their pins (`mandelbrot`, `nbody`, `merkle`). The C that `bend` emits for those benches is byte-identical on this branch and on `main`, so the difference is timing noise.
  - `ping` needs the `bend-lang.com` site repo, which wasn't available here; it covers the installer and releases, which this PR doesn't touch.

## Limits

A kind that reads a value through a recursive field can't be split, so it stays out of scope, even when it only reads a level or two:

```python
def elem_q(stages: List<&2, Mode>) -> Quant:
  match stages:
    case Nil{}: &1
    case Con{Shared{}, rest}: &2
    case Con{Owned{}, rest}: elem_q(rest)
```

Covering that in general needs kinds as terms in the kernel.

A constructor whose fields have no model (e.g. a `{3 == 0}` field of an indexed family at indices it can't take) makes its root out of scope. A constant with no model would be an axiom of a possibly empty type, and whether that type is empty is undecidable in general.

A split takes the first constant in the stuck term that can split, which may not be the one the term reads. The next attempt then splits the right one, so this only costs roots, multiplied by each extra split:

- `dup` goes out at 4 roots where 2 would do, since `len` comes before `mode` in `Cfg`.
- A kind on `Cq{q: Quant, mode: Mode}` that reads only `mode` gives 6 roots instead of 2, since `q` comes first.

`safe.ts`: +1,018 ttok (20,079 → 21,097, cap 24,000).

title: bend --check-only hangs indefinitely on let-bindings whose expressions check in 0.04s when hoisted to a def
BendTT: kinds as quantity terms, meets, Σ at any kind and subsumption under ∀; --verdict emits generic defs once
body:
## What

The BendTT kernel can now express bend2's kinds as terms, and it fits function types by their parts, as bend2's LE does. `--verdict` no longer monomorphizes on quantities: a `Quant` parameter, and any parameter a kind reads, is an ordinary kernel variable, and each def goes out once, as bend2 writes it. Only template (`~`) parameters are still specialized.

Trust moves from bend2 to the kernel:
- no quantity is computed by bend2's evaluator before the kernel sees it;
- subsumption under `∀` is a proven kernel rule, not a bridge in `safe.ts`.

(This includes what was #1344.)

Rebased on `main` (bf968271, which includes #1339's Lean-versioned kernel cache). At this head: repo PASS 50 / 50, test PASS 1559 / 1559, and `gates/safe.ts tests` gives 1004 agree, 72 unsafe, 491 bend2 rejects, 2 out of scope and 1 false reject (#1193).

## Closes and supersedes

Closes #1175, #1179 and #1180. Supersedes #1201 and #1208.

Each repro and test below fails `--verdict` on `main` and passes here.

| | what it was | why it goes away |
|---|---|---|
| #1175 | `run3`'s generic root went out of scope: "a Quant that is not a literal" (the head annotation was fixed in 01875127; this was the open part) | the root is emitted once, with `Kind(q1(f))` as a kernel term |
| #1179 | `spec_of`'s cycle guard under-approximated its fixpoint, so `--verdict` depended on declaration order ("a kind that depends on a run-time value") | `spec_of` only marks `~` parameters, so there is no fixpoint. `ab.bend` and `self.bend` both check, in either order |
| #1180 | `spec_of` lowered each domain at depth 0, so an inner binder marked a later live parameter as specialized. Its second file silently dropped `h` | same; `use` checks, and `h` is now emitted and checked by the kernel |
| #1201 (PR, for #1175) | split a root stuck on a constant at the constructors or Quant literals it reads | nothing is stuck on a Quant constant any more. Both of its tests pass here: `spec_root_split.bend` checks, and so does `spec_root_split_out.bend`, whose `ap_f` and `void_f` it left out of scope; both are emitted and checked here |
| #1208 (PR, for #1179) | made `spec_of` a least fixpoint | the computation it fixes is gone; its test `spec_cycle.bend` checks here |

Checked and not affected:
- #1186 / #1225 (a `~` parameter of an empty type gets no root): `~` parameters are still enumerated, so it stays open.
- #1182 / #1263 (no model for an opaque `~F`): it fails the same way on both.

Every Bend snippet in the 82 open issues (92 files) was also run under `--verdict` on `main` and here. #1175 and #1180 now pass. #984's chain and #1205's file now fail, as described under Elaborator.

### Kernel (`bend2/bendtt.lean`)

- **`Typ` carries a quantity term, as bend2's `Kind(g)` does:** `*(q)` is the kind of a quantity `q : <Q0, Q1, Q2>`, with `*1` = `*(.Q1)` (Type) and `*2` = `*(.Q2)` (Data). Two kinds convert where their quantities do (`conv_typ`), as in bend2's EQ, so `*(.Q0)` and `*(.Q1)` are two kinds that fit each other. Like every type, a kind is dead: it is never evaluated.
- **`(a <&> b)`, the meet (minimum) of two quantities.** It reduces as bend2's does: `.Q2` is its identity and `.Q0` absorbs, on either side, even next to a stuck quantity (`Term.qmin`). It may be live: `Term.live` and `Term.uses` read both sides, and a live meet steps to a label.
- **`Σ` at any kind `*(g)`,** with each field at `kindof(q, *(g))`, and `*(g)` shifted under the field binder. So `Either<a, b> is Kind(a <&> b)` goes out as written.
- **`Fits` is inductive**, with these rules:
  - conversion;
  - kinds: `*(g)` fits `*(h)` when `g` is `.Q2` wherever `h` is, under every substitution;
  - enums: fewer labels;
  - **`∀q A B` fits `∀q C D` when `C` fits `A` and `B` fits `D`**: the domain reversed and the codomain along, as in bend2's LE;
  - transitivity.

  The checker decides kinds with bend2's rules (`qge`): `.Q2` is the top, `.Q0`/`.Q1` the bottom, a meet on the left needs both sides, and a meet on the right needs either. `Term.fits` threads fuel, compares two `∀`s' binder quantities first, and then fits them by their parts. `qge_sound` and `fits_sound` prove the checker against the rules.
- **`Fits.at` / `fits_at`** read a fit at a type former, in both directions: where `T` converts to a former, `U` converts to one of the same former whose parts fit. `fits_all`, `fits_conv`, `fits2` and `fits_former` follow from it. Subject reduction and progress use them:
  - β casts the argument along the domains' fit and the result along the codomains';
  - a split, a hit and a miss do the same;
  - a λ-match on an enum may receive a smaller enum.
- **Unchanged:** binder quantities stay literal, so the live check still reads quantities off the syntax. A type of kind `*(q)` is Data only where `q` reduces to `.Q2`, so `canon_data` keeps its route.
- `lean bendtt.lean` checks with no `sorry` under Lean v4.34.0 (the pinned version) and v4.34.1. Every claim (`consistent`, `book_check`, `confluent`, `sr`, `progress`, `halts`, `empty`) depends only on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, as before. The claim statements are unchanged; the typing judgment they quantify over is more general.
- +5,146 ttok (58,839 → 63,985, cap 64,000). The next kernel change has to simplify first.

### Elaborator (`bend2/safe.ts`, −415 ttok against `main` at 1a2e5cd3: 21,749 → 21,334, cap 24,000)

- `Kind(g)` becomes `*(g)` with `g`'s term, and `a <&> b` becomes `(a <&> b)`, as bend2 writes them. A literal `Kind(&0)` and a generic `Kind(q)` at `&0` are then one kernel term, `*(.Q0)`: no quantity is raised to its rung.
- No quantity is folded, closed or not: the kernel computes every one itself, so `--verdict` does not trust bend2's evaluator for them. (`main` folded closed meets, and its specialized quantities, by bend2's evaluator.) Two consequences, both from the open issues' snippets:
  - #984's chain `q(n+1) = q(n) <&> q(n)` up to `q26` runs the kernel out of fuel, a false reject. The kernel does not share the two unfoldings of `q(n)`, as bend2 does.
  - #1205's `Kind(qsize(Array.join(...)))` names the `@unsafe` `Array.join` and fails, as #1205 asks.
- A datatype's kind is emitted as a term.
- `spec_of` specializes template parameters only.
- A self-call's argument goes out whole when its binder quantities match the column's (`qsig_eq`), since the kernel fits domains, codomains and kinds itself. For example, `K0 : Nat -> Kind(&0)` passed at a `Nat -> Type` column is no longer η-expanded, and a rewrite goes out as written.
- `uses` counts both sides of a meet, as the kernel does: a meet is live code.
- `kind()` reads a closed kind's quantity to pick how a λ that uses its variable twice goes out: rebuilt when the kind is Type, and at q=2 when it is Data or open. For an open kind, the kernel decides; after a match, the kind may reduce to `.Q2`. It shares `closed_val` with `spec_val`, which no longer throws to say that a term is open.
- The quantity-only out-of-scope guards are gone: a `Quant` bound inside a match, a `Quant` argument to a variable, a type over `Quant`.

## Now in scope

- #1175's `run3`, and kinds that read nested fields: no splitting needed, so #1201 isn't needed either.
- A kind that reads a value through recursion, e.g. `elem_q(stages)` over a `List`.
- Quantities picked at run time: `keep(pick(b), …)` and `meet(pick(b), …)` with `Kind(a <&> b)`, and a meet computed at run time (`m(a, b) = a <&> b`).
- Generic datatypes whose kind is a meet, and generic functions over them, each emitted once.

Hand-written books, run through the built kernel, check what should be rejected:
- a `+` copy of an `Either` of stuck kind, generic or `Either .Q2 b`, is rejected;
- a function type in a Data `Either` is rejected;
- a Data type passed at a stuck kind is accepted;
- through `∀`, these are rejected: `K : <A> -> *1` at `<A> -> *2`, `∀(∀ *1 -> <A>) -> <A>` at `∀(∀ *2 -> <A>) -> <A>`, a function on `<A>` at `<A, B>`, and a `∀` at a `∀+`. Each fit in the sound direction is accepted, two levels of contravariance included.

## Tests

- New tests in `tests/check/`, each passing `--verdict` here:
  - `kind_terms.bend` (fails on `main`), with a law on `main`'s value. It covers everything above, plus a branch that relies on its kind, `∀` subsumption in both directions, and the equation `{Kind(x <&> &2) == Kind(x)}`.
  - `kind_self_call_eta.bend` (fails on `main`): a self-call passing `Kq(q) : Nat -> Kind(q)` at a `Nat -> Type` column.
  - Regression guards that `main` passes and this branch once failed:
    - `kind_none_is_type.bend`: the same self-call with `Kind(&0)`.
    - `kind_generic_none.bend`: a generic kind at `&0` against a literal `Kind(&0)`, by a law and by a self-call.
    - `meet_at_run_time.bend`: a meet of run-time quantities in live code, with laws on every row of its table.
    - `kind_domain_self_call.bend`: a self-call passing `g : Type -> Nat` at a `Kind(&0) -> Nat` column.
    - `kind_rewrite_goal.bend`: a rewrite of type `Nat -> Kind(&0)` at a `Nat -> Type` goal.
    - `meet_uses_in_arms.bend`: a variable used inside a meet in one arm and again in another.
- Each rule for quantity terms in `bendtt.lean` was compared with bend2's. These agree: the meet's reduction, `conv` against EQ, `fits` against LE (now under `∀` too), `Kind`/`Min` typing, `kindof` against the binder, `let`, `λ` and constructor-field kinds, and the live check's usage of a meet. The last three regression guards above come from the three places where they did not. Two of those (the self-call's domains and the rewrite goal) are now decided by the kernel's `∀` rule.
- Known, harmless difference: `Quant` is an enum in the kernel, so it is Data there and Type in bend2; the kernel accepts more.
- Full local `--verdict` sweep over every file in `tests/`, on `main`, this branch before the fixes, and at each later head. The 1,554 files common to all of them get the same class on each (agree, unsafe, bend2 rejects, out of scope with the same reasons, false reject), and each new test agrees.
- `tsc`: the same 12 errors as `main`. `gates/repo.ts`: PASS 50 / 50.
- Cluster gates at 3548a98a, rebased on 1a2e5cd3:
  - `gates/_run.ts`: repo PASS 50 / 50, test PASS 1554 / 1554, all within the 30 s cap. perf reported PASS, but scored between 40 and 121 / 124 across today's runs, and `main` itself scored 49–89 / 124 back to back. This PR doesn't touch `bend.ts`, `comp.ts` or `main.ts`. ping was skipped: there is no site repo checkout here.
  - `gates/safe.ts tests`, on 26 nodes, side by side with `main` at 1a2e5cd3: per file, identical to `main`'s table plus the eight new `tests/check` files, all "agree". That is 1000 agree (992 on `main`), 71 unsafe, 491 bend2 rejects, 2 out of scope and 1 false reject (`conversion_shared_cells_once`, #1193), the same files on each.
  - Not run: `gates/safe.ts hub` (no BendHub store here).
- A fresh review of the final diff found no soundness issue. Its findings and what happened to each:
  - Fixed: the open-kind case of `kind()` (above), and the order of `Term.fits`'s ∀ case.
  - Not reproduced: a law over `Quant` losing its model (a law with no body is a TODO, so bend2 stops first), and a nested domain quantity mismatch (bend2's LE rejects it too).
  - Known: see below.

## Known limitations

- The kernel's meet evaluates its right side even when the left is `.Q0`, which bend2 skips. A costly right side can therefore run the kernel out of fuel where bend2 is instant: a false reject, never a false accept. Short-circuiting needs a `wnf` case and its proofs, and the kernel has 15 ttok left under its cap.
- #984's chain `q(n+1) = q(n) <&> q(n)` runs the kernel out of fuel, also a false reject: the kernel does not share unfoldings as bend2 does.
- `kind()` still uses bend2's evaluator, but only to choose how a term goes out. Whatever it chooses, the kernel checks the result.

## Performance

These are local measurements on an Apple M4 under background load, with the trees interleaved per file and per run in one process. Elaboration is `safe_emit`, kernel is the BendTT binary on its text, and figures are medians.

| | elaborator | kernel |
|---|---|---|
| all 994 files bend2 accepts, sum of per-file medians (3 runs) | `main` 5,687 ms, this PR 5,974 ms (+5%) | `main` 19,945 ms, this PR 20,196 ms (+1%) |
| 300 generic defs with `Kind(a <&> (b <&> (a <&> b)))`, used at `&2, &1` (15 runs, load average ~55) | `main` 76.9 ms, this PR 11.7 ms | `main` 44.6 ms, this PR 12.6 ms |

On the test corpus the difference is within noise. Per-file ratios swing between 0.2× and 6× in both directions, and the sums move by a few percent. The corpus row was measured at 1a3fa1e5, before the later commits. The stress row was measured before the `∀` rule, which emits the same text for that file. Kernel time with the `∀` rule was not measured separately. On kind-heavy code, emitting each def once instead of a copy per quantity cuts elaboration about 6× and kernel time about 3×.

## Paper

`bend2/docs/BendTT/main.typ` and `paper/BendTT.pdf` (rebuilt with typst 0.15.1, now 10 pages) describe the kernel as it now is:
- kinds over quantity terms, `*(g)` and `(g <&> h)`, with `Q = <Q0, Q1, Q2>`;
- `Σ` at any kind, and the kind case of `U <= T` with the checker's rules for it;
- the `SORT` and `MEET` rules;
- the meet's evaluation step and its place in the live check and in the measure;
- `*(g) ≡ *(h)` only when `g ≡ h`;
- generic defs going out once;
- the `∀` rule of `U <= T`, and subject reduction reading a fit at a former.

It said the compiler emits a copy of each generic def per quantity. It also gets Bend's `Kind(&1)` / `List<&2, Nat>` spelling and the Lean line count (4,158; it said 4,247).


Closes #1175
Closes #1179
Closes #1180
