    Darwin arm64

### clang --version

    Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)

title: A String match whose default arm uses the scrutinee takes memory and time quadratic in the keyword length
body:
### What you did

```
bun bend2/main.ts main.bend -o out.js
```

`main.bend` is the file below.  It matches a `String` against 8 keywords of 10 characters.  The default arm returns the scrutinee.

### What happened

The compile succeeds and the output is correct, but it uses 1.4 GB of memory and 20 s of CPU for a 460-byte file.

I measured each variant with one compile on bend2 at `57b6c150`. "Peak RSS" is the maximum resident set of the process.

| Arms x keyword length | Default arm | Source | Peak RSS | CPU | out.js |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 x 10 | `case s: 0` | 687 B | 317 MiB | 5.2 s | 98 KB |
| 2 x 5 | `case s: s` | 246 B | 256 MiB | 3.3 s | 20 KB |
| 8 x 5 | `case s: s` | 414 B | 564 MiB | 8.1 s | 43 KB |
| 8 x 10 | `case s: s` | 460 B | 1,388 MiB | 20.2 s | 89 KB |
| 16 x 10 | `case s: s` | 725 B | 2,237 MiB | 44.8 s | 167 KB |

- The cost is linear in the number of arms and quadratic in the keyword length.  At 8 arms, 5 to 10 characters gives about 4x.
- When the default arm does not use the scrutinee (`case s: 0`), the cost is small and linear.
- The emitted JS stays linear.  The cost is in the checked term.

To find where the memory goes, I added a hook after `book_valid` and counted the nodes of the checked term of `kw`.  These nodes have the form `Ann(tm, Var("_", -1, ty))`.  I then deleted the checked terms and ran a full GC:

| Arms x length (`case s: s`) | Nodes in the checked `kw` | Live heap after check |
|---|---|---|
| 8 x 5 | 238,578 | 143 MB |
| 8 x 10 | 926,298 | 515 MB |
| 16 x 10 | 1,852,290 | 1,020 MB |

Most of the nodes are `WCon`, `False` and `True` constructors, which are the bits of the characters of the scrutinee. v2.0.25 and v2.0.28 make 2x more nodes than `57b6c150` (16 x 10: 3,767,620).

This is not the conversion case in WONTFIX.txt ("the checker is not optimal").  No equality check is involved.  The elaborated term is quadratic in the source before the checker compares anything.

A real program shows the same effect.  In a 2,400-def book (1.5 MB of source), six such matches make 92% of the 2.96M checked nodes.  That book holds 1.3 GB after check.  Examples of the shape:

```
def Cli.Mapping.boolean(text):
  match text:
    case "true": IO.pure(Big, Big.one())
    case "false": IO.pure(Big, Big.zero())
    case _: Cli.Mapping.parse("expected true, false, ...", text)
```

### Root cause (my reading of `57b6c150`, not confirmed with a debugger)

1.  `parse_patt` expands a string pattern into a full bit-level pattern tree (bend.ts:1731-1733, `lit_step` at 1089-1094, `word_to_term` at 1064-1070).  The tree is `SCon`, then `Chr`, then `U32`, then 32 `WCon{True|False}`, then `WNil`: about 66 constructors per character.  The comment at bend.ts:94 says that this per-unit expansion is by design.  It is linear and is not the problem.
2.  `match_flatten` (bend.ts:2634-2716) makes one `Mat` per constructor column.  For the default row (a `PVar`), it substitutes the scrutinee with the rebuilt constructor `kx = PCtr(c.k, fresh vars)` through `body_sub` (bend.ts:2698-2700).  `body_sub` wraps the body in a lazy `Sub` node (bend.ts:2609-2632).
3.  `term_higher` resolves each `Sub` with `patt_term` at each occurrence (bend.ts:717-719, 702-703, `patt_term` at 2722-2732).  Each mismatch leaf gets a new copy of the whole prefix matched so far.  A keyword of L characters has about 32 L mismatch leaves, and the prefix at a leaf has O(position) nodes.  Thus each keyword costs O(L^2).
4.  `def.v = term_higher(term_lower(term_higher(body_flatten(...))))` (bend.ts:2484) keeps these copies.  `Check` and `Infer` (bend.ts:478-484) then put one annotation on each node.

### Possible direction

Make each mismatch leaf share the rebuilt prefix, or bind the matched value one time, so the default arm costs O(L) per keyword.  Keep the type refinement of the default arm and the usage counts of the binder unchanged.  I did not write a patch because AGENTS.md says that bend.ts is human-written.

Workaround for users: in a string-literal match, do not use the scrutinee in the default arm.  For example, compare with an equality chain.

### The file

```
import Base

law kw:
  for s: String
  String

def kw(s):
  match s:
    case "aaaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "baaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "caaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "daaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "eaaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "faaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "gaaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case "haaaaaaaaa":
      "k"
    case s:
      s

law main:
  String

def main(): kw("haaaaaaaaa")

#|"k"
```

To make the other rows of the table, add arms or make the keywords longer.  To make the control row, change `case s: s` to `case s: 0`.

### bend --version

bend2 from source at `57b6c150` (main, 2026-10-02), run with bun 1.3.11. v2.0.25 and v2.0.28 also show this.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)

title: Array.new of a boxed value works in JS but native fail-stops at depth 24
body:
### What you did

I built the same checked pure program for native C and JavaScript.

```bend
import Base

def got(r: Array<String> & String) -> Nat:
  (a, s) = r
  String.length(s)

def main() -> Nat:
  got(Array.get(String, Array.new(String, 24n, F32.show(1.0)), 0))
```

### What happened

Both `--check-only` and `--verdict` print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. Emitted JS exits 0 and prints `1n`. The native C binary exits 1 with `bend: runtime fail-stop`.

Changing only `24n` to `23n` makes both backends exit 0 and print `1n`.

`F32.show(1.0)` matters only because it creates a dynamic heap-allocated `String`. In native `blk_new`, a boxed array shares its default term across `2^d` cells. The redirect reference count has 24 bits (`RFC_CNT = (1 << 24) - 1`), so `blk_new` explicitly posts `ERR_RFCS` when `d >= 24` and a default word is nontrivial. The JS implementation is `Array(2 ** d).fill(v)` and has no corresponding restriction.

The 24-bit count itself is a documented BendRT limitation, and #975 mentions that refcount overflow is rejected with `ERR_RFCS`. The observable issue here is the resulting backend acceptance split in the public `Array.new` operation: the same checked source completes on JS and fail-stops on native C. I found no issue or WONTFIX entry covering that depth-24 boxed-array split.

This is below the documented/common array-depth wall. `tests/io/array_depth_bound.bend` makes both lanes reject only a depth past 31 and describes depth 31 itself as legal subject to host memory. Native C therefore has a hidden lower acceptance wall based on the runtime representation of the element: a static or flat value can work at depth 24, while a dynamic boxed value fail-stops.

The lanes should either share an explicit boxed-array limit or represent the repeated native default without requiring a 2²⁴ reference count. The current source type and `Array.new` API do not expose the native-only restriction.

### bend --version

Reproduced on v2.0.34 (`7d8a3eb036042c6549461054d25a10f26d361c5c`) and current main (`57b6c150f63704f53d533776deb3859578d4b09e`).

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)

title: Native C retains every buffered channel closed without a later receiver
body:
### What you did

I repeatedly created a room-one channel, buffered one value, closed it, and dropped every handle. I compared it with the same loop closing an empty channel.

```bend
import Base

def loop(+fuel: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match fuel:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("done")
    case 1n+more:
      do IO<Unit>:
        +c : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32, 1)
        ok : Bool <- Chan.send(U32, c, 7)
        Unit <- Chan.close(U32, c)
        loop(more)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  loop(2000000n)
```

I built native C and emitted JS, then measured each with `/usr/bin/time -l`.

### What happened

Both programs print `done` and exit 0, but native C retains about 65 bytes for every closed buffered channel. At two million iterations current main uses 131,792,896 bytes peak RSS; the empty-channel control uses 1,982,464 bytes. Emitted JS uses 45,252,608 bytes for the reproducer and 43,974,656 bytes for the control. At 500,000 iterations native C uses 35,684,352 bytes, confirming linear growth.

The same result reproduces on v2.0.34: 131,776,512 bytes for buffered close and 1,982,464 bytes for the empty control.

In `bend2/effs/chan.c`, `chan_shut` calls `chan_free` only when `row->size == 0`. A closed buffered row is freed if another copied handle later drains it, but if the program drops every handle the row, its ring, and its buffered term become unreachable without ever entering `chan_idle`. Every leak also consumes one entry from the 16,777,216-row limit, so a sequential program can eventually fail with `more than 16777216 channels at once` despite having only one source-level channel alive at a time.

The JS runtime does not keep a global row table; the closed object becomes collectible when its handles are unreachable.

I found no matching issue or WONTFIX entry. The leak discussed during #1162/#1172 concerned a dropped parked operation and its timer, not a `Chan.close` that has already completed. Open PR #1259 changes timed channel operations but preserves the same `chan_shut` rule, so it does not free this closed buffered row either.

An immediate `chan_free` in `Chan.close` would change the existing behavior where a copied handle can drain buffered values after close, so the native fix appears to need handle reachability/reference tracking or an explicit lifetime rule.

### bend --version

Reproduced on v2.0.34 (`7d8a3eb036042c6549461054d25a10f26d361c5c`) and current main (`57b6c150f63704f53d533776deb3859578d4b09e`). Both `--check-only` and `--verdict` print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)

title: The host's column grows to a LINE of tasks a thread again, a drain splits its rows into units of 32 a thread, and rings rewind between turns (stacked on #1092)
body:
**Stacked on #1092.** This branch carries #1092's two commits (`c3b3485a`, `869f3208`) plus four of its own: `eca79903`, `4443868d`, `c419a203` and `3e8f8a97`. Review those four only. They need #1092's row-bounded turns and its claim word, so this should merge after #1092. The numbers below compare main (57b6c150) with the whole branch, #1092 included.

## What changes

- **The host grows fewer tasks up front (`eca79903`).** #1171 grew the column to `pool_size` rows of 128 tasks: 2,048 at 16 threads. On tree-matmul that starts all 384 rounds at once, each holding its own matrices. The column now grows back to a `LINE` of tasks a thread. To keep #1171's balance gain, a drain splits its rows into finer units instead (`pool_step`: as few lanes as leave 32 units a thread). After a column grow, a turn's row bound is the rows that grow reached.
- **Rings rewind between turns (`4443868d`).** Ring positions only ever increased, so over a run a ring touched a new plane, a 16 KB page, for every push. Each plane holds one slot for 2,048 lanes, so this reached 14–43 MB on kmeans and tree-bitonic. Between turns no lane runs, so the host now moves each ring of the turn's rows back to slot 0. It re-pushes the ring's pending tasks and clears the slots it wrote, because their lap bit would otherwise read as written. The GPU path and the slot protocol are unchanged.
- **Cleanup (`c419a203`, `3e8f8a97`).**
  - `ring_rewind` re-pushes through `ring_push`, so the slot format lives in one place.
  - It skips a ring that an `ERR_RING` overflow left past `RING_LEN`, which would otherwise overflow its buffer.
  - `pool_step` is computed once per claim.
  - The comments added to `row_grow` and `pool_step` are dropped, and `ring_rewind`'s is one line.
- **Size:** `comp.ts` 63,399 → 63,821 ttok over #1092 (+422; 179 under the cap).

## Main vs this branch

Paired A/B on the cluster. Each bench and mode ran on one mini: both builds use the perf gate's cc line and flags, with one warm run each, then 5 alternating timed runs, and each value is the median. Every output matches.

**RSS (MB):**

| bench | SEQ-CPU main → branch | PAR-CPU main → branch |
|---|---|---|
| tree-matmul | 2.7 → 2.3 | **68.5 → 14.5** |
| tree-radix | 651.3 → 650.5 | **825.1 → 656.5** |
| tree-bitonic | **146.9 → 132.1** | **178.1 → 141.7** |
| kmeans | **20.8 → 9.3** | **22.9 → 10.8** |
| merkle | 130.0 → 129.7 | 131.1 → 130.3 |
| hashmap | 2.3 → 2.0 | 9.5 → 8.6 |
| the other 10 | 1.9–2.2 → 1.6–1.7 | 2.8–4.1 → 2.1–2.9 |

PAR-GPU RSS is unchanged: 13.4–14.0 MB on both.

**Time** (branch / main, median of the 5 paired ratios):

| | SEQ-CPU | PAR-CPU | PAR-GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| geomean | 1.001 | **0.985** | 0.995 |
| range | 0.999 to 1.009 | 0.929 to 0.999 | 0.965 to 1.024 |

- **PAR-CPU:** no bench is slower. The largest gains are on tree-radix (0.929), tree-matmul (0.953), kmeans (0.970) and tree-bitonic (0.982).
- **SEQ-CPU** is within 0.4% everywhere except tree-radix, which is +0.9%.
- **PAR-GPU** has no cell whose 95% interval excludes 1.

## Gates

- **Repo gate:** `gates/repo.ts` passes, 50 / 50.
- **Test gate:** `gates/test.ts` passes, 1514 / 1514.
- **Perf gate:** `gates/perf.ts` passes **113 / 117 on this branch, against 106 / 117 on main**.

Cells that pass here and fail on main:

| PAR-CPU space | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| tree-matmul | 4.35x | 0.94x |
| mandelbrot | 1.47x | 0.85x |
| tree-radix | 1.33x | 1.07x |
| nbody | 1.27x | 0.87x |
| gameoflife | 1.21x | 0.85x |
| raytrace | 1.18x | 0.84x |
| kmeans | 1.16x | 0.53x |

Still failing:
- **PAR-GPU time on mandelbrot, merkle and nbody.** These fail on both main and the branch. They're the 60–100 ms cells, which vary from run to run.
- **tree-matmul SEQ-CPU time** reads 1.24x on the branch and 1.05x on main. This is the node, not the code. The paired A/B ran main and the branch on the same mini and measured 2.30 s for both. A rerun of that cell alone, on another mini, measured 1.94–1.97 s for both. Both scripts give this cell the same job index, so it lands on the same mini, which looks about 18% slower here.

## Not run

- #1092's own many-turn workloads (bend-parallel's scan, sort and histogram);
- Linux, x86 and CUDA.

title: C emission expands an erased shared layout exponentially; depth 22 uses about 3 GiB
body:
## What I did

I passed a deeply nested `Choice<...>` only as the erased type argument of an identity function and emitted native C. No value of that type is constructed.

```sh
BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts erased_layout.bend --check-only
BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts erased_layout.bend -o erased_layout.mjs
BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts erased_layout.bend -o erased_layout.c
```

```bend
import Base

type Choice<-A: Data> is Data:
  Left{value: A}
  Right{value: A}

def id(-A: Data, x: U32) -> U32:
  x

def go(x: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(U32.show(id(Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<Choice<U32>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>, x)))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    x : U32 <- IO.thread_count()
    go(x)
```

## What happened

On main commit `57b6c150f63704f53d533776deb3859578d4b09e`, `--check-only` takes 0.46 s and JS emission takes 0.69 s, but C emission at depth 22 peaks at 3,063,728 KiB RSS. A harness that sampled the child with `ps -o rss` every 25 ms completed in 10.571 s. The emitted C is only about 78 KiB; it compiles normally, and JS and C both print `1`.

Depth 20 already peaks at 789,552 KiB. Released v2.0.34 (`7d8a3eb036042c6549461054d25a10f26d361c5c`) peaks at 740,464 KiB at depth 20.

The head of PR #1244 (`d4d27f3308c6c999d5aa3385d9a71040109a04e9`) still peaks at 755,760 KiB at depth 20 and 2,985,200 KiB at depth 22. That PR fixes a separate `JSON.stringify` in the constructor cache.

## Why

`emit_native` forms its specialization key with `ers.map((e) => JSON.stringify(lay_of(fl.book, e)))`. Each `Choice<A>` layout points both arms at the same child layout, so the layout is a linear DAG, but `JSON.stringify` expands both references recursively. The key therefore has exponential size even though the source type and emitted program are linear in the nesting depth and the parameter is erased.

A layout-identity key, using the same stable memoized `Lay` objects without structural serialization, avoids expanding the DAG. This is the same underlying data shape as #1244 but a separate keying site that its patch does not touch.

## Environment

```text
Bend main 57b6c150f63704f53d533776deb3859578d4b09e
Bend v2.0.34 7d8a3eb036042c6549461054d25a10f26d361c5c
macOS arm64
Bun 1.4.2
```

title: Checker template-instance depth limit does not bound breadth
feat(window): add Window.capture
body:
## Why

Window clients need an on-demand snapshot of their rendered pixels after output completes. `Window.capture` returns the same affine owner and a fallible `Capture{width, height, pixels}` with the actual client dimensions.

Native Linux uses X11 readback after `XSync(False)`. Pixels are top-left row-major U32 words in `0x00RRGGBB` format. The client must remain fully on-screen and unobscured throughout readback, as required by XGetImage.

## Scope

- Add `Capture` and `Window.capture` to Base, with an X11 effect and explicit ENOTSUP results on other backends.
- Preserve the owner and queued events on recoverable failures. Validate geometry, TrueColor masks, and Array capacity at the native boundary.
- Add a Bend example, arithmetic laws and proofs, and runtime fixtures for pixels, resize, errors, events, and ownership.

## Tradeoffs

An `Array<U32>` stores packed pixels rather than allocating a list or Image tree. Its capacity is a power of two, while width times height defines the logical length. The capacity tail is zero. There is no 512 by 512 capture limit.

## Blast Radius

Readback runs only when the caller requests capture. X11 protocol errors return a Result; transport loss and Bend heap exhaustion retain the runtime's fatal policy. X11 cannot guarantee valid obscured pixels or an atomic snapshot against arbitrary external changes.

## Verification

- Capture fixtures and existing graphics tests passed 24 lanes across Linux C, emitted JavaScript, and the interpreter. The native Bend example also passed.
- An independent process resized the client to 703 by 517 and painted it through another X11 connection. Capture read the new dimensions and literal server colors, returned EAGAIN while unmapped, preserved the owner, and left injected Key and Close events queued.
- `bend PROOF.bend` and `bend PROOF.bend --verdict` passed. These prove only pure coordinate arithmetic; native capture invariants have runtime tests.
- macOS, other native platforms, CUDA, and mini-cluster gates were not run locally.

title: C compiler reads a refcount redirect as a record when a shared Data type is hidden under rewrite
body:
## What I did

I shared a three-field `Data` value twice. Its type is definitionally the same `Rec`, but is wrapped in an open constant-motive rewrite. The program is closed and pure, and it contains checked proofs of both the numeric result and the Boolean returned by `main`.

```bend
import Base

type Rec is Data:
  Rec{a: U32, b: U32, c: U32}

def use(r: Rec) -> U32:
  Rec{a, b, c} = r
  (a + c : U32)

def unhide(e: {0 == 0 : U32}) -> ((%q@e : Data; Rec) -> Rec):
  %h@e : ((%q@h : Data; Rec) -> Rec)
  x => x

def twice(+e: {0 == 0 : U32}, +x: (%h@e : Data; Rec)) -> U32:
  (use(unhide(e, x)) + use(unhide(e, x)) : U32)

def hold(x: U32) -> U32:
  x

def opaque(u: Unit) -> U32:
  a b = hold(1) hold(0)
  (a + b : U32)

def result() -> U32:
  +x = opaque(Unit{})
  twice({==}, Rec{x, (x + 1 : U32), (x + 7 : U32)})

def result_ok() -> {result() == 18 : U32}:
  {==}

def runtime_tag() -> Bool:
  U32.is_eq(result(), 18)

def runtime_tag_ok() -> {runtime_tag() == True{} : Bool}:
  {==}

def main() -> Bool:
  runtime_tag()
```

I checked it with both public proof gates and ran the JS and native C outputs.

```text
$ BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend -o repro.js && bun repro.js
True{}
$ BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend -o repro && ./repro --threads 1
False{}
```

## What happened

The checker and BendTT accept the closed proofs, and JS returns the proved `True{}`, but native C exits 0 with `False{}`. Changing only `main` to return `result()` makes JS print `18` and native C print the stable wrong value `2301744268` on this machine. A recursive-tree version of the same trigger exits with `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)`; after disabling only the generated runtime's SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler for diagnosis, ASan reports an invalid read in `WL_FID_SUM`.

The C ownership analysis misses the datatype underneath the rewrite. `facts_hot` handles `Lam`, `Mat`, stuck families and ordinary `ADT` heads, but a stuck `Rwt` falls through without walking its body, so `Rec` remains cold. The duplicated binding nevertheless emits `_x_1 = term_keep(e, _x_1, 1)`, which replaces the raw constructor location with a one-word refcount redirect. The cold consumer then emits `term_loc(_x_1)`, reads offsets 0, 1 and 2 as if the redirect were the three-field record, and calls `heap_free(e, cls_fit(3), _sp_0)` on that class-0 redirect cell. This silently changes the value and also returns a one-word allocation to the wrong allocator class.

In a separate worktree, adding a `Rwt` case to `facts_hot` that recursively visits `w.f` makes both the silent-wrong-result and crash reproducers return `True{}`. This is related to the ownership failures fixed in #853, #901 and #916, but those issues cover stuck families, nested family matches and concrete family arguments; none covers a datatype hidden under rewrite.

## Environment

```text
main fb6f32a8711dd931315f62ef066d0fb3870f2886
v2.0.34 7d8a3eb036042c6549461054d25a10f26d361c5c
Bun 1.4.2
Darwin arm64
Apple clang 21.0.0
```

title: M1 and M2 build the GPU program again: a32_load_acq reads through Metal's volatile local, as a32_load does
body:
Fixes #1154.

## Cause

comp.ts already works around an Apple GPU compiler bug: "Metal's a32_load reads through a volatile local, or the M1 pipeline build dies." 87a1e9c9 (in 2.0.29) changed `a32_load_acq` from `a32_load(p)` to `atomic_load_explicit(A32(p), ACQ)`. That gave the host a real acquire, since its `FENCE()` is a no-op, but it also skipped the volatile local on Metal. Since then, `MTLCompilerService` crashes building the pipeline for any program with a `!` on M1 (g13, abort) and M2 (g14, SIGSEGV). M3 and M4 (g15/g16) are unaffected, which is why the gates and our M4s never saw it.

## Fix

```c
u32 v = DEVICE ? a32_load(p) : atomic_load_explicit(A32(p), ACQ);
```

- **Device:** `ACQ` is `RLX` (Metal has no `memory_order_acquire`), so this is the same relaxed atomic load followed by the same seq_cst device fence. The IR has the same `air.atomic.global.load` and `air.atomic.fence` calls; the only addition is the store and reload through a thread-private local. clang drops the dead branch even at `-O0`. CUDA expands to the same text as before.
- **Host:** keeps `memory_order_acquire`.

## Verification

- **Bisect:** offline with Apple's `metal-tt`, targeting `applegpu_g14s` with Metal 3.2 / macOS 15, the bisect lands on 87a1e9c9. Restoring only the volatile local makes 87a1e9c9, v2.0.32 and main build; removing only it from the last good commit makes that one crash.
- **Offline builds:** the issue's program and all 21 GPU tests that emit a kernel build for g13, g14, g15 and g16 with this change. On main, all of them fail on g13 and g14.
- **M4 run:** the issue's program prints `134209536`.
- **Test gate:** `gates/test.ts` passed 1526 / 1526 (together with an unrelated change in that run).
- **M4 performance:** 16 GPU runtime benches, 180 main/fix pairs per bench, run back to back on the same node across all 48 minis: fix/main = 1.0013, 95% CI [0.9993, 1.0033]. Every bench is within ±1.4%, and all outputs are identical.
- **Not tested on M1/M2 hardware;** only through the offline toolchain, whose compiler is newer than macOS 15.7.4's but hits the same crash on the same commits.

`gates/repo.ts`: comp.ts is already over its cap on main (64,274 > 64,000 ttok); this adds 9.

title: A template's cache is a Map: the next instance's ordinal is its size, not a list of every key
body:
The quadratic part of #1271.

## Cause

`def_inst` names each new instance `k~n` with `String(Object.keys(is).length)` (`bend.ts:3757`). Every cache miss rebuilds the list of every key the template has seen, so a template with n instances costs O(n²) to name them all.

## Change

- `book.tmps[k]` is a `Map<string, Name>`, and the ordinal is `is.size`. Names are the same `k~n` in the same order, and the instance still goes into the cache before its body is checked, which the self-call check relies on.
- `def_inst` looks the key up once (`let o = is.get(key)`), so a cache hit hashes the key once and the code needs no `!` assertions.
- `safe.ts` iterates the `Map` (`[...is]`), and `book_seed` in `main.ts` copies it (`new Map(...)`). Those are the only readers in this repo, and nothing serializes `tmps`. Out of tree, `nicolas-abril/bend2-fuzzer` reads the tables with `Object.entries`, which returns nothing for a `Map`; its fix is ready to push alongside this PR.

## Results (#1271's file, CPU time / peak RSS)

| depth | instances | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | 32,767 | 5.7 s / 353 MB | 1.0 s / 337 MB |
| 15 | 65,535 | 21.5 s / 572 MB | 1.5 s / 489 MB |

The doubling of instances at each level stays, as it should: every one of the 2¹⁶−1 instances is a distinct closed `~` argument reachable from `main`. That part of #1271 is how templates work: the 64-level and key-size guards catch non-termination, not size. That part should be closed under #784 and the "checker is not optimal" WONTFIX entry, not fixed here.

## Verification

- **Test gate:** `gates/test.ts` passed 1529 / 1529 on this branch, rebased onto e1ed2435.
- **BendTT output:** for all 94 tests that use `~`, the `.bendtt` from main and from this branch are byte-identical (50 files), and the logs match, rechecked against e1ed2435. I couldn't run the safe gate itself, because no BendTT kernel binary was built here.
- **tsc:** the same 8 existing errors as main.
- **`gates/repo.ts`:** bend.ts, safe.ts and main.ts stay under their caps (the only failure is comp.ts, already over on main).

AGENTS.md marks `bend.ts` as human-written, so this needs Victor's review.

title: A type under a stuck rewrite is read as its body, and a type the C facts can't read is a compile error (#1273)
body:
Fixes #1273.

## Root cause

The C lane's type passes normalize types with `ty_wnf`. That left a rewrite stuck on an open proof (`%h@e : Data; Rec` with `e` a variable) as an `Rwt`, so the passes never saw the datatype under it.

Sharing such a value runs `bind_pop`. That seals the node with `term_keep` and calls `facts_hot` on the binding's type to heat its constructors. `facts_hot` heated everything for `All`, `Var` and `App`, and did nothing for any other form it couldn't read, `Rwt` included. So `Rec` stayed cold, and its reader (which sees plain `Rec`) took the seal raw: `term_loc` on the redirect, three words read from it, and `heap_free(e, cls_fit(3), …)` on a one-word cell. The result is a wrong value, or a memory fault on a recursive type.

## Changes

- **`ty_wnf` reads a type through a stuck rewrite.** A rewrite runs as its body: `ty_peel` already drops it from terms, and a closed proof reduces it to the body. `ty_wnf` is where every type pass reduces types (sharing facts, layouts, `type_adts`, `ty_holds`), so all of them now see the datatype. A rewrite-typed `Rec` gets `Rec`'s flat layout instead of a box.
- **A type `facts_hot` can't read is a compile error.** Forms that hold no constructor pass as before: sorts (`Typ`, `Qnt`, `Qua`, `Min`), index values (`Lit`, `Ctr`, `Efq`, `Rfl`), `Eql`, and a `Ref` (a law, e.g. an IO handle). `All`, `Var` and `App` still heat everything, as before. Any other form now dies with `a type the C facts cannot read (<form>)`. Before, it heated nothing, which is how this bug and the cold readers before it (#853, #901, #916) turned into wrong results. Without the `ty_wnf` change, this regression dies at compile time with `(Rwt)`.

## Tests

- **Regression:** `tests/reg/rwt_type_share.bend` shares six shapes under a rewrite: a record, a sum, a rewrite of a rewrite, a type argument, a generic record's field, and a recursive tree. On `main` it dies natively with a memory fault. Here it prints `(18, 14, 18, 18, 218, 6)` in the interpreter, JS and native.
- **Corpus:** I emitted C for all 1,660 programs in `tests/`, `demos/` and `bench/` on `main` and on this branch. The only change is the new regression: C, output and exit codes match everywhere else. No program reaches the new `die`.
- **Size:** `comp.ts` is 63,749 ttok (cap 64,000).
- **Not run:** the cluster gates.

## Dropped from earlier revisions

Earlier revisions also had these changes. None changed any emitted program:
- reading through a rewrite at an application's head (a layout gain only; `App` already heats everything);
- `ty_all` through `ty_wnf`;
- a conservative fallback that heated everything for any unread form;
- an `INERT` list shared with `ty_clo`.

The fallback is replaced by the `die` above, because heating everything would have hidden the next bug of this kind as an unexplained slowdown.

title: U32 division and remainder halve the dividend only on Metal; the host and CUDA divide directly
body:
## The change

U32 `/` and `%` compile through `U32_QUO`, which halves the dividend, divides, and then fixes the odd bit. ef1328f4 (#824) added it because Metal folds a constant dividend within 128 of 2^32 through an f32. The macro was emitted for every backend, though, so the host and CUDA paid for a Metal workaround on every division.

`U32_QUO` now keeps that form only under `__METAL_VERSION__`; the host and CUDA divide directly. The Metal build compiles the same code as before.

- **Size:** `bend2/comp.ts` +19 ttok (+5 −4 lines).

## Main vs this branch

Paired A/B on the cluster. Each bench and mode ran on one mini: both builds use the perf gate's cc line and flags, with one warm run each, then 5 alternating timed runs, and each value is the median. Every output matches. The 16 `bench/runtime` benches plus the histogram bench from #1278:

| bench | SEQ-CPU | PAR-CPU | PAR-GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| histogram | 1.722 → 1.474 s (−14.5%) | 0.365 → 0.318 s (−12.8%) | unchanged |
| lexer | 2.189 → 2.100 s (−4.2%) | 0.382 → 0.367 s (−3.8%) | unchanged |
| hashmap | 2.432 → 2.372 s (−2.5%) | 0.397 → 0.391 s (−1.6%) | unchanged |
| bfs | −0.7% | −1.9% | unchanged |
| **geomean, all 17** | **0.987** | **0.989** | **1.001** |

On the histogram's key fill alone, the old form cost 0.25 s of a 1.15 s single-threaded fill.

The other benches are within ±1%. A few SEQ cells moved by a small but significant amount where the change isn't on the hot path: tree-bitonic +0.9%, and kmeans, raytrace and terrain about +0.4%. No PAR-GPU cell's 95% interval excludes 1.

## Gates

- **Test gate:** `gates/test.ts` passes, 1528 / 1528, including the Metal runs of every `!` test, which keep the #824 form.
- **Repo gate:** fails only on `bend2/comp.ts`'s cap, as main does today: main is at 64,274 ttok, this branch at 64,293. Main went over when #1269 merged; a trim is needed separately.

## Not run

- CUDA, Linux and x86.

title: A histogram bench: bend-parallel's parallel histogram over one shared Array<U32>, with C, TS and Lean twins
body:
## The bench

`bench/runtime/histogram`: a parallel histogram over one flat `Array<U32>`. It's the suite's first shared-array, multi-pass case: every other bench is one fork tree over tree-shaped data or independent items.

- **The library:** [bend-parallel](https://github.com/costamatheus97/bend-parallel)'s `histogram.bend` at 45a161a (Apache-2.0, the same license as Bend). It's ported as is, except that its sort-only path (`sc`, `ins.go`) is dropped and `Scan.half` is inlined. The header credits it.
- **What a run does:** 128 rounds. Each round:
  - refills 2^24 keys (64 MB) in parallel with a new seed;
  - counts them into 256 buckets with bend-parallel's two passes: per-block rows of a 2^11 × 256 table, then column sums;
  - folds that round's counts into the checksum, so every round is checked.
- **Buffers:** sized once, outside the `!`, and handed from round to round as the library intends.
- **Twins:** `main.c`, `main.ts` and `main.lean`, single-threaded and doing the same steps, including the two-step column pass the library uses from 2^12 rows up.
- **Unsafe code:** the lanes share the keys and the table through Base's `@unsafe` `Array.fork` and `Array.join`, as bend-parallel does. Bend has no safe way to give lanes disjoint slices of one array. So `--check-only` lists the 13 defs that rely on them and exits 1. `bend main.bend -o main`, which the perf gate runs, builds and runs normally.

## Correctness

| size | checksum | agrees across |
|---|---|---|
| small: 2^10 keys, B = 4, 2 rounds | 3825188900 | Bend (interpreter; 1 and 16 threads; GPU), the C, TS and Lean twins, an independent Python histogram |
| 2^12 keys, B = 12, 3 rounds (the two-step pass) | 1974811180 | Bend, the C and Lean twins, Python |
| big: 2^24 keys, B = 11, 128 rounds | 122845198 | Bend at 1 and 16 threads and on the GPU, the three twins |

## Pins

`apple_m4.txt` gains the histogram row. It was measured with the perf gate's own cell script for this bench only, three runs a cell, medians, the same way `--pin` takes them; the other rows are untouched.

| COMPILER | SEQ-CPU | PAR-CPU | PAR-GPU | OUTPUT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.033 s | 1.717 s, 67.7M | 0.367 s, 74.8M | 1.481 s, 80.0M | 122845198 |

`apple_m4_max.txt` (the record pins, from `gen_pins.ts` on the M4 Max) has no row yet, so the bench is not on the charts until that machine repins.

## Against C

On the cluster, single-threaded: Bend 1.72 s, the C twin 1.07 s. On 16 threads: Bend 0.367 s, against 0.248 s for a pthreads C version (per-thread private histograms, written for the comparison and not in the tree). Both scale about 4.6–4.7x, and both are near the minis' memory bandwidth.

Most of the single-thread gap is in two places:
- **About half is array index wrapping:** every access masks its index, which stops clang vectorizing the fill's stores.
- **About 0.25 s is the Metal division workaround** on the host, which #1277 removes. With it, Bend drops to 1.47 s single-threaded and 0.318 s on 16 threads.

## Gates

- **Perf gate:** 121 / 124. The histogram's 7 cells are at 0.99x–1.01x. The 3 failures are the 60–100 ms PAR-GPU time cells (mandelbrot 1.23x, merkle 1.16x, and nbody or terrain, both shown at 1.15x), which vary from run to run; the run before passed 124 / 124.
- **Repo gate:** fails only on `bend2/comp.ts`'s cap, as main does today (64,274 > 64,000 since #1269). This PR doesn't touch `comp.ts`.

## Not run

- CUDA, Linux and x86.

title: fix(compiler): isolate spare nodes across sum arms
body:
A specialized sum converted through an erased generic function can make one `val_arms` branch consume a parked constructor node while another branch leaves it untouched. Because the generated branches shared `fl.spares`, compile-time generation of the first branch removed the node for every runtime branch; the `Skip` path then allocated a replacement and leaked the original node on each pass.

On macOS arm64 at `e1ed243502764d013471a7338bc7ab2c8e62ff98`, the reproducer grows from 17,924,096 bytes maximum RSS at 1,000,000 passes to 81,920,000 bytes at 5,000,000 passes, exactly 16 bytes per extra pass. The opposite-tag `Put` control stays at 1,933,312 bytes.

This gives every multi-arm `val_arms` branch its own spare list and flushes branch-local leftovers, matching the branch isolation already used by `val_box` after #970. Spares parked before the branch remain available to code after the chain. With this patch, both 1,000,000 and 5,000,000 `Skip` passes stay at about 1.9 MB maximum RSS.

The regression test preserves the generic sum conversion and repeated list rebuild that trigger this compiler shape. The leak itself is not observable in Bend output, so the direct RSS measurement used the same program with 1,000,000 and 5,000,000 rounds.

Validation:
- New regression test: interpreter, emitted JS, and emitted native C all print `1`.
- Existing `list_rebox_sum`, `array_borrow_generic_sum`, and `brw_audit2_fresh_box_root` tests still print their expected output.
- The original reproducer passes both `--check-only` and `--verdict`.
- Full `tsc` reports the same pre-existing errors on clean `origin/main` and this branch, with no error in `comp.ts`.

title: Simplify Process.run polling
body:
`Process.run` compacted active descriptors into a polling array and tracked their pipe roles in a separate array. It now keeps stdin, stdout, stderr, and child-exit notification in fixed slots, relying on `poll` to ignore inactive descriptors (`-1`).

This removes the descriptor count and role mapping while preserving child-exit priority and the existing pipe handling.

Local checks: both native process tests pass. The original and updated implementations matched across 256 polling comparisons and 12 subprocess scenarios.

title: comp.ts back under its cap by removing mechanisms at their root: a global File, one way to read a shared cell, and effects that park themselves
body:
## Context

`comp.ts` sits just under its permanent 64,000 cap: main is at 63,971 ttok. This PR brings it to **62,978**.

The cuts are simplifications at the root rather than trimming: each removes a mechanism that existed only because another part behaved a certain way, or a second way of doing one job. Each was traced to the commit that added it, to check the reason no longer holds.

## Changes (one commit each)

- **The compiler's `File` is global and holds every cache.** The caches were module globals cleared per book, so the compiler already held one book at a time, yet 40 functions took `book` or `fl` only to reach it. `FL` is now the book being compiled and everything memoized about it; `FL.memo` holds what one def's walk memoizes. `type File` lists every field, `FL.memo`'s too. `show_main` now reads this book's caches, not the previous book's (it ran before the caches were cleared): this restores #961's fix, which main has lost. Two books compiled in one process now each emit what a fresh compile emits; on main the second either gets the first's stale layout or throws.
- **`Intr.call` goes:** an intrinsic that `arr_op` lays out has `C: null`; the flag's third use (blocking a fold rebuild) was redundant.
- **A foreign def's segment opens and returns through `emit_open`/`emit_put`**, like any def's.
- **No scan for the word `undefined` in the emitted C:** a leaked one is an undeclared name, which clang refuses.
- **`corpus_eval` is one loop with one post-condition**, and three guards for states that cannot occur go.
- **A redirect cell has one read, `term_peek`** (one relaxed 64-bit load, as #1155 made `blk_loc` do), and `rfc_view` goes; `ctr_take` acquires only as the last holder, before it owns the node. #975's reproducer under ThreadSanitizer: 0 reports in 10 runs on both trees (and 6 with the read made plain, as a control).
- **A JS foreign op is a node tagged with its def's name**, as in C, and an IO.OP match keeps its default arm in both lanes, so the JS-only `$FFI` goes. A user's `case _` in an IO.OP match takes only an Emit or a Halt: a request reaching it fail-stops in every lane.
- **An effect that waits parks itself:** `io_eff` takes no need, and the loop runs every request one way. `IO.sleep` parks on its deadline; `TCP.accept` and `UDP.recv_from` park until their socket is readable before their first try, as the need made them, so a backlog cannot starve the timers. The C effect table is not `static`, so it is zero fill rather than 512 KB of every binary.
- **The book and the emitter's scope are two things:** `FL` is the File being compiled, and a `Scope` (segment, local names, bindings, spare nodes, def) is where the emitter writes, so a nested arm, closure or fork copies only its scope.

The series also tried opening a constructor's own binders as `DUMMY` in place of `facts_hot`'s `local` flag, and reading Nat literals past 256 without `lit_call`'s `U32.to_nat` shim. Review found a C miscompile from the first and a compile-time blow-up from the second (7.3 s and 4.4 GB against 0.3 s and 324 MB on main), so both are main's again in later commits; a squash leaves neither.

## Breaking

- **The effect API:** `io_eff(cid, run)` takes no need. A third argument is a compile error in C, and in JS `io_eff` throws ("`<k>` takes no need: an effect that waits parks itself").
- **IO.OP matches:** a request reaching a user's `case _` in an IO.OP match fail-stops in C too. Main already refused it in JS and `bend run`, but ran the user's arm on it in C. Every waiting effect already had the self-parking form (`io_wait_on` / `io_park_on`), so nothing becomes impossible; `guide/EFFECTS.md` says so and shows how to wait on time alone. All 63 C registrations in `bend2/effs` and `tests` are updated.
- **JS registry check:** a foreign def without a registered JS effect fails when its request runs, naming the def ("bend: no effect registers `<def>`"; C says "an alien request"), not at load.

## Checks

**On main 1a2e5cd3 (after the review fixes and rebases)**, on an Apple M4:
- **Emitted output:** for all 1633 `.bend` files under `tests/`, `bench/` and `demos/`, each commit that says its output is byte-identical emits byte-identical C, JS and `.mjs` against its parent. Each review fix changes only what it says. Every rebase was checked file by file: an output main's new commits leave alone is unchanged, and the ones they change hold both main's change and this PR's.
- **New tests:** `udp_backlog_timer` (a 0 ms timer fires before 40 queued datagrams drain), `tcp_backlog_timer` (the same before 20 queued connections are accepted) and `request_wildcard` (an IO.OP `case _` takes a Halt but refuses a request) fail without their fixes and pass with them, in C and JS; `effect_unregistered` pins the named refusal.
- **Local full suite** (`gates/test.ts`'s shard script on this Mac): 1548/1550. The two failures are `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, which need a display.
- **Cluster gates** (`gates/_run.ts`): repo 50/50, test 1550/1550, perf 121/124 and 124/124 on reruns, against main's 88/124 to 124/124 on the same minis. The cells over 1.15x were PAR-GPU times under 0.1 s, on both trees. ping was skipped because the site repo is not checked out here.
- **Review:** two independent passes over the changed compiler and runtime code (generated C and JS against main across the corpus, a redirect-cell stress run at 8 threads, the IO.OP match cases in every lane) found no further bugs.
- Not re-run: the JS-lane timings and the commit audit below.

**The original series, before the rebases and the review fixes**, on an Apple M4 against main (fb6f32a8):
- **Emitted output:** the compiler-only commits keep the emitted C, JS and `.mjs` byte-identical for all 1608 `.bend` files under `tests/`, `bench/` and `demos/`; the rest change it as described in their messages.
- **Local full suite** (`gates/test.ts`'s shard script run on this Mac; every lane, Metal for the `!` tests): all pass but `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, which need no display and fail on main too.
- **Cluster gates:** repo 49/49, test 1526/1526, perf 115/117 against main's 117/117 back to back (geomeans: compiler 1.032, SEQ 0.993, PAR-CPU 1.015, PAR-GPU 1.035). The two cells over 1.15 are Metal times (nbody 1.17, terrain 1.19), which swing that much between runs on main too; on this M4, interleaved best of 3, Metal is 0.997 of main (nbody 1.018, terrain 0.991).
- **JS lane** (no gate covers it): the 16 benches compiled to JS, 2-3 interleaved runs each, geomean 0.983, every bench within ±2%; `within_busy` 0.75.
- **Demos:** all 15 build in C and JS.
- **Audit of every commit since 2.0.0** (453 commits, a7e0600e to fb6f32a8): for each, what it did, whether it aimed at compile or runtime performance or an edge case, its linked issues and PRs, and whether #1281 touches the same mechanism; where it does, the commit's or issue's reproducer was run on both trees. 123 preserved (verified), 329 no interaction, 1 regression, fixed: removing `FID_EXIT`'s continuation fast path (87a1e9c9) cost 28% more instructions at 8 threads in code that applies a closure which may fork (9.03G -> 11.54G; no bench takes that path), so the fast path stays. The 34 commits that aimed at performance are all preserved or untouched.
- **Tried and dropped, with measurements:** removing `FID_EXIT`'s fast path (above), element-wise block copy (10% slower on a block-heavy micro-benchmark), a shared device/host drain loop (Metal compiled the work loop twice), JS Nat matches through `==` (a host's raw BigInt), dropping `fl.consts` (b84b0047's 8 s compile guard), and two emitter shortcuts that relied on term identity.
- **Not run:** CUDA (the device read path and the CUDA `gpu_make` change are untested) and Linux.

title: A spin whose loop calls spins is one shared call on the devices when one function runs it twice, so raytrace runs 1.8x faster and editdist 1.1x
body:
Follow-up to #1102. Raytrace on the GPU got 38% slower between 2.0.3 and 2.0.26, when its bounce loop shrank under SPIN_FAR and got inlined into a shader that is itself inlined four times. Copies times size, as suggested on #1102, fixed raytrace (1.6x) but made gameoflife 7x slower, mandelbrot 1.85x and kmeans 1.45x, since it turned small helpers with many copies into calls inside hot loops. ncu on my RTX 3090 shows what actually costs raytrace (higher active threads and lower instruction counts are better):

| | Active threads per warp | Issued instructions |
|---|---:|---:|
| raytrace, shader inlined 4 times (now) | 2.1 of 32 | 101 billion |
| raytrace, one shared shader | 3.7 of 32 | 60 billion |
| gameoflife, spin_8 inlined 16 times (now) | 32 of 32 | 213 billion |
| gameoflife, spin_8 as one call | 32 of 32 | 1,192 billion |

Bend's GPU lanes run unrelated tasks, so a warp only runs threads together at the same instruction. Raytrace's pixel loop runs the shader four times in a row, and the bounce loop in it ends at a different depth per ray, so lanes drift into different copies and the warp runs the copies one after another. One shared copy lets them meet again. Gameoflife has no loops, so its lanes never drift and a call only adds work.

That only happens when all three hold, and each one has a case against it:

- One function runs the copies in turn. Mandelbrot's escape wrapper is called from two different functions; its lanes sit at 32 of 32 either way, and sharing it cost 1.6%.
- The spin holds a loop. Loop-free code rejoins after every branch (gameoflife).
- The loop calls other spins. Hashmap's bucket walk calls none, does a few loads per step, and sharing it cost 2.2% at the same 7.5 of 32 active threads.

So a spin becomes SHARE when it holds a loop that calls spins and some function runs two or more copies of it. Each segment records the spins it calls as emit_fuse emits them; copies count through inlined spins and stop at shared or FAR ones, deciding callers first. SHARE is FAR on the devices and INLINE on the host, where these calls cost raytrace 22%. SPIN_FAR, FAR, term_drop and the meaning of a segment's spin flag don't change. comp.ts goes from 63980 to 64305 ttok (+29 -4 lines), which puts it 305 over the 64k cap.

[bend-bench](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench) [`paired`](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/blob/main/RUNNING.md#comparing-bend-revisions) (fast-gpu-v2 sizes, RTX 3090, CUDA 13.1), main at a3f1782a against this PR in 10 blocks of A B B A / B A A B, each block scored (A1 + A2) / (B1 + B2); above 1x means this PR is faster:

| | Median block | 95% interval | All 10 blocks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| raytrace | 1.844x | 1.827x to 1.875x | 1.795x to 1.898x |
| editdist | 1.145x | 1.125x to 1.151x | 1.107x to 1.161x |

The other 20 workloads compile to the same program as main: the same GPU program and the same host code, since the SHARE definitions they don't use only change the source copy the binary embeds. So they weren't timed. The only other programs with SHARE spins are three demos and two tests: app_slash_boss_3d's headless probe gives the same output with frames at 60.9 -> 60.2 ms, pure_hvm5_mini is too short to time, and app_ray_tracer_3d needs a display. With bend-bench's [compiler-check](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/blob/main/RUNNING.md#comparing-bend-revisions), every test keeps its result. Metal is unmeasured since I don't have Apple hardware; SHARE is FAR there too, so timings of raytrace and editdist on an M-series Mac would be welcome.

title: The repo gate stops when ttok counts nothing, instead of passing every file
body:
`gates/repo.ts` reads `ttok`'s stdout with `Number(...)`, so a `ttok` that prints nothing counts as 0 tokens and every capped file passes. That's how main went over the `comp.ts` cap without anyone seeing it: #1269 measured 63,821 on its branch, but five merges had grown main by 429 tokens in the meantime, and the squash-merge put `comp.ts` at 64,250. It's 64,251 today, and the gate still reported 49/49 on main.

| `ttok` on the machine running `gates/repo.ts` | main before this PR | main with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| working (`pipx install ttok`) | 48 / 49, `bend2/comp.ts: 64251 > 64000 ttok` | same |
| prints nothing | 49 / 49, every file passes | stops: `ttok counted nothing for README.md (pipx install ttok)`, exit 1 |
| exits nonzero | 49 / 49 | stops with the same message, exit 1 |
| not installed | crashes on a null stdout | stops with the same message, exit 1 |

Token counts are `ttok` over `bend2/comp.ts` at each merge commit; it gives 64,172 at d7af6bf9, the figure recorded there.

The change only touches `ttok()`: it throws when `ttok` is missing, exits nonzero, or prints anything but a positive count. Caps and the allow list are untouched.

Heads-up: once this lands, the repo gate fails on main until `comp.ts` loses about 250 tokens, so that's the next thing.

title: comp.ts is back under its 64k cap: the compiler says the same in fewer tokens, with the same output
body:
## Context

`bend2/comp.ts` has been over its permanent 64,000 ttok cap since #1269, which took it from 63,536 to 64,250. Four later merges added more and #1230 took 110 back, leaving main at 64,251, so `gates/repo.ts` fails on main. This went unnoticed until #1283 because the gate read a failed `ttok` run as 0.

This PR brings `comp.ts` to **63,883 ttok** (−368). That leaves 117 tokens for the PRs waiting on the cap.

## Change (`bend2/comp.ts` only)

These are pure rewrites of the TypeScript compiler, the same kind as #1230. Nothing in the C or JS runtime templates changes.

- **`OPERATIONS`:** entries whose C and JS texts fit on one line are written on one line.
- **Early returns:** chains of early returns become ternaries in `val_to`, `emit_args`, `emit_match`, `js_match`, `js_call`, `term_force`, `tpl_nat`, `lay_of`, `anf`'s `Lam` case and `emit_unfold`'s `bind`.
- **Once-used helpers:** `facts_fam`, `facts_lend` and `mat_nats` move into their one call site each.
- **Once-used locals:** `load`, `last`, `ids`, `tag` and the `val_hold` results are inlined.
- **Loops:** the `#define` id loop becomes a `flatMap`; `graph_close` adds while it scans instead of filtering first; the `bind_pop` loop becomes a single `??=`.
- **`ERRS`:** the placeholders are filled with `replaceAll` before the split.
- **`show_main` and `val_arm`:** dot access, and `Number(bool)` instead of `? 1 : 0`, as `lay_pack` already does.

Not taken: rewrites that bypass an abstraction (pushing to `seg.lines` directly instead of `file_push`), parameter-default tricks, `Set.add` used for its truthiness, and turning `switch` dispatches into long ternary chains. The last would save about 44 more tokens if they are ever needed.

## Checks

On 0a1a7694, against main ee8a156e:

- **Emitted output:** I compiled every `.bend` under `tests/`, `bench/` and `demos/` (1,619 files) to `.c`, `.js` and `.mjs` with main and with this branch. All 4,857 results are byte-identical: the 2,528 emitted files and the error text of the 2,329 that fail to build.
- **tsc:** the same 12 errors as main; none is in `comp.ts`.
- **Gates:**
  - `gates/repo.ts`: PASS 49 / 49. Main fails it, on `comp.ts`.
  - `gates/test.ts`: PASS 1536 / 1536.
  - `gates/ping.ts`: PASS 46 / 46.
  - `gates/perf.ts`, run alone: 124 / 124 here, 123 / 124 on main back to back.
- No new line is wider than 80 columns.

#1281 also brings `comp.ts` under the cap, by removing mechanisms. It rewrites much of the same code, so whichever lands second will need a rebase.

title: Fix C emission when a native effect invokes a Bend callback
body:
A native C effect should be able to call a callback received from Bend. This can currently fail at compile time because the compiler resolves the runtime helper's ID before registering it.

### What you did

Saved the two files below and compiled on upstream `main` @ `947db722`, still the latest HEAD when checked on 2026-10-03:

```sh
bend main.bend -o main.c
```

The C effect calls the Bend callback with `40`; the callback adds `2`.

### What happened

C emission fails before clang runs:

```text
Error: FID(Clo~apply) names no constructor or def
```

Expected: compilation succeeds and the native program prints `42`.

### The file

`main.bend`:

```python
import Base

def native.apply(step: U32 -> U32, value: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  import "./native.c"

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  native.apply(x => (x + 2 : U32), 40)
```

`native.c`:

```c
static Term native_apply_run(Env e, Term* f, IoWork* w) {
  (void)w;
  u64 at = task_node(e, FID(Clo~apply), TERM_HOLE, 0, 0);
  e.mem[at] = f[0];
  e.mem[at + 1] = f[1];
  Term result = corpus_eval(e.mem, term_tsk(FID(Clo~apply), at));
  if (err_seen(e.mem)) err_fail("foreign closure application failed");
  printf("%u\n", (u32)result);
  return term_pak(CID(Unit), 0);
}

static void __attribute__((constructor)) native_apply_use(void) {
  io_eff(CID(native.apply), native_apply_run, 0);
}
```

### Why

`Clo~apply` applies a closure in the generated runtime; it is not declared in the Bend book.

`compile_book` reads foreign C sources through `effect_srcs` inside the fixpoint loop, before the runtime segments have been created. When no emitted Bend call has registered `Clo~apply` yet, `c_ids` rejects the valid runtime name.

### Change

Read the foreign C sources in the final `runtime_c` call, after every segment and ID exists. This reads each source once and preserves the existing ID assignment order, including user definitions whose C macro names collide with runtime names.

`foreign_runtime_apply` returns the callback's result as `IO(U32)` and prints it from Bend with `IO.print`. Both foreign implementations return the callback's value.

`foreign_runtime_apply_tail` uses the same C/JS sources with the foreign call as main's only effect. It retains coverage of the original missing-ID failure: adding an `IO.bind` continuation to print the result can itself register `Clo~apply` on unpatched main. This test succeeds without output, as an IO main's return value is discarded.

### Verification

Local checks against upstream `main` @ `565d7fde` on Apple M5/macOS:

- The original two-file reproducer and `foreign_runtime_apply_tail` fail C emission on main with `FID(Clo~apply) names no constructor or def`. Both compile with this patch; the original reproducer prints `42` with 1/4 threads and GPU off.
- Both new fixtures and twelve existing controls match their expected output in the interpreter, Bun, Node and C with 1/4 threads: fourteen programs, seventy executions. Controls include `ids_unique`, `name_owned_def`, foreign values and namespaces, and the two ownership regressions.
- Across 851 existing runnable-test candidates, emitted C is byte-identical for 701 programs and JS for 724 programs. The 277 compiler refusals across the two backends are also unchanged.
- `gates/repo.ts`: PASS 50/50. `comp.ts`: 63,951 → 63,938 ttok (cap 64,000, unchanged).

The cluster `gates/test.ts` could not start because this machine cannot resolve `cluster`. Full cluster test/perf/safe/ping gates and CUDA were not run locally.

### bend --version

Output of `bun bend2/main.ts version` (tested compiler):

```text
bend 2.0.35
```

Base: `565d7fdec289b1f2f5f5037bb58b5afb6738ff1d`; PR head: `72cfbe97de41add3cb993d924ccc14a37bfbab6b`.

### uname -sm

```text
Darwin arm64
```

Apple M5, macOS 26.6.2.

### clang --version (the first line)

```text
Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)
```

Created with AI assistance (Codex).

title: The repo gate runs on every PR, with main's gate files
body:
Follows #1283: #1269 passed the repo gate at 63,821 tokens on its own branch, but five merges had grown main in the meantime and the squash put `comp.ts` at 64,250. The gate only ran on someone's machine, on whatever branch they had.

This adds `.github/workflows/repo-gate.yml`, which runs `bun gates/repo.ts` (the allow list and the ttok caps) on every pull request:

- It runs on GitHub's Linux machines (`ubuntu-24.04`), read-only, with no secrets, so fork PRs are safe to run. Public repos have no minute limit.
- It runs **main's** `gates/` over the PR's tree (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- gates/`), so a PR can't pass by loosening the gate that checks it.
- Pinned: actions/checkout v7.0.1 and setup-bun v2.2.0 by sha, bun 1.4.0, `ttok==0.3`.
- It also triggers on `merge_group`, so if a merge queue is turned on later, the gate reruns on current main plus the queued PRs right before each merge. Nothing uses it yet.

`gates/repo.ts` gains one line, `allow(".github/workflows/repo-gate.yml");`. No caps change.

For now this only shows a ✓ or ✗ on each PR. It doesn't block merging; that would take a ruleset.

**This PR's own `repo-gate` run is expected to fail.** It checks with main's `repo.ts`, which doesn't allow the workflow file yet. Locally, with this branch's `repo.ts`, it passes 50 / 50. Every PR after this merges is checked normally.

title: The C compiler specializes calls with a known callback
body:
Based on main `5a0b523f` (Bend 2.0.35); reproduced locally on Apple M5/macOS.

## What Bend should do

Specialize calls that pass a known callback, avoiding closure allocation and dynamic application while keeping ordinary function types:

```python
def apply(x: U32, callback: U32 -> U32) -> U32:
  callback(x)

def run(+bias: U32, x: U32) -> U32:
  a = apply(x, y => U32.add(y, bias))
  apply(a, y => U32.add(y, bias))
```

## Why

I started this while building Bend bindings for [GPUI](https://gpui.rs/), connecting Bend-computed particle state to rendering without CPU readback. Small callbacks used to thread linear arrays through element reads became a bottleneck. The generated update had fourteen closure segments; rewriting those callbacks as explicit arguments made it much faster.

This lets the compiler remove that cost for supported calls while keeping the callback API. CPU and GPU share the C emitter. With unchanged Bend particle sources, update closure segments fall from fourteen to zero; two UI/IO closures remain.

One million particles on Apple M5, measured on main `947db722` vs fork `b59588e2`. Rebased particle C outputs are byte-identical:

| Update | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CPU, 1 thread | 160.881 ms | 69.830 ms | 2.30× |
| CPU, 10 threads | 24.472 ms | 12.108 ms | 2.02× |
| Metal, including completion wait | 8.653 ms | 1.625 ms | 5.32× |

GPUI is the application example. This PR changes the general compiler; application code is available as a [reusable Bend/GPUI library](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/blob/6c21544c51228c88e5ff1559236231a0b88727f7/packages/bend-gpui/README.en.md), a [minimal Bend application](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/blob/6c21544c51228c88e5ff1559236231a0b88727f7/examples/gpui/minimal.bend), and a [particle rendering example](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/tree/6c21544c51228c88e5ff1559236231a0b88727f7/examples/particles). The [benchmark reference implementation](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/tree/09fc6e6/compiler-patches/step-02-known-callbacks/refactored) remains pinned to the measured versions.

## Change

Two commits: first shorten type/import notation and comments without changing generated output, then add specialization (+69/-15 compiler lines) and two regression fixtures. `comp.ts` is 63,956 ttok; the 64,000 cap stays unchanged.

Specialize saturated defs with one literal lambda and unboxed captures. Reuse fusion and argument binding, preserve typed lambdas/constructor patterns and caller capture lifetimes, and cache admission across ANF rebuilding and fuel exhaustion.

Dynamic callbacks, boxed captures, multiple lambdas and foreign/bang calls retain the existing path. Callees with direct self-reference or parallel bindings are excluded. Non-tail expansion also excludes non-flat calls and callbacks with parallel bindings. Budget exhaustion falls back to closures.

Separate from #1286 (foreign-callback C emission). The notation/comment commit shares the size-reduction goal of open #1281.

## Verification

Local checks on main `5a0b523f` plus this patch:

- `gates/repo.ts`: 49/49.
- Thirteen callback contracts pass, including capture reuse, linear arrays, dependent types, non-flat calls, fallback, repeated compilation and fuel exhaustion.
- Sixteen upstream programs (including the two new fixtures and main's two new ownership regressions) agree across interpreter, JS and C with 1/4 threads: 64 executions.
- The compaction alone preserves generated C/JS byte-for-byte for fourteen programs. The eight particle C outputs match the published measured versions, including both flat controls.
- TypeScript reports the same two existing `bend.ts` errors on baseline and branch. Full cluster test/perf/safe gates and CUDA hardware have not been run.

Start with `tests/run/known_callback.bend` (stdout `42`); commands below.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and measurement details</summary>

Small regression (stdout `42`):

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/run/known_callback.bend -o /tmp/known_callback.c
clang -O3 -std=c11 -pthread /tmp/known_callback.c -lm -o /tmp/known_callback
/tmp/known_callback --gpu off --threads 1
/tmp/known_callback --gpu off --threads 4
```

The table was measured on [main 947db722](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/947db722640c86247849343657bf2f7ef01cb7f1) versus [fork b59588e2](https://github.com/mizchi/bend/commit/b59588e2a9c63092b542739bb6908c3329d2e353). After rebasing onto main 5a0b523f and compacting, all eight measured particle C outputs remain byte-identical in their respective lanes; timings were not rerun.

Apple M5 (10 CPU/10 GPU cores), macOS 26.6.2, Bun 1.3.5, clang 21.0.0. One million particles, 64 noise rounds, CPU grain 1,024, GPU grain 16,384, 960×540 offscreen output. Five warmup frames and fifteen measured frames per run; median of three run medians, configurations shuffled and run serially. Builds/startup/verification are excluded. Measured frames have zero CPU readback. This measures update time, not display/presentation latency.

The machine was shared. The byte-identical flat GPU control ranged 1.543–1.841 ms on main and 1.514–1.725 ms on the fork, so small timing differences should not be attributed to the compiler. Eight application binaries were checked with float32/image oracles: 36 configurations and 144 verified frames.

[Raw timings](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/blob/09fc6e6/compiler-patches/step-02-known-callbacks/refactored/results-macos-m5.json) and [application validation](https://github.com/mizchi/bend-playground/blob/09fc6e6/compiler-patches/step-02-known-callbacks/refactored/validation-macos-m5.json), with pinned source/compiler revisions and reproduction commands in the reference README.

</details>

Implemented and checked with OpenAI Codex assistance.

title: Only a statement a[i] <- v is the write let, so Array.set(..); in an inline match keeps the next row (#1126)
body:
Fixes #1126.

`term_write` treated any `Array.set(_, x, _, _)` followed by `;` (or a line at its column) as the write statement `x = x[i] <- v; rest`. That included an explicit call and a write inside parentheses, so in `\{False: w => Array.set(U32, w, 0, 9); sx => v => v}` the second row became the first arm's continuation. A write now counts only when its array variable opens the statement, which only `a[i] <- v` does. Explicit calls and parenthesized writes are now ordinary terms.

`tests/parse/array_set_call_row.bend` covers the explicit call and the parenthesized write. It fails on main and prints `([1, 1], [9, 1])` with the fix in the interpreter, JS and C. The existing `tests/parse/array_write_stmt.bend` still covers the `a[i] <- v` statement.

Local checks: I ran all 1,540 tests in `tests/` through the old and new `main.ts` (check + interpret) and their outputs are identical. `bend.ts` is at 43,676 ttok, under its 48k cap.

title: The refusal of a nested match on a split value names it and says where to match it (#1125)
body:
Addresses #1125 by keeping the refusal and rewriting its message.

In the issue's `g`, the later `[p, q]` row makes the outer match split `W`, so row 1's inner `match W` scrutinizes a value the outer match already split. That is the same situation the lint refuses for a value the program destructured itself (`consumed_column_error_001`), and folding the inner match into the outer one works:

```python
case 0n, Con{h, Nil{}}:     h
case 0n, Con{h, Con{a, b}}: a
case k, [p, q]:             p
case k, _:                  0
```

The old message ("this value is already a constructor … if an outer match destructed it, fold the pattern into the outer case") didn't fit, because the program never destructured `W`. The new one:

> 'W' can't be matched here (match it in the same match as the pattern that introduced it)

A constructor or literal written as the scrutinee (`match Con{1, Nil{}}:`) gets its own message instead, told apart by its source text (a split value is written as its variable):

> 'Con{1, Nil{}}' can't be matched (this value is already a constructor: bind its fields directly)

- `tests/flatten/consumed_column_error_001.bend`: its pinned message is updated.
- `tests/flatten/consumed_column_error_002.bend`: new; pins the issue's `g` and the new message.
- `tests/flatten/ctor_scrutinee_error.bend`: new; pins the written-constructor message.

The flattener is unchanged from main; only the message differs.
