title: Closed Nat terms over big literals overflow the checker stack (Nat.add(4294967294n, 1n) == 4294967295n), and the overflow can hide the real error
body:
## Summary

A Nat literal is one node, but `Nat.add`, `Nat.sub`, `Nat.mul`, `Nat.divmod` and `Nat.cmp` in Base recurse on successors. Reducing a closed call over a big literal and converting the result against another literal walks one `Succ` per JS stack level (`compare_go`, `Array.prototype.every`), so the check dies with "the machine stack overflowed" once the value passes about 58800 under the pinned stack settings. Literals go up to 4294967295n (`nat_from_term` limits them to 0xffffffff), so any statement that mentions a closed term such as `NMAX = 4294967294n`, `Nat.div(4294967294n, es)` or `Nat.mul(65535n, 65537n)` on both sides of an equation or an inequality is unprovable by `{==}`. A lemma stated for a variable and applied at the literal avoids the problem, so it only bites when the closed term is written directly.

A second symptom of the same family: when the failing equation's normal form is itself too deep, `expr_show` (error printing) normalizes it with `term_snf`, overflows inside the error handler, and the process dies with Bun's raw `RangeError` trace (no "SOME PROOFS FAIL" line). The real error, which was an ordinary mismatch, is lost.

## Minimal reproducer

`repro.bend` (8 lines, imports only Base):

```
import Base

law big_add:
  {Nat.add(4294967294n, 1n) == 4294967295n : Nat}

def big_add():
  {==}
```

Second reproducer, the hidden error (`repro_show.bend`):

```
import Base

law bad:
  {Nat.double(100000n) == 7n : Nat}

def bad():
  {==}
```


## Command

```
ulimit -s 16384
export BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 BUN_JSC_maxPerThreadStackUsage=10485760
bend repro.bend --check-only; echo "exit $?"
```

## Expected vs actual

Expected: `ALL PROOFS CHECK`, exit 0. The equation is true, and `{==}` should convert two closed Nat terms without evaluating them one successor at a time.

Actual (`repro.bend`), exit code 1, 0.4 s:

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error: the machine stack overflowed (a deep recursion, or a literal too large to expand)
```

Actual (`repro_show.bend`), exit code 1, 0.2 s. There is no "SOME PROOFS FAIL" line, only Bun's uncaught-exception output:

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
      at map (1:11)
      at term_snf (/$bunfs/root/bend:2407:32)
      at map (1:11)
      at async cli (/$bunfs/root/bend:10029:19)

Bun v1.4.2 (Linux x64)
```

Measured on the compiled checker of both pinned forks (identical result, exit 1 each):

| checker | `repro.bend` | `repro_show.bend` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Giulio2002/bend `rigid-memo` c55a7f03 | exit 1, "machine stack overflowed" | exit 1, raw RangeError |
| Giulio2002/bend `module-cache-rigid` 667dae82 | exit 1, "machine stack overflowed" | exit 1, raw RangeError |
| upstream bendlang/bend 01875127 (run from source with bun 1.4.2, not compiled) | exit 1, "machine stack overflowed" | exit 1, raw RangeError |

## Environment

- Bun 1.4.2 (Linux x64), `bun build --compile bend2/main.ts` (the forks) or `bun bend2/main.ts` (upstream).
- `ulimit -s 16384` and `BUN_JSC_maxPerThreadStackUsage=10485760` (JSC's default is 5242880). Raising the JSC budget to 41943040 under the same 16 MB stack limit does not help, and with `ulimit -s unlimited` and JSC's default budget it still fails.
- Checkers: the commits in the table above. The recursion is in code upstream shares (`compare_go`, `lit_step`, `term_wnf`); only c55a7f03's conversion pass differs from 01875127, and 01875127 fails identically.

## Smallest failing literal

For `{Nat.add(N, 1n) == (N+1)n : Nat}` under the settings above:

| checker | largest N that passes | smallest N that fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rigid-memo` c55a7f03 | 58800 | 58801 |
| `module-cache-rigid` 667dae82 | 58799 | 58800 |

The depth is proportional to the value; the exact threshold moves with the stack settings and the frame sizes of the build.

## Workaround

State the fact once for a variable, prove it by induction, and apply it at the literal. Nothing is expanded, because the instance's type `{Nat.add(4294967294n, 1n) == 1n+4294967294n}` converts against `4294967295n` in one literal step. It checks in 0.14 s on all three checkers (`workaround.bend`):

```
import Base

law add_one:
  for +n: Nat
  {Nat.add(n, 1n) == 1n+n : Nat}

def add_one(n):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      {==}
    case 1n+p:
      %Equal.sym(Nat, Nat.add(p, 1n), 1n+p, add_one(p)) : {1n+_ == 2n+p : Nat}
      {==}

law big_add:
  {Nat.add(4294967294n, 1n) == 4294967295n : Nat}

def big_add():
  add_one(4294967294n)
```

## Root cause

`Nat.add(a, b)` is `match a: 0n -> b; 1n+p -> 1n+Nat.add(p, b)`. The machine unfolds the literal `4294967294n` one layer at a time (`lit_step`) and returns `Succ(Nat.add(4294967293n, 1n))`. `compare_go` then compares that `Ctr` against the literal `4294967295n` (itself stepped to `Succ(Lit)` by `lit_step`) and recurses into the argument of `Succ`, which is again a call of `Nat.add`, one JS stack level per unit of the value. The same holds for `Nat.sub`, `Nat.mul`, `Nat.divmod` and `Nat.cmp` when both arguments are literals.

JS stack trace (top, with `Error.stackTraceLimit` raised; 58816 frames in all, 58803 of them `every`):

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
    at term_higher (bend.ts:751:17)
    at term_higher (bend.ts:751:17)
    at map (native:1:11)
    at term_higher (bend.ts:762:29)
    at term_wnf (bend.ts:2835:19)
    at compare_go (bend.ts:3101:11)
    at every (native:1:11)
    at every (native:1:11)
    ... (58800 more `every` frames: compare_go -> every -> compare_go, one per Succ)
    at term_check (bend.ts:3701:12)
    at def_check (bend.ts:3767:10)
    at book_valid (bend.ts:3904:17)
```

Second symptom: for the display path, the trace bottom is `cli_file -> book_err -> err_show -> expr_show -> term_snf`, followed by about 20000 `term_snf -> map -> term_snf` frames (the normal form of `Nat.double(100000n)` is a 100000-deep `Succ` chain). The RangeError is thrown inside the `catch` that prints errors, so nothing catches it.

## Proposed fix

Two commits on the fork branch (not a PR; filed here for review):

1. `Nat literals: add, sub, mul, divmod and cmp on two literals return a literal`. In `term_wnf`, at a saturated call of one of these five Base defs, reduce the arguments to whnf and, if they are Nat literals, return the result directly: `Lit(a+b)`, `Lit(max(a-b,0))`, `Lit(a*b)`, `(Lit(a div b), Lit(a mod b))` for `b > 0`, `LT/EQ/GT`. Details that keep it sound:
   - Only the `Def` objects read from `base.bend` (a `WeakMap` keyed by identity, filled in `book_load`), so a program that defines its own `Nat.add`, or does not import Base, is untouched; the rigid pass has no defs and is unchanged.
   - The result is a literal exactly when the unary reduction's result, converted, would be the same literal; `compare_go` already identifies a literal with its `Succ` chain. Results above 0xffffffff, `divmod` by zero, non-literal arguments, and literals up to 256 keep the unary path.
   - Arguments are forced in the order the unary def forces them; the second argument of `add`, `sub`, `mul` is forced early only when the first is a literal above 256.
   - Soundness argument: `bend2/docs/NAT_LITERALS.md` on the branch.
2. `An error prints even when its normal form overflows the stack`. `expr_show` catches the RangeError of the normalization and shows the term as written. Only the message of an already failed check changes.

Branch and commits: https://github.com/Giulio2002/bend/tree/nat-literals, head `c270f754` (`0664178d` is the Nat change, on top of `module-cache-rigid` 667dae82).

Results of the fix:

- `repro.bend`: exit 0, `ALL PROOFS CHECK`, 0.14 s. `{Nat.add(4294967293n, 1n) == 4294967294n}` and `{Nat.add(4294967294n, 1n) == 4294967295n}` both pass (no failing N below the literal limit).
- `repro_show.bend`: exit 1 with `SOME PROOFS FAIL`, `- expected : Nat.double(100000n)`, `- observed : 7n`.
- The repository's tests: 1526 tests/**/*.bend with `--check-only`: exit code and full output identical to c55a7f03 and to 667dae82 on every one (0 differences), plus the 3 new tests (`tests/check/nat_literals_big.bend`, `nat_literals_big_mismatch.bend`, `error_deep_normal_form.bend`).
- Differential: 363 equations over 0..20000 for the five ops (including `b = 0`) accepted by both the unary and the new checker; 363 wrong equations rejected with byte-identical output by both.
- A 30-file bend-ssz sample (two umbrellas) checks with the same verdict (ALL PROOFS CHECK) on the pinned checker and the fix.

Not covered: `--verdict` (the Lean kernel was not available where this was run), `Nat.pow`, `Nat.min`, `Nat.max`, `Nat.double` and other Nat defs stay on the unary path, and results above 0xffffffff keep the unary path.

## Lean 4 counterpart (expected to check instantly; not run here)

Lean 4's kernel has GMP-accelerated Nat literals: `Nat.add`, `Nat.sub`, `Nat.mul`, `Nat.div`, `Nat.mod`, `Nat.beq` and `Nat.ble` on literals are computed on big numbers, not unfolded to `Nat.succ` chains. These are the same statements as the Bend ones above, one for one. They were not run (no Lean toolchain on the machine, no network from the server), so no timing is claimed.

```lean
-- add
example : Nat.add 4294967294 1 = 4294967295 := rfl
-- sub (truncated), both orders
example : Nat.sub 4294967295 4294967294 = 1 := rfl
example : Nat.sub 1000 4294967294 = 0 := rfl
-- mul
example : Nat.mul 65535 65537 = 4294967295 := rfl
-- divmod, and division by zero (Nat.div n 0 = 0, Nat.mod n 0 = n)
example : (Nat.div 4294967294 3, Nat.mod 4294967294 3) = (1431655764, 2) := rfl
example : (Nat.div 4294967294 0, Nat.mod 4294967294 0) = (0, 4294967294) := rfl
-- both sides closed
example : Nat.add 4294967294 1 = Nat.mul 65535 65537 := rfl
-- nested
example : Nat.div (Nat.sub 4294967294 2) 2 = 2147483646 := rfl
-- cmp and is_le
example : compare 4294967294 4294967295 = Ordering.lt := by decide
example : Nat.ble 4294967294 (Nat.add 4294967294 1) = true := rfl
-- the wrong equation is refused (by decide reports the false proposition)
-- example : Nat.add 4294967294 1 = 4294967294 := by decide
```

title: --verdict fails on programs bend2 accepts: a match convoys an affine argument but not a later argument whose type mentions it
body:
### What you did

bend convoy.bend --check-only; bend convoy.bend --verdict

### What happened

```text
$ bend convoy.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bend convoy.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. [...]
```

The same happens on 2.0.34 (`947db722`) and on `main` at `653e391`.

### The file

```python
import Base

type Owner is Type:
  Owner{}

type Box<-original: Owner> is Type:
  Box{owner: Owner, -same: {owner == original : Owner}}

def convoy(-original: Owner, owner: Owner, -same: {owner == original : Owner}, flag: Bool) -> Box<original>:
  match flag:
    case False{}:
      Box{owner, same}
    case True{}:
      Box{owner, same}
```

### Root cause

`bend convoy.bend -o convoy.bendtt` shows the term the kernel checks:

```text
convoy : ∀-x0 : Owner -> ∀x1 : Owner -> ∀-x2 : {x1 == x0 : Owner} -> ∀x3 : Bool -> (Box -x0) =
  λ-x0 => λx1 => λ-x2 => λx3 => (λ{(,): λ{.False: λ{(): λx4 => (.Box, (x4, (-x2, ()))); λ{}}; λ{.True: λ{(): λx4 => (.Box, (x4, (-x2, ()))); λ{}}; λ{}}}} x3 x1)
```

The match convoys `owner` (`x1`), so each arm binds it again as `x4`. `same` (`x2`) does not ride the convoy and keeps its type `{x1 == x0}`, but the arm's `Box` needs `{x4 == x0}`, so the kernel rejects the arm:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In convoy:
expected: {x4 == x0 : Owner}
observed: {x1 == x0 : Owner}
```

The source term is fine: `owner` is the same variable in both arms. Carrying `-x2` through the convoy by hand (`λx4 => λ-x5 => (.Box, (x4, (-x5, ())))` in each arm, applied to `x3 x1 -x2`) makes the kernel print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

In `safe.ts`, `convoy_bind` moves only the q=1 variables (`scope_kq`: "a q=1 one may ride a convoy"). A later variable whose type mentions a convoyed one stays outside the arm whatever its quantity: with `same` live (`same: {owner == original : Owner}`) `--verdict` fails the same way. Probably the convoy should also carry every later binder whose type depends on a convoyed variable.

Putting the scrutinee first, `convoy(-original: Owner, flag: Bool, owner: Owner, -same: {owner == original : Owner})`, passes `--verdict`: both `owner` and `same` are then bound inside each arm (`λx1 => λ-x2 => ...`).

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

title: A match carries a later variable whose type names one it carries, at its own quantity, so --verdict checks what bend2 checks (#1292)
body:
Fixes #1292.

## Cause

`tree` in `safe.ts` picks the variables a match carries into its arms (`cv0`): q=1, used in more than one arm, not Data. Each arm binds them again, and `scope_move` renames their level. A later variable whose type names a carried one stayed outside the arms, at its type there. In the issue's file, `same : {x1 == x0}` reaches an arm whose `Box` needs `{x4 == x0}`, so the kernel rejects a program bend2 accepts. A live or `+` `same` fails the same way.

## Fix

- After `cv0`, the convoy also takes each binder the arms name, live or dead, whose type names one it carries. The scan runs in binding order, so a chain of such types is closed too. A binder counts and rides by every level it names. A default arm binds a pair of the tag and the fields, so its binder can be the variable carried or the later one.
- `convoy_bind` and the arm's application use the variable's own quantity instead of 1, so a dead `same` rides as `λ-x5` / `-x2`.
- A match built dry keeps its dead uses too, as dead arguments (`uses` still skips them, so live counts don't change). Without this, a match built again saw an inner match only through its live uses, and missed a dependent that is used only dead two matches down.
- `o_uses` walks a term once and gives each level it names its live uses, with 0 for a level named only dead. `tree` reads it once per match for `cv0`, the dependent scan and the dry summary, which before walked the arms once per level. `uses(o, l)` reads it too, so `o_uses` replaces `uses`' switch instead of adding a walk. A binder's type is lowered only when an earlier binder rides.

The issue's term now goes out as the hand-fixed one in the report: `λx4 => λ-x5 => (.Box, (x4, (-x5, ())))` in each arm, applied to `x3 x1 -x2`.

## Checks

On `f9c08807`, with main `1cce4999` merged in, Linux x86_64, kernel built from that `bendtt.lean`:

- `tests/check/convoy_dependent.bend` covers nine shapes, and each one fails `--verdict` on main when it is on its own: dead, live, `+`, nested in one arm, three deep with the dependent only in the innermost matches, a default arm, a self-call, a dependent of a default's binder (`pick_tag`), and a default's binder used in one arm as the dependent (`pick_pair`). A law pins `main` at `45n`. The file prints `45n` when run, under `--checkup`, and from the JS and C builds.
- Mutations: putting back quantity 1, the live-only dry summary, a carried binder that must be a single level, a dependent that must be a single level, or no dependents at all each makes the test fail. Two don't. Putting back only q=2 → 1 passes because `lams` already copies a binder used twice. Skipping an annotation's type in `o_uses` passes because no test has a dependent named only inside a type.
- `o_uses` against the old `uses` and `occurs`, compared at every call and every level in an instrumented `-o` run over all test, demo and bench files: 6.7M comparisons, no difference.
- Timing: interleaving main and this branch five times each with `-o` on `proofs_3200`, `generics_3200`, `defs_12800` and `app_slash_boss_3d`, the medians are within 3% of main.
- `--verdict` on the 1,570 other test files, 50 demos and 22 benches gives the same exit code and output as main: 1,048 check, 591 fail, and the same 3 mismatches (`conversion_shared_cells_once`, `model_false`, `model_no_base`).
- `-o` is byte-identical to main for every file that checks (1,048).
- A differential sweep over 162 generated convoy programs varied the quantity of `owner` and `same`, where the scrutinee sits, Type or Data, and flat, nested or default arms. Of the 81 bend2 accepts, 66 check on both main and this branch and 15 check only here. None checks on main and fails here.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 50 / 50. `safe.ts` grows from 21,334 to 21,837 ttok, under its 24,000 cap.
- `tsc`: 12 errors, the same as main.
- The cluster gates weren't rerun after the review. I ran `gates/safe_node.ts` locally instead.

## Limits

A binder with no known bend2 type is left out, as before. A scrutinee whose own type names a carried variable is unchanged: in `pick_pair`, if the first arm also uses `owner`, the outer match carries `owner` after the scrutinee, and --verdict fails as on main.

Written with help from Claude Opus 5.5.

title: fix(verdict): missing Lean leaves the temporary BendTT input behind
body:
## Summary

`--verdict` leaves its private `bendtt-*` translation directory behind when it cannot build the kernel because Lean is missing. The prerequisite error is correct; this report concerns cleanup of the temporary input after that error.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Bend source at commit `a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876` with Bun 1.4.2. Arrange a disposable home with no matching cached `bendtt` binary or Elan toolchain, unset `BENDTT`, and use a child `PATH` without `lean` or `leanc`. Set `TMPDIR` to an initially empty disposable directory and `BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1`.
2. Save this complete fixture as `main.bend`:

```python
import Base
def main() -> Nat:
  0n
```

3. Run `bun bend2/main.ts main.bend --check-only`. It exits 0 and prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK` followed by the recommendation to use `--verdict`.
4. Run `bun bend2/main.ts main.bend --verdict`, then inspect the disposable temporary directory after the process exits.

The fresh runtime control redirected `node:os.homedir()` into disposable storage through a Bun preload and set the child `PATH` to an empty directory. This avoided changing the regular home or requiring a Lean download. It invoked Bun by its absolute executable path while running the unchanged source CLI.

## Expected behavior

The missing-Lean error should still exit unsuccessfully, and the private translation directory and its `in.bendtt` file should be removed before the command finishes. A repeated failed attempt should not accumulate another translation directory.

## Actual behavior

The command exits 1 with this output, but one new `bendtt-*/in.bendtt` remains in `TMPDIR`:

```text
Error: the kernel did not build (lean: Executable not found in $PATH: "lean"); --verdict needs Lean v4.34.0 (elan toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0), or $BENDTT set to a built kernel
```

Each remaining translation was 174 bytes for this fixture. Repeating the failed command left two translation directories with byte-identical inputs. The failed build also left a copied `bendtt.lean` in the source-hash kernel cache, with no kernel binary. That cache observation is distinct from the temporary-input cleanup failure; this report does not require deleting a previously valid cache.

## Affected area

`bend2/safe.ts`, `kernel_check()` and its call to `kernel_bin()`.

## Runtime or environment

Current inspected source commit `a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876` prints `bend 2.0.35`. The fresh control ran with Bun 1.4.2 on Darwin arm64, with Lean and Elan absent from the isolated locations. Earlier runs of Bend 2.0.34 also observed this failure. Native C compilation and clang are not involved.

## Evidence

- [`kernel_check()` writes the private input and removes the directory only after `run_read(kernel_bin(), ...)` returns](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/bend2/safe.ts#L1525-L1532).
- [`kernel_bin()` copies the kernel source and throws on a failed Lean invocation](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/bend2/safe.ts#L1475-L1502).
- [`run_read()` already removes its own temporary log directory through a `finally` block](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/bend2/safe.ts#L1508-L1519). The fresh control left no `bend-run-*` log directory.
- The surviving translation had SHA256 `783127dbf5d090d167997f76da8339a0c63f0a808e387cd24c53c8fbccf1a13e`; the copied kernel source had SHA256 `e15042434e73aab07ab05cea4b77b5619082c00a6d4924ea2d4a2cdec05facce`.

## Impact

A routine missing prerequisite leaves generated proof material on disk and repeated attempts can accumulate temporary directories. The reproduction uses a harmless closed Nat term and makes no claim that the kernel accepted a proof.

## Additional context

The closure check is the same failed-kernel-startup run returning exit 1 with no surviving per-attempt translation directory. Successful verdict execution should continue to work and clean its temporary input as before.

title: fix(docs): README denies named hub packages and accounts documented by the guide
body:
## Summary

The README limitations list says the hub has no names, versions or accounts, while the guide and CLI describe named and versioned packages published after login. This gives readers conflicting answers about an existing workflow.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read `README.md` at commit `a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876`, under its limitations list.
2. Read the module section of `guide/GUIDE.md` at the same commit and compare the named import, named publish and login instructions.
3. Inspect the CLI help definitions and named-package handlers in `bend2/main.ts`. No login or publication is required to observe the contradiction.

## Expected behavior

The README limitations should agree with the guide and CLI about names, package versions and authenticated publishing. Any statement about search should be evaluated separately; this report does not claim search exists.

## Actual behavior

The README states:

```text
The hub has no names, versions, accounts or search yet. Packages are hashes.
```

The guide documents `import <name>@<version>/main.bend as P` and `bend main.bend --publish <name>@<version>` after `bend login`. The CLI advertises that named publishing needs login and implements authenticated name registration and version linking.

## Affected area

`README.md`, the hub entry in the limitations list.

## Runtime or environment

Documentation and CLI source inspected at commit `a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876`. That source declares version 2.0.35. The same contradiction was previously observed at commit `947db722640c86247849343657bf2f7ef01cb7f1`, which declared 2.0.34. The report is a source-backed documentation inconsistency; it does not assert a fresh end-to-end public hub test.

## Evidence

- [Contradictory README limitation](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/README.md#L249).
- [Guide module section describing named imports and publishing after login](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/guide/GUIDE.md#L527-L532).
- [CLI usage definitions for named publishing, linking and login](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/bend2/main.ts#L36-L44).
- [Authenticated name ownership checks, registration and version linking](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/a950fd683c0d76f09794078e6174fe98a1492876/bend2/main.ts#L559-L585).

## Impact

Readers may conclude named packages and account-based publishing are unavailable despite the documented CLI workflow. The contradiction can be checked and corrected without writing to the public hub.

## Additional context

The closure check is agreement between the README, guide and CLI about the named-package and login workflow, while retaining only limitations supported by the current implementation.

title: fix(formatter): preserve unsafe declaration suffixes
body:
## Why

formatting `def value?()` currently produces `def value ? ()`, so valid code stops parsing after format-on-save. The parser requires `?` to stay attached to the declaration name.

## Scope

Add two spacing rules in `needsSpace`. Tests cover unsafe declarations, split declaration headers, invalid gaps and existing hole formatting.

## Blast radius

Only the formatter changes. Existing gaps before `?` stay intact, so formatting doesn't silently turn an invalid declaration into an unsafe one.

## Verification

- `npm test --prefix tools/bend-fmt-lsp` passes all 17 tests, including the stdio LSP test. The new regressions fail before the fix.
- Ran nine original and formatted inputs through `bun bend2/main.ts`. Valid inputs return the same values, and the invalid-gap input stays rejected. Formatting is idempotent.
- Sent an unsafe declaration through the built LSP server. The returned edit matches the expected source and runs successfully in Bend.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` passes 50/50. `git diff --check` passes.

title: fix(docs): README denies named hub packages and accounts
body:
## Summary

The README limitations list said:

```text
- The hub has no names, versions, accounts or search yet. Packages are hashes.
```

Three of those four claims are stale against this same tree.

- `guide/GUIDE.md:530-532` documents `import <name>@<version>/main.bend as P` and `bend main.bend --publish <name>@<version>` **after `bend login`**.
- `bend2/main.ts` implements all of it: `bend login` writes the Bender key (`:67`, `:133`), `cli_link` calls `hub_name` (`:544-549`), `--publish <name>@<version>` parses a name and runs `hub_check` (`:248-253`, `:495-539`), and the help text already reads *"publish the file and its imports; a name needs login"* (`:41`) and *"log in to Bender for --publish <name>@…"* (`:43`).

The replacement bullet states what is actually true and keeps the shape of the surrounding limitations:

```text
- A hub package is a hash, unless its author names and versions it after `bend login`.
```

Fixes #1295.

## What I did not change, and why

The original bullet also claimed **no search**. I dropped that claim rather than restating it: `bend2/main.ts` has no search verb (`grep -c -i search bend2/main.ts` → `0`), but the hub UI lives in the sibling `bend-lang.com` checkout named in `AGENTS.md`, which I could not read, so whether search exists there is not answerable from this repo. #1295 scopes search out separately, so this PR asserts nothing about it. If search does not exist, it is a one-clause follow-up.

## Verification

- `README.md` is **2980 ttok** against the permanent **4000** cap in `gates/repo.ts:43` (`allow("README.md", 4000)`), measured with `ttok` as that gate does. Before: 2977.
- Diff is one line in one file. No code, no gate, no `guide/` change — note `guide/GUIDE.md` is already at 7968/8000 ttok, so I deliberately kept away from it.
- Read `README.md`, `guide/GUIDE.md` and `bend2/main.ts` at `a950fd68` (the commit #1295 pins) and again at current `main`; the stale bullet is unchanged between them, so the report holds against `main`.
- No build or test run: this is a prose change with no executable surface.

## Contract Routing

No contract touched. Documentation-only, outside every gate in `gates/` except the `README.md` ttok cap checked above.

title: graph_close indexes the edges once, so a closure is linear in the graph instead of the reached set times the edges
body:
`graph_close` rescanned the whole edge list for every node it reached, so a closure cost (nodes reached) × (edges). It now groups the edges by source once and walks only each reached node's own edges. The C emitter calls it three times per build (the lend fixpoint, live/device reachability, and `forky`), so large programs paid the quadratic term on every emission.

The result is unchanged: the same `Set` comes back with the same members in the same insertion order (`Set.prototype.forEach` visits values added during the walk, as the old `for..of` did). All three callers pass string keys, so map lookup matches the old `===`.

### Same output

- Emitting C for every `.bend` under `tests/`, `demos/` and `bench/` (1,626 files) with main and with this branch: the same exit status for all 1,626, the same stderr for all 1,626, and all 737 emitted `.c` files byte-identical.
- A randomized check of old against new on 20,000 string graphs (cycles, self loops, duplicate edges, unreachable nodes; the closure grew in 12,503 of them) compares members and order. Planting either a dropped edge or a non-transitive walk in the new version makes it fail.
- `comp.ts` is 64,000 ttok with this change (main: 63,980), at the cap, not over it. `tsc -p bend2/pack` reports the same 12 errors as main.

### Speed

C emission time (`bend chain.bend -o chain.c`, one run each, Apple M-series) for a chain of N defs where each calls the next:

| N | main | this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 0.22 s | 0.23 s |
| 4,000 | 1.06 s | 0.75 s |
| 8,000 | 2.33 s | 1.20 s |
| 16,000 | 12.82 s | 2.22 s |

The repository's own demos are too small to show it: `app_slash_boss_3d` (3.2 MB of C) emits in about 1.3 s either way, within run-to-run noise.

```sh
n=16000; { echo "import Base"; echo; printf 'def f%d(x: U32) -> U32:\n  x\n\n' $n
  for i in $(seq $((n-1)) -1 0); do printf 'def f%d(x: U32) -> U32:\n  f%d((x + 1 : U32))\n\n' $i $((i+1)); done
  printf 'def main() -> IO(Unit):\n  IO.print(U32.show(f0(0)))\n'; } > chain.bend
time bun bend2/main.ts chain.bend -o chain.c
```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: On MSL 3.2+, heap_free reads the error flag with a coherent volatile load, not an atomic one (#1143)
body:
Closes #1143 with its first option. **Needs a check on an M1 or M2 before merging** (see below).

`heap_free` checks the error flag on every free, and on the device that check is an atomic load of one shared word, which lanes are served one at a time. On MSL 3.2+, where `DEV` is `coherent(device)`, it now reads the flag with a volatile load. That keeps the check but lets the read come from cache. Below 3.2, and on the host and CUDA, `err_peek` is `err_seen`, unchanged.

**Speed (M4, wall time, `--gpu`, 20 alternating rounds, same outputs):**

| bench | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| tree-bitonic (768MB) | 1.756s | 1.662s | 1.06x |
| tree-radix | 1.182s | 1.160s | 1.02x |

The issue measured 1.12x and 1.07x in GPU time on an M5.

**Error path:** I ran both benches out of heap (`--gpu 512MB`) 150 times each, with the same volatile read patched into main's emitted C:

| build | bad outcomes |
|---|---|
| main | 1 / 300 (1 hang) |
| volatile read | 3 / 300 (3 hangs) |

Counting earlier, smaller runs too, main had 2 bad outcomes in ~400 and the volatile read 5 in ~384, which is within chance (Fisher's exact p ≈ 0.3). Main's out-of-heap path occasionally faults or hangs on its own; that's #1300. Removing the check instead and guarding only the sink page went bad in 19 of 60 runs, so the check itself has to stay.

**Before merging:**
- **M1/M2:** this is a new load form (`air.load.device_coherent.volatile`), and `a32_load`'s comment says M1/M2 pipeline builds die on some load forms. Nobody has built a `!` program on an M1 or M2 with this change; it needs one there.

**Gates** (rebased on main at `1487e77d`): repo 50 / 50, with `comp.ts` at 63,507 ttok, under its 64,000 cap (main is 63,464); test 1577 / 1577. perf scores 121 to 124 / 124 from run to run, on this PR and on main alike, failing on the same cells (the short GPU runs of nbody, mandelbrot and merkle, and raytrace's compiler time). ping was skipped: the site repo isn't checked out on the machine that ran them.

title: Simplify window image-depth calculation
body:
Both native `window_show` paths calculated image depth with a shift loop. They now use the existing `cls_fit` helper on the larger dimension, preserving the smallest power-of-two square covering the window.

Local checks: native macOS graphics output matches the baseline; emitted JS is byte-identical and passes. Extracted old/new depth blocks agree on 251,177 dimension cases under UBSan. The repository gate passes 50/50, and `git diff --check` passes.

title: Preserve column-sensitive block layouts
body:
Bend's parser pins some lines to a column. When a body shares a line with its `do`, `match`, `case` or `def` header, the lines after it line up with that body's first token. The formatter used to re-indent those lines, so its output no longer parsed:

```bend
def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>: IO.print("a")
               IO.print("b")
```

Main's formatter moves `IO.print("b")` to 4 spaces, and the file stops parsing.

Now a line at or right of an inline body's column moves as far as that body does. Declarations aren't skipped, so everything else still gets formatted. Two related fixes:

- Tabs count one column, as in the parser (they used to reach the next 8-column stop).
- Lines inside brackets and comment-only lines no longer shift the indentation level of the statements after them. A continuation that dedents between two levels used to push the rest of a `do` block off its column.

Covered (formatter.test.ts):
- statements after `do X: a`
- array writes after `case ...: a[0] <- 7` and after `def ...: a[0] <- 7`
- `match x: case ...` rows
- a between-level continuation line
- tabs
- nested `case: do` and `case: match`
- `do IO<@x: U32 -> U32>: ...`

The test that runs the formatted output through `bend2/main.ts` now runs by default. It skips only without bun or the compiler, and it checks that each layout runs the same before and after formatting.

Checks:
- All 1730 .bend files in the repo format byte-identical to main's formatter, with `{}`, `{tabSize: 4}` and `{insertSpaces: false}`. So no `do` header that main formats is left alone.
- Output is idempotent.
- `--check-only` exit codes are unchanged for every file.
- `npm test`: 30/30.
- gates: repo 54/54, test 1623/1623, ping 58/58.

Started by @dearlordylord. The column-shifting approach follows @nicolas-abril's review.

title: simplify pending links in io_str
body:
`io_str` now tracks the next writable string link with a pointer, replacing the tail offset sentinel and guarded finalization. The root remains unsealed, tail sealing follows `SCon` hotness, and UTF-8 decoding and allocation order are unchanged.

Local checks: 12 native macOS fixtures under UBSan/bounds and 13 JS fixtures pass on both versions. Extracted-function comparisons match across 2,426,440 hot/non-hot cases. Generated C differs only in `io_str`; JS output is unchanged. The repo gate and whitespace check pass, and local runtime benchmarks show no regression.

title: use memo in recursive code generation
body:
`emit_native` and `js_marshal` now use the existing `memo` helper instead of repeating cache lookup and return logic. Both still cache the generated name before recursing, and native dependency registration still runs on every lookup.

Local checks: 83 byte-identical C, JS, and module outputs, plus seven matching missing-C-import diagnostics across 30 inputs. All 23 native macOS and 30 JS runs matched expected output. A module export round-tripped 50,000 recursive Nat fields and preserved its invalid-tag diagnostic. The local repository gate and `git diff --check` passed.

title: A law `f(x) == f!(x)` passes --verdict, but the binary returns different values on CPU and GPU (F32.sin)
body:
### What you did

bend gpu_law.bend --verdict && bend gpu_law.bend -o gpu_law && ./gpu_law --gpu 4GB

### What happened

```text
$ bend gpu_law.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend gpu_law.bend -o gpu_law && ./gpu_law --gpu 4GB
both(1e6) = (1, 0)
```

Expected `both(1e6) = (1, 1)`: the file proves `decide(x) == decide!(x)` for every `x`, and `both_agree` states that `both(1e6)` returns the same answer twice. IEEE 754 gives 1.

`F32.sin` is one function in the logic, but the binary runs two implementations. `sin(1e6)` returns bits `3199414873` on the CPU (the correctly rounded IEEE value) and `3199414874` on the GPU, one unit in the last place apart, and the comparison in `decide` turns that into 1 versus 0. Over the inputs 0 to 2^20 - 1, the sum of the result bits on the CPU equals the sum of correctly rounded IEEE results (2231521338); on the GPU it is 2231625621.

Possible fix: compile one implementation of the F32 transcendental functions (`sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`, ...) into the shared C file and use it on both targets, in place of libm on the CPU and CUDA's `sinf` on the GPU (documented error up to 2 ulp). A correctly rounded implementation gives the same bits everywhere and could also let the checker compute these functions from F32 bits, as it already does for F32 literals.

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, driver 580.82.09, CUDA 12.9 (NVRTC 12.9.86).

### The file

```python
import Base

def pick(b: Bool) -> U32:
  match b:
    case True{}:
      1
    case False{}:
      0

def decide(+x: F32) -> U32:
  pick(F32.is_gt(F32.sin(x), F32.neg(0.3499935269355774)))

# the CPU answer and the GPU answer, side by side
def both(+x: F32) -> U32 & U32:
  (decide(x), decide!(x))

# the call placed on the GPU answers what the CPU call answers
law cpu_eq_gpu:
  for +x: F32
  {decide(x) == decide!(x) : U32}

def cpu_eq_gpu(x):
  {==}

# both() returns the same answer twice
law both_agree:
  {both(1000000.0) == (decide(1000000.0), decide(1000000.0)) : U32 & U32}

def both_agree():
  {==}

def show(p: U32 & U32) -> String:
  (a, b) = p
  "both(1e6) = (" ++ U32.show(a) ++ ", " ++ U32.show(b) ++ ")"

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(show(both(1000000.0)))
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 21.1.8 (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git 2078da43e25a4623cab2d0d60decddf709aaea28)

title: Native automatic erasure progressively slows repeated wrapped-list allocation; explicit traversal stays fast
body:
## Summary

On darwin arm64, native Bend 2.0.35 repeatedly building and automatically erasing the same affine list of wrapped one-word arrays progressively slows down. No bend-kit libraries, JSON, sockets, parallel calls, unsafe code, or background input are needed. This also reproduced on 2.0.34.

A structural traversal that explicitly matches the same wrappers before erasing their buffers stays roughly constant. The following is a performance regression within one process, not a correctness assertion or an established explanation of cache/allocator internals.

## Reproduction

Save as `repro.bend`:

```bend
# Base-only allocation/disposal control, with no bend-kit imports.
import Base

type Blob is Type:
  Blob{size: U32, buffer: Array<U32>}

type Item is Type:
  Item{blob: Blob}

def build(count: Nat, acc: List<&1, Item>) -> List<&1, Item>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+rest:
      build(rest, Item{Blob{1, Array.new(U32, 0n, 48)}} <> acc)

def elapsed(label: String, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    end : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ " " ++ Nat.show((end - start : Nat)))

def erased(value: List<&1, Item>, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  elapsed("DISPOSE_MS", start)

def retained(value: List<&1, Item>, +output: Chan(List<&1, Item>), start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    sent : Bool <- Chan.send(List<&1, Item>, output, value)
    elapsed("BUILD_MS", start)
    disposal : Nat <- IO.now()
    received : List<&1, Item> <- IO.join(List<&1, Item>, output)
    erased(received, disposal)

def measure(nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    output0 : Chan(List<&1, Item>) <- Chan.new(List<&1, Item>, 1)
    +output : Chan(List<&1, Item>) = output0
    start : Nat <- IO.now()
    retained(build(nodes, Nil{}), output, start)

def repeat(count: Nat, +nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("DONE")
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        measure(nodes)
        repeat(rest, nodes)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  repeat(24n, U32.to_nat(524283))
```

```
bend version   # bend 2.0.35
bend repro.bend -o repro
./repro --threads 1 --gpu off
```

Environment: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64. The program repeats 24 times and builds 524,283 elements per iteration. `IO.now` stage durations are milliseconds. Channel send/receive prevents erasure before the build timestamp.

## Expected

Identical build/drop cycles should not progressively become tens of times slower while the previous list is reclaimed and no payload remains retained. I would expect comparable steady-state costs, allowing normal timing variation.

## Observed

On 2.0.35, BUILD_MS starts at 6, 4, 14 ms and later reaches 152, 178, 265, 245, 312 ms. DISPOSE_MS starts at 10 ms and later includes 296, 212, 515 ms. The full sequence is retained in [the kit attribution dataset](https://github.com/paymog/bend-kit/blob/test/camber-ownership/camber/json_attribution_results.json).

## Controlled comparison

Replace `erased` with:

```bend
def erase(value: List<&1, Item>) -> Unit:
  match value:
    case Nil{}:
      Unit{}
    case Con{Item{Blob{size, buffer}}, rest}:
      erase(rest)

def after_erase(value: Unit, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  elapsed("DISPOSE_MS", start)

def erased(value: List<&1, Item>, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  after_erase(erase(value), start)

```

On the same compiler and machine, BUILD_MS stays 3–5 ms after the initial 5 ms; DISPOSE_MS stays 3–4 ms except one 7 ms sample, over all 24 repeats. The program still constructs, retains, receives, and disposes the same list. It adds a structural traversal rather than changing the payload shape.

A simpler `List<Array<U32>>` without wrappers also stays fast. Holding 126 MiB of independent Base arrays is not necessary for the degradation. Removing `List.reverse` does not remove it (this minimal reproduction has no reversal).

The JSON investigation which led here showed a native profile with 1880 of 4247 sampled main-thread stacks in `term_drop`; that profile is from the larger isolated JSON probe, not the minimal file. Generated native `heap_free` pushes nodes on a size-class free list, and automatic `term_drop` walks/reclaims children before their containers; allocation/reclamation order and locality are a hypothesis, not yet proven.

## Application consequence

Our JSON result has many nested wrappers and exact-number byte arrays. On one 2.0.35 binary with selectable disposal modes, a 126-body live batch with automatic disposal took 46.6/76.4/78.9 seconds for the ordinary request; explicit disposal took 4.65 seconds in a fresh process immediately afterward (and 3.18/3.70/4.06 seconds in three preceding trials). Automatic cost is unstable, so this is not a stable speedup claim or a claimed compiler-release regression. The intervention is not a general decoder fix or a scheduler fix. We are retaining the reproduction instead of introducing a special-case production workaround.

title: Documentation bug: The BendRT paper’s opening example fails type checking
body:
### Summary

The first program in the BendRT paper fails type checking with Bend 2.0.35 because its arithmetic expressions lack the required type annotations. Adding three U32 annotations makes the example check and run. Readers copying the published example otherwise encounter an error before they can run it.

### What you did

I saved the first Bend block of `bend2/docs/BendRT/main.typ` (lines 150-174, the same program as page 1 of `paper/BendRT.pdf`) as `example.bend` and ran:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only
```

### What happened

Exit 1:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- message  : a type for this operator (write (a * b : Nat))
Location:
11 |     case 1n+p:
12>|       l r = build(p, i * 2) build(p, i * 2 + 1)
   |                        ^
13 |       Node{l, r}
Note: we broke this after launch, sorry. Until 2.0.16 a bare operator meant Nat.
That was a bug: operators demand annotation. Wrap the expression and it'll work again.
```

Commit [176842d3](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/176842d35d39e160902aa2245d13e82cb2c12f9a) makes an operator take its type from the `( .. : T)` around its own expression. The paper's example still uses bare operators. Commit [573002f0](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/573002f01ec6c52416d44489543f69a9625facf8), a later commit, rebuilt both papers without changing this example.

### Expected behavior

The paper's first example checks and runs. For example, annotate the operators (`(i * 2 : U32)`, `(i * 2 + 1 : U32)`, `(a + b : U32)`; with these three changes the file checks, runs and prints `4294443008`), then rebuild `paper/BendRT.pdf`. A check that extracts this block and runs `--check-only` on it would catch the next drift.

### bend --version

`bun bend2/main.ts version` prints `bend 2.0.35` (bun 1.4.2), at commit `2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788`.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### The file

```text
import Base

type Tree is Type:
  Leaf{x: U32}
  Node{l: Tree, r: Tree}

def build(+d: Nat, +i: U32) -> Tree:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      Leaf{i}
    case 1n+p:
      l r = build(p, i * 2) build(p, i * 2 + 1)
      Node{l, r}

def sum(t: Tree) -> U32:
  match t:
    case Leaf{x}:
      x
    case Node{l, r}:
      a b = sum(l) sum(r)
      a + b

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  t = build(20n, 0)
  IO.print(U32.show(sum!(t)))
```

### Evidence

- [bend2/docs/BendRT/main.typ:161](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/docs/BendRT/main.typ#L161): the bare `i * 2`
- [paper/BendRT.pdf](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/paper/BendRT.pdf), page 1: the same example

title: Demo bug: HTTP fetch truncates responses after two TCP reads
Test gap: Compiler-cache tests never repeat compilations in the same process
body:
### Summary

The compiler-cache fixtures describe repeated and interleaved compilations, but the test runner executes each file once per execution mode. It does not check whether earlier compilations change later results or retain unnecessary compiler state. A historical retained-state defect provides a concrete regression case; the current probes found no incorrect compiler output.

### What Bend should do

Add an in-process compiler-state check with two cases: compile one checked program repeatedly, and alternate independently loaded programs. Compare the emissions with freshly loaded program baselines, and check that retained compiler state stays bounded across repetitions.

### Why

[`borrow_loop.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/reg/borrow_loop.bend#L6) says "The runner's reg_compiler_pure row recompiles this file in-process and byte-compares the emissions". That row lived in `check/test.ts` (present at [01902c52](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/01902c52a625959cb19c88a98835b10bb981f078/check/test.ts#L1113)); [0dffc607](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/0dffc607bf56a3bcf74e5235ae6057e24b0e91ee) deletes that file, and [d7af6bf9](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/d7af6bf92a5f4298cc61614f4808b41aa8588765) adds the current `borrow_loop.bend` with the comment and a `gates/test.ts` without the row. The `harness_cache_*` headers ([compile](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/harness_cache_compile.bend#L1), [purity](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/harness_cache_purity.bend#L1), [stats](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/harness_cache_stats.bend#L1)) describe repeated and interleaved operations on one cached program. The gate runs each file once per execution mode and compares its output ([`test_probes`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/test.ts#L81)), which cannot observe either sequence.

### A past retained-state defect

[ad424afe](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/ad424afe7ab112f9007c92fae44e525bca7186ab) (#976) adds `PROBES.length = 1` to `carb_book`, the program setup that both C and JS emission run (at the baseline it is [`file_book`, L1327](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/comp.ts#L1327), called from `compile_book` and `js_lib`). Its message says previous compilations' binder variables stayed retained and that "Bundles are byte-identical before and after". An emission comparison alone therefore does not detect this defect.

A local probe on the commit and its parent, reading `PROBES.length` after each C compilation, recorded:

| Sequence | Parent of ad424afe | ad424afe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `borrow_loop` × 3 | 118, 235, 352 | 118, 118, 118 |
| then `borrow_loop`, `harness_cache_compile`, `borrow_loop` | 469, 550, 667 | 118, 82, 118 |

In every sequence the repeated `borrow_loop` emission was byte-identical to its first one. The probe observes retained state only; it shows no wrong executable.

### Acceptance criteria

- One checked program: `C → C`, `C → JS → C`, and normalization between emissions; emitted bytes and values match fresh baselines.
- `A → B → A` with independently checked programs whose definitions differ; both A results match, and B matches its fresh baseline.
- A deterministic test hook or equivalent observable asserts bounded retained compiler state across repeated compilations. The parent of ad424afe fails this assertion although its emitted bytes agree.
- The gate runs these assertions, and the fixture comments describe the sequences actually exercised.

### Verification and scope

At the baseline, a local probe ran C, JS, C, normalization of each definition, JS and C on one checked program for `borrow_loop` and the three `harness_cache_*` fixtures; all emissions matched fresh baselines. No current cache-purity failure was observed.

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

title: Ineffective tests: Printer and value checks pass despite changes they should detect
body:
### Summary

Some printer tests compare output only after normalization has removed the syntax they intend to check. Some value tests compare a computation with itself. The examples below show which incorrect outputs these checks cannot detect and specify independent assertions that would detect them.

### What Bend should do

Test printer syntax before normalization erases it, and compare computed values with independent expectations. Start with the bang/let printer fixtures and the ineffective checks in `if_elif_desugar` and `word_bitwise_literals`.

### Why

Several expected outputs erase the syntax they are intended to check, while several value checks compare a computation with itself. Concrete historical and current demonstrations show which distinctions these assertions miss.

### A reproduced printer failure and its current guards

[Commit 025dcc76](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/025dcc76baa87e84195cbae77a5b5395ce9da4e1) fixes both printer behaviors named by these fixtures. Calling the printer on the same constructed terms using that commit's source and its parent's source reproduces:

| Term | Parent of the fix | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marked reference applied to a variable | `f(x^0)` | `f!(x^0)` |
| Let expression used as an argument | `f(y = a; y)` | `f((y = a; y))` |

To replay, in an empty directory:

```sh
git -C <bend-checkout> show 025dcc76^:bend2/bend.ts > before.ts
git -C <bend-checkout> show 025dcc76:bend2/bend.ts > after.ts
git -C <bend-checkout> show 025dcc76:bend2/base.bend > base.bend
```

then save as `probe.ts` and run `bun probe.ts`:

```ts
import * as Before from './before.ts';
import * as After from './after.ts';
for (const [name, B] of [['parent', Before], ['fix', After]] as const) {
  const bang = B.App(B.Ref('f', undefined, true), B.Var('x', 0));
  const letArg = B.App(B.Ref('f'), B.Let(['y'], [0], [B.Ref('a')], B.Var('y', 0)));
  console.log(name, B.term_show(bang), B.term_show(letArg));
}
```

```text
parent f(x^0) f(y = a; y)
fix f!(x^0) f((y = a; y))
```

The current `offload_bang_g` and `offload_bang_h` expected outputs (line 16 of each) are `n => n` and `n => Nat.add(n, n)`: neither observes a bang. The `let_in_argument_*` expected outputs (line 30) similarly normalize away their lets, for example `n => Nat.add(n, 2n)` and `q => Kind(q)`. [The test-format migration d7af6bf9](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/d7af6bf92a5f4298cc61614f4808b41aa8588765) adds these current fixtures and describes removal of `--show` blocks. The old printer bug is independently reproduced above; the previous test harness's effectiveness was not reconstructed.

### Small current demonstrations

In an isolated copy of `if_elif_desugar`, replace the `g.lo`/`g.hi` branch results `10`, `20`, `30` with `90`, `91`, `92`. The copy still checks, its interpreter `main.out` is `66`, and emitted JS prints the existing expected output `66`. Every `agree(x)` compares `g(x)` with itself, so these changed branch values remain invisible. The independent `nest` checks remain meaningful.

In a copy of `word_bitwise_literals`, replace the four comparisons for `3735928559`, `65`, `122`, and `48` with `U32.is_eq(0, 0)`. It still checks and both the interpreter result and emitted JS output remain `11`. This demonstrates four ineffective literal checks; its other bitwise/boolean checks still assert independent results.

### Acceptance criteria

- Print raw or suitably residual terms containing a marked reference and an argument-position let. Assert the mark and parentheses; verify parse/print round trips where supported. Restoring either historical printer defect must fail its test.
- Check `g(0), g(2), g(3), g(5), g(6), g(9)` against `10, 10, 20, 20, 30, 30`; the demonstrated branch mutation must fail.
- Replace literal self-comparisons with independent expected values for the supported literal forms. Give the scanner result in `match_call_flat` and the final constant digit in `list_map_fold_ops` assertions about the actual computed result.

### Evidence

- [tests/printer/offload_bang_g.bend:16](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/printer/offload_bang_g.bend#L16)
- [tests/printer/offload_bang_h.bend:16](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/printer/offload_bang_h.bend#L16)
- [tests/printer/let_in_argument_arg.bend:30](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/printer/let_in_argument_arg.bend#L30)
- [tests/printer/let_in_argument_knd.bend:30](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/printer/let_in_argument_knd.bend#L30)
- [tests/stats/match_call_flat.bend:97](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/stats/match_call_flat.bend#L97)
- [tests/run/if_elif_desugar.bend:57](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/if_elif_desugar.bend#L57)
- [tests/run/word_bitwise_literals.bend:42](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/word_bitwise_literals.bend#L42)
- [tests/run/list_map_fold_ops.bend:151](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/list_map_fold_ops.bend#L151)

### Verification and scope

The historical printer outputs and both current mutations were run locally; generated JS exited successfully with the unchanged expected outputs. The confirmed issue is the listed tests' inability to distinguish the stated behaviors; no current printer or scanner implementation defect is asserted.

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

title: Verification gap: Standard checks do not build the proof kernel or test its verdicts
body:
### Summary

The standard verification commands can pass without building the Lean proof kernel or checking its verdicts. Existing regression programs cover failures in translation and kernel checking, but the standard test run checks only the frontend. A small required kernel-verdict suite would make those regressions enforceable.

### What Bend should do

Add a small, enforced kernel/verdict regression suite to the standard gate workflow. Build the current Lean source with the pinned Lean 4.34.0 toolchain, then test explicit expectations for accepted, rejected and out-of-scope programs. Treat build, transport and child-process failures as infrastructure failures. Keep the larger safe survey descriptive if useful; its known mismatches need individual expectations before enforcement.

### Why

The [standard runner](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/_run.ts#L18) runs repo, test, perf and ping. The [test gate](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/test.ts#L142) invokes `--checkup`; the separate [safe survey](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L118) exits zero after reporting. Thus the standard gates do not require a kernel build or the independent verdict. This is a coverage gap, rather than a violation of the survey's existing pass/fail contract.

There are already specific regression cases to enforce:

- [#1181](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1181) reports frontend acceptance followed by a translator stack overflow, plus a nested-type case with unbounded memory growth. The inspected fix [25dc99a7](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/25dc99a707c10b1fd6df649c462e4e9c138d3609) bounds translator model search and adds `model_no_base.bend`. Its comment requires out-of-scope without exhausting the timeout, but its expected output only contains frontend proof-checking output. That expected output cannot distinguish bounded model search from the translator hanging.
- [#1133](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1133) reports a frontend-accepted `Equal.cong` proof rejected by the kernel. The inspected fix [3378e623](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/3378e6237ed431d17629efd36d24c96241815b7e) changes the kernel's application inference to annotate a lambda argument entering a dependent result type, adjusts the proof of checker soundness, and adds `cong_lambda_argument.bend`. A frontend-only run cannot establish that this kernel-specific regression remains fixed.
- [e1ed2435](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/e1ed243502764d013471a7338bc7ab2c8e62ff98) replaces the translator's reference/order-based recursive-group selection with live-cycle membership and adds `group_dead_forward.bend`. The fixture's laws distinguish unrelated helpers from group members; the translator must preserve them too.

These are inspected commit diffs, not an inference that missing gates caused the original defects.

### Reproduction on the current source

From the repository root, with Lean 4.34.0 available, run:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/model_no_base.bend --checkup
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/model_no_base.bend --verdict
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/model_no_base.bend -o /tmp/no-model.bendtt
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/group_dead_forward.bend --verdict
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/cong_lambda_argument.bend --verdict
```

Observed: `--checkup` exits 0; the second command exits 1 with `SOME PROOFS FAIL` followed by the line "Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. ..."; export exits 0 and explicitly reports `reflexive` out of scope because there is no model for its specialized argument; the group and lambda-argument fixtures each exit 0 with `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The expected out-of-scope case therefore requires more than a generic nonzero-exit expectation: a timeout or broken kernel must fail the regression test.

### Acceptance criteria

1. One documented standard verification command builds the current `bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0 and runs the verdict suite. The default kernel cache is already keyed by a hash of `bendtt.lean` ([bend2/safe.ts:1480-1484](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/safe.ts#L1480-L1484)); `$BENDTT` overrides it with any binary ([L1476-1478](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/safe.ts#L1476-L1478)). The suite either ignores `$BENDTT` or checks that it was built from the current source.
2. Start with the three fixtures above, `rewrite_motive_evidence.bend`, and a small genuinely rejected case. Expectations distinguish kernel acceptance, intentional source/translation rejection and finite-model out-of-scope. Unexpected omission, timeout or infrastructure error fails.
3. The harness is tested with a failing kernel executable and an expired deadline; it reports each as a failure, never as an expected rejection.

### Question for the maintainer

The standard run has a 30 s cap ([gates/_run.ts:4](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/_run.ts#L4), [L16](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/_run.ts#L16)), and the survey's kernel is built on a Lean node ([gates/safe.ts:12-13](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L12-L13)). Should the verdict suite join the four gates under that cap (with a prebuilt kernel), or run as a separate required command?

### Verification limits

The entry points, three historical diffs and the linked report bodies were inspected. Historical failure outputs are attributed to their reporters; the old revisions were not executed. The commands above were rerun locally with Bun 1.4.2 on Darwin arm64 and a kernel built from the baseline source using Lean 4.34.0. No mini-cluster gate run was performed. This request concerns regression enforcement; it does not assert a live proof of `Empty`.

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788); the source CLI reports `bend 2.0.35` through `bun bend2/main.ts version`.

title: Tooling bug: The proof survey mislabels infrastructure failures as proof rejections
body:
### Summary

The proof survey compares the source checker with the independent proof kernel. Its results can count a failed worker as a source rejection, a missing kernel executable as a kernel rejection, and time spent collecting diagnostics as a verdict timeout. These classifications make infrastructure problems appear to be disagreements about a program.

### What you did

Fed the survey's classifier, `judge` in gates/safe.ts, three rows. From the repository root, save as probe.ts and run `bun probe.ts`:

```ts
import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';
const source = readFileSync('gates/safe.ts', 'utf8');
const start = source.indexOf('function judge(');
const end = source.indexOf('\nconst rows', start);
if (start < 0 || end < 0) throw new Error('judge boundaries changed');
const js = new Bun.Transpiler({loader: 'ts'}).transformSync(source.slice(start, end));
const judge = new Function(js + '; return judge;')();
const v = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['bend2/main.ts', 'tests/proof/group_dead_forward.bend', '--verdict'],
  {encoding: 'utf8', env: {...process.env, BENDTT: '/nonexistent'}});
const out = v.stdout + v.stderr;
for (const row of [
  {f: 'a.bend', code: -1, ms: 0, out: 'shard failed on 206: transport broken'},
  {f: 'a.bend', code: v.status, ms: 90, out},
  {f: 'a.bend', code: v.status, ms: 29500, out},
]) console.log(JSON.stringify(judge(row)).slice(0, 60));
```

The second and third rows carry the real output of `BENDTT=/nonexistent bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/group_dead_forward.bend --verdict`, which exits 1 with `SOME PROOFS FAIL` and the "Sorry - this is a mismatch ..." line. The same file with a working kernel prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

### What happened

```text
[" ","bend2 rejects: "]
["!","Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript impl
["t","timeout"]
```

1. A shard whose node script fails is recorded as one row per file with `code: -1` ([safe.ts:70](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L70)). These rows lack "Sorry - ", so they are labeled `bend2 rejects` ([safe.ts:87](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L87)) and counted in `b2rej` ([safe.ts:105](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L105)).
2. A kernel that cannot run yields the same `--verdict` output as a kernel rejection, and the classifier labels it `!` false reject ([safe.ts:94](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L94)).
3. A mismatch whose diagnostics push `ms` past 29 s is labeled a timeout ([safe.ts:78](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe.ts#L78)). In safe_node.ts the deadline covers only the verdict child ([L20](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L20), cleared at [L22](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L22)). When the output contains "Sorry - " ([L23](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L23)), up to three synchronous diagnostic children run, each with a 20 s timeout ([L25-33](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L25-L33)), and `ms` is measured after them ([L35](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L35)).

Also observed: running `echo tests/proof/group_dead_forward.bend | BENDTT=/nonexistent bun gates/safe_node.ts` throws `TypeError: null is not an object` at [safe_node.ts:27](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L27) (`spawnSync` returns `stdout: null` for a missing binary), and the process then stayed at 100% CPU until killed after about two minutes.

### Expected behavior

The worker reports exit status, whether the deadline killed the child, and the verdict's own duration, separately from diagnostics. The classifier distinguishes infrastructure failure, frontend rejection, out of scope, kernel rejection and agreement, and keeps the underlying error text.

### Acceptance criteria

1. The shard-failure row and a row where the kernel did not run are classified as infrastructure errors that keep their message; neither is counted as `bend2 rejects` or `!`.
2. A child killed by the deadline is already classified `t` (`code === null`). The `ms >= 29000` test is replaced by the verdict's own duration or an explicit timeout flag, so diagnostic time never turns a completed verdict into `t`.
3. A failing diagnostic child (including a missing `BENDTT`) keeps the original verdict and reports the diagnostic failure separately.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35 (`bun bend2/main.ts version` at [2bfc83fd](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788)); bun 1.4.2.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### Scope

The probe runs the extracted classifier on these rows; no cluster run was performed, and no frequency of these rows on the cluster is claimed.

title: Test gap: Ownership tests miss memory leaks and omit the code they intend to check
body:
### Summary

Four ownership regression tests do not observe the properties described in their comments. Two check numeric output without checking memory use; two compile programs from which the relevant definitions are removed as unused. They therefore cannot detect the corresponding leaks or incorrect generated code. This report requests stronger tests and does not claim a current memory leak.

### What Bend should do

Give ownership regressions a resource assertion, and keep their target code reachable. Start with `closure_value_owns`, `list_rebox_sum`, `closure_slab_drop` and `match_absurd_tail`.

### Why

The gate compares each test's output with its trailing `#|` lines ([`test_read`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/test.ts#L50), [`test_judge`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/test.ts#L89)). Four ownership fixtures cannot fail that comparison on the property they name:

- [`closure_value_owns.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/reg/closure_value_owns.bend#L1) witnesses a leak of 47 MB per million applications "right answer printed", and its line 4 says "The rss pin below is the tripwire". The file has no rss pin; its only expectation is `#|41000000` ([L76](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/reg/closure_value_owns.bend#L76)). An earlier copy, `check/tests/reg_closure_value_owns.bend`, carried `# rss < 16`. [d7af6bf9](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/d7af6bf92a5f4298cc61614f4808b41aa8588765), which adds the current file, drops the pragma form (its message: "the `# rss`/`# csrc`/`# yellow` pragmas are gone").
- [`list_rebox_sum.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/run/list_rebox_sum.bend#L1), added by the [#970](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/970) fix [de63a6f0](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/de63a6f0f3a930484eeaa583d0d196c6f448214b), states that the leak is not visible in the output and that the fixture only holds the shape compiling and running. Its expected output is `7` and `3`.
- [`closure_slab_drop.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/compile/closure_slab_drop.bend#L28) binds an unused closure and prints `5`; [`match_absurd_tail.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/compile/match_absurd_tail.bend#L24) binds an unused partial-match function and prints `ok`. After loading and checking each program, `compile_book` and `js_book` emit neither `foo` in the first case nor `absurd.arm` in the second, so the drop and the stuck-default paths these headers describe are absent from the compiled programs. Dead-code pruning itself is intended.

### Acceptance criteria

- `closure_value_owns` and `list_rebox_sum` (repeatedly building, reboxing and consuming both `Scalar` and `Pair` lists) assert bounded live memory after warm-up, with allocator free-list retention accounted for. The pre-fix ownership behavior fails each check.
- `closure_slab_drop` and `match_absurd_tail` keep their target definitions in the emitted C and JS and assert the intended lowering. Inspecting the empty-elimination code needs no uninhabited argument.

Possible follow-up: several comptime and NOFK fixtures describe properties their expected outputs do not assert, for example [`nofk_closure.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/compile/nofk_closure.bend#L1) (no-fork marks; expected output `22`) and [`hand.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/comptime/hand.bend#L1) / [`tmpl.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/comptime/tmpl.bend#L1) (identical generated C).

### Verification and scope

The two pruning cases were checked in emitted C and JS at the baseline. The #970 leak and the closure-value leak were not rerun. This issue asks for stronger tests and claims no current leak.

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

title: Diagnostic bug: safe_diag cannot parse current rewrite syntax and misreports valid recursion
body:
### Summary

The safe_diag diagnostic tool fails to parse an exported program that uses current rewrite syntax. For a second program accepted by the proof kernel, it incorrectly reports that a recursive argument does not decrease. These failures affect the explanation produced by the diagnostic tool; the kernel verdict is computed separately.

### What you did

From the repository root, export two existing fixtures:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/rewrite_motive_evidence.bend -o /tmp/rewrite.bendtt
bun gates/safe_diag.ts /tmp/rewrite.bendtt
bun bend2/main.ts tests/halt/nested_literal_rebuild.bend -o /tmp/descent.bendtt
bun gates/safe_diag.ts /tmp/descent.bendtt parity
```

Both exports exit 0. The rewrite diagnostic exits 1 with `expected => at , x4 => {x3 == x0 : N}; {==}`. The descent diagnostic exits 0 but prints:

```text
parity: no descent at column 0 in (parity (.S, (x0, ())))
```

Check the same exported files with a kernel built from the current source. With `BENDTT` set to that executable:

```sh
LEAN_STACK_SIZE_KB=4194304 "$BENDTT" /tmp/rewrite.bendtt
LEAN_STACK_SIZE_KB=4194304 "$BENDTT" /tmp/descent.bendtt
```

Both exit 0 with `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The second fixture matches `S{S{p}}` and calls `parity(S{p})`: the reconstructed one-layer cell is a strict subterm of the refined input.

### Verified history

[27dc2f69](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/27dc2f69) changes the kernel's rewrite grammar from `%e : x => P; f` to `%e : x, h => P; f`, changes the elaborator accordingly, and adds `rewrite_motive_evidence.bend`. The diff changes `Term.parse_rwt` to consume the comma and bind both names. It does not change `gates/safe_diag.ts`.

`git log -- gates/safe_diag.ts` shows only its introduction in [a0107463](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/a0107463); that version's parser and the current parser both consume just one binder. This is a verified instance of grammar evolution leaving a diagnostic consumer behind. The separate descent discrepancy is established by the current executable comparison; no particular historical change is claimed to have introduced it.

### What happened

The diagnostic parser accepts one rewrite-motive binder, while the elaborator and kernel use two. The diagnostic tool parses the whole exported program before selecting a definition, so one rewrite anywhere in the book stops the diagnosis. Its descent check also lacks the kernel's path/tag and reconstruction rules, so it reports an accepted reconstructed recursive argument as non-decreasing.

The survey runs this diagnostic tool only on a mismatch whose kernel error matches `affine live code` ([gates/safe_node.ts:28](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/gates/safe_node.ts#L28)). Both failures above come from standalone runs; neither has been observed in a survey row. This tool is diagnostic only: the verdict comes from the Lean checker.

### Acceptance criteria

1. `safe_diag` parses the current `%e : x, h => P; f` rewrite syntax.
2. Its descent reconstruction is labeled as approximate in its output, or aligned with the kernel's `Term.pos`/`Term.tree`.

### bend --version

`bun bend2/main.ts version` reports `bend 2.0.35`; `bun --version` reports `1.4.2`. Product source baseline: `2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788`.

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### Evidence
