title: Test gap: The deep Nat thunk test runs compiled JavaScript instead of the source interpreter
body:
### Summary

The deep_thunk_chain test describes a source-interpreter stack-overflow regression involving a long chain of delayed Nat computations. Its IO main function routes execution through compiled JavaScript, so the test does not exercise that chain in the source interpreter. A pure main function is needed to cover this specific case.

### What Bend should do

Add a version with a pure `main` of `deep_thunk_chain.bend`, so that the source interpreter forces the Nat-shaped 262144-link thunk chain. This is a small coverage gap.

### Why

[`deep_thunk_chain.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/eval/deep_thunk_chain.bend#L1) describes the interpreter's `term_wnf` crashing on a deep lazy accumulator and says it adds "the Nat shape (Succ-node field thunks driven through the match walk) and the IO main" to `wnf_deep_chain`'s coverage. Its `main` has type `IO(Unit)` ([L48](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/eval/deep_thunk_chain.bend#L48)). [`book_run`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/main.ts#L849) runs an IO `main` through `Comp.io_run`, which evaluates the emitted JS ([L1294](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/comp.ts#L1294)), and a pure `main` through `Bend.term_snf`. This fixture's `interp` probe therefore runs the JS program, and its Nat chain is never forced by `term_wnf`.

[`wnf_deep_chain.bend`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/tests/reg/wnf_deep_chain.bend#L34) already covers frontend depth with a pure `main: Bool`. The missing case is the Nat shape alone.

### Acceptance criteria

- A fixture with a pure `main` builds and forces the Nat-shaped chain at the same depth, and its expected output is the interpreter's answer.
- The `deep_thunk_chain.bend` header describes it as an IO/backend case.

### Verification and scope

The routing in `book_run` and the fixture headers were read at the baseline. No interpreter failure is claimed; the request is one added fixture and a header correction.

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

title: Documentation clarification: State the limits of Bend’s guarantee that proved laws hold during execution
body:
### Summary

The README, guide introduction, and introductory film say that proved laws always hold. The project documents limits elsewhere: the source checker and translation are outside the kernel proof, and JavaScript execution has a known NaN representation difference. Linking those limits beside the first guarantee would make its scope clear.

### What Bend should do

A wording suggestion for the maintainer: qualify the law guarantee where it first appears, with a link to the existing limitations, and give the guide introduction and the film the same scope.

### Why

The [README](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/README.md#L47-L48) says the compiler guarantees that laws always hold, and its [example](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/README.md#L63) says breaking them is "mathematically impossible". The [guide introduction](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/guide/GUIDE.md#L6) and the [film](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/docs/intro/render.js#L63) make the same claim.

The README's [limitations](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/README.md#L245-L246) already say that the compiler is not fully audited and that the checker has no proof, and the [BendTT paper](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/bend2/docs/BendTT/main.typ#L1040) places the parser and the source-to-BendTT translation outside its proof. The suggestion is to make these reachable from the first guarantee.

A documented case where a proved law does not hold at execution on one execution backend, [WONTFIX: F32 NaN payload bits](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/WONTFIX.txt#L108) (#797, #872):

```bend
import Base

def as_f32(u: U32) -> F32:
  U32{w} = u
  F32{w}

def bits(f: F32) -> U32:
  F32{w} = f
  U32{w}

def proven() -> {bits(as_f32(2139095041)) == 2139095041 : U32}:
  {==}

def main() -> U32:
  bits(as_f32(2139095041))
```

At the baseline:

| Command | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `bun bend2/main.ts law.bend --verdict` | `ALL PROOFS CHECK` |
| `bun bend2/main.ts law.bend` (pure `main`, source interpreter) | `2139095041` |
| `bun bend2/main.ts law.bend -o law.c -o law.js -o law`, then `./law` | `2139095041` |
| then `bun law.js` | `2143289344` |

In [#872](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/872#issuecomment-5746201608) the maintainer confirms that this difference can select a different dependent branch and duplicate an affine value; WONTFIX keeps the behavior and names C the reference backend. This request leaves that decision as it is, and it claims no inconsistency in BendTT.

### Acceptance criteria

Next to the first guarantee, a short qualification with links to the README limitations, WONTFIX and the paper's proof scope, covering:

- `--verdict` checks the translated program with the proven kernel; the source checker and the translation have no proof.
- Execution can differ from a proved result on an execution backend with a documented limit, such as the JS NaN case.

The guide introduction and the film get the same scope. The detailed lists stay in WONTFIX and the paper.

### Verification and scope

The table was produced at the baseline on macOS with bun. The public claims were compared with the README limitations, WONTFIX and the paper. Translation identity and coverage cases are tracked in [#1174](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1174) and [#1131](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1131).

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

title: Documentation bug: Demo comments claim stronger properties than their laws prove
body:
### Summary

Two demo comments overstate their formal laws. The sorting demo claims that mixing preserves leaves, but its law preserves only their sum. The printer demo claims balanced braces, but its law counts only opening braces. The comments should state these narrower properties, or the laws should express the stronger claims.

### What Bend should do

Make two law comments say what their laws state, or strengthen the laws to match the comments.

### Why

#### pure_par_sort: "mix loses no leaf"

The header of `demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend` reads "mix loses no leaf, and sort keeps the leaves' sum". The second half is accurate: `sort_leaves` equates `Sort.sum` before and after `sort`.

The first half overreaches. `mix_leaves` also equates sums: the sum of `x` and `y` equals the sum of the two `mix` outputs. The leaf count is already fixed by the type, since `Tree(d)` is a perfect tree of depth `d`. Equal sums with equal counts do not preserve the leaves themselves: the leaves `[1, 4]` and `[2, 3]` have the same count and the same sum. So "loses no leaf", read as "the same leaves come out", is not what the law states.

Possible fixes: word it as "mix keeps the leaves' sum", or state the permutation by counts, as `demos/proof_insertion_sort/LAWS.bend` does ("A permutation is stated by counts").

#### pure_hvm5_mini: "the printer's packs are balanced"

The `pak_braces` comment begins "the printer's packs are balanced", then states the exact fact: a pack of run `p` around `x` opens `run_len(p)` more braces than `x`. The law counts only `{` (via `opens`), so the word "balanced" is the defect. Closing braces are unconstrained.

This was checked with a mutation of the demo's printer. In a copy of the demo with `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend` unchanged:

- The clause `"}" ++ bits_close(p)` in `bits_close` is replaced with `"" ++ bits_close(p)`, so `bits_close(2n)` prints `""`. Loading `PROOF.bend` with `Bend.book_load` and checking it with `Bend.book_valid` still passes.
- As a control, on top of that mutation, the `"{"` in `bits_open` is replaced with `"["`. `book_valid` then rejects the program.

Possible fixes: drop "balanced" from the comment, or add a law on closing braces.

### Evidence

- [demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend:1](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend#L1): the header
- [demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend:6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend#L6): `mix_leaves`
- [demos/pure_par_sort/main.bend:8](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_par_sort/main.bend#L8): `Tree(d)`
- [demos/pure_par_sort/main.bend:71](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_par_sort/main.bend#L71): `sum`
- [demos/proof_insertion_sort/LAWS.bend:1-2](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/proof_insertion_sort/LAWS.bend#L1-L2): permutation stated by counts
- [demos/pure_hvm5_mini/LAWS.bend:28-31](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_hvm5_mini/LAWS.bend#L28-L31): the `pak_braces` comment and law
- [demos/pure_hvm5_mini/main.bend:476](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_hvm5_mini/main.bend#L476): `opens` counts `{` only
- [demos/pure_hvm5_mini/main.bend:1803-1815](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788/demos/pure_hvm5_mini/main.bend#L1803-L1815): `bits_open` and `bits_close`

Source baseline: [2bfc83fd6cc6](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/2bfc83fd6cc64cc08c6eaa225aacb69c86072788).

Each linked report states the finding, supporting evidence, and limits of what was verified.

title: docs(demos): the sort and printer law comments state only what their laws prove
body:
Fixes #1318.

## Why

Two demo comments claim more than their laws prove, so a reader who trusts the
comment is misled about what the demo has actually verified.

`demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend` opened with "mix loses no leaf, and sort keeps
the leaves' sum". Only the second half held. `mix_leaves` equates the sum of
`x` and `y` with the sum of the two `mix` outputs, so both halves are sum laws.
The leaf count is already fixed by the type — `Tree(d)` is a perfect tree of
depth `d` — and equal sums over equal counts do not preserve the leaves
themselves: `[1, 4]` and `[2, 3]` have the same count and the same sum.

`demos/pure_hvm5_mini/LAWS.bend` opened its `pak_braces` comment with "the
printer's packs are balanced", but the law counts only `{` — `opens` is
"how many `"{"` a string holds" — so closing braces are unconstrained. The
issue's mutation shows the asymmetry concretely: emptying `bits_close`'s
`"}"` clause still passes `book_valid`, while changing `"{"` in `bits_open`
to `"["` does not.

## Scope

Comment-only, in the two files the issue names.

- `demos/pure_par_sort/LAWS.bend:1` — the header now reads "both mix and sort
  keep the leaves' sum", which is the property both laws state.
- `demos/pure_hvm5_mini/LAWS.bend:28` — the comment now says the packs add
  opening braces, and says outright that closing braces are not constrained by
  this law, so the next reader does not have to rediscover the limit.

I took the issue's first option — narrow the comments — rather than strengthen
the laws. Strengthening `mix_leaves` to a real permutation statement means
either changing the demo's type or writing a much harder law, and
`pak_braces`'s fix would be a second law on closing braces, which is new
surface for a docs correction to introduce. Narrowing keeps every verified
property exactly as it is and makes no demo easier to pass by weakening what
it checks. If you would rather have the stronger laws, the wording here is the
part to redirect.

## Blast radius

None beyond the two comment lines. No law, proof or definition changes; the
verified properties are untouched.

## Verification

- `bun gates/repo.ts` — **PASS: 50 / 50** on this branch.
- `bun bend2/main.ts demos/pure_par_sort/PROOF.bend` — **ALL PROOFS CHECK**,
  the same result as before the change.
- `bun bend2/main.ts demos/pure_hvm5_mini/PROOF.bend` — still reports
  `SOME PROOFS FAIL` on its 35 unsafe-or-foreign defs. I captured the output
  before and after: the two runs are **byte-identical**, so that failure is a
  pre-existing property of this demo and not something this change introduced
  or masked.
- Each `LAWS.bend` also loads and checks on its own (the only complaints are
  the 2 and 8 expected `{?}` TODOs — a laws file declares, `PROOF.bend`
  discharges).
- `git diff --check` clean. `grep -c` confirms every changed line still starts
  with `#`.

I did not re-run the issue's `bits_close`/`bits_open` mutation: the change
touches no Bend code, so its outcome is fixed by construction. The point of
the rewording is that the comment now matches the law that mutation already
characterises.

title: --verdict: the kernel runs out of fuel on a closed Nat comparison of literals around 3 000 000 that bend2 checks at once (2.0.34)
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend fuel.bend             # bend2 only
bend fuel.bend --verdict   # bend2, then the BendTT kernel
```

Bend 2.0.34 (release `v2.0.34`, `7d8a3eb0`), Bun 1.3.14, kernel built from `bend2/bendtt.lean` (digest of the file: `61e0d2d9f4ddd7dd`) with Lean 4.34.0.

### What happened

bend2 checks the file at once; the kernel runs out of fuel, and `--verdict` reports it as a mismatch:

```text
$ bend fuel.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bend fuel.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.

$ bend fuel.bend -o fuel.bendtt && ~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt fuel.bendtt
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In bigLe:
out of fuel
```

A `Nat` literal past `256n` is `U32.to_nat(n)`; bend2 evaluates it natively, the kernel evaluates it in unary and compares step by step, so one conversion on literals of a few million exhausts `FUEL` (400 000 000 in `bendtt.lean`). Measurements, one law per file, same machine (`--verdict` takes about 8 s to give up):

| Law (proven by `{==}`) | bend2 | `--verdict` |
|---|---|---|
| `{Nat.is_le(2500000n, 2500001n) == True{} : Bool}` | pass | pass (7 s) |
| `{Nat.is_le(3000000n, 3000001n) == True{} : Bool}` | pass | out of fuel |
| `{Nat.is_le(4200000n, 4200001n) == True{} : Bool}` | pass | out of fuel |
| `{Bool.and(Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n), Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n)) == True{} : Bool}` | pass | out of fuel |
| `{Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n) == True{} : Bool} & {Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n) == True{} : Bool}`, proven by `({==}, {==})` | pass | pass |

The last two rows show the budget is per conversion (`Term.check`'s `Rfl` case calls `Term.conv … FUEL` afresh, `bendtt.lean:1102`): two comparisons that pass as two separate equalities fail inside one Boolean conversion. The practical case that led here: a closed `Bool` computation over a list of 18 inclusive intervals of code points up to `1114111n` (Unicode's noncharacters), checked by bend2 in 13 s and rejected by the kernel with the same notice.

This is not #1193 (the kernel running out of fuel where bend2 shares a graph): no sharing is involved here, only the unary evaluation of literals. `WONTFIX.txt` covers bend2's own exponential or overflowing conversions and asks for large constants to stay abstract; it says nothing about the kernel's fuel, and the 2.0.34 changelog mentions it only for shared graphs. If the kernel's unary literals are a known limit, a line there and a verdict message that says "out of fuel" (what the kernel prints) instead of the generic mismatch notice would save the next person the diagnosis.

Expected: either a native path for `Nat` literals in the kernel's evaluator (a normal form for `U32.to_nat` of a literal that converts without unfolding), or the limit documented with its order of magnitude and surfaced by `--verdict`.

Workaround used: keep every large literal comparison in its own equality obligation (one `{==}` each) and derive the closed `Bool` form from a generic law, so that no single conversion evaluates more than one such comparison.

### The file

```python
import Base

law bigLe:
  {Nat.is_le(3000000n, 3000001n) == True{} : Bool}

def bigLe():
  {==}
```

The paired control (passes both checkers):

```python
import Base

law paired:
  {Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n) == True{} : Bool} &
  {Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n) == True{} : Bool}

def paired():
  ({==}, {==})
```

and the same two comparisons inside one conversion (bend2 passes, the kernel runs out of fuel):

```python
import Base

law combined:
  {Bool.and(Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n),
    Nat.is_le(1600000n, 1600001n)) == True{} : Bool}

def combined():
  {==}
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.34 (`bend --version` is not an option in this release; the version is the release tag `v2.0.34`, `7d8a3eb0`)

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)

title: `--verdict` hangs indefinitely under templated Curry
body:
### What you did

gtimeout 30 ~/.bend/bin/bend --verdict nt.bend

### What happened

```text
(or timeout if you're on Linux)

- Dead/live typing is sound.
- Instance type computation is trying to normalise expression under ~ template.
- Non-terminating argument hangs it before affinity check refuses it.
```

### The file

```python
import Base

# Book:
# Knot.arms : ∀x0 : <Roll> -> *1 =
#   λ{.Roll: Σx0 : ∀x0 : Knot -> Empty -> <()>; λ{}}
# 
# Knot : *1 =
#   Σx0 : <Roll> -> (Knot.arms x0)
# 
# Empty.arms : ∀x0 : <> -> *2 =
#   λ{}
# 
# Empty : *2 =
#   Σx0 : <> -> (Empty.arms x0)
type Knot is Type:
  Roll{run: Knot -> Empty}

# Book:
# sink : ∀-x0 : Empty -> *1 =
#   λ-x0 => Unit
def sink(-m: Empty) -> Type:
  Unit

# Book:
# CastT2 : ∀-x0 : Empty -> *1 =
#   λ-x0 => (sink -x0)
def CastT2(-n: Empty) -> Type:
  sink(n)

# Book:
# (no book entry)
def tmplType(~n: Empty, x: CastT2(n)) -> Unit:
  Unit{}

# Bend stuck!
def caller(x: Unit) -> Unit:
  tmplType(~(
    ({\{Roll: r => r(Roll{r})} : Knot -> Empty})(
      Roll{({\{Roll: r => r(Roll{r})} : Knot -> Empty})}
    )
  ), x)
```

title: Reset layout caches before showing a new book
body:
## What
- clear the global node and layout caches before building a pure main show descriptor
- run an in-process B → A → B C-emission regression with independently loaded books that reuse type and constructor names at different layouts

## Why
compile_book calls show_main before file_book performs its per-book cache reset. After compiling one book, a second book that reuses a datatype and constructor name with a different field layout can therefore make show_main consume the first book layout. The minimal one-field → two-field sequence throws at fs[f].ks; compiling the second book alone prints the expected value.

This is a concrete cache-purity failure exposed by the test gap in #1310; it is narrower than that issue’s full acceptance criteria.

## Verification
- both fixtures: checker and --verdict pass
- both fixtures: interpreter, JS, and native C print the expected values
- before the fix: the in-process sequence throws in show_main
- after the fix: both B emissions are byte-identical and both native binaries print correctly
- gates/test.ts reaches cluster acquisition after its new local cache check; the remaining full gate could not run here because the cluster hostname is unavailable

title: fix(formatter): preserve module import paths
body:
## Why

formatting a valid `import lib/dep.bend as Dep` adds spaces around `/` and makes Bend reject the file. Keeping the import operand together also lets dot-relative imports format the surrounding code.

## Scope

Scan the first unquoted import operand as one token in `splitLine`. Add path-preservation and control cases to the existing formatter tests, plus an import case in the built-server stdio test.

## Blast Radius

This affects module-import formatting. Quoted foreign imports retain literal scanning, and division retains expression spacing. Path validation stays with Bend's loader.

## Verification

- `npm test` in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp` passes 25/25 with no skips, including built LSP stdio and unsafe-suffix regressions.
- Real CLI reproductions of relative and absolute imports fail after formatting on main and pass with this fix. Dot-relative, parent-relative, CRLF, Base, quoted FFI, arithmetic, and unsafe-suffix controls also pass. Hash and named-package paths have offline formatter coverage.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` passes 50/50. `git diff --check` passes.

Mini-cluster gates were not run.

title: --verdict certifies a different main (kernel 1, bend2 0n): a let passed to a self-call is built at the let, so a convoy captures it (#1168 via let_term)
body:
### What you did

bend upstream.bend (run, --check-only, --verdict, -o k.bendtt); then appended `probe : {main == N : Nat} = {==}` to two copies of k.bendtt (N = 0 and 1 in the kernel's encoding) and ran the kernel --verdict builds on each: ~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt k.bendtt

### What happened

```text
$ bend upstream.bend
0n
$ bend upstream.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend upstream.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend upstream.bend -o k.bendtt          (exit 0, nothing out of scope; go's Succ arm)
λx0 => λ{(): λx1 => !x2 = {λx2 => (.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ())) : ∀x2 : Nat -> Nat};
  ({λx3 => (λ{(,): λ{.True: λ{(): λx4 => (go x0 λx2 => (x4 (.Zero, ()))); λ{}};
                    λ{.False: λ{(): λx4 => (x4 (.Zero, ())); λ{}}; λ{}}}} x3 x2) : ∀x3 : Bool -> Nat} (.True, ()))

Appended to a copy of k.bendtt (probe is just a def name; the kernel's 0 is (.Zero, ()) and its 1 is
(.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ()))), then ~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt on it:
probe : {main == (.Zero, ()) : Nat} = {==}
  -> SOME PROOFS FAIL
     In probe:
     expected: main
     observed: (.Zero, ())                 (exit 1)
probe : {main == (.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ())) : Nat} = {==}
  -> ALL PROOFS CHECK                      (exit 0)

The source passes at0 = (f => f(0n)). The text passes λx2 => (x4 0), and x4 is `one`, carried into the
arm by the convoy: λ_. one(0). bend2 runs main to 0n; in the book --verdict passed, main is 1: the kernel
checks main == 1 and rejects main == 0.
Adding `def main_is_0() -> {main() == 0n : Nat}: {==}` makes bend2 accept and --verdict FAIL (the
MISMATCH message).
```

### The file

```python
# bend2 runs main to 0n, yet --verdict passes a kernel text whose main is 1
import Base

def go(n: Nat, g: (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      g(x => 0n)
    case Succ{p}:
      at0 = {(f => f(0n)) : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat}
      one = {(x => 1n) : Nat -> Nat}
      {\{True: go(p, at0); False: one(0n)} : Bool -> Nat}(True{})

def main() -> Nat:
  go(1n, (f => 0n))
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35 (main)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64 (WSL2)

### clang --version (the first line)

_No response_










**This is not WONTFIX's "the checker skips dead code".**
* bend2 checks both arms of the λ-match: a False arm of the wrong type is rejected.
* The wrong value comes through the True arm, which runs. The literal `True{}` only keeps the file
  short.
* With the scrutinee a `Bool` parameter, the result is the same: bend2 still runs `0n`, `--verdict`
  still passes, and the kernel's `main` is still 1. That variant has `go(n, g, b)`, `go(p, at0, False{})`
  in the arm, the λ-match applied to `(b)`, and `main` = `go(1n, (f => 0n), True{})`.

`01875127` fixed #1168 and #1178 for a **specialized argument**, which now goes out where it is used
([safe.ts#L837](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L837)).
`let_term` has the same pattern, and the commit left it alone. A let that a self-call takes is inlined as
a kernel term built **at the let**. It is stored in the scope with no kernel binder of its own
([safe.ts#L1205-L1209](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L1205-L1209),
on the retry at [#L1220-L1222](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L1220-L1222)):

```js
const at = { ...s, D: s2.D, kq: s2.kq };
const v = term(e, at, x.v[j], live && q > 0);
const V = open(x.v[j])[1];
if (v.$ === "Var" || put.has(j)) {
  s2 = scope_bind(s2, v, V, false);
```

So `at0`'s `λf` takes level 2, and so does the next kernel binder, the let `one`. The λ-match in the body
goes through `tree`:
* **Convoy choice.** `uses` counts `f`'s bound occurrence as a use of level 2
  ([#L1310](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L1310)),
  so `one` counts as used twice and rides a convoy
  ([#L663-L666](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L663-L666)).
* **The rename.** `convoy_bind`'s `scope_move` renames every `Var` at level 2 in every scope entry,
  bound or not
  ([#L542-L547](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719/bend2/safe.ts#L542-L547)),
  so the stored `λx2 => (x2 0)` becomes `λx2 => (x4 0)`.
* **The parse.** The kernel's parser resolves `x4` innermost-first, to the convoy's binder. The text is
  well typed, and it means another program.

bend2 forbids `match` after a let, so the convoy comes from a `\{..}` λ-match in the let body. That is
also how a program branches on a computed value at that point.

It is not limited to this shape. Each case below gets an all-green `--verdict` PASS on main whose
certified value differs from bend2's.

**The colliding binder** need not be a let. It can be:
* a λ written after the let;
* a λ-match field;
* an outer convoy binder;
* a default arm's tag/field pair. This one captures a `Data` value too: bend2 computes `105n`, the kernel
  `107`.

**The other direction.** A convoyed **free** variable of the value can land on a level one of the value's
own binders took. Here `c = {Succ{app2((u => (w => m(u))))} : Nat}` goes out as
`(app2 λx3 => λx4 => (x4 x3))`: `m` became `w`. bend2 computes `6n`, the kernel `51`:

```python
import Base

def app2(f: Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat) -> Nat:
  f(1n)((z => 50n))

def fc(n: Nat, m: Nat -> Nat, acc: Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      acc
    case Succ{p}:
      c = {Succ{app2((u => (w => m(u))))} : Nat}
      {\{True: fc(p, (x => x), c); False: c} : Bool -> Nat}(True{})

def main() -> Nat:
  fc(1n, (x => 5n), 0n)
```

**Ordinary code.**
* A CPS builder over Base's `Array`,
  `k2 = {(a => k(ANode{a, ALeaf{1n}})) : Array<Nat> -> Array<Nat>}` plus a default array, certifies
  a sum of `10` for bend2's `1n`.
* A higher-order transformer, `t2 = {(h => (x => h(Nat.mul(x, 2n)))) : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Nat}`
  plus a default function, certifies `100` for `1n`.

**A theorem's statement.** A `-> Type` def with this shape makes `def thm() -> TT(1n, (z => z)): {==}`
pass `--verdict` as `{2 == 2}`, where bend2 states `{1 == 1}`.

<details><summary>The other files (n1_array_cps, f2_type_def, a5_default_pair)</summary>

```python
# ---- n1_array_cps.bend ---- (bend2 1n; the kernel's main is 10)
import Base

def asum(a: Array<Nat>) -> Nat:
  match a:
    case ALeaf{v}:
      v
    case ANode{xs, ys}:
      Nat.add(asum(xs), asum(ys))

def fill(n: Nat, k: Array<Nat> -> Array<Nat>, more: Bool) -> Array<Nat>:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      k(ALeaf{0n})
    case Succ{p}:
      k2 = {(a => k(ANode{a, ALeaf{1n}})) : Array<Nat> -> Array<Nat>}
      z = {ALeaf{9n} : Array<Nat>}
      {\{True: fill(p, k2, False{}); False: z} : Bool -> Array<Nat>}(more)

def main() -> Nat:
  asum(fill(1n, (a => a), True{}))
# ---- f2_type_def.bend ---- (the kernel accepts {(TT 1 λx0 => x0) == {2 == 2 : Nat} : *1} and rejects it at {1 == 1})
import Base

type Bx is Type:
  MkBx{f: Nat -> Nat}

def run(b: Bx) -> Nat:
  match b:
    case MkBx{f}:
      f(0n)

def apT(f: Bool -> Type, b: Bool) -> Type:
  f(b)

def EqT(b: Bx) -> Type:
  {run(b) == 0n : Nat}

def TT(n: Nat, g: Bx -> Bx) -> Type:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      {run(g(MkBx{(x => 1n)})) == run(g(MkBx{(x => 1n)})) : Nat}
    case Succ{p}:
      c = {(z => z) : Bx -> Bx}
      d = {MkBx{(x => 2n)} : Bx}
      apT(\{True: TT(p, c); False: EqT(d)}, True{})

def thm() -> TT(1n, (z => z)):
  {==}
# ---- a5_default_pair.bend ---- (bend2 105n; the kernel's main is 107)
import Base

def ap(f: Bool -> Nat, b: Bool) -> Nat:
  f(b)

def apn(f: Nat -> Nat, x: Nat) -> Nat:
  f(x)

def k(n: Nat, g: Nat -> Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      g(5n)
    case Succ{p}:
      c = {\{Zero: 0n; m => Nat.add(m, 100n)} : Nat -> Nat}
      apn(\{Zero: 1n; m => ap(\{True: k(p, c); False: m}, True{})}, 7n)

def main() -> Nat:
  k(1n, (x => x))
```
</details>

No test file on main (0 of 1525, instrumented) and no Base def reaches the retry at L1220. That is why no
test caught this.

**Suggested fix (tested).** Do for a put value what `01875127` did for a specialized argument: bind its
bend2 term, so that `term`'s `Var` case builds it at each use, at that use's depth and mode.

```diff
   for (let j = 0; j < x.k.length; j++) {
     const q = quant(x.q[j]);
+    const V = open(x.v[j])[1];
+    // an inlined value goes out at each use, at its depth (as a
+    // specialized argument does): built here, its binders would take
+    // levels a later binder takes too
+    if (put.has(j)) {
+      s2 = scope_bind(s2, { $: "Efq" }, V, false, x.v[j]);
+      continue;
+    }
     // a parallel let's value sees s's variables, below the lets before it
     const at = { ...s, D: s2.D, kq: s2.kq };
     const v = term(e, at, x.v[j], live && q > 0);
-    const V = open(x.v[j])[1];
-    if (v.$ === "Var" || put.has(j)) {
+    if (v.$ === "Var") {
       s2 = scope_bind(s2, v, V, false);
```

The fix also updates two comments: `Bind`'s at L79-81 ("the term a specialized one (or an inlined let)
stands for") and `let_term`'s at L1196-1198 ("…, which goes out at each use").

With it, `go`'s arm is `(go x0 λx3 => (x3 (.Zero, ())))` and the kernel's `main` is `0`. Results:
* **Repros.** Over our local repros (182 distinct programs), every PASS whose kernel `main` differed
  from bend2's now agrees with it. Each was probed at bend2's value and at another value. No PASS becomes
  a FAIL.
* **Adversarial programs.** 21 programs written against the fix find no wrong-value PASS. Two stay false
  FAILs with the same text as on main: when inlining copies a captured function variable, the kernel says
  `expected: *2 / observed: *1`.
* **Tests.** All 1525 test files on main give the same `-o` result with the fix, and the 1039 that bend2
  accepts give byte-identical texts. None of them reaches the retry, so this shows only that nothing else
  moved.
* **A side effect.** A let-bound constructor passed to a self-call is now built in self-call mode, so it
  stays η-short. `c = {MkBx{f} : Bx}; k(c, t)` then passes the kernel's descent check, where on main it
  fails with `affine live code, calls that descend`:

<details><summary>letctor.bend</summary>

```python
import Base

type L is Data:
  LNil{}
  LCons{h: U32, t: L}

type Bx is Type:
  MkBx{f: U32 -> U32}

def k(a: Bx, b: L) -> U32:
  match a:
    case MkBx{f}:
      match b:
        case LNil{}:
          0
        case LCons{h, t}:
          c = {MkBx{f} : Bx}
          k(c, t)
```
</details>

Making `scope_move`/`uses` stop at binders closes the first example but not the `fc` one (its text is
unchanged), so it is not a substitute for the fix above.

**What the kernel can check.** Nothing in the text is ill-typed, so the type check cannot see this. The
parser can.
* **The shape.** Each capture reuses a binder name that is already bound where the binder is introduced.
  In `go`'s arm, the value's `λx2` sits under the let `!x2`. In `fc`, the value's `λx3 => λx4` sits
  under the convoy's `λx4`.
* **Why it matters.** `parse_name` resolves a name to the innermost binder, so the reused name silently
  rebinds.
* **Why it is safe to refuse.** The kernel's own printer (`Term.show`) names each binder by its depth and
  never reuses a name in scope. With the fix, safe.ts doesn't either: every binder in the texts it emits
  for the tests is named `x<depth>`.

The parser could refuse such a binder, as `parse_enum` refuses a repeated label:

```diff
--- a/bend2/bendtt.lean
+++ b/bend2/bendtt.lean
@@ -589,6 +589,14 @@
   set (s.drop k.length)
   pure (String.ofList k)
 
+-- a binder's name: not bound where it is introduced, since a name
+-- resolves to the innermost binder (Term.show never reuses one)
+def Parse.fresh (vs : List String) : Parse String := do
+  let k ← Parse.name
+  if vs.contains k then
+    Parse.fail "a fresh binder name"
+  pure k
+
 -- a label name: a name, or ()
 def Parse.label : Parse String := do
   if ← Parse.take "()" then
@@ -658,7 +666,7 @@
 partial def Term.parse_let (vs : List String) : Parse Term := do
   Parse.eat "!"
   let q ← Quan.parse
-  let k ← Parse.name
+  let k ← Parse.fresh vs
   Parse.eat "="
   let v ← Term.parse vs
   Parse.eat ";"
@@ -668,7 +676,7 @@
 partial def Term.parse_bind (vs : List String) (c : String) : Parse Term := do
   Parse.eat c
   let q ← Quan.parse
-  let k ← Parse.name
+  let k ← Parse.fresh vs
   Parse.eat ":"
   let A ← Term.parse vs
   Parse.eat "->"
@@ -681,7 +689,7 @@
     Term.parse_match vs
   else
     let q ← Quan.parse
-    let k ← Parse.name
+    let k ← Parse.fresh vs
     Parse.eat "=>"
     let f ← Term.parse (k :: vs)
     return Lam q f
@@ -751,9 +759,9 @@
   Parse.eat "%"
   let e ← Term.parse vs
   Parse.eat ":"
-  let x ← Parse.name
+  let x ← Parse.fresh vs
   Parse.eat ","
-  let h ← Parse.name
+  let h ← Parse.fresh (x :: vs)
   Parse.eat "=>"
   let P ← Term.parse (h :: x :: vs)
   Parse.eat ";"
```

We ran main's kernel with this change:
* **Captures.** It refuses every capture text we have: this issue's on main, the same programs on
  `01875127` and 2.0.32, and #1168's and #1178's texts on 2.0.32. On this issue's file it prints
  `parse error: expected a fresh binder name at ' => (x4 (.Zero, ()))); λ{}; λ'`.
* **The fix's texts.** It accepts all of them, including every test text.
* **Order.** Land it with the fix, not before. On main, 6 correct texts also trip it: there the inlined
  value is closed (`(k x0 λx2 => x2)` under `!x2`), so the reuse does no harm.
* **Limits.** It guards names, not levels. A wrong level that reuses no name still parses.

A law on `main`'s value in the emitted book, as `tests/check/spec_arg_depth.bend` has, is still the
regression test. A test in that style (`go` + `fc`, `law let_put_depth_result: {main() == 6n : Nat}`,
`#|6n`) fails `--verdict` on main, where the kernel's `main` is `52`, and passes with the fix:

```python
# a let a self-call takes goes out at each use, at that depth: built where
# it was bound, its binders took the levels the next kernel binders take,
# and carrying such a binder into a λ-match's arms renamed the value too.
# In go, at0's body f(0n) went out as one(0n), so go(1n, g) was 1n; in
# fc, the free m moved onto the value's own w, so fc(1n, ..) was 51n. The
# law checks main's value in the emitted book too, where a wrong but
# well-typed body would still pass
import Base

def go(n: Nat, g: (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      g(x => 0n)
    case Succ{p}:
      at0 = {(f => f(0n)) : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat}
      one = {(x => 1n) : Nat -> Nat}
      {\{True: go(p, at0); False: one(0n)} : Bool -> Nat}(True{})

def app2(f: Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat) -> Nat:
  f(1n)((z => 50n))

def fc(n: Nat, m: Nat -> Nat, acc: Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case Zero{}:
      acc
    case Succ{p}:
      c = {Succ{app2((u => (w => m(u))))} : Nat}
      {\{True: fc(p, (x => x), c); False: c} : Bool -> Nat}(True{})

def main() -> Nat:
  Nat.add(go(1n, (f => 0n)), fc(1n, (x => 5n), 0n))

law let_put_depth_result:
  {main() == 6n : Nat}

def let_put_depth_result():
  {==}

#|6n
```

This is not a consistency problem: the kernel checked the text it was given. It is #1168's mechanism with
#1178's symptom: `--verdict` certifies a program other than the one bend2 checked and runs. So a bend2
checker error in a def of this shape would pass `--verdict`, and a true law about its value fails it
(`main_is_0` above). #1178's thread took the convoy drift to be gone after `01875127`. Through `let_term`
it is not, and it still reaches a type (the `TT` case).

title: fix(verdict): clean up temporary input when kernel build fails
body:
Fixes #1294.

`kernel_check()` writes a private `in.bendtt` file, then calls `kernel_bin()`. If Lean is unavailable, `kernel_bin()` throws before the existing `rmSync`, leaving that per-attempt directory behind. Put the write and kernel call inside `try/finally` so the directory is removed on both normal return and failure. This does not change verdict classification or the separate kernel-build cache.

The existing installer/CLI gate now checks the missing-Lean path in an isolated `TMPDIR`: the command must still fail, but leave no `bendtt-*` input directory.

Validation: with Bun 1.4.2 and a disposable HOME/TMPDIR, the source CLI left one translation directory before the fix and none afterward; an invalid `BENDTT` path also leaves none. A local stub exercised the cleanup on a successful return only; it was not a proof-validity test. `bun build bend2/main.ts gates/ping.ts --target=bun` succeeded and `bun gates/repo.ts` passed 50/50. The complete `gates/ping.ts` suite was not runnable here because its sibling site repository is unavailable (the gate reports `SKIP`).

title: A bare constructor name as a match pattern is silently a catch-all binder whenever the datatype comes from another file

Without import Base, safe.ts looks up the `Unit` it models a kind with, and a word literal's type, in the user's book: --check-only passes, then -o/--verdict crash or print the TS/kernel mismatch banner
body:
### What you did

For each of the three Base-free files below: bend F.bend, bend F.bend --check-only, bend F.bend -o out.bendtt (then bendtt out.bendtt), bend F.bend --verdict

### What happened

```text
crash.bend (no Unit anywhere; a def whose second ~ parameter is typed by its first)
$ bend crash.bend                 Mk{}                                                          exit 0
$ bend crash.bend --check-only    ALL PROOFS CHECK                                              exit 0
$ bend crash.bend -o out.bendtt   TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'tld.c')    exit 1
$ bend crash.bend --verdict       TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'tld.c')    exit 1
Adding def Unit() -> Type: In gives the same, with (evaluating 'tld.c.filter').

unit_param.bend (the book's own Unit takes one erased parameter)
$ bend unit_param.bend --check-only    ALL PROOFS CHECK                                      exit 0
$ bend unit_param.bend -o out.bendtt   (prints nothing)                                      exit 0
  out.bendtt ends with:  opaque idt_7e_A : *1 = Unit
$ bendtt out.bendtt                    SOME PROOFS FAIL                                      exit 1
                                       In idt_7e_A:
                                       expected: *1
                                       observed: ∀-x0 : *1 -> *2
$ bend unit_param.bend --verdict       SOME PROOFS FAIL                                      exit 1
                                       Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. ...

word.bend (a Base-free word type; bend2 takes the literal 7 at Box)
$ bend word.bend                  7                                                          exit 0
$ bend word.bend --check-only     ALL PROOFS CHECK                                           exit 0
$ bend word.bend -o out.bendtt    BendTT: out of scope, so not in out.bendtt:                exit 0
                                  - main: names U32.lit7, out of scope: names U32, out of scope: an unknown name U32
$ bend word.bend --verdict        SOME PROOFS FAIL / Sorry - this is a mismatch ...          exit 1
With a def U32() -> Bit: True{} added (word_def.bend), -o exits 0 and emits
  U32.lit7 : U32 = (.U32, ((.WCon, ...
typed at that def, and both kernels reject it: In U32.lit7: / expected: *1 / observed: Bit (exit 1).

With import Base (and no local Unit), crash.bend and unit_param.bend's idt/main pass --verdict.
```

### The file

```python
# ---- crash.bend ----
type In is Data:
  Mk{}

def bad(~A: Type, ~z: A, x: In) -> In:
  x

def main() -> In:
  Mk{}

# ---- unit_param.bend ----
type Unit<-T: Type> is Data:
  U{}

type In is Data:
  Mk{}

def idt(~A: Type, x: A) -> A:
  x

def main() -> In:
  idt(~In, Mk{})

# ---- word.bend ----
type Bit is Data:
  True{}
  False{}

type Word is Data:
  WNil{}
  WCon{h: Bit, t: Word}

type Box is Data:
  U32{d: Word}

def main() -> Box:
  7
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35 (source checkout of main at 565d7fde, bun bend2/main.ts); identical on 2.0.32

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

_No response_






safe.ts writes two names into the book it emits and looks both up in the user's book. With `import Base`
anywhere, both are Base's, because `parse_fresh` refuses a redeclaration. A book with no `import Base` may
declare its own versions of Base's types (CHANGELOG 2.0.18, #870/#875: such a book "checks and runs"). There,
each name means whatever the user's book has under it, or nothing.

**`model_at`'s model of a kind.** A root with a `~` parameter gets an opaque constant and asks `model` for a
value of the parameter's type
([safe.ts#L213-L218](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L213-L218)).
For a kind, that value is a bare book key, looked up in `e.mb`, which prototype-chains to the user's
top-levels ([L147](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L147)):

```ts
case "Typ": {
  return B.ADT("Unit", []);                 // L435-L436
}
...
case "ADT": {
  const tld = e.mb.tlds[F.k] as ADT;        // L444
  ...tld.c.filter(...)                       // L446
```

([safe.ts#L435-L446](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L435-L446).)
Nothing checks that `Unit` exists, is a datatype or takes no parameters:

* In `crash.bend`, `~z : A` is typed by the first parameter. Its model reduces `A` to the made-up
  `ADT("Unit", [])` and re-enters the `ADT` case, where `e.mb.tlds["Unit"]` is `undefined` (or a `Def`),
  and L446 throws.
* In `unit_param.bend`, `ADT("Unit", [])` gives zero arguments to a one-parameter datatype. That is a
  type-level function where a type is required.
* With one `~` and no `Unit`, `term`'s own `ADT` case catches it
  ([L813-L816](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L813-L816)),
  and the def goes out of scope as "an unknown datatype Unit", a name the user never wrote.

When the user's `Unit` has the right shape, it is used as is. A zero-constructor `Unit` makes the model of
`~A : Type` an empty type. The lookup also crosses files: a Base-free entry's `Unit` models an imported
module's `~` parameter.

**`word_ref`'s type for a word literal.** A U32/F32 literal goes out as a def of its own, typed at
`item_ref(e, T, …)`, where `T` is the literal's *constructor* name
([safe.ts#L1156-L1166](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L1156-L1166),
called at L1134). A constructor name isn't a top-level name. In the other branch, `ctr_term` finds the
family with `B.book_fam(e.book, x.k)`
([L1136](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L1136)).
The two agree only because Base names both `U32`
([base.bend#L57-L58](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/base.bend#L57-L58)).
In `word.bend` the family is `Box`, so `item_ref(e, "U32")` finds no top-level. With a `def U32`, the
literal is typed at that def.

**Suggested fix (tested on a copy of 7d24b8d).**

```diff
     case "Typ": {
-      return B.ADT("Unit", []);
+      return e.book.tlds["Unit"]?.b === true ? B.ADT("Unit", []) : null;
     }
@@
     case "ADT": {
       const key = B.term_key(B.term_lower(F, d));
-      const tld = e.mb.tlds[F.k] as ADT;
+      const tld = e.mb.tlds[F.k];
+      if (tld?.$ !== "ADT") {
+        return null;
+      }
@@ word_ref
-    e.out.push([k, { $: "Ref", k: item_ref(e, T, [], false) }, v, false]);
+    e.out.push([k, { $: "Ref", k: item_ref(e, B.book_fam(e.book, T), [], false) }, v, false]);
```

`.b === true` is the Base flag ([bend.ts#L1014-L1018](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L1014-L1018)).
check-lit already uses the same test for the same reason
([bend.ts#L3559](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L3559)).
`book_fam` is the identity on Base's `U32` and `F32`. Results with the patch:

* `crash.bend`, `word.bend` and `word_def.bend` pass `--verdict`.
* `unit_param.bend` goes out of scope with `no model for idt~A`. A `null` model already takes this path,
  and a Base-free book with no `Unit` already goes out of scope today.
* All 100 files in `tests/` and `demos/` that use `~` give byte-identical `-o` output and the same
  messages. So does a 75-file sample of files with number literals, 20 of which mint word defs.

To keep Base-free `~ : Type` roots emitting, one option is to mint a one-constructor datatype for the kind
model in place of the `null`, under a name the user can't take, the way `root_cols` already mints its
`k~p` constants (L209-L214). (Not tested.)

#1330  is the same missing guard in the long-Nat split (safe.ts:843-849). #1331   is the bend.ts side:
sugar names (`!=`, `exs`, literals) written as bare keys.

**Limits.** Not a proof of `Empty`. The kernel checks every def it is given and rejects the ill-typed ones
above. A Base-free book has no Base `Empty`, and the empty-`Unit` model certifies a valid book.

title: Without import Base, safe.ts writes a Nat literal above 4096 as the book's own Nat.add(Nat.mul(q, 4096), r), so --verdict passes a book whose certified main is 1n while bend2 runs it to 4097n
body:
### What you did

bend nat_tpl.bend (run, --check-only, --verdict, -o k.bendtt), then appended {main == 1n} and {main == 4097n} to k.bendtt and ran bendtt on each

### What happened

```text
$ bend nat_tpl.bend
4097n
$ bend nat_tpl.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend nat_tpl.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend nat_tpl.bend -o k.bendtt          (exit 0, nothing out of scope; excerpt)
id.qv_ : Nat =
  (Nat.add (Nat.mul (.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ())) <4096 as .Succ/.Zero>) (.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ())))
main : Nat =
  id.qv_

Appended to k.bendtt, then bendtt k.bendtt:
chk_main_is_1 : {main == (.Succ, ((.Zero, ()), ())) : Nat} = {==}
  -> ALL PROOFS CHECK (exit 0)
chk_main_is_4097 : {main == <4097 as .Succ/.Zero> : Nat} = {==}
  -> SOME PROOFS FAIL
     In chk_main_is_4097:
     expected: main
     observed: (.Succ, ((.Succ, …        (exit 1)

bend2 runs main to 4097n; the certified book proves main == 1n.
With `import Base` in place of the local Nat, Nat.add and Nat.mul, the same id/main certifies main == 4097n.
```

### The file

```python
type Nat is Data:
  Zero{}
  Succ{pred: Nat}

def Nat.mul(a: Nat, b: Nat) -> Nat:
  a

def Nat.add(a: Nat, b: Nat) -> Nat:
  a

def id(~n: Nat) -> Nat:
  n

def main() -> Nat:
  id(~4097n)
```

### bend --version

2.0.35 (source checkout of main at 565d7fde, bun bend2/main.ts)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64 (WSL2)

### clang --version (the first line)

_No response_




`term`'s `Lit` case in safe.ts splits a Nat literal above `NAT_MAX` (4096) through two bare book keys
([safe.ts#L843-L849](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/safe.ts#L843-L849);
safe.ts:869-875 on main, unchanged):

```js
if (x.k === "Nat" && x.v > NAT_MAX) {
  // a long Nat is q * NAT_MAX + r, by base's Nat.mul and Nat.add
  const [q, r] = [Math.floor(x.v / NAT_MAX), x.v % NAT_MAX];
  const mul = B.App(B.App(B.Ref("Nat.mul"), B.Lit("Nat", q)), B.Lit("Nat", NAT_MAX));
  return term(e, s, B.App(B.App(B.Ref("Nat.add"), mul), B.Lit("Nat", r)), live);
}
```

The comment says "base's", but nothing checks it. With `import Base` anywhere, the keys are Base's, because
`parse_fresh` refuses a redeclaration. A file without `import Base` may declare its own `Nat` (CHANGELOG
2.0.18), and then its own `Nat.add` and `Nat.mul` take those keys. bend2 never calls them for a literal.
check-lit takes a literal by name only for Base's `Nat`
([bend.ts#L3559](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L3559);
the #941 fix in 2.0.25), and otherwise it unfolds the literal structurally. So bend2 reads `4097n` as 4097,
while the kernel reads `Nat.add(Nat.mul(1, 4096), 1)`, which is `1` here.

The literal reaches the split raw by two routes. The first is a `~` argument: the instance is keyed on the
raw argument
([bend.ts#L3726](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L3726)),
and safe.ts rebuilds the arguments from that key. The second is a def's or law's type. The type route was
run on both versions:

* `def q1() -> {gt(5000n, 800n) == True{} : Bool}: {==}` (with `Nat.add(-a, b) = b`) passes `--verdict`,
  certified as a claim about `gt(904, 800)`.
* `{gt(5000n, 1000n) == True{}}`, and `def main() -> {big == 4097n : Nat}` where `big` is `4097n`, pass
  `--check-only` and MISMATCH on `--verdict`.

With no `Nat.add` in the book, `id(~4097n)` passes `--check-only` and MISMATCHes on `--verdict`, and `-o`
says `main: an unknown name Nat.add`.

A bend2-side oracle written with a literal does not catch it. `def oracle() -> {main() == 4097n : Nat}: {==}`
passes `--verdict`, because its type goes out through the same split.

**Suggested fix (not tested).** Split only when `e.book.tlds["Nat.add"]?.b === true && e.book.tlds["Nat.mul"]?.b === true`
(and `Nat`), as check-lit and the foreign-def check already do. Otherwise, emit the unary chain that
`lit_step` gives, or put the def out of scope with a reason. #1329  is the same missing guard at
`model_at`'s `Unit`.

This is not a consistency problem: the kernel checked the text it was given, and a Base-free book has no
Base `Empty`.

title: Without import Base, != and where/exs are parsed as bare Empty/Exists, so PROOF.bend decides what an imported LAWS.bend's != and where mean, even when LAWS.bend declares its own and checks alone
body:
### What you did

Three files, none of which imports Base (below): bend LAWS.bend; bend PROOF.bend --verdict; bend PROOF.bend -o p.bendtt

### What happened

```text
$ bend LAWS.bend
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error: 1 TODO found.
The code is incomplete, and not a valid proof yet.
(what a correct LAWS.bend with its law still open prints)
$ bend PROOF.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend PROOF.bend -o p.bendtt        (excerpt)
LAWS.Empty : *2 =
  Σx0 : <> -> (LAWS.Empty.arms x0)

Empty : *2 =
  Σx0 : <Boom> -> (Empty.arms x0)

LAWS.f_ne_g : ∀x0 : main.T -> ∀x1 : {(main.f x0) == (main.g x0) : main.T} -> Empty =
  λx0 => λx1 => (.Boom, ())

f and g both return A{}, so the law is false as LAWS.bend states it, over its own empty Empty.
The certified != negates into PROOF.bend's one-constructor Empty; LAWS.Empty is emitted unused.
If PROOF.bend declares no Empty, it fails at LAWS.bend's law line:
- expected : a defined name / - observed : Empty (caret on the !=).
If the law is written {Code.f(x) == Code.g(x) : Code.T} -> Empty instead of with !=, the same PROOF.bend
fails: - expected : Laws.Empty / - observed : Empty.
With import Base, LAWS.bend's own type Empty is already a duplicate declaration.
```

### The file

```python
# ---- main.bend ----
type T is Data:
  A{}
  B{}

def f(x: T) -> T:
  A{}

def g(x: T) -> T:
  A{}

# ---- LAWS.bend ----
import ./main.bend as Code

type Empty is Data:

# LAW: f and g never agree
law f_ne_g:
  for x: Code.T
  {Code.f(x) != Code.g(x) : Code.T}

# ---- PROOF.bend ----
import ./LAWS.bend as Laws

type Empty is Data:
  Boom{}

def Laws.f_ne_g(x):
  e => Boom{}
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.35 (source checkout of main at 565d7fde, bun bend2/main.ts)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64 (WSL2)

### clang --version (the first line)

_No response_




bend.ts writes sugar, and the constructors of a literal, as raw, unqualified names that never go through
`parse_reso`:

* `!=` is `Ref("Empty")`
  ([bend.ts#L1902](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L1902)).
* `exs`/`where` is `Ref("Exists")` (L2171, L2571, L2576).
* A Nat literal unfolds to `Zero`/`Succ` (`lit_step`, L1098, called by check-lit).
* `Nn+T` with n > 256 is `Ref("Nat.add")` (L2226).
* `a || b` is `Bool.or(a, b)` (the INFIX table; run, below).
* By reading, the same holds for list literals, `Array.new`, and the INFIX table's other named entries
  (`Pair`, `Or`, `Bool.and`, `Con`, `String.append`).

The checker looks each one up by bare key
([bend.ts#L3284-L3287](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/b2111cf43244e65f76ddc278ee695e669f720cbf/bend2/bend.ts#L3284-L3287);
3301-3304 on main) after every file is parsed. With Base loaded anywhere, those keys are Base's, and
`parse_fresh` stops anyone from redeclaring them. Without Base, the only namespace-`""` declarations are
the entry file's, so PROOF.bend supplies the meaning of LAWS.bend's `!=` and `exs`. A written `Empty` in
LAWS.bend is not captured: `parse_reso` makes it LAWS.bend's own name. Only the sugar is, so a LAWS.bend
that declares its own `Empty` checks alone (as the entry, its `Empty` is the bare key) and loses it once
imported (its `Empty` becomes `LAWS.Empty`).

Literals have a fail-closed face. A Base-free module's literal checks when the module is the entry, and
is refused when another file imports it: `- expected : a declared constructor (lib.Nat declares
lib.Zero, lib.Succ) / - observed : 2n`. The literal's bare `Zero`/`Succ` never match the module's
qualified constructors. There is also a single-file face. With a `Nat.add(-a, b)` that returns `b`,
`200n+one` runs to `201n` and `300n+one` runs to `1n`, and both pass `--verdict`. With no `Nat.add`, only
the second is refused.

The capture can also carry a literal across files into #1330 's split. Take an imported LAWS.bend with
`law l: 5000n || 800n`, under a PROOF.bend that declares its own `Nat`, a `Nat.add(-a, b)` that returns
`b`, and `def Bool.or(a: Nat, b: Nat) -> Type: {gt(a, b) == True{} : Bool}`. `bend PROOF.bend --verdict`
passes, and the certified `LAWS.l` is `Bool.or(Nat.add(Nat.mul(1, 4096), 904), 800)`: a claim about 904,
where bend2 checked one about 5000.

**`where` goes the same way.** A Base-free LAWS.bend that uses `where` has to declare its own `Exists` to
check at all. Imported, that declaration is `LAWS.Exists`, while the sugar still asks for the bare key.
Here the law is false: `g` is constantly `X{}` and `f` constantly `Y{}`. A PROOF.bend that declares
LAWS.bend's own `Sig`-based `Exists` is refused (`expected : D.Y{} / observed : D.X{}`). This one makes
`Exists` an empty type, so the law's binder ranges over nothing, and an empty match proves it:

```python
# ---- d.bend ----
type Two is Data:
  X{}
  Y{}

def f(t: Two) -> Two:
  Y{}

def g(t: Two) -> Two:
  X{}

# ---- LAWS.bend ----
import ./d.bend as D

type Sig<a, b, -A: Kind(a), -B: @-x: A -> Kind(b)> is Kind(a <&> b):
  Tup{fst: A, snd: B(fst)}

def Exists(-A: Type, -B: @-x: A -> Type) -> Type:
  Sig<&1, &1, A, B>

# LAW: for every w with g(w) = X, f(X) is X.
law holds_when_gx:
  for w: D.Two where {D.g(w) == D.X{} : D.Two}
  {D.f(D.X{}) == D.X{} : D.Two}

# ---- PROOF.bend ----
import ./LAWS.bend as Laws
import ./d.bend as D

type Vd is Data:

def Exists(-A: Type, -B: @-x: A -> Type) -> Type:
  Vd

def Laws.holds_when_gx(w):
  match w:
```

`bend LAWS.bend` prints `1 TODO found.` and `bend PROOF.bend --verdict` prints ALL PROOFS CHECK. In the
certified law, `w` ranges over PROOF.bend's `Exists`, and `LAWS.Exists` is emitted unused:

```text
Exists : ∀-x0 : *1 -> ∀-x1 : ∀-x1 : x0 -> *1 -> *1 =
  λ-x0 => λ-x1 => Vd

LAWS.holds_when_gx : ∀x0 : (Exists -d.Two -λ-x0 => {(d.g x0) == (.d.X, ()) : d.Two}) -> {(d.f (.d.X, ())) == (.d.X, ()) : d.Two} =
  λ{(,): λ{}}
```

bend.ts's header says "an unknown name is the file's own, unless its bare spelling is Base's", and the
2.0.28 notes (#1042) say a local file cannot register names in another file's namespace. GUIDE.md says
`bend PROOF.bend` prints SOME PROOFS FAIL while any law is open or false.

**Fix direction (not tested).** Bind sugar to Base only: have the checker require
`book.tlds[k]?.b === true` for a name that sugar introduced, as the foreign-def check does for `IO`, and
otherwise fail with "`!=` needs import Base". Alternatively, resolve sugar through `parse_reso` in the
file where it is written. For literals, use the target datatype's own `Zero`/`Succ`, or refuse with a
message, together with #1330 's guard in safe.ts. Either option closes both repros above. Resolving
through `parse_reso` keeps a Base-free LAWS.bend's own `Empty`/`Exists` working; binding to Base refuses
`!=`/`where` in a Base-free book outright.

This is not a proof of `Empty`. The kernel certified the entry's inhabited `Empty` (`Σx0 : <Boom> -> …`),
not `<>`, and with Base loaded the entry cannot declare `Empty`. The `where` case certifies a law under an
empty hypothesis: vacuity, not an inhabitant of `<>`.

title: --verdict: the cached kernel is reused whatever Lean built it, and the PATH fallback never checks the Lean version (2.0.35)
body:
## Where

`bend2/safe.ts`, function `kernel_bin`, at tag `v2.0.35` (commit `79df8d9c`), lines 1472 to 1500.

## What happens

The kernel is cached in `~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>`, where `<hash>` covers only the text of `bendtt.lean`. When `~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.34.0` is absent, the kernel is built with whatever `lean` and `leanc` are on `PATH`, and their version is never checked, although the error text says `--verdict needs Lean v4.34.0`. Once built, that binary is reused for every later run, even after the right toolchain is installed.

## Observed

On a machine whose only Lean toolchain was 4.32.1, `--verdict` on Bend 2.0.34 built and cached a kernel from Lean 4.32.1 output. Installing the `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0` toolchain later did not rebuild it: the cache key is unchanged, so the kernel built by 4.32.1 would still judge every 2.0.34 book.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use an environment with no `leanprover--lean4---v4.34.0` elan toolchain, Lean 4.32.1 on `PATH`, `BENDTT` unset and no cached kernel for the current `bendtt.lean`.
2. Run `bend --verdict` on any file. A kernel is built and cached under `~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt`.
3. Install `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0` with elan and run `bend --verdict` again. The cached binary from step 2 is reused unchanged.

## Expected

- Build the kernel only with Lean v4.34.0, or refuse with the existing message when the `PATH` Lean reports another version.
- Include the toolchain's `lean --version` in the cache key, or verify it on reuse, so a kernel built by another Lean is rebuilt rather than trusted.

title: ty_holds walks a type family's body, so a bang over a pair no longer puts every closure on the device
body:
## Cause

`A & B` is `Sigma<A, _ => B>`, so a pair's second half is a type family: a
`Lam`. `ty_clo` answered true for any `Lam`, so a bang with a pair parameter
set `wide`. The device then took every closure in `fl.clos`, plus everything
those closures reach. Any bang over an array pair hits this.

A bang `head!` over `Array<U32> & Array<U32>`, in a `main` with a few host-only
`IO.bind` continuations (device segments: those the C does not wrap in
`#if !DEVICE`):

| parameter                      | main     | this PR  |
|--------------------------------|----------|----------|
| `p: Array<U32> & Array<U32>`   | 24 of 28 | 5 of 28  |
| `a: Array<U32>, b: Array<U32>` | 5 of 28  | 5 of 28  |

## Fix

The change has two parts, both in `ty_holds` in `comp.ts`:

1. **Open a family's body.** `ty_holds` walks a `Lam`'s body, as
   `type_adts` already does, so its predicates no longer see a `Lam`.
2. **Skip an argument that takes a value.** A datatype's argument is walked
   unless its parameter's kind holds no sort (`ty_value`): a quantity, an
   equality, a datatype that holds none, or a function into one. A datatype
   kind is walked with `ty_holds` to tell, because a datatype value can carry
   a type: in `Hold<b: TyB>` with `TyB{T: Type}`, the argument of
   `Hold<TyB{U32 -> U32}>` is what names the function.

`js_marshal` runs a new Nat walk at each level of an effect's type, and each
walk now reaches into a pair's second half. So a right-nested tuple with a
Nat at the bottom costs O(n²) in its length. This was already so for
nesting through datatype arguments (`Maybe<Maybe<…<Nat>>>`). The walk runs
once per foreign def and `.mjs` export, on its signature, not per call, so
it is left uncached.

`ty_clo` is unchanged: a closure in either half of a pair, at any depth,
still puts the program's closures on the device, and a pair of closure-free
halves no longer does.

The other two `ty_holds` walks had the same blind spot, and the change closes
it for both:

- **JS marshaling:** `js_marshal`'s Nat walk found `U32 & Nat`'s Nat through
  the `Sigma`'s fields. In `U32 & U32 & Nat` it had already seen `Sigma`, so
  that Nat crossed the effect seam, and left a `.mjs` export, as a `number`,
  not the `BigInt` that `io/marshal_nat_bigint` pins. It's a `BigInt` now.
- **Layouts:** `lay_of`'s check for a field that re-enters its own datatype
  now also sees one through a nested pair's second half. No layout in the
  repository changes.

## Alternatives

- **Adding `"Lam"` to `ty_clo`'s list** fixes the array pair but loses real
  closures. `ty_holds` stops at a datatype it has seen, so in
  `U32 & U32 & (U32 -> U32)` nothing reaches the inner `Sigma`'s second half,
  and the lambda minted on the host has no device code.
  `compile/gpu_reach_closure_pair` fails on the GPU with that patch:
  `bend: a function the device does not hold`.
- **Opening the `Lam` only for `ty_clo`**, by having it answer `null` and
  `ty_holds` open it only then, emits the same C everywhere. But it leaves the
  marshal hole open, and it splits one rule about types between the walk and
  one of its predicates. It is also +45 ttok against this PR's +28.
- **Keying `seen` by the instantiated type rather than its name** also reaches
  the inner `Sigma`. But polymorphic recursion (`Nest<A>` holding a
  `Nest<List<A>>`) has unboundedly many instances; the name is what ends the
  walk.

## Checks

The branch is rebased on `main` (7b7559c4).

**For the whole branch** (on one Mac):

- **New test:** `compile/gpu_reach_closure_typed` is a bang over
  `Hold<TyB{U32}> & Hold<TyB{U32 -> U32}>`. It prints `43n` on the GPU, the
  CPU and JS. With the earlier rule, which counted every datatype kind as a
  value, it fails on the GPU with `bend: a function the device does not hold`.
- **All `gpu_reach*` tests and `io/marshal_nat_pair`** pass on the GPU, the CPU
  and JS.
- **Output:** for the 1,268 tests under `tests/` that import `Base`, the
  emitted `.c` and `.js` match the earlier, larger version of this fix
  byte for byte.
- **Not here:** a family that unfolds to itself
  (`def Stream(-A: Type) -> Type: A & Stream(A)`) makes `ty_holds` walk
  without end. On `main`, `type_adts` and `facts_hot` already overflow the
  stack on such a family, so that bound belongs in its own change, with a
  test that builds end to end.
- **Size:** `comp.ts` is 63,718 ttok, under the 64k cap.
- **Gates and types:** `bun gates/repo.ts` passes (50/50). `tsc -p bend2/pack`
  reports no errors in `comp.ts`.

**For the first commit only**, measured before the later commits:

- **Output:** of the 1,654 `.bend` files under `tests/`, `demos/` and
  `bench/`, 1,169 check. For each, the emitted `.c`, `.js` and `.mjs` are
  byte-identical to `main`'s except:
  - **C:** `reg/spin_array_hold`, whose `fan!` takes an
    `Array<U32> & Array<U32>`. Its device segments go from 27 of 28 to 8.
  - **JS:** the new `io/marshal_nat_pair`.
  - **`.mjs`:** `run/literal_sugar`, `show/literal_readback` and
    `io/readback_sugars`. Each exports a Nat in a nested pair's second half,
    which is now a `BigInt`.
- **New tests:**
  - `compile/gpu_reach_closure_pair` hands the device a closure in the second
    half of a pair's second half and applies it there. It prints `43n` on the
    GPU, the CPU, JS and the interpreter. It also passes on `main`, which puts
    every closure on the device; it guards the first alternative above.
  - `io/marshal_nat_pair` hands two JS effects `U32 & Nat` and
    `U32 & U32 & Nat` and prints the Nat's `typeof`. `main` prints `bigint`,
    `number`.
- **Test gate:** I ran `gates/test.ts`'s own shard script on one Mac, with
  the ssh hop swapped for a local shell. Result: **PASS: 1568 / 1571**. The 3
  failures fail the same way on `main` there:
  - `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window` expect no display, but this Mac has one.
  - `io_process_run` fails its inherited-pipe cases.
- **Benches (Apple M5):**
  - All 17 runtime benches emit byte-identical C, so the SEQ-CPU, PAR-CPU and
    PAR-GPU columns cannot move. Each prints its pinned OUTPUT in all three
    modes.
  - **Emit time** (`-o main.c`, hyperfine, 15 runs each): branch/main
    geomean 1.008 with `main` run first and 0.985 with the branch first. No
    bench moves more than 4%.
  - **COMPILER** (`-o main`, median of 5, interleaved): 0.98–1.04×.
  - **CHECKER:** all `ALL PROOFS CHECK`, and the emitted code is identical.
    A median of 3 gave 0.97–1.06×. I re-measured `generics_3200`'s 1.06 with

title: fix(verdict): respect Unit provenance and word constructor families
body:
Fixes #1329.

- `model_at` models `Type` with `Unit` only when `Unit` is a datatype with no parameters. A missing `Unit`, a `def Unit`, or a parameterized `Unit` gives no model, so the root goes out of scope instead of crashing or reaching the kernel ill-typed. A name that is not a datatype in the `ADT` case falls back to `hyp()` instead of crashing.
- Word literals are typed at their constructor's family (`B.book_fam`), computed once in `ctr_term` and passed to `word_ref`. A `Box.U32` literal is no longer typed at an unrelated `def U32`. A word literal of a parameterized family goes out of scope, since its def would be typed at an unapplied type function.
- Five fixtures, none importing Base:
  - `safe_no_unit_model`: no `Unit`; crashed under `-o`/`--verdict` on main, agrees now.
  - `safe_box_word_def`: `Box.U32` literal next to a `def U32`; kernel rejected it on main, agrees now.
  - `safe_parameterized_unit`: `Unit<-T>`; kernel rejected it on main, out of scope now.
  - `safe_unit_model`: a user's zero-parameter `Unit`; agrees on main and here, guards against a stricter Unit check.
  - `safe_parameterized_box_word`: word literals of `Box<T>`; out of scope on main and here, guards against typing them at the unapplied family.
- No CHANGELOG, guide, gate or bend.ts changes.

Verification, merged onto main 8828cc19: repo 50/50, ping 47/47, test 1565/1565, perf 124/124. `gates/safe.ts tests` matches main except the five new files (3 agree, 2 out of scope); the one false reject (`agree_32`) is also on main.

title: fix(demo): read fragmented HTTP responses until EOF
body:
Fixes #1309.

The HTTP fetch demo called `TCP.recv` twice and closed, so a `Connection: close` response that arrived in three or more pieces was cut short. It now reads until EOF (an empty receive), then closes and prints the body.

- **Reads bytes, bounded in bytes.** The reader uses `TCP.recv_bytes` and caps the response at 65536 bytes, headers included. Each receive asks for at most what is left of the budget (8192 at most). At exactly the limit, a one-byte receive must return EOF, otherwise the fetch fails with `HTTP response exceeds 65536 bytes`. A `Nat` fuel of 65536 keeps the loop structurally recursive.
- **Decodes UTF-8 once, at the end.** Decoding each receive separately split multibyte characters at chunk boundaries (`café` came out as `caf��`). Base has no bytes-to-text conversion, so the demo carries a small decoder (`utf8`) that follows the same replacement policy as the TCP text codec, including an incomplete final character.
- **Closes on every path.** EOF, the limit, and send/receive failures all close the socket once. Failures keep their original code and message.
- **Joins chunks without deep recursion.** Chunks are kept newest-first and folded once with `List.foldl`.

Tests (`tests/io/`):
- `http_fetch_eof.bend`: a real loopback listener sends the header separator, the body and a two-byte `é` across separate writes; also a response of exactly 65536 bytes whose last character's bytes arrive separately, an empty response, and one with no header separator. The test carries its own copy of the demo's reader, since tests import only from `tests/`.
- `http_fetch_limit.bend`: one byte over the limit fails with exit 1.

Verified locally:
- Both tests print their `#|` lines on the interpreted, JS and C lanes, each in about 1 s.
- Against a local TCP server on Bun JS and native C: fragmented headers and body print `ABC` (main prints an empty body), and split `café` and `x€😀ñy` sent one byte per write decode correctly.
- The `utf8` decoder matches `TextDecoder` on 433 byte strings (overlong, surrogate, above U+10FFFF, truncated, stray continuation, plus random), on C, JS and the interpreter.
- Repo gate: PASS 50 / 50. No changes to `gates/`, Base or the compiler.
- Cluster gates not run.

title: fix(runtime): report CUDA probe stage and Driver API error
body:
Fixes #1145.

`gpu_probe` returns `NULL` on success or the reason it failed, instead of one bool, so `--gpu on` no longer blames WSL2 for every failure.

- **CUDA:** `cuInit`, `cuDeviceGet`, the concurrent-managed-access query and `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain` go through `GPU_CHECK`, which reports `<function> failed: <cuGetErrorName>`, e.g. `cuInit failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`. A failed `cuCtxSetCurrent` releases the retained primary context and reports the same way. A device without concurrent managed access gets `CUDA device lacks concurrent managed access (WSL2 lacks it)`. The L2 size query stays best-effort.
- **Metal:** `this binary found no usable Metal GPU`.
- **No GPU backend:** `this binary has no CUDA or Metal GPU support`.
- `--gpu on` prints the reason and exits 1. Automatic mode still falls back to the CPU silently. `--gpu-build` uses the new return.
- `main()` keeps `dev` a compile-time `false` in GPU-less builds (`why` is `""` when the GPU is not requested). The first form, `active ? gpu_probe() : NULL`, kept clang from folding it, so `cube_run` and `corpus_lay` stopped inlining into `main` and editdist SEQ-CPU went from 1.92 s to 2.39 s (1.24x).

Verification, merged onto main 5169abf1:
- Cluster gates: repo 50/50, test 1569/1569, ping 47/47, perf 122/124 (main alone: 122/124). editdist SEQ-CPU 0.99x, tree-matmul SEQ-CPU 1.04x.
- comp.ts 63,132 / 64,000 ttok (main 62,940).
- The probe, taken from this branch's source, run against stub Driver API calls failing one stage at a time: each stage reports its function and error name, and a failed `cuCtxSetCurrent` releases the context.
- On an M4 Mac: the Metal build runs bfs with `--gpu on` and `--gpu off`; a CPU-only build exits 1 with the no-support message under `--gpu on` and runs normally without it.

Not tested on a CUDA GPU.
