title: File.read_into reads a file's bytes straight into an Array<U32>
body:
## Why

`File.read_at` returns a `List<&2, U32>` with one node per byte. A program that needs a file's bytes in an `Array<U32>`, such as a weight file, an image, or any other binary blob, has to build that list and then pack it into the array four bytes at a time. For large files, the list dominates both time and memory.

## Change

This change adds one effect to `bend2/base.bend`:

```
def File.read_into(file: File, offset: U32, max: U32, a: Array<U32>, at: U32) ->
  IO(File & (Array<U32> & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32>))
```

It reads up to `max` bytes at `offset` directly into `a`'s slots, starting at slot `at`. Bytes are stored little-endian, four bytes per slot. It returns the file, the array, and the byte count, or `(errno, message)`.

- The read stops at the array's end and at the file's end. If `at` is past the array, it reads nothing.
- A tail of fewer than four bytes overwrites only the low bytes of its slot. The slot's high bytes stay as they were.
- If a read fails immediately, as it does with a write-only handle, it returns the errno and leaves the array unchanged.
- The file position does not move, as with `File.read_at`.

Backends:

- **C** (`effs/file_read.c`): The IO worker calls `pread` in a loop and writes directly into the array's block, which it reaches through `blk_loc`. Each call asks for at most 1 GiB, because macOS `pread` returns `EINVAL` for any request past `INT32_MAX`, even on a small file. A forked handle reaches the same cells, as with `Array.set`.
- **JS** (`effs/file_read.js`): It calls `pread` in 16 MiB chunks, loops on short reads, and packs whole words into the JS array. Only unaligned edges and the short tail go byte by byte, so the JS backend and the interpreter produce the same slots as C. A large array over a small file allocates only one chunk.

## Verification

`tests/io/file_read_into.bend` covers the full read, the little-endian packing, the short tail that keeps its high bytes, a slot past the bytes that stays unchanged, an offset read into a later slot, clipping at the array's end, reads at the array's end and the file's end, the error on a write-only handle with the array left unchanged, and a good read issued right after that failure, which must report its own result. All 12 `#|` lines pass in all three paths:

- interpreted (`bun bend2/main.ts t.bend`)
- C binary (`-o t`)
- JS (`-o t.js`, run under bun)

`tests/io/file_binary.bend` still passes in all three paths. The test caught a real bug in an earlier draft: when the JS path dropped the last partial slot, the test failed with `FAIL short tail keeps high bytes`.

The last case caught a bug in a later revision: the C request is reused across a run's effects, and without resetting its error code, the good read reported the earlier `Bad file descriptor`. With the reset removed, the C lane fails the test; with it, all lanes pass.

Separate checks, all with the same result in C and JS:

- `Array.fork`: `read_into` through one handle, then a read through the other, which saw the bytes.
- 2 GiB of room (`Array.new(U32, 29n, 0)`, `max` 4294967295) over a 44-byte file: the first revision printed `fail Invalid argument` in both C and JS; this one prints `read 44`.
- A 33,554,430-byte read from offset 2 across the JS chunk boundary: the byte count and the slots on both sides of the boundary match Python's `struct.unpack('<I', ...)`.

### Timing

Benchmark: read a 16 MiB random file into an `Array<U32>` with 4,194,304 slots (`Array.new(U32, 22n, 0)`), then print slots 0 and 4,194,303. The baseline used `File.read_at(f, 0, 16777216)` and packed the list into the array with `Array.set`. The new path used one `File.read_into(f, 0, 16777216, a, 0)`. The test machine was an Apple M1 Pro running macOS. Runs were whole-process wall times, with 5 alternating rounds per lane after one warm-up. Outputs matched in every run and matched Python's `struct.unpack('<I', ...)` values for the file. The 1-minute load average was about 7.6.

| Lane | `read_at` + pack, median | `read_into`, first revision | `read_into`, this revision | Speedup vs `read_at` |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| C | 102.9 ms | 9.1 ms | 8.6 ms | ~12x |
| JS (bun) | 459.5 ms | 53.2 ms | 33.3 ms | ~14x |

The same change to a 1.3 GB quantized-model loader cut load time from about 10 s to about 1.6 s. Those runs were on a busy machine, so take that number as a rough indication only.

## Notes / open questions

- I tested this only on macOS arm64. It relies on `pread`, as `File.read_at` already does. I did not run it on Linux, and `gates/test.ts` needs the cluster, so I could not run it. As a stand-in, I ran all 187 tests in `tests/io` and `tests/base` locally on this branch and on `60fa05dc`, each through the interpreter, C, and JS. The 186 shared tests printed byte-identical output on both trees in every lane, and `file_read_into.bend` passes in all three.
- `offset` is a `U32`, the same as `File.read_at`, so this change does not address files larger than 4 GiB.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54 with `ttok==0.3`, the version pinned in `.github/workflows/repo-gate.yml`.
- I marked this PR as a draft. If you prefer different names or argument order, or if forked handles should be rejected instead of written in place, I can change it.

title: Array.q4mv: affine 4-bit matvec primitive (CPU 3.2-3.6x, bit-identical; over comp.ts cap)
body:
## What

Adds `Array.q4mv(w, x, y, +r, +n, +cols, +rows)`, a matvec over affine 4-bit weights with group size 64. One `Array<U32>` holds the codes, then the BF16 scales, then the BF16 biases. Activations are one `Array<F32>` with the per-group sums stored after the `cols` values. Each output row is rounded to BF16 and written to `y` at its index.

- `bend2/base.bend`: the pure Bend body defines the result. It sums each row group by group, left to right, then rounds to nearest-even BF16. `--check-only` passes.
- `bend2/comp.ts`: lowers the call to one C function, the same way `Array.clone` is lowered. It sums 8 rows side by side, and each row keeps its own add chain in the body's order. Clang vectorizes across rows, so every output keeps the body's bits. Only the rows asked for are written. Inside a bang, the same loop runs on the device.
- `bend2/comp.ts`: the collector now reads intrinsics per lane (`intr_of(k, FL.js)`). A C-only intrinsic therefore keeps its Bend body on the JS lane, and the interpreter and JS builds run the body.
- `tests/base/array_q4mv.bend`: 13 rows (a block of 8 and a tail of 5), then rows 3..8 alone. Expected bits come from an independent float32 reference. Slots that the call must not write keep their old value.

## Why

A Bend inference engine for a 2B-parameter 4-bit model spends its matvec time in one dependent F32 add chain per row. That is about 3 cycles per weight, or about 12 G weights/s on 10 cores. The same loop in hand-written C runs at the same speed, so codegen is not the limit. Reordering the sum would change the bits, so this PR uses independent chains across rows instead.

## Results

Apple M1 Pro, macOS. Each case ran 3 palindromic rounds (stock, patched, patched, stock), with milliseconds per call measured in-process after equal warm-up. Outputs matched stock and a float32 Python reference on every run. The 1-minute load average was 40 to 47 during these runs, so treat the spreads as wide.

| case | stock ms | patched ms | speedup (median) | per-round speedups |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU 2048x2048 | 0.750 | 0.235 | 3.19x | 4.10, 1.89, 2.70 |
| CPU 6144x2048 | 1.570 | 0.440 | 3.57x | 4.02, 3.20, 3.29 |
| CPU 2048x6144 | 1.630 | 0.470 | 3.47x | 3.57, 3.21, 3.27 |
| CPU 248320x2048 | 46.4 | 12.95 | 3.58x | 3.62, 3.62, 3.51 |

Bend's Mandelbrot and tree-matmul benchmarks do not call the primitive. Their outputs match stock on CPU and Metal. CPU medians are 966 vs 964 ms and 676 vs 679 ms (stock vs patched, 3 ABBA rounds). Metal fast-slot times are also equal: Mandelbrot 218-232 vs 207-233 ms and tree-matmul 1654-1735 vs 1646-1733 ms.

Every other test that imports Base produces byte-identical JS (1,281 tests). Its C output is byte-identical apart from the added function.

## Limits / open

- **The repo gate still fails:** `bend2/comp.ts` is 64,660 ttok (ttok 0.3, as CI uses) against the 64,000 cap. Upstream `main` is 63,905, so this change adds 755 tokens. No behavior-preserving cut of that size was found elsewhere in `comp.ts`. The gate forbids moving code out of the file, so this PR cannot merge as is.
- An earlier revision had a Metal kernel that made the 248320x2048 head about 11.5x faster than the best stock bang. That kernel was removed to save tokens.
- The same speedup is reachable in plain Bend on stock `main`, with no compiler change. A generated Bend kernel that sums 8 rows per pass, with one tuple per group, measured 3.0-4.1x and bit-identical in the same runs. That may make this primitive unnecessary in Base.
- No CUDA-specific path. Linux is untested.
- Out-of-range indices wrap like `Array.get`.
- A format-specific primitive in Base is the maintainers' call.

title: stabilize channel deadline regression timing
body:
Fixes #1396.

`chan_try_late` assumes 50 million spin iterations outlast its 10 ms receive deadline. On faster machines, the first receive can validly consume `7`, leaving the second receive deadlocked.

Replace the fixed spin with synchronous monotonic-clock reads that hold the event loop for 20 ms. Register the sender's 1 ms timer before the receiver's 10 ms deadline so scheduling pauses cannot reverse their order. Remove the spin's extra channel and preserve the strict timeout and subsequent-delivery assertions.

Local validation:
- Bend checker and BendTT kernel checks pass.
- 160 repeated native C, JavaScript, and CLI runs pass across macOS and Linux arm64.
- Injected pauses, fuel boundaries, and six related IO fixtures pass.
- Restoring the original scheduler bug still makes the fixture fail.
- Repository gate passes 54/54.

Linux validation used an arm64 container. The full test gate could not run because the configured `cluster` hostname is unavailable.

title: Metal's OUTLINE is noinline, so a large kernel stays under the AGX backend's 256 flow states
body:
## Why On an M1 Pro, a small `!` job gives a wrong answer on Metal when a large, unrelated function is compiled into the same program. The job is correct on the CPU, and correct on Metal in a small program. The repro is a 46-line driver (below) that runs `mk!(xs(2048n, 0))`: a tail-recursive `mulk` over 2048 `F32`s, then a sum. Its other branch would call one Qwen3.5 decode step (`M.step`, from a TensorFold model outside this repo). That branch never runs, but `M.step`'s device code is compiled into the same kernel. | | `--gpu off` | `--gpu 8GB` | |---|---|---| | upstream `60fa05dc` | `85.39297` | hangs (3/3 runs, 60 s timeout) | | this PR | `85.39297` | `85.39297` (3/3 runs) | Depending on the build, the wrong branch shows up as a hang (the host sums a garbage list), as `frontier drained without a result`, or as `a function the device does not hold`. ### How it failed The AGX backend miscompiles the kernel once its control flow needs more than 256 states. - **A device trace takes the wrong branch.** The lane runs `FID_ENTER → FID_MK`, and the inlined `mulk.go` spin runs all 2049 iterations. On the last one, `xs` is `Nil`, yet neither `else` branch runs. Control falls into MK's tail with the spin's output unwritten (`0`), or `work_loop` returns 0 and the task is lost. The front-end AIR (`xcrun metal -O2 -S -emit-llvm`) for that spin is correct. - **The backend tests a 16-bit state with an 8-bit immediate.** I extracted `_agc.main` from the `.gpu` archive and disassembled it with dougallj/applegpu. The backend's structurizer keeps one 16-bit flow-state register per function (`r4h`) and numbers states across the whole function. It sets a state with a 16-bit `mov_imm` or with `icmpsel`. The dispatch compares (`if_icmp`, `else_icmp`, `while_icmp`) only hold an 8-bit immediate, so a state of 256 or above is tested as `state - 256`. - **Upstream's mp3 kernel has states above 255.** It uses 262 distinct states, up to 335. Six of them are 256 or above, and every value from 0 to 255 is also in use, so each truncated test matches another real state: - `mov_imm r4h, 319` at `0x3158dc`, then `if_icmp r0l, ueq, r4h, 63` at `0x3158f2`; - `326` is tested as `70`, `332` as `76`, and `335` as `79`. - **Inlined helpers make the count grow with program size.** On Metal, `OUTLINE` was plain `static`, so the backend inlined every cold runtime helper (`heap_alloc_miss`, `rfc_wrap`, `blk_copy`, `span_fade`, `heap_hand`, …) at each call site inside the single `work_loop` kernel. Each inlined copy of the `rfc_wrap` → `heap_alloc` → `heap_alloc_miss` chain adds about 4 states, and mp3's kernel holds about 51 of them. That is why the failure needs enough unrelated code. When I made device segments host-only one at a time, the threshold was cumulative, with no single culprit. Filler code of the same size that adds no helper call sites does not reproduce it. Ruled out on the way: - `WL_RESW > 16` (a 22-word return without `M.step` passes); - `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, `maxCallStackDepth` and threadgroup memory; - the binary archive, the `volatile` local in `a32_load`, and uninitialized `WL_BANK` registers; - `coherent(device)`, the `blk_loc` arguments and the `err_spun` poll. ## Change On Metal, `OUTLINE` is now `static __attribute__((noinline))`, as it already is on the host and on CUDA. A comment above the dialect block says why. The helpers become real device calls, so their flow states stay in their own functions instead of piling into `_agc.main`. ## Verification Everything below was run on this branch (`60fa05dc` plus this commit) and on `60fa05dc`, on an Apple M1 Pro (Darwin 25.6.0, Metal compiler `32023.850`), with GPU jobs one at a time. - **mp3 repro:** see the table above. - **Flow states** in `_agc.main` (`r4h`): | program | upstream | this PR | |---|---|---| | mp3 repro | 262, max 335 | 134, max 134 | | same, with TensorFold's non-tail `V.mulk` | 262, max 333 | 132, max 132 | - **The 28 runnable tests in `tests/` that contain a `!`:** built `-o t` and run as `./t`, as `gates/test.ts` does. All 56 runs (upstream and this PR) print their `#|` lines. `printer/offload_bang_g` and `_h` can't be built, because their `main` is a function; the gate only checks and interprets them. - **An rms repro** (`mulk` without `M.step`): `591.4099` on GPU and CPU, upstream and this PR. - **mandelbrot (big):** `3101455856` in every run. Over 8 alternating pairs after a warm-up, both builds took 0.187–0.222 s. - **tree-matmul (big):** `3797651056` in every completed run. Over 10 alternating pairs: - upstream: median 1.74 s, fastest 1.43 s; - this PR: median 1.71 s, fastest 1.38 s. One upstream run was killed by macOS with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorImpactingInteractivity` (the machine was not idle), so that median is over 9 runs. `ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo < bend2/comp.ts` (the encoding that gives upstream's 63,905): 63,905 → 63,975 (+70), still under the 64,000 cap. Without the comment it would be +8.
mp3 repro driver (needs TensorFold's bend/model) ```python import Base import ./model.bend as M import ./vec.bend as V def xval(+i: U32) -> F32: (U32.to_f32((((i * 2654435761 : U32) >> 24n) : U32)) * 0.00390625 - 0.5 : F32) def xs(n: Nat, +i: U32) -> V.V: match n: case 0n: Nil{} case 1n+p: xval(i) <> xs(p, (i + 1 : U32)) def mulk.go(xs: V.V, ys: V.V, +k: F32, acc: V.V) -> V.V: match xs ys: case Con{x, xt} Con{y, yt}: mulk.go(xt, yt, k, (x * y * k : F32) <> acc) case _ _: List.reverse.go(&2, F32, acc, Nil{}) def mk(+x: V.V) -> V.V: mulk.go(x, x, 0.5, Nil{}) def stp(m: M.Model) -> M.Model & V.V: M.step(m, 760, 0) def snd.model(r: M.Model & V.V) -> V.V: (t, y) = r y def never(+k: U32, m: M.Model) -> IO(Unit): IO.print(F32.show(V.fsum(snd.model(stp!(m))))) def pick(xs2: List) -> IO(Unit): match xs2: case Con{_, Con{_, _}}: never(0, M.Model{M.HP{0.000001, 10000.0, 2048, 6144, 256, 8, 2, 64, 4, 16, 16, 2048, 4, 248320, 0}, M.Mat{0, 0, 0, M.Leaf{0, [0 : U32^0n]}}, Nil{}, Nil{}}) case _: IO.print(F32.show(V.fsum(mk!(xs(2048n, 0))))) def main() -> IO(Unit): do IO: a : List <- IO.args() pick(a) ```
## Notes / open questions - I tested only on an M1 Pro (G13). The gate's M4 minis may not have this 8-bit limit. If they don't, the change only turns cold helpers into calls there. - This lowers the count; it doesn't bound it. The count still grows by about 3 per inlined spin site and per `return 0` exit in the kernel, so a kernel about twice mp3's size could reach 256 again. A single-exit spin shape (`do { … } while (again)`) halves mp3's count again (67, measured on hand-edited generated C). It rewrites the spin macros, spin functions and call sites, so it's left as a follow-up with its own timing pass. Running `count` on the extracted `_agc.main` is the check. - There's no regression test. A failing case needs a kernel with more than 255 flow states, which takes a model-sized program, and the gate runs on M4. - This is separate from the #1393/#1394 lane-stack fix. With TensorFold's current non-tail `V.mulk`, the same repro also needs that fix, because 2048 frames overflow the 2048-word lane stack. The driver above uses a tail loop to isolate this bug. On a tree with both fixes, `deep`, `forks` and `lsum` from those issues still pass on GPU and CPU.

title: feat(io): add split wall and monotonic clocks
body:
## Problem

Base has only IO.now() in monotonic milliseconds. A package implementing wall/high-resolution clocks through foreign effects also causes its importers to lose their verdict.

Fixes #1149.

## Change

- Add Clock with Wall{} / Mono{} and IO.clock(which: Clock) -> IO(Nat & U32).
- C uses CLOCK_REALTIME / CLOCK_MONOTONIC; JavaScript uses performance.timeOrigin + performance.now() / performance.now(), as proposed in the issue.
- Return seconds plus nanoseconds in [0, 1000000000). Mono shares IO.now's origin; IO.now remains unchanged in milliseconds. Negative or out-of-range Nat seconds fail-stop, as do native clock-read failures.
- Reuse the existing now.c / now.js effect sources. Conditional native registration supports clock-only and now-only builds. No checker, compiler, kernel or protected gate/cap changes.
- Document the contract at the Base API. GUIDE and the maintainer-owned release CHANGELOG are unchanged.

## Verification

- New meaningful regression tests/io/clock.bend prints `ok` on source CLI, emitted Node JS and native C. It checks normalization and that converted Mono falls between IO.now samples, rather than pinning a timestamp.
- 30 real consumer runs (10 per lane): Wall timestamps fall inside independent Python time.time_ns start/end brackets; Mono agrees with IO.now's bracket and both ns parts are normalized.
- Original IO.now regression passes on source/native/emitted Bun. The existing sleep-containing fixture cannot run under Node because it imports bun:ffi; no Node IO.sleep claim.
- Clock-only native and Node builds also run successfully.
- Actual --verdict on a reflexivity law plus an unused Base clock call: ALL PROOFS CHECK. This verifies the foreign-import limitation is avoided, not a mathematical proof of the host clock.
- Actual native binary with a throwaway clock_gettime injection: maximum Nat seconds / 999999999ns succeeds; negative/overflow seconds and syscall failure exit 1 with their respective errors. No system clock changed.
- Actual JS effect arithmetic in a throwaway timer-controlled context covers zero, second carry, fractional nanoseconds, epoch anchoring and range errors.
- Existing repository gate: PASS: 54 / 54.

## Limits

Linux x86_64 only; no mini-cluster, physical macOS/Windows or browser run claimed. Nanosecond representation does not promise nanosecond timer resolution. JavaScript Wall is epoch-anchored and does not follow later wall-clock adjustments; C Wall follows the host realtime clock.

AI-assisted: omp / GPT-6.1 Sol, working without subagents.

### Release-note policy

Removed my unreleased changelog entry following maintainer review. CHANGELOG.md is now unchanged from main; implementation and previously exercised verification are unchanged.

title: Array.q4mv on Metal: one kernel thread per row for products of 4M weights or more, bit-identical (stacked on #1431; over comp.ts cap)
body:
Stacked on #1431. Only the last commit is new here; the first is #1431's.

## Why

#1431 adds `Array.q4mv` on the CPU. An earlier revision of it also had a Metal kernel, which I removed to keep `comp.ts` small. Without it, a program that runs on Metal still does every 4-bit product on the host. For a 2B-parameter 4-bit model, the output head alone (248320x2048) costs about 30 ms per decode step on 8 CPU threads.

## Change

`bend2/comp.ts` only.

- When a Metal heap is live and a product has `n * cols >= 2^22` weights, the host hands it to a new kernel, `bend_q4mv`, instead of the CPU loop.
- The kernel runs one thread per row and adds in the Bend body's order, so every row keeps the body's bits.
- Each call commits its own command buffer and waits for it. Smaller products, and programs without a Metal heap, stay on the CPU loop.
- The kernel ships in the program's Metal library, so it needs a program that already builds one (one with a bang).

## Verification

Apple M1 Pro, macOS, GPU runs one at a time.

- `tests/base/array_q4mv.bend` passes on the interpreter, C `--gpu off`, C `--gpu 8GB` and JS. Its products are below the threshold, so the Metal lane still runs the CPU loop there.
- **A product above the threshold.** A scratch program builds a 4096x2048 product (8.4M weights), with a dead bang so the build carries Metal. It runs `Array.q4mv` 400 times and prints a hash of `y`'s bits. The hash is `1289093127` on #1431 (CPU and `--gpu 8GB`) and on this branch (CPU and `--gpu 8GB`). Six alternating rounds, milliseconds per call (the 400-call run minus the 1-call run, divided by 400):

  | | `--gpu off` | `--gpu 8GB` |
  |---|---|---|
  | #1431 | 2.28 | 2.29 (no kernel) |
  | this PR | 2.36 | 0.30 (0.27–0.50) |

  The Metal time includes a command buffer and a wait per call.
- **Model head.** In a microbench, the 248320x2048 head takes 5.44 ms on this kernel. In a Bend inference engine (TensorFold), the same head takes 30.7 ms on the CPU with 8 threads.
- **Whole model.** In that engine, Qwen3.5-2B (MLX 4-bit) greedy decode with this kernel gives the same token IDs and printed logits as the CPU. On its own it does not speed up decode: `--gpu 8GB` had a median of 127.5 ms/step over 6 pairs, and the CPU 127 in separate runs. Most products are below the threshold, and every GPU product waits on its own. #1436 and #1437 build on this.
- **Regression.** All 186 tests that upstream `60fa05dc` has in `tests/base` and `tests/io` give byte-identical interpreter, C and JS output on upstream and on #1437, the top of this stack. The only difference is the temp path in 21 JS build-error messages. 120 of 186 match their `#|` lines on both trees. The new q4 tests pass on all three lanes.

`uvx ttok@0.3 < bend2/comp.ts`: 64,660 (#1431) → 66,466 (+1,806).

## Limits / open

- **Over the `comp.ts` cap**, as #1431 is. See the question on #1431.
- One thread per row reads the weights strided, so the kernel stays well below memory bandwidth. #1436 replaces it with one SIMD group per row.
- The 4M-weight break-even is fixed. Each call pays about 0.25 ms of command-buffer overhead.
- Tested only on an M1 Pro. No CUDA path. Linux is untested.

title: Array.q4mv sums in a fixed tree order, so NEON and one Metal SIMD group per row keep the body's bits (stacked; over comp.ts cap)
body:
Stacked on #1431 and #1435. Only the last commit is new here.

## Why

`Array.q4mv`'s body adds each row's terms in index order: one dependent F32 chain per row. The CPU loop can only go wide across rows, and the Metal kernel from #1435 needs one thread per row, which reads the weights strided. A faster kernel has to add in a different order. To keep the same bits on every lane, the Bend body has to define that order.

## Change

The order (T32), for row `i` and group `g` (64 weights, code words `k = 0..7`, nibbles `j = 0..7`):

1. Lane `j`: `L_j = 0; for k in 0..7: L_j = L_j + q(k,j) * x[64g+8k+j]`. Each mul and add is rounded; there is no FMA.
2. `qx = ((L0+L4)+(L2+L6)) + ((L1+L5)+(L3+L7))`.
3. `t_g = scale_g*qx + bias_g*xsum_g`.
4. 32 partials: `p[l] = 0.0 + t_l + t_{l+32} + ...`, with groups in order.
5. Fold `p[l] += p[l+o]` for `o = 16, 8, 4, 2, 1`, then round `p[0]` to BF16 (nearest even).

- `bend2/base.bend`: the body and its doc follow T32.
- `bend2/comp.ts`:
  - a scalar row (`q4_row`) and a NEON loop that runs 4 rows at once (`q4_neon4`, under `__ARM_NEON`);
  - the Metal kernel uses one SIMD group per row, 8 rows per 256-thread group. Lane `l` owns groups `l, l+32, …`, and step 5 is `simd_shuffle_down`;
  - one bounds check is shared by the NEON and GPU paths.
- `tests/base/array_q4mv_tree.bend` (new):
  - a 5x2176 product: 34 groups, so the partials wrap;
  - rows 1..4 alone;
  - lane and fold cancellations at ±2^25 and ±2^24.

  The expected bits come from an independent C model of the order.

This changes results. After BF16 rounding, 1 of 6144, 1 of 2048 and 58 of 248320 rows differ from #1431's order on real weights. `array_q4mv.bend`'s expected lines do not change.

## Verification

Apple M1 Pro, macOS, GPU runs one at a time.

- `array_q4mv.bend` and `array_q4mv_tree.bend` pass on the interpreter, C `--gpu off`, C `--gpu 8GB` and JS.
- The new test catches the defects it should:
  - #1431's order fails it on all three lanes.
  - A NEON lane-pairing mutation fails only the C lane.
  - The C model's mutants (wrong lane meet, 16 partials, sequential fold, reversed fold) all differ.
- **Kernel microbench.** The Metal tree kernel, the NEON tree loop and the C reference are bit-identical at these shapes:
  - 13x128, with a 3-row offset tail;
  - 64x2048, 192x2048, 2048x2048 and 7760x2048;
  - 6144x2048, 2048x6144 and 248320x2048.

  All 18 AB/BA runs exited bit-exact.
- **Whole model.** In a Bend inference engine (TensorFold), Qwen3.5-2B (MLX 4-bit) gives bit-identical full logits on the CPU (NEON) and with `--gpu 8GB` (248,320 of 248,320). Greedy token IDs match the old order.
- The 4096x2048 scratch program from #1435 prints the same hash on CPU and Metal (`1289093127`). Six alternating rounds, milliseconds per call (400 calls, single-threaded host):

  | | `--gpu off` | `--gpu 8GB` |
  |---|---|---|
  | #1435 (index order) | 2.36 | 0.30 |
  | this PR | 1.09 | 0.21 |

- **Kernel microbench timings** (best of 10 reps, 3 AB/BA pairs, against #1435's kernels):

  | shape | Metal | CPU, 1 thread |
  |---|---|---|
  | 6144x2048 | 0.55 → 0.29 ms | 1.06–1.10x |
  | 2048x6144 | 0.74–0.91 → 0.22–0.35 ms | 1.09–1.17x |
  | 248320x2048 | 5.44 → 3.64 ms | 1.10x |

  On Metal each lane now reads 32 contiguous bytes, and the head reaches 78 GB/s.

The CPU gain differs between the two measurements: 2.2x in the 400-call program, but 1.06–1.17x in the microbench. I have not explained the difference. Treat the CPU gain as somewhere in that range. In the inference engine, CPU decode improved by about 4% (127 → 121.5 ms/step, 10 pairs), which is inside the noise.
- **Regression.** All 186 tests that upstream `60fa05dc` has in `tests/base` and `tests/io` give byte-identical interpreter, C and JS output on upstream and on #1437, the top of this stack. The only difference is the temp path in 21 JS build-error messages. 120 of 186 match their `#|` lines on both trees. The new q4 tests pass on all three lanes.

`uvx ttok@0.3 < bend2/comp.ts`: 66,466 (#1435) → 67,215 (+749).

## Limits / open

- **Over the `comp.ts` cap**, as #1431 is.
- This changes the documented order of a Base primitive, so the bits differ from #1431.
- The NEON path is arm64 only; other hosts use the scalar row.
- Tested only on an M1 Pro. No CUDA path.

title: Array.q4go/Array.q4wait queue Metal Q4 products in one command buffer and wait once on a flag (stacked; over comp.ts cap)
body:
Stacked on #1431, #1435 and #1436. Only the last commit is new here.

## Why

Each GPU `Array.q4mv` commits its own command buffer and waits for it. That costs about 0.23–0.27 ms of host time per product, whatever the size. One decode step of a 2B-parameter 4-bit model has 187 products in 97 dependent stages:

- **One wait per product:** 86.7 ms/token in a microbench of those 187 products.
- **GPU work alone:** 26–32 ms.

## Change

- `bend2/base.bend`:
  - `Array.q4go(w, x, y, r, n, cols, rows)` has the same body as `Array.q4mv`, so the interpreter and JS run it unchanged.
  - `Array.q4wait(x)` is `x`.
  - The doc states the lifetime rule.
- `bend2/comp.ts`:
  - **`q4go`:** in a native build with a Metal heap, `Array.q4go` encodes a product of any size into one open, concurrent command buffer and returns at once. Without a heap it runs `Array.q4mv`.
  - **`q4wait`:** `Array.q4wait` commits the buffer, ends it with a barrier and a 1-thread kernel that stores a sequence number in shared memory, and spins on that number. It falls back on the buffer's status. The flag saves about 0.27 ms per wait over `waitUntilCompleted`.
  - A program that calls `Array.q4go` loads its Metal library without needing a bang.
  - `BEND_Q4_TRACE=1` prints each wait's product count, GPU time and wall time.
- `tests/base/array_q4go.bend` (new): `array_q4mv.bend`'s 13x128 case through the queue. On the C `--gpu 8GB` lane it really queues, because `q4go` has no size threshold.

Queued products run concurrently, so none may read another's `y`. Put a wait between dependent stages. The GPU reads `w` and `x` and writes `y` until the wait, and Bend frees a value at its last use. So wait on `x`, and use `w` and `y` after the wait.

## Verification

Apple M1 Pro, macOS, GPU runs one at a time.

- `array_q4mv.bend`, `array_q4mv_tree.bend` and `array_q4go.bend` pass on the interpreter, C `--gpu off`, C `--gpu 8GB` and JS.
- **Negative controls:**
  - a build whose `Array.q4wait` returns without waiting dies with `bend: memory fault`;
  - a test that dropped `w` before the wait got a wrong row 0 every time. The runtime had freed `w` and written its free-list link into word 0, which the GPU then read. The doc now states the lifetime rule.
- **Per-call cost.** The 4096x2048 scratch program from #1435, with one `q4go` + `q4wait` per call, prints the same hash (`1289093127`) as `q4mv` on CPU and Metal. Six alternating rounds: 0.25 ms/call, against 0.36 for `q4mv`'s own command buffer. These runs are noisy.
- **Microbench of one decode step** (the 187 products of one token, a wait per stage, 10 tokens):
  - one wait per product: 86.7 ms/token;
  - one buffer per stage with `waitUntilCompleted`: 50.5–53.8 ms/token;
  - one buffer per stage with this PR's flag wait: 24.2–28.5 ms/token.
- **Whole model.** In a Bend inference engine (TensorFold), the CPU runs the forward pass and queues each stage's products with `q4go`, then waits once per stage before reading. Qwen3.5-2B (MLX 4-bit) greedy token IDs and logits equal the CPU run over 40 tokens.
  - Eight queued runs (four alternating pairs of two engine builds that differ only in argmax): 59–73 ms/step, median about 65.
  - Three CPU runs of the same builds: 89–113 ms/step.
  - That is about 15 tokens/s, against about 11 on the CPU.
- **Regression.** All 186 tests that upstream `60fa05dc` has in `tests/base` and `tests/io` give byte-identical interpreter, C and JS output on upstream and on #1437, the top of this stack. The only difference is the temp path in 21 JS build-error messages. 120 of 186 match their `#|` lines on both trees. The new q4 tests pass on all three lanes.

`uvx ttok@0.3 < bend2/comp.ts`: 67,215 (#1436) → 68,289 (+1,074).

## Limits / open

- **Over the `comp.ts` cap**, as #1431 is.
- **Coherence.** The flag wait relies on the CPU seeing a GPU store to shared memory after a device barrier. That held in every run on an M1, but the Metal documentation does not promise it. Deleting the spin falls back to `waitUntilCompleted`, at about 0.27 ms per wait.
- **Lifetime.** The rule is easy to break: drop `w` early and the GPU reads freed memory. A safer API would take the whole `((w, x), y)` at the wait.
- **Time between waits.** In the inference engine, the CPU work between waits (norms, recurrence, attention) still dominates: about 55–65 ms per step. Moving it to the GPU needs more queued kernels.
- Tested only on an M1 Pro. No CUDA path.

title: fix(runtime): release tail-drop frames before the last child
body:
Fixes #1307.

`term_drop` frees a node's frame before descending into its last live child, so recursive spines release cell by cell. Every child is still dropped once.

This keeps the maintainer's `6f7d462d` commit and merges main through `b869cca4` (including #1581); no history was replaced. The no-live case uses the ordinary frame, `cid_spine` is gone, and spine metadata comes from the constructor's own type. `lay_holds` reuses `lay_pack` instead of maintaining a second word-by-word union algorithm; the one-use spine calculation lives beside its CID row. Wide-node distances still use the actual layout width, not the encoded arity.

The frame-invariant comment remains, tightened to describe the shortened-wide-end case. The `BEND_POISON` note is unchanged. Related C declarations and address calculations are simplified; no code moved out of comp.ts.

### Current Linux checks

Linux x86-64, Clang 22.1.8:

- Five existing RFC fixtures (`drop_spine`, `drop_array_spine`, `drop_spine_flat`, `drop_spine_wide`, `drop_spine_wordless`), each compiled at `-O3` with and without `BEND_POISON`, then executed with 1 and 4 threads: **20 exact-output native checks passed** on the integrated head.
- Constructor metadata compared against the exact pre-simplification merged head on a bounded 200-fixture sample: **141 identical CID tables, 59 inputs refused C emission on both sides, no differences or timeouts**. This is not an exhaustive repository comparison.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **PASS: 54 / 54**. `comp.ts`: **63,998 / 64,000 ttok**, including main's new host declaration. Caps unchanged; no WONTFIX or release changelog edits.

The full test gate was attempted but could not resolve the private `cluster` SSH host, before any shard ran. The installer gate reports SKIP because the sibling site checkout is absent. No current-head macOS, CUDA/Metal, hub, cluster perf/safe, sanitizer or performance result is claimed. Earlier measurements and the maintainer's Mac qualification remain in the review history; they are not fresh Linux evidence.

title: Metal: a full lane stack spills to the heap, so non-tail recursion under ! no longer faults at 1023 frames (#1393, #1394)
body:
Fixes #1393. Fixes #1394. ## Why On the GPU, a `!` job dies with `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)` once a lane's stack fills. The same binary with `--gpu off` finishes. Two shapes hit it: - **#1393:** a bang's root that recurses non-tail (`List.append` over a list) faults at 1023 elements. - **#1394:** a fork tree with one long spine beside a short one (365 + 3) faults, while each spine alone passes. The limit is the same on CUDA (see the comment by @nuxyel): it hits at 3 + w × depth > 2048 words, where w is the number of words a level keeps. Both programs from the issues, built from upstream `60fa05dc` and from this branch, on an M1 Pro: | run | upstream, `--gpu off` | upstream, Metal | this PR, `--gpu off` | this PR, Metal | |---|---|---|---|---| | `deep 1022` | 521738 | 521738 | 521738 | 521738 | | `deep 1023` | 522760 | fault | 522760 | 522760 | | `deep 2048` | 2096135 | fault | 2096135 | 2096135 | | `deep 100000` | 704982711 | fault | 704982711 | 704982711 | | `deep 1000000` | 1783293671 | fault | 1783293671 | 1783293671 | | `lsum 2048` | 2096128 | fault | 2096128 | 2096128 | | `lsum 1000000` | 1783293664 | fault | 1783293664 | 1783293664 | | `forks 64 800 365` | 4280936846 | 4280936846 | 4280936846 | 4280936846 | | `forks 64 800 365 365` | 4266906396 | 4266906396 | 4266906396 | 4266906396 | | `forks 64 800 365 3` | 2063974529 | fault | 2063974529 | 2063974529 | | `forks 64 800 174 3` | 3985679902 | fault | 3985679902 | 3985679902 | | `forks 64 418 365 3` | 875539697 | fault | 875539697 | 875539697 | | `forks 64 800 365 3 3 3 3` | 4003022170 | fault | 4003022170 | 4003022170 | `lsum` is `deep` with a hand-written non-tail sum (`h + LSum(t)`) in place of `List.append`. Its source is at the end. ## How it failed A bang's root and a fork kid run on the lane's own `STAK_LEN`-word (2048) stack on the device, as `tests/compile/fork_leaf_budget.bend` says. A non-tail call pushes its continuation frame through `WL_ROOM`. When the next push would not fit, `WL_ROOM` posted `ERR_DEEP` and the lane returned. Nothing moved the frames anywhere else, so the depth limit was about 1022 frames of `List.append`. In #1394's unbalanced tree, a leaf job runs above a deeper fork spine on the same lane, so it gets less of the stack. ## Change `WL_ROOM(N, D)` now takes `D`, the number of words that the calling def holds on the stack (`emit_fork` passes `depth - ws.length`). When a push would overflow on `DEVICE`, it calls `lane_spill` instead of failing: 1. If the def's `D` words, the frame and a 3-word exit frame would not fit even on an empty stack (`d + n + 3 > STAK_LEN`), it returns 0 and `WL_ROOM` posts `ERR_DEEP` as before. This check comes before any heap block is taken. 2. Otherwise it copies the lane's stack to a heap block of `cls_fit(STAK_LEN)` words. 3. It rebuilds the bottom of the stack as one exit frame: the task word `term_tsk(FID_EXIT, b)` points at the block, the next word holds `k`, the number of words below the def's own, and the third word is `FID_EXIT`. 4. It copies the def's `D` words back above that frame with `WL_ARGS` and returns the new `sp`. The push then goes ahead on an almost empty stack. When a return reaches that frame, the `FID_EXIT` case in `work_loop` sees a continuation whose function id is `FID_EXIT`. It copies the `k` words back with `WL_ARGS`, frees the block and returns into the restored top frame. Spills nest, because each spilled block keeps the exit frame below it, so the depth is bounded by the heap. When the heap runs out, the run stops with the usual out-of-memory message (`--gpu 512MB`, 80,000,000 levels). The host lane is unchanged, because `WL_ROOM` only checks on `DEVICE`. `lane_spill` is `FAR`, so Metal emits one copy of it instead of inlining it at every `WL_ROOM` site. An earlier version inlined it: symreg's `.gpu` grew from 220 KB to 283 KB, and the COMPILER column of the perf gate failed (symreg 1.24x, merkle 1.17x). `tests/compile/bang_lane_spill.bend` covers: - `deep!(5000n)`: one bang's root, 5001 `List.append` frames (#1393). - `two!(365n)`: a 365-fork spine beside a 3-fork spine (#1394). - `pair!(600n)`: the first spill happens at a fork call where the def still holds two words on the stack (`D > 0`), so a build that drops those words fails it. On main, its compiled run faults on the GPU. ## Verification **Merged onto main `cece1cbf`, Apple M4 Pro and the mini cluster:** - `repo` PASS: 54 / 54. `bend2/comp.ts` is 65,723 ttok, under the 66,000 cap (main is 65,424, so +299). - `test` PASS: 1693 / 1693. - `ping` PASS: 63 / 63. - `safe`: 1098 agree, 0 false rejects, 0 timeouts. - `perf` PASS: 124 / 124, the same as main. No bench fills a lane, so no spill runs, and every runtime cell is within noise of main. In the COMPILER column, symreg is 1.14x on this branch against 1.09x on main, and merkle 1.15x against 1.11x. - `deep!(1000000n)` (`deep(p) + 1`) prints 1000000 on Metal, the same as `--gpu off`. **CUDA:** @nuxyel built 6764c339 on an RTX 4050 (CUDA 12.9). It runs every depth past the old limit with the CPU's results, up to `deep!(100000n)`, and the two loop kernels they time run at the same speed. **Earlier, by @totaland, on an M1 Pro against upstream `60fa05dc`:** every test in `tests/` gave byte-identical output on both trees (interpreter, compiled and JS), except the new test's compiled lane, which faults upstream. The Metal benches (mandelbrot, tree-matmul, tree-bitonic, nbody) were within noise. ## Limits - **Spill cost:** a spill copies up to `STAK_LEN` words to the heap and back. A loop of calls at exactly the depth where the stack fills spills and restores the whole stack on every call: 100,000 calls there take 24.7 s, against 0.27 s one frame shallower. Main faults at that depth, so this is not a regression. Avoiding it would need a partial restore. - **Not tested:** Apple GPUs other than the M1 Pro and M4 Pro.
lsum.bend ```python import Base def Gen(n: Nat, +k: U32, acc: List<&2, U32>) -> List<&2, U32>: match n: case 0n: acc case 1n+p: Gen(p, (k + 1 : U32), k <> acc) # Non-tail sum: one frame per element. def LSum(xs: List<&2, U32>) -> U32: match xs: case Nil{}: 0 case Con{h, t}: (h + LSum(t) : U32) def Run(m: Maybe<&2, U32>) -> IO(Unit): match m: case Some{n}: IO.print(U32.show(LSum!(Gen(U32.to_nat(n), 0, [])))) case None{}: IO.die(Unit, 2, "usage: lsum ") def Args(args: List) -> IO(Unit): match args: case Con{_, Con{n, _}}: Run(U32.read(n)) case _: IO.die(Unit, 2, "usage: lsum ") def main() -> IO(Unit): do IO: args : List <- IO.args() Args(args) ```

title: Metal: queued rmsq, swq, gdn and atq kernels and a 4-row q4mv, so a decode token is one command buffer with one wait
body:
Stacked on #1431, #1435, #1436 and #1437. Only the last commit is new here.

## Why

With #1437, a model's Q4 products can share one Metal command buffer, but everything between them (norms, activations, recurrent and attention mixers) still runs on the CPU. So a decode step still has one wait per dependent stage. For Qwen3.5-2B (MLX 4-bit) that is 97 waits per token, and the GPU idles between short command buffers, which also makes the products themselves 2–3× slower than when they run back to back.

This PR adds the missing per-token kernels as queued intrinsics, so the whole token can be encoded into one command buffer and waited on once.

## Change

New Base intrinsics in `bend2/base.bend`. Each has a pure Base body that defines its meaning (the interpreter and JS run it), a C twin in `bend2/comp.ts` that follows the body's order, and a Metal kernel that is queued like `Array.q4go`: barriers on both sides, and the result is ready after the next `Array.q4wait`. Without a Metal heap, each runs its C twin at once.

- `Array.rmsq`: RMS norm with weights as `Array<U32>` (F32 bits), plus the 64-value group sums that `Array.q4mv` reads. The Metal kernel sums with `simd_sum` trees in one threadgroup.
- `Array.swq(a, o, n)`: SwiGLU, `round(silu(a[i]) * a[n + i])`, plus the group sums. One SIMD group per 64-value group.
- `Array.gdn(...)`: one token of a gated DeltaNet mixer: conv window and activation, q/k L2 norms, decay and beta, the delta-rule rows, the gated norm and group sums. One threadgroup per value head; every phase is local to its head, so there is no cross-threadgroup sync.
- `Array.atq(...)`: one token of gated attention over GPU-resident key and value caches: q/k RMS norm and rotation, the new k/v into the caches, scores, softmax, weighted values, sigmoid gate and group sums. One threadgroup per query head. The first head of each KV group writes the cache row; the others use the new k/v from threadgroup memory, so no head reads a row another head writes in the same dispatch. Metal handles positions below 4096 (`ATQ_MAX`); past that the C twin runs at once on the CPU, so the caller must wait first.
- `bend_q4mv`: a SIMD group now does 4 rows and reads each group's 64 activations once for all of them. Each row's arithmetic and reduction tree are unchanged from #1436, so it stays bit-identical to the Bend body.
- `tpl` in `comp.ts` now reads `$10` and up (`/\$(\d+)/`). Before, `$10` was split into `$1` followed by `0`. No upstream intrinsic has 10 or more arguments, so this only shows with `gdn` and `atq`.
- Tests (new): `tests/base/array_rmsq.bend`, `array_swq.bend`, `array_gdn.bend`, `array_atq.bend`.

`q4mv`, `rmsq` and the plumbing are exact. `swq`, `gdn` and `atq` are not bit-identical on Metal: Metal's `exp`, its summation order and fused multiply-adds move the last bits. `array_gdn.bend` prints its state rounded to bfloat16 for that reason (Metal moves the last F32 bit of 5 of its 64 values).

## Verification

Apple M1 Pro, macOS 26, GPU runs one at a time.

- The four new tests and `array_q4mv.bend`, `array_q4mv_tree.bend`, `array_q4go.bend` pass on the interpreter, C `--gpu off`, C `--gpu 8GB` (Metal) and JS against their `#|` lines.
- **Regression.** All 186 tests that upstream `60fa05dc` has in `tests/base` and `tests/io` give byte-identical interpreter, C and JS output on upstream and on this branch (temp paths in JS build-error messages normalized). 120 of 186 match their `#|` lines on both trees. The 7 new Q4/kernel tests pass on all three lanes.
- **Whole model.** In a Bend inference engine (TensorFold), one decode token of Qwen3.5-2B (MLX 4-bit) is now one command buffer: 194 kernels, about 9.4 ms of GPU time, one wait. Measured with these commits on a local build that also carries #1430, #1433 and #1439:
  - Greedy token IDs equal the CPU forward at every step over 40 and 200 tokens, and with the model state swapped out and back before every step. Max absolute logit difference: 0.234 over 40 tokens, 2.19 over 200. With the GPU off, the fused path is bit-identical to the CPU path.
  - Two sessions decoded in turn on one model each match their solo runs.
  - Four alternating pairs, previous queued path (#1437) vs this one: 66/11, 60/11, 63/11, 65/11 ms per decode step. A/A pairs: 11/11, 11/11.
- **4-row product kernel.** With CPU work still between the waits it made no difference (24 vs 24 ms/token, 4 pairs). Once the GPU stayed busy for the whole token it gave 12 vs 18–19 ms/token (4/4 pairs). 2 and 8 rows were no better.

`uvx ttok@0.3 < bend2/comp.ts`: 68,289 (#1437) → 78,654 (+10,365). Most of it is the C twins of `gdn` and `atq`.

## Limits / open

- **Far over the `comp.ts` cap** (64,000), like the rest of this stack. I'd welcome direction on whether model-specific kernels like `gdn` and `atq` belong in the compiler at all, or whether a smaller set of generic queued primitives would be preferred.
- **Not bit-exact on Metal** for `swq`, `gdn` and `atq` (see above). Greedy outputs matched in every run, but logits drift.
- **Lifetime.** As with `q4go`, every array the GPU reads or writes must stay alive until `Array.q4wait`; nothing in the types enforces it.
- **`atq` past 4096 positions** falls back to the CPU; that path is implemented but was not exercised (runs stopped at 205 positions).
- Tested only on an M1 Pro. No CUDA path.

title: feat(window): emit native text input events
body:
Closes #1019.

## Change

- Add `Text{text: String}` to native window events. `Key` keeps its original canonical codes; text follows key-down when the OS supplies characters.
- Linux: use a per-window XIM/XIC and `Xutf8LookupString`, preserving the original event before the legacy key-code lookup changes its modifiers. Focus and input-context resources follow the window lifetime. A missing UTF-8 context returns `ENOTSUP` instead of silently offering partial text input.
- macOS: enqueue UTF-8 from `NSEvent.characters` without lowercasing.
- Copy text into the existing event queue, not separately allocated C strings; decode mixed fixed/variable-size events in arrival order.
- Update the exhaustive game proof consumer and document the native text API.

## Exercised verification

Actual native Linux window on an isolated X11 display, not mocked events:

- Shift+A → A; Shift+1 → !; Caps Lock+A → A; Cyrillic Ж and emoji 🙂 retained. Text follows key-down; modifier/release events do not create extra text.
- Three-byte 你, four-byte 🙂, then 512 ASCII characters injected at zero delay: all 514 text events retained under AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and leak detection; exit 0, no diagnostics.
- Rebuilt the unchanged key-only consumer: its original 14 ASCII/modifier Key rows exactly match the pre-change runtime; Cyrillic, Chinese and emoji text is safely dropped under the same sanitizers.
- Existing headless native window behavior still reports ENOTSUP.
- Existing App.play program on native and Node: unchanged frame/state/quit output (7, quit, 7).
- Unchanged repository gate: **54/54**.
- Game proof check before/after reports the same four imported unsafe/foreign definitions (Play.loop, Play.run, Main.mode, main); no whole-proof pass is claimed.

## Limits

macOS code was not built or exercised on this Linux workstation. This does not implement full IME editing (#1022). JavaScript native windows remain unsupported as before.


### Release-note policy

Removed my unreleased changelog entry following maintainer review. CHANGELOG.md is now unchanged from main; implementation and previously exercised verification are unchanged.

title: perf(io): index parked descriptor waiters and timers
body:
## Status: draft — protected compiler budget decision required

Addresses #1250. This is **not merge-ready and not counted as a completed issue**: `gates/repo.ts` reports **53 / 54** because `bend2/comp.ts` is **67,176 ttok**, above its permanent **64,000** cap. Unchanged main `60fa05dc28f847382554dae6ee76cd1b2911bcc3` is **63,905 ttok**. The implementation adds 3,271 tokens; the excess is 3,176. `AGENTS.md` reserves budget changes to Taelin. I have not edited the gate/cap, split the compiler to evade it, deleted unrelated functionality, or bypassed a hook.

The issue mentions an existing working branch. Please point me to that intended implementation/integration boundary if this overlaps it; otherwise a maintainer budget decision is required before this can be made ready.

## Change

- Replace per-pass traversal of parked descriptors with persistent level-triggered epoll (Linux) / kqueue (macOS), indexed descriptor read/write waiter rings and indexed deadline/ready heaps.
- Preserve deadline and registration ordering, multiple waiters sharing one FD, re-parking, interrupted waits, worker wakeups and channel timer cancellation. Both parked and already-ready timer records remain removable before their storage is freed.
- JS uses dynamic numeric-FD Map/Set membership, retained poll buffers/views and a cancellation token; channel wakeups remove the timer directly instead of searching all parked requests.
- No per-descriptor native allocation: inline hash rows grow geometrically; an existing descriptor or reusable tombstone does not trigger an unnecessary resize.
- Remove obsolete select bindings/macros and update the interruption comments and existing runtime-paper source. No release changelog edit: maintainers own release commits.

## Actual Linux runtime qualification

Sixteen existing public IO programs were compiled and run natively and under Bun: timers/order, EINTR, spawned TCP connections, queued-accept fairness, receive/send deadlines, bytes and validation errors, EOF, UDP readiness, listener close, channel timeouts/close, concurrent Process.run/EOF and IO.within under a busy pipeline.

**31 / 32 program-lane checks pass.** The untouched native `chan_try_late.bend` fails identically on the unchanged baseline and this branch: `B: 767263360`, `S: sent`, `A: ready got 7`, then `bend: deadlock: every computation waits on a channel`. Its baseline and indexed Bun runs both pass with the original expected output. I have not suppressed, altered or presented the native baseline failure as passing.

New `poll_shared_fd` regression uses a real socketpair: two waiters share its readable FD, the first consumes `a` and re-parks, the second must consume `b`, and the first's next wake consumes `c`. Exact ordering/re-arming and completion pass on both baseline/final native and Bun backends. The final native consumer also passes ASan + UBSan with leak detection, output `3`, exit 0 and empty diagnostics.

## Actual serial-arrival scaling

A real writer thread/worker sends one byte to each watched socket and waits for acknowledgement before the next arrival; all remaining connections stay parked. Construction is outside the timed interval. Three interleaved before/after samples per size and backend; every sample completes every arrival. Median milliseconds on this Linux x86_64 host, not a universal performance claim:

| Backend | Watched connections | Baseline ms | Indexed ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Native | 128 | 1.297 | 0.975 |
| Native | 512 | 9.179 | 3.878 |
| Native | 2,048 | 103.133 | 16.229 |
| Native | 4,096 | 389.531 | 33.236 |
| Bun | 128 | 3.378 | 2.327 |
| Bun | 512 | 17.880 | 7.114 |
| Bun | 2,048 | 180.321 | 23.106 |
| Bun | 4,096 | 606.121 | 50.065 |

## Limits / review boundary

- Protected repository gate is **failing**, for the budget above; readiness awaits the maintainer decision. No green-full-gate claim.
- macOS kqueue code is implemented but has not been built or exercised on this Linux workstation.
- Mini-cluster test/perf gates and hosted CI are not claimed; the local real consumer results above are the exercised evidence.
- Existing native late-channel fixture failure is disclosed and unchanged. No interpreter/native effect parity claim beyond the exercised backends.

AI-assisted: omp / GPT-6.1 Sol, working alone without subagents.

title: feat(window): preserve logical rendering resolution in native fullscreen
body:
Adds `Window.fullscreen(window, on)` for #923. The window stays outside `Result`, so a refused request doesn't lose the handle. `Done` acknowledges the request, not the completed desktop animation; `Window.frame` keeps that moving.

The image keeps its logical size in fullscreen, with nearest-neighbour scaling and black bars. Mouse and grabbed-look coordinates stay in logical units. Ordinary windows still draw unscaled.

Checked af69e466 with a real X11/Openbox app, real queued XTest input, a build that deliberately rejects Xrender.h, and the repo gate (54/54). [The macOS 15 Cocoa run](https://github.com/oxura/bend/actions/runs/39868956760) also passes normal enter/exit, failure/ignored-toggle/scale cases, state restoration, and close during started enter/exit transitions. Fullscreen and restored-window screenshots were inspected on both platforms.

Failure, scale and delayed-notification cases are controlled OS-boundary injections, not naturally failing AppKit or physical Retina migration. No mini-cluster, Metal/CUDA throughput or ASan/UAF claim for this revision.

title: fix(safe): reuse checked definitions as opaque models
body:
## Problem

The original reproducer in #1182 defines a closed injectivity proof (`inj`), but the opaque `use~F` still has no model. Constructor, reflexivity, and projection models cannot construct that proof themselves.

This implements the checked-definition lookup direction requested in https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1263#issuecomment-6045064743. It does not restore the rejected backtracking implementation.

## Change

- Preserve the existing model builders and their precedence.
- If those builders fail, look through the checked book for a definition with a body, no template parameters, no `@unsafe` marker, and a definitionally equal type.
- Use a reference to that definition as the model. It remains an ordinary emitted dependency: the native BendTT kernel checks its body, rather than trusting its signature.
- Add a proof regression whose witness is declared after the generic root and whose `main` actually calls `use(~inj, ...)` to return an equality proof.
- Document the witness requirement in the BendTT paper. No parser/checker, kernel, gate, or cap changes.

## Verification

- The unchanged public `higher_evidence_base.bend` reproducer passes both `--check-only` and `--verdict` with the canonical Lean 4.34.0 BendTT kernel.
- The new forward-witness regression fails `--verdict` on untouched main (`8578b7cb`, `no model for use~F`) and passes with this change. Running it prints `{==}`.
- Baseline/treatment comparison across all 94 existing `tests/proof/*.bend` files: identical frontend classifications, out-of-scope reports, native-kernel results, and export hashes. All 61 previously emitted books are byte-identical. The new fixture adds one complete kernel certificate: 59 existing certificates become 60, with no existing outcome changed.
- `model_false.bend` and `model_no_base.bend` remain outside the translation's scope.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **PASS: 54 / 54**, including the staged new fixture and the unchanged 24k `safe.ts` cap.
- The edited BendTT paper builds with Typst.
- TypeScript 5.9.3 full-project checking is **not green**: untouched main and this branch both produce the same 12 diagnostics, ignoring shifted source locations. No new diagnostics; no suppression or unrelated repair.

## Scope and limits

This fixes the original reported case where the book contains a closed witness. It is not a general proof-search or mutually dependent model-selection change.

The public `law_higher_evidence_probe.bend` has no closed witness and still reports `no model for use~F`. The public `dependent_empty_result_probe.bend` also remains rejected; its opaque function would have to return an empty value at `Z`. Both were exercised explicitly, not treated as complete certificates merely because a partial book can be exported.

The separate `v_n` / bend-mathlib model-choice case from the issue comments is not claimed fixed. This PR intentionally does not auto-close that broader issue thread.

The proof comparison ran locally against the actual native kernel, not on the mini-cluster. The cluster gates were unavailable in the preceding qualification because the bastion hostname did not resolve; no gate was bypassed.

title: File writes do not terminate on zero progress
body:
### Nonempty file writes can spin indefinitely after a zero-byte host write

On current main `8578b7cbf2a7944218b750dcb62bd917babe5994`, both `File.write` and `File.write_bytes` use loops that advance only by the returned byte count:

- C: `bend2/effs/file_write.c`, `file_write_call`: the loop permits `n >= 0`, so `write(..., remaining) == 0` leaves `at` unchanged.
- JS: `bend2/effs/file_write.js`, `file_write_buffer`: `at += fs.writeSync(...)` likewise has no zero-progress exit.

A descriptor-scoped fault-injection fixture opens a real temporary file, allows a real seven-byte short write, then makes the next nonempty host write return zero. The other descriptors, including stdout/stderr, are unaffected. With a one-off zero return, all three tested consumers (native C, Bun CLI, and emitted standalone JS under Node) retry and incorrectly report success. With subsequent writes kept at zero, all three exceed an explicit two-second deadline (exit 124).

This is an injected host-return edge case, **not** a claim that a normal disk spontaneously produced it. The unchanged positive writes go through the real filesystem.

### Expected behavior

For a nonempty remaining buffer, stop on zero progress and return `EIO` (5), retaining the `File` handle outside the `Result`. Already-written bytes must remain available, and the caller must be able to recover using the returned handle. Empty text/byte writes should still succeed. Positive short writes should still be completed. Existing negative-error behavior should remain unchanged.

The incoming regression fixture exercises binary bytes (including NUL and values above 127), UTF-8 text, empty writes, the actual written prefix, and recovery with the returned handle. I will link the ready fix and executable reproduction here once published. No syscall retry policy, compiler budget, or gate changes are needed.

title: fix(io): fail file writes on zero progress
body:
Closes #1445.

`File.write` and `File.write_bytes` loop until every byte is written, moving on by the count the host returns. If the host returns 0 with bytes left, the loop never ends. Both the C loop (`effs/file_write.c`) and the JS loop (`effs/file_write.js`) now fail with `EIO` (5) when that happens. The handle still comes back outside the `Result`. Empty writes, short writes that make progress and existing errors (`ENOSPC`, `EFBIG`, ...) behave as before.

Test: `tests/io/file_write_zero.bend` opens `/dev/null` through a test effect whose nonempty writes all return 0, and checks that `File.write` and `File.write_bytes` give 5 and that an empty write still succeeds. On main it hangs in C, bun and the interpreter.

title: GPU bangs chain their rounds on the device, three command buffers in flight
body:
## Why

A bang runs in rounds. Every time a stage's joins finish and the next stage forks, that is a new round. On main each round goes back to the host: `cube_run` reads the frontier (`H_CURSOR`), picks which passes to launch from its size, commits one command buffer and waits. So the GPU sits idle for a full host round trip on every dependent stage.

#1431, #1435, #1436 and #1437 ran into this with a 4-bit matvec for LLM decoding (about 97 dependent stages per token). They worked around it with format-specific kernels and a `q4go`/`q4wait` queue. This PR removes the round trip in the runtime, so it works for any bang.

## Change

`bend2/comp.ts` only.

- **The device picks the next round.** The pack (pass 2), which is the last pass of a round, also takes the next frontier. Lane 0 swaps `H_CURSOR` into `H[H_FRONT]` and writes the group count for each of the five dispatches at `H_GROUPS` (`turn_set`). These are the same rules `gpu_run` used to apply on the host (`turn_groups`). A `typedef` check makes sure both fields fit before `H_ROOT_DONE`.
- **Metal:** each pass is an indirect dispatch from those counts, so a pass with no work launches no groups. Each round gets its own command buffer, with three in flight (`GPU_DEEP`). They are chained by one static `MTLEvent` whose value keeps going up, and each has its own autorelease pool. The host stops queueing once it reads an empty frontier from the heap it was given, then waits for the buffers still in flight. Rounds queued after the frontier empties dispatch nothing. There is no batch size and no timing rule, and nothing carries over between bangs.
- **CUDA:** each bang launches 1, 2, 4 … 64 rounds between syncs until the frontier is empty, starting from 1 every bang. Every kernel gets its dispatch slot `at` and returns at once when `turn_groups(H[H_FRONT], at)` says there is no work. This replaces the inverted pass→slot formula. `TURN_ROWS(at)` is the one group-size rule, shared by `turn_groups` and the CUDA launch.
- The host reads the cursor once, when the bang starts. The CPU path is unchanged.

## Measurements

PAR-GPU on the cluster, from `gates/perf.ts` (one Mac mini per cell, the gate's own build and timing). Main is `8f86f735`, the PR is `1ac32994`. Each side ran the gate once. Outputs match on every bench.

| bench | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| mandelbrot | 0.069 s | 0.060 s | 0.87x |
| tree-bitonic | 1.766 s | 1.582 s | 0.90x |
| histogram | 1.497 s | 1.375 s | 0.92x |
| nbody | 0.061 s | 0.057 s | 0.93x |
| merkle | 0.078 s | 0.073 s | 0.94x |
| kmeans | 0.682 s | 0.644 s | 0.94x |
| gameoflife | 0.084 s | 0.080 s | 0.95x |
| editdist | 0.511 s | 0.488 s | 0.95x |
| tree-matmul | 0.910 s | 0.882 s | 0.97x |
| raytrace | 0.267 s | 0.260 s | 0.97x |
| queens | 2.300 s | 2.260 s | 0.98x |
| symreg | 0.585 s | 0.577 s | 0.99x |
| tree-radix | 1.131 s | 1.118 s | 0.99x |
| lexer | 2.640 s | 2.620 s | 0.99x |
| bfs | 0.904 s | 0.904 s | 1.00x |
| hashmap | 1.235 s | 1.239 s | 1.00x |
| terrain | 0.313 s | 0.314 s | 1.00x |

- No bench is slower than main, and every cell is under its pin.
- SEQ-CPU and PAR-CPU are unchanged (0.99–1.00x).
- PAR-GPU memory goes up by about 0.3–0.5 MB per bench (for example 13.9M to 14.4M), which is about 3%. Every cell stays within its limit.
- Checker benches match main: compute 0.92x, defs 1.03x, generics 1.13x (main reads 1.11x on the same gate), proofs 0.98x, trees 1.04x.
- The number of command buffers in flight was picked on an Apple M4 desktop: 2 in flight was about the same as main, 3 was faster, and 4 or 8 did no better than 3.

## Gates

At `1ac32994`, on top of `648e4456`: repo 54/54, ping 61/61, test 1655/1655 and perf 124/124 (test and perf run on the cluster). `comp.ts` is 64,885 ttok, under its 66,000 cap.

## Not tested

- **CUDA:** no CUDA machine was available, and the CUDA path has not even been compiled. Changed there: the kernel takes a third argument `at`, the launch uses `TURN_ROWS(at)`, and `gpu_pass` doubles from 1 each bang.
- Linux and the hub were not run.

## Notes

- A lookup table inside `turn_groups` (`u32 g[5]`, indexed at runtime) made queens 8% and lexer 4% slower on the GPU, so it stays written as conditionals. The slot→pass table `{0, 0, 1, 3, 2}` exists only in `gpu_run`.
- Metal has no device-side frontier check. A pass with no work already has an indirect count of 0.

title: IO.get_env on Node truncates names at embedded NUL
body:
## Bug

`IO.get_env` on the emitted Node lane treats an embedded NUL as the end of an environment-variable name. The native C and Bun lanes reject that name with `Fail(ENOENT)` instead. This reads a different variable than the caller named.

## Reproducer

On main `8578b7c`, with HOME set (as required by the existing `tests/io/get_env.bend` fixture):

```bend
import Base

def report(tag: String, r: Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match r:
    case Done{value}:
      IO.print(String.append(tag, "=set"))
    case Fail{error}:
      (code, message) = error
      IO.print(String.append(tag, String.append("=error:", U32.show(code))))

def main() -> IO(U32):
  do IO<U32>:
    exact : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), String> <- IO.get_env("HOME")
    a : Unit <- report("exact", exact)
    nul : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), String> <- IO.get_env("HOME\0suffix")
    b : Unit <- report("nul", nul)
    return 0
```

Emit a standalone `.js` and run it with Bun and Node; emit `.c`, compile with clang and run with `--threads 1 --gpu off`.

Observed actual Bend output:

| Lane | Exact `HOME` | `HOME\0suffix` |
|---|---|---|
| C | `exact=set` | `nul=error:2` |
| Bun | `exact=set` | `nul=error:2` |
| Node | `exact=set` | **`nul=set`** |

## Cause / expected behavior

`get_env.c` already checks `io_nul(name, n)`. `get_env.js` relies on `Object.hasOwn(process.env, name)`, but Node's environment proxy truncates at NUL even for its own-property check. A direct host control with an owned sentinel key confirms `Object.hasOwn(process.env, key + "\0suffix") === true` on Node and false on Bun.

Reject NUL-containing names before asking the host environment, preserving the existing ENOENT result and exact-name / own-property semantics. No change to valid environment values, host FFI support, or error-code policy is needed.

Duplicate search for `get_env` found no matching open issue or PR (the closed #809 UTF-8 decoding report is a different boundary).

title: fix(io): get_env rejects a name with an embedded NUL
body:
## Problem

Closes #1449.

`IO.get_env` on the emitted Node lane treated an embedded NUL as the end of an environment-variable name. `get_env.c` already rejects such a name with `io_nul` before asking the host environment, so the C and Bun lanes answer `Fail(ENOENT)`. Node's environment proxy instead truncates the key, so `"HOME\0suffix"` answered `Done` with `HOME`'s value: the call read a variable the caller never named, on one lane only.

Confirmed here against `main` at `8578b7c`, with the reproducer from the issue and the lanes run on Node and Bun:

| Lane | Exact `HOME` | `HOME\0suffix` (before) | `HOME\0suffix` (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node | `Done` | **`Done`** | `Fail(ENOENT)` |
| Bun | `Done` | `Fail(ENOENT)` | `Fail(ENOENT)` |

## Change

- `bend2/effs/get_env.js`: reject a name containing `\0` with the same `io_fail(2)` the unset path already returns, before asking `process.env`. This matches `get_env.c`'s `io_nul(name, n) ? NULL : getenv(name)` guard, so the lanes agree.
- `tests/io/get_env_nul.bend`: a new `io` test pinning `HOME=set` and `nul=unset`.

Valid names, host FFI support, own-property semantics and the error-code policy are unchanged: the guard only fires on a name no lane can look up.

## Verification

```
$ node out.js   # before the fix
HOME=set
nul=set         # wrong: read HOME through a name the caller never used

$ node out.js   # after the fix
HOME=set
nul=unset

$ bun run out.js
HOME=set
nul=unset

$ bun run bend2/main.ts tests/io/get_env_nul.bend   # native lane

nul=unset
```

title: A flat generic def takes a record in words where its result does (#1195)
body:
Closes #1195.

## Problem

A flat generic def (e.g. `pick(-A: Type, c: Bool, a: A, b: A) -> A`) called at a record of scalars (e.g. `Tint{r, g, b: F32}`) had one generic `Fun` whose `A` parameters are boxed. Every call heap-allocated the record and the spin unboxed it again, so a linear function allocated even though it creates nothing.

## Change

- `fun_of(k, ers)` builds a def's `Fun` from its erased arguments. It specializes whenever the layout of **any** parameter or of the result changes, not only the result. If no layout changes, it reuses the generic `Fun`. So consume-only defs (`drop2(-A, x: A, y: A, k)`) and loops (`keep(-A, +n, x: A)`, `last`) take the record in words and never box it.
- `lay_key` keys erased **types** by their layout and erased **values** (`-n: Nat`, `-F: Nat -> Data`) by their term. `by_n(0n, ..)` and `by_n(1n, ..)` get separate spins, so a type computed from the value (`Sel(n)`, `F(A)`) gets its own layout instead of sharing the first call's.
- In a specialized spin, a self-call whose erased arguments keep the same layouts jumps (`WL_AGAIN`) as before. A self-call that changes them (polymorphic recursion such as `grow(A & U32, ..)` or `flip(B, A, ..)`) cannot jump into the same loop. It calls the def's generic spin instead, whose self-calls can always jump. The generic segment and generic spin always jump with the generic layouts, as on main.
- A non-flat def that is inlined at its only call site keeps the generic `Fun` (as on main), so values passed on to closures are not re-boxed.
- `lay_at`: a binder whose type is still open (a type variable or a stuck application like `F(A)`) keeps the layout its value arrived in.

## Results (M4 Pro, on main 25233fbf)

| repro | record alloc sites in C, main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| issue #1195 (F32 Tint tree) | 1 | 0 |
| `keep` loop over a Tint | 1 | 0 |
| `drop2` consume-only | 4 | 0 |
| `by_n` at 0n/1n (Two/Tint) | 2 | 0 |

- Output is the same on interp, JS, C and Metal `--gpu on` for all repros. That includes the polymorphic self-calls (`grow`, `flip`), where the earlier version of this PR built broken C.
- On all 775 test files that compile, 89 change their C and none gains a heap_alloc site (4,487 → 4,364 across them). Bytes go from 11,242,969 to 11,187,988. 21 files grow by 3–720 B, from extra spins per erased value (e.g. `convoy_dependent`) or the generic spin for polymorphic recursion.
- `tests/compile/generic_flat_record.bend` covers pick/swap/head/last, `keep`, `drop2`, `by_n`/`by_f`/`wrap` at different values, `grow` and `flip`.

Gates on main 25233fbf + this PR: repo 54/54 (`bend2/comp.ts` 63,963 ttok, main 63,474), test 1636/1636, ping 58/58, safe 0 false rejects, perf 124/124. One perf run hit tree-bitonic 1.32x on byte-identical C and the next two passed 124/124. CUDA, Linux and Windows are untested.

title: --check-only doesn't re-check the modules an earlier run checked (#1234)
body:
Closes #1234.

`bend f.bend --check-only` re-checks the whole import closure on every run. On the issue's repro, almost all of a client's time is re-checking lib.bend's 800 proofs (~650 ms here); parsing is ~20 ms and the client's own law <1 ms. Within one run nothing is checked twice already; the waste is every new run re-checking what an earlier run already checked.

With this PR, `--check-only` doesn't re-check a module an earlier run already checked. It is on by default.

How it works:

- Each module gets a key: a hash of the checker (version, binary identity, or bend.ts/main.ts in a dev checkout), the keys of Base and of the module's imports, and the module's parsed events. So editing a module invalidates it and everything that imports it.
- A module with no `import Base`, with a law filled in another module, or with a forward reference gets no key and is always checked.
- After a passing check, the keys of the newly checked modules are written to `~/.bend/checked` (`BEND_CACHE=<dir>` picks another dir, `BEND_CACHE=off` turns it off). A failed check writes nothing.
- bend.ts: `book_valid(book, done)` now also takes a set of names as `done`. The modules whose key is already recorded (and whose deps' are) are passed in that set: their bodies still unfold in place, they just aren't checked again. The load order is unchanged.
- `--check-only` only. `--verdict`, `-o` and plain runs are unchanged.

Timings (M4 Pro):

| | main | this PR, cold | this PR, warm |
|---|---|---|---|
| issue repro, 10 clients | 6.6 s | | 0.54 s |
| one client | 620-760 ms | 760 ms | 50 ms |

On a project with varied imports (20 libs, 50 clients, 5 random imports each): no cache 11.1 s, first pass 3.4 s, second pass 2.6 s. Editing or breaking one lib re-checks only it and fails exactly the 12 clients that import it.

Checks:

- Invalidation scenarios (broken proof, comment-only edit, added def, added `@unsafe` def must still fail `--check-only`'s promise check, both import orders, PROOF/LAWS, a lib seen from a subdir): same results as without the cache.
- gates/ping.ts: +4 checks (a checked import is skipped, an edited one is re-checked, an import loaded after another is warm too). They fail on main.
- Gates on main 3f80b064 + this PR: repo 54/54, test 1597/1597, ping 52/52 (48 + 4 new), perf 124/124. safe not run (no local bendtt binary).
- Tokens: main.ts 10,932 → 13,083 (cap 16k), bend.ts 43,759 → 43,799 (cap 48k).

Open points:

1. Anyone who can write `~/.bend/checked` can make `--check-only` pass (not `--verdict`).
2. Entries are never removed.
3. This edits gates/ping.ts.
