title: IO: an invalid descriptor aborts the readiness loop instead of returning EBADF
fix(io): resume invalid descriptor operations after EBADF
body:
## Current-head review qualification

Head `adb45dd5` is rebased on current main `d71f42ee` and preserves the maintainer's two-filter simplification. The selector invariant comment is shorter, but still names macOS FIFO EOF and `_DARWIN_UNLIMITED_SELECT`; no executable policy or cap was altered. The current repository gate passes **54 / 54**.

Fresh Linux installed-CLI smoke: `select_badfd` prints exactly `EBADF` then `continued`, exit 0, in emitted C, Bun JS and interpreted IO. The valid unwritten descriptor remains parked. `select_eintr` passes all three paths; `spawn_sleep`, `sleep_timer`, `udp_loopback` and `tcp_loopback` pass C and Bun against their existing expected outputs. No new macOS or distributed-mini run is claimed. The verification below that mentions ASan and 34 consumer/backend runs is historical qualification from the original head, not a rerun of those lanes on this rebase.

Fixes #1455.

## Change

- Handle readiness `EBADF` in C and Bun by checking parked descriptors with `F_GETFD` on that error path only. Invalid descriptors resume their normal effect handlers; valid descriptors remain parked unless their deadlines expire.
- Preserve `EINTR` retries and fatal handling of other selector errors. No selector-backend replacement, new retry policy, or normal-path descriptor validation.
- Keep the existing JS two-filter queue partition, as simplified by the maintainer. Descriptor checks still run only after `EBADF`, before callbacks execute.
- Add `select_badfd`: a real closed UDP descriptor must produce `Fail(EBADF)`, a separate valid unwritten pipe must not wake, and a later timer must complete. The idle pipe is terminated by explicit `IO.die`, following the existing `select_eintr` convention.
- Document the error-path contract in the existing runtime paper.

## Actual verification

- Permanent regression on unchanged baseline: both emitted C and Bun exit 1 with `bend: the poller failed`; no expected result is produced.
- Corrected regression: exact stdout `EBADF\ncontinued\n`, exit 0, in C and Bun. The C consumer also passes ASan + UBSan with four workers; no sanitizer diagnostics.
- A separate real timed binary receive returns `Ready(Fail(EBADF))`, rather than `Wait`, in Bun and ASan + UBSan native C with four workers.
- **34 / 34** existing consumer/backend runs match the unchanged golden output: 17 programs in emitted C and Bun, covering real interrupted `select`, timer order, spawned computations, TCP/UDP readiness, byte payloads, EOF, send/receive deadlines, backlog/timer fairness, and channel operations.
- Repository gate: **54 / 54**. `comp.ts`: **64,000 / 64,000 ttok** on rebased head `adb45dd5`. No cap, gate, allowlist, protected checker, or compiler-splitting change.
- Updated Typst paper compiles; actual rendered Effects section inspected on page 4. Release changelog left to maintainers.

## Boundaries

This is controlled real-OS error injection through a foreign fill, not a valid closed-alias program under affine `Socket` ownership. Ordinary valid waiters and signal handling are exercised separately above.

Linux x86_64 local verification only. macOS, GPU/mini-cluster gates, and hosted CI are not claimed. Socket readiness uses Bun FFI; no unrelated Node FFI port is included. Draft #1442 remains the separate unqualified #1250 indexing/budget proposal; this patch does not include that redesign.

AI-assisted: omp / GPT-6.1 Sol; working alone without subagents.

title: comp.ts simplifications: ty_holds, CID_T, tele_fill, corpus_at and more
body:
Behaviour-preserving simplifications of `bend2/comp.ts`. They free 183 ttok (63,905 → 63,722). Each commit covers one area:

- **ty_holds, lay_el, task_deliver, gpu_load, startup:**
  - `ty_holds` now looks inside every datatype except the words itself, so its predicate just returns `true`/`false` for what it is looking for. `ty_value`, `ty_clo`, `lay_of`'s recursion check and `js_marshal`'s `Nat` test no longer spell out the walk.
  - `lay_el` writes its type formers inline.
  - `task_deliver` computes its count cell once.
  - Metal `gpu_load` has one failure path.
  - `corpus_setup` and C `main` drop their one-use temporaries.
- **term_const, lay_el, mat_ctrs:**
  - Removes `term_const`'s dead `length === 0` guard (`[].every` is already `true`).
  - `lay_el` returns `BOX` directly for type formers, where `lay_of` always gave `BOX` on that branch.
  - Fixes a line break in `mat_ctrs` so its nested ternary reads the way it parses.
- **node_fields, emit_open, show_main:**
  - `node_fields` builds its scratch reads without patching strings.
  - `emit_open` names a parameter's words and marks the borrowed ones in one pass.
  - `show_main`'s `node` checks its cache before computing anything.
- **compile_book:**
  - The shown constructor names are worked out once, for both the roots and `SHOW_NAMES`.
  - `cid()` stores each encoded arity where the constructor is met, so the `ars` array zipped by index with `cids` is gone.
  - `js_def` uses `def_foreign`.
- **tele_fill:** a wrapper next to `tele_unbind` for the four `Bend.tele_fill(FL.book, T, xs, Bend.ctx_nil())` calls.
- **corpus_at:** one host-only helper for "map exactly at this address, give the mapping back otherwise", which `corpus_map` and `corpus_grow` both repeated.

Hot runtime paths and device code were deliberately left alone. During the drop work on #1438, an "obvious" merge of `ctr_take`'s two loops cost about 6% on lexer's Metal run.

## Validation
- **Generated code:** every `#|` test and all 17 runtime benches give byte-identical JS and compiler logs to `main`. Every `.c` file differs only in the `task_deliver`, `gpu_load`, `corpus_setup`, `main` and `corpus_at` lines. That was checked per commit, and again for the combined branch, where all 762 C diffs are identical.
- **Gates on the cluster:** repo 54/54, test 1597/1597, ping 47/47, perf 124/124.
- **Perf flake:** in 2 of 9 combined `_run.ts` runs on the first commit, perf came back 123/124. The full perf tables put the closest cells at `merkle` COMPILER and `generics_3200` CHECKER, which are near the 1.15× limit on `main` too. Alternating rounds against `main` passed 124/124 every time.
- **`corpus_grow`:** exercised with an 8 GiB array, so the arena doubled twice through the new helper. Metal builds and `--gpu on`/`off` outputs match `main`.

title: fix(compiler): preserve __proto__ JS module exports
body:
Exporting a pure `def __proto__` in a JS module currently changes the export object's prototype instead of creating an own property. Consumers lose the export when they enumerate keys or spread the module object.

Use the existing `js_key` helper in `js_lib` to emit `["__proto__"]` as a computed property. The export becomes an own, enumerable function property, and the module object retains `Object.prototype`.

## Blast radius

- The production change is one line in `bend2/comp.ts`, at the default export object shared by `.mjs` generation and the `.bend` loader. Export selection, public names and function wrappers are unchanged.
- `js_key` emits the same syntax for other names. Ordinary and namespaced module controls, standalone JS and C output were compared with the base compiler and were byte-identical.

## Validation

- `bun bend2/main.ts tests/io/module_export_keys.bend` compiles and loads a real `.mjs` module. It checks own properties, enumeration, spread, prototype and calls, with `constructor`, `toString` and an ordinary function as controls. It prints `2` with the base compiler and the expected `0` with this fix.
- The regression and nearby module/prototype fixtures pass through source execution and emitted JS, including `--checkup` and namespaced imports.
- Generated modules pass host assertions in Node and Bun. The Bun `.bend` loader also passes.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54 with CI-pinned ttok 0.3. `comp.ts` uses 63,907/64,000 tokens.

## Validation limits

Full cluster gates could not run locally because the `cluster` hostname is unavailable. Direct Node loading of the TypeScript compiler was blocked by Node's unsupported parameter-property syntax. Generated-module assertions passed in Node and Bun.

title: String.order walks both strings once and hands nothing back: a comparison is one tail call per char, 8x on the C lane, and String.eq of two 50000-char strings no longer overflows the JS lane
body:
`String.order` used to be `Pair.snd(String.cmp(a, b))`. That walk wasn't a tail call and rebuilt both strings, so the JS and interpreter lanes overflowed the stack on long strings. `String.eq` crashed on two 50,000-char strings.

The new `String.order.go(a, b, c)` walks both strings once and carries the order so far in `c`. It returns at the first differing char, or by length when one string is a prefix of the other. `String.cmp` and the Map ops that use it are unchanged.

- Matches `Pair.snd(String.cmp)` on all 116,281 pairs of strings up to length 4 (empty strings, prefixes, chars 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF).
- `tests/base/string_order.bend` covers the edge cases. Two of its cases check that the first difference beats later chars and lengths. It also runs 50,000-char strings, which crash main on interp, bun and node.
- Mac: C compares 8-19x faster, sorting 100k keys 7.7x faster, JS 1.3-1.9x faster.
- Gates on main d328354a: repo 54/54, test 1626/1626, perf 124/124, ping 58/58, safe 1637 files with no false rejects, `--verdict` ALL PROOFS CHECK.

title: fix(lint): respect module headers in declaration guard
body:
bend-lint refuses safe formatting when a valid module-import header is indented. Its declaration guard also removes import-looking lines throughout the file, so it can miss changes inside multiline strings or reject unchanged foreign-function bodies.

Limit masking to the initial module-import header, following `book_load`'s whitespace, comment and boundary rules. Recover fallback aliases from that same header while preserving parser-observed aliases. This adapts the [standalone bend-lint correction](https://github.com/MattCozendey/bend-lint/commit/cbcbe34e9489b5a6d50141def32a5ed3640c6208) to the bundled tool. Tests stay in bend-lint's suite, following the [maintainer guidance in #1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

## Blast radius

- The production change is confined to `sameDeclarations` in `tools/bend-lint/src/seam.ts`. It affects rules that use this guard, including the formatter's safety check.
- Only initial `import Base` and `import path as Alias` header lines are masked. Scanning stops at the first body line, including `@unsafe`. Foreign imports, later imports and multiline literal contents remain part of the comparison.
- The guard still compares parsed declarations using the already checked imports. Module loading, compiler/checker code and formatting rules are unchanged. The other changed file contains seven regressions in `rules/format.test.ts`.

## Validation

- `bun test` from `tools/bend-lint` passes all 122 tests. Each of the seven new regressions fails against the original guard.
- Actual CLI checks cover LF/CRLF, indented Base and module imports, foreign imports, and imported-law proofs. Safe fixes match the expected text, a second lint is clean, and tested source/emitted-JS output remains `7`.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. `git diff --check` passes.

## Validation limits

Typecheck still reports the same two pre-existing TS2339 errors in `bend2/bend.ts`, at lines 2040 and 3771. The before/after diagnostics are identical. These checks cover the bundled linter and tested programs; full cluster gates were not run.

title: A native build takes $CFLAGS after its -O3, as it takes $CC: with CFLAGS=-march=native the kmeans bench runs 2.3x faster and a U32 mix 3x, nbody 10% slower, so the flag is the builder's, not a default
body:
`cli_build` runs clang with a fixed line, `-std=c11 -O3`, so the C it emits targets the baseline x86-64: a U32 loop that clang vectorizes takes SSE2's `pmuludq` (two lanes, then a shuffle) where this machine has AVX2's `vpmulld` (eight lanes). The only way to get there was `-o file.c` and clang by hand.

Now `cli_build` reads `$CFLAGS`, as it already reads `$CC` to pick the compiler, and puts the flags after its own `-O3` (so a later `-O` wins). Nothing changes without the variable: a binary built the usual way is as portable as before, which is why this is not a default; a flag clang refuses fails the build as any other error does (`clang: error: unknown argument`, then `Error: clang failed to build`).

## Measured

Linux x86-64 (an i5-7600K, AVX2), one thread, five runs each.

A program that runs a murmur-style finalizer (two xor-shifts and a multiply, 16 rounds) over 16,777,216 ids and keeps the best score:

| build | time | the multiply in the loop |
|---|---|---|
| `bend mix.bend -o mix` | 113 ms | 64 × `pmuludq` |
| `CFLAGS=-march=native bend mix.bend -o mix` | 36 ms | 64 × `vpmulld` |

Same answer on both. Four benches of `bench/runtime`, medians of three runs:

| bench | `-O3` | `-O3 -march=native` |
|---|---|---|
| kmeans | 8570 ms | 3672 ms |
| nbody | 7947 ms | 8788 ms |
| mandelbrot | 6368 ms | 6430 ms |
| editdist | 4449 ms | 4435 ms |

So the flag pays where clang vectorizes (kmeans 2.3x, the mix 3x), does nothing for a scalar F32 loop, and costs nbody 10%: the choice belongs to whoever builds for the machine they measure on, which is why `-march=native` is not the default.

## The code

Four lines in `bend2/main.ts`, with a comment at `cli_build` that names the variable, as `cc_find`'s names `$CC`. The guide's tooling block is at its 8000-token cap, so the line that would go there (`CFLAGS=-march=native bend f.bend -o f  # clang flags, after -O3`) is in this description instead; I can add it if some other line makes room. Repo gate 54/54. No test file: the `#|` format tests programs, not the CLI; the three cases above (no variable, a good flag, a refused flag) were run by hand.

title: `bend PROOF.bend` fails over foreign defs that no law depends on
body:
### What Bend should do

`bend PROOF.bend` should fail only when a law's statement or proof relies on unsafe or foreign code. Other unsafe or foreign defs that happen to be in the import graph should be listed as a note, not turned into a failure.

Today, one foreign def anywhere in the graph fails every law. With the four files below, the only law is about `core.greet`, a pure function:

```text
$ bend PROOF.bend
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error: 2 defs rely on unsafe or foreign code:
- main.tty
- main.main
$ echo $?
1
```

Neither listed def is used by the law. Remove `import ./main.bend as M` from LAWS.bend and PROOF.bend, and the same law passes (`ALL PROOFS CHECK`, exit 0). `tty.c` doesn't need to exist for the check.

```python
# core.bend
import Base

def greet(name: String) -> String:
  "hi " ++ name
```

```python
# main.bend
import Base
import ./core.bend as C

def tty(fd: U32) -> IO(U32):
  import "./tty.c"

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    t : U32 <- tty(1)
    IO.print(C.greet(U32.show(t)))
```

```python
# LAWS.bend
import Base
import ./core.bend as C
import ./main.bend as M

law greets:
  {C.greet("x") == "hi x" : String}
```

```python
# PROOF.bend
import Base
import ./core.bend as C
import ./main.bend as M
import ./LAWS.bend as Laws

def Laws.greets():
  {==}
```

### Why

A program's laws usually import its modules, including the one that holds `main`. `demos/io_hello_world/LAWS.bend` does `import ./main.bend as Hello`. As soon as `main` uses a single foreign effect, for example `isatty`, which Base doesn't have, every law about the program fails, however pure the law is.

The only workaround is to split each program into a pure module, which the laws import, and a `main` module, which they must never import, even indirectly. Nothing enforces that rule except the failure itself.

This keeps what #776 and #966 asked for: a non-zero exit when a law rests on unchecked code. It only stops failing over code that sits next to the laws without being used by them.

bend 2.0.36 · Darwin arm64

title: Base: whether a descriptor is a terminal, and its width
body:
### What Bend should do

Add two terminal queries to Base:

```python
def IO.is_terminal(fd: U32) -> IO(Bool)
def IO.terminal_width(fd: U32) -> IO(U32)   # columns; 0 when fd is not a terminal or the width is unknown
```

| | C | JS |
|---|---|---|
| `IO.is_terminal` | `isatty(fd)` | `require("tty").isatty(fd)` |
| `IO.terminal_width` | `ioctl(fd, TIOCGWINSZ)`, then `ws_col` | `process.stdout.columns` (fd 1) or `process.stderr.columns` (fd 2) |

Example: color a message only when stderr is a terminal. Here `paint` is the program's own helper, which wraps its text in ANSI codes when its first argument is `True`.

```python
def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    tty : Bool <- IO.is_terminal(2)
    IO.print_err(paint(tty, "error:") ++ " file not found")
```

### Why

Almost every command-line program needs both:

- Color should go only to terminals. That's the convention behind `NO_COLOR` (no-color.org) and `CLICOLOR`, and it stops escape codes from ending up in pipes and log files.
- Help text and tables should wrap to the window width.

Today a Bend program can only get either through a user-written foreign effect. A foreign def in the import graph makes `bend PROOF.bend` fail for every law, even laws that don't use it (#1463). So a program that colors its output can no longer have its laws import its `main.bend`, the way `demos/io_hello_world` does. Base effects are trusted, as `IO.print` is.

Prior art: Rust `std::io::IsTerminal`, Python `os.isatty` and `shutil.get_terminal_size`, Node `tty.isatty` and `stream.columns`.

bend 2.0.36 · Darwin arm64

title: `main` cannot set an exit status without writing to stderr, and `IO.die` codes above 255 wrap (256 exits 0)
body:
### What Bend should do

1. A `main` of type `IO(U32)` exits with its result:

   ```python
   import Base

   def main() -> IO(U32):
     do IO<U32>:
       IO.print_err("error: unexpected argument '--frob' found")
       return 2
   ```

   This should print the line and exit 2, at the point where an `IO(Unit)` main exits today. Today it compiles, prints the line and exits **0**, natively, in compiled JS and under `bend status.bend`: the result is silently dropped.

2. An exit status outside 0..255, whether from `IO.die` or from `main`, should fail with a message and a non-zero status instead of wrapping. Today the OS wraps it modulo 256, so a failure can report success:

   ```python
   import Base

   def main() -> IO(Unit):
     IO.die(Unit, 256, "x")
   ```

   ```text
   $ ./big; echo $?
   x
   0
   ```

   The same happens with `bun big.js` and `bend big.bend`.

### Why

Command-line programs signal errors through the exit status: 2 for a usage error, by convention, after a formatted message of several lines. In Bend today, the only way to exit non-zero is `IO.die(code, msg)`, and it always writes `msg` plus a newline to stderr. #1101 confirms that newline is intended. So a program must either squeeze its whole message into `msg`, or print the message itself and then accept a stray blank line from `IO.die(code, "")`. It can never exit non-zero silently, for example after a child process has already reported the error.

The only workaround is a user-written foreign effect that calls `exit()`. A foreign def makes `bend PROOF.bend` fail for every law in the import graph (#1463).

Prior art: C `int main`, Rust `fn main() -> ExitCode`.

bend 2.0.36 · Darwin arm64 · bun 1.2.23

title: The runtime takes `--threads`, `--gpu`, `--gpu-build` and the first `--` from anywhere in a compiled program's argv
body:
### What you did

Built a program that prints its arguments, then ran it with arguments a typical command-line tool receives:

```
bend args.bend -o args && ./args grep -e --threads notes.txt
```

### What happened

The runtime takes `--threads`, `--gpu`, `--gpu-build` and the first `--` from anywhere in the program's argv, including where they are the values of the program's own options:

```text
$ ./args grep -e --threads notes.txt
bend: expected a thread count of 1 or more after --threads        # exit 1; main never runs
$ ./args compress --threads auto
bend: expected a thread count of 1 or more after --threads        # exit 1
$ ./args build --threads 4
[<./args>, <build>]
$ ./args fetch --gpu off
[<./args>, <fetch>]
$ ./args make --gpu-build                                          # exit 0; main never runs
$ ./args grep -- -v
[<./args>, <grep>, <-v>]                                           # the program never sees --
$ ./args grep -- -- -v
[<./args>, <grep>, <-->, <-v>]
$ bun args.js build --threads 4
[<…/args.js>, <build>]
```

So a compiled program cannot:

- take an option named `--threads` or `--gpu`;
- accept either word as an option's value (`grep -e --threads`) without the runtime failing before `main` runs;
- see `--`, so POSIX end-of-options handling costs its users `-- --`.

`--threads` matters most. It is the conventional name of the option that parallel tools expose: ripgrep `-j, --threads`, xz `-T, --threads`, zstd `-T, --threads`. A Bend program can read its worker count (`IO.thread_count`, #971), but it cannot offer the flag its users expect.

#934 moved the runtime's `--help` to `--bend-help`. This asks to finish that change for the remaining options.

### Request

1. `IO.args()` in a compiled program, native or JS, is exactly its argv, after the program name.
2. Runtime settings come from the environment, read once at startup: `BEND_THREADS=8`, `BEND_GPU=off|on|4GB`. Bad values fail as they do today. Prior art: `GOMAXPROCS`, `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS`. GHC made the same change in 7.0: compiled programs stopped accepting most `+RTS` options unless linked with `-rtsopts`.
3. `--gpu-build` and `--bend-help` move to `bend` itself (`bend main.bend -o main --gpu-build`) or to the environment (`BEND_GPU_BUILD=1 ./main`).
4. Optional: a build-time default, `bend main.bend -o main --threads 8`.

Migration: `./main --threads 8` becomes `BEND_THREADS=8 ./main`. This touches the GUIDE's Tooling block, `CLI_HELP` and the C `main` in comp.ts, `cli()` in comp.ts, `tests/io/args.bend`, and `FLAGS` in `gates/perf.ts`. I'm happy to send the patch if this direction is acceptable.

### The file

```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    xs : List<String> <- IO.args()
    IO.print(List.show(~&1, ~String, ~(s => "<" ++ s ++ ">"), xs))
```

title: A program whose stdout reader exits early prints `bend: a short write on a standard stream` and exits 1
body:
### What you did

```
bend flood.bend -o flood && ./flood | head -1
```

### What happened

```text
line of output for a pipe test
bend: a short write on a standard stream
```

`echo ${pipestatus[@]}` (zsh) prints `1 0`: the program exits 1 and writes an error to the terminal. `bend flood.bend -o flood.js && bun flood.js | head -1` does the same.

### Expected

The program stops quietly, as Unix tools do. `yes | head -1` writes nothing to stderr: `yes` is ended by SIGPIPE (status 141). Go does this on purpose: when a write to fd 1 or 2 fails with EPIPE, the program ends by SIGPIPE. #1211 fixed the same problem in `bend`'s own output.

Request: when a write to fd 1 or 2 fails with EPIPE, end the program silently, ideally by SIGPIPE, or at least without the message. Writes to files and sockets keep answering `Fail`.

This matters for any program whose output is piped into `head`, `less`, `grep -q` or similar.

### The file

```python
import Base

def flood(n: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("done")
    case 1n+p:
      IO.bind(Unit, Unit, IO.print("line of output for a pipe test"), _ => flood(p))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  flood(200000n)
```

title: Process.run ends the run on the Node host instead of running the program
body:
### What you did

`bend main.bend -o main.js`, then `node main.js`, with main.bend the file below (a Process.run of /bin/echo). The standalone JS program is a verification lane recent fixes check on Node too (#1446, #1450), and AGENTS.md names the loader "for bun and node".

### What happened

Under Bun the program prints the child's output and exits 0. Under Node the run ends before any answer:

```text
$ bun main.js
Done 0 [hello
] []
end

$ node main.js
ReferenceError: Worker is not defined
        at process_run (...)
exit 1
```

A host without Bun has no global Worker and no Bun.spawn, so Process.run cannot run its worker and the ReferenceError ends the run through io_errs: the effect never answers, and every computation after it is lost. The same host abort hits the effects that bind libc through bun:ffi (File.read, File.read_bytes, File.read_at, TCP.*, UDP.*, Socket.close, Listener.close), which end with `Error: Cannot find module 'bun:ffi'`; those may be a design call (answer Fail on a host without FFI, or grow node paths), so I am keeping this issue on Process.run, which has a direct fix: node:child_process.spawnSync is the semantics the C lane models (#1392), and the fix PR runs on it.

Measured on current main (5e708191), Linux x86_64: the permanent tests/io/process_run.bend, emitted standalone and run under Node with the fix branch, answers all 19 rows True, including timeout (ETIMEDOUT), the combined output cap (EFBIG), a runaway descendant past the cap, exit and signal codes, and a missing executable (ENOENT).

### The file

```python
import Base

def show(r: Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32 & (String & String)>) -> String:
  match r:
    case Done{(code, (out, err))}:
      "Done " ++ U32.show(code) ++ " [" ++ out ++ "] [" ++ err ++ "]"
    case Fail{(c, m)}:
      "Fail " ++ U32.show(c) ++ " " ++ m

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    a : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32 & (String & String)> <-
      Process.run("/bin/echo", ["hello"], "", 4096, 3000)
    x : Unit <- IO.print(show(a))
    IO.print("end")
```

### bend --version

main at 5e708191 (after 2.0.36), run through bun 1.4.2 and node v22.14.0

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

Debian clang version 14.0.6 (unrelated: the C lane was not part of this repro)

title: Process.run runs on the Node host, on child_process's spawnSync
body:
Fixes #1468.

## Problem

`Process.run` on the Node host ended the run with `ReferenceError: Worker is not defined` before any answer: the effect's worker path needs Bun's global `Worker` and `Bun.spawn`, and a host without them has no way to run the child. Recent fixes verify the emitted standalone program on standalone Node too (#1446, #1450), so the gap was reachable from a practiced lane.

## Change

`bend2/effs/process_run.js`: after the shared validation, a host without Bun takes a new `process_run_host`, on `node:child_process.spawnSync`, which is the semantics the C lane models (#1392): stdin fed, stdout and stderr read until they close (a descendant holding them extends the run), the exit code with signaled exits as 128 + the signal, a SIGKILL at the deadline, and the spawn error handed back as the errno.

The output cap needed care, since spawnSync bounds each stream and the C lane bounds the sum:

- `maxBuffer` is `max_output + 1` per stream, so a stream past it alone puts the sum past the combined cap, and the sum is checked after the read; the answer is `EFBIG` exactly when the C lane's combined cap says so. The interim buffer is at most twice the cap.
- Node reports the cap as `ENOBUFS` (v22 here; the older code is `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`, kept for older hosts), and a flood that a descendant keeps past the deadline may surface as `ETIMEDOUT` with the partial buffers attached, so any error whose buffered sum is past the cap answers `EFBIG`: the cap fired first either way.

The Bun worker path is unchanged behind `typeof Bun === "undefined"`.

## Verification

On Linux x86_64 (WSL Debian 12), main at 5e708191 plus this branch:

`tests/io/process_run.bend`, the permanent regression, emitted standalone (`-o out.js`) and run on every host. Before the fix Node ended the run at the first call; after:

| Host | Result |
|---|---|
| Bun 1.4.2 (`bun out.js`) | 19/19 True |
| Node v22.14.0 (`node out.js`) | 19/19 True |
| interpreted (`bend tests/io/process_run.bend`) | 19/19 True |
| native C lane | 19/19 True |

The Node run covers every row: stdin feeding, literal argv, exit and stderr, the at/over/combined cap rows (EFBIG), timeout (ETIMEDOUT), a missing executable (ENOENT), invalid limit and timeout (EINVAL), a NUL argument, a signal exit (143), SIGPIPE default, an inherited pipe past the deadline, descendant output after the child exits, a runaway descendant past the cap (this row is what pinned the ENOBUFS/flood rule above), closed stdio and the largest timeout.

`tests/io/process_run_parallel.bend` answers True on the interpreted, JS and C lanes.

Repo gate: 52/54 with and without this change. The two FAILs are the capped files `bend2/comp.ts` (64070) and `bend2/bendtt.lean` (64192) under this host's `ttok` (pip), files this PR does not touch; the same two FAILs appear on unmodified main here, and the maintainers' counter reports 63,995 for `comp.ts` (#1250), so the difference is the counter, not the tree.

No new test file: the gate runs the JS lane under Bun, where this path is unreachable (Bun keeps the worker path); the Node evidence above stands in for it, as in #1450.

title: A closed stdout or stderr reader ends a program by SIGPIPE, not with an error (#1467)
body:
Fixes #1467.

A program whose stdout or stderr reader exits early (`./flood | head -1`, `bun flood.js | head -1`, `bend flood.bend | head -1`) printed `bend: a short write on a standard stream` and exited 1. Now a write to a standard stream that fails with EPIPE ends the program by SIGPIPE, silently, the way `yes | head -1` does: status 141 in a shell, still non-zero for `pipefail`. Any other write error (EBADF, ENOSPC, EIO) keeps the message and exit 1. Files and sockets keep answering `Fail`, because `io_loop`'s `signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN)` is untouched.

- **C:** `io_out` and `io_sync` share a new `io_lost`. On EPIPE it restores SIGPIPE's default disposition and raises it; otherwise it calls `err_fail` as before. It is host-only (inside `#if !DEVICE`), like the rest of the IO runtime.
- **JS:** Bun ignores SIGPIPE too, and JS has no `signal()`. Adding and then removing a listener restores `SIG_DFL` (`onDidChangeListeners` in `BunProcess.cpp` calls `signal(n, SIG_DFL)` when the count drops to 0; `removeAllListeners` takes that path, the same in Bun 1.2.23 and 1.4.0), so `io_out` does that and sends SIGPIPE to itself. The in-process `bend f.bend` run uses the same `io_out`.

`tests/io/stream_epipe.bend` has a `.c` and a `.js` twin. The C twin forks a child that moves fd 1, then fd 2, onto a pipe whose read end is already closed and writes a line through `io_out`/`io_sync`. The JS twin spawns a child bun that runs the runtime's own `io_out` (`${io_out}`) the same way. Each answers the child's status as a shell shows it, and expects `141`. On main all three lanes print the message and `1` instead. Closing the read end before the write keeps it deterministic.

### Verification (macOS arm64, Apple clang 21, Bun 1.2.23)

- The issue's `flood.bend`: `./flood | head -1`, `bun flood.js | head -1`, `bun bend2/main.ts flood.bend | head -1` and `./flood 2>&1 | head -1` give `141 0` with nothing on stderr (main: `1 0` and the message). A full run still exits 0.
- `./flood >&-` (EBADF) still prints the message and exits 1.
- `tests/io` and `tests/halt`, run locally the way one `gates/test.ts` shard runs them (checkup, then the C and JS lanes): PASS 196 / 196, the new test included.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54. comp.ts is at 63,997 ttok of 64,000 (main: 63,905), so there are only 3 tokens of room. I shortened the comments to fit, and the merge queue will recount.

Not run: the cluster gates (`test.ts` on the minis, `perf.ts`) and Linux. The Bun 1.4.0 listener-removal path was checked in Bun's source, not run.

title: fix(io): end by SIGPIPE when stdout or stderr is a closed pipe
body:
Fixes #1467.

A compiled program whose output is piped into `head`, `less` or `grep -q`
dies on `EPIPE` with

```text
bend: a short write on a standard stream
```

and exits 1. Unix tools stop quietly in that spot instead, ended by
`SIGPIPE`: `yes | head -1` writes nothing to stderr and reports 141.

`bend2/comp.ts` ignored `SIGPIPE` in `io_loop` (so a dead pipe cannot kill
the runtime mid-turn), which turned every broken pipe into that message.
`io_out` and `io_sync` now share one `io_short` helper: on `EPIPE`
against `stdout` or `stderr` the runtime restores the default `SIGPIPE`
disposition and raises it, so the program ends the way `yes` does —
status 141, nothing on stderr. Every other failed write, and every write
to a file or a socket, still answers `err_fail` exactly as before, since
only `stdout` and `stderr` reach `io_out`.

The JS lane gets the same treatment: `EPIPE` on fd 1 or 2 exits 141
instead of printing the message and exiting 1.

The reproducer from the report, built at `2.0.36` and after this change:

```python
import Base

def flood(n: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("done")
    case 1n+p:
      IO.bind(Unit, Unit, IO.print("line of output for a pipe test"), _ => flood(p))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  flood(200000n)
```

```console
$ bend flood.bend -o flood && ./flood | head -1; echo "${pipestatus[@]}"
line of output for a pipe test
1 0                      # before: "bend: a short write on a standard stream"
$ bend flood.bend -o flood && ./flood | head -1; echo "${pipestatus[@]}"
line of output for a pipe test
141 0                    # after: nothing on stderr
```

Same under `bun`: `bend flood.bend -o flood.js && bun flood.js | head -1`
goes from `bend: a short write on a standard stream` / exit 1 to a silent
141.

Not covered by a `tests/io` case: the gate runs every test with its stdout
on a pipe it never closes, so a `#|` expectation cannot express a broken
pipe. Verified by hand in both lanes instead, plus the whole `tests/io`
and `tests/halt` suites interpreted against the unmodified baseline, which
moves nothing.

title: bend PROOF.bend fails only when a law or its proof relies on unsafe or foreign code (#1463)
body:
Fixes #1463.

Until now, `bend PROOF.bend` failed every law if any def in the import graph relied on unsafe or foreign code, for example an effect in the module that holds `main`. With this change, a PROOF.bend's claims are its own defs and its `LAWS.bend`'s. A def outside them that relies on a promise is listed in a note, and the run passes:

```text
$ bend PROOF.bend          # the issue's four files
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Note: 2 defs rely on unsafe or foreign code, but no law or proof does:
- main.tty
- main.main
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ echo $?
0
```

A law still fails when its statement or proof relies on a promise, directly or through anything it names. The walk is the same `book_promises` flood as before; only the split into a failure and a note is new. An unsafe fill of a law counts too, because it sets `u` on the law's own def. Roots other than PROOF.bend keep #1001's rule: every def outside Base is a claim. The `unsafe_*` import tests are unchanged.

- **`bend2/main.ts`**: `cli_verdict` takes the root file and splits `book_promises` into the failure and the note. A new helper, `relies`, formats both lists. The failure text is byte-for-byte the same as before.
- **`bend2/safe.ts`**: `safe_check` takes the noted defs and lets them be out of the kernel's scope. Without this, `--verdict` would answer an unused `@unsafe` def with the MISMATCH message. Everything else it checks is unchanged.
- **`guide/GUIDE.md`**: the `--verdict` paragraph now says "every law and proof" instead of "every def outside Base".

Tests (a test runs its file as the root, so each PROOF.bend has its own directory):
- `tests/proof/PROOF.bend`: a law about a pure `greet`, beside an imported `main` that loops by an `@unsafe` def. It passes with the note. Before this change it failed and listed `app/main.serve` and `app/main.main`.
- `tests/import/PROOF.bend`: a false law, proved by an `@unsafe` def of the PROOF.bend's own. It still fails, listing the law and that def, but no longer the unrelated `unsafe-law/safe.spin` it also imports.
- Each `LAWS.bend` run alone is an open claim, which the test pins.

How I checked it, all locally:
- The proof, import and check suites, run as one gate shard does: 414 / 414.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- `--verdict` with the Lean kernel on both the issue's files and `tests/proof/PROOF.bend`: ALL PROOFS CHECK plus the note.
- Every demo's PROOF.bend: the four that failed (`app_slash_boss_3d`, `io_http_server`, `io_tcp_echos`, `pure_hvm5_mini`) now pass with a note. In each, the noted defs belong to the module that holds `main`, and no law names them. The others are unchanged.

title: Base asks whether a descriptor is a terminal, and its width (#1464)
body:
Fixes #1464.

```python
def IO.is_terminal(fd: U32) -> IO(Bool)
def IO.terminal_width(fd: U32) -> IO(U32)   # 0 when fd is no terminal, or the terminal does not know its width
```

| | C | JS |
|---|---|---|
| `IO.is_terminal` | `isatty(fd)` | `tty.isatty(fd)` |
| `IO.terminal_width` | `ioctl(fd, TIOCGWINSZ)`, `ws_col` | a `tty.WriteStream` per fd, made once, with `_refreshSize()` on each call |

`process.stdout.columns`, as the issue suggests, covers only fds 1 and 2. A WriteStream reads its size only when it is made, and neither Node nor Bun refreshes one on another fd. So the JS lane caches one stream per fd and has it read the size again on each call. That keeps the width current, the way C's ioctl is. Node and Bun both have `_refreshSize`, and they run it on stdout's SIGWINCH. Garbage collection of a dropped stream doesn't close its fd in either runtime, but the cache avoids allocating a stream per call anyway.

As Base effects, both are trusted, as `IO.print` is. So a program that colors its output needs no foreign def of its own, and its laws can import its `main.bend`. Each effect has its own `.c`/`.js` pair. I first had them share one file, but the C build then failed for a program that used only one of them: the other's `CID(...)` is undefined unless guarded, as chan.c's are. comp.ts is unchanged.

Tests: `tests/io/terminal.bend` prints `False 0 True 77`:
- The test's stdout is a pipe, so it is not a terminal and is 0 wide.
- `Pty.open(77)` is a test twin that opens a pseudo-terminal with `openpty`, sized 77 columns, and answers the fd of its terminal side. The C twin calls `openpty`, and the JS twin calls it through `bun:ffi`. `openpty` takes the window size as an argument, so no variadic `ioctl` crosses the FFI.

How I checked it, all locally on macOS arm64:
- The io, base, stats and check suites, run as one gate shard does: 458 / 458.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- With stdout on a 101-column pseudo-terminal and stderr on a pipe, every lane prints `True 101 False 0`: native, `bun x.js`, `node x.js` and `bend x.bend`.
- A program that uses only one of the two effects builds on C and JS. That includes one that binds the Bool and never uses it.
- The issue's `paint` example runs, and `--verdict` on a program using both effects prints ALL PROOFS CHECK.

title: fix(io): use U32 main results as exit status
body:
## Fix

Closes #1465.

Use the returned word of an `IO(U32)` main as its process exit status in native C, generated JS, and the interpreter. Stderr remains independent: printing a usage error and returning 2 now exits 2 without printing the returned word. `IO(Unit)` and pure mains keep their existing successful exit behavior.

Validate main and `IO.die` statuses against 0..255 before process exit. In particular, 256 fails with a diagnostic and exit 1 instead of being silently truncated by the OS to success.

Native root tracking reads the existing Emit payload before dropping it, adds no allocation, and clears the completed root pointer so later spawned tasks cannot overwrite the status. Both runtimes still drain spawned IO. The `IO(Unit)` native control binary has no `io_root` or `io_result` symbols (`nm` checked).

Migrate three printing/channel/join fixtures from previously ignored nonzero main values to explicit successful returns, preserving their existing output goldens; remove the obsolete comments claiming that main's word is discarded. Update the existing IO guide within its unchanged token cap.

## Verification

Linux x86_64, Bun 1.3.13, Clang 22.1.8; native runs used 2 CPU threads with GPU off.

- Before: the same three issue reproductions on all three backends exited 0, including main-return 256 and `IO.die(..., 256, "x")`.
- After: five permanent regressions plus the existing `IO(Unit)` control passed on interpreter, generated JS, and native C: **18/18 real runs**. Includes silent status 255, out-of-range main/die, and root status 2 while a child and later grandchild finish with different values.
- Existing IO regression slice: **27/27 real runs** covering sleep ordering, spawn outliving main, fork/join, second-join failure, printing, and stderr/ENOENT exit 2.
- True pure `U32` main control: all three backends printed 42 and exited 0.
- Real `--checkup` continued through all six modules, recorded each expected nonzero exit, and reached the final successful control before returning aggregate failure as intended.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **PASS: 54 / 54** with all ten changed source/test/doc files staged. Permanent source and documentation caps unchanged; `bend2/bend.ts` untouched.

The remote 48-Mac-mini full gate matrix, macOS/Windows, and GPU lanes were not run. This is portable local qualification, not a claim that the complete cluster matrix passed.

title: On the CPU, a call before each fork keeps a fork tree on a few threads: 256 leaves get 3.5x from 16 threads instead of 14x
body:
I hit this batching nanoGPT inference on the CPU ([bend-bench ML.md](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/blob/main/ML.md)): one generation per leaf, and each level of the tree forked the model's weight handles before forking the generations. 16 threads gave about 2x. Building every handle first, so the generation tree's forks follow each other directly, gave 6.1x on the same work.

Here's a small version. Each inner node runs `k` steps of a fork-free `spin` before it forks, and each leaf runs `n` steps:

```python
import Base

type T is Type:
  Leaf{x: U32}
  Node{l: T, r: T}

def spin(+n: Nat, +acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      spin(p, U32.add(U32.mul(acc, 1664525), 1013904223))

@unsafe
def tree(+d: Nat, +i: U32, +n: Nat, +k: Nat) -> T:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      Leaf{spin(n, i)}
    case 1n+e:
      node(e, n, k, spin(k, i))

@unsafe
def node(+e: Nat, +n: Nat, +k: Nat, +j: U32) -> T:
  x y = tree(e, U32.mul(j, 2), n, k) tree(e, U32.add(U32.mul(j, 2), 1), n, k)
  Node{x, y}

def total(t: T) -> U32:
  match t:
    case Leaf{x}:
      x
    case Node{l, r}:
      U32.xor(total(l), total(r))

@unsafe
def run(+d: Nat, +n: Nat, +k: Nat) -> U32:
  total(tree(d, 0, n, k))

@unsafe
def go(md: Maybe<&2, Nat>, mn: Maybe<&2, Nat>, mk: Maybe<&2, Nat>) -> IO(Unit):
  match md mn mk:
    case Some{+d} Some{+n} Some{+k}:
      IO.print(U32.show(run!(d, n, k)))
    case _ _ _:
      IO.print("usage: spread log2_leaves leaf_work level_work")

@unsafe
def dispatch(args: List<String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match args:
    case Con{p, Con{d, Con{n, Con{k, Nil{}}}}}:
      go(Nat.read(d), Nat.read(n), Nat.read(k))
    case _:
      IO.print("usage: spread log2_leaves leaf_work level_work")

@unsafe
def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    args : List<String> <- IO.args()
    dispatch(args)
```

`taskset -c 0-15 ./spread 8 20000000 K --threads T --gpu off`, so 256 leaves of 20M steps each. Main at d5fe6566, Ryzen 9 3950X, median of 3 runs, each started with at most 1.5 CPUs busy with other work:

| Steps before each fork (K) | 1 thread | 16 threads | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 4.89 s | 0.34 s | 14.6x |
| 20,000 | 4.91 s | 0.35 s | 13.8x |
| 200,000 | 5.16 s | 0.38 s | 13.7x |
| 2,000,000 (a tenth of a leaf) | 5.31 s | 0.61 s | 8.7x |
| 10,000,000 | 7.47 s | 1.79 s | 4.2x |
| 20,000,000 (a whole leaf) | 10.15 s | 2.86 s | 3.5x |

The extra work parallelizes fine in principle: the 255 inner nodes are as independent as the leaves, and the longest root-to-leaf chain is 9 × 20M steps, about 0.2 s. At K = 20M the 16-thread time should be close to 10.15 / 16 + 0.2 ≈ 0.8 s, not 2.86 s.

From reading comp.ts, I think this is how it happens:

1. While the tree grows, a call to a fork-free def doesn't run: it's returned as a task, and the rest of the caller becomes its continuation ([comp.ts#L2087](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L2087)).
2. A growing lane skips fork-free tasks and pushes a returned one back ([#L4470](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L4470), [#L4484](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L4484)), and `row_grow` stops after a pass with no fork ([#L4679](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L4679)). So growth stops at the first `spin(k)` above a fork, and the forks under it are still inside its continuation.
3. The drain runs each ring sequentially ([#L4756](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L4756)). When a continuation forks there, `task_deal` with stride 0 puts the children back on the same ring ([#L4493](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L4493)), past that drain's snapshot, so they wait for the next round of `cube_run` ([#L5181](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/d5fe65662e02cce0261ad58234c2466f39a0736d/bend2/comp.ts#L5181)). Each round only spreads what the last one exposed, and every round waits for its slowest thread.

The obvious small patch doesn't help. I let host lanes run fork-free tasks during growth instead of skipping them (`DEVICE &&` on both checks in `monk_step`). Output is identical, and the times are too: 2.83 to 2.89 s at K = 20M, against 2.83 to 2.88 s before. Growth now gets past `spin(k)`, but the whole tree starts in one row, so that row's thread does all 255 inner nodes' `spin`s while the other rows stay empty. I think the real fix is a way for tasks that appear late to reach idle threads, such as idle threads stealing from other rows' rings. That's a bigger change to the pool loop, so I haven't tried it.

The workaround is to keep fork-free calls out of the levels of the tree. In my batch that meant building a tree of model handles first and then forking the generations over it.

title: fix(runtime)!: separate settings from program arguments
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1466. Native runtime settings are read from the environment, not consumed from a program's argument list. A compiled program receives its complete argv after its own name, including `--threads`, `--gpu`, `--gpu-build` and `--`.

- Native worker/GPU settings use `BEND_THREADS` and `BEND_GPU`. Native values are validated; supported worker limits remain 1..128.
- JavaScript and interpreted IO do not have native worker pools or device builds, so native-only settings do not reject these backends.
- The internal `BEND_GPU_BUILD=1` request succeeds without a usable GPU; ordinary bang programs retain CPU fallback.
- The bend-lint compiler seam remains compatible. The effect-table size regression is restored against the binary name actually generated by the test gate.
- Existing help, GUIDE, SHADERS, thread-count effect documentation and BendRT source/PDF use the environment settings. No token cap is changed.

## Review follow-up

Reviewer commit viridale/bend@1d2f5d72942ca5d52aa4dec72bfce1813e74482c was picked up with its original authorship; remaining docs, PDF and consumer regressions are in 22709c57.

## Real behavior proof

Linux x64; freshly compiled CLI from this PR, emitted C, Bun JS, Node JS and interpreted IO. No provider, model or GPU device was used. Exact argv retained on all four paths:
```
[<grep>, <-e>, <--threads>, <-->, <--gpu>, <off>, <>, <space value>, <🙂>]
```
JS/interpreted paths succeeded with native-only settings set to `auto` / `yes`. The real bend-lint executable printed its help and checked its sample file with exit 0. Native invalid settings returned exit 1. Native GPU build-only with no GPU returned exit 0 and empty output. The real `array_atomic_fadd` consumer ran on CPU with `BEND_GPU=off BEND_THREADS=4` and printed:
```
68
2448.25
```
The restored effect-table regression printed `True` in C and JS while opening the same existing 42,896-byte native binary. Its interpreter check still permits the pre-build missing-file case. The repository gate passed 54/54. The rebuilt paper's extracted text names `BEND_THREADS` and `BEND_GPU`.

Permanent argv regressions in the existing ping gate cover native, emitted-JS and interpreted execution, including flag-looking values, literal `--`, empty/spaced/Unicode arguments and irrelevant native settings.

## Not tested here

Full private-site ping installer suite; distributed mini gate; Metal/CUDA execution. The reviewer supplied macOS test/build evidence separately; the new local proof above is Linux-only.

title: fix(lint): use parsed declarations in formatting guard
body:
## Problem and fix

Bend accepts indented top-level declarations, but bundled bend-lint misses their names when rebuilding the declaration-comparison seed. Even comparing the original source with itself fails, so `--fix` refuses safe formatting of valid indented definitions, types, laws, and proofs.

Record the root parser's declaration keys through the existing in-memory seam and use them to rebuild the seed. Comparison-only parsing suspends and restores the observer, including on parse failures, so overlapping rules cannot overwrite another check's declarations. This adapts the parser-derived formatter guard from [MattCozendey's standalone bend-lint change](https://github.com/MattCozendey/bend-lint/commit/d79c4028a6b956f1cbea33beccb2ea0795f248b8).

## Blast radius

- `tools/bend-lint/src/seam.ts`: observes parser declaration keys during lint checks and changes the seed used by `sameDeclarations`. This affects rules using that comparison, including the `format/layout` safe-fix guard. Snapshot comparisons restore the active observer on success and failure.
- `tools/bend-lint/rules/format.test.ts`: adds regression coverage for indented declarations, semantic changes, multiline literals, and overlapping rules.

Only these two bundled-tool files change. The formatter layout engine, language/compiler sources, generated-program runtimes, and gates are unchanged. Tests remain in bend-lint's own suite, following [the maintainer guidance in #1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

## Regression evidence

- The three new declaration regressions fail against the original seam. They cover spaces/tabs, LF/CRLF, definitions, types, local/imported proofs, and unsafe declarations. Controls reject changed values, added/removed declarations, and changed literal contents.
- Removing only observer suspension makes the overlapping-rule regression fail. The corrected implementation also handles malformed comparison input without contaminating another check.
- Real CLI checks reproduce main's refusal and verify the safe fix on this branch. Execution remains `7`, and a second lint run is clean.

## Checks

- Original PR head (`c9b3283`, October 10) bend-lint suite: **126 passed, 0 failed; 827 assertions**.
- Original-head local repository gate: **54/54**, using CI-pinned ttok 0.3.
- GitHub [repo-gate](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38068733919/job/114261608480): **passed** on `c9b3283`.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

## Validation limits

On October 14, the `tools/bend-lint` suite on main `dbb3157` reports `109 pass / 9 fail / 1 error`; a private merge of this PR with that main reports `113 pass / 9 fail / 1 error`. Existing failing test names and diagnostics match, and all four added regressions pass. Both runs hit Base's new `Event.Text` constructor colliding with bend-lint's existing `Value.Text` after [#1441](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1441). This main regression is outside the declaration-guard change.

The original base and PR head also had the same two pre-existing TS2339 errors in protected `bend2/bend.ts` at lines 2040 and 3771. No new diagnostics were introduced in that comparison; typecheck was not rerun on the latest main.

Local tests ran on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.11. Windows and the cluster gates were not run. The additional in-memory parser hook depends on the current `parse_book` signature and declaration ordering; signature, startup, and patch-drift checks cover that dependency.

title: BendHub shows the alphabetically first file of a package as its import line and description, not the published entry
body:
### What you did

```
bend lib/tensor_f32.bend --publish stelliferous@0.0.2.0
```

### What happened

The publish itself went through, and the CLI printed the right line:

```text
published stelliferous@0.0.2.0
import stelliferous@0.0.2.0/tensor_f32.bend as Tensor_f32
```

The name page https://hub.bend-lang.com/n/stelliferous shows a different file:

```text
import stelliferous@0.0.2.0/default_kernel_cost.bend as Default_kernel_cost
```

The description of the package (`desc` in `/index.json` and `/packages.json`) is also taken from that file. It is the leading comment of `default_kernel_cost.bend`, an internal file of cost constants, and not the leading comment of the entry `tensor_f32.bend`.

### Cause, as far as I can read it

`name.html` takes the first top-level `.bend` key of the package's `files`:

```js
const bends = entry ? Object.keys(entry.files).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".bend")) : [];
const file = bends.find((f) => !f.includes("/")) || bends[0] || null;
```

The keys of `files` in `/index.json` are in sorted order, so the page shows the alphabetically first file. `desc` appears to follow the same rule.

`cli_publish` sends the entry as the first key of the posted `files`, but the hub does not seem to keep which file was the entry.

A package with one file is unaffected. Other packages with several files appear to get the same result. For example the `desc` of `bend-kit-http` reads like the comment of `admission.bend`, its first key, and that of `bend-kit-postgres` like the comment of `codec.bend`.

### Expected

The import line on the name page and the description use the entry file the package was published from.

### Suggestion

Keep the entry path with the package when it is published (the first key of the posted `files`), and use it for the import line and for `desc`.

title: fix(cpu): deal a slow grow's forks to idle threads (#1475)
body:
Fixes #1475.

One commit, `65a7b947`, in `row_grow` and `cube_run`. The token cut this PR first carried (`a7e927ed`) is already on main as `75d6f66d`, so it was dropped and the fix was rebased onto main. `comp.ts` is 63,972 ttok, under the 64,000 cap.

## The cause

A grow turn gives each row to one thread. The first turn has only the rows the root's fork reached: 2 for a binary tree. A row grows by running each ring's head up to its next fork. So when a tree does real work before each fork, its top levels ran on one or two threads while the rest waited at the turn's barrier. The drain that follows runs each task's subtree whole, so it can't make that back.

## What changes

- **`row_grow` notes when it starts.** In a turn with fewer rows than threads, a grow that is still growing after 1 ms makes one last pass. That pass deals its forks through `H_CURSOR` to row `g % CUBE_T` instead of within its own row.
- **`cube_run` repeats the grow turn** over the rows the cursor reached until no grow deals, then drains as before. The row bound still covers every task, because a dealt task `g` lands in a row below `g`. The Cube comment states this.
- **No dealing once a turn has as many rows as threads.** At that point every thread already has a row. Without this gate, a deep fine-grained tree (about 0.1 ms before each fork) went through about 30 extra barrier-bound grow turns: 12% slower and 3x the RSS (table below).
- **Benches never deal.** In instrumented builds of all 17 runtime benches, 3 runs each at 16 threads, there were 0 dealing passes. The longest single grow was 0.275 ms (tree-bitonic), so their schedules are unchanged.
- **SEQ is untouched by construction.** With one thread, `corpus_eval` never reaches the cube, and `rows < pool_size` is never true.
- **The device is untouched.** `monk_step` and the device kernel don't change. `row_grow` and `pool_*` are host-only (`#if !DEVICE`).

## #1475's tree

`./spread 8 20000000 K --threads T --gpu off`: 256 leaves of 20M steps each. M3 Max (12P + 4E), median of 3 runs, main (2343aec0) vs this branch. Every K prints the same output on both builds.

| Steps before each fork (K) | 1 thread | 12 threads, main → branch | 16 threads, main → branch | Speedup at 16 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 5.51 s | 0.48 → 0.47 s | 0.39 → 0.38 s | 14.1x → 14.5x |
| 20,000 | 5.49 s | 0.47 → 0.47 s | 0.37 → 0.39 s | 14.8x → 14.1x |
| 200,000 | 5.55 s | 0.50 → 0.48 s | 0.40 → 0.38 s | 13.9x → 14.6x |
| 2,000,000 | 6.03 s | 0.75 → 0.53 s | 0.65 → 0.44 s | 9.3x → 13.7x |
| 10,000,000 | 8.23 s | 1.85 → 0.78 s | 1.77 → 0.71 s | 4.6x → 11.6x |
| 20,000,000 | 10.99 s | 3.24 → 1.08 s | 3.15 → 0.88 s | **3.5x → 12.5x** |

At 4 threads with K = 20M it is 4.14 → 2.82 s (ideal ≈ 2.75 s). The 1-thread times are the same on both builds.

## Deep trees with little work before each fork

These are why the gate exists. Same program, 16 threads, median of 3, time and RSS. "Ungated" is this fix without the `rows < pool_size` condition.

| d, n, k | main | ungated | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16, 1000, 100000 (0.1 ms a fork) | 0.51 s, 8 MB | 0.57 s, 26 MB | 0.50 s, 9 MB |
| 18, 1000, 30000 | 0.61 s, 11 MB | 0.65 s, 34 MB | 0.61 s, 13 MB |
| 12, 1000, 1000000 | 0.43 s, 7 MB | 0.35 s, 14 MB | 0.32 s, 8 MB |
| 10, 1000, 3000000 | 0.59 s, 7 MB | 0.28 s, 10 MB | 0.25 s, 8 MB |

## Benches (local A/B)

All 17 runtime benches, main vs branch, run alternately, 3 runs each on this Mac:

- **Output:** every bench prints the same output in SEQ-CPU, PAR-CPU (`--threads 16 --gpu off`) and PAR-GPU (`--gpu on`).
- **RSS:** unchanged in every mode.
- **Time:**
  - SEQ-CPU is within 1% on 16 of the 17 benches. tree-radix reads 1.05, but its raw runs overlap (main 8.26/9.47/8.41 s, branch 9.57/8.48/8.85 s).
  - PAR-CPU and PAR-GPU scatter in both directions at `/usr/bin/time`'s 10 ms resolution. For example, queens' main build alone ranged 0.69–1.01 s.
  - Since no bench deals, I'd treat the dealing-pass count above as the evidence of an unchanged schedule. These timings aren't precise enough to show that, so the perf gate on the cluster is the real check.

## What I ran, and what I couldn't

- **Tests:** `gates/test.ts`'s shard script, run locally on this Mac in 4 shards (check, interpret, JS under bun, C), passes **1598 / 1600**. The two failures are `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`. They expect "no display", but this Mac has a desktop session, so a window opens. main's build gives the same output here.
- **Repo gate:** `gates/repo.ts` passes for `comp.ts`. With ttok 1.0 it flags `bendtt.lean` (64,192), which this PR doesn't touch; main counts the same.
- **Not run:** the cluster gates (I have no access to the minis), Linux and CUDA. Please run test and perf there. The perf gate's PAR-CPU cells are the ones that matter, and the dealing-pass count says they shouldn't move.
- **No test for the new path.** The test gate also interprets every test, and the path needs more than 1 ms of grow before it deals. The smallest tree that reliably gets there took the interpreter over 10 minutes. The issue's program reproduces it.
- **The 1 ms check is wall-clock.** On a loaded machine, a preempted grow can deal when it otherwise wouldn't. That changes only the schedule, never a result.

## Checked after the rebase (65a7b947 on main c25ee783)

- Gates: repo 54/54, test 1604/1604, ping 56/56. Perf on the cluster: PASS 124/124, same as main in the same session. PAR-CPU cells are within noise, PAR-GPU equal.
- #1475 on an M4 Pro (14 cores), `./spread 8 20000000 20000000 --threads 14 --gpu off`: main 2.79 s, this branch 1.05 s. 1 thread: 9.28 s vs 9.27 s.
- The `rows < pool_size` gate also keeps the ring from overflowing: with the gate removed, 8 of the 17 benches fail with ERR_RING at 16 threads.

## Not fixed here

If the work before each fork is a *non-flat* fork-free call (one that isn't tail-recursive, so it isn't inlined as a `spin_N`), this PR doesn't help. Example: the issue's `spin` with its result XORed by 1 after the recursive call. The program gets about 2x at 16 threads on main and on this branch, and that holds even at K = 0. The issue's tail-recursive `spin` doesn't have this problem. I'll look at it separately.

title: Bend 2.0.32 — False equalities accepted by `--verdict`
body:
### What you did

bend {file} --verdict

### What happened

```text
## Bend 2.0.32 — False equalities accepted by `--verdict`

I've found two cases where Bend reports `ALL PROOFS CHECK` for source code that appears to assert a false equality.

### 1. Arithmetic precedence


import Base

def Foo() -> {(3n * 0n+0n + 5n : Nat) == 15n : Nat}:
  {==}


**Result:** `ALL PROOFS CHECK`

Under ordinary arithmetic precedence, the claim is `5 == 15`. Bend instead parses the glued `0n+` as consuming the expression to its right, making the checked proposition `15 == 15`.

I couldn't find documentation specifying this precedence behavior.

### 2. Match indentation


import Base

def p4m(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Nat:
  match a:
    case True{}:
      match b:
        case True{}:
          1n
        case False{}:
          2n
       case x:
          7n
    case False{}:
      3n

def Foo() -> {p4m(False{}, True{}) == 7n : Nat}:
  {==}


**Reported result with the original definition name (`p4r`):** `ALL PROOFS CHECK`

The misaligned `case x` is treated as a branch of the outer match, causing the later `case False{}` branch to be dropped. Reading it as part of the inner match instead gives `3 == 7`, which is false.

Moving `case x` two spaces deeper reverses the result, as confirmed by control tests.

### Bounty eligibility

I recognize that the rules specify `Foo() -> Empty`, while these examples use false equalities. I'm submitting them because the bounty also asks for a proof of falsehood, and a false equality is mathematically sufficient to establish inconsistency.

If these don't qualify, I'd appreciate clarification on whether the issue is with these particular parsing behaviors, the literal `Empty` requirement, or the scope of the bounty itself.

**Specifically, if parser soundness bugs are excluded, which parts of Bend's verification pipeline are eligible? Does the bounty cover bugs in the TypeScript checker or the Bend-to-BendTT translator, or does it require finding an inconsistency in the already Lean-verified BendTT kernel itself?**
```

title: --verdict: a template lambda that captures a run-time value inside a type is out of scope for BendTT, but bend2 accepts it
body:
## Reproducer (bend 2.0.36)

```bend
import Base

def least(lo: Nat, xs: List<&2, Nat>) -> Data:
  {List.all(~&2, ~Nat, ~(y => Nat.is_le(lo, y)), xs) == True{} : Bool}

def least_nil(lo: Nat) -> least(lo, Nil{}):
  {==}
```

```text
$ bend u1.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend u1.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. ...
$ bend u1.bend -o u1.bendtt
BendTT: out of scope, so not in u1.bendtt:
- least: a template argument that depends on a run-time value
- least_nil: names least, out of scope: a template argument that depends on a run-time value
```

The same template applied in live code is rejected by bend2 itself, with a clear message (`expected : a template applied to closed ~ arguments (lo is a variable here, not comptime: pass it at run time)`). Inside a type, bend2 accepts it and only `--verdict` fails, with the generic mismatch message.

## Expected

One of:
- the BendTT translation handles a template lambda that captures a variable in a dead position (a type), or
- bend2 rejects it there too, with the same message it gives in live code, so the check and `--verdict` agree.

## Impact

bend-mathlib's `sort.bend` states "every element is at least `lo`" this way (`internal_least`), so all its merge-sort lemmas (`merge_by_sorted`, `msort_by_sorted` and helpers) are out of scope under `--verdict`. This is separate from #1182, which is the `~le_total` part of the same file.

Related: #1182, #1180 (closed; a different "depends on a run-time value" case).

title: fix(cli): fail updates when installer download fails
body:
## Problem and fix

`bend update` returns 0 when curl fails because the last `sh` in `curl | sh` succeeds on empty input. A failed partial download can also execute its prefix.

Capture the installer in a shell variable and invoke `sh` only after curl succeeds: `s=$(curl -fsSL ...) && printf '%s\n' "$s" | sh`. This follows [the maintainer's requested simplification](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1485#pullrequestreview-5483056714), replacing the previous temporary-file implementation. The displayed command uses the same guarded download. Shell diagnostics and installer signal exit statuses are preserved.

Fixes #1481.

## Blast radius

Only two files change. `bend2/main.ts` changes the sole-argument `update` command. `gates/ping.ts` adds a failed-download assertion beside the existing successful update check and updates that check's expected command text. Regression coverage stays in the existing installed-CLI gate, following the CLI exit-status precedent in [#1214](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1214).

The final change uses no temporary files or descriptors. Language/compiler/runtime sources, installer content, permanent caps and gate policy are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

Source and rebuilt compiled-CLI probes show the original implementation returns 0 for refused connections, HTTP 404 and truncated responses. The revision returns curl's 7, 22 and 18 respectively, and never executes the failed partial script. Controlled curl failure 23 also propagates. Successful scripts return 0; installer failure 17 and signal status 143 remain observable. Missing curl now reports the shell diagnostic and returns 127.

## Checks

- 60 isolated updater executions and eight version controls across the original and revised source/compiled CLIs, including real curl against loopback HTTP, missing tools, signals and scripts larger than 2 MiB.
- Exact failed-download and successful executable-replacement assertions from `gates/ping.ts` exercised against rebuilt CLIs. They pass on this revision and on current main (`d71f42e`) with the PR patch applied; the new failure assertion fails on the original implementation.
- Full PR patch applies cleanly to current main; source and compiled updater probes pass on that combined tree.
- Repository gate: **54/54** with CI-pinned ttok 0.3; permanent caps unchanged.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- GitHub [repo-gate](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38152442299/job/114508486881): **passed** on `8a76db3`.

## Validation limits

Full `gates/ping.ts` **skipped** because the sibling site repository is unavailable. Harmless local installer fixtures do not qualify the real archive/install/hub flow. Local tests ran on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.11 and curl 8.7.1; Linux/WSL, Windows, CI Bun 1.4.0 and cluster gates were not run locally.

TypeScript 7.0.2 with `bend2/pack/tsconfig.json` reports the same 12 diagnostics on the original base and this revision, including existing checker/elaborator/docs errors and missing optional `canvas` types. Typecheck is not clean; no new diagnostics were introduced.

The shell buffers the complete text installer before execution. Command substitution removes trailing newlines; `printf` adds one before passing the text to `sh`.

title: fix(compiler)!: stabilize JS constructor tags across modules
body:
## Problem

A constructor's JS tag includes the namespace of the book that loaded it. A value exported by `a.bend` has tag `Counter`, but a module that imports the same type expects `a.Counter`. So when one module's value goes into another, the match picks the wrong arm (on main, `score(Left)` gives 9 instead of 8, and `flag(Off)` gives 1 instead of 0).

Fixes #1105.

## Change

- A constructor's JS tag is now its name inside the file that declares it, with no namespace prefix from the loading file. This applies to JS constructor emission, type-local matches, and `CID(...)` for constructors.
- Foreign-def effect identities and public def export keys keep their full namespaces.
- Display names stay qualified, so JS and native C still print `a.Counter{5n}`. The show descriptor stores `[tag, display]` pairs.
- `tests/io/constructor_interchange.bend/.js`: two real modules, each using values built by the other (record, sum arms, enum arms). The test fails on main and prints `0` here.

Breaking: a host that hard-codes a book-qualified tag string (`"a.Counter"`) no longer matches. Hosts that use `CID()` are unaffected. The repo has no such literals.

Tags are unique only within a type. That is fine, because every JS dispatch on `.$` is type-local.

Rebased onto main 252752c9. Since #1506 removed the JS seam check (`js_marshal`), this PR no longer touches marshalling, `marshal_tag_unknown` is gone, and tests expect plain numbers (`4/8/9`). There is no unknown-tag check at the boundary, either on main or in this PR.

## Evidence

comp.ts 63,740 tok (cap 64k). Gates: repo 54/54, test 1635/1635, ping 58/58, perf 124/124, safe 0 false rejects. Interp, JS and C agree on cross-file cases (same ctor names in two files, generic holding the other file's type, three-level imports, effect building a value with `CID`). CUDA and Windows were not run.

title: fix(verdict): lift Data captures in type-only templates

Addresses #1483; still draft.

A predicate used in a type can capture a runtime value without turning it into a global constant. Each instance now owns its typed captures in `cols`, and its cache key names them by position. This fixes the collision between an outer capture and a local at the same frontend level.

The root `~` probe keeps its closed-instance fallback. Live runtime capture lifting still raises `Open_Error`; closing an argument also checks for leftover free variables.

The new dependent-proof regression failed in BendTT before and now checks. The full local safe corpus has 1,721 files: 1,111 agree, 492 frontend rejections, 115 unsafe, 3 out of scope, and no false rejects, timeouts or infrastructure errors.
