title: list_map_conversion regression only pins a legacy parser error instead of testing template conversion
body:
## What Bend should do

The migrated `tests/check/list_map_conversion.bend` fixture should check a template lambda used inside a theorem type and run a reachable mapped-value consumer. Its header explicitly says the old Bend3 `=` equation should become Bend `==`; the current fixture never reaches that property.

## Current main evidence

On main `2343aec` (Bun 1.3.13, Linux x64), running `bun bend2/main.ts tests/check/list_map_conversion.bend --verdict` exits 1 before elaboration:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : ':'
- observed : '='
```

The theorem still uses `{... = 2n : Nat}` and its fill `{=}`. It also uses old-style template applications without `~`, and omits `LL.length`'s explicit erased type argument. Instead of detecting this migration gap, its expected `#|` lines pin that exact parser failure. Its `main` then returns the literal `2n`, so simply fixing syntax without changing reachability would still not exercise mapped values in emitted code.

This reports an ineffective regression, **not a newly demonstrated compiler defect**. No matching open PR/report for `list_map_conversion` was found.

## Acceptance

- Use current equality/reflexivity and explicit template/type-argument syntax.
- The type-level mapped-list conversion theorem is accepted by the real source checker and proof kernel.
- `main` consumes actual mapped values so source, emitted JS and native C detect a dropped or incorrect callback rather than print a disconnected literal.
- Remove the old diagnostic-wording expectation; do not re-pin an exception or a source location.
- Do not change the checker, protected gates, allow list or caps.

title: test: restore semantic template list-map conversion coverage
body:
Fixes #1490.

The existing list-map conversion regression currently passes by expecting a legacy parser error. Its own comment says Bend spells equations `==`, but the theorem still has `=`/`{=}`, old template application syntax and a missing erased argument. Its main returns an unrelated literal, so mapped values are not exercised.

This is a regression-coverage repair, **not a claim of a new compiler fix**.

## Change

- Replace the diagnostic-wording expectation with a runnable semantic result.
- Use current equality/reflexivity, `~` application, explicit erased type argument and annotated operators.
- Use checked `Nat` arithmetic rather than native `U32` models, so the genuine kernel proves both mapped-list **length** and **values** (`[2n, 3n]`).
- Run the same closed callback through an actual mapped-value sum in main (`5n`), rather than a disconnected literal or a length-only consumer.
- Note the repaired coverage in the existing changelog. No GUIDE edit.

## Actual verification

- Untouched main `2343aec`: the fixture's `--verdict` exits **1** at `=` before elaboration.
- This branch: source interpreter prints **`5n`**, exit **0**.
- Real BendTT kernel (same unmodified Lean source as main): `--verdict` prints **`ALL PROOFS CHECK`**, exit **0**, including both equality obligations.
- Actual emitted standalone Bun JS, Node JS and native C executable each print **`5n`**, exit **0**.
- Repository gate **54/54**; checker, kernel, compiler, gates, allow list and caps unchanged.

Mini-cluster/GPU gates were not run. The old error sentence and location are deliberately not re-pinned.

title: fix(io): add quiet exit and reject out-of-range status codes
body:
Fixes #1465 using the narrower design requested in [the maintainer review of #1474](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1474#issuecomment-6108212595). This replaces that closed redesign; **`IO(U32)` main's result is still ignored**.

## Change

- Add pure checked `IO.exit(code: U32) -> IO(Unit)` and a distinct `Exit{code}` IO opcode. A valid exit writes nothing, including no empty stderr line. No user-defined foreign-effect workaround.
- Validate 0..255 in the shared interpreter/JS runtime and native host loop. Invalid `IO.exit` and `IO.die` codes fail with status 1 instead of OS modulo-256 wrapping. `IO.die` still writes its caller-supplied message and newline.
- Decode a packed native opcode directly from its immediate payload, not as a boxed heap address. The one-field U32 Exit constructor is emitted as `term_pak`.
- Treat Exit as a genuine IO.OP constructor in user wildcard guards and migrate the repository's exhaustive IO.OP consumers. Foreign requests still cannot enter those pure matches.
- Add consumer-visible termination/wildcard and boundary regressions. The boundary probe observes actual subprocess status, before/after reachability, byte-exact valid quiet stderr and IO.die's empty-message newline; it does not pin the range diagnostic sentence.
- **No GUIDE or CHANGELOG edit; no main/argv policy change, checker, Lean kernel, protected gate, allow-list or cap change.**

## Actual evidence

Linux x64, real generated programs, not source assertions:

- 6 terminal scenarios × **4 actual lanes** (source interpreter, standalone Bun JS, standalone Node JS, native C): valid quiet **0/255** produce zero stderr bytes; **256/UINT32_MAX** fail 1; empty-message IO.die keeps its one newline and code 7; IO.die(256, "reported") retains its caller message and fails 1. All print only `before`, never the continuation's `after`.
- Returned U32 main: prints `kept`, exits **0** in all four lanes, not its returned 37.
- Quiet opcode/wildcard regression: prints **91**, exits **23**, zero stderr in interpreter, Bun, Node and native C.
- Both existing alien-request tests retain their output, fail-stop status **1** and never print SECRET in all four lanes. The UTF-8 halt law retains **è❁** and status **7** in all four lanes.
- Genuine installed-layout compiled Bend CLI, **empty PATH**: quiet termination, the six-case boundary fixture and unchanged typed-main behavior all match. The final boundary fixture also prints **0** in source, standalone Bun and Node execution.
- Pure structural exit theorem: the genuine unmodified BendTT kernel prints **ALL PROOFS CHECK**, exit **0**. This proves formal admissibility, not a proof of OS exit behavior.
- Actual namespaced `--checkup` exercised all five opcode consumers with empty PATH, including their expected nonzero termination cases; no claim that its aggregate process returned 0.
- Repository shape/cap gate: **54/54**.

Baseline wrapping is the issue/maintainer's reported observation; it was not redundantly rerun to confirm it. Mini-cluster/GPU gates were not run.

title: Collect transient native-emitter garbage on heap growth
body:
Fixes the default-GC emission pressure reported in #1262. This addresses suggestion 1 (collect transient emission garbage), not the independent incremental-emission design in open #1386. I rechecked open PRs referencing #1262 before submitting; #1386 is the only existing one.

## Change

Sample Bun heap use every 64 emitted definitions. Once it exceeds 2 GiB, collect; set the next checkpoint to the post-collection live heap plus 2 GiB. This avoids using physical host RAM as the transient-garbage budget and avoids repeatedly collecting large live books that cannot be reclaimed. No re-exec, global JSC environment override, scheduling rewrite, or per-definition full GC.

The guarded checkpoint leaves non-Bun compilation unchanged. README states the resource policy and explicitly says live state is not capped. No GUIDE or CHANGELOG edit; no protected checker/kernel/gate/allow-list/cap changes.

## Actual before/after

Same public [Chromi Eco entry](https://github.com/amage-si/chromi/blob/70555a40a809ca95c4ccc39ca381d9524bd5ec22/examples/eco/main.bend), same dependency revisions and Linux x64 host (31 GiB RAM), same Bun executable. BUN_JSC_forceRAMSize was unset. The unchanged source compiler is main 2343aec; the treatment differs only by this checkpoint and its documentation.

| Executed compiler | Peak RSS (KiB) | Wall time (s) | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Source, before | 4483420 | 27.35 | 0 |
| Source, after | 3026800 | 26.58 | 0 |
| Genuine installed-layout compiled CLI, after | 3059936 | 26.60 | 0 |

All three generated C files are **byte-identical**, checked with cmp; SHA-256: 1170f0ac04a8116080efadd8394bc896eaf5cc05a6f373ad2bbbaa2be4ba0f34.

Repository shape/cap gate: **54/54**. No nondeterministic memory assertion added to the permanent test suite.

Limits: the issue's private 27k-line Darwin application was unavailable; this is a real public large application, not a reproduction claim for that exact input. No Darwin/GPU run. This is a heap-growth collection policy, **not a hard RSS limit** and not a solution to intrinsically oversized live compiler state.

title: fix: spill wide live segments beyond the 247-word C bank
body:
Fixes #1069.

The limit is on live segment arguments, not just constructor width. Increasing the shared C register bank reintroduces the Clang failure, and an 8-bit logical arity loses large closure/fork arguments.

This keeps the physical bank at 247 words and spills excess segment arguments through the existing evaluator stack. Continuation entry consumes its frame and spill tail before loading locals; closure application appends its final argument after spilled captures. Ordinary native C spins retain their own C parameters, including self jumps. Logical arity is `u32`; the flat result width and frame/fork flags remain compact. The existing foreign-request width guard is unchanged.

Four permanent consumer regressions cover 248 live boxed fields, a materialized 300-capture callback, a 300-live-value fork, and a weighted 301-word native self-spin which always recurses. Before the change all four are valid interpreter programs but native emission fails with `an arity over 247`. Generated observation: callback logical arity 301, fork arity 303, physical bank still 247.

Verification on Linux x64:
- Real standalone compiled CLI built all four permanent inputs to native binaries and executable JS.
- All four returned the interpreter results under native 1/4 threads, Bun and Node: 16 actual executions.
- Four existing word-copy/native-spin/wide-record-drop/stale-field consumers matched their expected results in source, native 1/4 threads, Bun and Node: 20 executions.
- Real namespaced `--checkup` passes for all four new consumers.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54/54 on the rebased branch; permanent token limits and allow-list are unchanged.

Older Clang versions and Metal/CUDA hardware are not available here, so I am not claiming those runs. `bend2/bend.ts`, the kernel, GUIDE and CHANGELOG are untouched. README documents the bounded bank/spill distinction.

title: CLI: -o through a hard-linked alias silently overwrites a program input
body:
### What happened

On current main `d71f42ee287bd7b9f86b44df44b210ac5eb651bd`, an existing output hard link to a program input bypasses the `-o` input protection. JS emission opens the alias for writing and overwrites the original input inode.

Minimal input:
```bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print("original input still runs")
```

Reproduce with a disposable input:
```sh
ln input.bend alias.js
bun bend2/main.ts input.bend -o alias.js
bun bend2/main.ts input.bend
```

Observed on Linux x64 with Bun 1.3.13: compilation exits 0, `input.bend` now starts with generated `function word_to_u32(w) {`, and the subsequent original run exits 1 with a parser error. Canonical path resolution cannot detect a hard link: the names differ but `(dev, ino)` is identical. The same guard also covers imported source and foreign implementation inputs, so an alias to those should be protected too.

### Expected

Reject an output which is the same existing file as any program input, including a hard-linked alias, before writing through it. Preserve the original program so it still runs. Normal independent outputs must still compile.

### Scope

The output guard in `cli_file` currently checks resolved path names and directories only. This is a filesystem identity gap, not a language/checker issue. No matching hard-link fix or issue was found; #1485 mentions an installer executable inode but fixes the separate update download bug.

title: fix(cli): reject outputs that alias inputs or earlier outputs
body:
Fixes #1495 and #1694.

Kept Nicolas's `f0327f11` file-identity guard and merged current main. It now also remembers each successfully emitted output. A later `-o` alias fails instead of silently replacing the first program with another format. Recording the identity after emission also catches a dangling symlink to an output that did not exist yet.

Added an installed-CLI regression that creates hard-linked JS/C targets, rejects the second write, and runs the surviving JS. The existing input-hardlink regression remains.

Checked both the source CLI and a freshly compiled CLI on Linux: hard links, symlinks, dangling symlinks, repeated paths, protected inputs, and independent JS/C/native outputs. All 12 scenarios passed; the emitted programs printed `7n`. Repository gate: 54/54. The full installer/hub gate was not run locally.

AI-assisted.

title: CLI: --checkup exits green without checking imports that have trailing comments
body:
### Observed on current main

`--checkup` silently skips valid imports with trailing `#` comments and exits 0 without checking or running the imported program.

`bad.bend`:
```bend
import Base
def main() -> Nat:
  True{}
```

`aggregate.bend`:
```bend
import ./bad.bend as Bad # inline comment
```

Actual commands on `d71f42ee287bd7b9f86b44df44b210ac5eb651bd` (Linux x64, Bun 1.3.13):
- `bun bend2/main.ts aggregate.bend --check-only` exits 1 with the imported definition's Nat-versus-Bool type error.
- `bun bend2/main.ts aggregate.bend --checkup` exits 0 with empty stdout and stderr.

This is valid import syntax: an equivalent good imported program passes `--check-only`, but its commented `--checkup` also emits nothing instead of its `5n` result.

### Cause and expectation

`cli_checkup` uses an end-anchored import regex which accepts only whitespace after the alias, so the trailing comment removes the module from the check/run set. A comment should not turn a failing imported program into a green checkup or suppress a good run. Preserve independent per-module checks and ordinary uncommented imports.

No matching open PR or issue was found. The language parser is not at fault and does not need to change.

title: fix(cli): check and run imports with trailing comments in checkup
body:
Fixes #1497.

A valid `import ./bad.bend as Bad # comment` checks the imported file normally, but `--checkup` treated it as a non-import: it exited 0 without any check/run. Good commented imports were skipped too. Accept the language's trailing `#` comment in the existing checkup import matcher; do not change the language parser or independent per-module execution.

The new permanent installed-CLI assertion checks both consequences: a commented bad import exits 1, and a commented good import actually runs and returns `5n`. Existing uncommented checkup/closed-reader controls remain. The exact new assertion fails on unchanged source behavior and passes with the real rebuilt standalone CLI. No diagnostic wording or implementation-source assertions. README documents aliased checkup imports; hand-written GUIDE/CHANGELOG are unchanged.

Actual Linux x64 verification:
- Before: the ordinary checker accepts the good aggregation syntax and rejects the bad module, while both commented checkups incorrectly return 0 with empty output.
- Twenty real source/compiled CLI checkup executions cover good/bad comments, original plain imports, comments immediately after the alias, CRLF, a commented-out nonexistent import, a real missing import, an absolute path, and a mixed failing-then-good aggregation. Failures remain nonzero and the mixed aggregation still runs the good module.
- Exact permanent assertion executed fail-before/pass-after using real CLI processes.
- Standalone CLI rebuilt from this branch.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54/54; permanent caps and gate policy unchanged.

Full installer/archive/hub ping was not run because the sibling site checkout is unavailable; isolated assertion proof is not a claim that the full ping gate passed.

title: CLI: --checkup treats valid hub imports as unrelated local files
body:
A documented content-hash import works through the ordinary checker/interpreter, but `--checkup` treats the same import as an unrelated local path.

Current main: d71f42ee287bd7b9f86b44df44b210ac5eb651bd, Linux x64, Bun 1.3.13.

A hash-consistent cached package contains `main.bend`:
```bend
import Base
def main() -> Nat:
  Nat.add(2n, 3n)
```
Its SHA-256 manifest gives package `0x21370a2927727e0639e2a011d71cd94d`; the cache is selected with the existing `BEND_LIB` setting. An aggregation containing
```bend
import 0x21370a2927727e0639e2a011d71cd94d/main.bend as Remote
```
loads normally: a parent `Remote.main()` passes `--check-only` and returns `5n`. Running the import aggregation with `--checkup` instead exits 1 with `ENOENT`, looking for `<aggregation-dir>/0x21370a2927727e0639e2a011d71cd94d/main.bend` rather than resolving the actual hub package.

The independent runner should use the same content-hash/named package resolution and hub namespace restrictions as the normal loader, not reinterpret a valid hub import as a local file. Local independent checks and their failure/continuation behavior should remain unchanged.

I checked existing PRs/issues matching checkup + hub. The closed folder-import proposal #1070 is unmerged; #1498 changes recognition of trailing comments, not source addressing.

title: fix(cli): resolve and run hub imports in independent checkup scopes
body:
## Current-head review qualification

Head `cfd7b3d8` preserves the maintainer's generated-root refactor and fixes its reproduced traversal/symlink regressions. Both the initial parse and checked load use a hub-owned wrapper namespace so the existing loader's library-confinement checks apply. Protected `bend.ts` and compiler APIs are unchanged; no resolver/name/hash-cache copies or token-cap changes were added.

Before `67d6f8e4`: both `0x<hash>/../../outside.bend` and a cached entry symlinked outside the library executed the outside file (`99n`, exit 0). After: exit 1 and no outside output, while a later valid named IO import still executes. Cold hash/named loads use real loopback HTTP manifests and SHA verification. Warm hash, local IO, a no-main library, failure continuation, independent Base scope and SHA-mismatch rejection were exercised with the source CLI and a newly compiled CLI. Temporary roots were removed after success and failure.

The exact existing/new ping hub-consumer assertion block passed against this compiled CLI; repository gate **54/54**. The full private-site installer suite, mini cluster and macOS were not run here. The older proof below is retained as historical qualification, not represented as a rerun on this head.

Fixes #1499.

`--checkup` currently turns a documented content-hash or named hub import into a file beside the aggregation. The ordinary checker/runner resolves the same cached package and returns `5n`; independent checkup instead fails with ENOENT.

Resolve package names using the existing public name/version grammar, name-cache layout and immutable hash lookup protocol. Hand acquisition and manifest/file digest verification to the unchanged loader. Keep the module's hub namespace while parsing/checking, then select its actual pure or IO `main`; the shared JS generator now accepts an explicit entry root rather than only rooting `main`. Ordinary CLI, JS and module entry defaults remain unchanged. Reuse checked Base when source is already present, but do not inject Base into a module that did not import it. Cache confinement is checked before executing an entry.

The permanent installed-CLI consumer uses the gate's existing manifest hash helper to create a valid isolated cache: one content-hash pure entry returns `5n`, and a different named effectful entry actually prints `hub-io`. The exact new assertion fails against unchanged main and passes against the genuinely rebuilt standalone CLI. No wiring/source-shape/diagnostic-text assertion. README documents independent hub scope.

Actual Linux x64 evidence:
- Four cold source/installed runs fetch real SHA-verified manifest/file responses from an isolated HTTP content server selected by BEND_HUB. Hash imports return `5n`; named imports resolve and execute `hub-io`. This is local HTTP protocol proof, not a claim that a test package was published to the public hub.
- Twenty-four source/installed boundary runs cover warm hash/name/IO entries, a conflicting local decoy, rejection of a bad proof and missing Base, a quiet exit status 37, continued good execution after a bad module, ordinary local IO, package traversal, invalid version/hash and a missing package.
- Eight actual source/installed integrity/confinement runs reject corrupt manifests/files without writing the package, and reject warm/cold external-cache symlinks before IO entry execution.
- Eleven ordinary consumer executions preserve direct root CLI, native C, Bun/Node JS, Bun/Node MJS and actual Bun .bend-loader behavior; two real emission commands built those artifacts.
- Exact new permanent consumer assertion: fail-before/pass-after with real CLI processes.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54/54.

The human-written bend2/bend.ts, GUIDE, CHANGELOG, kernel, gate policy and permanent token limits are untouched. Full installer/archive/hub ping was not run because the sibling site checkout is unavailable; executing its new assertion is not a claim that the complete gate passed. No GPU/platform qualification.

title: CLI: --checkup treats import-looking text in a valid multiline string as another module
body:
Current `--checkup` scans the entire source for import-looking lines instead of only the language's import header. A valid multiline string can therefore add an unintended module check and make a valid aggregation fail.

Actual Linux x64/Bun 1.3.13 reproduction (current upstream header-scanning logic; the ordinary checker and runner accept it):
```bend
import Base
import ./good.bend as Good

def ignored() -> String:
  "text
import ./missing.bend as Fake
more text"

def main() -> Nat:
  Good.main()
```
`good.bend` has a valid `main() -> Nat` returning `5n`. Ordinary `--check-only` exits 0 and normal execution prints `5n`. `--checkup` executes Good, then tries the text inside the string as a real import and exits 1 for missing.bend.

Only actual header imports should be checked/run independently; comment/blank header lines remain allowed, and body/literal text must not create extra filesystem or hub work. This is header scanner state, separate from #1497's trailing-comment recognition or #1499's hub addressing. Duplicate searches for checkup + string/header found no existing fix.

title: fix(cli): checkup reads only the import header
body:
Fixes #1501.

`--checkup` scanned every trimmed line of the source. A legal multiline `String` body containing `import ./missing.bend as Missing` therefore caused an independent filesystem lookup and failed an otherwise valid aggregation; import-looking text naming a real IO module could also select a module outside the import header.

Follow the existing normal loader's header rule: skip blank/comment lines, and stop at the first non-import line. The aliased-import selector and independent module checking/running remain unchanged. No parser or `bend2/bend.ts` changes.

Added a consumer regression in `gates/ping.ts`: the aggregation first passes ordinary `--check-only`, then its real imported sum must independently return `5n` without treating a multiline body string as an additional import. The exact assertion fails against unchanged upstream (`--checkup` exits 1 with ENOENT) and passes against the compiled, installed-layout CLI (`--checkup` exits 0 and returns `5n`).

Verification:
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- Built an actual installed-layout executable with `bun build --compile` and an adjacent `bend2` installation.
- 18 actual source/installed CLI executions: multiline body missing/real/IO import-looking text, interleaved blank/comment header lines, multiple header imports, CRLF, absolute imports, a bad header module followed by a good one, no aliased header imports, and ordinary checker/runner controls.
- The bad real header import still makes the command fail while the later good header import still returns `5n`; hidden body IO is not run.

The full private-site-dependent `gates/ping.ts` installation suite was not run here; its newly added assertion was executed directly with the real before/after CLIs. `GUIDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and protected human source were not changed.

title: CLI: --verdict silently ignores extra program/file arguments
body:
`bend <file> --verdict` accepts trailing positional/program arguments although this is a single-file verification mode. They are silently ignored, unlike `--check-only`.

Actual reproduction on current main (d71f42ee):
```bend
import Base
def good() -> {1n == 1n : Nat}:
  {==}
```
With a second file:
```bend
import Base
def bad() -> {1n == 2n : Nat}:
  {==}
```
Using a real BendTT kernel:
```text
bend good.bend --verdict              # exit 0, ALL PROOFS CHECK
bend bad.bend --verdict               # exit 1, expected 1n, observed 2n
bend good.bend --verdict bad.bend     # exit 0, ALL PROOFS CHECK
```
The last invocation does not check the extra file; it treats it as an unused runtime argument. This is a CLI invocation-contract problem, not a claim that the kernel certified the bad proof.

Expected: reject trailing program arguments in `--verdict`, as the CLI already does for `--check-only`. Ordinary run-mode program arguments must remain supported. Multi-file verification is not requested.

The current `cli_file` runtime-argument guard includes output/check-only/checkup/publish modes, but omits `verdict`. Targeted existing issue/PR searches did not find a competing CLI-argument fix.

title: fix(cli): reject program arguments in verdict mode
body:
Fixes #1503.

The existing runtime-argument guard omitted `verdict`. Thus `bend good.bend --verdict bad.bend` reported `ALL PROOFS CHECK` and exited 0: only `good.bend` was verified and the second pathname was silently ignored. This is not a claim that the kernel certified the bad proof; the invocation is invalid for this single-file mode.

Include `verdict` in the existing guard. Keep ordinary run arguments, the `--` separator, help actions, unknown-option handling, and all verifier/mismatch diagnostics unchanged. Multi-file verification is not added.

Permanent regression: after a kernel corpus worker has obtained an actually accepted proof, invoke that same file with an extra program argument and require exit 1. This reuses the worker's real proof/kernel context, so a missing kernel cannot make an unexercised argument check appear to pass. One check per accepted shard, not one per definition or corpus file. The parent propagates nonzero worker exits so an assertion failure is not classified as an ordinary proof rejection.

Verification:
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- Built and exercised a compiled, installed-layout CLI with an adjacent `bend2` directory.
- Real BendTT kernel controls: `{1n == 1n : Nat}` accepted; `{1n == 2n : Nat}` rejected; a trailing bad-proof pathname rejected after this fix.
- Ran the actual updated `gates/safe_node.ts` with both proof files: it fails against unchanged upstream because the extra argument is accepted, and passes against the fixed CLI while retaining the false-proof rejection.
- 32 source/installed CLI executions covering extra path/value/empty arguments, arguments after `--`, literal option-like arguments, a separator with no following argument, valid/invalid proofs, ordinary IO.args (including Unicode, an empty string and escaped `--verdict`), and existing check-only/mutually-exclusive-mode behavior.

The distributed mini-cluster `gates/safe.ts` corpus was not run here; its actual worker and new assertion were run locally with the real Linux BendTT kernel. Protected `bend2/bend.ts`, `GUIDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, kernel semantics and cap policy were not changed.

title: fix(formatter): preserve separated brace arguments
body:
## Problem and fix

Formatting a valid comma-optional call such as `choose(id {42 : U32})` produces `choose(id{42 : U32})`. Bend reads the glued name and brace as a constructor, so the formatted program no longer parses.

Reuse the token's existing `gap` flag to preserve one space between a name and a separated brace. Adjacent constructors stay glued. This also preserves separated equality and reflexivity arguments without adding parser logic or helpers.

## Blast radius

Two files in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: the formatter's name-before-brace spacing rule and its unit tests. The rule serves direct `formatBend` calls and LSP document formatting; other separated name/brace forms, including constructor declarations, also retain one space. Spacing after closing braces and angle brackets keeps its existing behavior. No language, compiler, bundled bend-lint, gate, dependency, or changelog changes.

This addresses a different defect from #1302's column-sensitive layouts, although both PRs touch nearby formatter code.

## Regression evidence

The new seven-case table covers ordinary/dotted names, equality and reflexivity arguments, explicit commas, nested constructors, and case-lambda braces, including idempotence. With the original spacing expression, the final suite has 25 passing tests and the new regression fails; with the fix, all 26 pass.

Real Bend CLI checks cover nine programs before and after formatting. Four annotation/equality/reflexivity/constructor-field cases fail after baseline formatting and print `42` with the fix. Five constructor/pattern, comma, and closing-brace/angle controls print `42` throughout.

## Checks

- `npm test` in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: TypeScript build and all 26 formatter/LSP tests pass, with no skips.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` with CI-pinned `ttok` 0.3: 54/54 pass.
- Real Bend CLI comparisons and formatter idempotence pass; `git diff --check` passes.

## Validation limits

Local checks ran on macOS arm64 with Node 26.8.2 and Bun 1.3.11. Windows, the minimum supported Node 22, and the cluster test/performance/safety/ping gates were not run. These focused checks do not establish semantic preservation for every formatter input. #1302 may require a context rebase if it lands first; its complete suite was not rerun here.

title: A Nat crosses to a JS host as a plain number
body:
The JS runtime has held Nats as numbers since 87a1e9c9 (2.3x), and it kept BigInt only at the host seam. This PR removes that seam conversion. An effect's `.js` gets and answers a number, and a def exported through the `.bend` loader or `-o x.mjs` takes and returns one. `js_marshal`, `js_host`, `nat_host` and the `marsh` memo are gone. `comp.ts` goes from 63,788 to 62,883 ttok.

**Breaking for JS callers:** a host that passed or expected `5n` now uses `5`. EFFECTS.md, main.ts's header, `effs/now.js` and the `app_win_is_bug_2d` demo are updated.

## Nat check at the seam
`nat_in` lets a value through only if it's a whole number from 0 to 2^53. Anything else stops the run with the usual Nat error, as the C lane does. It runs on:
- each answer of an effect whose type is exactly `Nat`
- each `Nat` argument of an exported def, curried calls included

Nats nested in fields or containers aren't checked. EFFECTS.md says so.

## Tests
- `marshal_nat_bigint` → `marshal_nat_number`. `marshal_nat_pair` and `marshal_native_forms` now expect `number`. `marshal_array_depth` and `nat_host_bounds` answer numbers.
- `nat_host_neg` is kept: a negative host answer fail-stops on interp, C and JS.
- New `nat_host_export`: `inc(-1)`, `inc(1.5)`, `inc(1n)`, `inc(2^53+2)` and `add(1)(-1)` throw the Nat error, and good calls still run.
- **Deleted `marshal_tag_unknown`:** the #1105 tag check lived inside `js_marshal`. #1488 removes the cause.

This also fixes the return-type marshal behind #1150.

## Validation (on main c25ee783)
- **Mac gates:** repo 54/54, ping 55/55, test 1604/1604, perf 124/124.
- **Linux (x86_64, bun 1.4.2, local run of gates/test.ts):** test 1604/1604, the same as main.
- **Generated C:** byte-identical to `main` for all 17 runtime benches.
- **JS export calls:** 2M `inc` calls take 74 ms on main, 21 ms here (20 ms without the check).

title: comp.ts: one function makes the per-pass File state
body:
`File` held ten fields that each emitting pass writes and the next pass clears (`lend`, `segs`, `spins`, `spun`, `clos`, `tabs`, `img`, `lits`, `consts`, `brws`). They were listed three times: in the type, in `file_new`, and in `compile_book`'s clear-and-reset before each pass. `file_pass()` now builds them. `file_new` spreads it, `compile_book` does `Object.assign(FL, file_pass())`, and `File` takes its type from it. This frees **62 ttok** (63,929 → 63,867).

## Validation
- **Generated C:** byte-identical to `main` for all 17 runtime benches.
- **Gates on the cluster:** repo 54/54, test 1602/1602.

title: fix(audio): keep Linux partial writes and stop on a dead device
body:
The Linux audio pump loses audio when ALSA takes only part of a 256-frame chunk: the rest of the chunk is dropped. A failed write also drops the chunk, and a dead device makes the pump spin, because the result of `snd_pcm_recover` is ignored.

The pump now keeps the chunk until ALSA has taken all of it, and moves on through it as writes succeed. It stops when a write returns 0 or recovery fails. Audio then goes quiet, as it already does on macOS. The Audio effect types and the error behavior are otherwise unchanged.

`tests/io/audio_linux_progress.{bend,c,js}` replaces ALSA's write and recover calls with a small test shim on ALSA's `null` output. It covers every short first write (1-255 frames), EINTR and EPIPE once, writes capped at 17 frames, partial writes followed by EINTR or EPIPE, a dead device (stops after one write, no retry), and zero writes. It checks that all 512 frames arrive in order and that `Audio.close` joins the pump. On macOS and JS it runs no cases.

Validation:

- Linux (Docker, Debian, clang-19, libasound2): the test fails on main (case 0 loses frames) and passes here. Mutants that drop the offset, ignore a failed recover, ignore a zero write, or drop a chunk on error are all caught.
- Gates: repo 54/54, test 1605/1605, ping 56/56.
- Not tested on a physical ALSA device. The gates cluster runs macOS, so the Linux cases only run on Linux.

title: comp.ts sheds 468 tokens, so the next changes fit under its cap
body:
comp.ts is at 63,929 of its 64,000 ttok cap with ttok 0.3, which CI pins. With ttok 1.0 it is over the cap, at 64,098. This PR frees 468 tokens without changing what any program prints, so the next fix has room. comp.ts ends at 63,461 with ttok 0.3 and 63,637 with ttok 1.0.

It takes over #1479's token commit, so that all the trimming lives in one PR. Once this merges, #1479 can be the fix alone.

## Commits

- **`3b4a864e`** is #1479's `a7e927ed`, cherry-picked onto today's main without conflicts. It saves 250 tokens:
  - `File` and `Scope` become `ReturnType<typeof file_new>` and `ReturnType<typeof scope_new>`.
  - `pool_rows`' drain loop drops `!err_seen(e.mem)`. The loop runs only on the host, where that test is always false.
  - `task_deal` computes its cursor start in one expression.
  - The f32 `show` and `read` operations use `tpl_ops`.
  - `src_add` uses `memo`.
- **`707eba89`** is new. It saves 181 tokens:
  - **`File` spreads its book** (`...book`) instead of holding it, so `FL.book.tlds` becomes `FL.tlds` across 50 lines (−52). The spread is safe: `tmps` is a record mutated in place, only the checker bumps `hols`, and `io_base` already spreads a book.
  - **`Seg` is `ReturnType<typeof seg_new>`** (−40). `spin` and `fork` now start `false` instead of absent, so `emit_jump`'s `bang` defaults to `false`.
  - **`ctr_take` copies a node's fields in one loop** from `term_peek`, which is `term_loc` for an unshared node (−38).
  - **The `TODO(#1105)` comment in `js_marshal` is deleted** (−37). The error string right below it says the same and names the issue.
  - **`term_peek` and `blk_read` each return a ternary** (−14).
- **`6a663300`** fixes or cuts five comments. It saves 37 tokens:
  - The C and JS show comments both said `show_chr` escapes "as char_show". `bend.ts` no longer has a `char_show` (it is now `chr_show`, inside `term_show`), and both comments already say the output matches `term_show`, so the clause goes.
  - The show descriptor comment now lists Char's boxed flag, which `show_main` writes and the C `show_val` reads.
  - "EPIPE ends the program by SIGPIPE" above `io_lost` restated its three lines.
  - The note on `let FL: File` repeated the File comment.

`ReturnType` for record types is new to comp.ts; #1479 introduced it. If you'd rather keep hand-written types, `File`, `Scope` and `Seg` would cost back about 235 of the 468 tokens.

## What I ran

- **JS:** for all 899 runnable tests, the generated `.js` and `.mjs` match main's byte for byte, except for the one runtime comment line `6a663300` shortens. The build messages are identical.
- **C:** every generated file differs from main's by the same five hunks: `term_peek`, `ctr_take`, `blk_read`, `task_deal` and `pool_rows`, plus `6a663300`'s comment lines.
- **`6a663300`** changes only comments, so I didn't rerun the suite for it. I built one test (`show/char_unicode`) to C and JS before and after it: only comment lines differ.
- **Codegen:** with Apple clang at -O3 (queens, raytrace, tree-radix):
  - `term_peek` and `blk_read` compile to identical assembly.
  - The `ctr_take` merge keeps the same loads and stores, with one more conditional branch per program.
  - Alternating SEQ-CPU runs, 5 each, show no difference. Median user time, before → after: queens 8.45 → 8.44 s, raytrace 7.49 → 7.49 s.
- **Tests:**
  - `--checkup` (check and interpret) over all 1,602 test modules prints the same as main.
  - Every C-lane test was built and run on this Mac, with Metal for the bang tests: 746 pass.
  - 123 tests are refused at build, exactly as on main, because main's type can't be printed.
  - `gfx_window` and `gfx_clicks` fail as on main: they expect "no display", but a window opens on this desktop.
- **Types:** `tsc` reports no new errors.
- **Repo gate:** `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54 with ttok 0.3. With ttok 1.0 it flags only `bendtt.lean` (64,192), which this PR doesn't touch.
- **Not run:** the cluster gates, Linux and CUDA. The perf gate is the real check on `ctr_take`.

title: `+` and `-` change meaning with spacing, and the errors suggest a fix that fails or point at the wrong line
body:
### What you did

`bend f.bend` on the file below, once for each body of `f` in the table.

### What happened

Spacing picks one of three parses for `+` and `-`:

- With no space after a `Nat` literal, `Nn+e` is a successor, not the `+` operator, and `e` runs to the end of the expression.
- Directly after a term, `+x` and `-x` read as a reusable or erased let binder.
- Spaced, `a + b` is the operator, which needs `(… : T)`.

Five natural spellings fail. None of their errors names the cause, two suggest a fix that also fails, and one points at the wrong line:

| Body of `f` | Error |
|---|---|
| `case 1n + p: p` (a pattern) | `a type for this operator (write (a + b : Nat))` |
| `case (1n + p : Nat): p` (doing what that error says) | `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` / `observed : Nat.add(1n, p)` |
| `(5n+x - 4n : Nat)` | `a type for this operator (write (a - b : Nat))`. It is already wrapped: the successor takes `x - 4n` as its operand, which leaves the `-` outside the annotation |
| `x+y` | `expected : '='` / `observed : 'd'`, located at the next `def`, not at `x+y` |
| `(1+x : U32)` | `expected : '='` / `observed : ':'` |
| `5n-x` | `expected : 'def', 'type' or 'law'` / `observed : '-'` |

The full output for three of them:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- message  : a type for this operator (write (a + b : Nat))
Location:
5 |     case 0n: 0n
6>|     case 1n + p: p
  |             ^
7 |
Note: we broke this after launch, sorry. Until 2.0.16 a bare operator meant Nat.
That was a bug: operators demand annotation. Wrap the expression and it'll work again.
```

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- message  : a type for this operator (write (a - b : Nat))
Location:
3 | def f(x: Nat) -> Nat:
4>|   (5n+x - 4n : Nat)
  |         ^
5 |
Note: we broke this after launch, sorry. Until 2.0.16 a bare operator meant Nat.
That was a bug: operators demand annotation. Wrap the expression and it'll work again.
```

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : '='
- observed : 'd'
Location:
5 |
6>| def main() -> Nat:
  | ^
7 |   f(3n, 4n)
```

These work: `case 1n+p:`, `case 1n+ p:`, `2n+x`, `(x+1n : Nat)`, `(x + 1n : Nat)`, and `((5n+x) - 4n : Nat)`, which prints `2n` for `x = 1n`.

None of the spellings I tried returns a wrong value, because each misparse is refused. The cost is the diagnosis. The guide's reference lists `(a + b * c : T)` among terms and says "Operators need spaces on both sides". It never lists `Nn+e`, yet its examples use it in patterns (`case 1n+p:`) and in expressions (`1n+length(a, A, t)`). Following the stated rule (`case 1n + p:`) fails, and following the error's suggestion then fails again. Every recursion over `Nat` meets this, so it is among the first errors a new program hits, whether a person or an AI agent writes it from the guide.

### What Bend should do

1. List `Nn+e` in the guide's reference for terms and patterns, as a successor written with no space before `+`.
2. In a pattern, accept `1n + p` as `1n+p`. Failing that, make the error there say "write `1n+p`, with no spaces".
3. End a successor's operand at a spaced operator, so that `(5n+x - 4n : Nat)` reads as `((5n+x) - 4n : Nat)`. Every case I tried that this changes is refused today. Failing that, make the error say "the successor `5n+` takes `x - 4n`; write `(5n+x)`".
4. When `+name` or `-name` directly follows a term on the same line, report "operators need spaces on both sides" at that token, not at the next `def`.

### The file

```python
import Base

def f(x: Nat, +y: Nat) -> Nat:
  x+y

def main() -> Nat:
  f(3n, 4n)
```

For the pattern rows, `f` is:

```python
def f(n: Nat) -> Nat:
  match n:
    case 0n: 0n
    case 1n + p: p
```

For the other rows, `f` takes only `x` (of type `U32` in the `U32` row), and `main` calls `f(1n)`, `f(3n)` or `f(3)` to match.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.36

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)

title: `F32.show` takes `+a`, so `~F32.show` cannot be passed to `List.show` or `Maybe.show`, unlike every other Base show
body:
### What you did

`bend show.bend` on the file below.

### What happened

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : @_:F32 -> String
- observed : @+a:F32 -> String
Location: main
3 | def main() -> String:
4>|   List.show(~&2, ~F32, ~F32.show, [1.5, 2.5])
  |                         ^^^^^^^^
5 |
```

`Maybe.show(~&2, ~F32, ~F32.show, Some{1.5})` fails the same way.

Every other numeric type's show fits:

- `List.show(~&2, ~U32, ~U32.show, [1, 2])` prints `"[1, 2]"`.
- `List.show(~&2, ~Nat, ~Nat.show, [1n, 2n])` prints `"[1, 2]"`.

Here is why, in `bend2/base.bend` on main:

- `List.show` and `Maybe.show` take `~f: A -> String`.
- `Nat.show`, `U32.show`, `Char.show` and `Bool.show` take a plain parameter.
- `law F32.show` declares `for +a: F32`. It is the only one of the 36 `F32` laws with a `+` parameter; the other 34 take `a: F32`, and `F32.read` takes `s: String`.

WONTFIX.txt (#1111) makes `@+x:A -> B` and `A -> B` different types. So the working form is `~(x => F32.show(x))`, which prints `[1.5, 2.5]` under `bend` and in a native build. That rule is fine. The problem is that Base's show for `F32` is the one show in Base that doesn't fit Base's own `~f: A -> String` slot, so every program that prints a list or `Maybe` of floats needs the lambda.

### What Bend should do

Declare `law F32.show: for a: F32`, as for the other `F32` laws and the other shows, so `~F32.show` fills `~f: F32 -> String` in `List.show` and `Maybe.show`.

### The file

```python
import Base

def main() -> String:
  List.show(~&2, ~F32, ~F32.show, [1.5, 2.5])
```

### bend --version

bend 2.0.36

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)

title: A tree borrowed by both tasks of a fork is freed by one lane at the join, and on CUDA that serial `term_sink` takes most of the device time
body:
### What you did

bend fork_drop.bend -o fork_drop.c

### What happened

Everything below uses the published `bend-2.0.36-linux-x64.tar.gz` (sha256 `02089dc0eed0fd5fd6d73c74cc9cffcb2c6638dd3b02ae83f7b8cc57fbe381ba`) on WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04. `fork_drop.bend` is the file at the end of this report. `mode 0` passes one tree as a `+` parameter to a def whose two fork tasks only read it (`a b = walk.a(t) walk.a(t)`). `mode 1` builds the tree twice and gives each task its own copy. Both modes print the same number.


tar -xzf bend-2.0.36-linux-x64.tar.gz
bend version                                      # bend 2.0.36
bend fork_drop.bend -o fork_drop.c
CUDA_HOME=/usr bend fork_drop.bend -o fork_drop   # Ubuntu's CUDA packages put nvrtc.h in /usr/include
./fork_drop 0 20 1 --gpu off                      # CPU
./fork_drop 0 20 1 --gpu 4GB
# bend: CUDA device lacks concurrent managed access (WSL2 lacks it)


WSL2 has no concurrent managed access, so the binary that the CLI builds refuses the GPU. To reach the CUDA path I changed one host line of the emitted C, `if (managed == 0) {` in `gpu_probe`, to `if (0 && managed == 0) {`, and built the copy with the same two steps that `bend -o` runs (the clang line and `--gpu-build`). The device code is unchanged. On a Linux machine with concurrent managed access, `bend fork_drop.bend -o fork_drop` and `./fork_drop <mode> <depth> <rounds> --gpu 4GB` should be enough.


sed 's/^  if (managed == 0) {$/  if (0 \&\& managed == 0) {/' fork_drop.c > fork_drop_wsl.c
clang-19 -DBEND_CUDA=1 -I/usr/include -L/usr/lib64 -L/usr/lib -std=c11 -O3 fork_drop_wsl.c \
  -lpthread -lm -o fork_drop_wsl -lcuda -lnvrtc
./fork_drop_wsl --gpu-build


To check the cause, I also built a copy without the `term_sink` line of the mode 0 join. It leaks the tree and prints the same result.


sed '/WL_CASE(FID_ROUND_J43)/,/^  }}/{/term_sink(e, _h_3);/d}' fork_drop_wsl.c > fork_drop_nosink.c
# then the same clang line and --gpu-build


Wall time, one run per line, with `fork_drop` for `--gpu off` and `fork_drop_wsl` for `--gpu 4GB`:


for depth in 18 20; do for gpu in off 4GB; do for mode in 0 1; do for rounds in 1 9; do
  bin=./fork_drop; [ $gpu = off ] || bin=./fork_drop_wsl
  t0=$(date +%s%N); out=$($bin $mode $depth $rounds --gpu $gpu); t1=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "depth=$depth gpu=$gpu mode=$mode rounds=$rounds result=$out wall_ms=$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000000 ))"
done; done; done; done


Device time, with Nsight Systems 2026.3.2, 3 rounds per run and 2 runs of each binary and mode:


nsys profile --trace=cuda --cuda-um-cpu-page-faults=true --cuda-um-gpu-page-faults=true \
  -o m0_d20 ./fork_drop_wsl 0 20 3 --gpu 4GB
nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_trace,cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum,um_total_sum m0_d20.nsys-rep


Every round runs 8 `bend_dev` launches. The seventh holds the join. Removing the `term_sink` line takes it from hundreds or thousands of milliseconds to tens, and in mode 0 every other launch stays under 210 ms, with or without the line. The table gives the device time from `cuda_gpu_trace` as the range over 6 rounds (2 runs of 3 rounds):

| CUDA | launch with the join | device time per round |
|---|---|---|
| depth 18, mode 0 (`+t` read by both tasks) | 429 to 496 ms | 468 to 551 ms |
| depth 18, mode 1 (two copies) | 71 to 86 ms | 182 to 398 ms |
| depth 18, mode 0 without the `term_sink` | 33 to 42 ms | 113 to 264 ms |
| depth 20, mode 0 | 1,804 to 7,173 ms | 1,853 to 7,386 ms |
| depth 20, mode 1 | 71 to 300 ms | 166 to 824 ms |
| depth 20, mode 0 without the `term_sink` | 21 to 24 ms | 86 to 116 ms |

At depth 18 the free costs about 0.4 s of device time in every round. At depth 20 the tree has 2^21 - 1 nodes, and the free takes 1.8 to 7.2 s per round, varying between runs. Without the `term_sink`, both tasks still read every node of the same tree, and the launch with the join takes 21 to 42 ms. Mode 1 builds twice as many nodes and still uses less device time per round than mode 0.

On WSL2, Nsight recorded no Unified Memory migrations or page faults in any run. `um_total_sum` finds no transfer data, and the only memory operation is one 143 MB `[CUDA memset]` on managed memory at startup. The numbers above are kernel durations. Whatever WSL2 does to move managed pages happens outside the launches or is not visible to Nsight, and the control without the `term_sink` reads the same pages in the same launches.

Wall time from the second run, on an idle machine. The time per round is (9 rounds - 1 round) / 8, which removes startup and the NVRTC load:

| | 1 round | 9 rounds | per round |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth 18, CUDA, mode 0 | 3,737 ms | 9,500 ms | 720 ms |
| depth 18, CUDA, mode 1 | 2,238 ms | 4,239 ms | 250 ms |
| depth 18, CPU, mode 0 | 9 ms | 37 ms | 3.5 ms |
| depth 18, CPU, mode 1 | 8 ms | 18 ms | 1.3 ms |
| depth 20, CUDA, mode 0 | 6,360 ms | 32,783 ms | 3,303 ms |
| depth 20, CUDA, mode 1 | 2,410 ms | 7,904 ms | 687 ms |
| depth 20, CPU, mode 0 | 18 ms | 100 ms | 10.3 ms |
| depth 20, CPU, mode 1 | 13 ms | 58 ms | 5.6 ms |

CUDA wall times on WSL2 vary a lot between runs. In the first run, with another job loading the CPU, depth 20 took 4,740 ms per round in mode 0 and 170 ms in mode 1. On the CPU, mode 0 is also about twice as slow as mode 1.

The emitted C shows the cause. `shared` is inlined into `round`, and only the join of mode 0 frees the tree:


  WL_CASE(FID_ROUND_J43)            // mode 0: a b = walk.a(t) walk.a(t)
  {
    Term _h_3 = r0;
    u32 _a_2 = r1;
    u32 _b_1 = r2;
    WL_OPEN
    term_sink(e, _h_3);
    r0 = U32_BIN(_a_2, +, _b_1);
    WL_RETN(1);
  }}
  WL_CASE(FID_ROUND_J47)            // mode 1: p q = walk.b(a) walk.b(b)
  {
    u32 _p_2 = r0;
    u32 _q_1 = r1;
    WL_OPEN
    r0 = U32_BIN(_p_2, +, _q_1);
    WL_RETN(1);
  }}


In mode 0, `walk.a` only matches its parameter, so it borrows, and both tasks read the tree without a count. The def that owns the tree frees it after the join with `term_sink`, which walks every node in the one lane that runs the join while the other lanes are idle. In mode 1 each copy has one reader, the reader owns it, and each task frees its nodes as it walks them, in parallel.

I found this in a larger program with the same shape. There the free at the join took about 2.8 ms of a 5 ms device step, and giving each task its own copy brought the step down to 1.8 ms.

Expected: when the last readers of a borrowed value are the tasks of a fork, the free after the join should not run in one lane. For example, the free could be split into tasks like other recursive work, or the compiler could give ownership to one of the two readers.

Related issues:

- #836. The behavior here follows the borrowing rule in `guide/SHADERS.md` (Ownership): "The compiler borrows a boxed parameter (not an `Array`) that the def only matches or passes to a borrower". `walk.a` borrows, and the owner frees the tree at the join. This report is not about the rule. It is about the cost of that free when it runs serially after a fork.
- #1307 reports that the automatic drop gets slow over time while an explicit walk stays fast.

### The file

```python
import Base

# A tree passed as a `+` parameter to a def that only forwards it to both tasks of a fork,
# where each task only reads it. The def keeps the tree until the join and then frees all
# of it in the one thread that runs the join. With two copies, each read once, the readers
# own them and free each node as they walk, in parallel.
#
# Usage: ./fork_drop <mode> <depth> <rounds>
#   mode 0: shared(+t): `a b = walk.a(t) walk.a(t)`, both fork tasks read the same tree
#   mode 1: split(x): the tree is built twice and each fork task reads its own copy
# Each round builds a full tree of 2^depth leaves inside a `!` call, runs the fork and
# returns the sum of the leaves read by both tasks. Prints the total of all rounds, which
# is the same in both modes.

type Tree is Data:
  Leaf{v: U32}
  Node{l: Tree, r: Tree}

type Two is Data:
  Two{a: Tree, b: Tree}

def gen(+d: Nat, +i: U32) -> Tree:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      Leaf{i}
    case 1n+p:
      a b = gen(p, i) gen(p, (i + U32.shln(1, p) : U32))
      Node{a, b}

def two.node(x: Two, y: Two) -> Two:
  match x:
    case Two{xa, xb}:
      match y:
        case Two{ya, yb}:
          Two{Node{xa, ya}, Node{xb, yb}}

def two.leaf(+i: U32) -> Two:
  Two{Leaf{i}, Leaf{i}}

def gen2(+d: Nat, +i: U32) -> Two:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      two.leaf(i)
    case 1n+p:
      a b = gen2(p, i) gen2(p, (i + U32.shln(1, p) : U32))
      two.node(a, b)

# Two copies of the same reader: it only matches the tree. The compiler decides per def
# whether a parameter is borrowed, so each variant below gets its own copy.
def walk.a(t: Tree) -> U32:
  match t:
    case Leaf{v}:
      v
    case Node{l, r}:
      a b = walk.a(l) walk.a(r)
      (a + b : U32)

def walk.b(t: Tree) -> U32:
  match t:
    case Leaf{v}:
      v
    case Node{l, r}:
      a b = walk.b(l) walk.b(r)
      (a + b : U32)

# The tree is a `+` parameter that the def only forwards to the two fork tasks.
def shared(+t: Tree) -> U32:
  a b = walk.a(t) walk.a(t)
  (a + b : U32)

# Each fork task gets its own copy, and nothing is shared.
def split(x: Two) -> U32:
  match x:
    case Two{a, b}:
      p q = walk.b(a) walk.b(b)
      (p + q : U32)

def round.go(c: Bool, +d: Nat) -> U32:
  match c:
    case True{}:
      shared(gen(d, 0))
    case False{}:
      split(gen2(d, 0))

def round(+m: U32, +d: Nat) -> U32:
  round.go(U32.is_eq(m, 0), d)

def rounds(k: Nat, +m: U32, +d: Nat, +acc: U32) -> U32:
  match k:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      rounds(p, m, d, (acc + round!(m, d) : U32))

def rd(s: String) -> U32:
  Maybe.default(&2, U32, U32.read(s), 0)

def run.go(a: String, b: String, c: String) -> String:
  U32.show(rounds(U32.to_nat(rd(c)), rd(a), U32.to_nat(rd(b)), 0)) ++ "\n"

# Takes the last three arguments, whether or not IO.args starts with the program name.
def run.args3(a: String, b: String, t: List<String>) -> String:
  match t:
    case Nil{}:
      ""
    case Con{c, u}:
      match u:
        case Nil{}:
          run.go(a, b, c)
        case Con{d, _}:
          run.go(b, c, d)

def run.args2(a: String, t: List<String>) -> String:
  match t:
    case Nil{}:
      ""
    case Con{b, u}:
      run.args3(a, b, u)

def run.args(xs: List<String>) -> String:
  match xs:
    case Nil{}:
      ""
    case Con{a, t}:
      run.args2(a, t)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    args : List<String> <- IO.args()
    IO.print(run.args(args))
```

### bend --version

The 2.0.36 CLI has no `--version` flag (`bend: unknown option --version`). `bend version` prints `bend 2.0.36`, from the published `bend-2.0.36-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

### uname -sm

`Linux x86_64` (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, on Windows 11; NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, driver 616.92; libnvrtc 12.0.140)

title: ty_holds skips a closure in a later instance of the same datatype
body:
### What you did

Build and run the program below on the CPU and Metal lanes:

```sh
bend main.bend -o main
./main --gpu off
./main --gpu on
```

### What happened

The file checks, and JS and the native CPU lane print `42`. Metal fail-stops with:

```text
bend: a function the device does not hold
```

`ty_holds` sees `Box<Num{}>` first and records `Box` in `seen`, so it does not inspect the fields of the later `Box<Fun{}>` instance. `Pick(Fun{})` and its function are therefore missed. Reversing the two fields of `Duo`, so `Box<Fun{}>` comes first, makes Metal print `42`.

This looks like a remaining case after #1336: the `Tag` argument has a value-taking kind and is skipped, but its value selects the type-family result stored in `Box.value`.

Reproduced on current `main` at `d71f42ee287bd7b9f86b44df44b210ac5eb651bd`.

### The file

```python
import Base

type Tag is Data:
  Num{}
  Fun{}

def Pick(t: Tag) -> Type:
  match t:
    case Num{}:
      U32
    case Fun{}:
      U32 -> U32

type Box<-t: Tag> is Type:
  Box{value: Pick(t)}

type Duo is Type:
  Duo{plain: Box<Num{}>, callable: Box<Fun{}>}

def use(d: Duo) -> U32:
  match d:
    case Duo{plain, callable}:
      match plain:
        case Box{x}:
          match callable:
            case Box{f}:
              f(x)

def make() -> Duo:
  Duo{Box{41}, Box{x => (x + 1 : U32)}}

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(U32.show(use!(make())))

#|42
```

### bend --version

`bend 2.0.36`

### uname -sm

`Darwin arm64`

### clang --version (the first line)

`Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)`

title: An imported forward dotted datatype is resolved as lib.lib:Type
body:
### What you did Check an entry file that imports a library whose type-level family names a dotted local datatype declared later: ```sh bend main.bend --check-only ``` `main.bend`: ```python import Base import ./lib.bend as L def main() -> U32: L.main() ``` `lib.bend`: ```python import Base def Fam(n: Nat) -> Data: match n: case 0n: Unit case 1n+p: Cell.At

type Cell.At<-p: Nat> is Data: Cell{} def main() -> U32: 6 ``` ### What happened `lib.bend` checks by itself, but importing it fails even though `Fam` is unused: ```text SOME PROOFS FAIL Error: - message : a declared datatype (unknown: lib.lib:Cell.At) Context: - p : Nat Location: Fam 5 | case 0n: Unit 6>| case 1n+p: Cell.At

| ^^^^^^^^^ 7 | ``` Moving `type Cell.At` above `Fam`, or renaming it to an undotted `CellAt`, makes the imported file check. This also reproduces by importing the existing passing `tests/check/mutual_type_def.bend`, where `Vec.Con

` becomes `tests/check/mutual_type_def.tests/check/mutual_type_def:Vec.Con`. The `<..>` parser appears to resolve the family head twice. `parse_var` first turns `Cell.At` into the internal key `lib:Cell.At`; because the datatype is declared later, the `<..>` branch then passes that key to `parse_reso` again and gets `lib:lib:Cell.At`. Forward datatypes are available during validation, but the malformed key is already stored in the parsed term. Reproduced on current `main` at `d71f42ee287bd7b9f86b44df44b210ac5eb651bd`. I could not turn this into an `Empty` inhabitant: legal declarations cannot create the two-colon internal key, so this fails closed as an import/order bug. ### bend --version `bend 2.0.36` ### uname -sm `Darwin arm64` ### clang --version (the first line) `Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102)`

title: fix(base): retain representable F32.hypot lengths
body:
`F32.hypot` squares both components before it takes a square root. Those squares can become infinity or zero even when the vector length is representable. For example, `hypot(1e30, 0)` returns infinity and `hypot(1e-30, 0)` returns zero.

Take the absolute values, order them as `hi` and `lo`, and compute `hi * sqrt(1 + (lo / hi)^2)`. Handle zero and infinity before division. The existing NaN result policy stays the same. The examples above return `1e30` and `1e-30` with this change.

This change uses existing Base operations. It adds no compiler primitive, dependency, or effect. The parser and compiler token caps stay unchanged.

Add two regressions. The first checks axis lengths across the F32 exponent range, scaled 3-4-5 triangles, argument order, negative components, the largest finite value, subnormal values, signed zero, infinity, and NaN. The second checks parallel vector lengths with the GPU entry point.

Validation:

- Rebased onto current `main`. The repository gate passes 54/54. `git diff --check` passes.
- All 22 selected math regression programs pass in source, native C, Bun, and Node. The local plan records 121 checks, including controls that reproduce the failure on unchanged upstream code.
- The parallel regression and full exponent-range axis checks pass on Metal. The parallel regression also passes with GPU execution disabled.
- 10,640 reference vectors pass in C, Bun, and Node. Linux C and Bun checks also pass. The largest observed difference from the host `hypotf` or F32-rounded `Math.hypot` reference is two units in the last place. The checks reject an output infinity for a finite reference and an output zero for a positive reference. This sample does not establish a universal error bound or correct rounding.
- The complete generated exponent-regression program passes AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer at `-O0` on macOS and Linux. Linux leak detection is enabled.

CUDA and the repository cluster were not tested. The performance, proof, and release gates were not run. This patch makes no performance claim.

title: fix(cli): extra arguments only for a plain run
body:
Closes #1503

`bend good.bend --verdict bad.bend` checked `good.bend` alone, printed ALL PROOFS CHECK and exited 0. The extra word was kept as an argument for the program, and each mode had to refuse such arguments itself; `--verdict` was missing from that list.

This turns the rule around: extra arguments go to a plain run only. If any option is given (`--verdict`, `--check-only`, `--checkup`, `--publish`, `-o`), extra words are refused with the existing message `arguments go to a run: bend <file.bend> [args]`. A new mode can't miss the list again. Words after `--` still go to the program as before.

Test: `gates/ping.ts` checks that `sum.bend --verdict bad.bend`, `sum.bend extra --verdict` and `sum.bend --check-only extra` exit 1 with that message, and that a plain run still gets its arguments (`argn.bend x -- --verdict` sees 3). With the `main.ts` change reverted, the two `--verdict` cases fail.

Gates: repo 54/54, test 1602/1602, ping 53/53 (main: 49/49).

title: fix(cli): --checkup reads imports with a trailing # comment
body:
Closes #1497.

`bend file.bend --checkup` picked imports with a regex stricter than the loader's (`bend.ts`), so `import ./x.bend as X # note` was skipped silently and the run exited 0.

- `bend2/main.ts`: the import regex and the `import Base` test both accept a trailing `# comment`, like `bend.ts`. No other change; `bend.ts` untouched.
- `gates/ping.ts`: a `--checkup` of two commented imports (one good, one bad) must check both and exit 1.

Gates: repo 54/54, test 1602/1602, ping 54/54. With the import-regex change reverted, the new ping check fails.

title: fix(base): use a plain parameter for F32.show
body:
## Problem and fix

`List.show` and `Maybe.show` accept a plain `A -> String` formatter, but `F32.show` alone declares a `+` input. Passing `~F32.show` directly therefore fails to check. Remove that one `+`, matching the other Base shows and F32 primitives while preserving the language's distinction between plain and `+` function types.

Closes #1511.

## Compatibility break

The public type changes from `@+a: F32 -> String` to `@a: F32 -> String`. Code explicitly expecting the old type can no longer pass `F32.show` directly; use `(x => F32.show(x))` in that expected `+` slot. Type-dependent annotations and proofs may need updating. Direct calls, existing plain lambda adapters, and repeated showing of explicitly `+`-bound values remain covered by checks.

## Blast radius

Two files: one signature line in `bend2/base.bend` and an 11-line regression in `tests/base/f32_show.bend`. The type change affects checked references to `F32.show`, including higher-order consumers beyond List and Maybe. Formatting algorithms, numeric representation, compiler/checker code, and gates are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The new IO test passes `~F32.show` directly to both collection formatters and expects `[1.5, 2.5]` and `Some(1.5)`. On unchanged main it fails checking, CLI execution and compilation with the reported quantity mismatch. With this change, actual CLI IO, emitted JS and native C output match both lines.

## Checks

- New regression and ten controls/adjacent programs check and produce their expected output through CLI IO, emitted JS under Bun, and native C. The new regression's emitted JS also passes under Node.
- All ten controls pass on unchanged main. The regression fails there as described above. The old-signature rejection and its contextual lambda adapter are verified before/after; affine duplication and unrelated quantity conversion still reject.
- Repository gate passes 54/54 with CI-pinned `ttok` 0.3; staged and unstaged `git diff --check` pass.

## Validation limits

Local execution uses macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11, Node 26.8.2 and clang 23.1.3. CLI IO and emitted JS share the JS runtime; native C is also exercised. Full cluster test/perf/ping/safe gates, Lean verdict, GPU execution, and Linux/Windows program execution were not run. These checks do not establish ecosystem-wide compatibility or pure reduction of the axiomatic formatter.

title: fix(io): flush buffered output before IO.exit
body:
## Problem and fix

Native `IO.print("buffered")` followed by `IO.exit(0)` can report success even when stdout's reader has closed. The short output stays buffered, and libc's implicit exit flush bypasses Bend's stream-error handling.

Call the existing `io_sync()` after exit-code validation and before native `exit`. This applies the [accepted stream-error policy](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1470): EPIPE terminates quietly by SIGPIPE; other flush failures use the existing diagnostic/status 1. This intentionally changes the exit status when earlier buffered output fails. Healthy output, requested exit codes, quiet exit behavior and invalid-code validation remain intact.

## Blast radius

Four files: one added line in `bend2/comp.ts` and an extension to the existing `tests/io/stream_epipe.{bend,c,js}` regression. The native Halt/Exit branch shares the flush; Halt already flushes through its error writer. No Base API, parser, device runtime, main-result semantics, gate or cap changes.

## Regression evidence

The existing native pipe/fork fixture now resumes its first child into checked `IO.print` followed by `IO.exit(7)`. It reports `exit: 7` on main and `exit: 141` with the fix, including under a PTY; removing only the flush restores the failure. Existing stdout/stderr cases remain. The JS twin continues to check its synchronous writer, which encounters EPIPE before exit.

## Checks

- Repository gate: 54/54; compiler 63,071/64,000 tokens with CI-pinned ttok 0.3.
- Final regression passes source interpretation, emitted Bun JS and native execution. Focused native controls preserve healthy exit codes 0/7/255, reject 256, and preserve Halt behavior.
- Nearby print, UTF-8, exit and main-result fixtures checked through source, emitted JS and available native lanes; Node controls also run.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Validation limits

Local execution used macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11, Node 26.8.2 and clang 23.1.3. Linux, Windows, GPU paths, installed compiled CLI and full cluster test/perf/ping/safe gates were not run; the cluster hostname is unavailable locally.

Node's `stderr_failure` fixture has the same pre-existing `errno 2` versus `No such file or directory` output mismatch on main and this branch. Node stream_epipe was skipped because its existing twin requires bun:ffi; exit_status has no native twin. `--check-only` rejects these two foreign fixtures identically on main and this branch; their normal build and execution lanes pass.

title: fix(compiler): hand last fork readers counted ownership together
body:
Fixes #1512.

The fork emitter retained a locally owned tree until its last borrowed readers joined, then erased the entire tree in one lane. Last fork readers now receive counted ownership together through the existing `val_own` fact gate. Argument materialization accounts for the still-pending calls and continuation, so earlier readers obtain their references before the last argument consumes the original. The obsolete fork-specific argument-counting mode is removed. A retained continuation owner remains live; an outside borrow follows the existing loan propagation. No one-owner/one-borrower handoff, leak, unsafe mode, GPU guard bypass, or new runtime scheduler.

Permanent lifetime coverage uses two different recursively forked readers, a returned tree consumed after the join, and a bang. Existing mixed consumer/dead-reader/array/fork cases remain. Obsolete comments promising a whole-value join sink were updated; hand-written GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, protected bend.ts and all gates/caps are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

Linux x86_64, Bun CLI 1.3.13, Node v22.23.1, clang 22.1.8. Refreshed onto main `381dc877`, including the merged #1509 budget reduction and #1506 number seam.

- Original issue program, mode 0, depth 20, 25 rounds, 8 CPU workers. Seven interleaved before/after pairs, alternating order: current-main median **552.711 ms**, fixed median **278.720 ms**. Every run prints `4268752896`. These are local CPU whole-process measurements, not GPU/kernel timings; all samples retained, including two slower early fixed runs.
- The generated mode-0 join previously captured the tree and executed `term_sink(e, _h_3)`; the fixed join captures only the two U32 results. The readers own and free their references instead; the sink was not merely deleted.
- Fourteen lifetime/fork programs were built to native C and each executed with 1 and 8 workers: **28/28** expected outputs. The new program also ran through the real CLI and standalone Node, printing `6144`, `11264`, `6144`.
- Final current-main code compiled with `clang -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer ... -lpthread -lm`; original shared-tree workload at depth 16, 40 rounds, 8 workers prints `4292345856`, with no sanitizer findings observed. The custom heap pool means ASan alone does not prove zero pool leaks.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **54/54**. Existing 64,000-token compiler cap unchanged.

Exact workload command: `./fork_drop 0 20 25 --gpu off --threads 8`. Safety commands: `bend tests/reg/fork_last_readers_tree.bend -o safety`, then `./safety --gpu off --threads 1` and `--threads 8`.

## Limits and tradeoff

No CUDA/Metal execution or GPU performance claim; an actual `--gpu on` attempt reports that this Linux binary has no CUDA or Metal support. The 48-mini test/perf gates and graphical shader benchmarks were not run. Borrow/own calling convention is inferred per definition, so ownership facts can affect other calls to a reader; retained-owner and mixed-reader paths are covered locally, but device performance still requires upstream hardware qualification. No flaky permanent wall-clock threshold was added: interleaved benchmark evidence covers the performance change; permanent regressions cover consumer-visible lifetime correctness.

title: fix(compiler): inspect sibling datatype instances independently
body:
Fixes #1513.

`ty_holds` used a datatype-name set as a global visited set. After opening `Box<Num{}>`, it skipped the fields of the sibling `Box<Fun{}>` and missed the host-minted closure. Track active datatype expansions instead: remove the name after scanning its constructor fields. Recursive-name cycle protection remains, but sibling value-indexed instances are inspected independently. No type-key serialization, copied visited sets, checker changes, runtime workaround, or special-case Box/Tag handling.

Adds the original two-Box closure-bang program as a permanent regression for the existing GPU-enabled test gate. The helper's source documentation explains the active-path invariant. Protected `bend2/bend.ts`, hand-written `guide/GUIDE.md`, release-only CHANGELOG.md and gates/caps are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

Linux x86_64, Bun CLI 1.3.13, Node v22.23.1, clang 22.1.8. Based on current main `381dc877`.

- Actual CLI and native C (`--gpu off --threads 4`) run the reported program and print **42**. CPU execution is a control: it already succeeds on main and does not reproduce the original Metal failure.
- Build the same program to C with current main and the fixed compiler. Run **actual CUDA-branch preprocessing**, `clang -E -P -x c -D__CUDACC_RTC__=1 program.c`, without emulating a GPU or changing its guards. The host-minted closure is FID 4 in these artifacts. Before: the device evaluator has no case 4 and retains the missing-function error default. After: case 4 is included in the real device dispatch. This proves the changed compiler path, not a GPU runtime pass.
- **17** existing/new closure, recursive indexed/pair/list, and current plain-number Nat seam CLI executions match their expected outputs.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **54/54**.

An earlier real JS BigInt-seam reproduction was removed from this patch after upstream #1506 changed Nat host values to numbers and removed the old converter. It is not repinned to an incidental new default.

## Validation limits

Metal/CUDA hardware and the 48-mini distributed gate were unavailable. The permanent original regression must run on the existing upstream GPU-enabled gate; no actual device success or performance is claimed here. The preprocessing comparison is a throwaway artifact check, not a permanent source-text test.
