title: JS IO: a nested run overwrites the outer scheduler and silently drops IO.spawn work
body:
### Reproduction on current main

Verified on Linux x86_64, Bun CLI 1.3.13, current main `0e14aa8b3082e68f419320b2c785762de1d0577b`. A foreign JS effect runs a nested IO action, then the outer program spawns a child. Both IO programs exit successfully, but the child's effect never runs.

`main.bend`:
```bend
import Base

def Host.nested() -> IO(Unit):
  import "./nested.js"

def child() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print("child")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    Unit <- Host.nested()
    IO.spawn(Unit, child())
```

`nested.js`:
```js
function host_nested(k) {
  const code = io_run(() => (cont) => ({
    $: CID(IO.print), args: ["inner"], kont: cont,
  }));
  if (code !== 0) throw "nested IO failed";
  return { $: CID(Unit) };
}
io_eff(CID(Host.nested), host_nested);
```

Run: `bun bend2/main.ts /absolute/path/main.bend`.

Expected stdout:
```text
inner
child
```
Observed stdout (exit 0):
```text
inner
```

### Mechanism

`RUNTIME_MAIN` stores the running scheduler in `globalThis.BEND_IO`. The nested `io_run` overwrites that value and never restores it. `io_push` subsequently enqueues the outer `IO.spawn` action onto the already-finished inner scheduler; the outer scheduler reaches live=0 and exits without executing the child. `io_park_on` and channel deadline removal read the same global.

This is distinct from the closure reentry regression in `tests/io/reenter_closure.bend`: the lost state is the IO scheduler rather than the pure-function trampoline. It also makes independently generated IO programs share one process-global scheduler pointer.

I will isolate scheduler state per generated program and restore the active scheduler across nested completion or failure, with real CLI and emitted-JS before/after evidence. No parser/theory/checker or gate changes are needed.

title: fix(runtime): isolate nested JS IO schedulers
body:
## Description
Fixes #1524.

Keep IO scheduler state local to each generated JS program and restore the parent scheduler in `finally` when an effect enters a nested `io_run`. Migrate channel deadline removal to the same local state; remove the process-global scheduler pointer rather than retain an alias.

## Real behavior proof
Linux x86_64, Bun CLI 1.3.13 and Node v22.23.1; pristine upstream base `0e14aa8b3082e68f419320b2c785762de1d0577b`.

Actual CLI regression:
```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/io/reenter_scheduler.bend
```
Before (exit 0):
```text
inner
outer-complete
```
After (exit 0):
```text
inner
outer-complete
child
after-error
```
The fixture runs real nested IO on the success path and a real throwing inner computation on the failure path; the outer spawned effects must execute in both cases. The same four-line output was observed after emission with `-o after.js`, on both `node after.js` and `bun after.js`.

## Regression checks
- 18 real CLI cases passed against their checked-in expected stdout and exit codes: scheduler/closure reentry, channel try/close/rendezvous/pipeline/deadlines, sleep ordering, fork/join, spawned-work lifetimes, timeout and confluence paths.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 54 / 54`.
- No edits to `bend2/bend.ts`, `guide/GUIDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, gates or caps.

## Limits
No native C scheduler change or GPU runtime claim. No remote mini-cluster run. The new foreign regression is JS-only, matching the existing closure reentry convention.

title: fix(cpu): a grow runs a fork-free task in place when a fork follows it (#1475)
body:
Follows #1479, which fixed #1475 for flat code and left one case open. If the work before each fork is a non-flat call (one that isn't a tail loop, so it isn't inlined as a `spin_N`), a fork tree still got about 2x from 16 threads, even when that call does nothing. #1479 put that down to the non-flat leaves, which was wrong: the leaves scale fine. What caps it is the call before the fork.

## The cause

`./nonflat 8 2000000 0 --threads T --gpu off` is #1475's tree with a non-flat `spin`. At K = 0, the call `spin(0, i)` before each fork returns at once. M3 Max, median of 3:

| tree | 1 thread | 16 threads, main | 16 threads, this branch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| non-flat `spin` at the leaves only | 0.93 s | 0.09 s | 0.09 s |
| the same, plus `spin(0, i)` before each fork | 0.94 s | 0.47 s | 0.09 s |

Removing the empty call removes the cap. Here is how the call stops the grow:

- **Handoff.** Outside sequential code, `emit_jump` doesn't run a fork-free (nofk) callee inline. It returns it to the caller as a task (`!DEVICE && !seq && fid_nofk(fid)`), and the continuation K after the call waits on it.
- **The grow defers it.** When `monk_step` is growing (`stride != 0`), it pushes any ready nofk task back onto a ring for the drain and ends the pass. That's right for a call that a join follows. It's wrong for a call that a fork follows, because the grow never reaches that fork.
- **The drain serializes the subtree.** The drain runs the task sequentially, and `FID_EXIT` keeps it sequential for the K. So the fork after the call, and every level below it, runs on one thread's stack.
- **In #1475's tree:** the root's fork deals 2 tasks, and each row's first grow step returns `spin`, so nothing grows. The drain then holds 2 tasks, each a 128-leaf subtree, on 2 threads, and the other 14 sit idle. Flat `spin` is inlined, so there's no handoff, and the grow runs it and reaches the fork.

## What changes

`monk_step` runs a ready nofk task in place, inside the grow, when its continuation can fork:

```c
if (stride != 0 && nofk && (DEVICE || k == TERM_HOLE
  || !fid_resw((u32)term_aux(k)) || fid_nofk((u32)term_aux(k)))) {
  ring_push(H, ring_pick(base, stride, cur), r);
  return 2;
}
t      = r;
seq    = false;
stride = nofk ? stride : 0;
```

Each condition has a reason:

- **`fid_resw(k) != 0` picks out a K:** a segment with a frame, whose results arrive in registers. A join has no frame, so its `resw` is 0. Without this check, a leaf that tail-calls a nofk function into a join that can fork would run leaf work inside the grow.
- **`!fid_nofk(k)` means the code after the call can fork.** A task followed by a fork-free K stays deferred, as before.
- **`k == TERM_HOLE` guards the root.** Its `term_aux` is 0xFFFF, which would index past `FID_T`. `FID_EXIT` has the same guard.
- **`DEVICE ||` keeps the GPU schedule exactly as it was.** The device never hands off calls.
- **The stride is kept.** The fork after the call then deals within the row, as inlined code does. Setting it to 0 would send its kids out through `H_CURSOR` instead.

The ring-head skip doesn't change. No nofk task whose K can fork reaches a ring head: the grow no longer pushes one, and `task_deal` pushes only fork kids, which a join follows.

The risk is the same one inlined code already carries. If the K forks in only some branches (`x = heavy(d); match d: 0 → x; _ → fork`), a grow runs `heavy` at the leaves too.

`comp.ts` goes from 63,067 to 63,147 tokens.

## Results

M3 Max, `--gpu off`, median of 3. Both builds print the same output in every row.

| non-flat tree, 8 levels, 2M leaf steps | 1 thread | 4 threads, main → branch | 16 threads, main → branch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K = 0 | 0.94 s | 0.47 → 0.24 s | 0.48 → 0.09 s |
| K = 2M | 1.87 s | 0.93 → 0.48 s | 0.94 → 0.19 s |

The flat tree from #1475 (`spread 8 20000000 K`) is unchanged, at K = 0 and K = 20M, on 4 and 16 threads.

## Test

`tests/run/fork_after_call.bend` covers both shapes that reach the new path. An instrumented build confirmed each:

- **`spin` before `spread`'s fork:** reached 254 times at 4 and at 16 threads.
- **`pair`'s join, which tail-calls `spin` and returns into `chain`'s fork:** reached once.

`pair`'s kids call `leaf`, which can fork, so the grow runs them and reaches the join. Fork-free kids would be left for the drain, and the join would never be reached in the grow. The test prints `417464320` and `2860191008` in the interpreter, under bun, and in C at 1, 4 and 16 threads, on main and on this branch.

## Benches (local A/B)

- **Output:** every bench prints its pinned output on the 16-thread CPU path, and spot checks on one thread and with the GPU on printed the same.

title: feat(cli): emit faithful TypeScript module declarations
body:
## Description
Fixes #1144.

`-o core.mjs` now emits `core.d.mts` from checked telescopes and constructor fields. Runtime and declaration export filtering share `js_exports`; the module retains its default object, while declaration named exports are type-only. Native Nat follows current main's number ABI (#1506), not the older BigInt example in the issue.

The declarations preserve recursive tagged values, generic datatype fields, arrays, callback shapes and every prefix of a partially applied exported function. Private identifiers are encoded separately from public type names, including reserved names. Erased/template, kind-returning and unresolved type-family signatures remain runtime exports but are omitted from declarations; an unmapped concrete type reports the def and writes neither file. No `any` approximation.

Both generated paths use the existing input/directory guard before either is written. The separate existing hard-link issue #1495 / PR #1496 is not claimed fixed here.

## Real behavior proof
Linux x86_64; Bun CLI 1.3.13, Node v22.23.1, TypeScript 5.9.3 installed as isolated verification tooling, not a repository dependency.

Before, the real typed consumer failed with exit 2 / TS7016 (no declaration for `core.mjs`). After actual CLI emission:
```sh
bun bend2/main.ts core.bend -o core.mjs
node path/to/typescript/bin/tsc --strict --module nodenext --target esnext good.mts
node good.mjs
```
Four actual TypeScript-compiled Node hosts passed:
- Slot/List consumer: `true 9`.
- Recursive Tree, callback and full/partial/zero-prefix calls: `10 10 9 9 9 9`.
- Reserved type name `class` and helper-like type `BendFn`: `7 8`.
- Native array update: `[8,5]`.

Negative TypeScript consumers are rejected with TS2614 (invented named value export), TS2345 (invalid direct/partial call), TS2322 (malformed constructor field) and TS2339 (intentionally omitted erased signature). A concrete indexed type not mapped by this emitter exits 1 naming `identity`; neither output is created.

## Regression checks
- Permanent `tests/io/module_declaration_safety.bend` and its real JS effect invoke the actual CLI against a derived-sidecar input symlink and directory. Before: prints `1`; after: `0`, source preserved and no partial module output.
- 20 real existing module/FFI/closure/marshal CLI cases matched their checked-in stdout and exit statuses.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 54 / 54`.
- README updated. No parser/theory/checker, GUIDE, CHANGELOG, gate or cap edits.

## Limits
No remote mini-cluster/macOS execution. Full dependent type semantics cannot be represented by TypeScript; only faithfully mapped signatures are declared, following the omission/error policy above. Static host checks were exercised with TypeScript 5.9.3.

title: fix(js): integrate host promises and event-loop callbacks into IO
body:
Fixes #1148. Depends on #1525's program-local/reentrant scheduler; that commit is included in this stacked branch.

The JS IO dispatcher is now asynchronous. Idle runs use host timers; continuously runnable chains yield to the host event loop every 64 dispatcher operations. Descriptor readiness remains Bun FFI, polled nonblocking at a 1 ms interval while parked rather than blocking the JS thread in select. Timer-only and Promise-only runs do not load bun:ffi.

`io_park_promise(promise, k, done, fail)` captures the owning run, maps fulfillment/rejection into a resumed continuation, propagates mapper exceptions, and ignores settlements after exit without claiming to cancel the underlying host operation. Pending host operations prevent false channel-deadlock detection and premature event-loop shutdown. `Comp.io_run` returns Promise<number>; CLI plain runs/checkup, emitted standalone exit handling, and nested-run consumers have been migrated. Pure evaluation remains synchronous.

Actual Linux verification (Bun 1.3.13, Node 22.23.1):
- Parked Promise microtask reproducer: before `4294967295`, after `1`; always-runnable IO reproducer: before `0`, after `1`.
- Actual CLI and emitted Node/Bun complete already-resolved, timer-backed, rejected and WebCrypto SHA-256 promises; digest of abc is ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad.
- Actual asynchronous localhost DNS lookup completes in all three runtimes.
- Sent SIGTERM after each program printed ready: the installed host handler ran and Bend received 15 in all three runtimes.
- Mapper exceptions terminate with exit 1 and the expected stderr, rather than becoming unhandled rejections or a hung run.
- Public Comp.io_run consumer returned exit 7; after the real delayed host operation settled, its mapper had not run.
- 26 actual CLI consumer/deadlock scenarios pass, including timer ordering, channels, nested scheduler success/error, TCP concurrency, parallel subprocesses and exit status.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54; protected files and gate limits unchanged.

Native C/GPU scheduling is unchanged. Host descriptor polling has an explicit 1 ms latency/CPU tradeoff; this does not introduce a native asynchronous descriptor API. Existing effects documentation describes the Promise contract and cancellation boundary.

title: A long spin is a call on the host too: nbody 1.17x on SEQ and PAR (#1240)
body:
`emit_native` marks a spin of `SPIN_FAR` (8192) or more characters `DFAR`, which was `FAR` (`static __attribute__((noinline))`) on the device and `INLINE` on the host. #1240 measured that nbody's one long spin runs 1.18x faster on the CPU as a call, and asked why. This makes `DFAR` `FAR` on both lanes and drops the macro.

## The cause

With the spin inlined into its caller, clang's SLP vectorizer packs the step's three pair kernels (scalar f32 math on 24 live words) into 2-lane NEON ops. The step loop in `WL_FID_BATCH` is 261 instructions: 24 `fmul.2s`, 14 `fadd.2s`, 12 `dup.2s`, 9 `mov.s`, 8 `fmov` and the `eor.8b`/`and.8b`/`shl.2s` of the boxing, plus a scalar `fsqrt` next to an `fsqrt.2s`. As a call, `spin_4`'s loop is 118 instructions, all scalar (60 `fmul`, 30 `fadd`, 15 `fsub`, 3 `fsqrt`, 3 `fdiv`).

Two checks that it is the vectorizer and not the call itself:

- `cc -O3 -fno-slp-vectorize` on the inlined build gets the same time as the call (nbody SEQ: inlined 9.68 s, call 8.28 s, inlined without SLP 8.27 s).
- The flag is not the fix: it costs kmeans 1.25x on SEQ (6.53 → 8.14 s) and 1.2x on PAR, where SLP packs its U32 math well. `gates/perf.ts` carried `-fno-slp-vectorize` until 386b7fc1 dropped it to grade what `bend -o` builds, and `bend -o` never had it.

So the rule is the one the device already has: a spin past `SPIN_FAR` is a call. The device side is unchanged.

## Results

M3 Max, `cc -std=c11 -O3 main.c -lpthread` (the gate's line), `--gpu off`, each binary warmed once, then 5 interleaved rounds, medians. Every output matches. Only four benches have a spin past `SPIN_FAR`, so the other thirteen emit the same C.

| bench | SEQ main | SEQ branch | PAR (16) main | PAR branch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| kmeans | 6.562 s | 6.542 s | 0.597 s | 0.592 s |
| merkle | 7.908 s | 7.910 s | 0.596 s | 0.596 s |
| nbody | 9.604 s | 8.234 s (1.17x) | 0.677 s | 0.589 s (1.15x) |
| raytrace | 7.554 s | 7.630 s (0.99x) | 0.566 s | 0.569 s |

raytrace's 1% on SEQ is the 0.98x #1240 measured on the M4; kmeans and merkle are unchanged. The C twin of nbody runs in 9.13 s here, so the Bend build now beats it.

nbody on Metal (`--gpu 768MB`) prints 3516450380 as before; the device program is the same.

## Tests

Eight tests emit a `FAR` spin on the host now (`compile/nat_pattern_deep`, `compile/record_deep_boxed`, `compile/record_wide_node`, `compile/string_match_sparse`, `flatten/literal_rows_cubic`, `reg/nat_chain`, `reg/wide_record_drop`, `reg/wide_record_stale`); each builds with `bend -o` (clang -O3) and prints its `#|` lines. No test is added: the change is codegen, and the perf gate grades it. `comp.ts` goes from 63,291 to 63,237 tokens.

title: fix(runtime)!: runtime options go between +RTS and -RTS (#1466)
body:
Fixes #1466. Follows #1476, which read the runtime's settings from the environment. It was closed in favor of "a solution that is more similar to what haskell does" ([comment](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1476#issuecomment-6129883098)). This PR is that design: a compiled program reads its argv the way GHC's RTS does. It also finishes what #934 and #988 started for `--help`, for the remaining runtime options.

## The rule

- **The bracket:** the runtime's options are the words between `+RTS` and `-RTS`. A trailing `-RTS` can be left off.
- **Everything else** is the program's (`IO.args`), in order. Outside a bracket, `--threads`, `--gpu`, `--gpu-build` and `--bend-help` are ordinary arguments.
- **`--`** stops the runtime from reading options and is passed to the program. So runtime options are still taken only until the first `--`, and the program now sees that `--`.
- **`--RTS`** does the same as `--` but is dropped.
- **`BENDRTS`** holds options too. It's read before the command line, so `./main +RTS --threads 4` overrides `BENDRTS="--threads 8"`.
- **Spans:** `BENDRTS` and each bracket are read separately, so an option's value must be in the same span. `BENDRTS="--threads" ./main +RTS 2` fails, and so does `./main +RTS --threads -RTS x +RTS 2`.
- **Unknown options:** an unknown word inside a bracket fails with `bend: unknown runtime option --bogus`. So does an empty word.
- **Values:** `--threads` takes digits, at least 1. `--gpu` takes `on`, `off`, or digits with at most one point followed by `GB` or `MB`, above zero. main's C parser (`strtol`, `strtod`) also took a sign, leading spaces, an exponent or hex, so `--gpu 1e2GB` and `--threads +4` worked there; they fail now, on C and JS alike.

GHC does the same in its [argv loop](https://github.com/ghc/ghc/blob/f217fc315b7fc67a7a96bafc08f30399e634f537/rts/RtsFlags.c#L798-L829) and with [`GHCRTS`](https://github.com/ghc/ghc/blob/f217fc315b7fc67a7a96bafc08f30399e634f537/rts/RtsFlags.c#L768-L786).

## Before and after

`args` prints `IO.args()`, #1466's program; the head is left out below. These rows are from the C binary. The JS build of this branch prints the same lists.

| `./args …` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `grep -e --threads notes.txt` | `bend: expected a thread count of 1 or more after --threads`, exit 1 | `[<grep>, <-e>, <--threads>, <notes.txt>]` |
| `compress --threads auto` | the same error, exit 1 | `[<compress>, <--threads>, <auto>]` |
| `build --threads 4` | `[<build>]` | `[<build>, <--threads>, <4>]` |
| `make --gpu-build` | no output, exit 0; `main` never runs | `[<make>, <--gpu-build>]` |
| `grep -- -v` | `[<grep>, <-v>]` | `[<grep>, <-->, <-v>]` |
| `grep +RTS --threads 4 -RTS -v` | `[<grep>, <+RTS>, <-RTS>, <-v>]` | `[<grep>, <-v>]` |
| `--bend-help` | the runtime's usage | `[<--bend-help>]` |

## Migration

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `./main --threads 8` | `./main +RTS --threads 8`, or `BENDRTS="--threads 8" ./main` |
| `./main -- -v` | `./main -v` |
| `./main --bend-help` | `./main +RTS --bend-help` |
| `./main --gpu-build` | `./main +RTS --gpu-build` (`bend -o` passes it itself) |

A binary keeps its old behavior until it's rebuilt.

## What changes

- **`bend2/comp.ts`:**
  - The C `main` collects `BENDRTS`'s words and the bracketed words, then parses them with the existing option code. A NULL closes each span, so a value can't come from the next one and an empty argument stays an argument.
  - `CLI_HELP` describes the bracket.
  - The out-of-memory error's hint reads `+RTS --gpu 8GB`, since a bare `--gpu 8GB` is now the program's argument.
  - The JS `cli()` drops the bracket the same way. The JS runtime has no options to set, but it checks a bracket's option names and values with C's grammar and messages, so a typo fails on both. `+RTS --gpu-build` exits 0 with no output. JS ignores `BENDRTS`.
  - `let cli_args = [];` is unchanged, since bend-lint's seam matches that line.
  - Size: comp.ts goes from 63,495 to 63,953 tokens, under its 64k cap. Rebased as is, it came to 64,151, so the last commit makes room without changing behavior. It drops `main`'s and `cli`'s comments, since `CLI_HELP` states the rule. It also drops three comments that repeat another: JS `show_val`'s and `io_list`'s (the C ones say the same) and `ring_rewind`'s. An unknown option prints and returns 1, as `--gpu-build`'s failure does, and JS's size pattern is shorter but accepts the same set.
  - `BENDRTS` is 90 of those tokens, so it can be dropped if you'd rather not have it.
- **`bend2/main.ts`:** `bend -o` runs `+RTS --gpu-build`, with `BENDRTS` cleared so the user's options can't change or break the build.
- **`gates/perf.ts`:** `FLAGS` gets the bracket. `gen_pins.ts` reads the same constant.
- **`gates/ping.ts`:** adds two checks beside "a plain run gets its arguments":
  - A built program's argv on C and JS: runtime option names, `--`, an empty argument and a space are kept, and a mid-line bracket is dropped.
  - `--RTS` is dropped and ends the options, a valid `BENDRTS` is accepted, and `BENDRTS="--threads 0"` exits 1, as does a value in the span after its option.
  - `+RTS --thread 2`, `+RTS --gpu of`, `+RTS --gpu 1e2GB`, `+RTS '' -RTS` and a value across brackets fail with exit 1 and the same stderr on C and JS.
  - The test gate passes no arguments, so it can't cover this.
- **`tests/io/args.bend`:** only its comment changes.

## Not in this PR

- **`bend file.bend …` is unchanged.** The driver accepts its options after the file (`bend <file.bend> -o <out>`), so the program's arguments still follow its `--`, as with `cargo run -- …`. The interpreter has no runtime options, so it passes the words after `--` through unchanged, `+RTS` included.
- **Build-time defaults are left out.** GHC's `-with-rtsopts` and `-rtsopts` could come later.
- **The BendRT paper doesn't change.** It names `--threads` and `--gpu`, and those names stay.

## Suggested doc changes (not committed)

**guide/GUIDE.md:** it's human-edited and sits at 7,998 of its 8,000 tokens, so the two GPU lines become one. With this change it's at 7,993:

```diff
-answers the command line, less the runtime's own options (a `--` ends them):
-its head is the program as invoked, like C's `argv[0]`. A handle (`File`,
+answers the command line, less the runtime's options (`+RTS` to `-RTS`): its
+head is the program as invoked, like C's `argv[0]`. A handle (`File`,
```

```diff
-./file --threads 8        # run a native binary on 8 CPU threads
-./file --gpu off          # run ! calls on the CPU (the GPU is on by default)
-./file --gpu 4GB          # cap the GPU's heap at 4GB
+./file +RTS --threads 8   # run a native binary on 8 CPU threads
+./file +RTS --gpu 4GB     # cap the GPU heap at 4GB; off runs ! calls on the CPU
```

**guide/SHADERS.md:24:** `` `--gpu off` `` becomes `` `+RTS --gpu off` ``.

## Spelling

`+RTS` and `-RTS` match GHC exactly, so GHC's documentation of them applies here as written. If you'd prefer a Bend-specific spelling like `+bend` and `-bend`, it's a rename in the C and JS loops.

## What I ran

All on an M3 Max Mac, rebased onto main at d2aeefc1.

- **The table above:** built with main's compiler and with this branch. I also checked both builds against the bracket mid-line and at the end, `--RTS`, `--` inside a bracket, `BENDRTS` with extra whitespace, and an empty, a spaced and a Unicode argument.
- **Options take effect:**
  - `IO.thread_count` prints 3 with `+RTS --threads 3`, and 5 with `BENDRTS="--threads 5"`.
  - It prints 3 when given both, so the command line wins.
  - Without a bracket, `./tc --threads 3` prints the CPU count.
- **Metal:** `bend -o` on `tests/run/array_atomic_fadd.bend` writes `fadd.gpu`, and the binary prints `68` and `2448.25`, also with `+RTS --gpu 512MB`, `--gpu .5GB` and `--gpu off`. It still does with `BENDRTS="--bend-help"` or `BENDRTS="--threads 0"` set. `./fadd +RTS --gpu-build` exits 0 with no output. I didn't test a host with no GPU; that code path is unchanged.
- **The new ping checks:** the full ping gate needs the site repo, which I don't have. I ran the same checks with `bun bend2/main.ts` as `bend`. All 7 pass on this branch, and 6 fail on its first commit.
- **C and JS agree** on 41 bracket inputs, with the same exit code and stderr. Accepted: `--gpu 4GB`, `512MB`, `0.5GB`, `.5GB`, `5.GB`, `on`, `off`, and `--threads 3`, `007`. Rejected: `--gpu +1GB`, `1e2GB`, `" 4GB"`, `0x10GB`, `infGB`, `0GB`, `4gb`; `--threads " 3"`, `+3`, `0`, `3x`; an empty word; `constructor`; and `--threads -RTS 2`.
- **Tests:** `gates/test.ts`'s shard script, run locally on this Mac in 4 shards, passes **1633 / 1635**.
  - The two failures are `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`. They expect "no display", but this Mac has a desktop session, so a window opens.
  - main fails the same two here.
- **Repo gate:** `gates/repo.ts` passes, 54 / 54.
- **tsc:** no new errors.
- **bend-lint:** loads and checks a file.
- **Not run:** the cluster gates, the perf gate (only its `FLAGS` change), Linux and CUDA.

title: The verdict says why each def it lists relies on unsafe or foreign code
body:
Many useful programs rely on a foreign effect: a SQLite binding, a DNS lookup, a folder listing for a small glob engine. About a quarter of BendHub's packages ship effects of their own (90 of 362). Their users' verdict prints `SOME PROOFS FAIL` with the same message as a program with an `@unsafe` def that can prove anything. A reader cannot tell "this app trusts host code to list a folder" from "this app's proofs may be false". So an app looks less trustworthy than it is, only because it uses a simple effect.

This PR keeps the verdict as it is, and says what each listed def relies on: the promise it is (`@unsafe` or `foreign`), or the promises it relies on, nearest first:

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error: 4 defs rely on unsafe or foreign code:
- lib.Clock.now: foreign
- spin: @unsafe
- tick: through lib.Clock.now
- both: through spin, lib.Clock.now
```

- Only the text changes. The defs listed, their order, PASS or FAIL and the exit code are as on `main`: `book_promises` finds the same set, then walks each listed def's names to the promises it reaches.
- The 14 tests that print the list gain the label on each line, and nothing else. In `check/unsafe_kind*`, it shows that their defs rely on Base's own `@unsafe` `Array.join`.
- `bend.ts` and GUIDE.md are unchanged.

## What I verified

- On WSL (Ubuntu, Bun 1.4.3), each of the 14 tests, with the new labels removed, prints exactly its old `#|` lines. Its new lines are that output.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54 (`main.ts`: 11,360 of 16,000 ttok).
- `tsc -p bend2/pack`: no error in `main.ts`.
- The full test gate was not run.

title: fix(runtime): reclaim native channel rows and unread buffered values
body:
Fixes #1268. Native Chan is now an owned heap row with an owned FIFO of two-Term nodes, using existing ARR reference counting and iterative term_drop. The global row table, generation handles and deferred row recycling are removed. Each effect consumes its handle; parked operations retain it until wake/deadline. Close still wakes waiters and preserves buffered FIFO contents for copied handles. Receiving transfers a value out, and a full-channel dequeue reuses its node when waking a queued sender. Capacity is logical: creating a channel no longer reserves/touches a capacity-sized ring. No new runtime tag, finalizer framework or garbage collector.

Actual Linux/clang 22.1.8 verification:
- 500,000 room-one buffered send/close iterations, --threads 4, exit 0 and done: baseline peak RSS 40,728 KiB; treatment 2,232 KiB. Empty-close control: 2,268 -> 2,140 KiB. Exact commands use /usr/bin/time -f 'RSS_KIB=%M elapsed=%e'. Single-run elapsed samples are not a general performance claim.
- 26 actual native consumer runs at 1/4 threads pass: copied closed-buffer FIFO, boxed values, final parked handle/deadline, rendezvous, try-send/receive, wake/timer cancellation, fork/join and channel-only deadlock termination.
- Earlier clang AddressSanitizer runs at 4 threads reported no diagnostics for ordinary allocations such as waiter timers. ASan cannot see Bend heap row/node bounds or prove their reclamation. This x86 runtime pins registers; those builds use -fomit-frame-pointer -mllvm -x86-use-base-pointer=false with -fsanitize=address.
- Both new consumer fixtures also pass the actual Bun CLI's unchanged JS backend.
- Repository gate: PASS 54 / 54. Protected files and gate limits unchanged.

There is deliberately no permanent RSS threshold: standalone before/after/control measurements prove reclamation; deterministic regressions cover ownership transitions without depending on platform RSS or sanitizer overhead. Native Chan's opaque foreign representation changes, documented in EFFECTS; foreign effects already have no ABI promise. Lifetime follows the existing native reference-counting model, not tracing collection of cycles. No Metal/CUDA run is claimed.

### Review follow-up (a781bf72)

Preserved maintainer d95603ca: Chan handles are born RFC-wrapped so sharing a Data container does not fail-stop. The retained chan_shared_node fixture prints 78end on actual native 1/4-thread runs, interpreter and emitted JS. Rebuilt 26 existing native channel/fiber consumer runs pass their success/error contracts. Repo gate passes 54/54.

Added chan_reclaim_limit.bend: 16,777,217 discarded, never-explicitly-closed handles. Original main fails with the old lifetime-limit diagnostic; after-fix native and JS print done. Single Linux samples: native 1.23s / 2,228 KiB peak RSS, emitted JS 3.10s. Neither timing nor RSS is a permanent assertion.

**Tradeoff:** maintainer measurements show channel-only loops 6–13% slower due to node allocation and handle dropping; there is no channel perf bench covering this cost. This is a memory-lifetime correction, not a blanket speedup. No fresh GPU, Mac, mini-cluster or ASan run is claimed for this follow-up.

title: -o fails when two versions of one hub package define the same C effect: redefinition of <effect>_run
body:
## Summary

A program that imports two versions of one hub package whose effect has a C twin runs under `bend main.bend`, but `-o` fails: the C file defines the effect's host function once per version, and clang refuses the redefinition.

## Version

- `bend 2.0.36`
- macOS 25.6.0, arm64 (Apple clang 17.0.0)

## Repro

`main.bend`:

```python
import Base
import bend-kit-time@0.1.2.1/time.bend as T1
import bend-kit-time@0.1.3.0/time.bend as T2

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    a : T1.Instant <- T1.now()
    b : T2.Instant <- T2.now()
    IO.print("two versions of one effect ran")
```

```sh
bend main.bend          # prints: two versions of one effect ran
bend main.bend -o m     # fails
```

## Expected

`-o` builds, as the interpreter runs it. Two versions of one package are distinct modules (their types differ), so their effects should get distinct host symbols, or identical C twins should be emitted once.

## Actual

```
m.c:9424:6: error: redefinition of 'wall_raw_run'
 9424 | Term wall_raw_run(Env e, Term* f, IoWork* w) {
m.c:9377:6: note: previous definition is here
m.c:9428:42: error: redefinition of 'wall_raw_use'
```

## Why it matters

Hub packages pin their siblings by version, so a program that uses two libraries soon imports two versions of a common one (here `bend-kit-webhooks@0.4.0.0` pins `bend-kit-time@0.1.2.1`, and `bend-kit-runner` takes `bend-kit-time@0.1.3.0`). Such a program cannot be built natively.

title: `IO.safe_eval` and `IO.unsafe_eval`: check and run Bend source at runtime
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# Two effects in Base: run a source string as a program whose main has
# the type the caller names, and answer main.
def IO.safe_eval(-A: Type, src: String) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, A>)
def IO.unsafe_eval(-A: Type, src: String) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, A>)

# A type whose values carry a proof:
type Small is Data:
  Small{n: U32, ok: {U32.is_lt(n, 100) == True{} : Bool}}

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    # src arrives at runtime: a file, a socket, a user
    a : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Small> <- IO.safe_eval(Small, "def main(): Small{42, {==}}")
    # Done{Small{42, {==}}}: the proof holds
    b : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Small> <- IO.safe_eval(Small, "def main(): Small{420, {==}}")
    # Fail{(22, why)}: the proof does not hold; why is the checker's message
    f : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32 -> U32> <- IO.safe_eval(U32 -> U32, "def main(x): U32.mul(x, 2)")
    # Done{f}: a closure the program can call
    return Unit{}
```

### Why

A program could accept code from someone it doesn't trust and know what that
code does before running it. A game could let players write their own items or
abilities and accept one only if it proves the game's balance rule. An app
could load plugins whose type gives them no way to touch files or the network.
Bend checks the code against a type the caller names, so every law in that
type holds for it as a proof. Code that `safe_eval` accepts is total, and it can cause effects
only if `A` contains `IO`.

#### What the two effects do

1. `src` is a Bend file, and its `main` is the answer. Relative imports
   resolve from the current directory.
2. `main` is checked against `A` as if the caller had declared `law main: A`
   and `src` filled it. So `src` writes `def main(): …` or `def main(x): …`
   without a return type, and `A` must be concrete at the call.
3. Of the caller's defs, `src` sees only those `A` names, directly or through
   others.
4. The answer is `Done{main}` when `src` checks and `Fail{(22, why)}` when it
   doesn't. That is the shape of other IO errors, so `IO.try` works on it.
5. `safe_eval` also refuses `@unsafe` and foreign code, and anything that
   relies on either, as `--verdict` does. `unsafe_eval` takes any code that
   checks.
6. Either may `Fail` for a reason outside `src`, such as an unsupported
   platform or a resource limit.

#### Open questions

- Should a compiled binary support eval, or should a build refuse it at
  compile time?
- Should an eval bound a snippet's time and memory, for example with a
  deterministic step budget that answers `Fail`?

title: `--verdict` reports a kernel "out of fuel" as a TypeScript/kernel mismatch, without the def or the reason (2.0.36)
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend PROOF.bend                 # bend2 only
bend PROOF.bend --verdict       # bend2, then the BendTT kernel
bend PROOF.bend -o PROOF.bendtt # the kernel's input
~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/bendtt PROOF.bendtt
```

`<hash>` is `57dc4b2aa41362ae`, the kernel `--verdict` builds from 2.0.36's `bendtt.lean`.

### What happened

bend2 accepts the law. The kernel runs out of fuel on it, and `--verdict` reports that as a mismatch, without the def or the reason:

```text
$ bend PROOF.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.

$ bend PROOF.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.

$ bend PROOF.bend -o PROOF.bendtt && ~/.bend/bendtt/57dc4b2aa41362ae/bendtt PROOF.bendtt
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In LAWS.copy_long:
out of fuel
```

`main` (`0e14aa8b`) prints the same.

The kernel says which def failed and why, but `--verdict` drops both:

- [`kernel_check`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/0e14aa8b/bend2/safe.ts#L1541-L1563) reads the kernel's output, then returns only a boolean.
- [`cli_verdict`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/0e14aa8b/bend2/main.ts#L816-L819) then prints the fixed notice.

Running out of fuel isn't a mismatch: the kernel stopped before it reached a verdict on the def. Because the notice asks for an issue, every such case looks like a soundness bug until someone runs the kernel by hand. #1193 and #1322 both had to do that. #1322 suggests this change in passing.

### Expected

Under SOME PROOFS FAIL, `--verdict` prints the kernel's own message: the def's name and the reason.

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In LAWS.copy_long:
out of fuel
```

The mismatch notice could then be kept for the kernel's `expected:` / `observed:` failures, where bend2 and the kernel really disagree.

A def the translation leaves out of scope reaches the same notice too, because [`safe_check`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/0e14aa8b/bend2/safe.ts#L1570-L1573) returns false; #1483 shows one. `-o` already lists such defs with their reasons, so `--verdict` could print those lines as well.

### The file

`LAWS.bend`:

```python
import Base

# h then r, or r alone when cut
def push(h: Char, r: String, cut: Bool) -> String:
  match cut:
    case True{}:
      r
    case False{}:
      SCon{h, r}

# copies s through push, one char at a time
def copy(s: String) -> String:
  match s:
    case SNil{}:
      SNil{}
    case SCon{h, t}:
      push(h, copy(t), False{})

# LAW: copy keeps a long string
law copy_long:
  {copy(String.repeat("ab", 1000n)) == String.repeat("ab", 1000n) : String}
```

`PROOF.bend`:

```python
import Base
import ./LAWS.bend as Laws

def Laws.copy_long():
  {==}
```

### Why this law runs out of fuel

This is background for the case above, not a second request.

`bend PROOF.bend` takes 0.1 s. The kernel's time grows with the square of the string's length:

| `"ab"` repeated | kernel |
|---:|---|
| 200n | passes, 0.5 s |
| 400n | passes, 2.0 s |
| 600n | passes, 4.6 s |
| 800n | out of fuel, 4.7 s |

The cause is how `push` is translated. Its `r` is Data, and [both arms of the match use it](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/0e14aa8b/bend2/safe.ts#L718-L719), so it gets a q=2 λ:

```text
LAWS.push : ∀x0 : Char -> ∀x1 : String -> ∀x2 : Bool -> String =
  λx0 => λ+x1 => λ{(,): λ{.True: λ{(): x1; λ{}}; λ{.False: λ{(): (.SCon, (x0, (x1, ()))); λ{}}; λ{}}}}
```

On a closed term, [`Term.val`](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/0e14aa8b/bend2/bendtt.lean#L944-L953) takes a q=2 argument to normal form before binding it, and walks the whole value even when it's already normal. Here `r` is `copy(t)`, the rest of the string, so each char walks the whole tail again.

Matching the first parameter avoids this: `def push(cut: Bool, h: Char, r: String)`, called as `push(False{}, h, copy(t))`. Then `r` is a plain λ inside each arm, and the kernel checks the same law at `1000n` in 0.06 s.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.36 (`bend --version` isn't an option in this release).

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)

title: fix(verdict): show kernel failure details (#1535)
body:
Closes #1535.

When the kernel rejects a book, `--verdict` printed only `SOME PROOFS FAIL` and the mismatch notice, so you couldn't see which def failed or why. Now it prints the kernel's why between the two lines. The notice stays on every failure, out of fuel included.

Before:

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, ...
```

After (out of fuel):

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In LAWS.copy_long:
out of fuel
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, ...
```

After (a def out of the kernel's scope; these are the same lines `-o` prints):

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
BendTT: out of scope:
- reflexive: names reflexive_7e_n, out of scope: no model for reflexive~n
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, ...
```

A type rejection shows the kernel's `In <def>:` and `expected:` / `observed:` lines the same way. If the kernel fails without giving a why, the line says how it exited (`kernel exited 1 after ALL PROOFS CHECK`).

Nothing else changes. Exit codes, stdout, the unsafe/foreign list, passing output and infrastructure errors are the same as on main. Everything still goes to stderr. `gates/safe.ts` and `gates/safe_node.ts` are untouched.

Changes:
- `safe.ts`: `kernel_check` and `safe_check` return null on a pass, else the why.
- `main.ts`: `cli_verdict` prints the why above the notice.
- `gates/ping.ts`: one test. A stub kernel reports out of fuel, and the test checks for exit 1, empty stdout, and the why above the notice.

Checks (on main 213cd5ec; test and safe gates on the minis, the rest on macOS arm64):

- Safe gate, tests corpus (real kernel): same table as main (1042 agree, 88 unsafe, 490 bend2 rejects, 4 out of scope, 1 false reject). Same exit code on all 1625 files. Only the 5 failing files' text changes, by gaining the why.
- 60 hub package files: same exit codes as main. Only the 4 out-of-scope failures change.

title: fix(gates): classify translator failures as infrastructure errors
body:
When the frontend accepts a program but BendTT elaboration throws, `--verdict` prints an error without a failure marker. The survey then counts the program as `bend2 rejects`.

Catch exceptions from elaboration and report `BendTT infrastructure: elaboration failed:` with the original error text. The existing survey worker uses this marker to classify the result as `e infrastructure`.

The recursive type program from #1164 reproduces the classification error on current main (`0e14aa8b`):

```bend
import Base

def G() -> Type:
  (G -> U32) -> U32

def run(g: G, k: G -> U32) -> U32:
  g(k)
```

`--check-only` accepts this program. Before this change, the real survey worker reports `bend2 rejects: ` after the translator stack overflow. After this change, it reports `e infrastructure` and keeps the `RangeError` text.

Add `tests/check/verdict_recursive_type.bend` and a standalone regression command:

```sh
bun gates/safe_node.ts --test
```

The regression requires frontend acceptance. The survey result must then be one of two exact outcomes:

- Exit 1 with the translator elaboration marker, a stack `RangeError`, the preserved error field, and `e` classification.
- Exit 0 with the exact `ALL PROOFS CHECK` output, no process error, and `agree` classification.

Missing-kernel errors, frontend rejections, kernel rejections, other translator errors, timeouts, and failed success statuses must fail the regression. The success outcome allows a future translator fix. The translator stack overflow remains; this change corrects its survey classification.

GitHub CI runs this regression before it replaces the PR gate files with main's gate files. The regression does not require the site repository.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.14:

- The standalone regression passes `9 / 9`: frontend acceptance, the real survey result, one success-result guard, and six rejection guards. The guard rows are synthetic; the frontend and survey checks run real subprocesses.
- The same regression fails against current main's unmarked translator overflow.
- The Bend fixture prints its expected `#|` lines in a normal CLI run.
- The repository gate passes: `54 / 54`. The diff check passes.
- GitHub CI passes on commit `8e3a306a`. The `survey translator regression` step and the repository gate both ran and passed.
- The type check reports the same 12 errors on current main and this branch.
- The full installer gate, mini-cluster gates, and a real proof kernel were not run. The standalone regression runs without the site repository.

title: fix(cli): preserve @unsafe in filtered base output
body:
`bend base Array.fork` and `bend base Array.join` printed the def without the `@unsafe` line above it. `cli_base` splits Base before every `type`, `law`, `def` and `@` line, so the `@unsafe` line became a block with no name and was dropped.

Fix: an `@` block now carries over into the block after it (bend2/main.ts, +4/-1). The split is unchanged.

title: Bend 2.0.37
body:
- **A Nat crosses to a JS host as a plain number** (PR #1506 by
  nicolas-abril). **Breaking for JS callers:** an effect's `.js` and a
  caller of an exported def pass and get `5`, not `5n`. A `Nat` answer or
  argument that isn't a whole number from 0 to 2^53 stops the run with the
  Nat error, as in C. Calls into exported defs are about 3.5x faster.
- **`IO.exit(code)` ends a program quietly** with a status from 0 to 255
  (#1465, PR #1492 by oxura). A code above 255, in `IO.exit` or `IO.die`,
  exits 1 instead of wrapping.
- **`F32.show` takes a plain parameter**, so `~F32.show` fits `List.show`
  and `Maybe.show` (#1511, PR #1518 by vicmcorrea). A caller passing it as
  `+` now wraps it: `(x => F32.show(x))`.
- **bend-lint**, a standalone linter with rules written in TS or Bend, in
  `tools/bend-lint` (PR #1389 by MattCozendey).
- **Faster**:
  - The CPU hands a slow grow's forks to idle threads, so a wide late fork
    runs 2.6x faster at 14 threads (#1475, PR #1479 by viridale).
  - BendTT's parser reads the text's bytes, so `--verdict` parses twice as
    fast in a quarter of the memory (PR #1380 by nicolas-abril); safe.ts
    walks each term once (PR #1384 by nicolas-abril).
  - A bang over a pair no longer sends every closure to the device (PR
    #1336 by chaserelock); a spin is a device call by its C's length in
    characters, and always inline on the host (PR #1413 by nicolas-abril).
  - A native build frees the compiler's memory before clang runs (PR #1385
    by Iann29).
  - On Linux a window paces at the display's refresh rate, not 60 Hz (PR
    #1379 by igorhasse).
- **CLI**:
  - `bend update` fails when the installer download fails (#1481, PR #1485
    by vicmcorrea).
  - `--checkup` reads only the import header, and imports with a trailing
    `# comment` (#1501, #1497, PRs #1502 by oxura and #1517).
  - `bend a.bend --verdict b.bend` is refused: extra arguments go only to a
    plain run (#1503, PR #1516).
  - Inline HTML module scripts are bundled (#1400, PR #1412 by oxura), keep
    their diagnostic positions (PR #1454 by Osraka), and a bundler failure
    is a formatted error (#1399, PR #1406 by oxura).
  - An unreachable hub is a formatted error, not a TypeError (PR #1428 by
    HamedShams); a native build that fails before clang removes its
    `/tmp/bend-*` dir (#1402, PR #1405 by Yi-111-a).
  - A `!` build finds CUDA at `$CUDA_PATH` and `/opt/cuda` (PR #1373 by
    igorhasse).
- **Fixes**:
  - Linux audio keeps a partially written chunk until ALSA takes it, and
    stops on a dead device instead of spinning (PR #1508 by
    sebastian-griego).
  - `F32.hypot` keeps lengths past 1.8e19 and below 1e-19 (PR #1515 by
    sebastian-griego).
  - A closed stdout or stderr reader ends a program by SIGPIPE (#1467, PR
    #1470 by viridale); `Process.run` reads until stdout and stderr close
    (#1343, PR #1392 by nicolas-abril); `get_env` rejects a name with a NUL
    (#1449, PR #1450 by Yi-111-a).
  - An erased last argument no longer cuts its call (#1374, PR #1377 by
    nuxyel); the effect table is sized to the program's constructor ids
    (#1163, PR #1378 by vicmcorrea); arrays of concrete functions compile
    (#1404, PR #1410 by oxura); `lay_el` takes only datatypes and type
    formers (PR #1426 by nicolas-abril); a `__proto__` export survives in
    JS (PR #1458 by vicmcorrea).
  - Match-refined Data views stay in copyable lets (#1349, PR #1369 by
    oxura); Array-wrapped JS marshalling is stack-safe (#1346, PR #1370 by
    oxura).
  - `--verdict` builds inlined recursive let arguments at each use (#1326,
    PR #1368 by oxura), keeps Base-free large Nat literals (#1330, PR #1337
    by oxura), and parses both rewrite motive binders in its diagnostics
    (#1315, PR #1407 by oxura).
  - The formatter keeps module import paths (PR #1325) and separated brace
    arguments (PR #1505), by vicmcorrea; the linter keeps quoted foreign
    import paths (PR #1422) and module headers (PR #1460), by vicmcorrea.
- **Docs**: README Limitations names backend divergence and the unproven
  translation (#1423, PR #1424); the formatter README installs
  `bend2-fmt-lsp` on PATH (PR #1486 by Osraka); IO forks vs CPU parallel
  calls (#1375, PR #1415 by oxura); BendRT's opening program checks again
  (#1308, PR #1382 by oxura).

title: fix: namespace imported C effect functions
body:
Fixes #1533.

## Change

- Qualify directly defined C effect functions, helpers and registration constructors by the declaring Bend module.
- Save and restore source-defined macro state around each twin. This is necessary for the identical `TIME_EFFS` guard in the two real time-package versions; qualifying only the functions leaves the second version calling a suppressed helper.
- Preserve runtime/header references, record member names, literals and macro-parameter bindings. C global objects and type names retain their existing C scope.
- Add a consumer regression with two imported types, a shared helper guard, function-local counters, a function-pointer call, a field named like its helper and `offsetof` access. Both versions must execute independently.

## Real behavior proof

Linux x64, Bun and clang. The exact public issue program imports `bend-kit-time@0.1.2.1/time.bend` and `bend-kit-time@0.1.3.0/time.bend` from the real hub.

Untouched current-main base: native compilation fails with redefinitions of `wall_raw_run` and `wall_raw_use`.

After this patch: `bun bend2/main.ts hub-repro.bend -o hub-native && ./hub-native` builds and prints `two versions of one effect ran`.

`bun bend2/main.ts tests/io/foreign_versions.bend`, its emitted standalone JS under Bun, and its actual native binary all print:
```
8
71
9
72
```

Existing native namespace-capture and sharing consumers retain `None / 6` and `216`. `bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 54 / 54`; permanent caps unchanged.

`bend2/bend.ts`, GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md and gates are unchanged.

## Limits

No mini-cluster, macOS or GPU gate run. This fixes imported C host-symbol and guard collisions; it does not introduce separate C translation units or a new public C ABI.

title: ty_holds opens a datatype once with DUMMY for its value arguments (#1513)
body:
Fixes #1513. Supersedes #1522 (its test is kept as `gpu_reach_closure_instances`).

## The bug

`ty_holds` opens each datatype once per walk, keyed by name, with the arguments it first meets. For `Duo{plain: Box<Num{}>, callable: Box<Fun{}>}`, `Box<Num{}>` is opened (its field is `U32`) and `Box<Fun{}>` is skipped, so the bang's closure check says "no closure" and the GPU build fails with "a function the device does not hold". The same skip makes `lay_of` lay a family flat and overflow when it re-enters through a second instance, and makes `lay_holds` pick a spine by argument order (@nicolas-abril's review).

## The fix

`seen` keys a datatype by its name and the `term_key` of its value arguments, so each instance's fields are looked into, for every caller (`wide`, `lay_at`, `lay_of`, `lay_holds`, `ty_value`).

A family can reach infinitely many instances (`Ch<n>` with a field `Ch<1n + n>`). When an instance re-enters its own family on the walk's path with a value argument whose key grew, the walk opens it once with its value arguments unknown (`DUMMY`), keyed by name. A field stuck on the unknown index (`Pick(n)`) is not an ADT, so the `wide` and `lay_at` predicates count it as holding: the safe side. An index that does not grow (`Vec(2n)` counting down) stays concrete, so the C is the same as main's.

The path keeps, per family, the shortest key of each value argument, so a step costs O(arguments), and an instance's answer is cached per file in `FL.hold` when it holds or met only instances opened under it (@nicolas-abril's suggestions). A predicate is keyed by its text, which is sound while no predicate captures a variable (true for all three call sites).

There is no constant: along a path, the concrete instances of a family have keys no longer than the first one's, so they are finitely many, and the unknown instance is opened once. The previous version's 8-deep / 64-key bound fell back to main's rule past it, so a big enough type still missed the closure; the two new tests show it.

Known approximations:
- Keys are the raw syntax of the arguments, so one index written two ways counts twice.
- `ty_value` has no safe side (either wrong answer can hurt). In it, a field stuck on the unknown index also counts as holding, so a kind whose family grows its own index with an index-computed field reads as a type, not a value. No test or repro reaches this.
- `lay_of`'s re-entry check reads the constructors' fields with the family's parameters free, so a re-entry behind a call stuck on the family's own index still overflows, as on main (@nicolas-abril's third repro of 10-21). Instances that differ only in a type-function argument still collapse, and a kind that re-enters its own family still loops, both as on main.

`comp.ts`: 66,000 tokens (main 65,612, cap 66,000).

## Checks (merged with main 5ce1e07f)

- repo 54/54, test 1707/1707, ping 73/73, safe 1110 agree / 0 false reject; perf 123/124, the same cell as main (histogram PAR-CPU 1.25x, identical C).
- The emitted C of all 1,786 tests, demos and benches is byte-identical to main, except `chain`, `instances`, `mutual` and `family_cyclic_two`, which fail on main.
- New: `wrapped` (two `Box` instances under ten type arguments) and `far` (a closure only at index 12 of a growing chain). Both fail on main and on this PR's previous head with "a function the device does not hold".
- All 15 tests of the PR pass on CPU, Metal and JS. `deep`, `grow`, `nested` and `wrap` check that the walk ends.
- `Vec(5000n)` builds in 0.14 s (0.9 s before the path and cache changes) and a 32-way branching index in 0.2 s.
- @nicolas-abril's repros:
  - The `Vec(2n)` bang emits the same C as main.
  - The two-instance `Nest` builds.
  - `More`'s spine row is `{2,0,1}` in both argument orders.
  - The deep-kind `Ch` with 12, 70 and 300 wrappers builds and prints 9; main overflows.
  - The `L<(k => Gr<k>)>` lambda emits the same C as main.

Not run: CUDA, Linux, Windows (GPU checked on Metal only).

title: Descent checking is exponential on deep nested patterns, in bend2's term_descend and the kernel's port
body:
Descent checking (`term_descend` in `bend2/bend.ts`, and its kernel port `Pat.cmp` / `Pat.fields` / `Pat.visit` from #1200) takes exponential time on deeply nested patterns.

### Why

Both compare top-down with no memoization. When a constructor's field compares GT, the fallback compares the **whole** argument again against each other field of the pattern. Each of those calls does its own field comparison and fallback, so the same (sub-pattern, subterm) pairs get recomputed along exponentially many paths. The kernel branches more: constructors become nested binary pairs, and the search also tries the pairs along the chain.

### Repro

```
type T is Data:
  L{}
  N{l: T, r: Nat}

def f(x: T, n: Nat) -> Nat:
  match x:
    case N{N{...N{N{a, t[k-1]}, t[k-2]}..., t1}, t0}:   # k levels
      1n+f(N{...N{a, t[k-1]}..., t0}, n)                # the inner k/2 levels, outermost tail swapped for t0
    case _:
      0n
```

| k | `--check-only` (bend2) | kernel on the emitted `.bendtt` (#1200) |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.09 s | 1.5 s |
| 30 | 6.1 s | > 120 s (killed) |

`main`'s kernel checks the same files almost at once (it only accepts rebuilds and pieces).

### Fix

Keep the logic and memoize it per (pattern piece, subterm), in bend2 and the kernel the same way. In the kernel this needs a proof that the memoized check equals the plain one, and `bendtt.lean` is about 360 ttok under its 64k cap, so it will need cuts.

A polynomial bottom-up version of the kernel check exists on `ai/1200-bottomup` (commit 73d7baf1, local). It accepts a superset of `term_descend` and checks k=30 instantly, but it doesn't follow bend2's structure, so it wasn't merged.

title: safe: refute empty ~ columns in a specialized def's cover instead of leaving it out of scope
body:
A `~` parameter whose type is empty at some value of an earlier finite `~` parameter leaves the def out of scope in `--verdict`. Instead, the kernel could check that the leaf can't be reached.

## Repro

```
import Base

law only_true:
  for ~b: Bool
  for ~h: {b == True{} : Bool}
  Nat

def only_true(b, h):
  1n

def main() -> Nat:
  3n
```

- **main:** `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The `False` instance is `1n` and never names `h`'s root constant, so it never goes out.
- **#1225:** `SOME PROOFS FAIL`, `- only_true: names only_true_7e_h, out of scope: no model for only_true~h`. The cover annotates every leaf with `G` applied to every `~` column, so the `False` leaf names `only_true~h : {False == True : Bool}`, which has no model.

On main, the same def fails as soon as the body uses `h` (return `h` at type `{b == True{} : Bool}`): the `False` instance is missing from the `.bendtt`. So an empty `~` column was already out of scope. #1225 makes it out of scope every time. `~e: {1n == 2n : Nat}` fails the same way.

For now, #1225 leaves these cases out of scope on purpose.

## Proposal: refute the leaf with an absurd

The kernel has J (`%`) and `λ{}`, so the cover can prove the leaf is unreachable instead of naming a constant that can't go out. This leaf checks on `bendtt.lean`:

```
Bool.ok : ∀x : Bool -> *1 =
  λ{(,): λt => λr => (λ{.False: <()>; λ{.True: <>; λ{}}} t)}

G : ∀-b : Bool -> ∀-h : {b == (.True, ()) : Bool} -> *1 =
  λ-b => λ-h => Bool

no : ∀h : {(.False, ()) == (.True, ()) : Bool} -> (G -(.False, ()) -h) =
  λh => ({λ{} : ∀x : <> -> (G -(.False, ()) -h)} (%h : x, p => (Bool.ok x); ()))
```

`ALL PROOFS CHECK`. As a control, the same refutation at `{False == False}` is rejected (`expected: <>` / `observed: (Bool.ok (.False, ()))`).

Sketch:

- When a non-finite `~` column has no model, try to refute its type. For an equation `{a == b}`, build a motive "x has `a`'s shape" from `a` alone: through pairs and labels, `a`'s label maps to `<()>` and continues inside, and every other label maps to `<>`. The kernel checks that the motive is `<()>` at `a` and `<>` at `b`, so a wrong motive is rejected, never trusted. It has to look inside fields: `{1n == 2n}` differs only at depth 2.
- The leaf becomes `{λh. efq(%h : x, p => motive x; ()) : ∀h:H. G v h}`, and that value's instance is skipped. This also helps defs whose body uses `h`, which main can't emit at all today.
- When no refutation is found (a stuck equation, an opaque call), the def stays out of scope. "No model" doesn't mean empty: the model search is bounded.

## Cost

`safe.ts` is at 23,340 ttok on #1225, against the 24k cap, so 660 are left. The estimate is about 500–700 ttok for equations only: ~300–450 for the refuter, ~150–200 to hook it into `root_emit`, plus comments. The cleanups from #1225's review (reuse `lams`, derive Quant's values from `QS`, pass column terms down) should free 100–200. Empty datatypes would need more.

title: Effect-defined C names use explicit HID markers
body:
Related to #1533; replaces the rejected identifier-inference approach from #1541 with the explicit marker direction requested in review.

`HID(name)` gives an effect-defined C symbol a per-module host identifier through the existing `c_ids` pass. It does not look up a Bend constructor/def. Ordinary identifiers, members, headers and source macro scope are not rewritten or analyzed; there is no C lexer/declaration inference or push/pop macro layer. The compiler change is the existing marker regex accepting H plus one three-line HID branch. The effect documentation shows definition/reference usage and the adoption boundary.

The fixture's two imported modules explicitly mark their colliding functions, registration constructors, global counter state, typedef/tag, include guard and macros. Both modules interleave calls through function pointers and retain independent state; record member `code` and runtime `w->code` stay ordinary C names. The JS twins are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

Linux x64, Bun 1.3.13, clang 22.1.8; based on upstream main f846cb5a.

Before marker adoption/support, `bun bend2/main.ts tests/io/foreign_versions.bend -o <binary>` fails with duplicate now_run and now_use. After the change:

- `bun bend2/main.ts tests/io/foreign_versions.bend`: 8, 71, 9, 72.
- Build emitted JS with `-o <out>.js`, then run under Bun: 8, 71, 9, 72.
- Build the native binary with `-o <out>`, then run: 8, 71, 9, 72.
- Existing native cid_capture fixture: None, 6.
- Existing native foreign_shared fixture: 216.
- Staged-file repository gate: PASS 54/54; caps and protected files unchanged.

## Adoption boundary

This does **not** transparently repair already-published packages that contain plain colliding C names. Package authors must adopt HID at definitions/references and republish; #1533 should stay open for those old versions. No claim that the original unmarked bend-kit-time versions now build, and no automatic-renaming compatibility layer.

No GPU, Mac, Node-host, mini-cluster test/perf or live package republishing proof claimed. GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, gates and bend.ts are unchanged.

title: fix(base): avoid intermediate rounding in F32.round
body:
## Problem and fix

`F32.round` adds 0.5 in binary32 before flooring. That intermediate rounding makes `0.49999997` round to 1 and changes already-integral values such as `8388609` to `8388610`.

Compute the floor first, compare the remaining fraction with 0.5, and add one or zero using existing Base operations. This corrects the arithmetic error [previously identified in review](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/929#issuecomment-5795417074) while preserving existing ties toward positive infinity, including -2.5 to -2, and positive-zero behavior.

## Blast radius

Two existing files, +12/-1: the `F32.round` body in `bend2/base.bend` and four added outputs/pins in `tests/base/num_kit.bend`. The public function type stays unchanged. Callers receive corrected rounding results on existing execution lanes; no compiler/runtime primitive, helper, gate or cap change is introduced.

## Regression evidence

With main's round body, the extended number-kit fixture fails three added assertions: below-half rounding and positive/negative integral inputs. With the correction, all 35 pins pass through source CLI execution, emitted Bun/Node JS and native CPU. The fourth added assertion guards the existing negative tie; positive tie checks remain.

## Checks

- Repository gate: 54/54 with CI-pinned ttok 0.3; `git diff --check` passes.
- `num_kit`, `f32_hypot_range`, `f32_show` and `float_roundtrip`: check/build and all four execution lanes pass.
- Independent boundary probe: 142 finite inputs and three specials match an exact oracle on CLI, Node JS, native CPU and real Metal; main fails the same seven finite cases. The final branch was freshly built and exercised on CPU and Metal.
- A dynamic JS export matches the exact oracle on 232,782 sampled binary32 inputs; main has 4,521 mismatches. Separate controls preserve zero behavior, infinity signs and NaN category.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11, Node 26.8.2 and clang 23.1.3. The Metal probe used a 512 MB heap. CUDA, Linux/Windows, installed compiled CLI, Lean/verdict, performance benchmarks and full cluster test/perf/ping/safe gates were not run; the cluster hostname is unavailable locally.

The numerical sample is not exhaustive over binary32. NaNs are checked by numeric category, without a payload/sign preservation claim. Private oracle scripts and probes are validation evidence, not additions to the repository.

title: fix(base): stop list searches when the result is known
body:
On the C and JavaScript backends, `List.any`, `List.all`, `List.find` and `List.contains` evaluate the recursive search as a strict argument. Because of that they:

- scan the whole list after the result is known,
- run `List.find`'s predicate from the end of the list, and
- overflow the stack on long lists (interpreter and JavaScript, 50,000 elements).

This PR has each function call a tail-recursive `.go` helper that carries the previous result. The helper stops when `any` or `contains` finds a match, when `all` sees a false, or when `find` reaches its first match. The signatures, the empty-list results and support for affine elements stay the same.

`tests/base/list_search.bend` covers:

- empty lists
- that `find` returns the first match
- affine closures
- 50,000-element lists with a match last or no match

On main, the long-list cases overflow on the interpreter and JavaScript lanes.

Checks (macOS arm64, merged with main):

- repo 54/54, test 1622/1622, perf 124/124
- interpreter, C and JS give the same answers as main on small lists, with matches at the head, middle and tail, several matches, and none
- an early match with a costly predicate after it: C 7.5s -> 0.5s, JS 45s -> 0.5s
- 1,000,000 elements: main overflows on the interpreter and JS; this branch passes on all three
- a `!` call runs the same with `--gpu on` and `off` (Metal)

Not run: CUDA, Linux, Windows.

title: fix(runtime): correct JS text boundaries after the Char rewrite
body:
Follow-up to the reproduced review findings on #1411, which merged while I was verifying them. Based on current main 63b2c0d3, preserving the maintainer's later edits and the merged channel/F32.round work.

## Correctness

- A module return is converted using the type after the function's actual `n` parameters (`tele_fill`), not the eventual result after every type parameter. Exporting `pre(a: String) -> String -> String` no longer passes a closure to `str_out`. Output conversion runs once after `run_lib` finishes the trampoline and survives partial application.
- A non-scalar u32 is packed in **four low-surrogate units**: DC00..DC03 carries the high two bits; three DC00..DFFF units carry ten bits each. No raw NUL/control/ASCII payload leaks into nested host-visible text. Length/decoder/display/output all recognize the same valid packet; malformed lone-marker text does not swallow subsequent ASCII.
- A Char getter recognizes packets, rather than treating any four-unit string as a packet. A trusted wide host Char such as `gbab` now yields the leading code **103**, not **411240546**.
- Non-string direct Char/String inputs and effect answers produce a Bend-category diagnostic rather than an opaque `.replace` TypeError.
- Host conversion selection uses explicit converter names. Non-text continuations reuse the original callback.

## Runtime work

- String length walks by Char without creating a converted string or a code-point array.
- Matched/captured Char codes are held once per binder body/invocation. Private emitted field-read markers preserve constructor-view folding; user string literals escape the marker and remain unchanged.
- Direct effect text is converted once by the effect wrapper. Redundant passes in `io_bytes`, `get_env`, and the direct `Process.run` program name are removed. Nested process args and Halt messages retain their explicit conversion.

## Verification

The retained `module_text_boundaries` fixture invokes the actual compiler and generated host module. It failed on merged main, and now exercises exported/curried closures, DC00/DC05 nested text with preserved tails, control-free packets, scalar/non-scalar text, all u32 marker classes and Unicode boundaries, wrong host types, captured code, literal marker preservation, and Char rebuilds.

| Actual consumer work | Merged baseline | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary repeated-code binder: code-point calls | 3 | 1 |
| Two captured-function invocations: code-point calls | 4 | 2 |
| String length: replacement passes / iterators | 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| IO.print: replacement passes, same text | 2 | 1 |
| Char identity: Char constructor calls | 0 | 0 |

- **76 actual runtime/fixture outcomes passed**: 23 interpreter, 23 emitted-Bun, 21 emitted-Node, 9 native C. Marshal-only fixtures have no C counterpart; Node Process.run and the old module-export-keys child-compiler driver are excluded for known lane limitations.
- The non-scalar Halt probe produced exact **EF BF BD EF BF BD 0A**, exit 7, in interpreter/Bun/Node/native; the invalid host effect answer produced a Bend-category error instead of a TypeError.
- Staged repository shape/cap gate **54/54**; comp.ts **63,972 ttok**, cap **64,000 unchanged**. Latest commit 13e612e1 also removes the compiler's temporary emitted-lines array; the complete 76-outcome runtime matrix passed again.
- Local Node v22.23.1, three interleaved fresh processes per state, 1M ASCII code units, 3 warmups and 50 measured public module calls: median **362 ms → 212 ms**. This is one local case, not a general speed guarantee; max RSS was identical in all six measurements, so no RSS reduction is claimed.
- No CUDA/Metal/macOS/mini-cluster or `safe.ts --verdict` claim.

## Limits

This does not add a recursive host-value marshaler. Nested host strings still use the existing pass-through ABI; a well-formed reserved four-low-surrogate packet remains Bend's internal encoding. It does not address #1468's existing Node Process.run Worker limitation. No edits to human-written bend.ts, GUIDE.md, gates or caps; no CHANGELOG entry.

title: perf(js): reuse unchanged records after pattern matching
body:
Matching a record and returning it unchanged can emit a new JavaScript object:

```bend
def keep(+p: Point) -> Point:
  Point{x, y} = p
  p
```

The JS backend now returns `p` instead of constructing another `Point` object.

Track matched records within each branch. Reuse a source record only when
its constructor and every live field match. Resolve nested record reuse
before emitting fields. Keep the original variable term so the existing
closure capture logic can retain it. Changed fields, field order, and
constructor tags still produce new records.

Add value and JS identity regression tests for nested records, changed
fields and tags, erased fields, generic records, empty records, and closures.
The identity test fails on `main` and passes with this change. It checks the
optimization; it does not define a Bend identity rule.

Validation:

- Both new tests pass in Bun and Node. The value test also passes in native C.
- 353 selected compiled fixtures pass. Five unprintable fixtures are skipped.
  All 358 selected outcomes match `main`.
- 200 local simulation runs match after every step: 255,290 state comparisons.
- 50 repeated compiler emissions preserve output and probe counts.
- C output is identical for the new value test and three existing workloads.
- Repository gate: PASS 54/54. `comp.ts`: 63,925 of 64,000 ttok.

A local simulation benchmark on an Apple M5 Max measured:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bun 1.3.14, 100 runs | 104.974 ms | 93.326 ms |
| Node 24.19.0, 100 runs | 126.790 ms | 90.451 ms |
| V8 allocated bytes, 1,000 runs | 21.428 GB | 15.075 GB |

Timing uses three fresh processes per runtime, with warmup and 15 alternating
A/B batches per process. These results apply to this local workload and

The maintainer cluster gates have not run. Strict TypeScript checking reports

title: Simplify bendtt.lean proofs (-999 tokens, same claims)
body:
Shortens the proofs in `bend2/bendtt.lean` from 63,091 to 62,092 tokens (-999), on main after #1200. The proofs check at the same speed.

**The claims don't change.** Everything before line 1784 (definitions and the `Claim.*` statements) is identical to main. The theorems that prove the claims (`consistent`, `sr`, `progress`, `halts`, `confluent`, …) keep their statements.

title: fix(cli): distinguish exhausted kernel conversion budget
body:
## Description

Closes #1322 via the issue's documented-limit/diagnostic alternative; no native Nat optimization or fuel increase.

The CLI retains the kernel's failure details but now classifies an explicit out-of-fuel result as an exhausted conversion budget, not a generic frontend/kernel disagreement. Exit status remains 1: the proof remains unvalidated. WONTFIX documents the current 400,000,000-step per-conversion budget, unary large-literal behavior and the separate-equality workaround.

## Verification

Linux x86_64, Bun, actual current-source kernel built with pinned Lean 4.34.0; isolated HOME/TMPDIR under the Bend workspace.

- Actual `bigLe` at 3,000,000/3,000,001: exit 1; kernel reports `In bigLe: out of fuel`, followed by the explicit exhausted-budget/unvalidated explanation.
- Actual paired 1,600,000/1,600,001 obligations: exit 0, `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- Existing `tests/proof/model_no_base.bend --verdict`: exit 1 with the existing out-of-scope explanation and generic mismatch note, not the new fuel explanation.
- Local repository gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`; permanent caps unchanged.
