Not tested: the remote mini-cluster/HOC gates, GPU runtimes or a faster Nat evaluator. AI-assisted, without subagents. No manual CHANGELOG edit.

title: fix(js): let parked IO await host events
body:
## Description

Closes #1148.

Park JS foreign effects on host Promises without blocking the host event loop. Add io_park_promise(promise, k, done, fail), await the IO driver from every repository caller and generated program entry, and keep pure module exports synchronous.

Native readiness waits use one lazy worker with POSIX poll and a wake pipe; Promise completion interrupts the native wait. Descriptor buffers are transferred rather than copied. The driver closes its worker, pipe and Promise keep-alive ports on exit; fulfillment/rejection mappers run inside the normal IO error boundary. Existing deadline, channel and deadlock behavior is retained. Base does not gain DNS/TLS/crypto APIs or cancellation of arbitrary host operations.

Existing EFFECTS documentation and WONTFIX are updated. Redundant JS/IO boundary commentary was consolidated into the guide to fit the permanent compiler cap; no code moved out and no cap changed. The protected human-written bend.ts, kernel and gate files are unchanged.

## Verification

Linux x86_64, actual Bun 1.3.13 and Node 22.23.1.

- Permanent JS-only regression: microtask observed after the first deadline park; fulfilled Promise maps 21→42; rejected Promise maps errno71; real native pipe receives43. A second concurrent channel/Promise/pipe case interrupts an already-warm native wait and receives the later byte exactly once. CLI and emitted executable .js both print 1 /42 /71 /43 /42 /43, exit0.
- Independent real-runtime smoke uses the actual node:dns resolver for localhost and sends native SIGTERM from the parent only after the child's handler is registered. Interpreted CLI, emitted Bun program and emitted Node program each print 127.0.0.1 /ready /signal15 /flushed and exit0.
- Eight actual control executions: host_event_loop, sleep_order, chan_pipe and tcp_loopback, each through the CLI and emitted Bun program; outputs match their existing fixture contracts, exit0. TCP uses an actual loopback socket, not a mocked handler.
- Existing deadlock control prints waiting, reports the channel deadlock and exits1.
- Changed --checkup caller completed with exit0.
- Local repository gate: PASS:54/54 after the final changes; the compiler stays below the unchanged64k ttok cap.
- Ordinary commit/push, head c746eef6. No hooks bypassed, error suppressed or fixed-delay descriptor polling.

The reporter's microtask starvation and signal0 output provide the before evidence; those reported failures were not rerun merely to confirm them. The first independent smoke accidentally selected .mjs (a library target); it correctly emitted no executable entry. The corrected executable .js target is what the successful runtime proof exercises.

Not verified: the repository's remote mini-cluster/HOC gates, macOS, Metal or CUDA. No hardware result inferred from Linux. The existing JS-only fixture convention intentionally omits a nonexistent native-C twin; no placeholder C effect was added. AI-assisted without subagents.

title: fix(gates): enforce current-source kernel verdict regressions
body:
Fixes #1312.

Adds `bun gates/safe_node.ts --required` and a separate `kernel-verdict` CI job on pull requests and merge groups. Cold Lean builds do not fit the existing four-gate runner's 30-second cap, so that runner and the authoritative repo-gate job remain unchanged. Repository administrators still control required-status policy; no GitHub settings or token caps are changed.

The required command uses a fresh private HOME and ignores inherited `$BENDTT`. The existing source-keyed builder checks Lean 4.34.0 and compiles the current `bend2/bendtt.lean`. CI installs the official 4.34.0 Linux asset with its published SHA-256. No alternate builder, source-checker edit, kernel edit or prebuilt kernel trust.

Explicit expectations cover:
- kernel acceptance of `cong_lambda_argument`, `group_dead_forward` and `rewrite_motive_evidence`;
- finite out-of-scope for `model_no_base`, requiring exactly `reflexive` to be omitted;
- source rejection of a generated false U32 equality;
- direct kernel acceptance of a Unit inhabitant and rejection of a Unit label as an inhabitant of Empty;
- a real kernel executable exiting 23 classified as infrastructure failure, not proof rejection;
- a real child with an expired deadline classified as timeout, not proof rejection.

The runner kills the timed-out process group, including compiler descendants. It uses `Promise.withResolvers()`. Private build/input files are removed in `finally`. Unexpected omissions, outcomes, signals and diagnostic failures fail the command. The existing larger stdin survey remains descriptive.

Observed on Linux x86_64 with pinned Lean 4.34.0:
```
BENDTT=/definitely/not/a/kernel bun gates/safe_node.ts --required
... three existing accepted fixtures ...
model_no_base.bend: out of scope (474 ms)
rejected.bend: source rejection
unit.bendtt: accepted
empty.bendtt: kernel rejection
cong_lambda_argument.bend: infrastructure [failing-executable control]
expired deadline: timeout
PASS required kernel verdicts

bun gates/repo.ts
PASS: 54 / 54
```

The command was exercised twice locally with fresh private caches. Hosted [run 38560195585](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38560195585) then passed both `repo-gate` and `kernel-verdict` on the PR merge tree with Bun 1.4.0 and the checksum-verified Lean 4.34.0 asset; its log shows all nine expected outcomes and `PASS required kernel verdicts`. No remote mini-cluster, macOS or GPU run is claimed. README documents the command and deadlines.

title: BendTT kernel runs out of fuel on shared cells bend2 compares once
body:
`tests/check/conversion_shared_cells_once.bend` (from #1151) checks that bend2 compares a shared graph once: each level of `root_loop(d, x)` and `root_rec(d, x)` uses the level below twice, so walking it as a tree takes 2^d steps. bend2 merges equal shared cells and passes at any depth. The BendTT kernel doesn't share them, so it walks the tree and runs out of fuel.

On main (e78dc9c6), with the kernel built from `bend2/bendtt.lean`:

- `agree_16`: ALL PROOFS CHECK in 0.6 s
- `agree_20`, `agree_24`, `agree_32`: SOME PROOFS FAIL after about 7 s (BendTT: out of fuel), with the mismatch message

So `--verdict` gives a false reject for any program that relies on this sharing past about 20 levels. `gates/safe.ts` reported it as the only `!` in `tests` (1635 files).

The gate PR for #1312 lowers the test to 16 levels so the `safe` gate starts clean. The real fix is for the kernel to compare shared cells once, like bend2 does. When it does, the test can go back to 32 levels.

title: gates/safe.ts exits non-zero on a false reject, timeout or infra error
body:
Closes #1312.

`gates/safe.ts` always exited 0, so a false reject only showed up if someone read the tally. Now it exits 1 when any file is a false reject (`!`), a timeout (`t`) or an infrastructure error (`e`). It still writes the same table and tally.

On main the gate had one false reject: `tests/check/conversion_shared_cells_once.bend`, where BendTT runs out of fuel on `agree_32` because it doesn't share cells (#1555). This lowers that test to 16 levels, which BendTT checks in 0.6 s, so the gate starts clean. The test can go back to 32 once #1555 is fixed.

Gates on main e78dc9c6: repo 54/54, test 1624/1624, safe on `tests` 1635 files: agree 1053, `!` 0, `t` 0, `e` 0, exit 0. With the old 32-level test, `safe` exits 1.

title: fix(safe): refute empty specialized equation columns
body:
Fixes #1544. Parent #1225 is merged; main dbb3157 is integrated normally. Current head is e4d52cd25e5359cd88daa01706abf636fd17e0a9, preserving peer normalization commit 4ecba085 and adding its permanent regressions. This remains the empty-equation follow-up, not a second claim to resolve #1186.

A specialized equation with incompatible closed constructor shapes contributes a kernel-checked empty-domain proof to the root cover. A discriminator maps the left endpoint to Unit and the incompatible endpoint to Empty; equality rewriting transports the Unit inhabitant, and Empty elimination closes the Unit-valued coverage branch. Nested dependent fields retain their prefix matches. Model failure is never evidence of emptiness; failed attempts restore exporter state.

Equation-only refutations trigger coverage even without a finite datatype parameter. The merged parent's Open_Error-only type fallback, per-column cache, transactional exporter log and selector encoding are preserved. Two private variable/application AST constructors replace repeated node literals to fit the permanent safe.ts cap; the actual parent finite-cover export is byte-identical after this cutover. No protected checker, kernel, gate, cap or workflow edits; no unrelated comment trimming.

Both equation endpoints are evaluated to constructors before mismatch detection, including nested fields and U32 literal Word bits. That normalization and the shared EFQ simplifications are the peer contribution in [4ecba085](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1557#issuecomment-6178245392), explicitly disclosed by its author as unsupervised AI work without human review. Linux qualification and the four added regression cases below are separate from the peer's reported macOS/cluster runs.

Verification on Linux x86_64, Bun 1.3.13 and the actual source-built Lean 4.34.0 kernel:
- `BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/empty_equation_cover.bend --verdict`: ALL PROOFS CHECK. Eleven laws retain the seven original cases and add `flip(b) == False`, `Bool.and(a,b) == True`, `Nat.add(1n,1n) == 3n`, and `1 == 2 : U32`.
- Actual emitted JS and native C programs both print `3n`.
- The source-matched kernel rejects the original seven-law certificate with a constant Unit discriminator (exit1, expected Empty); the current eleven-law export passes. Kernel source SHA256 is cc78aa9ff3491ff1b788797bdcab4cb98107dcb1730ed99834f6933b11d88335.
- A nonempty but unmodelled `probe(n) == False` equation whose evidence is used stays out of scope (`no model for stuck~h`), not an absurd branch.
- Earlier finite-match, lambda-congruence and rewrite-motive verdicts remain recorded separately. Current local `bun gates/repo.ts` passes54/54 with the persisted cl100k tokenizer cache; the first post-restart combined command timed out after printing its kernel verdict and is not claimed as a gate pass.

The maintainer-reported #1544 failure and the peer's pre-normalization failures are the before evidence, not rerun merely to confirm them. Positive, wrong-motive and nonempty-unmodelled controls were exercised locally. The fixture participates in the existing proof corpus; no separate Lean job is proposed. No cluster, GPU, macOS or hosted-current-head pass is claimed as our execution. AI-assisted, no subagents.

title: Proof verdict: hint when unsafe/foreign defs come only through unused imports
body:
Closes #1463.

A file checked as proofs (`--verdict`, or a file with no `main`) still fails when any def outside Base relies on unsafe or foreign code, including defs it imports but never uses. That rule doesn't change. What changes is the error: when none of those defs is a law or a def of the checked file, no law or proof uses them, and the error now ends with a hint that names them:

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error: 2 defs rely on unsafe or foreign code:
defs that depend on @unsafe: app/main.serve, app/main.main
Hint: no law or proof uses these defs. Move them to a file this proof does not import, and the proofs will check: app/main.serve, app/main.main
```

The rule is the same for every file. There's no special case for `PROOF.bend`. Laws are now marked when parsed (`Def.l`), so a law filled by unsafe code in an imported file doesn't get the hint (`unsafe_law_fill`, `unsafe_law_own`, `unsafe_law_derived` stay as they were).

Tests: `tests/proof/PROOF.bend` (hint) and `tests/import/PROOF.bend` (a law relies on unsafe, no hint) come from #1472, with expectations updated. `unsafe_unused` and `unsafe_law_unused` now show the hint.

Gates on top of main 15a336cc: repo 54/54, test 1630/1630, perf 124/124, ping 58/58, safe 1643 files with 0 `!`/`t`/`e`, exit 0. Not run: Linux, Windows, CUDA.

title: One `+` on a `List<&2, U32>` seals every `List` cell a native build makes, `List<&1, U32>` ones included: a loop that shares nothing runs 2x slower
body:
Hi! I've been writing some larger programs in Bend lately, and reading the emitted C next to BendRT has been one of the nicest parts of it: the design is easy to follow once you have the paper open. That's how I ran into this one. I think it's mostly a question about a trade-off, so here's what I found, in case it helps.

### What you did

bend heat.bend -o heat && ./heat --threads 1

and the same with `cold.bend`, which is `heat.bend` without `sum2`, `twice` and the `twice(...)` term in `main`.

### What happened

Both programs build a 1M-cell `List<U32>` and sum it, 30 times. `heat.bend` adds one function that uses a `List<&2, U32>` twice, called once on a one-element list. That alone doubles the run time of the loop, which never shares anything:

| Linux x86-64, `--threads 1`, medians of 9 interleaved runs (peak RSS of one run) | cold.bend | heat.bend |
|---|---|---|
| main (d328354a) | 162 ms, 17.8 MB | 313 ms, 25.5 MB |
| 2.0.37 | 157 ms, 17.9 MB | 310 ms, 25.6 MB |

The emitted C of the two programs differs only where `List` is built and matched. `build` seals both fields of every cell, and `sum` takes instead of reading in place:

```c
// cold.c
e.mem[_nd_0 + 0] = _i_0;
e.mem[_nd_0 + 1] = _acc_1;
...
u64 _sp_0 = term_loc(_xs_0);
Term _f_0 = e.mem[_sp_0 + 0];

// heat.c
e.mem[_nd_0 + 0] = rfc_seal(e, _i_0);
e.mem[_nd_0 + 1] = rfc_seal(e, _acc_1);
...
u64 _sp_0 = ctr_take(e, _xs_0, 2, _fb_0);
Term _f_0 = _fb_0[0];
```

The shared list doesn't even exist at run time: `twice(7 <> Nil{})` is folded into `U32_BIN(0ull, +, 7ull)` twice.

### What I read

As far as I can tell, this is the design working as intended. BendRT says it in three places:

- section 3.1: "a type is hot when some binder of it is used more than once […]; everything else is built and consumed through plain stores and loads";
- section 4.2: "Only hot types pay any of this, and they seal every stored field with a count at build time";
- section 11: "contraction exists only at `Data`, so counts are minted only where a whole-program analysis finds sharing […], and the unshared majority of a program compiles to moves, borrows and frees with no count traffic".

I can see why it's built this way, and I like it. A cold type pays nothing at all, not even a test in its matches. A keep is one redirect. And a shared node's fields never change, which is what lets a take copy them out before it acquires (the comment above `term_peek` puts it better than I can). In `comp.ts`, `facts_hot` heats `"t:" + w.k`, the datatype's name, so a share of any `List` makes `Con` hot and `node_fill` seals every `Con` the program builds.

Two things in this repro surprised me, though:

- The cells being sealed are `List<&1, U32>`. If I read the Kinds section right, `List<&1, U32>` is a `Type`, not `Data`, so it can never be used with `+`. Only the `List<&2, U32>` in `twice` can be shared, and none of its cells come from `build`.
- The guide's runtime section says "only `+` values carry a reference count", and section 4.2 says "an unshared value carries no count anywhere". That holds for the value itself, but here every field of every unshared cell carries one.

### What I tried

In the emitted C only, not as a patch: I removed the two `rfc_seal` calls from `build` in main's `heat.c`, left `sum`'s `ctr_take` alone, and compiled it with `clang -std=c11 -O3 heat.c -lpthread -lm -ldl` (the same line gives 318 ms for the unedited file). It ran in 176 ms and 17.8 MB, so most of the difference is the seal at build time. The `ctr_take` that stays costs the rest, about 14 ms.

Then I went through the history and saw that you'd tried the general version of this: 257b8c33 ("a keep seals its tree in place (term_seal); builds store raw words") moved the seal from the build to the first keep, and 527c68bc brought the build-time seal back 73 minutes later. I couldn't work out from the commits what made you go back, and I'd be curious to know. My guess is the cost it moves onto a keep: walking and allocating for the whole raw part of the tree, where today a keep mints one redirect. Section 4.2 is careful that drop allocates nothing and runs from any code on either processor, and a keep that walks and allocates might not have that property. But it could just as well have been a correctness case, or a benchmark (the hvm5 demo landed in between).

### A narrower idea, if it fits

**A build whose type has a literal `&1` quantity could store raw words, even when its datatype is hot.** It's section 11's principle applied one level down: contraction exists only at `Data`, and a `List<&1, U32>` isn't `Data`, so nothing can ever keep it. As far as I can see, it also keeps every property the design protects:

- a keep is still one redirect;
- a shared node's fields still never change: a raw `&1` cell is never shared, so no take ever copies its fields out while another owner holds it;
- there is no walk, on either processor;
- matches stay as they are: a hot datatype's match already goes through `ctr_take`, which handles raw and sealed nodes alike;
- a generic build over an erased quantity still seals, as today.

For this repro, that is exactly the hand edit above (176 ms). It doesn't help a `Data` type that has no quantity, like `String`; there, something like 257b8c33 would be the way. I may well be missing a path where a `&1` value meets a keep, so please take it as a question.

If the build-time seal is the trade-off you want everywhere, a sentence in the guide would help whoever meets this next, in the spirit of section 11's "a cost model a programmer can read": one `+` on a type anywhere in the program makes every value of that type carry counts on its fields.

### Some context

This isn't only a micro-benchmark effect. In a larger program I profiled on 2.0.36, a server whose requests build, filter and print lists of records and strings, 281 of its 337 constructors were hot, and `term_drop`, `rfc_wrap` and `span_fade` together were 28–33% of the CPU samples on its list-heavy requests. I can't say how much of that is the build-time seal, since `term_drop` runs for unshared values too, but it's what sent me looking.

I'd be happy to help with whichever direction you prefer, whether that's a PR for the `&1` build with these two files as its test, the guide sentence, or more measurements. No rush at all. And thanks for the paper: it made all of this much easier to follow.

### The file

```python
# heat.bend: a 1M-cell List<U32> built and summed 30 times. cold.bend is this
# file without sum2, twice, and the twice(...) term in main.
import Base

def build(n: Nat, +i: U32, acc: List<U32>) -> List<U32>:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      build(p, U32.add(i, 1), i <> acc)

def sum(xs: List<U32>, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match xs:
    case Nil{}:
      acc
    case x <> t:
      sum(t, U32.add(acc, x))

def rounds(r: Nat, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match r:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      rounds(p, U32.add(acc, sum(build(1000000n, 0, Nil{}), 0)))

# All that cold.bend lacks: sum2, and twice, which uses a List<&2, U32>
# twice; main calls it once, on a one-element list.
def sum2(xs: List<&2, U32>, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match xs:
    case Nil{}:
      acc
    case x <> t:
      sum2(t, U32.add(acc, x))

def twice(+xs: List<&2, U32>) -> U32:
  U32.add(sum2(xs, 0), sum2(xs, 0))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(U32.show(U32.add(rounds(30n, 0), twice(7 <> Nil{}))))
```

`cold.bend` prints `1959202368`, `heat.bend` prints `1959202382`.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.37, and main at d328354a

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8

title: EFFECTS.md: a handle owns its descriptor
body:
#1455 showed that a parked fd closed under the loop ends the run with `bend: the poller failed`. That can only happen when a foreign effect breaks handle ownership: handles are affine and opaque, so no Bend program can close a descriptor another computation is waiting on. The reproducer's fill closes the socket it hands back.

Recovering in the runtime (#1456) only hides that bug, and can't catch its dangerous form: a closed number reopened by something else, so the waiter reads another owner's data. This PR instead writes the rule down for effect authors, after the paragraph on handles in `guide/EFFECTS.md`:

- an effect that answers a new handle gives its fd away open, and does not close it later or keep its number;
- an effect that takes a handle borrows the fd and hands back the same one, still open; only a close effect, which consumes the handle, closes it;
- an fd that never becomes a handle belongs to the effect, which closes it on every path.

Docs only; the repo gate passes 54/54.

Closes #1455.

title: fix(kernel): reuse successful shared conversion pairs
body:
Fixes #1555.

BendTT now carries a fresh positive-result memo through one conversion. A pair enters it only after normalization and every child comparison succeed. Keys include the unfolding mode; no failures or results from another conversion/book are reused. `withPtrEq` is only a proof-backed equality shortcut with structural equality as its fallback.

`convMemo_sound` proves both that returned memo entries remain sound and that a successful comparison implies the existing `Conv` relation. The kernel's typing, consistency and termination proofs compile without added axioms, `sorry`, `admit`, or changed fuel. `Term.conv` keeps its existing result contract.

Restores `conversion_shared_cells_once.bend` from 16 to 32 levels.

Observed on Linux, Lean 4.34.0, source-built kernel:

| Shared depth | Warm `--verdict` wall time | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| 16 | 0.132 s | ALL PROOFS CHECK |
| 20 | 0.134 s | ALL PROOFS CHECK |
| 24 | 0.134 s | ALL PROOFS CHECK |
| 32 | 0.137 s | ALL PROOFS CHECK |

These include the Bend CLI, not just kernel execution. The issue's reported fuel failures are the before evidence; these timings are not a cross-machine speedup claim.

Native kernel controls: a valid pair equality is accepted; an unequal second field, different definition bodies, and an attempted `Empty` inhabitant each exit 1. Existing lambda-congruence and rewrite-motive proofs still pass. `model_no_base.bend` remains explicitly out of scope rather than gaining a fabricated model. Current-main integration and repo gate pass 54/54.

The memo uses a list: lookup remains linear in stored pairs. This removes repeated successful graph-path comparisons, not a claim of constant-time indexing.

Not run: mini-cluster corpus, macOS, CUDA/Metal. No protected `bend.ts`, gate, token-cap or workflow edits; no unrelated comment trimming.

title: comp.ts sheds 65 tokens with the same output
body:
`comp.ts` goes from 63,968 to 63,903 ttok, against its 64k cap. The emitted C is unchanged, and the emitted JS changes only in two line joins.

Every cut keeps the output the same:

- **Folded helpers:** `quant_live` (4 callers) and `ty_clo` (1 caller) inline into their callers.
- **`OPTIMIZED.F32.F32.intr`:** reads group 2 of `VIEW` (its `f32_bits` arm) instead of repeating that regex.
- **`bind_pop`, `emit_args`:** recount through `bind_set`. `n` is at least 1 at both sites, so `bind_set` always takes its set branch.
- **Line joins:** the wrapped ternaries in the emitted JS runtime's `cmp_new` and `f32_show` go on one line each, as do two wrapped TS lines (`ctr_adt`, `js_expr`).

An earlier version also cut comments and turned if/return pairs into conditionals. Those are reverted: the comments carried information the code doesn't, and the if statements read better.

## Verification

- **Emitted output:** generated `compile_book`, `js_book` and `js_lib` for all 1,705 `.bend` files under `tests/`, `demos/` and `bench/runtime/` with the old and new `comp.ts`. Outputs are byte-identical apart from the two JS line joins. This ran on the larger cut, of which this PR is a subset.
- **Runs:** for 64 sampled tests, the build output, interpreter, native C and Bun runs match current main exactly (stdout, stderr and exit code).
- **Gates:** repo gate 54/54.

title: comp.ts simplifications: helpers reused, dead code and redundant casts gone (-447 ttok)
body:
This makes room under comp.ts's 64,000 ttok cap for #1438, which adds about 810 ttok. comp.ts goes from 63,968 to 63,521 ttok. It also absorbs #1562. Every change is a plain simplification: no code moves out of the file, and no `if` is rewritten as an expression.

**Compiler (TypeScript)**
- `bind_set`, `ty_adt` and `ck.tld` are used where the code repeated what they do.
- `quant_live` and `ty_clo` fold into their callers (from #1562).
- `seg_new` takes its parameters' values instead of words and kinds flattened at each call site.
- `emit_match` names its tag test once, as `js_match` already does.
- `js_call`'s `tail` and `js_expr`'s `ty0` default to the value most callers pass.
- F32's intrinsic reuses `VIEW`, and tag lists are a single string, as one site already did.

**C runtime**
- `ERR_*` is an enum.
- `term_buf` folds into `term_blk`.
- `WL_ARGS` takes the count directly and pushes with `WL_PUSHN`; `WL_FRAME` and `FID_EXIT` reuse `WL_PUSHN` and `WL_POPN`.
- A dead `show_val` prototype, redundant casts and single-use temporaries are gone.

**IO layer**
- `io_wait`'s two walks over the parked ring share one `io_parked` loop.
- `fcntl.h` is included once, and `IoWork` is declared once.

**JS runtime**
- `f32_show` lets its shortest-text loop reach infinity and fixes only the spelling.
- `io_strerror` folds into `io_fail`, and `io_addr` checks a byte with one test.
- `cmp_new` is one line (from #1562).

**Review fixes (second commit, +135 ttok)**
- `emit_clo` sets a captured binding's count directly again. `bind_set` could sink the value and leave `bind_pop` reading a deleted binding.
- Tag lists test exact membership through `ty_tag` instead of a substring test.
- The `IO_EMIT` and `CLO_APPLY` entries take plain words (`W64`) again.
- `js_expr` captures each outer variable once.
- Metal keeps its own `ulong`/`uint`/`uchar` typedefs.
- `WL_POPN`, `WL_ARGS` and the term bit macros parenthesize their arguments.
- `term_rfc` tests `RFC_BIT`. `io_again`, `io_wait` and `io_late` say "no deadline" plainly instead of through unsigned wraparound.
- `show_val` writes fixed text with `fputs`, not a format string (`-Wformat-zero-length` on Linux GCC).
- `io_addr` names its byte test, and `io_push` adds a number.

The fixes change no emitted code on the compiler side. The emitted C and JS differ from the first commit only in the runtime lines above, identically across all 772 compiled tests. Building and running every compiled test (C and JS, 5 s each) gives the same pass set on both commits: C 756/772, JS 758/772. The failures are expected-error IO tests that the local harness doesn't model. A `!` test's Metal shader builds with `--gpu-build`, and `tsc` reports no errors in comp.ts.

**Perf fix (third commit, +20 ttok)**
- `err_post` is a function again. As a macro, combined with the `WL_ARGS` rewrite, it pushed editdist's SEQ-CPU time from 1.90 s to 2.38 s (1.24x, over the gate's 1.15x limit) and its PAR-CPU time to 1.11x. Neither change slows editdist alone, so this looks like clang laying out the hot loop differently. Bisected locally by applying groups of runtime hunks to main's emitted C.

**Gates (minis, at the third commit)**: repo 54/54, ping 57/57, test 1631/1631, perf 124/124. editdist reads 0.99x on SEQ-CPU and 0.96x on PAR-CPU.

**Verification (macOS, M-series)**
- Absorbing #1562 changes no emitted C. The only JS change is `cmp_new`'s line join, the same in all 802 JS outputs.
- Emitted C and JS are byte-identical to main for all 1,631 `tests/*/*.bend` wherever only the compiler side changed. Where the runtime text changed, the diffs are exactly the runtime edits.
- Test runs on the C and JS lanes (rfc, run, reg, base, io, state, eval, halt, stats, show, printer) match main exactly: C 375 pass / 14 fail, JS 399 pass / 20 fail on both. The failures come from my local harness, not from this change.
- `!` programs built and ran on Metal.
- `tsc` reports no new errors in comp.ts.
- Benches (tree-bitonic, hashmap, symreg, raytrace) are within noise of main.
- Linux (Arch, x86_64, GCC 16, a local port of the test gate that runs shards in bwrap): test passes 1631/1631 at the third commit and on its base. editdist's SEQ-CPU median is within 1% of the base's over 15 interleaved runs. The Linux GCC `-Wformat-zero-length` concern from the review doesn't reproduce: GCC warns about `printf("")` but not about the conditional `printf(i > 0 ? ", " : "")`, so the `fputs` revert is cleanup only.
- Not run: CUDA.

title: A name a module uses above its def means that def, even when Base has a constructor of that name (#1236)
body:
Closes #1236

A name a module uses as a term above its def now means that def, even when
Base has a constructor of that name (Done, Some, Key, Move, ... 36 names).

parse_reso treated a name as "far" if Base had it as a def or a
constructor. A term reference can only be a def (infer-ref reads tlds), so
for those 36 names a law in LAWS.bend that used its own helper above the
helper's def named the bare key instead, and PROOF.bend's def of that name
filled it in: --verdict certified a law LAWS.bend never stated. Term
references now count only defs as far; constructor syntax is unchanged.

The fresh name check could refuse such defs instead, but that breaks 4
tests, the app_win_is_bug_2d demo (type Move) and 6 hub packages (Key,
Look, Ready). This change alters no output on the hub store, demos or
benches.

Test: tests/import/ctor_named_law.bend (fails on main).
Gates: repo 54/54, test 1632/1632, ping 58/58, perf 124/124, safe 0 false
rejects.

title: fix(lint)!: prefix option constructors to avoid Base collisions
body:
## Problem and fix

Base's `Text` constructor for `Event`, added in [#1441](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1441), collides with bend-lint's text option constructor. Bend-written rules, including the bundled file-length rule, fail to load with `duplicate declaration: Text`.

Use consistent `OptionNum`, `OptionFlag`, and `OptionText` names for the three option constructors, their helper match arms, and their JavaScript bridge tags. Document the constructor migration in the README's rule-authoring section.

## Blast radius

- `tools/bend-lint/src/bend/lint.bend`: three option constructors and nine helper match arms.
- `tools/bend-lint/src/bend/effects.js`: the tags used to send number, boolean, and string options to Bend rules.
- `tools/bend-lint/README.md`: migration guidance for rule authors.

**Compatibility impact:** direct construction or matching of `Lint.Num`, `Lint.Flag`, and `Lint.Text` must use `Lint.OptionNum`, `Lint.OptionFlag`, and `Lint.OptionText`. Bare constructor names and handwritten foreign `CID(...)` references also need updating. Documented option helpers, JSON configuration, and TypeScript option APIs retain their behavior; bundled rules use the helpers.

The compiler, Base, formatter, and gates are unchanged. Existing tests stay in bend-lint's suite, following [the maintainer guidance in #1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

## Regression evidence

The existing `a Bend rule reads its options with defaults` test compiles the actual contract and executes the JS bridge with number, boolean, and string options. It fails on base `dbb3157` at the duplicate declaration and passes with this fix. Restoring only the old `CID(Text)` bridge tag in the final source makes that same test lose the configured string (`none` instead of `x`), so it also detects an incomplete rename. No additional test is needed.

Clean base's tool suite reports `109 pass / 9 fail / 1 error`; the fixed suite reports `122 pass / 0 fail`. The file-length test module now loads and its tests register.

## Checks

- `bun test` in `tools/bend-lint`: **122 passed, 0 failed; 700 assertions**.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **54/54**, with CI-pinned ttok 0.3.
- Actual CLI with the Bend file-length rule: loads, reports the expected warning for three lines with `maxLines: 1`, and exits 0.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

## Validation limits

Local checks ran on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.11. Windows, the cluster gates, and typecheck were not run. External third-party rules and alternative Bend releases were not tested; direct constructor consumers require the migration described above. Other bare tool constructor names remain subject to collisions with future Base additions; this change only updates the option constructors.

title: fix(compiler): leave literal affine constructor fields raw
body:
Fixes #1559.

A constructor built at a known literal `Kind(&1)` now keeps its fields raw, even when another instantiation makes that constructor hot. Generic quantities still use conservative sealing. Matches still go through the existing `ctr_take`; keep and drop behavior is unchanged.

The regression mixes literal-affine construction with a generic constructor used at both `&1` and `&2`, then consumes the Data result twice. It prints `499500, 999000, 499500` in the interpreter, native C (1 and 4 threads), and emitted JS on Bun. Seven ownership programs pass those lanes; the repository cap gate passes.

I merged main and removed the unrelated layout and GUIDE changes in `7896a14e`.

[The issue author's server measurements are now in](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1566#issuecomment-6204087851): neutral. Almost all of that program's data is shared, so this literal-affine rule does not change its hot request path. The earlier microbenchmarks are not evidence of a production speedup, and no real-app speedup is claimed here.

**Still on hold:** this changes compiled-C behavior for an `@unsafe` copy of `Kind(&1)`, including the reported Base `Array.fork` case. That needs @VictorTaelin or @nicolas-abril to sign off.

Not tested: macOS, Metal, CUDA, or the mini-cluster corpus.

AI-assisted with GPT-6.1 Sol; no subagents on this PR.

title: perf(c): compute U32.pow by exponentiation by squaring
body:
U32.pow performs one multiplication per exponent step on the C backend. Use exponentiation by squaring to reduce that work to the exponent's bit length. Keep multiplication modulo 2^32, return one for exponent zero, and retain all 48 bits of the compiled Nat exponent.

Keep the Base definition and generated JavaScript unchanged. This preserves the existing proof reductions and reference backend. Select the backend's intrinsic table once per file so C-only entries do not suppress JavaScript definitions. Add tests for overflow, zero exponents, partial applications, larger exponents, and the symbolic successor equation.

On an Apple M5 Max, 500,000 calls with exponent 4,096 took 1.827 s on main and 1.810 ms with this change. The base changes on every call. For exponent 2, 5,000,000 calls took 9.728 ms and 2.514 ms. All measured exponents from 0 through 4,096 improved on macOS Clang 21 and Linux ARM64 Clang 19. These are focused benchmark results, not application speedups.

Validation:

- Checker and BendTT outcomes match main for all 1,646 test files, including expected rejections.
- All 791 successful JavaScript emissions are byte-identical. Unrelated C emissions add only an unused inline helper. All 17 runtime benchmarks have identical CPU assembly.
- 20,000 native cases match an independent modular-power reference on each OS, including exponents above 2^32. Both new tests pass through the source CLI, C, Bun, and Node.
- Parallel validation passes on CPU and Metal. CUDA compilation passes for sm_80 and sm_90; CUDA hardware execution was not available.
- 320 repeated emissions match. The final compiler-time comparisons show no material regression in the tested programs.
- AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer pass at -O0. The existing optimized-runtime sanitizer failure also occurs on main.
- The repository gate passes. The compiler remains below its 64,000-token cap. Strict TypeScript checking reports the same 11 existing errors.

The maintainer cluster gates have not run. Linux ran in an ARM64 VM on the same physical CPU.

title: JS F32 scalar inputs keep binary64 precision across the module and effect boundary
body:
### Exported F32 scalar parameters retain binary64 input precision

Current main `dbb31574`, Linux x86-64, Bun 1.3.13 and Node 22.23.1. No source edits are needed to reproduce.

```bend
import Base

def add(a: F32, b: F32) -> F32:
  F32.add(a, b)

def main() -> F32:
  add(16777217.0, 1.0)
```

Build both `-o sample.mjs` and a native executable. The native executable prints `16777216.0`. Importing the emitted default export and calling `B.add(16777217, 1)` returns **16777218**, whereas `Math.fround(Math.fround(16777217) + Math.fround(1))` and `B.add(Math.fround(16777217), 1)` both return **16777216**.

The distinction is observable at a normal typed scalar function boundary: 16777217 rounds to 16777216 as an F32 before the addition. The JS wrapper forwards its original binary64 argument and rounds only the result of the operation. `host` in `bend2/comp.ts` converts text and validates scalar Nat inputs, but leaves scalar F32 inputs unchanged.

The focused fix is to round a statically known scalar F32 as it enters Bend, including a partially applied exported call. This does not propose recursively traversing host-owned containers or changing the existing host responsibility for values inside them. No GPU result or NaN-payload preservation is claimed. A search of existing issues and PRs for F32 + host found no report of this scalar rounding defect.

title: fix(runtime): round scalar F32 host inputs before use
body:
Fixes #1568.

The existing JS host conversion rounds a statically known scalar F32 on entry. This covers exported `.mjs`/loader parameters (direct and curried) and foreign scalar answers. It does not traverse host-owned containers, change the Nat seam, or add a second marshalling convention.

Observed before on main dbb31574: a native F32 addition of 16777217.0 and 1.0 prints 16777216.0, but the emitted module's `add(16777217, 1)` returns 16777218. The owned real-module regression returned failure code 2, and the foreign-answer path printed 16777218 on both interpreter and emitted JS.

Observed after on Linux x86-64:
- Actual interpreter and emitted JS execute the new consumer regression and foreign-answer path: `0`, `16777216`.
- Node 22.23.1 calls the emitted default export directly and curried: both return 16777216; opposite overflowing operands produce NaN rather than zero, and subnormal rounding returns 1.401298464324817e-45.

title: Node loader checks the complete URL suffix, rejecting .bend cache-busting imports and intercepting JS modules
fix(loader): classify decoded module file paths
body:
Fixes #1570.

Classify a local module by its decoded file path rather than the suffix of its complete URL. Convert a `file:` URL once, compile only a `.bend` path, and forward other file and non-file modules to Node's next loader with the original URL/context. Node retains ownership of module-cache identities; no query stripping/re-keying or cache layer is added.

Observed before:
- A plain real Bend import returns 42; `?version=2` and `#module` imports fail with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION.
- `plain.mjs?asset=types.bend` is incorrectly parsed as Bend.
- The owned real-Node regression returns 1 before the fix.

Observed after, Linux x86-64 / Node22.23.1:
- Plain/query/fragment imports all execute the real Bend function and return 42.
- A stateful consumer changes a file between imports: the cached plain module remains 42, a query identity reads the changed code and returns43, a fragment identity reads the next change and returns44.
- Ordinary JS with a `.bend` query suffix returns88; a data-URL module ending in `.bend` returns7.
- The permanent regression passes in ordinary CLI IO execution and emitted JS on Bun (status0).

The regression uses actual Node import hooks and files (including a space in the pathname), not a mocked `next` callback or source-text assertions. CHANGELOG.md documents the behavior. Protected bend.ts, compiler APIs, hub resolution, gate files and caps are unchanged. No GPU or cluster claim.

`bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54/54 on the final source and regression files.

title: A shared Chan heats nothing: its handle is born counted and its values only move, so IO.fork, IO.join and one +c no longer heat every type the program builds
body:
Hi again! While measuring #1559 I found a second way a whole program goes hot, and this one felt small enough to send as a PR straight away.

### What happens on main

`facts_hot` falls back to heating every site type (the `*` fact) for a shared binder whose type it can't name. 5ce3ee54 added that for `F(A)` and computed types, and `tests/rfc/share_kind.bend` and `share_computed.bend` show why it matters. `Chan(A)` applies a law, so it's a stuck application too, and a keep of any channel takes the same fallback. Base does that itself: `IO.fork.go` keeps its channel (`+c = chan`) and `IO.join` takes `+chan`. So on main, every program that calls `IO.fork`, `IO.join` or `IO.within` has every datatype hot before it shares anything of its own.

The same build-and-sum loop as in #1559, alone, beside one `+c: Chan(U32)` (send, recv, close), and run inside `IO.fork` and `IO.join`:

| Linux x86-64, `--threads 1`, medians of 9 interleaved runs (peak RSS of one run) | alone | one `+c: Chan(U32)` | inside `IO.fork` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (dbb31574) | 143.7 ms, 22.6 MB | 322.4 ms, 33.0 MB | 282.9 ms, 32.9 MB |
| this branch | 144.8 ms, 22.7 MB | 142.7 ms, 22.6 MB | 143.6 ms, 22.7 MB |

In a larger program, a server whose connections ask a single task for answers over a reply channel, that one channel was the only `*` of the build. The same change took it from 228 to 151 of its 292 constructors hot (measured on d328354a).

### Why a channel needs nothing heated

A copy of a channel copies its handle, and nothing else:

- `chan_open` mints the handle counted ("Data: born shared, so a node that holds a copy may itself be shared"), so keeping it is a bump on its own cell;
- the effects move every value: `chan_put` moves it into a FIFO node or to a parked receiver, `chan_take` and `chan_wake` hand it to exactly one receiver, and a send on a closed channel hands it back in `Fail`;
- `Chan(A)` takes `-A: Type`, so its values may be affine, and the runtime never copies one.

`Chan` is also Base's only `Data` handle (`File`, `Socket`, `Listener`, `Window` and `Audio` are `Type`), so the branch names it directly:

```ts
} else if (m && (m.t as Of<"Ref">).k === "Chan") {
  return;
```

### What still has to hold, and the test

The `*` fact was also covering one thing: a hot `Some`, `Ready` or `Fail` seals the value `io_box` wraps, so the payload's type has to be hot as well. Without the fallback, that comes from the site-type fixpoint that `cold_in_hot.bend` pins, through the binder of whatever the effect answers.

`tests/rfc/share_chan.bend` builds that case on purpose:

- a kept `Rope` heats `Maybe`, `Poll` and `Result`;
- the `Duo`s that cross the channel are built at run time, so none is a static node, and recursive, so none is flattened;
- `wrap` owns each one, so a raw open would read the count-1 cell as the node.

With the fixpoint's type-argument heat turned off on this branch, both C lanes die with "memory fault" at the first `Duo` out of the channel. With it, every lane prints the expected lines. The test passes on main too, where everything is hot.

### How I checked it

- `tests/rfc` (the new file included) interpreted, on JS, and in C at 1 and 4 threads: all pass.
- All 175 `tests/io` files on JS and in C at 1 and 4 threads, against main with the same local harness: identical results. That includes `channel_fork_join`, `chan_shared_node`, `chan_try*` and the rest that share channels. (The files my harness can't read, compile refusals and pinned exit codes among them, fail it the same way on both.)
- `gates/repo.ts`: 54/54. `comp.ts`: 63,993 ttok.
- Not run: the mini-cluster, Metal, CUDA, macOS.

One thing to flag: #1566 also grows `comp.ts`, and the two together come to 64,021 ttok, 21 over the cap. Whichever lands second will need those tokens from somewhere. I'm happy to rebase onto #1566 and find the room in whatever way you'd prefer, or to leave the trimming to you if you'd rather choose where it comes from.

Thanks for taking a look!

title: A file read into an Array<U32>, so loading model weights is not one list cell per byte
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# File.read_at and File.read_bytes return a List<U32> with one cell per byte.
# A read straight into an Array<U32>, four little-endian bytes per word:
def File.read_at_u32(file: File, offset: U32, count: U32) ->
  IO(File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Array<U32>>)

# A loader of F32 weights then needs one bitcast per element, and no list:
r : File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Array<U32>> <- File.read_at_u32(f, off, n)

# Smaller alternatives, in order of how much they would change:
# - File.read_at with four bytes packed per U32 (a quarter of the cells, same shape)
# - a read-only map of a file into an Array<U32> (like mmap), for programs that only read
```

### Why

Loading a neural network means reading hundreds of megabytes of little-endian F32, and in Bend almost all of that time goes to building and walking the per-byte lists, not to decoding the numbers.

Standalone repro: read a 384 MiB file in 1 MiB blocks with `File.read_at` and add up the bytes, against the same loop in C with `pread`. Bend 2.0.37, Core Ultra 7 155H, Linux, one thread pinned to a P-core, five alternated runs each, same sum:

| program | time |
|---|---|
| Bend, `File.read_at` | 1.52-1.57 s |
| C, `pread` | 56-58 ms |

The work per byte is one addition in both; the difference is the list.

In [llama.bend](https://github.com/nuxyel/llama.bend), loading SmolLM2-1.7B (6.8 GB of F32) and generating one token takes 66 s at 16 threads, against 4.1 s for transformers and 0.5 s for llama.cpp; loading alone takes as long as ~150 generated tokens. In [bend-ml](https://github.com/nuxyel/bend-ml) I tried decoding in parallel lets (NOTES, exp. 13): no gain and twice the memory, since the cost is the list the host builds, not the decoding. Dropping a block unread is even slower than walking it. So I can't work around it from user code.

Repro (`head -c 402653184 /dev/urandom > w.bin`):

```python
import Base

def walk(bs: List<&2, U32>, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match bs:
    case Nil{}:
      acc
    case Con{b, t}:
      walk(t, (acc + b : U32))

def loop(k: Nat, +off: U32, m: File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, List<&2, U32>>, acc: U32) -> IO(U32):
  match k m:
    case 0n Tuple{f, r}:
      do IO<U32>:
        File.close(f)
        return acc
    case 1n+p Tuple{f, r}:
      do IO<U32>:
        bs : List<&2, U32> <- IO.pass(List<&2, U32>, r)
        m2 : File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, List<&2, U32>> <- File.read_at(f, (off + 1048576 : U32), 1048576)
        loop(p, (off + 1048576 : U32), m2, walk(bs, acc))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    t0 : Nat <- IO.now()
    f : File <- IO.try(File, File.open("w.bin", "r"))
    m : File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, List<&2, U32>> <- File.read_at(f, 0, 1048576)
    s : U32 <- loop(384n, 0, m, 0)
    t1 : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print("sum " ++ U32.show(s) ++ "  ms " ++ Nat.show(Nat.sub(t1, t0)))
```

The C twin and the full numbers: [bend-ml docs/upstream](https://github.com/nuxyel/bend-ml/tree/devel/docs/upstream).

title: C runtime faults under AddressSanitizer at -O1 and above: the base pointer x19 is clobbered by a preserve_none callee (arm64)
body:
- **What you did:** `bend tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend -o n.c`, then `clang -std=c11 -O1 -fsanitize=address n.c -lpthread -lm -o n && ./n`
- **What happened:** `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)`, exit 1 (expected `6n`)
- **bend --version:** bend 2.0.37 (checkout 014ccd03c43270c151f46679075f7f04593077ea)
- **uname -sm:** Darwin arm64
- **clang --version:** Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)

## Summary

A native program built from the emitted C with `-fsanitize=address` at
`-O1` or higher crashes with `bend: memory fault (machine stack
overflow?)`. This happens for most programs, even tiny ones, and also with
`--threads 1`. The same C file runs correctly at `-O0` with ASan, and
without ASan at any optimization level. UBSan, built together with ASan,
first reports `applying non-zero offset 256 to null pointer` in
`root_done`. That report is a symptom of the same bug, not a separate
problem: the heap pointer `H` is never null.

The cause is a codegen hazard in how the runtime enters its
`preserve_none` segments, not ASan itself. ASan makes `corpus_eval`
realign its stack frame. On arm64 the frame then uses `x19` as its base
pointer, and a `preserve_none` callee may clobber `x19`.

## Repro

Revision: 014ccd03c43270c151f46679075f7f04593077ea. The program is the
in-tree test `tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend`:

```bend
import Base

law main.out:
  Nat

def main.out():
  (1n + 2n + 3n : Nat)

law main:
  IO(Unit)

def main():
  IO.print(String.append(Nat.show(main.out()), "n"))
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend -o /tmp/n.c
clang -std=c11 -O1 -fsanitize=address /tmp/n.c -lpthread -lm -o /tmp/n
/tmp/n                  # bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?), exit 1
clang -std=c11 -O0 -fsanitize=address /tmp/n.c -lpthread -lm -o /tmp/n0
/tmp/n0                 # 6n
clang -std=c11 -O1 /tmp/n.c -lpthread -lm -o /tmp/n1
/tmp/n1                 # 6n
```

`tests/run/binary_search.bend` faults the same way, also with
`--threads 1`. With the runtime's SIGSEGV handler removed, ASan reports
`SEGV on unknown address 0x...cb ... in work_loop`, inlined into
`corpus_eval`.

Environment: Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2), macOS 27.0.1
(26A434), arm64.

## Root cause

All line numbers below are in `bend2/comp.ts` at 014ccd03.

- The segments are `WL_FN` functions, which are `preserve_none`
  (`#define WL_FN static PRESERVE(preserve_none) ...`, line 3369; and
  `PRESERVE`, line 3339). They musttail into each other (lines
  3372-3373).
- `work_loop` (line 4308) is the one function with the C calling
  convention that calls into them (`return WL_FID_ENTER(WL_ALL);`, line
  4321). It is `static` and gets inlined into `corpus_eval` (line 5270,
  `OUTLINE`, which is `preserve_most`, line 3343).
- Under ASan, `corpus_eval` realigns its stack to 32 bytes for its
  instrumented locals. AArch64 then keeps a base pointer in `x19`. In the
  disassembly of the `-O1 -g -fsanitize=address` build:

  ```
  _corpus_eval:
    ...
    and  sp, x9, #0xffffffffffffffe0
    mov  x19, sp                 ; base pointer
    ...
    bl   _WL_FID_ENTER           ; preserve_none callee
    ldr  x12, [x19, #0x68]       ; frame read through x19 after the call
  _WL_FID_ENTER:
    ...
    mov  x19, x22                ; the callee overwrites x19
  ```

- `preserve_none` makes `x19` a scratch register for the callee, and
  clang does not save the base pointer around the call. After
  `WL_FID_ENTER` returns, `corpus_eval` reads its frame through a garbage
  `x19`: the value it loads for `H` is 0, which UBSan reports in
  `root_done`, and the next access faults.
- Without ASan the frame needs no realignment and no base pointer, so the
  bug stays latent. Any future change that gives a frame on this path a
  base pointer (a VLA, `alloca`, over-aligned locals) would expose it in
  release builds too.

The cause is not:
- **A null-based heap pointer:** the corpus is mapped at a 2^45 hint and
  `H` is valid. With the fix below, UBSan with `pointer-overflow` on is
  clean.
- **The fixed-hint corpus mapping colliding with ASan's shadow memory:**
  `corpus_at` maps without `MAP_FIXED` and accepts only an honored hint,
  so it cannot overlap the shadow. Under ASan the corpus still lands at
  2^45.

## Suggested fix

Keep `work_loop` out of line. It then becomes a small C-convention
trampoline: its own frame needs no base pointer, it saves `x19` itself,
and its callers keep their frames intact.

```diff
-static Term work_loop(Env e, DEV Term* sp, Term t, u32 seq) {
+FAR Term work_loop(Env e, DEV Term* sp, Term t, u32 seq) {
```

`FAR` is `static __attribute__((noinline))`. On this Mac the change costs
nothing measurable: the CPU lane (`--gpu off`) gives a median of 7 runs of
1.29 s before and 1.27 s after for `bench/runtime/queens`, and 0.823 s
both before and after for `symreg`, with identical output. With it,
`nat_add_infix` and `binary_search` pass under `-fsanitize=address,undefined`
at `-O1` and `-O3`, with UBSan's `pointer-overflow` on, and under TSan.

A related clang/LLVM bug is likely worth reporting too: a `preserve_none`
call from a frame that uses a base pointer does not preserve the base
pointer on AArch64.

title: IO request to evaluate a pure function off the IO loop thread
body:
### What Bend should do

An IO request that evaluates a pure function off the IO loop thread and resumes the computation when the value is ready, so the loop keeps polling fds and running other computations meanwhile:

```python
# hypothetical
def IO.eval(f: U32 -> T) -> IO(T)

# a hub folds eight terminal panes' output (parallel calls inside)
h2 : Hub <- IO.eval(u => Hub.fold(h))
```

### Why

Today the pure part of a computation runs inside `io_step` on the loop thread; for a large value with parallel calls, the loop thread joins the pool in `pool_turn`, so no fd is polled until the value is done. In a terminal multiplexer written in Bend (8 panes x 256 MiB of VT output, plus a ninth pane timing echoes) folding the panes in parallel on the loop gives 33-55 MiB/s but an echo p99 of 6.6-15 ms; with a prototype of the request above, 69-74 MiB/s at an echo p99 of 0.3-2 ms, identical results.

The prototype, against v2.0.35, is about nine small edits to `comp.ts`: `io_stk` and the allocator row become thread-local; a mutex marks who owns the worker pool; a loop step that cannot take it evaluates sequentially and delivers to a host-side alternate root instead of `H_ROOT_WORD`; plus an effect that runs `Clo~apply(f, 0)` on an `io_work` helper thread and hands the value back through `io_wake_fd`. 20 TSan and 20 ASan stress runs were clean (macOS arm64). I can open a PR if this direction fits the runtime.

title: comp.ts sheds 266 tokens
body:
comp.ts goes from 63,652 to 63,386 ttok tokens on top of main. These are structural simplifications. The emitted program code is unchanged, and comments, if statements, types, section-prefixed names and every runtime cast stay as on main.

**Compiler**
- ty_srcs roots a type's datatypes directly, replacing type_adts.
- val_arms takes a `box` flag instead of a condition callback.
- emit_chain takes `[cond, body]` pairs.
- show_main reads main's layout from fun_of.
- emit_ctr's word and Array branches share their field emission.
- nat_add and nat_double share one tpl_ops entry.
- view_root folds into its one caller.
- emit_clo drops a binding copy.
- The lend edges come from `split("<").reverse()`.

**C runtime**
- WL_CASE opens its own brace.
- WL_FN and OUTLINE reuse FAR.
- io_wait uses one fd-set buffer.
- f32_text NUL-terminates and prints its exponent with `%+d`.
- main starts thr at the CPU count.

**JS runtime**
- char_new, now in a Char section, is bound from the TS function, as f32_round is. The Chr builder reuses it.
- f32_show's digit loop covers nan, ±inf and -0.

## Same output as main
- For all 1714 programs under tests/, demos/ and bench/runtime/:
  - the emitted C tables, spins and segments are byte-identical to main's, except for WL_CASE's brace;
  - the emitted JS program text is identical, except that non-scalar Char literals fold into string literals of the same value.
- Two review rounds reverted everything that was not a pure refactor:
  - term_aux's return type
  - the JS f32 bit views (Node keeps signaling-NaN payloads differently)
  - node_fill's name stems, wpoll and TAB_AT, which could flip INLINE/DFAR
  - task_deliver's loop bound
  - io_wait's running max fd
  - emit_jump's ref
  - WL_LOAD/WL_TAKE
  - emit_task's return
  - `#undef WL_X`
  - file_book's error order

## Verification
- **Gates:** test 1634/1634, perf 124/124, ping and repo all pass. comp.ts typechecks clean.
- **Both lanes:** all 1710 non-network programs print the same as with main's comp.ts on the JS and C lanes, GPU builds included. The one mismatch was tree-radix's JS timeout under 8-way load. Its program JS is identical, and alone or under synthetic load it times the same: 9.0 s on both.
- **Sanitizers:** 745 test builds with `-fsanitize=undefined` print the same as with main's comp.ts, and report nothing.
- **f32 text:** C f32_text and JS f32_show were fuzzed against main's (2^24 and 2M+ bit patterns, plus edge values, under Bun and Node) with no differences.

title: The != and where sugar mean the Empty and Exists of the file they are written in, not the entry's
body:
Closes #1331.

The `!=`, `exs` and `where` sugar wrote `Empty` and `Exists` as bare names that never went through `parse_reso`. With Base loaded that is harmless, since the bare key is Base's and `parse_fresh` keeps anyone from redeclaring it. Without Base, the bare key is whatever the entry file declares, so a library's `!=` meant the entry's `Empty`, and its `where` the entry's `Exists`. The issue's PROOF.bend certifies a false law that way, and a LAWS.bend that declares its own `Empty` checks alone but loses it the moment it is imported.

The sugar now takes its name from `parse_own`, in the file where it is written: the file's own `Empty`/`Exists` if the file declares one, else the bare name, which is Base's when Base is in scope; a user alias is not consulted, and when neither exists the usual "a defined name" error points at the sugar. The four sites write the call as plain `App`s around `Ref(parse_own(p, …))`, so against `main` the diff is mostly `Ref("X")` → `Ref(parse_own(p, "X"))`. Nothing changes for a book that imports Base. A local binder still cannot capture the codomain, since the sugar yields a top-level `Ref`, never a `Var`; `tests/check/neq_qualified_capture.bend` is unchanged.

@nicolas-abril's commits on this branch put the rest of the sugar through the same rule: `Array.new`, `xs[i]` and `xs[i] <-` (`Array.get`/`Array.set` and the `U32` index), the infix operators and `<>`, and the `&&`/`||`/`++` check. `parse_own` looks in one table: sugar that names a def or type (`!=`, `&`, `|`, `&x: A -> B`, the operators) looks in `tlds`, sugar that builds a constructor (`<>`) in `ctrs`, so a file's constructor named `Empty`, `Pair`, `Or` or `Exists` no longer takes over `!=`, `&`, `|` or `&x: A -> B`, and a def named `Con` no longer takes over `<>`. List and tuple literals (`[a, b]`, `(a, b)`) now build the file's own `Con`/`Nil`/`Tuple`, as `<>` already did. Char, string and number literals (`Zero`/`Succ`) stay bare, as on `main`, like the `Lit` nodes they unfold from: a file with its own `Nat` gets a type error rather than its own constructors, which also avoids a stack overflow on large literals. The one name the literal path still wrote bare was the `Nat.add` a big literal (`300n+x`) lowers to; the fifth commit sends it through `parse_own` as well, since a Base-free LAWS file's `300n+Zero{}` otherwise reaches for the proof file's `Nat.add` and a law that 300 is zero certifies (`tests/import/big_lit_add` pins the pair, refused now). The literals themselves stay plain.

Of the two directions the issue lists, this is the second. Binding the sugar to Base only would refuse `!=` and `where` in a Base-free book outright; resolving in place keeps a Base-free module's oWhat I ran: every file under `tests/` through `bend <file>` on `main` and on each commit of this branch, byte-identical output on the shared files (1,641 files at the time). Rebased on `main` (757180e3); gates on Mac: repo 54/54 (bend.ts at 44,493 of 48,000, `main` is 44,345), test 1768/1768, perf 124/124, ping 80/81 (the BendHub `lic_bom--name` check, which fails on `main` too). Not run: safe (needs a `bendtt` build), the cluster gates.

title: IO.eval: run a pure computation off the IO loop thread; keep work_loop out of line
body:
Two commits:

1. **`work_loop` stays out of line** (fixes #1574). Under ASan at `-O1` and above, `work_loop` was inlined into `corpus_eval`. Its realigned frame keeps a base pointer in x19, and a `preserve_none` segment clobbered it. As a `FAR` function, `work_loop` is a C-convention trampoline that saves x19 itself. With this change, `tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend` prints `6n` under `-fsanitize=address` at `-O1` and `-O3`, where it faulted before.

2. **`IO.eval(f)` runs a pure computation off the IO loop thread** (closes #1575). While a long pure computation runs, the loop keeps serving fds, timers and channels.
   - `IO.eval` queues `f` for one dedicated eval thread, not the IO helpers, so a long eval never holds a helper that a file or socket effect needs.
   - The eval thread owns the worker pool through a mutex, `io_owner`. It allocates from the spare row `ALC[CUBE_T]`, which was unused, and uses its own stack. `io_stk` and the new `io_alc` are thread-local, and `pool_turn`, `cube_run` and `corpus_eval` use `ALC[io_alc]`.
   - The loop may need to evaluate a continuation while the eval thread owns the pool. It then evaluates sequentially (`seq` true, also in programs with bangs: no pool, no device) and delivers its result to a host-side alternate root (`io_alt`), not the shared root in the heap header.
   - The JS twin applies `f` at once.

`comp.ts` is at 63,912 ttok, under the 64k cap with 88 to spare.

Tests:
- `tests/io/io_eval.bend`: a parallel sum by `IO.eval` while the loop computes its own.
- `tests/io/io_eval_hold.bend` is deterministic. A test effect returns only once another thread holds `io_owner`, so the loop's next continuation, which calls a bang's def, always runs on the alternate path. With the previous `seq` expression (`!BANGS && (pool_size == 1 || io_alt)`) it failed with `frontier drained without a result` (10/10 with the GPU, 8–9/10 with `--gpu off`). With this one it passed 30/30.

Checked on an M-series Mac with Apple clang 21:
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54.
- I ran every `tests/io` and `tests/run` test with `#|` lines through the C and JS lanes, on `main` and on this branch. The same 140 lanes fail on both, and the branch adds the new tests' passes.
- 20 ASan and 20 TSan runs of `io_eval` were clean. The hold test ran under TSan with Metal on and off.
- I did not run the mini-cluster gates or a CUDA build. The new host code sits under `#if !DEVICE`.

This was prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed by other models before submission.

title: fix(runtime): keep the preserve-none entry bridge out of line
body:
Fixes #1574.

Keep `work_loop` out of line. It is the C-convention bridge into `preserve_none` segments; inlining it lets a segment clobber the caller's frame base register. This uses the existing `FAR` attribute, not a sanitizer-only workaround.

The issue includes the arm64 disassembly and before/after evidence for this change. Locally I built the two reported programs with Clang 22.1.8 on Linux x86-64:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend -o nat.c
clang -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined nat.c -lpthread -lm -o nat
./nat --threads 1 --gpu off
# 6n
```

Both `nat_add_infix` (`6n`) and `binary_search` (`4169`) pass ASan+UBSan at -O0, -O1 and -O3 with 1 and 4 threads: 12 native runs. Their emitted JS also returns the expected results. Repository gate: 54/54.

I did not run macOS/arm64, Metal, CUDA, or the mini-cluster gates here. The macOS evidence is the issue author's, not a new run from me. No duplicate test was added: these are the existing repro fixtures.

AI-assisted with GPT-6.1 Sol; no subagents.

title: --verdict takes a ~ constant's model from the template's instances, not from a search
body:
Supersedes #1444. Refs #1182.

## Problem

`--verdict` checks a template root once, with each `~` parameter as an opaque constant `k~p`. The kernel has no axioms, so each constant needs a closed model of its type. Today the model is searched for: constructors, `{==}`, projections, in bounded rounds. That search can't prove an injectivity law (#1182's `use~F`), and it picks models one constant at a time, so later ones may not fit (#1263).

#1444 adds a lookup: any def in the book whose type is definitionally equal. That fixes the reported case, but it makes a root's verdict depend on unrelated defs, and it starts selecting premises by type, the first step of a prover. Each case it misses invites another rule. safe.ts should translate the program, not solve for terms.

## Change

A constant's model is the argument that a bend2 instance of the root passes at that parameter (`book.tmps`, already read as `e.inst`). It is the user's own term, and bend2 already checked it at that type. All of a root's models come from one instance: `inst_pick` takes the first instance whose `~` arguments all fit, each checked in the model book at its parameter's type after the ones before it. Each model is checked again at its constant's type. The search builds a model only for a root with no instance that fits, e.g. a law nobody calls.

- The constant stays opaque in the root, so the root is still checked for every argument, not just the instance's. The kernel checks every model.
- One call supplies all of a root's constants, so they fit together without backtracking, and the verdict doesn't depend on the order of the calls. `use2(~pred, ~inj2, …)` in the new test: a built model `f := n => Z{}` leaves no model for `P`, and pred plus inj2 fit. In `t`, `ia`'s `g` (`n => pp(n, n)`) uses `n` twice, so `ia` doesn't fit, and `t` takes `f`, `g` and `P` all from `ib`, in either order.
- An instance argument is checked as the root's own code. An argument that calls a template (`~(n => app(~pred, n))`) used to throw a TypeError, which was read as "doesn't fit". It now checks. Only bend2's check errors count as "doesn't fit", and any other error is thrown.
- `def_emit` reuses the model chosen in `root_emit` instead of searching again, and `root_emit` fits the instance's argument before it searches, so the search runs only for a constant with no fitting argument.
- Roots share a `~` constant (#1358) only where they give it the same model (d913fa46), so a root's models are its own whatever the order of the book. On `tests/` that loses a little sharing: the BendTT is 33.70 MB against 33.58 MB on main.
- The search is unchanged, projection models included. 90a03b64 dropped them and c7c96fbc restores them: a template that nothing calls still needs them. `tk` in the test is an example: its `~p: Pk` record needs `g := n => n`.

## Checks

- New `tests/proof/template_inst_model.bend`: on main, `--verdict` gives `no model for use~F` and `no model for use2~P`. Here it gives `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. Running it prints `({==}, {==}, Z{})`. It also covers both of @Lorenzobattistela's review cases (`use4`, and `t`/`ia`/`ib`), plus the uncalled `tk`. On 90a03b64, `t` fails with `ia` first (`no model for t~P`) and `tk` fails (`no model for tk~p`).
- Every `tests/**/*.bend` (1,648 files) ran under `--verdict` with the local Lean 4.34.0 kernel, at d08a415d (5363880e gives the same verdicts):
  - Against 90a03b64: identical verdicts.
  - Against main: identical except the new test and `tests/check/safe_parameterized_unit.bend`, which goes from out of scope (`no model for idt~A`; no Base, so no `Unit` model) to `ALL PROOFS CHECK`, with `A := In` from `main`'s call.
- Gates (macOS, 5363880e): repo 54/54, ping 57/57, test 1635/1635, perf 124/124. `gates/safe.ts tests`: agree 1060, unsafe 93, bend2 rejects 492, out of scope 3, 0 false rejects. `safe.ts`: 23,978 / 24,000 ttok.
- `tsc`: same diagnostics in `safe.ts` as 90a03b64.

## Limits

- #1182's literal repro defines `inj` but never calls `use`, so `use~F` still has no model and stays out of scope. That is deliberate: nothing in the program says which term stands for `F`.
- If an instance's argument is something the kernel can't express (foreign or `@unsafe` code), its root now goes out of scope where a built model used to reach the kernel. No test in `tests/` does this; the hub corpus was not run.
- If an instance's argument is out of scope, the template is reported out of scope with the argument's reason, for example "a word literal of a parameterized datatype". The verdict doesn't change.
- Cost: `--verdict` on `demos/app_slash_boss_3d/bend3d.bend` takes 0.26 s against 0.28 s on main; `nat_literal_no_arithmetic.bend` takes 0.12 s against 0.06 s.
- Not run: the hub corpus, Linux, CUDA.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(runtime): keep the host work-loop entry out of line
body:
## Problem and fix

Generated C can crash on arm64 when built with optimization and AddressSanitizer, even with one thread. For example, `nat_add_infix` faults instead of printing `6n`. Inlining the C entry into a caller with a realigned stack frame lets a call into a `preserve_none` segment clobber the caller's `x19` base pointer.

Add one `FAR` declaration for `work_loop` inside the existing `#if !DEVICE` block. It keeps the host entry out of line through `FAR`'s existing `noinline` attribute. The shared definition and calling convention stay as they are.

Fixes #1574.

## Blast radius

Only `bend2/comp.ts` changes: one host-only declaration affecting evaluator and pool-worker entry. No new helper, macro, allocation, or public API change. The device dispatcher is unchanged; baseline/candidate CUDA and Metal preprocessing tokens match. This avoids the broader GPU outlining change discussed in [#1433](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1433#issuecomment-6079307232).

## Regression evidence

Fresh base `25233fb` runs reproduce the `nat_add_infix` failure at O1/O3 with ASan+UBSan on Apple Clang 17.0.0 and LLVM 23.1.3. The corrected generated C passes 24 sanitizer runs across `nat_add_infix`, `binary_search`, and `fork_leaf_result_loop`, both compilers, O1/O3, and threads 1/4 with GPU off. Candidate O0 ASan and O3 unsanitized Nat controls also pass across both compilers and thread counts. Disassembly confirms that the outlined wrapper saves and restores `x19` around `WL_FID_ENTER`.

A separate diagnostic build confirms `work_loop` entry on actual non-main pool workers with both compilers and the expected fork result `4000`. Diagnostic hooks are not part of the patch or the sanitizer regression binaries.

Repeatable manual regression using an existing fixture:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts tests/run/nat_add_infix.bend -o /tmp/bend-1574.c
clang -std=c11 -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined /tmp/bend-1574.c -lpthread -lm -o /tmp/bend-1574
/tmp/bend-1574 --threads 1 --gpu off
```

Expected output: `6n`. The ordinary gate does not enable ASan, so a duplicate Bend fixture would pass on the broken baseline too.

## Checks

- Local repo gate: **54/54**, with CI-pinned ttok 0.3; `comp.ts` is **63,495/64,000 tokens**.
- Nine check/interpreter/emitted-JS controls pass across three existing fixtures. Their emitted JS is byte-identical to base.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

CPU timing used an Apple M1 Pro, Apple Clang 17.0.0, `cc -std=c11 -O3`, GPU off, and threads 1/4. Each cell has one warm run per variant and five alternating base/fix pairs. All 96 release runs (16 warm, 80 measured) produced the expected output with exit 0 and empty stderr.

| Workload / threads | Base median [min–max], s | Fix median [min–max], s | Fix/base medians |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| queens / 1 | 9.382 [9.205–12.591] | 9.401 [9.189–12.905] | 1.002 |
| queens / 4 | 2.348 [2.262–3.742] | 2.372 [2.308–3.260] | 1.010 |
| symreg / 1 | 6.553 [6.008–6.792] | 6.319 [6.237–6.554] | 0.964 |
| symreg / 4 | 1.643 [1.640–1.774] | 1.671 [1.612–1.786] | 1.017 |
| deep fork / 1 | 0.939 [0.922–0.999] | 0.952 [0.949–1.039] | 1.013 |
| deep fork / 4 | 0.273 [0.249–0.304] | 0.274 [0.258–0.309] | 1.002 |
| repeated shallow fork / 1 | 2.900 [2.825–3.345] | 2.343 [2.300–2.569] | 0.808 |
| repeated shallow fork / 4 | 12.830 [12.588–13.425] | 12.359 [12.000–14.186] | 0.963 |

The scratch fork workloads reuse `fork_leaf_result_loop`: a depth-22 tree with 16 Result turns per leaf, and 1,000,000 repeated depth-2 calls with 16 turns per leaf. Separate diagnostics count 767 host entries for the deep tree and about 12 million for the repeated shallow case; timed binaries have no diagnostic hooks. The shared desktop had material background activity, and timings include visible outliers. These are local measurements, not a performance-neutrality claim or the cluster perf gate.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS 15.8.1 arm64 with Bun 1.3.11. The reporter's exact Apple Clang 21, Linux, Windows, TSan, and the cluster gates were not run. GPU preprocessing equality is not GPU compilation/execution: Metal preprocessing used an empty header shim because the Metal compiler is unavailable. Other than manual sanitizer coverage, no test gate was added or changed. Existing sanitizer-build `sprintf` deprecation warnings remain.

title: fix(runtime): isolate trampoline frames in ASan builds
body:
Fixes #1574. Replaces the rejected approach in #1579; that PR stays closed.

Keep `work_loop` out of line only when Clang's AddressSanitizer feature is active. This protects its frame base across `preserve_none` calls without changing the normal runtime. Sanitizer instrumentation is not disabled.

The reported 17–24% normal-build slowdown is accepted; I did not rerun those benchmarks to dispute it. Instead, I compared generated code against fresh main `25233fbf`: both preprocessed normal C and `-O3` assembly are byte-identical for `nat_add_infix`, `binary_search`, and the reported `editdist` workload.

- `nat_add_infix` returns `6n`; `binary_search` returns `4169` under ASan+UBSan at `-O0`, `-O1`, and `-O3`, each with 1 and 4 threads: 12 successful native executions.
