title: fix(formatter): preserve inline lambda body alignment
body:
## Problem and fix

Formatting an inline lambda can move its aligned continuation to ordinary indentation, turning a valid program into a parse error. For example, a lambda containing two array writes prints `[7, 8]` before formatting and fails afterwards.

Recognize the first body token after `=>` and reuse the existing column pins to move its continuations together. This adds two executable lines and follows the [column-shift approach requested in #1302](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1302#pullrequestreview-5421381492).

## Blast radius

Two bundled-tool files: `tools/bend-fmt-lsp/src/formatter.ts` and its existing formatter test. The shared `formatBend` path serves direct callers and LSP formatting requests. Existing header state and delimiter tracking are preserved. There is no exported API or source compatibility break.

The regression stays in the tool's own suite, following [the external-tool gate guidance in #1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

## Regression evidence

Add one fixture to the existing pinned-layout cases, checking exact formatting, idempotence and equivalent execution through the real Bend CLI under default, four-space and tab options.

With the exact new test and the baseline formatter from `b869cca`, the normal package build succeeds and tests report **28 passed, 2 expected failures, 0 skipped**. Both failures catch the lambda defect: the expected continuation column and actual CLI execution. The corrected formatter preserves `[7, 8]` and passes the same checks.

## Checks

- `npm test` in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: TypeScript build and Node formatter/server suites; **30 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Additional nested, parenthesized and annotated lambda checks: 18 baseline-failing cases pass with the fix; six control cases retain their results. Candidate formatting is idempotent.
- Repository gate with CI-pinned ttok 0.3: **54/54**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64, Node 26.8.2 and Bun 1.3.11. The existing stdio LSP test covers ordinary formatting; the lambda regression exercises the shared formatter and real CLI, rather than an editor session. Windows, actual editor clients and mini-cluster gates were not run.

title: fix(formatter): preserve inline bodies after operators in types
body:
The formatter can turn a valid inline function body into a parse error when a type or proof annotation contains `<`, `>`, `<<`, or `>>`. It counts these operators as generic brackets, misses the body's colon, and moves the next statement away from the required column. The regression programs print `[7, 8]` before formatting but fail to parse after formatting.

Count angle tokens only at the header's bracket depth. Add four proof-parameter cases to the existing tests for column-sensitive layouts. These tests check the output, check idempotence, and run the programs through Bend before and after formatting with default settings, four-space indentation, and tabs.

This covers an additional case in the inline-body tracking from #1302. The change is one formatter condition and regression tests.

Validation on macOS arm64:

- TypeScript build and formatter/LSP tests: 30/30 pass, zero skipped. The new cases fail with the original condition.
- Five focused programs, including a return-type case, under three formatting settings: 15/15 fail before the fix and 15/15 pass after it.
- All 1,745 tracked Bend files under three settings: 5,235 outputs match the original formatter. All outputs remain idempotent.
- Repository gate: 54/54 pass. `git diff --check` passes.

The private cluster, Lean, GPU, and performance gates were not run.

title: The root file gets its own namespace, so sugar's bare names can only mean Base's
body:
> 🤖 Written by an AI agent for @nicolas-abril; not yet reviewed by a human.

The root file and Base shared the empty namespace. Because of that, a bare name written by sugar (`Empty` for `!=`, `Exists` for `where`, `Nat`/`Succ` for literals, `Con`/`Nil` for lists, `Tuple` for pairs, `Type.op` for operators) resolved to whatever the root file declared. One result is that a module's `!=` law could take its `Empty` from the entry that imported it (#1331).

With this PR the root file loads under its own namespace, the one an import of it would get (its file name). Base keeps the empty one. Sugar itself doesn't change: it still writes Base's bare names. In a file without Base those names are undefined, and a literal never means a file's own `Nat` or `List`. This matches the guide: "Operators, literals and brackets are sugar for names in Base."

**Code** (`bend.ts` +136 tokens, `main.ts` +110):
- `book_read` loads the root under `basename(file)`. `tlds["main"]` points at the root's `main`.
- `name_key` prints the root's own names bare, so output is unchanged.
- `cli_verdict` decides whether a def belongs to the root by checking the root's namespace.
- Fixed a bug that already existed in imported modules: a forward reference to a dotted type applied to `<..>` was qualified twice (`lib:lib:Vec.Con`).
- `parse_qual` now builds each `ns:name` only once, and `parse_reso` checks the far name only when the own one is missing. Without these two changes, the longer root keys made `generics_3200` about 7% slower and pushed it past the perf gate's 1.15x limit.

**Dropping the TLD `b` flag** (dc7c14d9). Once the root file has its own namespace, a name with no `:` belongs to Base. The `b` ("from Base") field on top-level definitions doesn't tell you anything the name doesn't, so this commit removes it:
- `Bend.is_base(k)` (the name has no `:` and no `~`) replaces every read of `b` in `bend.ts`, `comp.ts`, `main.ts` and `safe.ts`.
- `b` also marked a template's stand-in constants (`f~T`) while `def_check` runs. That job now has its own flag, `o`.
- Removed the checks that refused a root file for declaring a name the compiler encodes itself (`OWNED` in `comp.ts`, plus the `b` guards in `intr_of`, `io_base`, literals and foreign IO). The root's `Nat` is now `file:Nat`, so it can't be taken for Base's. A Base-free file that declares its own `Nat` now builds, where main refused it with "Nat is a name the compiler encodes itself".
- `book_load` refuses the empty namespace for any file except Base. `gates/test.ts` (`state_run`) loads each file under its own namespace, the way the CLI does.
- Tokens against the previous head: `bend.ts` +59, `comp.ts` -111, `safe.ts` -5, `main.ts` -1.

**bend-lint** (22764c34). bend-lint found the root file by the empty namespace, so on this PR its self-check threw `DriftError` on every file. `tools/bend-lint/src/seam.ts` now finds the root by its namespace and shows rules the root's own names bare: fact names, owners, the `defs`/`names` filters, `body(name)` and the self-check. Rules and their configs don't change. The format guard also deletes the `main` alias when it removes `ns:main`. Without that, every format fix failed with "duplicate declaration: main". The tests that read bend's internal data now expect `ns:name` keys. bend-lint: 126/126 pass, the same as main. The gates don't run bend-lint.

**Behaviour change.** These Base-free tests declare their own `Nat`/`String`/`List`/`U32` constructor in the root and relied on literals or printing using them. Their expected output changed:
- Now refused: `nat_literal_custom_arithmetic`, `nat_literal_no_arithmetic` (#1337), `nat_literal_own_succ`, `string_literal_own_scon` (#941, still refused, with a different message), `nat_literal_pattern_arity`, `nat_literal_pattern_empty`, `safe_box_word_def`, `safe_parameterized_box_word` (#1338).
- Print the constructors instead of sugar: `cop_bare_trio_000`, `flatten/type_param_match_000`.
- Rewritten to use explicit constructors (their point wasn't literals): `beta_ann_match`, `grade/accept_data`. `show/cons_chain_readback` now uses Base's `List`.
- The checker benchmarks (`bench/checker/*`, Base-free) spell `Tuple{..}` and `Pair(..)` instead of tuple and `&` sugar.
- New test: `import/root_ns_empty`. The entry offers its own inhabited `Empty` for a module's `!=` law. It was certified on main and is refused here.

**Relation to #1577.** #1577 fixes #1331 from the module's side, making sugar use the writing file's own name. This PR fixes it from the entry's side. Whichever merges second will need its `tests/import` expectations re-pinned.

**Checks** (macOS M-series, at 22764c34): repo 54/54, ping 57/57, test 1637/1637, perf 124/124; bend-lint 126/126. safe.ts on 1650 files: 0 false rejects (run with dc7c14d9; 22764c34 only touches bend-lint and doesn't change `bend2/`). No new tsc errors in `bend2/`. Not run: bend-lint's `tsc` (its `@types/bun` dev dependency isn't installed here), Linux, CUDA, hub corpus.

title: fix(gates): restore names in verdict summaries
body:
## Problem and fix

Since [#1531](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1531), `--verdict` groups affected names under `defs that depend on @unsafe:` and `foreign effects:`. The safe gate still extracts old `- name` lines, so its table prints an empty `unsafe: ` reason even when the verdict names the affected defs.

Read the two current group labels, split their comma-separated names, and retain the existing first-three-entry limit and printed order.

## Blast radius

The regression reuses ping's existing unsafe file, CLI runner and check helper.

## Regression evidence

Five real CLI cases reproduce empty names with baseline `b869cca` and recover the expected names with this fix: unsafe-only, foreign-only, mixed groups, repeated names and the three-entry bound.

The exact new ping assertion was also executed locally through the existing subprocess helper and real source CLI: it fails with baseline `judge` and passes with the corrected function (`u|unsafe: main`).

## Checks

- Five actual CLI regression cases passed.
- Ten synthetic classifier controls retain their results, including agreement, rejection, out-of-scope, timeout, infrastructure and diagnostic precedence.
- `bun build --target=bun` for both changed gate files: passed.
- Repository gate with CI-pinned ttok 0.3: **54/54**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Validation limits

Mini-cluster gates and Windows were not run. Synthetic classifier controls do not establish live kernel, timeout or SSH behavior.

title: fix(lint): limit Base seeding to the import header
body:
## Problem and fix

bend-lint treats any source line exactly equal to `import Base` as a module import, including lines inside multiline strings. This can silently supply undeclared Base types or reject valid Base-free programs for duplicate declarations.

Use the same initial-header predicate as the current CLI's `--checkup`, preserving the existing Base cache and loader. This follows the [loader/seeding consistency feedback in #1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#pullrequestreview-5445845798).

## Blast radius

Three bundled-tool files: the seeding predicate in `src/seam.ts`, one regression beside the existing Base-cache test in `src/lint.test.ts`, and the README's seeding explanation. Tests stay in bend-lint's own suite, following the [later #1389 guidance](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

No public API or configuration migration. Files accepted only because literal text accidentally injected Base now report the same undefined-name error as Bend. The language, compiler/runtime and root test gate are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The retained four-line input has `import Base` only inside a string and refers to undeclared `String`. Direct Bend rejects it; baseline lint incorrectly accepts it. With only the new test added, baseline fails at the intended `ok` assertion; the fix passes. The test covers disk and unsaved text, absence of injected Base, and genuine plain/commented/indented headers.

Supplemental CLI checks also cover the opposite failure: a valid Base-free program defining its own types runs in Bend, but baseline lint rejects duplicate `Bool`; this fix accepts it.

## Checks

- `bun run test` in `tools/bend-lint`: **127 passed, 841 assertions**.
- Six real CLI outcomes confirm the expected baseline/corrected behavior for both fixtures above.
- Repository gate with CI-pinned ttok 0.3: **54/54**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64 and Bun 1.3.11. TypeScript 5.9.3 reports the same two pre-existing TS2339 errors in protected `bend2/bend.ts`, at lines 2040 and 3771; before/after diagnostics are identical. Installed-release and mini-cluster checks were not run.

Pending [#1585](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1585) currently stops bend-lint at its compatibility self-check with both the old and corrected predicates. Combined behavior remains unverified; this patch does not expand into that namespace-seam repair.

title: A flat generic def's spin takes words at its instance's layouts (#1195)
body:
Closes #1195.

## Root cause

A generic def (`-A: Type`) already gets one spin per layout of its erased types, but every spin kept the generic calling convention: a value of type `A` crosses the call as one boxed word. So `Bool.pick(Tint, ...)` with a flat `Tint{r, g, b}` made the caller heap-allocate a node, the callee drop the unpicked one through the generic `term_drop`, and the result come back boxed to be unpacked again (`ctr_take` + free). On the device each small spin is inlined at every call site into the one kernel, so that heap round trip is copied per site, which is what blows up the Metal program.

## Fix

A flat def's spin takes and returns words at its own instance's layouts. An open type takes the layout of the value that reaches it (`lay_at`). If a self-call changes an erased type (polymorphic recursion, e.g. `grow(Dup<A>, ...)`), the def keeps the generic convention, so there is no extra copy. Spins are the ones that already existed: the corpus has 1825 spins before and after.

## Numbers

- Issue repro (`Bool.pick(Tint, ...)`): Metal program 96,176 -> 74,816 B (the `match` version is 74,784); heap_alloc 14 -> 13.
- Bendcraft at af8da15 with the issue's `Bool.pick(Tint, ...)`: main 17 s / 4.20 MB Metal, this PR 9 s / 2.15 MB (no-pick baseline: 9 s / 2.25 MB). v2.0.34 did not finish (killed at 240 s, 3.4 GB). `make test-native` passes, bench checksums identical.
- Emitted C over the 775 test files: 85 change, heap_alloc 16,223 -> 16,100, no file gains an allocation, total -57 KB.
- Repro scaled to tree 22n: 1 thread 33 -> 15 ms, GPU 86 -> 81 ms.

New test `tests/compile/generic_flat_instance.bend` covers pick at Tint/V2/U32/List, a type-changing self-call (`grow`) and a type-keeping loop (`last`).

## Gates

repo 54/54, test 1636/1636, ping 58/58, perf 124/124. comp.ts 63,997 / 64k tokens. Not run: safe (local `bendtt` not built; change is comp.ts only), CUDA, Linux, Windows.

title: fix(gates): recognize valid Base import headers
body:
## Problem and fix

The test gate requires an exact `import Base` line before selecting compiled lanes. Existing `reg/framed_cell_dep.bend` deliberately uses `import   Base  # the import head obeys the lexer`, so it is checked and interpreted but silently omitted from C and JS execution.

Recognize Base within the initial import header, allowing spaces, tabs and trailing comments while excluding import-like body text and longer names. This changes one selector line and preserves the fixture's explanatory header.

## Blast radius

One file: `gates/test.ts`. Only compiled-lane selection changes; foreign-twin filtering, failed-test exclusions and shard execution remain unchanged. Across all 1,635 current fixtures, only `reg_framed_cell_dep` gains lanes: one additional JS run and one C run. There is no language or public API compatibility change.

## Regression evidence

Local verification calls the actual `test_read`, `test_runs`, `test_probes` and `shard_script` functions through scratch-only exports. Requiring the existing fixture's JS/C lanes fails against baseline `d2aeefc` and passes with the fix. Its compiled build command is absent from the baseline shard and present afterward. No probe export or verification harness is added to the repository.

The existing fixture also runs through the real source CLI, emitted JavaScript and native C binary; each prints the expected `3` and exits zero.

## Checks

- Complete 1,635-fixture scheduling comparison: only the intended fixture changes; header, body-literal, Base-boundary and foreign-lane controls pass.
- Existing local `state_run`: four fixtures pass repeated C/JS emission and normalization checks.
- `bun build --target=bun gates/test.ts`: passed.
- Repository gate with CI-pinned ttok 0.3: **54/54**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64 and Bun 1.3.11; CI uses Bun 1.4.0. The full mini-cluster gate was not run because the configured `cluster` hostname does not resolve locally. Windows and GPU execution were not tested. The fixture inventory verifies scheduling metadata, not execution of the entire suite.

No permanent scheduling assertion is added. The fixture gains compiled coverage, but a future selector reversion could silently remove those lanes again. The predicate covers ordinary ASCII import-header spacing; it does not reproduce every Unicode whitespace character accepted by the loader.

title: fix(formatter): preserve semicolon body alignment
body:
## Problem and fix

Formatting a valid inline binding followed by `;` can misalign the following body. An array-update program that prints `[7, 8]` becomes a parse error because spaces inserted before its first update move that update farther than its aligned continuation.

Recognize `;` in the existing inline-body pin condition, retaining `open === 0`. This reuses the [column-shift approach requested in #1302](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1302#pullrequestreview-5421381492) and preserves the [delimiter restriction added by the maintainer in #1583](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/8819cd91e5d4422e0e9e057c4a67abbf0ac9bf67).

## Blast radius

Two files in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: one condition and its explanatory comment in `src/formatter.ts`, plus regression coverage in the existing formatter test. The shared formatter serves direct callers and LSP formatting requests. There is no exported API or source compatibility break.

The compiler, parser, LSP transport and root gates are unchanged. Tests stay in the tool's own suite, following [#1389](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

## Regression evidence

Add the valid array-update program to the existing pinned-layout cases. It checks exact formatting, idempotence and equivalent execution through the real Bend CLI with default indentation, four spaces and tabs. Compact controls cover semicolons inside parentheses/brackets, literals and comments.

With the exact final tests and baseline formatter from `d2aeefc`, the package builds successfully and reports **29 passed, 2 expected failures, zero skipped**. Both failures catch this defect: the continuation column and actual CLI execution. The corrected formatter passes all 31 tests and preserves `[7, 8]`.

## Checks

- `npm test` in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: TypeScript build and Node formatter/server suites; **31 passed, zero failed, zero skipped**.
- Supplemental real CLI checks cover multiple semicolons, rewrite bodies, final-newline/EOF variants and delimiter controls. Corrected formatting preserves execution and is idempotent.
- Removing only the semicolon depth guard changes the delimiter controls, confirming their sensitivity.
- Repository gate with CI-pinned ttok 0.3: **54/54**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64, Node 26.8.2 and Bun 1.3.11. The existing stdio LSP test covers ordinary requests; the new regression exercises the shared formatter and actual CLI rather than an editor session. Full mini-cluster gates, GPU execution and other host platforms were not run. This fixes depth-zero semicolon body anchors without changing the existing nested-delimiter policy.

title: perf(runtime): reuse rounded digits in native F32 formatting
body:
Native `F32.show` finds the shortest round-trip precision with scientific notation. For many values in fixed decimal notation, it then calls `snprintf` again. That second call repeats the decimal conversion and rounding.

Reuse the rounded digits and move the decimal point instead. For example, turn `1.25e-01` into `0.125` without a second conversion. Keep the precision search, notation thresholds, special values, and scientific-notation path unchanged.

The change adds 11 net lines to `comp.ts`. The regression test covers decimal-point positions, signs, negative zero, notation thresholds, large values, infinity, and NaN.

Measured complete CSV exports (milliseconds):

| Workload | macOS before | macOS after | Linux before | Linux after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Waveform | 444.3 | 406.6 | 510.0 | 465.6 |
| Short decimals | 166.7 | 135.9 | 157.0 | 135.6 |
| Integer-valued floats | 282.7 | 260.5 | 397.8 | 360.8 |
| Scientific notation | 435.3 | 439.5 | 698.1 | 699.2 |

Fixed decimal workloads used 7.9–18.5% less total time on macOS and 8.7–13.6% less on Linux. The scientific path is unchanged. Its small timing increase does not establish a regression.

Each program exports 200,000 generated rows with an integer index and three F32 columns. Each version ran 15 times in alternating order. The table gives the median after excluding the first two runs. Timing includes the native process and output to a pipe read by Python; it excludes compilation. Runs used `--threads 1 --gpu off`. All 120 outputs per platform had matching before/after hashes within each workload.

Both environments used an Apple M5 Max and Bun 1.3.14. macOS used Apple clang 21.0.0. Linux ran in an OrbStack ARM64 VM with Debian 13, glibc 2.41, and Clang 19.1.7. The baseline was `d2aeefc1902d617340e26f7fab5c1ef50fe28efa`.

Validation:

- Old/new formatter comparisons produced identical text and return lengths for 10,393,728 inputs on macOS, Linux glibc, and Linux musl 1.2.5. The inputs include every positive F32 in `[1, 2)`, two million pseudorandom bit patterns, and 5,120 exponent/mantissa boundary cases.
- The same comparison passed AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer on macOS and Linux glibc.
- All 24 focused native tests passed on macOS and Linux. The Linux compiler and native tests ran inside Linux.
- The new test also passed through the source CLI and emitted JavaScript under Bun on macOS.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54/54. `git diff --check`: passed.

Linux x86-64, CUDA, and the full test/performance cluster were not tested.

<details>
<summary>Waveform CSV workload</summary>

Save this as `/tmp/f32-csv.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def row(+i: U32) -> String:
  +t = F32.div(U32.to_f32(i), 48000.0)
  +a = F32.mul(6.2831855, F32.mul(440.0, t))
  U32.show(i) ++ "," ++ F32.show(t) ++ "," ++ F32.show(F32.sin(a))
    ++ "," ++ F32.show(F32.mul(0.75, F32.cos(a)))

def export(n: Nat, +i: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Unit <- IO.print(row(i))
        export(p, U32.inc(i))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  export(200000n, 0)
```

Build it from each checkout. Use a separate output path for each version:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts /tmp/f32-csv.bend -o /tmp/f32-csv-before
bun bend2/main.ts /tmp/f32-csv.bend -o /tmp/f32-csv-after
```

Run this Python script after both builds. It uses the same timing method as the table:

```python
import hashlib
import statistics
import subprocess
import time

bins = ["/tmp/f32-csv-before", "/tmp/f32-csv-after"]
times = {name: [] for name in bins}
hashes = set()
for repeat in range(15):
    for name in bins if repeat % 2 == 0 else bins[::-1]:
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        run = subprocess.run(
            [name, "--threads", "1", "--gpu", "off"],
            capture_output=True, check=True,
        )
        times[name].append((time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1e6)
        hashes.add(hashlib.sha256(run.stdout).hexdigest())
assert len(hashes) == 1
for name in bins:
    print(name, statistics.median(times[name][2:]), "ms")
```

</details>

title: Freestanding C builds: a BEND_HOST hook that replaces the runtime's OS host
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# Build a Bend program (no `!`) for a target with no OS by supplying the
# host the C runtime calls, instead of the OS one:
#
#   bend main.bend -o main.c
#   clang -ffreestanding -include mylibc.h -DBEND_HOST='"myhost.c"' main.c -o main
#
# With BEND_HOST set, the runtime skips its OS headers and main(), and
# includes myhost.c where the OS host (descriptor event loop, helper
# threads, sockets, float text) would be. myhost.c defines six functions
# and an entry point:

static void io_take(Env e);                                // hand finished calls back to the loop
static Term io_work(IoWork* w, IoCall call, IoPack pack);  // run a blocking call
static void io_wait(Env e, bool block);                    // wait for timers (and descriptors, if any)
static int  f32_text(char* buf, f32 v);                    // float text; may fail-stop
static Term f32_show(Env e, Term x);
static Term f32_read(Env e, Term s);

int main(void) {                                           // or _start / bend_main
  io_loop(corpus_setup(false, 1, arena_bytes));            // one core, the arena it was given
  io_sync();
  return 0;
}

# A single-core host that runs blocking calls inline and has no
# descriptors is about 60 lines.
```

### Why

Today the emitted C always includes the OS headers (pthread, sockets, select, mach-o) and defines main. There's no way to build a Bend program for a target without an OS: bare metal, a hypervisor or unikernel guest, or an embedded board.

My fork uses this hook to boot Bend programs at EL2 under QEMU with no OS. I'm not asking you to take the hypervisor; it stays on my fork. This issue is only about the hook.

Implementation: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/compare/main...GunnarZarncke:bend:freestanding-host
- The OS host (io_take, io_work, io_wait with its helper threads, io_sys_addr and the float text) moves verbatim from comp.ts into bend2/effs/host.c. The emitter includes it where that code used to be, unless BEND_HOST names another file.
- corpus_setup also accepts an explicit memory size on the CPU, so a host can fit an arena it was given. main still passes the size only on the GPU.
- A normal build is unchanged. The emitted C differs only in comments, preprocessor guards and the two corpus_setup lines. Nine native tests (float text, TCP, select, pipes, args, EPIPE) give the same output as on main.
- A 60-line host on macOS runs a plain program, and the binary links no socket, select, inet or pthread_create symbols.

The open question is the comp.ts cap. The move brings comp.ts from 63,495 to 62,011 tokens, and gates/repo.ts says files shrink "by simplification, never by moving code out". My argument is that this code is the OS backend's IO, which is what effs/ holds. The alternative, #ifdefs inside comp.ts, would take it over 64k. If neither is acceptable, feel free to close this.

Known gaps:
- io_loop still calls pipe, fcntl and signal itself, so a host has to provide stubs for them; moving that setup behind the host would close this.
- Someone who knows the release script should check that the compiled bend ships effs/host.c. The compiler reads it from BEND_DIR the same way it reads the other effs/ sources.

title: fix(gates): suppress telemetry in safe-worker children
body:
## Problem and fix

A newer-release notice on stderr contaminates the safe worker's combined CLI output. It can miscount `ALL PROOFS CHECK` as a frontend rejection and, during diagnostic export, classify a kernel rejection as out of scope. The latter hides a failure that should fail the safe gate.

Set the existing `BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1` switch in the worker's shared child environment. Reuse ping's controlled fuel kernel and private update cache for a regression through the actual worker.

## Blast radius

One spawn-environment line in `gates/safe_node.ts`, plus nine regression lines in `gates/ping.ts`. This covers verdict and diagnostic subprocesses. Ordinary CLI notices, stderr diagnostics, exit codes, classification rules, timeouts and failover are preserved. No public API or compatibility break.

## Regression evidence

With a cached newer release and the inherited telemetry opt-out cleared, the retained assertion fails on main: the kernel rejection becomes `-|out of scope: `. With the fix it passes as `!|In Sum.f: | out of fuel`.

Actual-worker controls also confirm accepted input is classified as agreement and kernel errors written entirely to stderr remain visible. A direct CLI control still prints the release notice and preserves its rejection text and exit code.

## Checks

- Repository gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`, using CI-pinned ttok 0.3.
- Both changed gate files bundle successfully with Bun.
- Exact retained regression fails baseline and passes the applied fix through the existing subprocess helper.
- Acceptance, rejection, unsafe-input, frontend-error and missing-kernel controls preserve their expected outcomes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64 and Bun 1.3.11. The complete ping gate skips because the sibling site repository is absent. Controlled shell kernels test process plumbing and classification; real Lean/BendTT, remote cluster gates, GPU and Windows execution were not run.

title: perf(c): hoist arm allocations, return through frame addresses, keep escaping fields of borrowed parameters
body:
## What changes

Rebased on main at 881cb2e5. After review, the refcount commit is gone, and the fork frame write-back went in on its own as #1615. `file_new` keeps its typed literal and `emit_fold` keeps its early returns. All five commits are in `bend2/comp.ts`; the fourth also adds or updates borrow witnesses under `tests/reg`.

1. **Shed 25 comp.ts tokens with the same output.** Compacts `scope_new`, folds `call_eta`'s early return, and joins wrapped lines that fit in 80 columns. C and JS output is byte-identical to main for all 840 programs that build (tests, benches and demos).
2. **Hoist the node allocation every match arm makes.** When each arm of an `if`/`else` chain allocates one node of the same size class outside any inner block, `emit_chain` allocates it once before the chain. Before, the inline `heap_alloc` fast/slow branch in each arm kept clang from merging the arms. Now their stores become selects instead of a branch on the tag. The C of 41 programs changes, 3 of them benches (tree-bitonic, tree-radix and symreg).
3. **Return through code addresses in host frames.** A host continuation frame stores its segment's address (`WL_K`), so `WL_RETN` tail-calls `STK(0)` directly instead of loading it from `wl_tab` first. Device frames keep fids. `WL_JMP` still compiles to a direct branch.
4. **Keep a borrowed parameter's field where it escapes.** A def that only reads a borrowed parameter, but passes one field of it to an owned position, used to own the whole parameter. A lookup that returns its match's value is the typical case. Owning it sent every node it walked through `ctr_take`, which on a shared value bumps each field, releases the node and sinks the rest. Now `val_own` keeps that field where it escapes (`term_keep`), and the parameter stays borrowed, so its nodes are read with `term_peek`. The root itself is never kept.
   - A kept field must already be sealed, so the root's type is heated (`FL.heat`), but only once a pass changes no fact. The first pass borrows every parameter, and heating there left types hot for roots that later become owned (merkle's `Mt`).
   - The root's def is read from its key, not from the scope, because a fused callee's body runs under the callee's def. `tests/reg/brw_field_fuse.bend` printed freed memory when that callee's parameter types were heated instead.
   - The C of 12 test programs and the `pure_hvm5_mini` demo changes, and of no bench.
5. **Cut comp.ts back under its cap.** See below.

## comp.ts tokens

Main is at 65,916 / 66,000 by itself (#1626 raised the cap to 66,000). Commits 1 to 4 take it to 66,223, and commit 5 brings it to **65,811**. On the rebase, one cut met a new sentence from #1653 in the same comment: the cut is kept and the new sentence stays.

Commit 5 makes two code edits, both with the same output. `emit_native` hands `emit_body` its own `f`, because `fun_at`'s copy holds the same `h`. It also sizes a spin with `body.join("\n")` instead of a reduce. Everything else in it is a comment cut, each one restating code a few lines away or a twin elsewhere in the file:

- **comp.ts emitter:**
  - the header's note that the runtimes close the file (the section headers show it);
  - the constants' `SPIN_FAR` sentence (the C runtime's long-spin comment says it in full);
  - "the Array operations have no C text" (`array_clone` and the atomics have some; `arr_op`'s call shows the rest);
  - the Optimized comment's gloss of `Native`'s fields (its type);
  - `char_new`'s encoding (its body) and the note that the JS runtime holds its text (the line that splices it in);
  - the Term comment's literal sentence (`lit_call`, below it);
  - `ty_holds`' lead clause (its signature);
  - the Lay comment's parenthetical on an element's open layout (`lay_el`);
  - `lay_at`'s comment (its one-line body);
  - the Mat comment's U32 table rule (`mat_rows`' condition);
  - the normal-form comment's erased-application clause (`anf`'s `Var` case);
  - the Emit comment's "a read asks a lend" (the File comment);
  - `emit_open`'s note on a foreign def's continuation (the Emit comment and `fun_of`'s lays);
  - "an effect source is read once, in one namespace" (`effect_srcs`' map and its error);
  - the JS comment's closure, `$pc` and direct-call clauses (`js_lib` and `js_def`);
  - `host`'s U+FFFD clause (the Char comment).
- **C runtime:**
  - the Dialect comment's segment-dispatch sentence (the `WL_` macros below it);
  - the Globals comment's device-program source (`BEND_SRC`);
  - the Gpu comment's "a launch loads it, else notes and compiles" (both `gpu_load` bodies);
  - the Corpus comment's GPU sentence (`corpus_grow` and `corpus_setup`);
  - the Io comment's request and parked-field sentences (`io_step` and `io_wait_on`);
  - `io_loop`'s busy-loop comment (the `(n & 63)` block);
  - the Show comment's `show_f32` sentence (`f32_text`'s round trip).
- **JS runtime:**
  - the Io comment's deadline-order sentence (`io_park_on`'s sorted insert, and the C `io_park` comment);
  - `io_fail`'s errno fallback (its first line).

Commit 4 also rewords the File, Scope and val_own comments to share less. It drops `compile_book`'s note that a pure main's descriptor roots the datatypes it prints: the Show section describes the descriptor, and the next lines root them.

## Checks

- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- `tsc -p bend2/pack/tsconfig.json` (TypeScript 5.9.3): the same 11 errors as main, none in `comp.ts`. The TS2352 from `file_new`'s cast is gone.
- Each commit against its parent, over the 840 programs that build to C and JS:
  - commit 1: byte-identical;
  - commit 2: only the hoisted chains change, in 41 programs;
  - commit 3: only the frame lines and the dispatch macros change;
  - commit 4: the C of 13 programs changes, and JS of none;
  - commit 5: only comment lines change, in the C and JS of all 840 programs (the cut runtime comments).
- Commit 4's 13 programs, built before and after it: all 12 tests print their expected output at `--threads 1`, `8` and `16`, and `pure_hvm5_mini` prints the same under both builds.
- `gates/test.ts`, run locally: PASS 1675 / 1677. The two failures, `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, expect "no display" and fail the same way on main here, because this Mac has a desktop session.

## Lookup repro (commit 4)

The program below walks a shared 20000-entry `List<&2, Entry>` 500 times, missing every time. `find` returns the match's value and `has` returns a Bool. It was built with `clang -O3`, each binary warmed once, then run 3 interleaved rounds with `./walk --threads 1 -- 20000 500` on an Apple M3 Max:

| build | has | find |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 44–45 ms | 146–147 ms |
| this branch before commit 4 | 44 ms | 146–148 ms |
| this branch | 44 ms | 46–47 ms |

<details><summary>main.bend</summary>

```python
# Purpose: time two walks over one shared list of records. Both compare every
# key and miss. find returns a field of the match; has returns a Bool.
# Run: bend main.bend -o walk && ./walk --threads 1 -- 20000 500

import Base

type Entry is Data:
  Entry{key: U32, value: String}

def entries(n: Nat, +i: U32) -> List<&2, Entry>:
  match n:
    case 0n: []
    case 1n+p: Entry{i, U32.show(i)} <> entries(p, (i + 1 : U32))

def hit(same: Bool, value: String) -> Maybe<&2, String>:
  match same:
    case True{}: Some{value}
    case False{}: None{}

def entry_hit(e: Entry, +query: U32) -> Maybe<&2, String>:
  match e:
    case Entry{key, value}: hit(U32.is_eq(key, query), value)

# The value of the first entry keyed query.
def find(es: List<&2, Entry>, +query: U32, found: Maybe<&2, String>) ->
    Maybe<&2, String>:
  match es found:
    case Nil{} f: f
    case e <> tail Some{v}: Some{v}
    case e <> tail None{}: find(tail, query, entry_hit(e, query))

def entry_is(e: Entry, +query: U32) -> Bool:
  match e:
    case Entry{key, value}: U32.is_eq(key, query)

# Whether some entry is keyed query.
def has(es: List<&2, Entry>, +query: U32, found: Bool) -> Bool:
  match es found:
    case Nil{} f: f
    case e <> tail True{}: True{}
    case e <> tail False{}: has(tail, query, entry_is(e, query))

def score(m: Maybe<&2, String>) -> Nat:
  match m:
    case Some{s}: String.length(s)
    case None{}: 1n

def finds(k: Nat, +es: List<&2, Entry>, acc: Nat) -> Nat:
  match k:
    case 0n: acc
    case 1n+p:
      finds(p, es, Nat.add(acc, score(find(es, 4000000000, None{}))))

def hass(k: Nat, +es: List<&2, Entry>, acc: Nat) -> Nat:
  match k:
    case 0n: acc
    case 1n+p:
      hass(p, es, Nat.add(acc,
        Bool.pick(Nat, has(es, 4000000000, False{}), 2n, 1n)))

def nat_of(s: String) -> Nat:
  Maybe.default(&2, Nat, Nat.read(s), 0n)

def nums(args: List<String>) -> (Nat & Nat):
  match args:
    case _ <> (n <> (k <> _)): (nat_of(n), nat_of(k))
    case _: (0n, 0n)

def timed(+n: Nat, +k: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +es : List<&2, Entry> = entries(n, 0)
    +t0 : Nat <- IO.now()
    a : Nat = hass(k, es, 0n)
    +t1 : Nat <- IO.now()
    b : Nat = finds(k, es, 0n)
    +t2 : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(String.concat(["has: ", Nat.show(Nat.sub(t1, t0)), " ms, find: ",
      Nat.show(Nat.sub(t2, t1)), " ms (", Nat.show(Nat.add(a, b)), ")"]))

def run(nk: (Nat & Nat)) -> IO(Unit):
  match nk:
    case (+n, +k): timed(n, k)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    args : List<String> <- IO.args()
    run(nums(args))
```

</details>

## Benches

Measured on the previous base, main at 234cb9b9. The rebase left the five commits' diffs unchanged but for the one resolved comment. Apple M3 Max, `--gpu off`. Each binary runs once to warm up, then the builds alternate for 3 rounds (SEQ, `--threads 1`) or 5 rounds (PAR, `--threads 16`). The tables show the minimum, and each ratio is to main (lower is faster). "PR, aligned" compares main and this branch with both built with `-falign-functions=64`. That column takes function layout out of the comparison, since layout alone moves some of these benches by a few percent. The PR binaries are built from commit 4; commit 5 changes only comments in the C.

### SEQ

| bench | main (s) | PR | PR, aligned |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

title: fix(audio): use monotonic time for the JS queue
body:
## Problem and fix

The silent JS Audio ring measures elapsed time with `Date.now()`. A one-second wall-clock rollback at 48 kHz makes an empty write report 48,000 queued frames, exceeding the 4,096-frame ring and causing later writes to be dropped. A forward jump can drain queued frames prematurely.

Use `performance.now()` for the existing open/write timestamps, matching JS `IO.now` and `IO.sleep`. The queue calculation needs no other change.

## Blast radius

Two production-line changes in `bend2/effs/audio_open.js` and `audio_write.js`, plus one regression in `tests/io/audio_monotonic_clock.bend` with its JS foreign twin. This affects the source IO runner and generated JS's silent Audio model. Native Audio, sample-rate validation, ring capacity, sample policy and public API remain unchanged; no API migration is required.

## Regression evidence

The fixture simulates a one-second rollback, opens Audio at 48 kHz and writes no samples. It prints `48000` on main, failing its expected `#|0`, and `0` with the fix through the actual CLI and generated JS under Bun and Node. It restores `Date.now` immediately after the write. A following module in the same `--checkup` process verifies the original function identity is restored on both paths.

## Checks

- Repository gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`, using CI-pinned ttok 0.3.
- New regression and existing Audio open/write/close reachability fixtures pass through the CLI and generated Bun/Node JS.
- Deterministic Audio controls pass those three lanes: wall-clock jumps, monotonic draining, rate bounds, refill and full-ring dropped writes.
- Existing `IO.now` control passes through the CLI and generated Bun JS.
- Baseline-sensitive regression, shared-process clock restoration and staged whitespace checks pass.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11 and Node 26.8.2. The adjacent `IO.now` control's generated Node run fails to load `bun:ffi`; main emits byte-identical JS and fails the same way. The Audio regression and controls pass under Node.

Browser execution, native audio-device playback, full cluster gates and GPU execution were not run. The tests simulate clock readings; they do not change the machine clock or play audio.

title: wasm32/Emscripten CPU-only build mode for generated C?
body:
Hi! I'm trying to run Bend 2 programs as WebAssembly in a browser (CPU only, one worker; rendering stays in the JS host). Before patching anything downstream I'd like to know whether this is in scope and which shape you would accept.

**Setup**: Bend v2.0.35 (79df8d9), Bun 1.4.2, Emscripten 6.0.10, macOS. Programs: a hello world (from `demos/io_hello_world`) and a pure `Nat` sum (shaped after `demos/pure_par_sum`, without `!`).

```sh
bend hello.bend -o hello.c
emcc -std=c11 -O2 -mtail-call hello.c -o hello.js                       # wasm32
emcc -std=c11 -O2 -m64 -mtail-call -sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH \
     -sMAXIMUM_MEMORY=16GB hello.c -o hello.js                          # wasm64
node hello.js
```

**What happens** (unmodified generated C, build flags only):

- Everything compiles and links for wasm32 and wasm64; `-mtail-call` takes care of `musttail`.
- wasm32: the default corpus size `1ull << 33` (comp.ts ~5231) is truncated to a 32-bit `size_t`, so `mmap` gets 0 bytes; hello then traps with `memory access out of bounds`, the sum program fails with `bend: reservation failed`.
- wasm64: `corpus_map` (comp.ts ~5175) always passes an address hint (`1 << 45`, halving); Emscripten's `mmap` returns `EINVAL` for any non-null address, so both programs fail with `bend: reservation failed`. `mmap(NULL, …)` of the same size works.
- From reading the runtime (not reached at run time): the 2 GiB per-thread stack with an `mprotect` guard page and `SIGSEGV` overflow detection, the pthread pool, the `poll`-based IO loop and sockets have no browser equivalent; `runtime_c` has guards for `__APPLE__` and `__linux__` only.

**Questions**

1. Is a wasm/Emscripten CPU-only target in scope for Bend at all?
2. Preferred guard: `#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__` in the emitted runtime, or a Bend flag (e.g. `--target wasm32`)?
3. Would you accept a single-thread mode (no pthread pool) for that target?
4. A heap-size knob (CLI flag or `-D`), with `mmap(NULL, …)` and no in-place growth on that target?
5. A JS-only effect seam, so effects there need no `.c` twin?

I'm happy to send a patch and tests for whatever shape you prefer. Which upstream change would make a downstream patch unnecessary?

title: `tests/io/process_run.bend` fails two cases on the JS lane (Bun 1.4.2, v2.0.35)
body:
On v2.0.35 (79df8d9), macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Bun 1.4.2, the native build of `tests/io/process_run.bend` prints every expected `#|` line, but the JS lane prints `unexpected failure` for the two cases where a descendant keeps the pipe open:

```sh
bend tests/io/process_run.bend -o p && ./p                     # all True
bend tests/io/process_run.bend -o p.js && BUN_JSC_maxPerThreadStackUsage=33554432 bun p.js
```

```diff
-inherited pipe: True
-descendant output: True
+inherited pipe: unexpected failure
+descendant output: unexpected failure
```

The cases are `Process.run("/bin/sh", ["-c", "sleep 3 & echo hi"], "", 128, 1500)` and `Process.run("/bin/sh", ["-c", "yes & echo hi"], "", 1048576, 1500)`. Every other line matches native. It reproduced in all three runs I made.

This looks like the JS-side counterpart of #1051 (fixed for C by #1054): the run should end at the child's exit even when a grandchild holds the pipes. Possibly related to #1468.

Found by a differential harness that runs Bend's own tests native vs JS lane; 51 other programs match byte for byte.

title: comp.ts: a fact stales only the units that read it absent
body:
The compile-speed half of #1601, rebased on main f3115277. Seven commits, `comp.ts` only.

`compile_book` emitted every def again until a pass added no fact. Now a read of an absent fact registers its unit in `FL.when`, and adding that fact marks only those units stale (`FL.stale`). `c_units` sweeps stale units forward, which finds the callees, then backward, which lets a fact climb a call chain at once, until none remain.

A def becomes a unit only once something names it: `unit_need(k)` makes it, called by `emit_jump`, by a foreign def's closure and by `js_call`. JS does the same: `main` (or a module's exports) is a unit at once and `js_call` makes the rest, so a def nothing reaches cannot fail one backend's build but not the other's. The roots are `main`, bangs and fids, so unreachable defs are never emitted. The own pass walks the own facts some unit read, not every def, so a def with no unit yet keeps its borrowed parameters.

Compared with the earlier versions of this PR, `unit_order`, `unit_lazy`, `FL.miss` and `FL.lazy` are gone, and `emit_native` and `seg_ref` are main's. One loop sweeps the stale units and, when none is left, runs the own pass. `done_defs` had one caller left and is inlined there.

**Compile time** (C emit, median of 7 on an M4 Max under load)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| boss_3d | 589 ms | 334 ms |
| hvm5_mini | 229 ms | 160 ms |
| 3,200-def chain, an own fact climbing it | 311 ms | 389 ms |

C and JS emit over all 1,378 tests, demos and benches took 24.4 s on main and 21.3 s here, in one concurrent run. The chain scales linearly: 108 ms, 344 ms and 1,240 ms for 800, 3,200 and 12,800 defs. It takes 2 rounds, and no program in the corpus takes more than 2.

**Output** (all 1,944 `.bend` files in tests, demos and bench, against main d18110b6)

C differs from main on 923 of the 938 programs that emit C. Exit status and diagnostics are identical everywhere. After normalizing order (FID numbers, segment, spin and declaration order) and following static-image and table references to their contents:

| What differs | Programs |
|---|---:|
| FID numbering and segment order only | 340 |
| + static-image strings only unreachable defs used (offsets shift) | 214 |
| + tables only unreachable defs used, spin declarations reordered | 344 |
| identical as line sets (a block boundary moves) | 19 |
| two defs with the same sanitized name swap FIDs (`js_def_names`, `ids_unique`) | 2 |
| fewer hot constructors, so fewer `rfc_seal`s (`check_kind_terms`, `grade_accept_fill`, `parse_def_typed`) | 3 |
| `Xs.k`'s `+all` becomes owned (`reg/spin_lent_sink`) | 1 |

The last two rows lose facts that only unreachable code contributed. In `spin_lent_sink`, main folds `other(3n, …)` to a constant, so `other` gets no unit and stops lending `ys` to `Xs.k`; `Xs.k` now sinks `all` itself and `go2` no longer needs to, so that half of the test no longer exercises the lent path.

JS differs from main on 966 programs: 807 only drop top-level functions (and 10 `$$` entries) that nothing calls, 157 only reorder them, and the same two name swaps as in C. No reached function changes.

Run on this Mac (M5 Max) on main and this branch, natively and under bun, each against its `#|` lines: 840/980 C and 892/1,032 JS CPU tests pass on both, with byte-identical output for every failing run (242 have a main that cannot be printed, the rest expect a nonzero exit or a window, which the gate handles). 43/45 GPU tests pass on both (the other two cannot print main). All 17 benches and the 8 runnable demos print the same output on both.

**After the rebase on f3115277 and the simplification:** against the rebased PR before it, JS is byte-identical on all programs, and C differs on 22 of them: 20 only in unit order (a foreign def's unit is made before its arguments are emitted), and 2 only in which of two defs with the same sanitized name gets the `_1` suffix. `gates/test.ts` passes 1,854 / 1,854. `gates/repo.ts` is 55 / 56: `comp.ts` is 66,061 ttok, 61 over the 66,000 cap (main is 65,962). Perf was not re-run. The compile times and the comparison with main above are from before this rebase.

title: bend_dev on CUDA declares vote[3] with 0 dynamic shared memory, so SMs keep their L1 cache
body:
Today on main (since 5d6004a2), gpu_kernel passes TG_HOLD * 8 (18,432 bytes) as the per-group shared-memory reservation on both Metal (setThreadgroupMemoryLength:TG_HOLD * 8 atIndex:0) and CUDA (cuLaunchKernel sharedMemBytes), while bend_dev on CUDA declares extern __shared__ u32 vote[] and only uses three u32 words in vote (vote[0] as the round-robin cursor in monk_step, task_deal, and ring_pick; vote[1] for grew; vote[2] for has; 12 bytes total). On Apple GPUs, threadgroup memory is a dedicated 32 KB block separate from the L1 data cache, so reserving 18 KB on Metal caps residency at one group per core without touching L1. On NVIDIA GPUs, shared memory and the L1 data cache share one 128 KB physical pool per streaming multiprocessor (SM), and default shared memory is 48 KB per block, so passing TG_HOLD * 8 to cuLaunchKernel neither caps residency at one block per SM (floor(48 KB / 18 KB) = 2; and under l2 >> 16, CUBE_G is already at or below the SM count on RTX 3090 at 64 <= 82, RTX 4090 at 128 <= 128, and H100 at 128 <= 132) nor leaves the L1 data cache intact: each SM carves 32 KB (at 1 block/SM) or 64 KB (at 2 blocks/SM) out of its 128 KB L1 cache for unused dynamic shared memory.

[NVIDIA Nsight Compute (ncu)](https://developer.nvidia.com/nsight-compute) on editdist (depth 12, RTX 3090, CUDA 13.1) measures main's 18,432-byte dynamic reservation (d2aeefc1) against declaring vote[3] statically with 0 bytes of dynamic shared memory (higher L1 hit rate and lower off-chip memory traffic and kernel time are better):

| Configuration | Dynamic sharedMemBytes | L1 data cache hit rate | Off-chip device memory read + write | Kernel time (sum of passes) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Today on main (d2aeefc1): extern __shared__ u32 vote[] | 18,432 B | 6.32% | 315.55 GB | 1,039.8 ms |
| This PR: __shared__ u32 vote[3] | 0 B | 84.14% | 128.65 GB | 688.8 ms |

This PR changes CUDA's bend_dev (#else) from extern __shared__ u32 vote[] to __shared__ u32 vote[3] and changes CUDA's gpu_kernel (#elif BEND_CUDA) to pass 0 instead of TG_HOLD * 8 for sharedMemBytes in cuLaunchKernel. TG_HOLD and Metal's setThreadgroupMemoryLength:TG_HOLD * 8 atIndex:0 stay untouched, as do host C and JS paths. comp.ts goes down by 2 ttok (+2 -2 lines): 63,495 -> 63,493 on d2aeefc1, or 64,092 -> 64,090 on current main (234cb9b9, where #1588 + #1591 pushed main over the 64,000 cap, so repo-gate is red from main until main drops below 64,000).

Measured with [bend-bench](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench) `gpu fast` ([8c09ff37](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/tree/8c09ff37)) on an RTX 3090 (CUDA 13.1, 4 GB heap, 3 measured runs per workload after a correctness check and warmup), d2aeefc1 against this PR; lower ms and speedup above 1x mean this PR is faster:

| Workload | d2aeefc1 (ms) | This PR (ms) | Speedup (base / PR) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Edit distance | 1,101.23 | 760.34 | 1.448x | -31.0% |
| Procedural terrain | 733.06 | 544.11 | 1.347x | -25.8% |
| Block matrix multiply | 943.01 | 786.67 | 1.199x | -16.6% |
| Symbolic regression | 527.54 | 446.02 | 1.183x | -15.5% |
| N-Queens | 1,257.56 | 1,114.52 | 1.128x | -11.4% |
| Tree breadth-first search | 1,001.19 | 905.73 | 1.105x | -9.5% |
| Alpha-beta tree search | 406.40 | 387.60 | 1.049x | -4.6% |
| Bitonic sort | 1,008.39 | 962.00 | 1.048x | -4.6% |
| Ray tracing | 1,119.89 | 1,070.37 | 1.046x | -4.4% |
| Geomean over all 21 workloads | - | - | 1.071x | -6.6% total time |

Of the remaining 12 completed workloads, 8 are 1% to 3% faster (tree-radix 1.028x, bfs-shared 1.027x, gameoflife 1.026x, hashmap 1.019x, merkle 1.019x, lexer 1.017x, mandelbrot 1.013x, summation 1.011x) and 4 are within run-to-run noise (nbody 1.008x, pricing 0.998x, kmeans 0.997x, and Rodinia HotSpot: 6,162 -> 6,580 ms in the single-sweep run, then 6,351 -> 6,228 ms, -1.9%, p = 0.62 across 6 interleaved AB/BA pairs, dominated by ~2.2 s of host ASCII file I/O, which I plan to work on in the next version of bend-bench). Compact UTS hits the existing ERR_DEEP overflow on both.

title: fix(cli): preserve command status when update checks fail
body:
## Problem and fix

A fresh, parseable update cache with a non-string `ver`, or a newer version with a non-string `notice`, can throw after the command finishes. A program may print its correct result but exit 1; an explicit exit 7 also becomes 1.

Catch rejection from the optional daily check at its sole CLI callsite. This preserves the documented rule that the check never fails the command, without adding cache-validation or repair machinery.

## Blast radius

Two files: one production line in `bend2/main.ts`, and eight regression lines in the existing `gates/ping.ts` daily-check cases. The tests reuse its private cache and helpers; existing cleanup resets the cache afterward.

Valid notices, refresh behavior, telemetry opt-out and command failures retain their behavior. No public API or cache-format change.

## Regression evidence

The two fresh-cache cases cover null version and null notice. Both exact assertions fail against the original compiled CLI, which prints help then exits 1 with a TypeError, and pass against the corrected binary with identical help, exit 0 and empty stderr.

Source and compiled CLI controls also cover valid current/newer/stale-offline caches. Independent source checks verify preserved checker failures, exit 7, notice sanitation/truncation and no HTTP requests for fresh caches.

## Checks

- Source and freshly compiled CLI probes, including the exact added regression assertions, pass their baseline/branch expectations.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Scoped TypeScript checking reports seven byte-identical existing diagnostics in `bend.ts` and `safe.ts`; no new diagnostics. This is not a clean typecheck.
- Repository gate: 53/54. Its sole failure is unchanged `comp.ts` at 64,092/64,000 ttok, also present on [main's #1600 check](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38916753417/job/117026066036). This PR leaves `comp.ts` untouched.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64 and Bun 1.3.11. Full ping skips because the sibling site repository is unavailable; replaying its added assertions does not validate the full installer/release flow. Linux/WSL, Windows and cluster checks were not run. The inherited compiler-cap failure prevents a green repository gate.

Malformed cache data remains on disk until normal refresh; this change preserves the command result rather than repairing that data.

title: Foreign effect ID scanning uses the wrong line-continuation rules
fix(lint): show help before loading the compiler
body:
## Problem and fix

`bend-lint --help` and `-h` currently load and self-check Bend before printing usage. An unavailable or drifted compiler therefore makes help exit 2 without showing usage.

Retain the parsed startup options and route help through the existing `cli()` handler before `load()`. This reuses its strict argument validation and usage text; ordinary commands and library imports still load and check Bend as before.

## Blast radius

Two tool-owned files: six added/two removed source lines in `tools/bend-lint/src/lint.ts`, plus one regression in `src/lint.test.ts`. Tests remain in the tool's suite, following the [#1389 guidance](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1389#issuecomment-6062222047).

No public rule/API change. Normal linting, compiler selection and drift checks retain their behavior. Help-related argument errors still exit 2, now before compiler initialization.

## Regression evidence

The added subprocess test supplies a nonexistent compiler, covers both help spellings and explicit `--bend`, and checks exit 0, usage stdout and empty stderr. It fails against unchanged baseline source with exit 2/no usage, and passes on this branch. An unknown-option control prevents help from bypassing strict parsing.

Additional CLI controls preserve help-looking option values, real `--` delimiters, explicit compiler priority, ordinary linting, drift failures and library imports.

## Checks

- Complete bend-lint suite: 128 passed, 0 failed, 845 assertions.
- Baseline-sensitive regression and focused CLI controls pass their expected before/after assertions.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Tool typecheck reports the same two existing protected `bend.ts` errors at lines 2040 and 3771; diagnostics are byte-identical to baseline. This is not a clean typecheck.
- Repository gate: 53/54, solely unchanged `comp.ts` at 64,092/64,000 ttok, also present on [main's #1600 check](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38916753417/job/117026066036). This PR leaves compiler source and caps untouched.

## Validation limits
