title: fix(effects): respect C and JS line continuations
body:
Fixes #1604.

A backslash at the end of a JS comment hid the next line from ID expansion. C had the reverse problem with CRLF continuations. Splicing C lines before scanning fixes both, including a `CID` token split across physical C lines.

The regression returns a real `Some{42}` from each foreign backend. It fails before the patch (unexpanded JS `CID`; undeclared C `CID`/`Some`) and prints `42` after it. I also ran the existing comment regression on Bun and native C, and the CRLF C reproducer as a native binary. Repository gate: **54/54** on this branch.

I left this draft because main is already over its permanent compiler cap: `234cb9b` has 64,092 ttok. This branch is based on `7e120d5` and adds 18 tokens (63,618 → 63,636); no cap changes or comment trimming. It needs rebasing once main has room.

Linux x86-64, Bun 1.4.3, clang 22.1.8. I have not run the mini-cluster/Metal/CUDA gates. AI-assisted patch.

title: F32.lerp overflows between finite endpoints and loses endpoint values
body:
`F32.lerp(3.0e38, F32.neg(3.0e38), 0.5)` returns `-inf`, although both endpoints are finite and the midpoint is zero. The subtraction `b - a` overflows before multiplication by `t`.

There are two related endpoint failures: `F32.lerp(1.0e20, 1.0, 1.0)` returns `0` instead of `1`, and interpolating from `-0` at `t = 0` loses the sign bit.

Reproducer:
```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(F32.show(F32.lerp(3.0e38, F32.neg(3.0e38), 0.5)))
```

I reproduced this on `7e120d5`; the implementation is unchanged on current main `234cb9b`. A fix uses the weighted sum for opposite signs and returns endpoints directly at `t = 0` and `t = 1`, without changing the public function type. The boundary regression and existing number kit pass on Bun and native C after the patch. AI-assisted investigation and fix.

title: fix(base): keep lerp finite and preserve endpoints
body:
Fixes #1607.

`a + (b - a) * t` overflows when finite endpoints of opposite signs are far apart (`F32.lerp(3.0e38, -3.0e38, 0.5)` gave `-inf`), and it is not exact at `t = 1` (`F32.lerp(1.0e20, 1.0, 1.0)` gave `0`). `F32.lerp` is now the weighted sum `a*(1-t) + b*t`. It is exact at both endpoints, it does not overflow between finite endpoints of opposite signs, and it has no branches. The public type stays the same.

The trade-offs match GLSL `mix`: `lerp(x, x, t)` can be 1 ulp off `x`, it is not strictly monotonic in `t`, and `-0` at `t = 0` becomes `+0` (as on main).

Speed: 50M calls where each lerp feeds the next (hashed signs), Apple M4, median of 7 (C) / 5 (Bun) runs:

| | main | branchy fix (152bbf7) | weighted sum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C | 97 ms | 259 ms | 76 ms |
| Bun | 388 ms | 336 ms | 287 ms |

`tests/base/f32_lerp_boundaries.bend` checks the overflow midpoint, both endpoints, an exact large quarter-point and a same-sign value. `num_kit` output is unchanged. Gates on main e5527d5b: repo 54/54, test 1649/1649, perf 124/124, ping 62/62, safe 1071 agree / 0 false reject.

title: F32.from_nat wraps values at 2^32
body:
`F32.from_nat` narrows through `U32.from_nat`, so it silently wraps at 2^32 even though these values fit the supported Nat range.

```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(F32.show(F32.from_nat(Nat.double(2147483648n))))
```

On `7e120d5` this prints `0`. The input is 4294967296, an exactly representable F32; it should not become zero. The literal is built with `Nat.double` because Nat literals themselves stop at U32_MAX. Current main has the same definition.

The fix removes the narrowing conversion, with a direct Nat-to-F32 intrinsic on compiled lanes. I checked the 2^32 boundary, rounding just above half an ulp, a tie to even, and the maximum supported Nat on Bun and native C; the existing number kit still passes. AI-assisted investigation and fix.

title: fix(base): convert Nat to F32 without narrowing to U32
body:
Fixes #1609.

`F32.from_nat` keeps the full Nat instead of narrowing through U32. It is a law with a direct intrinsic, like `U32.to_f32`; no host-only `F32.read` or NaN fallback.

Merged main `aee1b1f`. The cap blocker is gone: `comp.ts` is **65,989 / 66,000** tokens and repo-gate passes **54/54**. The four cast rules share the existing `tpl_ops`; no caps changed or code moved out.

All five cases, both ordinary and inside `!`, pass on native CPU, Bun and Node. Four existing U32/Nat/float control programs also match their expected output on the interpreter, native CPU and compiled JS on both hosts. Native runs use the new `+RTS` option brackets.

I have not run Metal, CUDA or the private mini-cluster suite.

title: F32.round loses the sign of negative zero
body:
`F32.round` turns negative zero into positive zero. It does the same when a negative fraction rounds to zero, including the negative half under the existing ties-toward-positive-infinity rule.

```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(U32.show(F32.bits(F32.round(F32.neg(0.0)))))
    IO.print(F32.show(F32.div(1.0, F32.round(F32.neg(0.1)))))
```

On `7e120d5`, this prints `0` and `inf`; preserving the sign would give `2147483648` and `-inf`. Current main has the same definition. The sign is observable through both the public bit conversion and ordinary arithmetic.

I kept the existing tie rule and restored the input sign only when the rounded result is zero. Negative zero, negative fractions, the half boundary and the number kit now pass on Bun and native C. AI-assisted investigation and fix.

title: JS String.length allocates an array proportional to the whole string
body:
The JS `String.length` intrinsic expands the whole string with `[...str_out(s)]` just to count its characters. That adds O(n) temporary storage, including a second representation of every supplementary Unicode character.

I compiled this real Bend consumer on `7e120d5`:
```python
import Base

def payload() -> IO(String):
  import "./payload.js"

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    s : String <- payload()
    IO.print(Nat.show(String.length(s)))
```

```js
function payload() { return "😀".repeat(2000000); }
io_eff(CID(payload), payload);
```

It correctly prints `2000000`, but three fresh Bun processes peak at 170988, 171744 and 170592 KiB RSS (`/usr/bin/time -f %M bun program.js`). The payload itself is four million UTF-16 code units; counting it should not require a two-million-element array. Current main keeps the same intrinsic.

The existing internal Char-width decoder can walk the string with an offset and a counter, preserving arbitrary U32 Chars as well as Unicode scalars without text-edge conversion. I am checking that change against the existing Char/string regressions and the same payload. AI-assisted investigation.

title: fix(base): preserve negative zero in F32.round
body:
Fixes #1611.

When rounding produces zero, this restores the input sign instead of returning the positive zero created by the final addition. Other results and the existing ties-toward-positive-infinity rule stay unchanged.

The regression covers `-0`, a negative fraction through its reciprocal, the negative half, and the adjacent value that must still round to `-1`. Before: `0, False, 0, True`. After: `2147483648, True, 2147483648, True` on both Bun and native C. The existing number kit also passes on both.

Linux x86-64, Bun 1.4.3, clang 22.1.8. Current main has an unrelated compiler token-cap failure; this changes only Base and its regression, not the compiler or caps. The mini-cluster/Metal/CUDA gates were not run here. AI-assisted patch.

title: perf(js): count String characters without materializing an array
body:
Fixes #1612.

Counting a String no longer expands it into a character array or converts its non-scalar Chars at a text edge. The loop walks the existing internal Char widths; the head/tail decoder now accepts an offset, and both existing call sites pass zero. Extra counting storage changes from O(n) to O(1).

I compiled the same Bend program returning two million emoji, then measured three fresh Bun processes per build with `/usr/bin/time -f %M`. Every run printed `2000000`. These are whole-process peak RSS medians, not an allocation-profiler estimate:

| build | median peak RSS (KiB) |
| --- | ---: |
| before | 170988 |
| after | 56092 |

The mixed ASCII/astral/arbitrary-U32 regression, `string_kit`, `char_any_code` and `string_unicode` all pass on Bun and native C. Repo gate: **54/54**.

Based on `7e120d5`; compiler size is 63,618 → 63,696 (+78). I left this draft alongside #1606/#1610 while main remains at 64,092 against the permanent 64,000 cap. No cap changes, comment trimming or new dependencies.

Linux x86-64, Bun 1.4.3, clang 22.1.8; the mini-cluster/Metal/CUDA gates were not run here. AI-assisted patch.

title: fix(c): write a shared word back to the fork frame slot that holds it
body:
Split out of #1596, as asked in its review.

## What changes

In sequence, a fork's middle steps read the words they hold from the frame without popping it (`STK(-k)`). When such a step shares one of them, `term_keep` may wrap a raw root in a redirect and return a new word, but the frame slot kept the old one. The step that pops the frame then read the raw word, and the join's sink freed the cell the redirect still pointed at.

In `Push` below, `Xs.cnt` borrows the list and `Xs.push` stores it. At `--threads 1` the freed cell loops the free list and the program hangs on main:

```python
def Push(+xs: Xs) -> U32:
  a b = Xs.cnt(xs, 0) Xs.push(xs)
  (a + Xs.cnt(b, 0) : U32)
```

`bind_pop` now writes the kept word back to the slot it came from:

```c
STK(-1) = _xs_1 = term_keep(e, _xs_1, 1);
```

## Witness

`tests/reg/brw_fork_push.bend`. The gate runs each binary at the default thread count, where a direct `Push(Xs.build(100n, 1))` takes the parallel path and passes. So the test runs `Push` at the leaves of a depth-12 fork tree, and the leaves run in sequence at any thread count. On main it hangs at `--threads 1`, `2`, `8`, `128` and the default. On this branch it prints 823296 at all of them, as do the JS lane and the interpreter.

## Checks

- A/B against main over the 809 programs that build to C and JS (tests, benches, demos). The code changes in 4 programs and no bench:
  - `brw_fork_push` gains 1 write-back;
  - `brw_fork_cross` gains 1;
  - `compile/family_two_indices` gains 3, for the quadrants that `Mat.sq` shares, whose second use read the stale raw word;
  - the `app_slash_boss_3d` demo gains 10, in `Cloth.mesh` and `Scene.build`.

  Otherwise, C and JS output lose only the cut runtime comments listed below.
- `brw_fork_cross` prints 199 and `family_two_indices` 64 and 512, as on main. `SLASH_PROBE=600` on the slash demo prints the same game state as main at `--threads 1` and `16`. Only the audio queue and voice counts and the frame timings differ, and those vary between runs of either build.
- `gates/test.ts`, run locally: PASS 1638 / 1640. The two failures, `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, expect "no display" and fail the same way on main here, because this Mac has a desktop session.
- `tsc -p bend2/pack/tsconfig.json` (TypeScript 5.9.3): the same 11 errors as main, none in `comp.ts`.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- The A/B, the program runs and the test gate above were done before the last five comment cuts (`ring_rewind`, `io_park_add`, the Heap and Blk comments, `show_main`). Against that build, this branch changes only comment lines: in the C of all 809 programs, and in no JS.

## comp.ts tokens

Main is at 64,092 / 64,000 by itself, so the repo gate currently fails on every open PR. This PR brings `comp.ts` to **63,990**. To fit, these comments are cut, each one a twin or a restatement of code:

- **C runtime:**
  - the twin of the JS `io_list` comment, "Bytes cross as they are…" (the JS one says it in full);
  - `io_park_add`'s double-link note (`io_park_cut`);
  - `ring_rewind`'s comment (its body);
  - the Heap comment's bump sentence (the sentence before it lists the misses in order);
  - the Blk comment's `blk_node` and `blk_copy` mappings (their call sites).
- **JS runtime:** the `show_val` comment (the C twin says it in full).
- **Emitter:**
  - `seg_new`'s comment. It restated `seg_take` and the runtime's Segments comment, and said a segment pops its frame, which a fork's middle steps do not.
  - `show_main`'s last sentence (the `refuse` error and the `io_type` check below it).

#1596, rebuilt on main, makes a disjoint set of cuts. The two merge cleanly, and with both merged `comp.ts` is 63,886.

title: Since #1548, List.all/any/find/contains of `h <> t` stay stuck when `h` decides the result, so a lemma over an erased tail has no proof
body:
Since #1548 (32d23b43), `List.all(~a, ~A, ~f, h <> t)` unfolds to `List.all.go(~a, ~A, ~f, t, f(h))`, and `.go` matches the list before the flag. When `f(h)` is `False{}` the result is known, but the term stays stuck until `t` is a constructor. If `t` is erased, that never happens: an erased binder can't be matched (`a live scrutinee (a - scrutinee matches only in a dead region)`), and `{==}` doesn't apply. So a statement whose list tail is erased no longer has a proof. `List.any`, `List.find` and `List.contains` do the same when the head decides the result.

### What you did

`bend head_fails.bend --check-only`

### The file

```python
import Base

def head_fails(-t: List<Nat>) -> {List.all(~&1, ~Nat, ~(n => Nat.is_le(n, 3n)), 5n <> t) == False{} : Bool}:
  {==}

def main() -> Bool:
  List.all(~&1, ~Nat, ~(n => Nat.is_le(n, 3n)), [5n, 1n])
```

### What happened

At 234cb9b:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : List.all.go(&1, Nat, n => Cmp.is_le(Nat.cmp(n, 3n)), t, False{})
- observed : False{}
Context:
- t : List<&1, Nat>
Location: head_fails
3 | def head_fails(-t: List<Nat>) -> {List.all(~&1, ~Nat, ~(n => Nat.is_le(n, 3n)), 5n <> t) == False{} : Bool}:
4>|   {==}
  |   ^^^^
5 |
```

On v2.0.37 the same file prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. These fail the same way at 234cb9b and pass on v2.0.37, each proved by `{==}` with `-t` erased:

- `{List.any(~&1, ~Nat, ~(n => Nat.is_le(n, 3n)), 1n <> t) == True{} : Bool}`, `t : List<Nat>`
- `{List.find(~Nat, ~(n => Nat.is_le(n, 3n)), 1n <> t) == Some{1n} : Maybe<&2, Nat>}`, `t : List<&2, Nat>`
- `{List.contains(~Nat, ~Nat.is_eq, 3n <> t, 3n) == True{} : Bool}`, `t : List<&2, Nat>`

### Where it bites

bend-mathlib 0.7.3.0 on BendHub has an append-only API. At 234cb9b, 23 definitions in its `list.bend` (proofs and their helpers) stop checking. I stubbed each failing one in turn, so later failures show too:

- 14 check again through small lemmas about the `.go` loops, proved by a case split on the flag or an induction that carries it.
- 7 have no proof, because the statement erases the tail where the search stops: `all_append`, `any_append`, `contains_append` (`-ys`); `mem_cons_self`, `mem_cons_of_mem` (`-xs`); `sorted_cons_cons_elim_le`, `sorted_cons_cons_elim_tail` (`-t`, where `sorted_by` is `List.all` over `List.zip(x <> y <> t, y <> t)`).
- 2, the accumulator helpers behind `all_reverse` and `any_reverse` over `A: Kind(a)`, I couldn't prove: every invariant I tried needs the reversed prefix or the accumulator twice after a false head, and the elements are affine.

### What I tried

A loop that reads the flag before the list would keep the early stop and the tail call, and would reduce `go(t, False{})` for any `t`. I couldn't write one:

- As a user def, it fails the decreasing-call check: the flag changes before the list shrinks.
- In a scratch `base.bend`, the `String.starts_with.if` shape (a helper that calls a `law` filled below it, #793) fails the same check at `List.all.if~0` for these template defs, with the flag before or after the list.

So this is a report, not a patch.

### bend --version

bend 2.0.37, and main at 234cb9b

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

Ubuntu clang version 21.1.8 (6ubuntu1)

title: Emission allocates 40% less on large files: per-file literal steps, per-def probes, no memo closures (#1262)
body:
> 🤖 Written by an AI agent for @nicolas-abril; not yet reviewed by a human.

Part of #1262. This lowers how much `compile_book` allocates while it emits a large file. It doesn't fix the root cause: emission still re-runs the whole file about 8 times while facts settle (#1386).

Measured on Chromi's `examples/eco/main.bend`. On main that file fails with `duplicate declaration of Text`, so I renamed its `Text{` to `AText{` for the measurement. The emitted C is byte-identical to main's.

| | main 234cb9b9 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| allocated during emit (V8 sampling) | 29.2 GiB | 17.4 GiB |
| `bun main.ts` wall time, 3 runs | 10.3–11.0 s | 8.0–8.2 s |
| max RSS, 3 runs | 3.5–5.4 GB | 4.2–4.8 GB |

RSS depends on when Bun's GC happens to run, and it is too noisy to call a win or a loss.

**Changes** (`comp.ts` only, +58/−47):
- `term_force` memoizes literal steps per file, keyed by `k + v`. Before, they were memoized per def and keyed by the term object, so the same literal got stepped again in every def and in every pass (29.2 → 23.1 GiB).
- `compile_book` resets `PROBES` before each def. Before, it only reset in `file_new`, so it grew from about 131k to 1M entries across the passes. Now it stays at about 430 (23.1 → 22.4 GiB). **This is the part to review closely.** It's only safe if no probe from an earlier def is still alive in a cache that outlives `memo_gc()`. The new `steps` and `opens` maps hold only probe-free results. `teles` predates this PR and isn't cleared per def.
- `lay_at` memoizes its open-type check (`ty_holds(A, Var|App)`) per file, keyed by `term_key(term_lower(A))` (22.4 → 18.8 GiB).
- `term_uses`, `term_open` and `term_spine` pass named functions to `memo` and no longer allocate a closure on every call. `term_uses` folds with a loop (18.8 → 17.4 GiB).

What's left, from the heap profile: each of the ~8 fixpoint passes allocates about 2.2 GiB (#1386). U32 literal matching (`mat_rows`/`mat_lits`) takes about 1.5 GiB, and `term_higher` about 2.5 GiB.

**Checks** (macOS M-series, at 539c7e69): ping 59/59, test 1639/1639, perf 124/124, repo 53/54. The one repo failure is the token cap: `bend2/comp.ts` is 64187 > 64000 ttok. main is already over it at 64092 (repo-gate is red on main), and this PR adds 95. Not run: Linux, CUDA, Metal, hub corpus. `safe.ts` isn't touched.

title: fix(js): validate TCP.connect arguments before FFI setup
body:
## Problem and fix

Malformed IPv4 addresses and out-of-range ports passed to `TCP.connect` should return `Fail(22, ...)`. Emitted JS instead aborts on Node because it initializes `bun:ffi` before validating those arguments.

Move the existing `io_sys()` declaration below the existing address guard, matching `TCP.listen` and `UDP.bind`. Reuse `io_addr` and `io_fail`; no new fallback or exception handling.

## Blast radius

One statement moves in `bend2/effs/tcp_connect.js`; two JS-specific regression files are added under `tests/io`. The compatibility change is limited to invalid arguments returning the declared failure instead of terminating when FFI is unavailable. Valid Node TCP remains unsupported. Valid Bun networking, descriptor ownership, native C, public signatures and the compiler are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The new foreign twin makes FFI initialization throw once and restores the previous global property descriptor before throwing. The same test fails on main and passes with this fix in source execution and standalone JS under Bun and Node. Both shared `--checkup` orders preserve subsequent networking tests.

Ordinary programs without fault injection reproduce the Node failure for malformed IPv4, an oversized port and a NUL-containing host; each now prints `22`. Bun/native results remain `22` before and after.

## Checks

- Focused regression and valid TCP loopback pass in source and emitted Bun; the regression also passes in emitted Node.
- Present/absent FFI-state restoration and valid-address socket controls pass under Bun and Node. Generated C is byte-identical for four input cases; native behavior matches main.
- Both JS syntax checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- [Repository gate in CI](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/actions/runs/38946717972/job/117185014966): **54/54** on the unchanged PR head, using main's 66,000-token compiler cap from [#1626](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1626). This PR does not change `comp.ts`.

## Validation limits

Local checks ran on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.11 and Node 26.8.2. The full IO suite and mini-cluster/Linux/GPU gates were not run. The regression exercises FFI absence in the Bun lane; it does not add a Node CI lane or support valid Node TCP.

title: `--verdict` mismatch: a function in a type-parameter field (pair, `Some`) is η-expanded on only one side of an equation
body:
### What you did

`bend eta.bend --verdict`

### What happened

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In t:
expected: (keep λx1 => (x0 x1))
observed: (.Tuple, (x0, ((.False, ()), ())))
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.
```

`bend eta.bend --check-only` prints ALL PROOFS CHECK.

### The file

```python
import Base

def keep(v: U32 -> U32) -> (U32 -> U32) & Bool:
  (v, False{})

def t(v: U32 -> U32) -> {keep(v) == (v, False{}) : (U32 -> U32) & Bool}:
  {==}
```

### bend --version

2.0.37 (main at `234cb9b`)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64 (WSL2)

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.4 (bundled with Lean 4.34.0; not used by `--verdict`)

### Diagnosis

In `bend2/safe.ts`, `arg_term` writes a function-typed argument η-long, so `keep(v)` goes out as `(keep λx1 => (x0 x1))`, which reduces to `((λx1 => (x0 x1)), False)`.

The right side `(v, False{})` is a term inside a type, so it reaches the elaborator bare, with no type. `arg_term` gives a bare λ or match its goal `A`, but returns a bare constructor without it (`safe.ts:1339`):

```ts
return term(e, s, T === null && tree ? B.Ann(x, A) : x, live);
```

`ctr_term` then sees `T === null`, so the pair's parameters are unknown (`ps` are placeholders). The field's type is a bare parameter, not a `∀`, so `v` stays `x0`. The kernel converts without η, so the sides cannot meet.

Variations:

* `Some{v}` through a template fails the same way.
* A constructor whose field is *declared* `U32 -> U32` passes, because the field type is known without the parameters.
* `id(v) == v` passes, because the equation's sides are η-long leaves.

Related, but not the same path: #1133 (closed by #1136), where the η-long argument had no annotation. Here both sides are annotated, and only one side is η-long.

It is a false rejection, not a soundness problem. On BendHub it causes the `--verdict` mismatch in `bend-collections-laws-containers@1.0.0.0` (`0x5c489f5d9646d7cc9aa3dd8137e9dc07`), files `proofs/containers/dynamic_array/proof.bend` and `owned_instances.bend`, at `swap_rejected` instantiated at `~(U32 -> U32)`.

### A candidate fix (one line)

Give a bare constructor its goal, as is already done for a bare λ or match:

```diff
-  return term(e, s, T === null && tree ? B.Ann(x, A) : x, live);
+  return term(e, s, T === null && (tree || y.$ === "Ctr") ? B.Ann(x, A) : x, live);
```

Tested locally:

* the file above, plus pair, `Some` and template variants, pass `--verdict`;
* the controls still pass;
* all 1,666 `tests/` and `demos/*/PROOF.bend` files keep their exact verdict class (1,071 agree, 492 bend2-rejects, 99 unsafe, 4 out of scope).

On all of BendHub (4,832 files from 631 packages), comparing per file with and without the fix:

* the two files above move from mismatch to agree;
* no file moves between agree, bend2-rejects, unsafe and out-of-scope;
* the only other moves are timeouts and memory caps under load. The two files that moved *into* a timeout give the same verdict with and without the fix at 180 s.

A PR with this change and a regression test follows.

Found and tested with Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5.5, during an audit of `--verdict`.

title: fix(verdict): a bare constructor in a type goes to the kernel at its goal (#1619)
body:
Fixes #1619.

`--verdict` reported a mismatch for a proof bend2 accepts when a function sits in a field whose type is a parameter (a pair's component, `Some`'s value):

```python
def keep(v: U32 -> U32) -> (U32 -> U32) & Bool:
  (v, False{})

def pair(v: U32 -> U32) -> {keep(v) == (v, False{}) : (U32 -> U32) & Bool}:
  {==}
```

```
In pair:
expected: (keep λx1 => (x0 x1))
observed: (.Tuple, (x0, ((.False, ()), ())))
```

**Cause.**

* `arg_term` sends the call's function-typed argument η-long.
* The equation's `(v, False{})` is a term in a type, so it arrives bare.
* `arg_term` gives a bare λ or match its goal `A`, but not a bare constructor.
* So `ctr_term` gets `T === null`, cannot fill the pair's parameters, and leaves `v` bare.
* The kernel converts without η, so `λx1 => (x0 x1)` never meets `x0`.

**Fix.** Give a bare constructor its goal too:

```diff
-  return term(e, s, T === null && tree ? B.Ann(x, A) : x, live);
+  return term(e, s, T === null && (tree || y.$ === "Ctr") ? B.Ann(x, A) : x, live);
```

**The same cause, two more symptoms.** Sebastian Griego reached the same fix independently (#1621). His two tests show that a bare constructor losing its goal breaks more than η:

* `tests/proof/generic_constructor_erased_lambda.bend`: a lambda in a generic `Box` at `@-x: Type -> Type`. The kernel reported `a λ of its binder's liveness`.
* `tests/proof/generic_constructor_dependent_function.bend`: a field whose type depends on an earlier field. Export reported `an application past its head's known type`, and `--verdict` rejected the file.

They are added here unchanged, with him as co-author.

**Tests.**

* `tests/check/ctr_param_field_eta.bend` covers the pair and a template's `Some{v}`.
* The two tests above.

All three check as before. On `main` (`234cb9b`), `--verdict` rejects each; with the fix, each prints ALL PROOFS CHECK. So `gates/safe.ts tests` fails without the fix.

**What I ran** (Linux x86_64 under WSL2; I can't run the minis):

* `bend2`'s check and `--verdict` on the three tests: rejected on `main`, ALL PROOFS CHECK with the fix.
* `gates/safe_node.ts` locally over all of `tests/` and `demos/*/PROOF.bend`: every file keeps its verdict class (1,071 agree, 492 bend2-rejects, 99 unsafe, 4 out of scope).
* The same over all of BendHub (4,832 files), per file, with and without the fix:
  * `bend-collections-laws-containers@1.0.0.0` `dynamic_array/{proof,owned_instances}.bend` goes from mismatch to agree;
  * no file moves between agree, bend2-rejects, unsafe and out-of-scope;
  * the only other moves are 30 s timeouts and memory under load, and the two that slowed into a timeout give the same verdict with and without the fix at 180 s.

**Not run:** `gates/test.ts` and `gates/perf.ts` (the minis).

**Size.** `safe.ts` is 23,978 ttok on `main` by my local `ttok==0.3`, and 23,986 with this change, under the 24,000 cap. My local count also reads `comp.ts` on unmodified `main` as 64,092, over its cap, so it differs a little from CI's. The repo gate here will say.

Found and tested with Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5.5, during an audit of `--verdict`.

title: Preserve expected types for generic constructor arguments
body:
Generic constructor arguments can pass Bend's source checker but fail
--verdict. During BendTT export, arg_term does not pass their expected type
to ctr_term. Generic fields then use placeholder datatype parameters. This
can assign the wrong quantity to a lambda or leave a call through a bound
function without a known type.

Pass the existing expected type to unannotated constructor arguments through
the annotation path already used for lambdas and matches. ctr_term can then
use the datatype parameters to instantiate each field type. Existing explicit
annotations remain in use.

Add two proof tests:

- generic_constructor_erased_lambda.bend compares Box{x => Type} values at
  Box<@-x: Type -> Type>. The expected field type requires an erased lambda
  binder. Before this change, export gives it a live binder.
- generic_constructor_dependent_function.bend stores a function in a generic
  constructor field. Its result type depends on an earlier field. Before
  this change, export loses the type needed for a call through its argument.

Both tests pass source checking before and after the change. Both fail
--verdict before the change and pass after it with the unchanged BendTT
kernel. The local safety-gate run covers all 1,652 existing upstream files
and retains every baseline classification. This was a local gate run, not
a full CI run. With CI's ttok 0.3, safe.ts uses 23,986 of its 24,000 tokens.

The local repository gate reports one existing failure: bend2/comp.ts uses
64,092 tokens against its 64,000-token limit. The file is unchanged from
main (234cb9b9), where it has the same count. All other repository rules
pass.

title: fix(gates): safe_node can cap each check's memory (MEM_MB), so one heavy file cannot take down a node
body:
Running `safe_node.ts` over BendHub ran out of memory for me. One heavy check (bend2 plus the kernel it starts) can pass 3 GB, and with several checks at once the OOM killer fires. Twice the run died and lost its results; once it took down the machine.

**Change** (`gates/safe_node.ts` only):

* Each check runs in its own process group (`detached: true`).
* With `MEM_MB` set, the runner sums the group's RSS every 0.5 s with `ps -A -o pgid=,rss=`, which works on macOS and Linux. Past `MEM_MB` it kills the group, and the file reports `memory cap: the check passed N MB` as an infrastructure error, like a timeout.
* **With `MEM_MB` unset (the default), nothing is capped** and verdicts are unchanged. Checks still run in their own process groups, and the runner kills every live group on exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP, so no check outlives it (SIGKILL to the runner's process group can't be trapped; see the review thread).
* The 30 s deadline now kills the whole group, so a kernel that bend2 started does not outlive its check.

**What I ran** (Linux x86_64 under WSL2):

* `MEM_MB=300` on a heavy BendHub file (`hairpin.bend`) and a light demo: the heavy one ends as `e` (`memory cap: the check passed 300 MB`) in about 1 s, and the light one still agrees.
* `MEM_MB` unset, all 1,666 `tests/` and `demos/*/PROOF.bend` files: every verdict class matches the unpatched `safe_node.ts` on the same `main`.
* All of BendHub (4,832 files) at a 3 GB cap, 4 at a time: the run completed, where uncapped runs at 8 and 16 at a time were killed by the OOM killer. 15 files passed 3 GB and were reported as `e`.

* After review: with 4 heavy hub checks running, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP to the runner leaves 0 checks behind after 1.5 s (8d6888e left all 4); a 2 s deadline leaves nothing running; with `MEM_MB` unset all 1,666 files keep their verdict and output text.

**Not run:** on the minis (macOS). The repo-gate workflow checks out `main`'s `gates/`, so CI will not exercise this change.

Found and tested with Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5.5, during an audit of `--verdict`.

title: --verdict rejects a reused proof after reconstructing a constructor with a function field
body:
### What you did

From Bend source commit `234cb9b950800f20b15feafcb4ce2f43e76e7fae`, run:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts proof_reuse.bend --check-only
bun bend2/main.ts proof_reuse.bend --verdict
bun bend2/main.ts proof_reuse.bend -o proof_reuse.bendtt
```

The verdict run uses the unchanged BendTT kernel built with Lean 4.34.0.
The same failure occurs with the constructor expected-type fix in #1620.
I tested a checkout whose `safe.ts` is byte-identical to that PR's version
at `9144e4e95a69ae9ed325628b84fd79ba7a92ea16`.

### What happened

Source checking exits 0:

```text
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
```

`--verdict` exits 1 and reports:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In use:
expected: {(.Box, (x0, ())) == (.Box, (x0, ())) : Box}
observed: {(.Box, (λx1 => (x0 x1), ())) == (.Box, (λx1 => (x0 x1), ())) : Box}
```

The usual TypeScript/BendTT mismatch message follows. Export exits 0, emits
the complete theorem, and gives no out-of-scope diagnostic. Running the
unchanged kernel directly on that export gives the same rejection.

### The file

Save this as `proof_reuse.bend`:

```bend
type Box is Type:
  Box{value: Type -> Type}

def reflexive(-x: Box) -> {x == x : Box}:
  {==}

def use(h: Box) -> {h == h : Box}:
  match h:
    case Box{f}:
      reflexive(Box{f})
```

This file has no imports, generic type parameters, templates, recursion,
unsafe code, or open laws.

### Controls and expected behavior

Both of these replacements for `use` pass source checking and `--verdict`:

```bend
# Pass the original value to the same proof.
def use(h: Box) -> {h == h : Box}:
  reflexive(h)
```

```bend
# Prove the same branch goal directly.
def use(h: Box) -> {h == h : Box}:
  match h:
    case Box{f}:
      {==}
```

As a negative control, a proof of `Box{f} == Box{g}` from only
`reflexive(Box{f})`, with unrelated `f` and `g`, fails source checking.
These results are the same on main and with the #1620 fix.

The reused reflexivity proof should verify as the direct proof does.
The current behavior prevents this helper from being reused after matching
and reconstructing a value that contains a function.

### Where the comparison differs

In `safe.ts`, `ctr_term` knows the field type `Type -> Type`. Its call to
`arg_term` expands `f` to `x => f(x)`. The emitted branch calls:

```text
(reflexive -(.Box, (λx1 => (x0 x1), ())))
```

The helper's result type is `{x == x : Box}`. Application substitutes the
expanded constructor into that result type. The branch's expected type
still contains the matched field `x0`, as the diagnostic shows.

Bend source conversion accepts this η equation. BendTT conversion does not
identify the neutral function `x0` with `λx1 => (x0 x1)`. Thus a source
proof that works directly fails when the same goal is obtained through a
helper's dependent result type.

This is distinct from #1619/#1620: the field type is declared directly,
and no generic parameter or expected constructor type is missing. It is
also distinct from the lambda-quantity conversion change in #1224. The
comparison here is between a function variable and its η expansion.

### Experimental solution

I have an experimental extension of BendTT conversion that accepts this same
emitted proof. It includes Lean proofs of the revised checker's safety
properties. The complete development still exceeds the kernel's file
limit, so it is not ready for an upstream PR. These proofs do not establish
`safe.ts` translation correctness.

### Environment

- Bend: source commit `234cb9b950800f20b15feafcb4ce2f43e76e7fae`.
- Additional run: the identical constructor fix from #1620; unchanged kernel.
- Bun: 1.3.14.
- Lean: 4.34.0.
- `uname -sm`: `Darwin arm64`.
- Clang: `Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)`; not used by these checks.

title: err_fail's _exit and stdio leave an embedder no fatal path (terminal state, signals)
body:
## Summary

A native program's fatal path gives an embedder no way to undo shared state it changed, such as a terminal's termios. `err_fail` (`bend2/comp.ts:3726` on main at 234cb9b) does:

```c
static void err_fail(const char* msg) {
  fflush(stdout);
  fprintf(stderr, "bend: %s\n", msg);
  _exit(1);
}
```

It is reached from about 30 places (a deadlock, an out-of-memory in `io_mem`, a failed reservation or `pthread_create`, ...) and from `err_trap`, the `SIGSEGV`/`SIGBUS` handler installed with `sigaction` (`comp.ts:4726-4728`).

## Why it matters

- `_exit` skips `atexit`, so an effect that put the terminal in raw mode (our `Tty.raw_on`, a C effect) cannot restore it: after a runtime deadlock or memory fault the user's shell is left raw.
- The runtime catches `SIGSEGV`/`SIGBUS` itself and turns them into `_exit(1)`, so a host cannot catch those signals either: a crash looks like a plain exit 1.
- `fflush`/`fprintf` are not async-signal-safe, and `err_trap` runs them from a signal handler (a fault while another thread holds the stdio lock can hang the process instead of ending it).

## What we do now

A small supervisor process that saves the termios, runs the Bend program, waits for it and restores (it covers `SIGKILL` too). That works, but it costs a second process; an in-process fatal path would let simpler embedders stay correct.

## Possible changes (any one would help)

1. A documented fatal hook: a C function an effect registers, called by `err_fail` before `_exit`, with the contract that it must be async-signal-safe.
2. `write(2)` instead of stdio in `err_fail` (async-signal-safe), and, for `err_trap`, re-raise the original signal with its default action after the message, so the process ends by `SIGSEGV`/`SIGBUS` and a parent sees the real cause.

## Version / system

Bend v2.0.35 (we pin it); checked the same code on main at 234cb9b. Darwin arm64.

title: avoid quadratic rejection in F32.read
body:
F32.read’s JS matcher allows two digit repetitions to consume the same integer when the optional decimal point is absent. A long digit string followed by an invalid character causes quadratic rejection. Require the decimal point before the second repetition, preserving the accepted grammar and existing rounding behavior.

Add a focused regression that constructs 100,000 digits followed by `x` at runtime. It exceeds the test runner’s existing five-second limit before the fix and returns `None` afterward.

Local checks: the regression and existing whitespace, rounding and formatting fixtures pass through source/compiled CLIs, emitted Bun/Node and native C on macOS arm64. TypeScript diagnostics match baseline.

The repository gate remains blocked by the existing compiler token overage: main is 64,092/64,000; this fix adds two tokens, reaching 64,094.

title: gates: raise comp.ts cap to 66k
BendTT: adequacy, a checked law holds at each closed instance
body:
Opened after Nico's go-ahead on Discord.

`Claim.consistent` says no checked def has type `<>`. This adds the claim a law's user relies on: a checked proof of `{a == b}` means `a` and `b` convert. It holds for any closed, live term, so a checked law holds at each closed instance (its proof def applied to closed values), in the kernel's own reduction (opaque defs at their models, as in Part 2).

```lean
def Claim.adequate : Prop :=
  ∀ bk t T a b A, Book.check bk = .ok () → Term.Closed t → Term.Live bk t →
    Typed bk [] t T → Conv bk T (Eql a b A) → Conv bk a b
```

The proof is `adequate`, after `consistent`. It reuses `halts`, `progress`, `pars_sr`, `value_form`, `gen` and `fits_conv`, plus two small lemmas after `canon_enu`: `eql_inj` (the sides of convertible equations convert) and `canon_eql` (a closed value at an equation is `{==}`). It changes no line that `Book.check` or `main` runs.

**What I ran** on this exact file (identical to `main` at `22d627b` plus this patch; `bendtt.lean` is unchanged since `234cb9b`, where I ran these):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `lake build` (Lean 4.34.0) | builds |
| `#print axioms` on all 10 theorems, `Book.check`, `main` | `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only |
| `leanchecker --fresh` | passes |
| Lean4Lean `--fresh` (its 4.33.0-rc2 toolchain) | 93,251 declarations checked |
| `lean -c` + `leanc -O3 -DNDEBUG` kernel binary | **byte-identical** to `main`'s |
| `tests/` + `demos/*/PROOF.bend` (1,666 files) through `--verdict` | same verdict and output text for every file |
| Size (`ttok==0.3`, which matches CI) | 62,092 → 62,676 of the 64,000 cap |

Happy to shorten it, rename, or restate it in the file's style.
