title: fix(js): explain the host Nat input range
body:
Fixes #1634.

Invalid JavaScript Nat inputs reported the 2^48-1 arithmetic limit, even for a negative number, fraction, BigInt, NaN or Infinity. `nat_in` now throws its own message, `bend: expected a Nat host number: an integer from 0 to 2^53`. The accepted range and the arithmetic limit are unchanged.

Tests:
- `tests/io/nat_host_export`: the exported-argument rejections (one call and curried, plus NaN/Infinity) check the exact new message; 0, 2^48 and 2^53 round-trip through `identity`.
- `tests/io/nat_host_neg`: a foreign effect answering -3 is now a JS-only golden with the new message. The C lane reads that answer as a word past the cap and fail-stops later in `Nat.show` with the 2^48-1 limit, so the two lanes cannot share one golden; the C twin is removed.

title: fix(safe): preserve neutral function fields in constructors
body:
Fixes #1623.

The translation expanded a stored function `f` to `λx => f(x)` when rebuilding a constructor. The dependent proof goal still contained `f`, and BendTT does not identify those terms by eta conversion.

Constructor fields now keep their original function values. Non-field argument translation and the Lean kernel are unchanged. The regression rebuilds a matched constructor and reuses a proof helper; the direct and original-value cases remain checked too.

Verified with the actual `--verdict` CLI: the new case and five existing eta/congruence/dependent-constructor examples all report `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The repository gate passes 54/54. I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

Removed the GUIDE.md changes as requested in #1644.

title: JS String.trim_end rebuilds the whole string twice even when there is no trailing whitespace
body:
The JS target currently compiles `String.trim_end` through `reverse(trim_start(reverse(s)))`. A long retained prefix is visited and rebuilt twice, even when the last character is not whitespace.

I measured the actual `.mjs` exports from current main and a suffix-scan implementation on Linux x64, Bun 1.4.3. These are medians of five interleaved rounds, 100 calls per round, including the normal host-string conversion:

| Input | Main | Suffix scan |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 7,000 UTF-16 units, no whitespace suffix | 150.90 ms | 1.07 ms |
| Same prefix plus four whitespace units | 148.16 ms | 1.13 ms |

The fix is in https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/b6d8f303 . It scans the ASCII whitespace suffix backward. Packed non-Unicode Char payloads can themselves end in a whitespace code, so the scan preserves them and distinguishes their marker from a valid scalar’s low surrogate.

Before/after values match for 1,295 packed/scalar codes, including all 1,024 astral scalars whose low surrogate is DC00, and ten ordinary string cases. The focused boundary program returns `True{}` on both JS and native C. The repository gate passes 54/54, with the existing caps unchanged.

title: perf(js): scan only the whitespace suffix in String.trim_end
body:
Fixes #1658.

The JS implementation now scans backward over `Char.is_space` codes instead of reversing the retained prefix twice. It keeps packed Char payloads intact and does not confuse their marker with the low surrogate of a valid astral scalar. C and the Base definition are unchanged.

The focused regression returns `True{}` on both JS and native C. Before/after exports match for 1,295 packed/scalar codes and ten string cases. Local interleaved timing results are in the issue. The repository gate passes 54/54 with the existing caps.

The guide documents the suffix scan; the Base-library introduction is shortened without dropping its operation list. I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

title: feat(base): Byte and Word16, with byte conversions for U32 (draft, for consideration)
body:
**A draft, for consideration: take it, change it or close it.** It adds 8- and 16-bit word types to Base. I know bytes are `U32` by ruling today (`tests/base/bytes_ops.bend`, and `File.read_bytes`/`TCP.send_bytes` take `List<&2, U32>`), so this is an option, not a request to change that.

**Why it might be worth having.** A typed byte makes wrapping at 8 bits, byte order and range part of the type, which suits proofs about encodings: UTF-8, checksums, crypto, wire formats. Several hub packages build their own version today.

**What it adds** (250 lines of `base.bend`, plus a test):

* `type Byte is Data: Byte{data: Word(8n)}` and `type Word16 is Data: Word16{data: Word(16n)}`, built the way `U32` is:
  * `add sub mul and or xor not inc shl shr`, which wrap;
  * `cmp is_eq is_lt is_le is_gt is_ge`;
  * `to_nat to_u32 from_nat show`.
* `U32.to_byte` and `U32.to_word16`, which keep the low bits.
* `U32.byte(a, i)`, byte `i` of `a`, least significant first.
* `U32.of_bytes(b0, b1, b2, b3)`, least significant first, and `U32.of_bytes_be`, most significant first.
* `Word16.of_bytes`.
* `Word.lo`, `Word.hi` and `Word.cat`, to split a `Word(m + n)` and join it back.
* One law, `Byte.to_u32_to_byte`: `U32.to_byte(Byte.to_u32(b)) == b`, proved by cases on the 8 bits.

There are no natives, so these run as Base defs in every lane. Natives can follow if you want them.

**The names.** `U8` and `U16` would be the natural names, but 11 hub packages declare their own `U8` (3 also declare `U16`). A redeclared Base name is refused (#1042), so those packages, and 6 files that import them, would stop checking. Eight of the 11 are UTF-8 decoders where `U8` is the decoder's state, not a byte. `Byte` and `Word16` collide with nothing:

* I checked every one of the 52 type, constructor and def names against all 647 packages on the hub (pulled today, hash-verified) and against the repo's tests, demos, benches and Base.
* As a stronger check, every hub file that mentions any of the names (107 files) gives the same `--check-only` output with this Base as with `main`'s.

**Tested** on `main` at e5527d5:

* `tests/base/byte_word16.bend`: the interpreter, JS and C lanes all print the expected line, and `--verdict` prints ALL PROOFS CHECK. So does Base on its own.
* All 1,665 test files: `--check-only` output is identical with this Base and with `main`'s.
* Cost: Base grows by 8%, which adds roughly 5–10 ms to every check (about 113 ms against 121 ms, averaged over warm runs on a one-law file; the gap is close to run-to-run noise).

Not run: `gates/test.ts` and `gates/safe.ts` on the minis.

If you'd rather not grow Base, I'll publish it as a hub package instead.

Found and tested with Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5.5, during an audit of `--verdict`.

title: JS Array.to_list copies array slots at every tree level
body:
`Array.to_list` walks the Base array tree. JS arrays are flat, so each ANode match slices the backing array in two before the walk continues. This copies O(n log n) slots to produce an O(n) list.

I profiled the actual generated `.mjs` export with 4,096 elements on Bun 1.4.3:

| Work per conversion | Main | Flat walk |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Array.slice calls | 8,190 | 0 |
| Copied array slots | 49,152 | 0 |

The fix is in https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/de9bf2f8 . It walks the flat array backward and prepends list nodes without mutating the input. `Array.to_list` is a template: its checked specializations have generated names and no Base flag, so JS dispatch recognizes those instances through the Base template’s metadata. Arbitrary user definitions do not become intrinsics, and C keeps the existing implementation.

The generated exports preserve order for six valid power-of-two sizes from 1 to 4,096, accept frozen input arrays, and preserve record-element identity. A focused regression covers U32 and record elements plus a first-class function reference; it returns `True{}` on both JS and native C. The repository gate passes 54/54. I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

title: perf(js): convert Array.to_list without slicing the flat array
body:
Fixes #1661.

JS now builds the list directly from the flat array, in index order, instead of slicing both halves at each tree level. The input is not mutated. Only checked specializations of the Base template get this intrinsic; generated names and the missing Base flag on those instances are handled explicitly. C keeps the Base implementation.

The generated API preserves order for six sizes from 1 to 4,096, works with frozen arrays, and preserves record-element identity. Runtime profiling of 4,096 elements records no slice calls or copied slots after the change; the original counts are in the issue. The focused U32/record/first-class-reference program returns `True{}` on JS and native C, and repo passes 54/54.

The array guide notes conversion order and the JS flat walk. No cap, parser, or Lean-kernel changes. I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

title: JS String.repeat performs per-repetition calls instead of using the host primitive
body:
The JS target currently follows the recursive Base implementation of `String.repeat`. Even ordinary bounded counts pay for a language call and concatenation at every repetition.

I compared the actual `.mjs` exports from main and a native-repeat implementation on Linux x64, Bun 1.4.3. Medians of five interleaved rounds, 2,000 calls per round, count 256:

| Seed | Main | Host repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `ab😀` | 8.15 ms | 2.24 ms |
| Empty string | 4.75 ms | 0.22 ms |

The fix is in https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/7ecc1bf3 . A small JS helper evaluates the seed once, returns an empty seed directly, and otherwise uses the host repeat primitive. Repeating whole internal strings keeps both astral scalars and packed non-Unicode Char codes intact. C and the Base implementation are unchanged.

Thirty ordinary before/after cases match, including zero counts and empty seeds. The generated API also returns an empty string for an empty seed at the maximum accepted host Nat. A focused mixed packed/scalar regression returns `True{}` on JS and native C, and the repository gate passes 54/54. This is not a larger-fold or stack-limit change; I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

title: perf(js): use host repetition for String.repeat
body:
Fixes #1663.

JS now repeats the whole internal string with the host primitive rather than making a language call for each repetition. The helper evaluates the seed once and returns empty seeds directly. C and the Base implementation are unchanged.

The generated exports match main for 30 ordinary cases. The empty-seed case also works at the maximum accepted host Nat. A focused regression checks packed non-Unicode Char codes, an astral scalar, zero repetitions, and an empty seed; it returns `True{}` on JS and native C. Local interleaved timing results are in the issue, and repo passes 54/54.

The Base-library guide notes host repetition. No cap, parser, or Lean-kernel changes; I did not run the macOS/Metal gate cluster.

title: `--verdict` mismatch: an η-expanded argument keeps old binder levels in its inner annotations (`Bool` where `Nat` is expected)
body:
### What you did

`bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --check-only`, then `bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --verdict`

### What happened

On main (e5527d5b):

```text
$ bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --check-only
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend --verdict
SOME PROOFS FAIL
In passed:
expected: Nat
observed: Σx3 : <False, True> -> (Bool.arms x3)
Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug.
```

### The file

```python
import Base

type Fact<-P: Type> is Data:
  Fact{-proof: P}

type Box<-P: Type> is Data:
  Box{}

def Cells() -> Type:
  @+b: Bool -> {b == b : Bool}

def cells(-keeps: @+n: Nat -> {n == n : Nat}) -> Fact<Cells()>:
  Fact{b => {==}}

def take(-p: Cells()) -> Box<Cells()>:
  Box{}

def passed(-kf: @+n: Nat -> Fact<{n == n : Nat}>) -> Box<Cells()>:
  take({\{Fact: q => q} : Fact<Cells()> -> Cells()}(
    cells(n => {\{Fact: q => q} : Fact<{n == n : Nat}> -> {n == n : Nat}}(kf(n)))))
```

### bend --version

2.0.37 (tag `v2.0.37`, 4ff8545f). Same result on main at e5527d5b and on PR #1657 at 4d5f6625. Each version's kernel was built from its own `bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0 (the PR doesn't change `bendtt.lean`). On 2.0.37, `--verdict` fails the same way, but without the `In passed: expected/observed` lines.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

No `clang` on PATH; `clang-19 --version`: Ubuntu clang version 19.1.1 (1ubuntu1~24.04.2). `--verdict` doesn't use it: it returns at main.ts:308, before `cc_find`.

### Diagnosis

The argument of `take` is an application, and its type `Cells()` is a function type. So `arg_term` makes it η-long: [safe.ts:1332-1340](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c/bend2/safe.ts#L1332-L1340) calls `eta` ([safe.ts:953-955](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c/bend2/safe.ts#L953-L955)), which wraps the argument in a new binder, `λ+x1 : Bool`. That moves the inner `n => ...` down one level, from `x1` to `x2`. Its body moves with it. The `Nat` annotations on the inner eliminator don't move and still say `x1`, which is now the `Bool`. From `-o`:

```
passed = λ-x0 => (take -λ+x1 => ({…} : ∀x2 : (Fact -Cells) -> Cells}
  (cells -λ+x2 => ({…} : ∀x3 : (Fact -{x1 == x1 : Nat}) -> {x1 == x1 : Nat}} (x0 +x2))) +x1))
```

The η-expanded form written by hand (below) emits the same term, character for character, except for `{x2 == x2 : Nat}` in those two places, and it passes. So the kernel is right to reject this term: it really is ill-typed.

To find where the stale level comes from, I dumped the argument at `arg_term`'s `eta` branch. The λ bodies in it use whatever variable they are instantiated with. But the annotations bend2 attached to the inner eliminator (`Var("_", -1)` with `v` set) hold `n` as `Var(n, 1)`, a fixed level. I didn't trace where `bend.ts` writes those annotations.

Here the stale level gives an ill-typed term, so a valid proof gets rejected. I didn't look for a case where the stale level lands on a binder whose type fits and the term is accepted.

`tree` also calls `eta`, at [safe.ts:772](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c/bend2/safe.ts#L772) and [safe.ts:879](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c/bend2/safe.ts#L879). I didn't test those paths.

### Workaround

Writing the η-expanded argument by hand passes `--check-only` and `--verdict` on all three versions above:

```python
  take(b => {\{Fact: q => q} : Fact<Cells()> -> Cells()}(
    cells(n => {\{Fact: q => q} : Fact<{n == n : Nat}> -> {n == n : Nat}}(kf(n))))(b))
```

### Related

- #1623 / PR #1657: the same trigger (`arg_term` η-expands a function-typed argument) with a different failure. There the expanded field `λx => f(x)` doesn't convert with `f`. PR #1657 stops η-expanding constructor fields. With the PR applied, my first version of this bug, where the proof goes into a `Fact{...}` field, passes. This file still fails, because the proof is an ordinary erased argument. I'm filing it separately so it stays open if #1657 closes #1623.
- #1168 (closed by 01875127, together with #1178): the same kind of bug, a term built at one depth and placed at another. That fix covers specialized arguments, not `eta`.

title: A def's body goes to --verdict through its lowered form once, so its annotations move with its binders under η, rebuild and let inlining (#1665, #1669)
body:
Fixes #1665. Fixes #1669. This follows @Lorenzobattistela's suggestion in review: fix the levels once, where `arm` reads a def's body, instead of at each step that moves a term. It supersedes #1670, whose test is here.

## Cause

bend2 wraps each node it checks in its type, as a cell (`Infer` and `Check` in `bend.ts`). `arm` raises a def's body with `term_higher`, which keeps a cell as it is. So a binder in the body becomes a closure, but an annotation still names it by the level bend2 checked it at. Any step that puts part of the body under binders bend2 didn't check it under leaves those annotations at the old levels:

- `eta` puts a term under a new λ (#1665).
- `rebuild` puts a λ's body under a binder per field (#1669).
- `let_term` builds a let's value at the self-call it is passed to, at the call's depth (the case from the review).

A template's body already goes through `subst(t0, 0, …)`, which lowers and raises it. The issue's term in a def with a `~` parameter checks on main.

## Fix

`arm` lowers and raises every other def's body once, `term_higher(term_lower(t0))`. Lowering forces each cell, so an annotation names the body's binders as the body's own uses do, and raising binds both. `eta`, `rebuild` and `let_term` are as on main.

The review's line sends every body through `subst`. The output is the same, but `subst`'s copy recurses deeper per node than lowering does. With it, `-o` overflows the stack on a def whose body is a 3,800-element list literal, with or without η. Without the copy, the limit is main's. Here 4,000 elements pass and 4,500 overflow, on both, and a chain of 4,000 lets passes on both with the same `-o`. The exact limit depends on the machine's stack.

## Checks

With main 64230dcb merged in, Linux x86_64, kernel built from main's `bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0:

- `eta_levels` (the four η sites), `rebuild_levels` (#1669: a type with two constructors, one with no fields, and a λ inside the body) and `let_levels` (the review's let) each fail `--verdict` on main and check here. Each prints its `#|` value when run and from the JS and C builds, and `--checkup` exits 0. Lowering at depth 1 instead of 0 fails all three.
- On main's 1,760 test, demo, and bench files, `--verdict` gives the same exit code and output as main: 1,137 check, 623 fail. `-o` differs in 15 files, all through three Base defs (`String.cmp.group`, `Map.get.leaf`, `Str.split.fin`). There, a variable that main passes through a match's convoy is now a copied binder, `λ+x`. Each of the three defs verifies in the 9 of those files that check. The other 6 fail on `@unsafe` before the kernel, as on main.
- Cost: lowering every body takes time. Over two sets of sequential runs on the checker benches, `-o` is 5 to 9% slower on `defs_12800`, 10 to 15% on `generics_3200`, and 14 to 21% on `proofs_3200` (3.2 s on main, 3.8 s here). `--verdict` on `proofs_3200` goes from 4.0 s to 4.7 s. Most of it is the lowering itself, which forces the cell at each node and lowers its type: 0.71 s of the 1.94 s `safe_book` takes on `proofs_3200`. With `subst` on every body, `-o` takes 1.8, 2.6, and 6.5 s on those three. Plain runs and `--check-only` don't change, so the perf gate's checker benches don't either. Over the 1,760-file sweep, total CPU goes up 1 to 2%.
- The review's 400-ary leaf: `-o` takes 2.7 s, the same as main, with the same output.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54. `safe.ts` goes from 23,992 to 24,000 ttok, at its cap. `tsc`: 11 errors, the same as main.
- I didn't run the cluster gates.

## Limits

`safe.ts` is at its cap, so this adds no comment at `arm`. The three test headers say why the body is lowered.

A fix at each site instead (η in one pass per leaf, plus `rebuild` and `let_term`) would keep `--verdict` near main's cost. The first version of this PR fixed only η that way and was within 3% of main on these benches. With all three sites, it doesn't fit under the cap today.

title: fix(safe): rebind inner annotations under eta expansion
body:
`eta` adds a lambda around an argument, but annotations inside that argument can still contain fixed levels from before the new binder. In the report, the inner `Nat` annotation ends up pointing at the new `Bool` variable.

Reopen the argument with the existing `subst` helper before wrapping it, preserving variables from the surrounding scope. The three eta callers now pass their current depth. The emitted annotation refers to `x2` again, and the reported program passes `--verdict`. Neither `bend.ts` nor the Lean kernel changes.

Added the reported program as a proof regression. Checked it with both `--check-only` and `--verdict`, plus five existing eta/dependent-function files with `--verdict`; all passed with Lean 4.34.0. The kernel matches the base byte for byte (SHA-256 `cc78aa9ff3491ff1b788797bdcab4cb98107dcb1730ed99834f6933b11d88335`). The repository gate passes without changing caps; the related comments and verdict paragraph are shorter.

Fixes #1665.

title: bend-lint format/layout: an under-indented case body moves the next case into the outer match
body:
`format/layout` re-indents the line after an under-indented case body relative to that body, which moves a later `case` into the enclosing `match`. The rule's same-parse check catches it, so nothing is broken on disk, but the file can never be formatted: the only output is "Cannot safely format this syntax: the result parses differently", with no location.

bend-lint at e5527d5, bend 2.0.37.

## Repro

```bend
import Base

def g(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Nat:
  match a:
    case True{}:
      match b:
        case True{}:
  1n
        case False{}:
  2n
    case False{}:
      3n

def main() -> Nat:
  g(True{}, False{})
```

`bend repro.bend` accepts it and prints `2n`: a case body may sit left of its `case`.

`bun tools/bend-lint/src/lint.ts repro.bend --rules tools/bend-lint/rules/format.ts` reports:

```
Warning [format/layout]:
- message  : Cannot safely format this syntax: the result parses differently. No fix was offered.
```

What `format()` produces:

```bend
      match b:
        case True{}:
  1n
    case False{}:
  2n
    case False{}:
      3n
```

The inner `case False{}:` moved from column 8 to column 4, so it now belongs to `match a`. Checking that output fails with `expected: cases for False` in `g`.

## Where it came from

Machine-written proofs produce this layout: a prover emitted `%Equal.sym(...) : {...}` rewrite lines and the `{==}` after them at a fixed small indent inside deeply nested matches. We re-indented our file, so this is not blocking us.

## Expected

Either keep each `case` at its own column (the layout of lines after a dedented body should follow the enclosing structure, not the previous line), or, if that is out of scope, name the first line whose parse changes in the warning so the user can fix the source by hand.

title: `--verdict` mismatch: a λ rebuilt as a match keeps its variable's old level in its annotations (`Nat` where `P` is expected)
body:
### What you did `bun bend2/main.ts twice.bend --check-only`, then `bun bend2/main.ts twice.bend --verdict` ### What happened ```text $ bun bend2/main.ts twice.bend --check-only ALL PROOFS CHECK Use --verdict for mathematical validity. $ bun bend2/main.ts twice.bend --verdict SOME PROOFS FAIL In main: expected: P observed: Σx2 : -> (Nat.arms x2) Sorry - this is a mismatch between the TypeScript implementation, and the formalized BendTT kernel. Your proofs may or may not be correct, and we cannot validate them yet. This will be addressed in a future update. Meanwhile, feel free to open an issue to report this bug. ``` ### The file ```python import Base type P is Type: P{a: Nat, b: Nat} type Tag<-x: P> is Data: Tag{} def first(p: P) -> Nat: match p: case P{a, b}: a def tag(-p: P) -> Tag

: Tag{} def use(-f: P -> Nat) -> Nat: 0n def main() -> Nat: use(p => Nat.add(first(p), {\{Tag: first(p)} : Tag

-> Nat}(tag(p)))) ``` ### bend --version main at e5527d5b (`VERSION` 2.0.37), run as `bun bend2/main.ts`. The result is the same on #1666 at fce97a9b. I built the kernel from main's `bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0. ### uname -sm Linux x86_64 ### clang --version (the first line) No `clang` on PATH. `clang-19 --version` gives Ubuntu clang version 19.1.1 (1ubuntu1~24.04.2). `--verdict` doesn't use it. ### Diagnosis `use` takes `f` erased, so bend2 lets the λ passed for it use `p` twice. `tree` sends that λ to `rebuild` ([safe.ts:929-944](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c/bend2/safe.ts#L929-L944)). `rebuild` turns the λ into a λ-match on `P` and builds its body with `p` as `P{a, b}`, under new binders for `a` and `b`. The annotations bend2 attached to the body still name `p` by the level bend2 checked it at, and that level now belongs to `a`. From `-o`: ``` main : Nat = (use -λ{(,): λ{.P: λ{(,): λ+x0 => λ{(,): λ+x1 => λ{(): (Nat.add (first (.P, (x0, (x1, ())))) ({…} : ∀x2 : (Tag -x0) -> Nat} (tag -(.P, (x0, (x1, ())))))); λ{}}}}; λ{}}}) ``` `x0` is `a : Nat`, so `Tag -x0` is ill-typed. The type should be `Tag -(.P, (x0, (x1, ())))`. The rebuilt λ written by hand passes `--check-only` and `--verdict`: ```python use(\{P: a => b => Nat.add(first(P{a, b}), {\{Tag: first(P{a, b})} : Tag -> Nat}(tag(P{a, b})))}) ``` When the constructors have no fields, `rebuild` adds no binder, so no variable in scope has the old level. `--verdict` then reports `out of scope: main: a free variable u` instead:

twice0.bend ```python import Base type U is Type: U1{} U2{} type Tag<-x: U> is Data: Tag{} def code(u: U) -> Nat: match u: case U1{}: 1n case U2{}: 2n def tag(-u: U) -> Tag: Tag{} def use(-f: U -> Nat) -> Nat: 0n def main() -> Nat: use(u => Nat.add(code(u), {\{Tag: code(u)} : Tag -> Nat}(tag(u)))) ```
The wrong levels are only in annotations inside a def's body, never in its type. So the bug can reject a valid proof, but it cannot make the kernel accept a wrong one. No test, demo, or bench file reaches it. ### Fix On top of #1666, the fix is one line in `rebuild`. It passes the λ through `subst(x, s.d)`, as #1666 does in `eta`, so the body's annotations move with its binders: ```diff - return G.$ !== "All" ? x.f(B.Ann(B.Ctr(k, xs), F)) : B.Lam(G.k, 0, (v: HTerm) => arm(k, G.B(v), [...xs, v])); + return G.$ !== "All" ? (subst(x, s.d) as typeof x).f(B.Ann(B.Ctr(k, xs), F)) : B.Lam(G.k, 0, (v: HTerm) => arm(k, G.B(v), [...xs, v])); ``` With the fix, both files pass `--verdict`, and the `-o` of `twice.bend` is byte-identical to the hand-written version's. `--verdict` and `-o` don't change on any of the 1,734 test, demo, and bench files. `safe.ts` goes from 23,987 to 23,997 ttok (`ttok==0.3`). With #1657 merged as well, it would be at 24,006, over the 24,000 cap. ### Related - #1665 and #1666: the same bug in `eta`, which puts a term under one new λ. - #1349 (closed by #1369): the same `rebuild` path, with a different failure (out of scope when a field is not Data). - #1168: the same kind of bug, a term built at one depth and placed at another.

title: A λ rebuilt as a match keeps its annotations on its own binders, so --verdict checks what bend2 checks (#1669)
body:
Fixes #1669. Depends on #1666, whose `subst(t, d)` the fix uses. Until #1666 merges, this PR's diff also shows its two commits. Only the last commit, 45716b3b, is new here.

## Cause

`use(-f: P -> Nat)` takes `f` erased, so bend2 lets the λ passed for it use its variable twice. `rebuild` in `safe.ts` turns that λ into a λ-match on the variable and calls the λ's body on each constructor, under a binder per field. bend2's annotations name a variable by the level bend2 checked it at, so they still name the variable's old level. With fields, that level now belongs to the first field, and the kernel rejects the term (`expected: P`). With no fields, no variable in scope has that level, and `--verdict` reports a free variable.

## Fix

`rebuild` passes the λ through `subst(x, s.d)` before it calls the body, as #1666 does in `eta`. In the lowered form, an annotation names the body's binders as the body's own uses do, so the annotations move with the binders.

## Checks

On #1666's head (fce97a9b), Linux x86_64, kernel built from main's `bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0:

- `tests/check/rebuild_levels.bend` covers an annotation that names the variable, for a type with two constructors (`pair`) and for one with no fields (`unit`), and one that names the binder of a λ inside the body (`inner`). Each one fails `--verdict` on #1666 when it is on its own. `pair` and `inner` fail in the kernel, and `unit` fails as out of scope. A law pins `main` at `6n`. The file prints `6n` when run and from the JS and C builds, and `--checkup` exits 0.
- Mutations: the old line, or `subst` at `s.d + 1` or `s.d - 1`, fails all three.
- On the other 1,734 test, demo, and bench files, `--verdict` gives the same exit code and output as #1666, and `-o` is byte-identical. Both files in #1669 check, and the `-o` of its `twice.bend` is byte-identical to the hand-written version's.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` with `ttok==0.3`: 54 / 54. `safe.ts` goes from 23,987 to 23,997 ttok. `tsc`: 11 errors, the same as main.
- I didn't run the cluster gates.

## Merge order

With #1657 as well, all three PRs apply cleanly and the tests above check, but `safe.ts` comes to 24,006 ttok, over its 24,000 cap. Whichever of #1657 and this PR lands second has to save 6 tokens.

title: perf(io): remove expired native channel waiters in constant time
body:
A timed channel operation can delay unrelated IO when it expires behind many blocked operations. `chan_cut` scans the channel queue to find the previous waiter. Even when timeouts fire in queue order, removing T timed waiters behind B blocked waiters requires O(B × T) queue traversal on the IO loop.

Use the existing `IoWork.prev` field to remove each expired channel waiter in O(1). Maintain both links when a waiter enters the queue, leaves on timeout, or wakes in FIFO order. The waiter and its timer use separate `IoWork` objects, so this adds no allocation or struct field.

Add `chan_waiter_links.bend` to check sender and receiver queues. It covers head, middle, tail, and singleton removal; enqueue after timeout; wake before timeout; close; and activation reuse. The test checks results without a performance threshold.

This targets native IO performance. It is separate from #1250 and #1442, which concern the global poll and timer queues. This change only updates the channel waiter ring.

### Measurement

The Base-only program below parks 32,768 blocking senders and then starts 4,096 sends with 100 ms timeouts. A separate fiber sleeps for 100 ms. Every run returned all 4,096 expected timeout results.

| Platform | Original 100 ms timer | Changed 100 ms timer | Method |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Apple M5 Max, macOS 26.6.2, Apple Clang 21 | 376 ms | 110 ms | Median of three alternating pairs after warmup |
| Debian 13 ARM64, Clang 19, Linux container | 418 ms | 106 ms | One before/after pair |

Both versions use `-O3` and `--threads 1`. The baseline is `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`. The changed binaries use C emitted from this branch. These results measure this workload; global timer insertion costs remain.

### Validation

- Repository gate: 54/54.
- macOS: 22 IO tests pass in the interpreter, native runtime with 1 and 4 threads, and Bun.
- Linux: 15 channel and deadlock tests pass on both versions with 1 and 4 threads (60 runs).
- The new regression passes under ASan and UBSan. Removing any of the four required link updates makes it fail.
- A scratch ASan/UBSan test passes one million randomized queue operations. It checks FIFO order, both links, tail identity, and singleton removal.
- The full test gate requires the maintainer cluster and was not run.

<details>
<summary>Timing reproduction</summary>

Save this as `mixed_timeouts.bend` in the repository root. Run it on the baseline and this branch:

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts mixed_timeouts.bend -o mixed_timeouts
./mixed_timeouts --threads 1
```

```bend
import Base

def plain(blocked: Chan(U32), ready: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    ack : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, ready, 1)
    result : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, blocked, 7)
    IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

def score(result: Poll<&1, &1, Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit>, U32>) -> U32:
  match result:
    case Ready{result}: 0
    case Wait{rest}: Bool.pick(U32, U32.is_eq(rest,9),1,0)

def timed(blocked: Chan(U32), done: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : Poll<&1, &1, Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit>, U32> <- Chan.try_send(U32, blocked, 9, 100)
    sent : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, done, score(result))
    IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

def start_plain(n: Nat, +blocked: Chan(U32), +ready: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, plain(blocked,ready))
        start_plain(p, blocked,ready)

def start_timed(n: Nat, +blocked: Chan(U32), +done: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, timed(blocked, done))
        start_timed(p, blocked, done)

def get(got: Maybe<&1, U32>) -> U32:
  match got:
    case None{}: 0
    case Some{x}: x

def wait_all(n: Nat, +done: Chan(U32), acc: U32) -> IO(U32):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(U32, acc)
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<U32>:
        got : Maybe<&1, U32> <- Chan.recv(U32, done)
        wait_all(p, done, U32.add(acc,get(got)))

def report(started: Nat, label: String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    now : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ Nat.show(Nat.sub(now, started)))

def canary() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    started : Nat <- IO.now()
    Unit <- IO.sleep(100)
    report(started,"canary_ms=")

def run(+blockers: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +blocked : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,0)
    +ready : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,U32.from_nat(blockers))
    +done : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,4096)
    Unit <- start_plain(blockers,blocked,ready)
    queued : U32 <- wait_all(blockers,ready,0)
    Unit <- IO.print("queued=" ++ U32.show(queued))
    started : Nat <- IO.now()
    Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, canary())
    Unit <- start_timed(4096n,blocked,done)
    count : U32 <- wait_all(4096n,done,0)
    Unit <- report(started,"complete_ms=")
    Unit <- IO.print("count=" ++ U32.show(count))
    Chan.close(U32,blocked)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  run(32768n)
```

</details>

title: fix(audio): count complete frames in JS Audio.write
body:
JS Audio.write counts each unmatched stereo sample as half a frame, so two separate one-sample writes can report one queued frame. Count complete frames per write, matching native behavior, and preserve whole-request rejection above 8192 samples.

Add a focused regression that prints 1 before the fix and 0 afterward through source/compiled CLIs and emitted Bun/Node. Local Audio fixtures and capacity checks pass; repository gate 54/54.

title: demos: proof_userland_tactics — a tactic from userland
body:
A demo, not a proposal: on stock 2.0.37, a tactic as a library.

- propositions as data (`P`), `Interp : P -> Type` into native goals
- `auto(p) -> Maybe<Interp(p)>` decides the fragment; `Some{...}` carries the proof term, `None{}` is the honest refusal
- quantified laws (`min_le`, `le_succ_r`) stay hand-proved beside it; instances go through the tactic, definitionally — `Interp(PLe{a, b})` normalizes to the native goal itself, so there is no glue

The README shows the run transcript, including what happens when a bug is introduced in `min`: the tactic flips `Some -> None` and names the unprovable goal, and the quantified law fails with it. That `None` is the agent-facing signal: not "error", but "here is what I could not prove".

The load-bearing feature is a computed type family in a generic signature (`Maybe<Interp(p)>` as a return type). No quote, no unify, no compiler changes — reflection, not metaprogramming; the Limits section says so plainly (`match A` on a Type parameter is a dead-region error, and goal introspection does not exist, so the framework reaches exactly the fragment you embed, soundly, and nothing else).

Verified on 2.0.37 (darwin/arm64):

```
$ bend demos/proof_userland_tactics/main.bend
Some Some None
$ bend demos/proof_userland_tactics/PROOF.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
```

and the buggy-`min` edit reproduces `Some None None` + `SOME PROOFS FAIL`.

fix(cli): protect HTML bundle inputs
body:
`bend page.html -o <dir>` can overwrite the page it bundles: directly (`-o` is the page's own directory), through a symlink, or through a hard link at `<dir>/page.html`.

In a Bun bundle only the page keeps its own name; chunks, CSS and assets are content-hashed. So the page is the one input an `-o` can overwrite by accident. `cli_bundle` now:

- builds from the page's real path (`path_real`), so the output name is known and a symlinked page builds to `<dir>/<target>.html` instead of `<dir>/_.._/<target>.html`;
- refuses the build when `<dir>/<page>` is already the page by device and inode (`same_file`), which covers the direct, symlink, hard-link and case-alias cases;
- keeps Bun's `outdir` writing, so a non-directory `-o` and a missing page still get Bun's own errors.

Not covered on purpose: a link planted at an output path that points at another input (main behaves the same).

`tests/io/bundle_page_input` covers the refused cases, the symlinked build (its chunk runs) and the missing-page error; it fails on main. `bend2/main.ts` +172 ttok (11,871). Gates on ed186a48: repo 54/54, test 1683/1683, ping 63/63, perf 123/124, safe 0 false rejects.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cli): complete short output writes
body:
CLI output could end successfully after a short write to a nonblocking pipe.
The writer now encodes each message once and continues from the last byte
written until the output is complete. Temporary write errors are retried,
zero progress fails, and closed readers leave the command's exit status intact.

The new compiled-CLI test sends Unicode guide text through a real nonblocking
pipe and restores the guide afterward.

The regression fails on the baseline and passes with the fix in source and
compiled CLIs on macOS and Linux arm64. Local retry and closed-reader checks
pass, as does the repository gate (54/54). Strict TypeScript retains the same
11 baseline diagnostics.

title: JS U32.to_f32 can give unsigned host zero a negative float sign
body:
On main e5527d5 (2.0.37), a zero-valued unsigned argument can acquire a negative floating-point sign on JS. The C primitive explicitly casts to u32 before converting; the JS primitive calls Math.fround directly.

`lib.bend`:
```bend
import Base

def as_float(n: U32) -> F32:
  U32.to_f32(n)
```
Build with `bun bend2/main.ts lib.bend -o lib.mjs`, then:
```js
import M from "./lib.mjs";
console.log(Object.is(M.as_float(-0), -0)); // true on main; should be false
```
The sign matters to F32.bits and division by zero. An unsigned zero has no negative sign; this should not change how a genuine F32 negative zero crosses the boundary.

I also reproduced it through a typed IO(U32) host answer, not just a module call. The same consumer prints `2147483648` on JS and `0` on C for the converted value. Its F32 negative-zero control prints `2147483648` on both lanes. With the unsigned cast in the JS conversion, both lanes print `0` for U32 zero while preserving that F32 control.

The local fix passes 4,103 actual exported conversion cases, including the full U32 range boundaries and fixed-seed values. Integer host marshalling is unchanged. No parser, kernel, cap or CHANGELOG change.

title: Keep unsigned zero positive in JS U32.to_f32
body:
The C path casts to u32 before converting. Do the same before Math.fround on JS, so a host value of -0 cannot introduce a floating-point sign into an unsigned zero. Integer marshalling and genuine F32 negative-zero inputs stay unchanged.

The regression feeds zero through real typed U32/F32 host answers on both lanes. Before: JS prints 2147483648 for the converted U32, C prints 0. After: both print 0; the F32 negative-zero control still prints 2147483648. Another 4,103 actual exported conversion cases passed, including full-range boundaries. Repository gate: 54/54 with existing caps. No parser, kernel or CHANGELOG edits.

Fixes #1692.

Removed the GUIDE.md changes as requested in #1644.

title: CLI outputs can silently overwrite an earlier emitted program through file aliases
body:
Two `-o` targets can refer to the same file, so the CLI reports success while replacing its first output with the second format.

```sh
printf 'import Base\n\ndef main() -> Nat:\n  7n\n' > main.bend
printf '' > first.js
ln first.js second.c
bun bend2/main.ts main.bend -o first.js -o second.c
bun first.js
```

On current main `e5527d5b`, compilation exits 0, but `first.js` contains C and the JS consumer fails on `#pragma`. Reversing the formats silently destroys the C output instead. The same problem happens through a symlink, a dangling symlink to the first newly created output, or the exact same output path twice.

The input-identity guard in #1496 does not yet cover an earlier output; I reproduced this on that branch after merging current main too. A colliding later output should fail without replacing the program already emitted. Independent outputs should still build normally.

Observed on Linux x86-64 with Bun 1.3.13. No source file was lost during this reproduction.

title: UDP receive buffers grow beyond the maximum IPv4 payload
body:
UDP.bind is IPv4-only, but UDP receive currently sizes its buffer from the caller's max: the JS backend reserves max bytes, and C reserves min(max, INT32_MAX) plus one spare byte. An IPv4 UDP payload cannot exceed 65,535 - 20 - 8 = 65,507 bytes.

On main e5527d5b, I sent a real one-byte loopback datagram and received it with max=1,048,576. A typed-array constructor trace records a 1,048,576-byte JS buffer; a native build linked with --wrap=malloc records a 1,048,577-byte allocation. Both consumers receive x successfully. This measures requested buffer sizes, not RSS; I did not try allocating 4 GiB.

Bounding the payload capacity to min(max, 65507) reduces those requests to 65,507 and 65,508 bytes with the same received data. max=0 must still fail without consuming a datagram; smaller positive limits must keep their existing truncation behavior. This applies to the text/byte and blocking/try receive variants sharing these helpers.

Observed with Bun 1.3.13 and clang 22 on Linux x86-64.

title: JS text I/O constructs a new UTF-8 codec for every buffer
body:
On 2.0.37/main e5527d5b, the emitted JS io_bytes creates a TextEncoder for every write, and io_text creates a TextDecoder for every read. Both codecs can be reused without streaming UTF-8 state between reads.

A real Bend loop doing 10,000 IO.write("") calls constructs 10,000 encoders, even though it writes no bytes. A host probe counts constructor calls and still invokes the real encoder.

I also timed the emitted helpers without instrumentation: 100,000 six-byte encodes take a median 22.182 ms; 100,000 decodes take 25.847 ms. Lazy codec reuse takes 8.682 ms and 13.529 ms respectively. Seven warmed, interleaved runs on Linux x86-64/Bun 1.3.13; output-length checksums stay unchanged. This is a local helper benchmark, not an end-to-end filesystem speed claim.

Reuse must keep BOMs as data and decode each input independently: an incomplete UTF-8 prefix in one read must not combine with a continuation byte in the next.

title: JS binary writes allocate an intermediate number array for every byte
body:
On main e5527d5b, the emitted io_unlist walks a List<U32> into a growing JS number array, checks that array for values above 255, then copies it into Uint8Array.from. File.write_bytes and the TCP/UDP byte send effects all use this conversion.

A probe of the actual emitted helper observes Uint8Array.from receiving a 100,000-element number array for a 100,000-byte payload. This temporary storage is in addition to the input list and the output byte buffer.

Counting/validating the list first and filling one owned Uint8Array removes that number array. Twenty conversions of the same 100,000-byte list took a median 13.575 ms before and 8.171 ms after, over seven warmed, interleaved Bun 1.3.13/Linux x86-64 runs. All 100,000 output bytes were compared against their expected values. These timings measure conversion, not disk or network throughput.

The replacement still needs whole-request validation before any write, must preserve empty lists and byte order, and must leave a shared input list unchanged.

title: Bound UDP receive buffers to the IPv4 payload limit
body:
Fixes #1695.

A caller can ask for more bytes than a legal IPv4 datagram can contain. Cap the receive allocation at 65,507 bytes on both backends, without changing truncation or zero-limit errors.

Removed the JS codec and byte-list optimizations following #1644. The reference helpers are unchanged; this PR now just covers UDP capacity.

The real socket regression prints `x` and `abc` on Bun and native C. Local repo gate: 54/54. The original largest-payload checks are in #1695; private mini-cluster gates weren’t run.

AI-assisted.

title: JS Nat.pow performs one recursive multiply per exponent step
body:
Nat.pow still lowers through its linear Base recursion on the JS lane. U32.pow already has a host path, but the Nat operation doesn't.

A small exported wrapper is enough to measure it:

```bend
import Base
def power(a: Nat, n: Nat) -> Nat:
  Nat.pow(a, n)
```

I compiled that to .mjs and called power(i & 1, 512 + (i & 511)) 1,000 times per round. Nine warmed alternating rounds on Linux x64/Bun 1.3.13: median 4.297 ms at PR #1682's existing 0b82c20 head, 0.199 ms with checked repeated squaring. Both sums were 500. This is a bounded workload, not an application-wide speed claim.

The new path keeps the 48-bit result limit, uses arithmetic halving for the full Nat exponent, and skips an unused final square. Regression coverage includes zero-to-zero, wide exponents for zero/one, the largest valid base to power one and an overflowing result. This is an algorithmic lowering improvement, not a request to reopen the deferred general JS stack issue #798.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/aa331dfd
Included in existing PR #1682; no duplicate PR.

title: JS Nat boolean predicates still lower through an intermediate Cmp
body:
Nat.is_lt already lowers to a host comparison, but is_eq, is_ne, is_le, is_gt and is_ge still call Nat.cmp and inspect the resulting Cmp. The generated JS can use the same direct numeric comparison scheme as U32.

I exported one wrapper per predicate and measured all five over 48-bit operand pairs containing less/equal/greater cases. Nine warmed alternating rounds, one million iterations per round: median 169.796 ms before and 150.430 ms after, identical checksum 2,655,265. Linux x64, Bun 1.3.13; baseline is the existing #1682 head 0b82c20. I am not claiming physical allocation counts or a general program speedup.

The patch adds the missing comparison lowerings through the existing operation template. The C expressions use the same operators, and the packed-string/numeric fixture passed on both emitted Bun and native C. Equality and both ordering directions are covered.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/aa331dfd
Included in existing PR #1682; no duplicate PR.

title: JS String.cmp rebuilds both input strings while finding their order
body:
String.cmp returns both original strings along with their order, but its JS Base path recursively reconstructs those strings even though the host representation is immutable text.

For an exported wrapper returning (String & String) & Cmp, I compared two strings with a 256-character common prefix, 100 calls per round. Nine warmed alternating rounds: median 4.771 ms before, 0.140 ms after, with the same LT results and both returned texts unchanged. Linux x64/Bun 1.3.13, existing #1682 head 0b82c20 versus the patch.

The lowering reuses string_compare already in that PR and returns the two original host strings. It does not substitute JS UTF-16 lexical order: full U32 Chars, packed non-scalars and astral characters still use numeric Char order. The updated runtime fixture checks both returned strings through their Char codes, including U+0000, a surrogate, U+10000 and U32 max.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/aa331dfd
Included in existing PR #1682; the earlier String.order/eq reports are not being counted again.

title: JS Map.bit reconstructs the key prefix just to return the unchanged key
body:
Map.bit walks to a requested key bit and reconstructs the traversed String prefix on the way back. The returned key is unchanged, so that reconstruction isn't needed by the JS host representation.

Repro wrapper:

```bend
import Base
def bit(key: String, position: Nat) -> String & Bool:
  Map.bit(key, position)
```

With key = 'x'.repeat(256) + 'q' and position 8480, 1,000 exported calls per round: nine warmed alternating rounds measured 27.712 ms before and 2.444 ms after. The returned key was checked on every call and both boolean sums were 1,000. Linux x64/Bun 1.3.13, existing #1682 head 0b82c20 versus the patch.

The new walk returns the original key and preserves the 33-bit encoding: one presence bit, then 32 U32 bits most-significant first. Oracle checks cover all bit positions in mixed Unicode/NUL keys, EOF and wide Nat positions; the emitted Bun/native C fixture checks packed U32 Chars too. No change to the Base theory or the C path.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/aa331dfd
Included in existing PR #1682.

title: JS Map.msb.u shifts through Base for a bounded U32 bit-width query
body:
Map.msb.u finds a U32's bit width one shift at a time, bounded by its Nat fuel. It is also the bit-width worker used by Map.diff. The JS host has an exact constant-time clz32 primitive for this.

Repro wrapper:

```bend
import Base
def width(fuel: Nat, x: U32) -> Nat:
  Map.msb.u(fuel, x)
```

Nine warmed alternating rounds of 100,000 exported calls over varying U32s/fuel: median 10.386 ms before, 2.859 ms after; checksum 2,064,398 on both. A real consumer call, Map.diff('x', '0'), improved from 14.364 ms to 11.052 ms for 100,000 calls. Linux x64/Bun 1.3.13, baseline #1682 head 0b82c20. No gain is claimed for a long-prefix Map.diff workload, where its separate String walk dominates.

The lowering is min(fuel, 32 - clz32(x)). Independent bit-length checks include zero fuel, zero value, high-bit U32s, truncated fuel and fuel above 2^32. C keeps its existing Base path.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/aa331dfd
Included in existing PR #1682.

title: fix(safe): consume the full shared group prefix
body:
A recursion group can share an argument bound by a returned lambda beyond a member's declared parameters. For `g(n: Nat) -> Nat -> Nat`, the group can consume both `n` and `x` before its selector. `group_emit` previously consumed only the declared `n`. The generated `g` mode still returned `Nat -> Nat`, so `--verdict` rejected the book when the call expected `Nat`.

Consume `max(declared parameters, shared parameters)` when constructing each member's remaining type and body. Require the same lower bound at group calls. This prevents a call from receiving the selector in a missing shared argument slot. Calls that reach `group_call` without the full prefix remain out of scope.

The five tests cover a returned helper lambda, a structural decrease in that lambda's argument, a helper with no declared parameters, a returned lambda in the leading member, and a dependent result. They use a forward law in an erased lambda. All five source programs check and run on main, but their BendTT books fail. This change makes all five pass the unchanged kernel and `--verdict`.

Validation:

- Five regressions pass source checking, `--checkup`, interpretation, JavaScript, C, and the unchanged kernel. Source checking, interpretation, export, kernel checking, and `--verdict` were also rerun on the final branch.
- A local `gates/safe_node.ts` sweep preserves every result across 1,733 existing test, demo, and benchmark files. There are no timeouts or infrastructure errors. Existing rejections remain rejections.
- The repository gate passes 54 / 54. `safe.ts` adds six tokens and uses 23,992 / 24,000 `ttok` tokens.
- TypeScript diagnostics are unchanged from main. The cluster gates have not been run locally.

The patch changes two lines in `safe.ts`. It does not change the source checker or the kernel.

title: test(gates): check comptime C equivalence
body:
## Problem and fix

The comptime twins print the same value, but their documented same-C claim was untested, as noted in [#1314](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1314#issuecomment-6174246623). Compare their emitted C after replacing declared FID names with their numeric IDs, preserving the identifier prefix and every other byte.

Load `hand` and `tmpl` explicitly, once each, in `comptime_run`, before any state-fixture work. A mismatch reports the first differing line number and both normalized C lines, including an end-of-file marker when needed.

## Blast radius

`gates/test.ts` adds the local comparison and updates its comments; `tests/comptime/hand.bend` only corrects its stale report/benchmark comment. The existing four-fixture state sequence, raw output hashes and probe-count checks remain intact. The twins stay outside those repeated compiles and term-normalization steps. Compiler/runtime code, fixture behavior, APIs and token caps are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The original local state check accepts changing the template from `~U32.inc` to `~(x => U32.sub(U32.add(x, 2), 1))`. The revised check rejects its different C and shows both statements at the first differing line. Hand, template and mutant still print `50005000` in source execution, emitted JavaScript under Bun and native C. Unmodified twins and a consistent definition rename pass.

## Checks

- Repository gate: 54/54 locally with CI-pinned ttok 0.3; GitHub `repo-gate` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Actual local gate functions pass healthy/rename controls and reject the same-output mutant. The revision also passes on current main `f5cee564` and rejects that mutant there.
- All 48 prior raw C/JS state observations and post-emission probe counts match the original gate. Tracing confirms each twin loads and validates once, before all state-fixture work.
- Focused comparison controls cover first-line diagnostics, EOF, final-newline/whitespace differences and prefix-preserving FID renames.
- Targeted #1585 (`22764c3`) loader/compiler probe passes with its external namespace/main-alias adaptation and rejects the mutant.
- Project typecheck has the same 11 pre-existing diagnostics as the base, with identical normalized logs and none in this gate.

## Validation limits

Taelin's sign-off on gate placement is still pending, as the [review requests](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1705#pullrequestreview-5572906366); this revision does not claim that approval. Local checks used macOS arm64 and Bun 1.3.11. Full cluster, GPU and performance gates were not rerun for this revision. This checks emitted C text, not machine-code identity or runtime performance. The #1585 probe covers only the adapted parser/compiler dependencies; its existing `safe.ts` merge conflict prevents a full-branch integration claim. Node runtime checks were not rerun.

title: refactor(safe): share BendTT text rendering
body:
`safe.ts` has 14 tokens available below its 24,000-token cap. This refactor puts the recursive term renderer inside `book_show`, so all calls share the selected variable-name prefix. It also shares the `All`/`Sig` format and uses template strings for the fixed output syntax.

With `ttok` 0.3, the file falls from **23,986 to 23,821 tokens**. This saves **165 tokens** and leaves **179 tokens** below the cap. The change is limited to text rendering. It preserves the declaration order, quantity marks, variable names, application order, and output whitespace.

I compared the change with `main` at `e5527d5b`:

- Repository gate: **54/54**.
- All **1,733** files in `tests`, `demos`, and `bench`: identical export results and normal `--verdict` results. All **1,226** emitted books are byte-identical, including partial exports. No timeouts or infrastructure errors occurred. Both versions accept 1,114 files and retain the same rejections.
- **4,806** focused renderer comparisons pass. These cover all 19 term constructors, quantities, nested terms, prefix collisions, and long application chains. Separate checks cover error text and newlines.
- Five checker benchmarks, with 12 alternating pairs per benchmark: median export times range from 1.5% faster to 0.7% slower. Separate renderer measurements range from 7.5% faster to 1.7% slower. These are local measurements on Bun 1.3.14.
- TypeScript reports the same **11 existing errors** on both versions. I did not run the distributed cluster gates.

title: fix(bendtt): distinguish free variables in diagnostics
body:
## Problem and fix

`Term.show` prints every free index as `x0` because natural-number subtraction saturates. For example, `Ctx.fit (Book.of []) [] (Var 1) (Var 0)` reports `expected: x0 / observed: x0` even though the terms differ.

Preserve bound-variable names and print `free[i - d]` when index `i` is outside depth `d`. This isolates the diagnostic portion of [#1448](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1448), following the [maintainer's separate-scope guidance](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1418#issuecomment-6174630681).

## Blast radius

Only the `Var` branch of `Term.show` in `bend2/bendtt.lean` changes (+3/-1). The change affects printing open terms; parser/checker logic, reduction, claims and proofs are untouched. The default `--verdict` kernel cache uses a new source key.

## Regression evidence

Two native Lean harnesses use the actual source's THEORY section and its existing `Ctx.fit`/`Term.check` consumers. The baseline fails the diagnostic guards; this change passes them. The example above now reports `expected: free[0] / observed: free[1]`.

Controls cover distinct free indices, depth-relative shifts, nested binders and rewrite motives. Bound names, successful closed checks and the direct `unbound variable` error remain unchanged.

## Checks

- Full `lean bend2/bendtt.lean` with Lean 4.34.0: passes.
- Native baseline/updated harnesses: updated versions pass all 13 and 9 controls respectively; baseline versions fail the intended diagnostic guards.
- Repository gate: 54/54; `git diff --check` passes.

## Validation limits

The reproduction constructs malformed open terms through the Lean API. Ordinary parsed `.bend`/`.bendtt` CLI reachability has not been established; this is a diagnostic cleanup, not a soundness fix. The native harnesses are private validation, not a new tracked test suite. Checks ran on macOS arm64; full cluster, GPU, performance gates and a full native-kernel CLI corpus were not run.

title: Native Nat.pow still scales with the exponent
body:
On main e5527d5b, an IO program compiled to C still evaluates Nat.pow through Base's recursive definition. The JS work in #1699/#1682 does not change this path. A large exponent spends a multiply and runtime call per step, even for bases 0 and 1.

The C-only patch uses checked repeated squaring. Base's definition and proof behavior are unchanged; multiplication still checks the 48-bit immediate limit, and the unused final square is skipped.

Real behavior proof: the shared fixture below returns checksum 10000 in both arms. Median wall time was 12.202 ms before and 0.891 ms after on this Linux x64 host. This is a bounded local measurement, not a general speed guarantee. Separate compiled C/JS programs cover zero, 3^7, 2^47, the largest immediate at powers 0 and 1, and two overflow boundaries. Native-only smoke inputs also accepted exponents 2^32 and 2^48-1; 2^(2^32) correctly stopped at the Nat wall.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/ba5a8b13e655d7a67fa33812dd03d4c85b98404a

<details><summary>Shared numeric reproducer and paired measurement driver</summary>

Save these as `native-map-power.bend` and `measure.mjs`. Build the same Bend file at main e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c and at the patch commit, naming the binaries `native-map-power-before` and `native-map-power-after`. Run `bun measure.mjs ./native-map-power-before ./native-map-power-after`. The input comes from the environment, not a compile-time constant; every run checks an independent JS oracle. Each arm gets a warmup, then nine fresh-process runs in alternating order, one CPU thread, GPU off. The map-bit case is an unchanged control.

```bend
import Base

def powers(+n: Nat, +seed: U32, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      +u = U32.add(U32.from_nat(p), seed)
      a = U32.to_nat(U32.and(u, 1))
      b = Nat.add(256n, U32.to_nat(U32.mod(u, 128)))
      powers(p, seed, U32.add(acc, U32.from_nat(Nat.pow(a, b))))

def bit_result(pair: String & Bool) -> String & U32:
  (key, b) = pair
  (key, Bool.to_u32(b))

def bit_add(pair: String & U32, acc: U32) -> String & U32:
  (key, b) = pair
  (key, U32.add(acc, b))

def bits(+n: Nat, pair: String & U32, +seed: U32) -> String & U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      pair
    case 1n+p:
      match pair:
        case Tuple{key, acc}:
          +u = U32.add(U32.from_nat(p), seed)
          pos = Nat.add(Nat.mul(U32.to_nat(U32.mod(u, 257)), 33n), 32n)
          bits(p, bit_add(bit_result(Map.bit(key, pos)), acc), seed)

def widths(+n: Nat, +seed: U32, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      +u = U32.add(U32.mul(U32.from_nat(p), 2654435761), seed)
      fuel = U32.to_nat(U32.mod(U32.from_nat(p), 40))
      v = U32.from_nat(Map.msb.u(fuel, u))
      widths(p, seed, U32.add(acc, v))

def logs(+n: Nat, +seed: U32, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      u = U32.add(U32.mul(U32.from_nat(p), 2654435761), seed)
      logs(p, seed, U32.add(acc, U32.from_nat(U32.log2(u))))

def print_bits(pair: String & U32) -> IO(Unit):
  (key, total) = pair
  do IO<Unit>:
    u : Unit <- IO.print(U32.show(total))
    IO.print(key)

def work(kind: Nat, seed: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  match kind:
    case 0n:
      IO.print(U32.show(powers(20000n, seed, 0)))
    case 1n:
      print_bits(bits(1000n, (String.append(String.repeat("x", 256n), "q"), 0), seed))
    case 2n:
      IO.print(U32.show(widths(1000000n, seed, 0)))
    case 1n+rest:
      IO.print(U32.show(logs(1000000n, seed, 0)))

def parsed(m: Maybe<&2, Nat>) -> IO(Unit):
  match m:
    case None{}:
      IO.print("invalid input")
    case Some{n}:
      +n = n
      work(Nat.mod(n, 4n), U32.from_nat(Nat.div(n, 4n)))

def read_input(r: Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match r:
    case Fail{error}:
      IO.print("missing input")
    case Done{value}:
      parsed(Nat.read(value))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    r : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, String> <- IO.get_env("BEND_BENCH_INPUT")
    read_input(r)
```

```javascript
import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
const paths=process.argv.slice(2),names=['power','map-bit','map-width','u32-log2'],seed=7;
const expected=[0,0,0,0];
for(let p=0;p<20000;p++){const u=(p+seed)>>>0;expected[0]=(expected[0]+Math.pow(u&1,256+u%128))>>>0;}
const key='x'.repeat(256)+'q';
for(let p=0;p<1000;p++)expected[1]+=key.charCodeAt(((p+seed)>>>0)%257)&1;
for(let p=0;p<1000000;p++){const x=(Math.imul(p,2654435761)+seed)>>>0;expected[2]=(expected[2]+Math.min(p%40,32-Math.clz32(x)))>>>0;}
for(let p=0;p<1000000;p++){const x=(Math.imul(p,2654435761)+seed)>>>0;expected[3]=(expected[3]+(x===0?0:31-Math.clz32(x)))>>>0;}
const result={};
for(let k=0;k<4;k++){
 const samples=[[],[]];
 const run=i=>{const t=performance.now();const r=spawnSync(paths[i],['--threads','1','--gpu','off'],{env:{...process.env,BEND_BENCH_INPUT:String(seed*4+k)},encoding:'utf8',timeout:30000});const elapsed=performance.now()-t;assert.equal(r.status,0,r.stderr);const lines=r.stdout.trim().split('\n');assert.equal(lines[0],String(expected[k]));if(k===1)assert.equal(lines[1],key);else assert.equal(lines.length,1);return elapsed;};
 for(let i=0;i<2;i++)run(i);
 for(let round=0;round<9;round++)for(const i of round%2?[1,0]:[0,1])samples[i].push(run(i));
 const beforeMs=[...samples[0]].sort((a,b)=>a-b)[4],afterMs=[...samples[1]].sort((a,b)=>a-b)[4];
 result[names[k]]={checksum:expected[k],beforeMs,afterMs,ratio:beforeMs/afterMs,samplesMs:samples};
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(result,null,2));
```
</details>

title: Native Map.msb.u walks the bits of each U32 query
body:
The C backend on e5527d5b still runs Map.msb.u's recursive Base body: shift until zero or fuel exhaustion. #1703/#1682 cover the JS backend, not this one.

The native patch computes the U32 width with CLZ and limits it by the original Nat fuel. Zero input and zero fuel both return zero; fuel is not narrowed to U32. No change to Base or the checker.

Real behavior proof: the shared reproducer in https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1708 runs one million data-dependent queries. Both builds returned 18575001; nine alternating runs measured median 31.207 ms before and 2.371 ms after. Compiled C and JS boundary programs also agree at fuel 0/1/31/32/99 and U32 values 0/1/2^31/2^32-1.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/ba5a8b13e655d7a67fa33812dd03d4c85b98404a

title: Native U32.log2 retains the Base bit search in numeric folds
body:
On e5527d5b, U32.log2 has no C intrinsic. Numeric folds keep the Base bit search instead of using the backend's existing CLZ operation. #1688/#1682 are the JS-specific work.

The native expression is 31 - CLZ(x | 1), so log2(0) stays 0 and there is no undefined zero-input CLZ. Base's Nat-valued result and checked definition stay unchanged.

Real behavior proof: the shared fixture in https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1708 returns 29999970 in both arms for one million changing U32 values. Nine alternating CPU runs measured medians 2.825 ms before and 1.579 ms after. The permanent C/JS program checks zero, adjacent small powers, 2^31-1, 2^31 and 2^32-1.

Patch: https://github.com/oxura/bend/commit/ba5a8b13e655d7a67fa33812dd03d4c85b98404a

title: A function used only through foreign FID is not emitted
CID scanning rewrites suffixes of legal host identifiers
Use checked native paths for Nat powers and bit widths
body:
This adds C paths for Map.msb.u and U32.log2. Base, the checker and the JS backend are unchanged: a JS file runs Base's defs, as intr_of skips an op with no JS.

Map.msb.u computes the U32 width with CLZ, capped by the Nat fuel; zero fuel or zero input return 0. U32.log2 is 31 - CLZ(x | 1), so log2(0) stays 0. Map.msb.u sits on Map.diff.chr, the per-character step of string key comparison.

| Native workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Map.msb.u fold | 31.207 ms | 2.371 ms |
| U32.log2 fold | 2.825 ms | 1.579 ms |

(Linux x64, nine-pair medians; fixture in #1708.)

tests/run/native_numeric_boundaries.bend checks zero, bit boundaries and fuel 0/1/31/32/99 on every lane.

The Nat.pow native was dropped in review: any base >= 2 hits the 48-bit Nat wall by exponent 47, so Base's linear def already takes at most 48 steps, and nothing outside tests calls it.

title: Keep foreign-only functions reachable and preserve host identifier boundaries
body:
C effects can call functions that Bend never calls, or calls just once. Keep a native entry for those FID references instead of dropping or fusing it away. This rooting is C-only; JS FID stays a name string.

Host identifiers and JS private names stay untouched, without breaking C token pasting. Your d48dfb36 merge is included, and the guide prose is out.

All three fixtures pass --checkup, the interpreter, emitted JS and native C locally. Repo: 54/54. No private-cluster run claimed.

Fixes #1711
Fixes #1712

title: perf(c): lower Nat.pow, U32.log2 and Map.msb.u to native C intrinsics
body:
Resolves #1708, #1709, #1710

## The problem

On `main`, the C lane still evaluates these through Base's recursive definitions:

- `Nat.pow` scales with the exponent (a multiply and runtime call per step, even for bases 0 and 1).
- `U32.log2` keeps the Base bit search in numeric folds.
- `Map.msb.u` walks the bits of each U32 query.

The JS lane is unchanged (it runs Base's definitions); only the C lane gains native paths.

## The fix (`bend2/comp.ts`)

Three C-only intrinsics added to `OPERATIONS` (JS runs Base's), plus their C implementations in `NATIVE.C`:

- `u32_log2: { C: "(31 - CLZ((u32)$0 | 1))" }` — `log2(0)` stays 0, no undefined CLZ.
- `nat_pow: { C: "nat_pow(e, $0, $1)" }` — checked repeated squaring, using `nat_mul` so the 48-bit immediate wall is checked (no u64 wrap); the unused final square is skipped.
- `map_msb_u: { C: "map_msb_u($0, $1)" }` — CLZ-based width, clamped by the original Nat fuel; zero input / zero fuel return 0; fuel is not narrowed to U32.

GUIDE.md updated to mention the native scalar paths. Three run-lane tests added with the exact expected outputs (boundary values, two overflow cases).

## Verification

- `--check-only` on all three new tests: `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- C lane (gcc 16, `-std=c11 -O1`): `native_numeric_boundaries` prints all 23 expected lines; `nat_power_overflow` / `nat_power_wide_overflow` print `bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1` and exit 1.
- JS lane on `small_num.bend` (3 values) agrees with C: `2187 / 31 / 31`.
- Full `tests/**.bend --check-only` sweep (1661 files), before vs after: byte-identical — 588 pre-existing failures both ways, **0 new, 0 changed.**
- `comp.ts` token count: 64,561 → still under the 66,000 cap (headroom 1,439).
- JS behavior unchanged (Base's definitions run on JS), so existing JS-lane tests are unaffected.

## Notes

- The intrinsics are C-only by design, matching the existing `u32_pow` pattern (`intr_of` skips an op with no JS). JS continues to use Base's recursive definitions.
- Test expected outputs and boundary cases follow the behavior proofs in the linked issues (zero, adjacent small powers, 2^31-1, 2^31, 2^32-1, fuel 0/1/31/32/99, and two overflow boundaries).
- This change is credited to the analysis in #1708/#1709/#1710 (oxura).
