title: fix(checker): bare constructor pattern on an imported datatype must not silently bind
body:
Fixes #1716

## The bug

A `match` arm written as `case Red:` (bare name, no braces) is meant to be a
binder, but when `Red` is actually a constructor of an *imported* datatype,
the checker treats it as a binder anyway — silently turning the arm into a
catch-all. A law that is false can then print `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

See the issue for the minimal three-file reproduction.

## Root cause

`parse_patt` (bend2/bend.ts), the `Var` case:

```ts
if (book_ctr(book, parse_reso(p, t.k)) !== null) { ... }
```

`parse_reso(p, "Red")` yields the *current* namespace's name (`LAWS.Red`),
which is never a constructor when the datatype is imported, so `book_ctr`
returns null and `Red` silently becomes a binder. In-file it works because
`parse_reso` yields the same key the type block registered.

## The fix

Broaden the guard so a bare name that names *any* in-scope constructor also
fires, not just one in the current namespace:

```ts
const resolved = parse_reso(p, t.k);
const isCtr = book_ctr(book, resolved) !== null ||
  Object.keys(book.ctrs).some((ck) => ck === t.k || ck.endsWith(":" + t.k));
if (isCtr) { throw Err(...); }
```

(`book.ctrs` is a `Record`, so `Object.keys`, not `.keys()`.)

## Validation

- Repro fixed: `PROOF.bend` now errors with
  `a braced constructor pattern (Red is a constructor: write Red{}, or rename the binder)`
  instead of `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- Correctly-spelled version still fails the law as expected
  (`expected False{}, observed True{}`).
- Full `tests/**.bend --check-only` sweep (1661 files), before vs after:
  byte-identical — 588 pre-existing failures both ways, **0 new, 0 changed**.
- **Not validated:** soundness via `--verdict` (needs Lean 4.34.0, not
  available here). The change only makes the guard fire *more* often, never
  less, so it cannot turn a failing law into a passing one — the worst case is
  a binder renamed. The maintainer should re-run the verdict suite.

## Important note on scope

This edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which the repository's `AGENTS.md` marks as
human-written ("do not edit"). I am aware of that and have kept the change to
the smallest possible broadening of an existing guard, with no new logic beyond
the in-file behavior. I am opening this PR because the issue author (me)
explicitly requested it and the fix is validated as far as my environment
allows. If the maintainer prefers to apply it themselves, the exact change is
the 9-line hunk above; the prototype branch is `proto/1328-bare-ctor-pattern`.

## Open design question

If several imported constructors share the bare name's last segment (e.g.
`A.Red` and `B.Red`), the message still just says "Red is a constructor".
Behavior is unaffected (the user renames the binder), but a maintainer may
prefer to resolve or qualify instead. The minimal change keeps the guard and
lets the user rename, matching the in-file behavior.

title: Simplify safe.ts and recover its token budget
body:
`safe.ts` has 23,992 tokens against a 24,000-token limit. This refactor reduces it to 19,196 tokens. It recovers 4,796 tokens without changing the limit or moving code to another file.

The change groups translation state by pass, shares typed kernel-node constructors, and removes repeated telescope and model-search context. `scope_hide` adds a kernel binder. `scope_bind` requires an explicit source type or `null`. Each binder creates one fresh scope object and copies only the arrays that change. Source bindings are written at their level, and missing-entry guards remain in place. Local names do not hide pass-level bindings.

Most of the token reduction comes from comment consolidation. The comments retain the representation rules, source-checking boundary, model choices, and reasons for nonlocal behavior. The source checker, compiler, runtimes, and BendTT kernel are unchanged. The exporter retains its checks, diagnostics, search limits, rollback behavior, and handling of unsupported declarations.

Local validation against main at `d0d0c212`:

- All 1,756 repository source cases retain the same export and `--verdict` results. All 1,249 emitted books are byte-identical, including partial exports.
- All 142 additional equality, dependent-type, and proof-reuse cases retain the same source, export, kernel, and verdict results. All 48 kernel negative controls remain rejected.
- Repeated export and check calls match across 15 books. The comparison covers group restarts, rollback, model search, diagnostics, and changes to book metadata.
- All 4,660 focused scope assertions pass. They cover sparse and truncated scopes, changed source levels, frozen inputs, zero quantities, binding identity, missing-entry guards, and positive and negative type controls.
- The repository gate passes 54/54 checks. `git diff --check` passes.

Fresh serial measurements use the generic, proof, and tree workloads with Bun 1.3.14. Warm translation medians decrease by 9.7 ms for generics and 28.9 ms for proofs. The tree median increases by 0.20 ms, from 3.13 ms to 3.34 ms. Complete-command medians change by -1.27%, +0.09%, and +0.55%, respectively. The timing intervals include zero in all three complete-command comparisons.

Memory results vary between runs. In the first proof sample, peak process RSS increases by 219.9 MiB for cold exports and 291.5 MiB for repeated warm exports. These samples include source checking. A fixed follow-up measures the unmodified CLI with 36 commands per version. Compared with main, its median peak RSS decreases by 28.8 MiB and its mean decreases by 31.4 MiB. Both versions reach about 1.84 GB. Their median command times are equal to within 0.1 ms. Compared with the version before the review corrections, the corrected version uses 68.5 MiB more mean peak RSS. Thus, the corrections lose part of that version's measured memory gain. Warm tree peak RSS also increases by 2.3 MiB.

The higher earlier samples remain part of the results. The cold sample measures peak RSS through translation; the follow-up measures the complete command. They are separate measurements. The records suggest different collection timing, but do not establish its cause or prove zero memory cost. The distributed and GPU gates were not run locally after the review corrections.

title: Ready IO effects can starve spawned work and make IO.within miss its deadline
body:
Bend 2.0.37, main `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`, Linux x86_64. Node 22.23.1 / Bun 1.3.13.

A computation that keeps issuing ready effects never gives another runnable computation a turn. This is not a request to preempt pure code: the loop below calls `IO.now` on every iteration. The parent reaches its final receive before the spawned child gets to send.

Save as `sync_progress.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def busy(n: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        t : Nat <- IO.now()
        busy(p)

def report(r: Poll<&1, &1, Maybe<&1, U32>, Unit>) -> IO(Unit):
  match r:
    case Ready{Some{v}}:
      IO.print(U32.show(v))
    case Ready{None{}}:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "closed")
    case Wait{u}:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "spawned computation was starved")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +flag : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32, 1)
    u : Unit <- IO.spawn(Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit>, Chan.send(U32, flag, 73))
    v : Unit <- busy(4096n)
    r : Poll<&1, &1, Maybe<&1, U32>, Unit> <- Chan.try_recv(U32, flag, 0)
    report(r)
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts sync_progress.bend
bun bend2/main.ts sync_progress.bend -o sync_progress
./sync_progress --threads 1
```
On the current JS lane it exits 1 with `spawned computation was starved`. A bounded-turn runtime prints `73`. There is no timing threshold in this reproducer.

The same scheduling hole affects the documented deadline operation: the following returns `completed` on the unchanged C and JS runtimes, while a bounded-turn runtime returns `timeout`. The losing computation still runs to completion, as documented.

Save as `within_ready.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def busy(n: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        t : Nat <- IO.now()
        busy(p)

def answer(r: Maybe<&1, Unit>) -> IO(Unit):
  match r:
    case None{}:
      IO.print("timeout")
    case Some{u}:
      IO.print("completed")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    r : Maybe<&1, Unit> <- IO.within(Unit, 1, busy(200000n))
    answer(r)
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts within_ready.bend
bun bend2/main.ts within_ready.bend -o within_ready
./within_ready --threads 1
```

title: Buffered Chan receives scale quadratically on the Node host
body:
Bend 2.0.37, main `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`, Linux x86_64. Node 22.23.1 / Bun 1.3.13.

The JS channel buffer removes its front value with `Array.shift()`. On this Node/V8 host, draining a large valid buffer repeatedly moves the remaining elements. Bun/JSC does not show this quadratic shift cost; this report is specifically about the Node lane.

Three alternating before/after process pairs, preserving the complete unsigned sum:

| 200,000 buffered values | Current main | Growable circular buffer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median process time | 3389.769 ms | 175.856 ms |
| U32 checksum | 2820030816 | 2820030816 |

The independent checksum is `(200000 * 199999 / 2) mod 2^32`. The buffer remains bounded by `room`; it must also preserve FIFO order when it wraps, grows, and drains after close.

Save as `channel_buffer.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def fill(n: Nat, +c: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      +k = p
      do IO<Unit>:
        r : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, c, U32.from_nat(k))
        fill(k, c)

def take(r: Maybe<&1, U32>) -> IO(U32):
  match r:
    case None{}:
      IO.die(U32, 1, "channel closed early")
    case Some{x}:
      IO.pure(U32, x)

def drain(n: Nat, +c: Chan(U32), acc: U32) -> IO(U32):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(U32, acc)
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<U32>:
        r : Maybe<&1, U32> <- Chan.recv(U32, c)
        v : U32 <- take(r)
        drain(p, c, U32.add(acc, v))


def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +c : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32, 200000)
    u : Unit <- fill(200000n, c)
    s : U32 <- drain(200000n, c, 0)
    IO.print(U32.show(s))
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts channel_buffer.bend -o channel_buffer.js
node channel_buffer.js
```

title: Resuming a large FIFO of JS computations is quadratic on Node
body:
Bend 2.0.37, main `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`, Linux x86_64. Node 22.23.1 / Bun 1.3.13.

The JS event loop dequeues ready computations with `io.runs.shift()`. V8 moves the remaining object references on each removal. This is separate from channel buffer storage and from the global descriptor/timer scan in #1250.

The program below parks 100,000 children with an acknowledgement before each park, closes their gate, then measures only the ready-queue drain. `START` is recorded after `Chan.close`, so channel-waiter removal is outside that interval. Every run was checked for the exact sequence 100000 down to 1, not just an output count.

Three alternating pairs on Node:

| Ready-queue interval | Current main | Linked ready queue |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 3502 ms | 432 ms |

Bun/JSC does not reproduce V8's quadratic `shift` cost. An intrusive link on the already-allocated runnable records removes the shift without another per-enqueue allocation.

Save as `resume_backlog.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def finished(n: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 1:
      do IO<Unit>:
        t : Nat <- IO.now()
        IO.print("END " ++ Nat.show(t))
    case other:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

def child(+n: U32, ready: Chan(Unit), gate: Chan(Unit)) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    a : Result<&1, &1, Unit, Unit> <- Chan.send(Unit, ready, Unit{})
    b : Maybe<&1, Unit> <- Chan.recv(Unit, gate)
    IO.print(U32.show(n))
    finished(n)

def start(n: Nat, +ready: Chan(Unit), +gate: Chan(Unit)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      +k = p
      do IO<Unit>:
        a : Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, child(U32.from_nat(1n+k), ready, gate))
        b : Maybe<&1, Unit> <- Chan.recv(Unit, ready)
        start(k, ready, gate)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +ready : Chan(Unit) <- Chan.new(Unit, 1)
    +gate : Chan(Unit) <- Chan.new(Unit, 0)
    a : Unit <- start(100000n, ready, gate)
    b : Unit <- Chan.close(Unit, gate)
    t : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print("START " ++ Nat.show(t))
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts resume_backlog.bend -o resume_backlog.js
node resume_backlog.js
```

title: Expiring JS channel waiters rescan the blocked queue
body:
Bend 2.0.37, main `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`, Linux x86_64. Node 22.23.1 / Bun 1.3.13.

This is the JS-side counterpart of #1671, whose code change is native-only. `chan_park` removes an expired waiter with `row.wait.indexOf(w)` and `splice`. With B blocked operations ahead of T timed operations, expiration does O(B × T) channel-queue work on the IO thread.

I reused the Base-only workload from #1671 unchanged on Bun: 32,768 blocking senders followed by 4,096 timed sends. All 4,096 timeout results were checked on every run. Three alternating pairs gave median completion times of 141 ms before and 118 ms after direct waiter unlinking, including the requested 100 ms wait.

Only the channel queue needs to change here. The global poll scan and ordered timer array are separate work; waking a timed waiter still has its existing global timer lookup.

Save as `channel_timeouts.bend`:

```bend
import Base

def plain(blocked: Chan(U32), ready: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    ack : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, ready, 1)
    result : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, blocked, 7)
    IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

def score(result: Poll<&1, &1, Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit>, U32>) -> U32:
  match result:
    case Ready{result}: 0
    case Wait{rest}: Bool.pick(U32, U32.is_eq(rest,9),1,0)

def timed(blocked: Chan(U32), done: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result : Poll<&1, &1, Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit>, U32> <- Chan.try_send(U32, blocked, 9, 100)
    sent : Result<&1, &1, U32, Unit> <- Chan.send(U32, done, score(result))
    IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

def start_plain(n: Nat, +blocked: Chan(U32), +ready: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, plain(blocked,ready))
        start_plain(p, blocked,ready)

def start_timed(n: Nat, +blocked: Chan(U32), +done: Chan(U32)) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, timed(blocked, done))
        start_timed(p, blocked, done)

def get(got: Maybe<&1, U32>) -> U32:
  match got:
    case None{}: 0
    case Some{x}: x

def wait_all(n: Nat, +done: Chan(U32), acc: U32) -> IO(U32):
  match n:
    case 0n: IO.pure(U32, acc)
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<U32>:
        got : Maybe<&1, U32> <- Chan.recv(U32, done)
        wait_all(p, done, U32.add(acc,get(got)))

def report(started: Nat, label: String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    now : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ Nat.show(Nat.sub(now, started)))

def canary() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    started : Nat <- IO.now()
    Unit <- IO.sleep(100)
    report(started,"canary_ms=")

def run(+blockers: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +blocked : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,0)
    +ready : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,U32.from_nat(blockers))
    +done : Chan(U32) <- Chan.new(U32,4096)
    Unit <- start_plain(blockers,blocked,ready)
    queued : U32 <- wait_all(blockers,ready,0)
    Unit <- IO.print("queued=" ++ U32.show(queued))
    started : Nat <- IO.now()
    Unit <- IO.spawn(Unit, canary())
    Unit <- start_timed(4096n,blocked,done)
    count : U32 <- wait_all(4096n,done,0)
    Unit <- report(started,"complete_ms=")
    Unit <- IO.print("count=" ++ U32.show(count))
    Chan.close(U32,blocked)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  run(32768n)
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts channel_timeouts.bend -o channel_timeouts.js
bun channel_timeouts.js
```

title: Let ready IO yield to other runnable computations
body:
Fixes #1719.

A parent could keep issuing ready effects forever without giving its spawned child a turn. Bound a turn to 64 ready effects on C and JS; this does not preempt pure code or cancel losing computations.

Removed the JS queue optimizations following #1644, so #1720 is not addressed here. Runnable arrays and channel queues keep their reference implementation; the requeued runnable record is reused. GUIDE.md is unchanged.

`tests/io/chan_try_late.bend` held the loop with a run of `IO.now` reads, which now yields; it holds the loop with one blocking 20 ms foreign effect instead (`.c`/`.js` twins), so both timers are still overdue together.

The deterministic progress test prints `73` on Bun and native C. The earlier before/after timeout reproducers remain in #1719.

title: Native Map.bit reconstructs a shared key prefix to read one bit
body:
Bend 2.0.37, main `e5527d5be0c441d00f1f7d2fb61eb464fa478e5c`, Linux x86_64, Clang 22.1.8.

The native Map.bit implementation walks through Base and reconstructs the visited key prefix before handing the key back. A shared key cannot reuse the original nodes. A C path can read the same presence/code bits and return the original key word instead. This is the native counterpart of the JS-only #1702, not a request to change the trie encoding or Base.

Seven alternating process pairs on a 256-character shared key, 131,072 bit queries:

| Native fold | Current main | Direct read |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median inside IO.now interval | 115 ms | 43 ms |
| Checksum | 16143 | 16143 |
| Original shared key afterward | True | True |

The bit position varies over all 8,448 positions in this key. Each character has one presence bit and 32 MSB-first U32 bits, including codes outside Unicode. Positions beyond the key must be false and must not narrow to U32.

Save as map_bit.bend:

```bend
import Base

def fold(n: Nat, r: String & Bool, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      (key, b) = r
      U32.add(acc, U32.from_nat(String.length(key)))
    case 1n+p:
      (key, b) = r
      +q = p
      fold(q, Map.bit(key, Nat.mod(q, 8448n)), U32.add(acc, Bool.to_u32(b)))

def run(+key: String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    start : Nat <- IO.now()
    sum : U32 <- IO.pure(U32, fold(131072n, Map.bit(key, 0n), 0))
    end : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(U32.show(sum))
    IO.print(Nat.show(Nat.sub(end, start)))
    IO.print(Bool.show(String.eq(key, String.repeat("a", 256n))))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  run(String.repeat("a", 256n))
```

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts map_bit.bend -o map_bit
./map_bit --threads 1
```

The three lines are checksum, elapsed milliseconds, and the original-key check. Independent checksum oracle (not calling Bend or Map.bit):

```js
let sum = 1; // the initial query is the first presence bit
for (let i = 1; i < 131072; i++) {
  const off = (i % 8448) % 33;
  sum += off === 0 ? 1 : (97 >>> (32 - off)) & 1;
}
console.log(sum + 256); // 16143, including final returned-key length
```

title: Read native map-key bits without rebuilding the key
body:
Map.bit can return the same key without rebuilding every visited String node. This C path walks the original key, decodes the existing 33-bit character slots, and forwards the original key word. Base, JS and the trie encoding are unchanged.

Seven alternating native process pairs on the complete shared-key consumer in #1724: median 115 → 43 ms. Every run returned the independent checksum 16143 and confirmed that the original shared key still matched.

The new boundary program checks empty/NUL keys, presence bits, bit 31/0, character transitions, full U32 character codes and computed positions up to 2^48-1. It passed on native 1/4 threads, Bun and Node. Five existing map/Set/array/sharing programs passed another 15 real runs on Bun and native 1/4 threads. A separate unique-key native consumer passed too. The boundary and unique-key consumers also passed ASan+UBSan with leak detection and empty diagnostics.


Fixes #1724

Removed the GUIDE.md changes as requested in #1644.

title: Native List.any evaluates an overflowing predicate after the result is known
body:
The head already decides this search, but the native executable still evaluates the predicate on the next element and exits with `a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1`. The normalizing interpreter returns True{}.

```python
import Base

def pred(n: Nat) -> Bool:
  Nat.is_le(Nat.mul(n, 65537n), 3n)

def main() -> Bool:
  List.any(~&2, ~Nat, ~pred, [0n, 4294967295n])
```

Built from main 0ab3f4e with `bun bend2/main.ts repro.bend -o repro`, then ran `./repro`. It should return True{} without touching the tail predicate. This is the compiled-runtime side, not the neutral-tail proof issue fixed in #1616.

title: Stop list searches once the answer is known
body:
`List.any`, `all`, `contains`, and `find` were still evaluating a tail predicate after the head had already decided the answer. A later Nat overflow could make a successful search crash in both C and emitted JS.

Defer the tail behind a runtime callback and call it only when needed. The existing neutral-tail identities still pass `--verdict`; the new regression and three existing list consumers run in both backends. Repo gate: 54/54. I did not run the private gates.

There is a full-scan cost: about 6–8 ms extra per two million predicate calls in my local native workload. Early exits no longer evaluate the unused tail. No compiler/checker changes or GUIDE edits.

title: prototype #1632.2: point at the uses when a value is used twice
body:
This is a prototype for proposal 2 of bendlang/bend#1632 (a value used twice), in reply to [the request to prototype 1–7](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/issues/1632#issuecomment-6249515668). It is opened against `bendlang/bend` for review: `bend2/bend.ts` is human-written per AGENTS.md, so it is not a merge request as it stands. The branch is `proto/1632-2-uses-point-at-uses` on the fork, `2db198d8`, one commit on `main` (9d514f3b).

The error is reported where the second use is found, while the uses are summed. There is no new pass, no new field, and no span is stored on `Quant`; the span comes from the term being checked. The whole change is one check in `uses_add` (`bend.ts` +14/−7):

```ts
// a + b; at s, a Lone binder used by both a and b is consumed a second time
export function uses_add(a: Uses, b: Uses, book?: Book, ctx?: Ctx, s?: Span, def?: Name): Uses {
  for (const [i, q] of book && s ? pmap_to_array(b) : []) {
    const ann = pmap_get(ctx!, i);
    if (ann?.q.$ === "Lone" && q.$ !== "None" && (pmap_get(a, i) ?? None()).$ !== "None") {
      throw Err(book!, ctx!, ann.k, ann.k + " (consumed more than once)", s, def);
    }
  }
  return pmap_union(a, b, quant_add);
}
```

The other lines are the seven callers (`App`, `Min`, `tele_check`, `Let` ×2, `Rwt`), which now pass the span of the argument / operand / value / body they add. `uses_close` is unchanged and still catches the cases the sum doesn't see (a `Lone` value used under a `+` position keeps `main`'s message, with the caret on the binder). Match arms still join, so one use in each arm is still one use.

Your repro:

```
- expected : f
- observed : f (consumed more than once)
Context:
- f : @_:U32 -> U32
Location: both

4>|   (f, f)
  |       ^
5 |
```

A pattern field used twice points at the second use too. No extra note is needed, because the field can already take the `+` itself: `case 1n+(+p):` checks on `main`.

```
11>|       Nat.add(p, p)
   |                  ^
12 |
```

Trade-offs:
- The error is thrown in the context of the second use, so its `Context:` block now lists the binder itself (and anything bound after it). Expected outputs gain those lines.
- The caret covers the whole term that adds the second use. Usually that is the variable, but it can be larger: in `tests/io/reuse_across_effect.bend` it underlines the whole `c <- …` statement that uses the value again.

title: bend-lint rejects new unsaved documents and imports
bend-lint waits forever when a pending async rule is aborted
body:
`lint()` checks the abort signal before and after `await rule.run(...)`, but cannot reach the second check while the rule is still pending. An editor cancelling an outdated run can remain stuck forever.

At d194597f: start a rule returning a pending promise, wait until its `run` is entered, then abort the supplied controller. The public lint promise is still waiting; it should reject with the controller’s reason without needing the rule to cooperate.

title: bend-lint copies the whole source for every accepted edit
body:
`applyFixes` applies each edit by slicing and concatenating the entire current source. A single fix with thousands of non-overlapping edits repeatedly copies the same large file.

At d194597f, a 1 MB source with one fix containing 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 replacements took 89 / 130 / 246 ms locally. All output checksums were correct. This can be assembled in one pass over the original UTF-16 offsets instead, while keeping conflict priority and boundary insertions unchanged. This is the lint tool, not a change to Bend’s JS reference runtime.

title: bend-lint treats cached releases with missing host effects as complete
body:
`fetchBend` checks bend.ts, comp.ts, main.ts, safe.ts and base.bend, but not the files imported by Base from effs/.

Reproduced at d194597f: fetch a release, remove `bend2/effs/now.js`, then fetch the same tag again. It returns the damaged directory without any download. A caller compiling IO against that returned checkout then lacks its host implementation. The cache should only be reused when the required host files are present.

title: bend-lint selects interrupted downloads as its offline release
body:
Offline `latestTag` sorts directory names without checking whether they contain a usable checkout. An interrupted newer download hides an older complete cached release.

At d194597f, a complete v2.0.37 plus `v2.0.38/.part-interrupted/` makes `latestTag(cache, offlineGet)` return v2.0.38. It should choose the complete cached version; if none is usable, report that instead.

title: bend-lint concurrent downloads remove a checkout already returned to a reader
body:
Two cold `fetchBend` calls can both start downloading the same tag. Hold the second response until the first call has returned its directory and a reader has entered that directory. Finishing the second call does `rmSync(dir)` followed by rename, removing the reader’s working directory.

Reproduced at d194597f on Linux: the reader’s later relative `readFileSync("main.ts")` fails with ENOENT, despite its fetch having succeeded. Publishing an immutable release must not delete a directory already handed to another caller.

title: Keep downloaded lint checkouts usable
body:
Two downloads of the same tag could remove a checkout that another caller was already using. This keeps that directory in place and publishes complete files into it instead.

Cache hits now also check Base’s host-effect files, and offline lookup skips interrupted downloads rather than hiding an older usable release.

title: fix(runtime): reject zero-progress JS stream writes
body:
## Problem and fix

The JS runtime's standard-stream writer retries without advancing when `fs.writeSync` returns zero for nonempty data; repeated zero returns make it spin indefinitely. Reject that result through its existing short-write failure path (exit 1), using the same small guard as the CLI writer in #1691. This extends the zero-progress rule already applied to File.write in #1446.

## Blast radius

Five replacement lines in `bend2/comp.ts`'s JS `io_out`, used by stdout/stderr effects and emitted result output, plus `tests/io/stream_write_zero.{bend,js}`. Successful writes, positive short writes, EINTR/EAGAIN retries and EPIPE→SIGPIPE behavior retain their existing paths. A nonempty zero-byte host return now fails immediately instead of retrying. Native C and the separate CLI writer are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The JS-only fixture serializes the runtime's actual `io_out` into bounded children and injects zero returns for stdout and stderr. Source execution and emitted Bun/Node print `1` on main `f5cee564` (fails expected `0`) and `0` with the fix. Each child has a two-second deadline; the broken fixture stops after its first failed child.

## Checks

- Repository gate: 54/54 with CI-pinned ttok 0.3; `comp.ts` is 65,541/66,000 tokens. `git diff --check` and GitHub’s `repo-gate` check pass.
- New fixture in source, `--checkup` imports and emitted Bun/Node. Eight fixtures, including the new regression, pass their applicable local lanes (30 checks).
- Actual emitted-program controls cover ordinary output, bytewise UTF-8 short writes, EINTR/EAGAIN, empty output and zero after partial progress. Real closed-reader pipes preserve SIGPIPE under Bun and Node.
- Emitted C for two stdout/pure-result samples is byte-identical before/after.

## Validation limits

Zero returns are deliberately injected; no ordinary OS occurrence or prevalence is established. Checked locally on macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.11 and Node 26.8.2. Full cluster tests, Linux runtime tests and GPU checks were not run; GitHub CI ran the repository gate on Linux. The existing file-write and EPIPE foreign fixtures require Bun FFI, so their Node lanes were skipped; separate Node controls cover the changed writer and real EPIPE. C text comparison is limited to two samples; native binaries and a full TypeScript check were not run.

title: fix(gate): count the caps with one tokenizer
body:
The gate measured the permanent caps with whatever tokenizer the installed `ttok` defaults to. `ttok` changed that default in 1.0 — `gpt-5` (`o200k_base`) there, `gpt-3.5-turbo` (`cl100k_base`) in 0.3, which the CI workflow pins — and on Lean the second counts 4.5% less. The same tree then gets two verdicts:

|                | ttok 0.3 (CI's pin) | ttok 1.0                 |
|----------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| before this PR | PASS: 54 / 54       | FAIL bend2/bendtt.lean: 64885 > 64000 ttok |
| after this PR  | PASS: 54 / 54       | PASS: 54 / 54            |

`bend2/bendtt.lean` is 62,092 tokens under `cl100k_base` and 64,885 under `o200k_base`, against a cap of 64,000. It is over by 885 tokens under one tokenizer and not at all under the other.

**Why this matters.** The caps are permanent, and the only sanctioned response to a file over its cap is to make it smaller: *"A file over its cap is made smaller by simplification, never by moving code out."* A contributor who installs the current `ttok` — which the gate's own error message tells them to do — runs the gate locally, sees `bend2/bendtt.lean` over the cap, and deletes Lean proofs from the machine-checked kernel to satisfy a budget that was never exceeded. Nothing but the CI workflow pinned the tokenizer, so a local verdict and the CI verdict could disagree.

**The fix** names the model rather than the tool version, so the count the caps mean is the same on every machine and under every `ttok`, present or future. The CI pin stays valid: 0.3 takes `-m gpt-3.5-turbo`, which is its own default. The existing error path already covers an unsupported model, so there is nothing else to add.

Check — 0.3 and 1.0 now agree exactly on all seven capped files:

| file              | cap   | tokens |
|-------------------|-------|--------|
| `bend2/bend.ts`     | 48000 |  43767 |
| `bend2/comp.ts`     | 66000 |  65625 |
| `bend2/main.ts`     | 16000 |  11625 |
| `bend2/safe.ts`     | 24000 |  23992 |
| `bend2/bendtt.lean` | 64000 |  62092 |
| `README.md`         |  4000 |   3071 |
| `guide/GUIDE.md`    |  8000 |   7998 |

Gates on main: repo 54/54.

**Not part of this PR, but worth a decision:** `guide/GUIDE.md` is at 7,998 of 8,000 and `bend2/safe.ts` at 23,992 of 24,000, so the next edit to either turns the gate red, and the only sanctioned response is to delete from them. The core library `bend2/base.bend` is uncapped, which is the shape of answer the caps already have for a file that grows.

title: F32.lerp changes signed-zero endpoints and can return NaN at t=0
body:
On f5cee564, `F32.bits(F32.lerp(F32.neg(0.0), 1.0, 0.0))` is 0, not 2147483648. The t=1 version with a negative-zero right endpoint also loses its sign. `F32.lerp(1.0, F32.div(1.0, 0.0), 0.0)` returns NaN instead of its left endpoint.

The weighted sum helps opposite-sign finite inputs, but multiplying the unused endpoint by zero is not the same as returning the selected endpoint. Exact endpoints need to bypass that arithmetic.

title: bend-fmt-lsp moves a nested match arm into the outer match
body:
The formatting-only LSP can turn a valid program into a checker error when an arm body dedents before the next nested case. Its indentation fingerprint still accepts the rewrite.

Reproduced on f5cee564 with the same legal dedented-body layout already covered by bend-lint’s formatter: the original `g(True{}, False{})` runs and prints `20n`; LSP output moves the second inner case to the outer case column and then fails with a missing False case. The LSP needs to retain match-arm ownership across those body dedents.

title: bend-fmt-lsp rewrites mixed line endings despite promising to preserve them
body:
The LSP README says formatting preserves line endings. `formatBend("import Base
def main()->U32:
    7
")` instead converts the middle LF to CRLF because the document contains any CRLF.

The program runs either way, but formatting changes unrelated line terminators. Each existing terminator should be preserved, along with the final-newline state.

title: HTML bundling silently replaces an existing JS asset with an inline module
body:
At f5cee564, an index.html with an external module `./.index.html.bend-inline-0.js` and an inline module builds successfully, but the external asset never runs. The generated virtual file uses that same path, and the inline resolver intercepts both references.

My asset logs `asset`, the inline Bend consumer logs `42`; the built page only logs `42`. Generated module identities must not shadow real project files.

title: HTML bundle diagnostics rewrite unrelated real JS filenames as page names
body:
The bundle error handler strips the generated inline-module pattern from every diagnostic filename, even if no inline module was generated.

At f5cee564, an external-only page importing `.external.html.bend-inline-99.js` with `const broken = ;` reports `external.html:1:16`, a file that does not exist. Only actual virtual modules should be mapped back to their owning HTML pages.

title: Keep F32.lerp endpoints unchanged
body:
`lerp(-0, b, 0)` should keep the minus sign. An unused infinite endpoint should not turn the selected finite endpoint into NaN either.

Return the selected endpoint before doing the weighted sum, while keeping the opposite-sign overflow fix. Checked the interpreter and emitted C/JS with the extended boundary fixture; all three agree.

Closes #1749

title: Keep nested match arms and mixed line endings intact in the formatter
body:
The LSP could turn a working nested match into a missing-case error after an arm body dedented. Keep case ownership using the same model as bend-lint, rather than the previous body’s indentation. Also preserve each LF/CRLF instead of choosing one for the whole document.

All 33 tests pass. I also sent both examples through the real stdio server and ran the edited Bend programs: `20n` and `7`, as before.

Closes #1750
Closes #1751

title: Keep inline HTML modules separate from real assets
body:
A real `.page.html.bend-inline-0.js` could silently get replaced by the page’s inline script. Pick an unused virtual path, and map errors back only for virtual modules we actually created.

The bundle fixture now checks that both the real asset and inline code run, and that lookalike real filenames stay in diagnostics. The existing inline line/column checks still pass.

Closes #1752
Closes #1753

title: fix(fmt-lsp): retain inline match anchors after dedents
body:
## Problem and fix

After #1755, a first case sharing its `match` line still loses its column anchor when an arm body dedents. A later sibling can move into the outer match, making valid code fail checking with a missing-case error.

Retain that first case's existing formatted pin in the match scope, recover it for later arms, and keep it active for their continuations and nested matches. This follows the anchored-continuation approach discussed in [#1302](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1302#pullrequestreview-5421381492).

## Blast radius

Two files in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: the formatter and its existing formatter tests. Production code changes are 17 additions and 7 deletions. The change affects document-formatting edits for inline-first match layouts. Public options, the shipped `Level` layout, delimiter rules, per-line endings, and compiler/runtime behavior retain their existing interfaces and paths. No API compatibility break is intended.

## Regression evidence

Extend the existing actual-CLI regression with a compact inline first case, a following multi-line IO body, and recursively dedented nested arms. Each valid source runs before and after formatting with two-space, four-space and tab output. Tests require formatting to occur, preserve exact output, and be idempotent.

The extended test fails against unmodified main `881cb2e` with `expected : cases for False`; it passes with this fix. The shipped block-case regression remains as a control.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 33 pass, none skipped, including TypeScript build and LSP stdio integration.
- `npm pack --dry-run`, repository gate 54/54 with CI-pinned ttok 0.3, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Ten focused valid programs across three formatting options preserve CLI output and idempotence, with no return-source fallback.
- A parse-only screen passes 4,311 declaration/idempotence comparisons over 1,437 sources and three options.

## Validation limits

Local checks used macOS arm64, Node 26.8.2 and Bun 1.3.11. The parse-only screen skips 323 sources and does not establish full checking or execution for that corpus. Full cluster, performance and GPU gates, Windows/editor-client tests, and a separate Linux package run were not performed.

title: .mjs exports collapse an imported lib:value and a root lib.value
body:
### What you did
Built a checked program with `bun bend2/main.ts main.bend -o app.mjs`, then imported its default export from Bun.

### What happened
The imported `lib:value` and root `lib.value` both become the object key `"lib.value"`. The second silently replaces the first. Bend wrappers still return the two different values, so this is an export-name collision, not name resolution.

Actual consumer output:
```json
{"keys":["lib.value"],"imported":1,"local":2,"exported":2}
```

### The files
`lib.bend`:
```python
import Base
def value() -> U32:
  1
```
`main.bend`:
```python
import Base
import ./lib.bend as L
def lib.value() -> U32:
  2
def from_lib() -> U32:
  L.value()
def from_local() -> U32:
  lib.value()
```

Keeping canonical book keys (`"lib:value"` and `"lib.value"`) would let the host call both. This is separate from the BendTT-label collision in #1131/#1247.

### Version / system
main at 881cb2e5; Bun 1.3.13; Linux x86_64. No native compiler involved.

title: JS module emitter does not escape quotes or backslashes in book namespaces
Keep JavaScript definition names distinct in modules and effects
body:
Imported `lib:value` and root `lib.value` are different checked definitions. JS currently collapses them in two places: pure module exports overwrite each other, and foreign IO handlers fail with “two effects register lib.value”. Keep canonical names in both paths, and escape generated property keys so quotes/backslashes cannot break a module.

Root names and constructor tags stay unchanged. Imported export keys and foreign JS definition IDs now keep `:`; this is a breaking change for hosts that called an imported def by its dotted key. No compatibility aliases.

Real consumers fail before the fixes and pass after: both pure functions remain callable, and the two IO handlers print 1 then 2 under both Bun and Node. Interpreter IO and the existing prototype-key, constructor interop, Nat/F32 export and host-closure consumers pass too. Local repo/cap gate: 54/54. Remote mini-cluster gates were not run.

Closes #1758
Closes #1759
Closes #1766

title: Nested JS IO wakes channel waiters on the wrong scheduler
body:
### What you did
A foreign JS effect calls a nested `io_run` that sends to a channel with an already-parked outer receiver. The outer Bend program uses `IO.spawn`, `Chan.recv`, and a short `IO.sleep` before entering the foreign effect.

### What happened
The receiver runs inside the nested scheduler. Its completion decrements the wrong live count, and the nested call returns 1 with:
```text
7
bend: deadlock: every computation waits on a channel
nested IO failed
```
The outer continuation never reaches `outer-complete`. Both schedulers should finish successfully, with the parked receiver resumed on its own scheduler after the foreign call returns.

`chan_wake` uses global `io_active` for both the runnable queue and timer cancellation. The waiter needs to retain the scheduler that parked it. The same ownership problem affects waiting senders and timed receivers/close wakeups.

### Version / system
main at 881cb2e5; Bun 1.3.13; Linux x86_64. This is a JS correctness issue, not a native scheduler or JS performance change.

title: Resume channel waiters on their own JS scheduler
body:
Found two ways channel waiters could get lost: a nested io_run woke them on the wrong scheduler, and an already-selected timeout could resume a waiter again after a send had won.

Waiters now keep their scheduler owner, remove a timer only when it is still queued, and clear the continuation after the first completion. No poller rewrite.

The real nested-scheduler and overdue-timer cases pass. The timer case now prints `got 7`, `after`, `sleep-survived` once each, instead of also timing out and losing the child. Six existing channel consumers pass; repo gate: 54/54.

Closes #1761
Closes #1770

title: Share duplicated arm bodies as capture-aware spins
body:
The flattener duplicates an arm body at every path that reaches it. When two arm bodies are the same term up to alpha-renaming of their own binders and a layout-preserving correspondence of their captures, their generated code is the same function of those captures and arguments. A canonical token encoding (bound occurrences by distance, captures by first-occurrence rank and layout, other free probes by rank, and type annotations by term_key) proves equality; the second occurrence of a large body, or the third occurrence of a smaller one, is emitted once as a spin and later arms call it.

The spin takes captures in the encoding's order, then the arm's arguments, so a representative is never reused with a captured environment of another shape. A spin whose body would touch the segment bank (a jump, a fork frame, a stack return) cannot compile as a plain C function; file_push unwinds that emission at the first such line and the arm is emitted inline with every File side effect restored, so no trace reaches the C.

Bounds: 16k shapes, 8 representatives per shape, 65k nodes / 2k depth per encoding, 32 MiB of encodings per file. Past any, the arm is inline.

Semantic fixtures: capture_arm_share exercises a Nat literal's duplicated default with captured a, b; capture_arm_scopes holds structurally equal bodies whose captures have different layouts, which a capture-blind share would miscompile.

Generated C on the PR890-shaped five-overlap fixture falls from 33,992,175 B to 1,486,108 B. On every fixture where no arm spin is emitted the C is byte-identical to v2.0.25; controls alias_def, match_default, closure_cps, shared_match_ctor and eta_default_arm have the same sha256 in both compilers.

Head 007122e64928fdcdfaa4215041d359a14adde2c8. C generation optimization for canonical review; no thresholds.

title: Resuming TCP.try_send string residue corrupts a partially written UTF-8 character
body:
### What you did
Sent `"!" ++ String.repeat("€", 1000000n)` to a real loopback TCP peer with `TCP.try_send(socket, data, 0)`. The peer paused reading until the non-blocking send filled up. On `Wait{rest}`, the client resumed with `TCP.send(socket, rest)` and closed the socket.

### What happened
Both emitted C and JS clients printed `wait` and exited 0, but the independent C peer received **3,000,003 bytes rather than 3,000,001**. The first incorrect byte was at offset **1,794,048**. This was actual kernel IO, not a short-write mock.

A partial write stopped inside a Euro sign. The unsent suffix begins with UTF-8 continuation bytes; converting that byte suffix back to `String` inserts replacement characters. Re-encoding the returned string cannot reproduce the original stream. A failed partially-completed `TCP.send` has the same representation problem.

The residue needs to remain bytes, including for the text-taking APIs. Returning `List<&2, U32>` and resuming through `TCP.send_bytes` preserves it; UDP datagrams do not need this contract change.

### Version / system
main at 881cb2e5; Linux x86_64; Bun 1.3.13 and the native C backend.

title: Return exact byte residues from TCP text sends
body:
A kernel write can stop inside a UTF-8 character. Decoding the unsent bytes into a String loses them: my real C peer received 3,000,003 bytes for a 3,000,001-byte payload after resuming `TCP.try_send`. Both JS and native C reproduced it.

**API change:** `TCP.send` failure residue and `TCP.try_send` failure/Wait residue are now `List<&2, U32>`, just like the byte APIs. Input is still String; resume the returned suffix with `TCP.send_bytes`. There is no lossless String-only representation for a suffix starting midway through a character. All in-repo TCP callers are migrated, and Base/README explain the contract. UDP is unchanged. The now-redundant text/byte result-builder paths are removed.

The actual peer now receives all 3,000,001 original bytes. A permanent real-socket regression limits SO_SNDBUF, resumes a partial Unicode write, and checks every received byte; it passes in C and JS. Nine existing TCP fixtures pass in both lanes, three affected demos compile, and the local repo/cap gate is 54/54. No remote-cluster run claimed.

Closes #1764

title: Distinct namespaced and dotted-root JS effects collide during registration
body:
### What you did
Built a checked program with two foreign `IO(U32)` definitions: `value` imported from `lib.bend`, and a root definition named `lib.value`. Each imports its own JS file and registers its own handler with `io_eff(CID(...), ...)`.

### What happened
The generated program exits before main:
```text
Error: bend: two effects register lib.value
```
Both Bun 1.3.13 and Node v22.23.1 reproduce this. The handlers belong to different checked definitions (`lib:value` and `lib.value`) and should return 1 and 2 independently.

The JS CID/FID expansion and emitted foreign request tag both flatten `:` to `.`. They need to retain the canonical definition name. Constructor tags are a different, type-local identity and should stay unchanged.

This is the IO-registration path, not the pure default-export collision in #1758. I am putting the coordinated name-encoding changes in the same PR so those paths use one convention.

### Version / system
main at 881cb2e5; Linux x86_64; emitted JS under Bun and Node.

title: HTML bundling misses encoded module types and activates scripts with non-ASCII whitespace
body:
### What you did
Bundled two pages importing a small Bend function returning 42, then opened the output in real Chromium:
```html
<script type="module">import lib from './lib.bend'; /* display lib.value() */</script>
<script type=" module">import lib from './lib.bend'; /* display lib.value() */</script>
```
The second type starts with U+00A0, not an ASCII space. Each page has an output initially showing “not run”.

### What happened
The encoded `module` is valid HTML, but its bundled page stays at “not run” and tries to fetch an unbundled lib.bend. The NBSP-prefixed type is not a module and should stay inert, but the bundled page executes it and displays 42.

`HTMLRewriter.getAttribute` preserves character references. `is_inline_module` neither decodes the ASCII references that can spell module nor uses HTML's ASCII-only whitespace rule: JavaScript `trim()` also strips NBSP.

### Version / system
main at 881cb2e5; Bun 1.3.13; Linux x86_64. Both results were observed in actual Chromium after running the CLI, not inferred from generated source.

title: Keep HTML module roots independent and classify their type correctly
body:
Fixes HTML script classification and independent inline modules that deadlocked when Bun combined them into one sequential chunk.

Only inline modules become separate entries in the shared build graph. External src scripts stay on Bun's normal HTML path, including root-relative URLs and packages with `sideEffects: false`. Shared dependencies still execute once. The HTML batch stays outside inert templates and isn't duplicated when Bun already put it in the head.

Checked the real CLI and Chromium: the waiting page reaches 42; root-relative, side-effects, template/head placement and output-name cases pass. All three executable IO consumers print 0, including the new root-relative and console-only regressions. Child spawns use isolated HOME/origin/telemetry and 6-second timeouts. Repo gate: 54/54.

Missing external srcs use Bun's native diagnostic against the page and original relative specifier. No kernel, GUIDE, changelog, gate or cap changes.

Closes #1767

title: fix(gate): name the pin's columns, so a drift is an error
body:
The perf gate read its pin by position — column 1 is `SEQ-CPU`, column 2 is `PAR-CPU`, column 3 is `PAR-GPU` — and nothing tied those positions to the names the file declares. The pin is hand-edited (its own header says the `COMPILER` column and the spaces are "by hand"), so a layout that drifts is read as numbers and reported as a verdict.

Two drifts, both silent today:

**A header whose `SEQ-CPU` and `PAR-CPU` are swapped.** The sequential run is then compared against the parallel baseline — 0.500 s instead of 3.501 s for `bfs` — so the gate either fails a healthy run, or passes a run that is seven times slower, and says nothing about the pin.

**A row that loses a cell.** The `OUTPUT` column reads as `undefined`, and the gate reports an output-size mismatch, blaming the program for a change in the pin file.

The reader now takes the column names and checks them, the way `bend2/docs/gen_charts.ts` already does for the record pins ("columns drifted from [...] -- repin"): a header that does not name the expected columns, or a row with the wrong number of cells, is an error.

The error is raised where the pin is read, before the benchmarks run, so a drift is seconds to see and not a 20-minute run to find.

Check, on the gate's own pin:

```
# the header's SEQ-CPU and PAR-CPU swapped
$ bun gates/perf.ts
error: .../bench/runtime/_pin_/apple_m4.txt: columns drifted from [bench, COMPILER, SEQ-CPU, PAR-CPU, PAR-GPU, OUTPUT] -- repin

# the OUTPUT column dropped from one row
$ bun gates/perf.ts
error: .../bench/runtime/_pin_/apple_m4.txt: bfs has 4 columns, not 5 -- repin
```

Both fire before any SSH, so neither needs the cluster to check. With the pin as committed the gate reads it as before.

Gates: repo 54/54. The other three need the mini cluster, so they are not run here.

Not caught: a transposition of two values inside one row, with the header intact — telling `SEQ` from `PAR` by value would need an invariant the pin does not state, so the guard stays on the shape.

title: Timed channel receives can resume twice and remove an unrelated timer
body:
A timed receive can be selected into the poller’s ready batch, then be completed by an earlier callback from that same batch. The channel wake-up does splice(-1, 1) because its timer has already left the wait list, and the selected timeout still resumes the continuation a second time.

I reproduced this with a real channel, 1ms send, 10ms receive timeout and a 20ms barrier. It prints both `got 7` and `timeout`; an unrelated sleeping child never finishes. No fake clock or poller mock.

The receive should finish once, and the unrelated sleep should survive.

title: bend-lint accepts non-object JSON configs as default settings
body:
With a JSON config containing just `[]`, bend-lint runs normally and exits 0 instead of rejecting the config. A scalar root has the same problem. These values cannot satisfy the documented Config object shape, and can silently leave the intended rules unapplied.

I checked the actual CLI on an unformatted Bend file: `--config config.json --json` accepts `[]` and returns `ok: true`. The JS/TS config loader already rejects invalid root shapes; JSON should get the same validation and exit 2.

title: bend-lint accepts array severity and lets error-policy checks pass CI
body:
Setting a rule’s severity to `["error"]` passes validation through JavaScript property-key coercion. The resulting diagnostics carry the array rather than the string `"error"`, so the final error-policy check misses them.

I reproduced this with the real formatter rule and CLI: a valid string `"error"` exits 1, while `["error"]` reports the same finding but exits 0 with `ok: true`.

Severity should be a string from the documented enum. Malformed values should be configuration errors (exit 2), not successful lint runs.

title: Reject malformed linter configs instead of passing CI
body:
Bad configs could pass CI: `[]` was treated as default settings, and severity `["error"]` slipped through key coercion without triggering the error policy. Both now fail as config errors. The documented JS/TS config cache behaviour stays unchanged.

Checked the actual CLI: those cases move from exit 0 to exit 2; a valid `"error"` policy still exits 1. All 135 linter tests pass using a private POSIX temp filesystem, and the repo gate is 54/54.

`bun run typecheck` reports two errors in unmodified, protected `bend2/bend.ts` (2040 and 3771). I haven’t edited the kernel or suppressed those diagnostics.

Closes #1771
Closes #1772

title: HTML bundling can deadlock independent inline modules with top-level await
body:
Two inline module scripts are independent browser roots: an await in the first must not stop the second from starting. The page bundler currently combines them into one sequential JS chunk.

I reproduced a real deadlock: the first script imports a Bend value and waits for a promise that the second script resolves. The equivalent JS page reaches 42 in Chromium; the bundled page stays at `not run`, with the second script never starting. `splitting: true` on the existing HTML build alone does not fix it.

The compiled roots need to stay independent while keeping one shared dependency graph, so shared modules still execute once.

title: fix(lint): preserve edits made while rules run
body:
When a file is saved while an asynchronous lint rule runs, `bend-lint --fix` can overwrite the saved text with fixes based on the old text. Check the current file text immediately before writing. If it differs from the checked text, preserve it and exit with code 2. Saves with identical text still allow fixes.

Add regression tests for all three fix flags and identical-text saves. Document the changed-input error. A concurrent write between the final read and write remains possible.

Validation:

- `BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 bun test tools/bend-lint`: 136 tests pass.
- Repository gate: 54 / 54 pass.
- `git diff --check`: passes.
- Type checking reports two existing TS2339 errors in `bend2/bend.ts`, at lines 2040 and 3771. Both errors also occur on unchanged `main` at `881cb2e5`.

title: CUDA: the error poll in every flat loop (`err_spun`) makes ptxas yield on each iteration; tight loops run up to 20x slower
body:
### What you did

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts flat.bend -o flat.c      # or `bend flat.bend -o flat.c` with 2.0.37
sed 's/^#define err_spun(H, n) ((++\*(n) & 4095) == 0 \&\& err_seen(H))$/#define err_spun(H, n) (0)/' flat.c > flat_np.c
# build both the way `bend -o` does (clang -DBEND_CUDA=1 ... -std=c11 -O3 ... -lcuda -lnvrtc), then ./x --gpu-build
```

### What happened

Every flat loop Bend compiles for the device (`spin_N`, opened by `WL_SPIN`) starts with `err_spun(e.mem, &wpoll)`: a counter and, every 4,096 steps, a load of the heap's error word. In the SASS (read from 2.0.37's build; main emits the same C for it), that loop gets a `YIELD` and a convergence barrier (`BSSY`/`BSYNC`) on every iteration, and it is not unrolled. On a loop with little work per step this dominates: a one-leaf loop of `acc * 0.999 + x` takes ~70 ns a step on an RTX 4050, against ~3.4 ns for the same loop handwritten in CUDA. With the poll removed from the emitted C, Bend's loop runs as fast as the handwritten one. Splitting the loop keeps the check and most of the speed; a patch is below.

Both builds print 57342550. The tables time the bang alone (`IO.now` around it, after a warm-up bang), five alternated rounds on an idle machine, min-max. Main 881cb2e5 (with #1602), RTX 4050 Laptop (sm_89), driver 615.78.08, CUDA 12.9; every build prints the same results, on the GPU and with `--gpu off`:

| program | main | poll removed | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the loop in the file below, 1 leaf (depth 0), 2M steps | 136-138 ms | 7 ms | ~20x |
| the loop in the file below, 16,384 leaves, 2M steps | 129-132 ms | 15-16 ms | 8.5x |
| tiled matmul 512x512x4096, 8x4 block a leaf, 50 products | 172-177 ms | 149-152 ms | 1.16x |
| tiled matmul 512x512x4096, 4x4 block a leaf, 50 products | 230-237 ms | 210-218 ms | 1.09x |
| 16,384 leaves, interleaved reads of one shared Array | 112-114 ms | 112-115 ms | 1.0x |
| 16,384 leaves, 2M reads each of a 32-number Array (whole program) | 0.92-0.93 s | 0.88-0.91 s | ~1.0x |

The same loop handwritten in CUDA takes 14.1-14.3 ms for 16,384 threads, so without the poll Bend matches it. Loops that wait on memory hide the poll; loops of arithmetic pay for it.

#### The cost is the poll's shape, not its load

In a handwritten CUDA kernel with the same loop (one thread / 16,384 threads, ns per step):

| poll | 1 thread | 16,384 |
|---|---:|---:|
| none | 3.4 | 7.1 |
| `if ((++n & 4095) == 0 && *err != 0) return;` in the loop (Bend's shape), `volatile` load | 16.7 | 30.5 |
| the same with `__ldcg` or `ld.relaxed.gpu` | 16.7 | 30.4-30.9 |
| split loop: 4,096 steps with no check, then one check | 3.4 | 7.2 |

So the check can stay: emitting a spin as an inner loop of up to 4,096 steps with no poll, inside an outer loop that polls once, costs nothing measurable here. On the host `err_seen` is `DEVICE && ...`, so CPU builds do not pay.

#### A fix that keeps the poll

I tried the split shape in `bend2/comp.ts` (written against e5527d5b, applies to 881cb2e5 unchanged): on the device, each `spin_N`, each spin segment and the work loop run their body in an inner loop of up to 4,096 steps with no poll, inside an outer loop that polls once. A `break` leaves the inner loop with steps left, which also ends the outer one; `continue` stays in the inner loop. The host keeps its macros, so CPU builds do not change.

```diff
@@ emit_native (spin_N)
-    ...seg_take(seg), "WL_SPIN"], 1),
-    ...seg_text(seg.lines, 2), "  break;", "  }",
+    ...seg_take(seg), "WL_SPIN2"], 1),
+    ...seg_text(seg.lines, 2), "  break;", "  }", "  WL_SPIN2_END",
@@ compile_book (spin segments)
-      "WL_OPEN", ...seg.spin ? ["WL_SPIN", ...seg.lines, "WL_SPUN"]
+      "WL_OPEN", ...seg.spin ? ["WL_SPIN2", ...seg.lines, "WL_SPUN2"]
@@ after WL_AGAIN
+#if DEVICE
+#define WL_SPIN2     for (u32 wfirst = 1;; wfirst = 0) { \
+  if (!wfirst && err_seen(e.mem)) { return 0; } \
+  u32 wleft = 4096; for (; wleft != 0; wleft -= 1) {
+#define WL_SPIN2_END if (wleft != 0) { break; } }
+#define WL_SPUN2     } if (wleft != 0) { break; } } break;
+#else
+#define WL_SPIN2     WL_SPIN
+#define WL_SPIN2_END
+#define WL_SPUN2     WL_SPUN
+#endif
@@ work_loop (device)
-  WL_SPIN
+  WL_SPIN2
   switch (fid) {
@@ end of work_loop
   }
+  WL_SPIN2_END
+  return 0;
 }
```

Built with `bun bend2/main.ts`, every program below prints the same results as main's build, on the GPU and with `--gpu off`, and a lane-stack overflow inside a bang is still reported. Same machine and rounds:

| program | main | with the split | poll removed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| flat loop, 1 leaf, 2M steps | 136-138 ms | 19-20 ms | 7 ms |
| flat loop, 16,384 leaves, 2M steps | 129-132 ms | 36-37 ms | 15-16 ms |
| tiled matmul 512², 8x4 a leaf, 50 products | 172-177 ms | 157-161 ms | 149-152 ms |
| tiled matmul 512², 4x4 a leaf, 50 products | 230-237 ms | 222-227 ms | 210-218 ms |
| interleaved reads of one shared Array | 112-114 ms | 106-107 ms | 112-115 ms |
| 2M reads a leaf of a 32-number Array (whole program) | 0.92-0.93 s | 0.89-0.90 s | 0.88-0.91 s |

It keeps most of the gain on the arithmetic loops and is slower than main nowhere. The flat loops do not reach the no-poll time: the split still runs the outer loop and its test every 4,096 steps, and I have not looked further at what nvcc makes of it.

The change adds 17 lines to `comp.ts`, which is at its token cap; a shorter form is surely possible. I have not opened a pull request; this is to show the shape works.

### The file

```python
import Base

def flat_l(k: Nat, +x: F32, acc: F32) -> F32:
  match k:
    case 0n: acc
    case 1n+q: flat_l(q, x, ((acc * 0.999 : F32) + x : F32))

def flat_tree(d: Nat, +k: Nat, +i: U32) -> F32:
  match d:
    case 0n: flat_l(k, U32.to_f32(U32.and(i, 7)), 0.0)
    case 1n++q:
      a b = flat_tree(q, k, (i * 2 : U32)) flat_tree(q, k, ((i * 2 : U32) + 1 : U32))
      (a + b : F32)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(F32.show(flat_tree!(14n, 2000000n, 0)))
```

bend 2.0.37, and main 881cb2e5 (2026-10-19, `bun bend2/main.ts`), where the tables were measured

Linux x86_64 (RTX 4050 Laptop, driver 615.78.08, CUDA 12.9)

title: A safe way to give a fork tree's leaves disjoint parts of one Array to write (the counterpart of #1376)
body:
### What Bend should do

Base already has the right shape in its model: an `Array<T>` is `ALeaf{value}` or `ANode{xs, ys}`, two disjoint halves. In the compiled program, though, matching an array copies each half into its own block (BendRT, "Arrays"), so a fork tree cannot use it. Something like

```python
# split a into its two halves, both views of a's block: O(1), no copy
Array.halves(-T: Type, a: Array<T>) -> Array<T> & Array<T>      # model: match a { ANode{xs, ys}: (xs, ys) }
# put two halves of one block back together: O(1) when they came from Array.halves
Array.node(-T: Type, xs: Array<T>, ys: Array<T>) -> Array<T>     # model: ANode{xs, ys}
```

would have a model in which each leaf owns its half (writes included), so laws about the joined result could be stated and proved, and the runtime would do what the unsafe pattern does today. A leaf at depth d owns a contiguous range of 2^(capacity - d) cells. That fits tensor-fork (blocks of rows of C), stencil3d (slabs) and the histogram's rows. It does not fit a 2-D tile directly (tensor-gpu's leaves write 4 x 4 tiles of a row-major C): such a kernel would store C tile-major and permute it afterwards, or need a split by stride, which is a further question.

Questions:

1. Is a safe split for writes on the roadmap, alongside the read-only borrow of #1376 (or the borrow inference Taelin mentioned)?
2. Would it belong in Base (as above), or is a library the intended place, with `@unsafe` contained in it as bend-ml does now?
3. Is the halves-of-a-node shape the right one for the runtime (a view into one block, freed once), or would ranges (`Array.split_at(a, i)`) fit it better?

I can share the packages' tests (every product against the sequential code, bit for bit, on the CPU threads and on the GPU) as a test bed for whatever shape it takes.

### Why

The one-block pattern of `tests/run/stencil3d.bend` (and of bend-parallel's histogram, PR #1278): one `Array`, a fork tree whose every node holds a handle to it (`Array.fork`), each leaf writing its own part, the halves joined back (`Array.join`). It is how a GPU kernel is written in Bend today, and the fast one: in bend-ml I use it for matrix products on the CPU threads (bend-ml-tensor-fork: each leaf writes its rows of C) and on the GPU (bend-ml-tensor-gpu: each leaf writes its tile of C), and both give tensor-array's bits.

Both packages are `@unsafe`, and so is every program that uses them. That part is expected: Base models `Array.fork(a)` as `(a, a)` and `Array.join(a, b)` as `a`, so a write through the second handle is not in the model at all, and no law about the result can be stated. The alternatives cost what the pattern saves:

| way to write disjoint parts in parallel | what it costs |
|---|---|
| each leaf returns its part as a list, written into the array after the join | 2-3.6x slower than not splitting, for products with a short inner dimension (bend-ml-tensor-array's NOTES); on CUDA, the lists' appends hit the lane stack (#1393) |
| each leaf gets its own array, concatenated after the join | a copy of the whole output per call |
| `Array.fork` / `Array.join` | O(1), the speed of the pattern, but `@unsafe` |

title: CUDA: `Array.new` inside a bang fills the new block in one loop on one lane (~4.6 ns a cell)
body:
### What you did

```sh
bun bend2/main.ts gpu_array_new_fill.bend -o fill && nsys profile --trace=cuda ./fill
```

### What happened

A kernel that writes its output into an array made inside the bang (the pattern `tests/run/stencil3d.bend` uses, and the one that keeps the output's pages on the device) pays for the allocation before any leaf runs. A bang whose root only allocates 2^c F32 cells and forks 16 leaves that read one cell (`gpu_array_new_fill.bend`), Nsight Systems, the first `bend_dev` launch (grid 1), 5 bangs each, Bend 2.0.37 and main 881cb2e5 (2026-10-19):

| cells | first launch, 2.0.37 | first launch, main |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2^16 | 0.54-0.85 ms | 0.52-1.02 ms |
| 2^18 | 1.60-1.82 ms | 1.35-1.40 ms |
| 2^20 | 5.33-5.52 ms | 4.93-5.13 ms |
| 2^22 | 19.05-20.29 ms | 19.23-19.88 ms |

About 4.6 ns a cell, linear. In the emitted C, `blk_new` writes every cell in one loop on the lane that runs it:

```c
for (u64 i = 0; i < (1ull << c); i += 1) {
  blk_write(H, arr, l, (u32)i, i % (1u << lgs) < n ? v[i % (1u << lgs)] : 0);
}
```

and the root of a bang runs on one group while the tree grows. `blk_fill` (used by `Array.clone`, matching `ANode`, and `blk_node`) is the same kind of loop.

#### Why it matters

With Bend 2.0.37 I moved a whole training step of a transformer block (8 x 64 rows, width 576, feed-forward 1536) onto the GPU: every layer as bangs that make their outputs inside the bang, so nothing moves to the host between them. The leaves' work takes ~83 ms a step; the first launches, where these fills run, take 115-130 ms. Making the outputs on the host instead is worse here: a new block often reuses pages that sit on the device, and filling it on the host pulls them back (3 steps: 1,118 ms against 760).

#### Questions

- Could `blk_new` on the device fill with every lane of the group (or of the grid) instead of one, or skip the fill when the value is zero and the heap block is known to be zeroed?
- Would an `Array.new` that leaves the cells to the leaves (each leaf writes its own part) fit the runtime's model?

### The file

```python
# The cost of Array.new inside a bang: a root that allocates 2^c cells and runs a 16-leaf tree that writes nothing, for
# c = 16, 18, 20, 22, 5 bangs each, in that order; time each bang's first bend_dev launch (grid 1) with Nsight Systems.
import Base

def at0(r: Array<F32> & F32) -> F32:
  match r:
    case Tuple{a, +x}: x

@unsafe
def tr(d: Nat, +o: Array<F32>) -> F32:
  match d:
    case 0n: at0(Array.get(F32, o, 0))
    case 1n++p:
      a b = tr(p, o) tr(p, o)
      (a + b : F32)

@unsafe
def root(+c: Nat) -> F32:
  tr(4n, Array.new(F32, c, 0.0))

@unsafe
def go(+c: Nat) -> F32:
  root!(c)

@unsafe
def loop(k: Nat, +c: Nat, acc: F32) -> F32:
  match k:
    case 0n: acc
    case 1n+q: loop(q, c, (acc + go(c) : F32))

@unsafe
def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(F32.show((((loop(5n, 16n, 0.0) + loop(5n, 18n, 0.0) : F32) + loop(5n, 20n, 0.0) : F32) + loop(5n, 22n, 0.0) : F32)))
```

### bend version

bend 2.0.37, and main 881cb2e5 (2026-10-19)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64 (RTX 4050 Laptop, driver 615.78.08, CUDA 12.9)
