title: bend -o: a $CC that is not a runnable clang is skipped silently, and the build uses plain clang
body:
### What you did

```sh
CC="clang -mavx2" bend prog.bend -o prog     # flags in $CC, as make and most build systems take it
CC=/usr/bin/clang-1 bend prog.bend -o prog   # a path that does not exist
CC=gcc bend prog.bend -o prog                # a compiler that is not clang
```

### What happened

All three exit 0 with no output, and the binary is built by plain `clang` (`readelf -p .comment` shows `clang version 23.1.3` for all three; on a larger program, `CC="clang -mavx2"` gives a binary with no `ymm` instruction, while a wrapper script that runs `clang -mavx2 "$@"`, set as `CC`, gives 8,093). Nothing tells the user that the `$CC` they set was not used.

`cc_find` in `bend2/main.ts` tries `$CC`, then `clang`, then every `clang-NN` on `PATH`, running each name with `spawnSync` (no shell) and taking the first whose `--version` is clang 14 or newer. A `$CC` that cannot run, or is not clang, is pushed to the list that the final error prints, but that error only appears when no candidate works, so when plain `clang` works the skip is silent. It is the same on main at 40402b42.

I am not asking for compiler flags again (#1461 settled that: `bend f.bend -o f.c` and clang by hand works, and so does a wrapper script set as `$CC`). The issue is only the silence. Either of these would fix it:

- fail when `$CC` is set and cannot be used, as the user asked for that compiler: the existing error already has the words (`found <CC>, which is not clang`);
- or keep going with the next candidate, but print one line first, e.g. `bend: $CC ("clang -mavx2") is not a runnable clang 14+; building with clang`.

Why I hit it: building the emitted C of a training step for the host (`-march=native`) made it 12.5% faster on one thread with the same bits, and setting `CC` with the flag was the first thing I tried. It looked like it worked.

### The file

```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print("hi")
```

### bend version

bend 2.0.37

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 23.1.3

title: fix(formatter): preserve nested lambda body columns
body:
Formatting an inline lambda inside parentheses or a call argument can move its continued statements to different columns and make valid Bend source fail to parse. The formatter now pins nested lambda bodies and their semicolon continuations, and expires those pins at their enclosing delimiter or argument boundary. Generic commas and ordinary delimiter indentation retain their existing behavior.

Three regressions extend the existing formatting/idempotence and real-CLI preservation tests, with controls for following arguments and closing delimiters. Local npm tests pass 33/33, the repository gate passes 54/54, and actual LSP edits preserve the programs’ execution. The same regression tests fail against the unchanged formatter.

title: bend -o: a $CC that is not a usable clang ends the build, instead of a silent plain-clang build (#1802)
body:
Fixes #1802.

## What this does

`cc_find` (bend2/main.ts) now ends the build when the first candidate, `$CC`, cannot be used, instead of silently falling through to plain `clang`. The three failure shapes the issue lists each get their reason in the error:

- not runnable: `CC=/nonexistent/definitely bend prose.bend -o prose` → `Error: bend uses the compiler $CC names, and $CC ("/nonexistent/definitely") is not runnable; unset $CC to build with the best clang on the path`
- not clang: `CC=gcc ...` → `... is not a clang; ...`
- too old: `CC=clang10 ...` → `... is clang 10, and bend needs clang 14; ...`

A build without `$CC` keeps the old behaviour exactly (same picks, same `bend needs clang 14 or newer ... found ...` error).

This fixes only the silence; the handling of flags inside `$CC` is untouched (issue #1461 settled that, as the issue notes). The second bullet the issue offers — warn and continue — was not taken, since a skipped `$CC` that the user asked for is still a build the user did not intend; fail-with-reason is the half the issue leans on first.

## Self-review checklist

- [x] The diff matches the issue
- [x] Self-reviewed the full diff
- [x] Tests or gates were run, or an explanation is included

## AI/LLM Assistance

This change was written by an AI coding agent (opencode, via the account Yi-111-a). The behaviour was verified locally by running the CLI from source with `$CC` set to a nonexistent path, to a fake non-clang compiler and to a fake too-old clang.

## Notes on testing

No clang on this machine, so a completed native build was not possible locally; what was verified is exactly the decision `cc_find` makes: with `$CC` failing, the build now stops (three shapes above), and without `$CC` the error line is unchanged. `bun x tsc --noEmit` reports the same 45 pre-existing errors with and without the change; none are in `main.ts`. The full gates run on the mini cluster (`gates/test.ts`), which this environment cannot reproduce.

title: A read-only walk owns its list when a sum type puts an unboxed field where another constructor has a boxed one
body:
On Bend 2.0.38, a def that only reads a list of a sum type takes the list
(`ctr_take`) instead of borrowing it (`term_peek`) whenever two of the
type's constructors put an unboxed word (a `Bool`, say) and a boxed one at
the same field position. When the list is shared, every cell the walk
passes is then copied out and faded.

```bend
import Base

type Ev is Data:
  Hit{key: String, value: String}
  Flag{key: String, on: Bool}

def evs() -> List<&2, Ev>:
  [Hit{"a", "1"}, Flag{"b", True{}}, Hit{"c", "2"}]

# Only reads evs, so it should borrow them.
def hits(evs: List<&2, Ev>, n: Nat) -> Nat:
  match evs:
    case Nil{}: n
    case Hit{k, v} <> tail: hits(tail, 1n+n)
    case Flag{k, on} <> tail: hits(tail, n)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  +xs = evs()
  a = hits(xs, 0n)
  IO.print(Nat.show(Nat.add(a, List.length(&2, Ev, xs))))
```

`bend mixed.bend -o mixed.c` gives `hits`:

    u64 _sp_0 = ctr_take(e, _evs_0, 2, _fb_0);

With `on: String` in place of `on: Bool` it gives:

    u64 _sp_0 = term_peek(e.mem, _evs_0);

Expected: `term_peek` in both, since `hits` stores and returns nothing it
reads.

Cause, as far as I can trace it in the compiler: when `val_arms` merges the
arms of an unboxed match, each out slot collects one borrow label per arm,
and a word that is not a box pushes `""`. Field 2 collects `"evs…"` from
`Hit` and `""` from `Flag`, so the labels differ, and every non-empty one
goes into `FL.own`. `val_own` likewise adds a label for a borrowed word that
is not a box. A non-box word holds no reference, so neither should count.
Two changes make both versions emit `term_peek`:

- in `val_arms`, push a label only for a slot whose kind in that arm is
  `"box"`;
- in `val_own`, look up the borrow label only when `v.lay.ks[j] === "box"`.

On a parser that walks a list of such events once per option, the change
made parsing a large argv about 10% faster.

title: A read-only walk borrows its list when a word shares a slot with a box (#1805)
body:
Fixes #1805.

## What changes

A word that is not a box holds no reference, so the borrow analysis now ignores it in the two places the issue names:

- `val_arms` merges an unboxed match's arms into one set of out slots, and each slot collects one borrow label per arm. An arm now adds a label only where that arm has a box in the slot. Before, `Flag`'s `Bool` added `""` next to `Hit`'s `hits~0`, the labels disagreed, and `hits~0` became owned.
- `val_own` looks a word's label up only when the word's kind is `box`. With the first change alone, the merged slot keeps `Hit`'s label, so `Flag`'s `Bool`, read back out of that slot, carries it. Passing that `Bool` to a call (`ons` in the new test) made its root owned again.

The `val_own` change also covers a case beyond the issue. `lay_node` lays out a generic constructor once, so `Con`'s head is a box field, and `node_fields` labels it. A `List<&2, U32>` then reads that head as a `U32` that still carries the label. So a walk that kept its head across its own call (`h + sum(tail)`) took its list.

The comment above `val_new` now says a non-box word neither roots nor owns. `comp.ts` goes from 65,807 to 65,872 ttok (cap 66,000).

## What it reaches

I built every runnable test, bench and demo to C and JS with main's compiler and with this one:

- **JS:** identical everywhere. The JS lane doesn't use this analysis.
- **Benches:** identical C.
- **Five programs' C changes.** In each, takes become peeks. The `term_keep`s that shared the value go away too, and so do the `rfc_seal`s of the types that sharing heated.
  - `demos/pure_par_sort`: `Tree(d)` keeps `Nat`s in `Sigma`'s generic fields.
  - `tests/check/data_table_inferred`: the `sum` above, so `main.out` no longer keeps `xs`.
  - `tests/run/family_arg_hot`, `tests/run/family_field_hot` and `tests/rfc/drop_spine`: see below.

`demos/pure_par_sort` on an M3 Max (medians of 7 interleaved runs after a warm-up; both print `sorted`):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 16 threads | 0.090 s | 0.064 s |
| 1 thread | 0.160 s | 0.122 s |
| GPU (Metal) | 0.148 s | 0.138 s |
| 16 threads, `-falign-functions=64` | 0.087 s | 0.066 s |
| 1 thread, `-falign-functions=64` | 0.158 s | 0.120 s |

## Three tests needed an owner

`family_arg_hot`, `family_field_hot` and `drop_spine` each need a value to be shared, so that its type is hot. Each got that sharing from a reader that owned its argument only because of a stray label. With this PR those readers borrow and nothing is shared: each test's C has no `term_keep` and no `rfc_seal`. The tests still pass, but they no longer test what they were written for. To show this, I removed each test's guard from scratch copies of both compilers:

| guard removed | test | main | this PR, test as it was | this PR, with `give` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `facts_hot` walks a stuck family's arguments | `family_arg_hot` (want 29) | 2198905222 | 29 | 2198905222 |
| `emit_ctr` heats a hot build's fields (#853) | `family_field_hot` (want 5) | 1 | 5 | 1 |

Each test now passes the shared value through `give`, an identity def that owns what it returns:

- `family_arg_hot`: `heat` is `first(give(c)) + first(c)`.
- `family_field_hot`: `total(s, build(give(s)))`.
- `drop_spine`: the matcher is renamed `head`, and `first(xs)` is `head(give(xs))`, so each sum owns its copy as before.

Each test's C now has main's keeps, seals, takes and `CID_T`. I found no removed guard that `drop_spine` catches: zeroing `CID_T`'s drop column (#1438) passes on main too, with and without `BEND_POISON`. Its header says it shares one copy, and with `give` it does again. Each header gets a line naming its owner.

## Tests

`tests/reg/brw_mixed_word_slot.bend` is a borrow witness with three readers: the issue's `hits`; `ons`, which passes the `Bool` to a call; and `sum` over a `List<&2, U32>`. `main` reads both lists after them. On main all three take; with this PR all three peek. Neither change alone makes `ons` peek.

I ran the gate locally on four shards: `PASS: 1692 / 1694`. The two failures, `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, expect "no display", and they fail on main here too because this Mac has a desktop session. Repo gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`. `tsc` reports the same 11 errors as on main.

title: A do-block bind or let written without its type gets a note on its error
body:
Closes #1787.

`parse_term_do_stmt` reads a statement's first term before it knows what the statement is, and only a `:` after a variable makes it a bind or a let. So a bind or a let written without its type is read as something else:
- `x <- m` becomes the exec form `A <- m`, with `x` as the type. That reports "a defined name" for a new `x`, and "expected Type, observed U32" when `x` is a `U32` parameter.
- `x = v` becomes the block's result, and the `=` then fails as "a pattern (a binder or a constructor)".

None of these errors mentioned the annotation.

**Change.** This is an error report only: the parser and checker are unchanged, and every program that parsed and checked before still does. `err_show` adds a note to an error at a statement's bare first name followed by `<-` or `=`, and only when it is the error an untyped bind or let produces:

```text
- expected : a defined name
- observed : x
Location: main
7>|     x <- IO.pure(U32, 1)
  |     ^
Note: in a do-block, x <- m runs m at type x; to bind its result, write x : A <- m.
```

- **`<-`:** the error is "a defined name" or an expected `Type`.
- **`=`:** the error is "a pattern (a binder or a constructor)", and the note reads `Note: in a do-block, a let names its type: x : A = v.` An ordinary `x = v` never hits that error, since a bare name is a valid pattern.

**History.** The first two commits refused these statements at parse time: first by the case of the name, then by its scope (a `vals` set of the def's value binders). Both rejected valid programs, such as the exec form at a type declared later in the file, and the first also refused the exec form at a lowercase type variable. 7fce6e4f replaces them with the note; see the comment thread.

**Tests** (`tests/parse/`):
- `do_bind_untyped`, `do_let_untyped` and `do_bind_untyped_param` are the three cases from the issue. Each pins main's error plus the note.
- `do_exec_type_var` (an exec form at a type variable) and `do_exec_lower_type` (at a lowercase type declared after its use) print `ok`.

**Gates:** test 1702/1702, repo 54/54, ping 72/72. perf is noise.

title: A def call short of its arguments converts up to eta (#1190)
body:
Addresses #1190.

Conversion treated eta inconsistently. A bare def name (`case "Ref"`) was eta-expanded, so `l == r` held when `l` and `r` agree on fresh arguments. A partial call like `l(U)` went through the stuck-call path, which compares the head by name, so `l(U) == r(U)` failed. With an inline `{==}`, the shared-cell merge in `compare_go` repointed `r`'s cell, so `Box<r(U)>` read as `Box<l(U)>`. As a result the inline proof was accepted and the same proof written as a named def was rejected.

`compare_go` (`bend2/bend.ts`) now does this, with no new helpers:
- `Var`, `Ref` and `App` are one case. A single loop walks both spines while either side is an `App`, compares the argument pairs, and counts each side's arguments. After the loop, the two sides are `same` if both spines had the same length, every argument pair matched, and the heads match (same variable, same def name, or otherwise equal).
- If they are not `same` and a head is a `Ref` short of its def's arity (`book.tlds[k].n`), both sides get that many fresh arguments and are compared again. A bare def is a call with zero arguments. Eta runs only after a failed comparison, so terms that already compare equal never pay for it.
- `Mat` keeps its own case, as on main.
- The first pass (`RIGID`, empty book) sees every def as arity 0, so it never expands and calls still compare by name there.

Doing the eta in `term_wnf` instead (a short call reduces to a lambda) was tried and rejected: it changes partial calls outside conversion, and `tests/check/template_inst_cycle.bend` hangs.

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| inline `make()({==})` | accepted | accepted |
| named `make()(proof())` | rejected | accepted |
| `{l(U) == r(U) : Type -> Type}` | rejected | accepted |
| `x: Box<r(U)>` returned as `Box<l(U)>` | rejected | accepted |
| `r(A,B) = B` (really different), inline `{==}` | rejected | rejected |
| `r(A,B) = B`, `{l(U) == r(U)}` | rejected | rejected |

Tests: `tests/check/partial_call_eta.bend` (the issue's example and its variants) and `tests/check/partial_call_eta_distinct.bend` (the different-`r` case, which must fail).

Gates (macolas, on 749eb6d3): repo 54/54, test 1699/1699, safe `tests` 1712 files: agree 1101, false reject 0, timeout 0. Not run: ping, perf gate, `tsc`, CUDA, Linux.

Cost: checker benches, main vs this PR, 9 interleaved rounds on one machine (median s): compute_1600 .529/.523, defs_12800 .324/.320, generics_3200 .409/.408, proofs_3200 .857/.858 (15 rounds: .850/.851), trees_400 .641/.641. The first version (ccbcfbb7, eta before the switch with `term_unapply`) was 4-9% slower on all five.

— written by an AI agent (Unii) for @nicolas-abril

title: Remove the Metal lane spill (#1439): `bend -o` of a `!` program built 17% slower
body:
Removes the functional part of #1439 (40402b42, shipped in 2.0.38); its other changes (the token cuts across `comp.ts`) stay.

## What goes

- `WL_ROOM(N, D)` → `WL_ROOM(N)`: a full lane errors with `ERR_DEEP` again instead of calling `lane_spill`
- `lane_spill` itself
- the work loop's unspill at `FID_EXIT`
- `tests/compile/bang_lane_spill.bend`

## Why

The perf gate fails its COMPILER column on main, two runs out of two: symreg **1.16x**, merkle **1.17x**.

Bisected over `v2.0.37..main` on one M4 mini (median of 7 `bend main.bend -o main` of `bench/runtime/symreg` after a warm build; each measure repeated within ~1%): **0.747s** at `10256a7b`, **0.793s** at `40402b42`, and the same on a second mini. The emitted C and its `cc` step cost the same at both; the whole ~45 ms is the Metal GPU program's build (`./main +RTS --gpu-build`, which `bend -o` runs for any `!` program): **0.257s → 0.300s (+17%)**, since `lane_spill` joins the device code.

With this PR, on the same mini: main **0.791 / 0.795s**, this branch **0.749 / 0.750s**.

## Gates

- repo: **54 / 54**
- test: **1697 / 1697**
- perf: symreg **1.08x / 1.10x**, merkle **1.14x / 1.14x** (two runs). Each run still had two red cells, which are not this change:
  - editdist PAR-CPU **1.25x** in both: the emitted C differs from the full revert's (which read 0.96x) only in two comments, and built from either commit it runs 0.378-0.380s on the same mini. The gate does not log which node ran a cell, but node 31, in the gate's slot, was running two orphaned `bend --checkup` processes from an earlier test-gate shard at 100% CPU each, the likeliest cause.
  - checker generics_3200 1.28x in one run, defs_12800 1.18x in the other: one-offs, they pass in every other run.

## Cost

#1393 and #1394 come back: non-tail recursion under `!` faults at 1023 frames on Metal. The spill can return in a form whose cost only a program that needs it pays.

title: Build constructors before the calls that fill them (constructor tails and forks)
body:
A clean rewrite of the idea in #1793 (tail modulo cons), sequential path only.

## What

A def whose body ends in a constructor that boxes a call's result once now builds that constructor **before** the call, and the call fills the field.

- **One call** (`t = f(p); Link{t}`): list, string and chain builders (`List.map`, append, a `Link` chain, a `String` builder) run as loops with constant stack, and reuse the cell they consume: `List.map` over a list allocates and frees nothing.
- **A fork** whose constructor is made only of its calls' results (`l r = f(a) g(b); Node{l, r}`, each once, in box fields): the node is built before the first call, reusing the consumed node, and every call fills its own field. A child that is itself a constructor tail writes its root straight into the parent's field.

## How

`bend2/comp.ts`:

- `ctr_hole` finds a call's field: a non-hot, non-Array `Ctr` that holds the result once, in a `BOX` field, with the segment and the callee returning one `BOX`.
- **One call** (`emit_fork`'s sequential arm): `emit_dest` emits the constructor with an empty placeholder (`node_fill` skips the store), hands over the consumed node's spare, then `WL_DEST(root, field)` and the existing tail jump.
- **Fork** ("tree" in `emit_fork`): `emit_dest` builds the node before the first call and publishes the root through `WL_DEST` to the last call's field. Each earlier call's frame holds its field (the first frame also holds the node, which later continuations read at its fixed stack offset), and its continuation stores the result there. The last call pops the fork's words and tail-jumps. Values the fork drops are freed there, where the join would have freed them.
- Runtime: a `Dst~put` frame `[root, field, FID]` stores the returned value into the field and returns the root. A fork's continuations are **dst segments** with the same layout (field just under the fid): they take the fids right after `Dst~put`, so `WL_DEST` recognizes any of them with one unsigned range check, writes the root into that field and points the frame at its own field, or else pushes a `Dst~put`.
- Unchanged: the `!seq` heap continuation, the fork's parallel arm and its join (whose parameters the tree rebuilds in the same order), `WL_RETN`. No new tag, no bits packed into continuation words.

Two `comp.ts: shed tokens with no output change` commits make room under the 66k cap (type aliases, an `op()` helper, a variadic `file_push`, inlined single-use locals, redundant checks dropped, tighter comments). Over every test, bench and demo, the first leaves JS byte-identical and changes C only in runtime comments; the second leaves C and JS byte-identical.

## Measured

Gates on main 5ce1e07f: repo 54/54 (`comp.ts` 65,989 / 66,000), test 1699/1699, ping 73/73, safe 0 false rejects. Perf fails only `histogram:PAR` in both runs, which main fails in both runs too.

Perf against main, best of two cluster runs each:

| bench | SEQ | PAR | GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| tree-radix | 3.688 → 3.114 (−16%) | 0.652 → 0.532 (−18%) | 1.118 → 0.820 (−27%) |
| kmeans | 3.744 → 3.711 | 0.771 → 0.771 | 0.638 → 0.557 (−13%) |
| lexer | 1.940 → 1.953 | 0.353 → 0.342 | **2.598 → 0.747 (−71%)** |
| tree-bitonic | 5.459 → 5.387 | 1.305 → 1.285 | 1.699 → 1.660 |
| tree-matmul | 1.926 → 1.880 (−2%) | 0.385 → 0.379 (−2%) | 0.858 → 0.931 (**+9%**) |

Everything else is within noise. tree-matmul GPU is the one cost: +5% to +9% across runs (median of six alternating runs on one mini: 0.877 → 0.922). Building each `Qd` before its four `add` kids, rather than after, is the difference there. The gate's tree-radix compile cell (0.515 → 0.721 s) is placement: the same build on one mini, alternating with each tree's compiler, takes 0.72–0.84 s on main and 0.71–0.76 s here.

Tests: `tests/compile/ctor_tail_dest.bend` (a box between word fields, a mutual even/odd chain, `List.map` in place, a three-way fork filled in turn, and a shared result that must keep the old order) and `ctor_tail_dest_bang.bend` (a chain, a left fork whose left kids nest, and `!` kids meeting at a join, on each lane). Twelve probe programs also match main at 1 and 8 threads and on Metal, including one that drops a field at every fork node (same output and peak RSS as main).

title: fix(lsp): preserve grouped semicolon body alignment
body:
## Problem and fix

A valid parenthesized array-update sequence prints `[9, 8]`, but formatting a continuation after `;` can move it away from its required column. The formatted program then fails to parse; the shared layout fingerprint accepts that output.

Let semicolons start the existing scoped body pins, as nested lambdas already do. This removes the special semicolon branch while retaining delimiter, argument-comma, and type-argument boundaries. Rename the existing scope stack and update its comment to cover both openers.

## Blast radius

Two files in `tools/bend-fmt-lsp`: the inline-body scan in `src/formatter.ts` and fixtures in its existing CLI-backed tests. The change affects alignment before the existing fingerprint check. No public API or language compatibility break; no parser, compiler, runtime, gate, or dependency changes.

## Regression evidence

Three added fixtures cover grouped array updates, generic commas, and a leading closer followed by another argument. Each original must print `[9, 8]`; all three indentation styles must actively change the source, preserve that output, and be idempotent. They reuse the existing test harness.

The runtime paragraph's `+`-only wording can make an affine value appear free of reference-counting costs. Clarify the concrete trigger: copying a value of a datatype makes all its nodes count their fields, including nodes used without sharing.

title: BendRT: a hot type counts the fields of every node, shared or not
body:
#1812 fixed the guide's "only `+` values carry a reference count"; BendRT said the same in two places. §4.2 claimed "an unshared value carries no count anywhere", two sentences before saying hot types seal every stored field at build time, and §11 claimed "the unshared majority of a program" has no count traffic. Neither holds for a hot datatype: once any value of it is copied, every node of that type seals its fields, `&1` ones included (#1559).

Both passages now say it per type: §4.2 drops the claim and says hot types pay on every node, shared or not; §11 says counts are minted for the types the analysis finds shared. §3.1 already defines hotness this way and is unchanged. The PDF is rebuilt with typst 0.15.1 and is still 6 pages.

Closes #1559.

title: A long loop over F32 is a call on the host too: nbody 1.19x SEQ, 1.15x PAR (#1240)
body:
Closes #1240. #1413 already fixed that issue's GPU half: raytrace's and nbody's long loops are calls on the device. This PR fixes the half that remained, nbody on the CPU.

## The bug

On the host every spin is `INLINE`. nbody's integration loop (`spin_4`: 15 KB, 21 F32 loop-carried words, one call site) is inlined into `WL_FID_batch`, whose setup computes four PRNG streams in 4-lane vectors. clang's SLP vectorizer carries those vectors into the loop: in the inlined build, 233 of the function's 571 instructions are vector or lane-shuffle ops, and two of the three pair kernels run as `fsqrt.2s`/`fdiv.2s`. As a separate function, the state arrives as 22 scalar arguments, SLP leaves the loop scalar (0 vector instructions in 313), and it runs 18% faster.

SLP is the whole difference. With `-fno-slp-vectorize`, the inlined build runs as fast as the call: 4.880 s against 4.840 s, and 5.746 s with SLP on. Register pressure, the guess in #1240, isn't the cause.

## The fix

A spin of `SPIN_FAR` characters or more that loops (`seg.spin`) with an F32 among its live parameters is `FAR`, a call on both lanes. On the device `FAR` is what `DFAR` already was, so device programs don't change.

Across the 1,729 benches, demos and tests, 4 spins change, in nbody (`spin_4`), raytrace (`spin_18`) and `app_slash_boss_3d` (`spin_39`, `spin_53`). The emitted C of every other program is byte-identical to main, and every program builds or fails as it does on main.

## Numbers

Apple M4, built with `gates/perf.ts`'s cc lines, each cell the median of 5 interleaved runs, outputs identical:

| bench | mode | main | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nbody | SEQ-CPU | 5.769 s | 4.853 s | 1.19x |
| nbody | PAR-CPU (16) | 0.827 s | 0.717 s | 1.15x |
| nbody | PAR-GPU | 0.159 s | 0.159 s | 1.00x |
| raytrace | SEQ-CPU | 4.538 s | 4.638 s | 0.98x |
| raytrace | PAR-CPU (16) | 0.713 s | 0.727 s | 0.98x |
| raytrace | PAR-GPU | 0.365 s | 0.365 s | 1.00x |

`gates/perf.ts`, alternating with main (4 runs each):
- **nbody PAR-CPU:** 0.717 s in both runs where the cell ran on this branch, against 0.831–0.835 s on main.
- **raytrace PAR-CPU:** 0.702–0.703 s against 0.691–0.695 s.
- **GPU and COMPILER cells:** within noise on both benches.
- **Failing cells:** 4–18 cells per run read `err` (`exit 127` or an empty build error) on both main and this branch, in the same bench/mode pairs, nbody SEQ-CPU among them every time. That looks like a cluster problem, not this change.

`bend -o` time doesn't change: `app_slash_boss_3d` takes 9.59–9.84 s on main and 9.59–9.60 s here.

## Alternatives measured and rejected

All 17 benches, SEQ-CPU and PAR-CPU (16):

| rule | nbody | raytrace | rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-fno-slp-vectorize` | 1.18x / 1.15x | 1.00x | within ±3% |
| host `FAR` for every loop with F32 state | 1.19x / 1.17x | 0.75x / 0.76x | unchanged |
| host `FAR` for every loop | 1.16x / 1.14x | 0.75x | terrain 0.90x |
| empty-asm barrier on a float loop's inputs (inlined, but opaque to clang) | 1.16x / 1.14x | 0.73x | not run |

- **The broader `FAR` rules and the barrier:** raytrace's `spin_13` and `spin_16` are 8-iteration F32 loops called once per ray. Inlined, clang unrolls and specializes them at each call site. Behind a call, or behind a barrier, it can't, and raytrace loses 25%. Requiring `SPIN_FAR` keeps them inline; only long loops become calls.
- **`-fno-slp-vectorize`:** matches this PR on nbody, but turns SLP off for every program. On synthetic loops with independent float lanes, SLP gains up to 1.48x as a call (8 lanes) and 1.18x inlined (4 lanes, as complex pairs). This PR keeps SLP on, and lets a long loop's vectorization depend on the loop body alone.

## Checks

- **Gates:** repo 54/54, test 1697/1697, ping 72/72; perf as above.
- **Size:** `comp.ts` is 65,690 ttok (main 65,612, cap 66,000).

**Not run:** Linux/x86, CUDA hosts. `app_slash_boss_3d` builds but is interactive, so its two changed spins aren't timed.

title: comp.ts: nothing reads emitted text, pure mains print through Bend
body:
The simplification half of #1601, split out so it can be reviewed apart from the compile-speed change (#1601, which goes on top of this). `compile_book` keeps main's loop: it emits every def again until a pass adds no fact.

Rebased on main (34c7abbb). comp.ts is 65,974 ttok, under the 66,000 cap (main: 65,996). Gates on a Mac: repo 54/54, test 1747/1747, perf 124/124, ping 80/81 (the one failure, the BendHub hyphenated-entry check, fails on main too).

The rebase conflicted only in comp.ts. #1792's shared-allocation hoisting in `emit_chain` is kept as main has it, so one place still reads emitted text: a regex finds each arm's leading `heap_alloc`. Replacing it structurally is left for a follow-up.

**Fitting the cap** (second commit, no change to what a program does)
- A spin is declared before the spins are defined, so the C file needs no callee-first order and `unit_order` goes. The prototype comes from the spin's own `Seg.head`, not from its emitted text.
- `unit_emit` alone fills a unit; `main_pure` opens its own file; `def_answer` is inlined at its one call; a Nat match pushes each row where it is built; `fact_add` drains its implications in one call.
- JS: a `$$k` entry is a `const` arrow in both cases; a write of 64 KiB or more joins the held output and is flushed with it instead of going out alone.
- Comments from the first commit are tightened.
- Checked by emitting all 1,791 tests and demos with both commits: C differs only by the spin prototypes and the order of spins; JS differs only in the three changes above.

**Facts are one set**
- `own`, `stat`, `ctr`, `type`, `fam`, `arg` and `open` are strings in one set read through `fact()`, replacing `Hot`, `FL.stat`, `FL.own`, the `brws` memo and the hand-written reset of ten fields per pass. A fact that only leads to other facts is an implication (`fact_when`), not a dependency.
- Each def and spin keeps its own output (segments, lends, closures), so a pass replaces a def's output instead of clearing the file's.

**Nothing reads the text it emitted**
- A value carries the borrowed root of each box (`Val.rs`), replacing a lookup of the word's string in a scope map. #1805's rule (only a box roots) sits in `val_new`.
- A Nat's Succs are counted on the term (`nat_peel`), not by regexes over emitted `nat_chk(... + n)`.
- A table's rows are words on both lanes, folded on values: an F32 constant keeps its bits, and an op over rows runs its JS on their values only if it calls nothing past `Math.fround` and `Math.imul`. The C lane no longer runs JS text that the JS lane printed.
- A local is a name `name_local` made, not a name's shape. An op's argument is held in a local unless it is a variable or a constant (`op_bare`), replacing the bracket counting.
- A JS call that waits on its callee calls the callee's entry (`$$k`), declared after the last def, instead of a marker rewritten by a regex over the finished program. A JS closure captures the variables free in its term. A line is indented as it is pushed.

**Match arms that rebuild their scrutinee read it**
- A U32, F32, Nat or Char default arm often rebuilds its scrutinee from the bits and fields it knows. `arm_self` reads each such rebuild as the scrutinee itself; an arm that no longer reads its fields binds none.
- The JS lane then needs no views (`FL.views`, `js_view`, `word_u32` go).

**A pure main prints through Bend code**
- It printed three ways: a descriptor of main's type built by the compiler, a C printer and a JS printer. Now a pure main of type T builds as a Bend printer of main's value: `main_pure` writes it as Bend source, parses it into a copy of the book and checks it. The printer writes as it goes, so a 3M-element `List<U32>` peaks at 49.6 MB on C as on main (49.4 MB); an Array of Data is read in place by index (`Array.write` on C, `Array.show` on JS). A pure main prints imported types too.
- Base gains `Char.quote`, `String.quote`, `F32.show.dot`, `U32.hex`, `Array.write` and `Array.show`.
- JS holds stdout off a terminal and writes it before a wait, an error, an exit, a `File.write` or at 64 KiB.

**Smaller things**
- The term caches live as long as the file; the fold cache is cleared per def, as a hit costs no fuel.
- A spin is one per def. `lay_eq` walks the layout DAG instead of comparing JSON. Reserved names are refused before anything else, on both lanes.

**Compile time** (C and JS emit, median of 5, M4 Max): boss_3d 1,127 ms on main, 587 ms here; the 35 demos and benches that build, 3.04 s → 1.89 s in total.

**Verification**
- JS output is byte-identical to #1601's on all 1,820 programs; C matches it up to the order of segments, spins, tables and static nodes, except 17 programs where a def nothing reaches adds a fact here (#1601 never emits such defs); those 17 pass on all three lanes.
- Tests added: `f32_table_math_op`, `f32_neg_const_js`, `const_array_op_js`, `array_elements`, `imported_adt`, `imported_adt_alias`, `stdout_file_order`.
- Test added: `once_box_return`. Review found that the first commit had dropped main's `once` guard (`ret !== BOX || sc.seg.ret === BOX`, from 30e5b936). Without it, a once-called def with an index-dependent return fused into a caller typed at one index, and the C build crashed (`TypeError` on `v.lay.arms`). The third commit restores the guard.
- Perf gate on the cluster: 123/124, every runtime and checker cell within 1.15x. The one miss is merkle's compiler time (1.18x; 1.15x on an earlier run). Locally, merkle builds in 778 ms here against 780 ms on main (median of 7), so it reads as node noise. An earlier run lost 8 SEQ-CPU cells to exit 127 (the timing wrapper never ran); a rerun measured them all, matching main.

title: A full device lane moves its stack to the heap, so non-tail recursion under ! goes past 1,023 frames
body:
Fixes #1393. Fixes #1394. Follow-up to #1439, which #1809 reverted.

Today on main, a lane on the GPU has a 2,048-word stack (`STAK_LEN`), and once it fills, the next call posts `ERR_DEEP` and the run stops. A non-tail `List.append` under `!` fails at 1,023 frames (#1393), an unbalanced fork tree such as `two!(365n)` fails (#1394), a split-then-append recursion fails at 2,046 elements, and [Unbalanced Tree Search (UTS)](https://sourceforge.net/projects/uts-benchmark/) (`uts-compact`) exits with `ERR_DEEP` on the GPU. The host has no such limit.

This PR lets a full lane keep going. A call that may leave no room for the next frame copies the lane's whole stack to a 16 KB heap block and leaves a 3-word exit frame at the stack's base. A return into that frame gives back whole defs, walked down from the top of the block, until about half a stack, and leaves the rest under the exit frame for later returns.

## What a call pays

- Every non-tail call on the device checks, after its frame is pushed and its arguments are loaded, whether the widest frame any device segment pushes still fits: one compare against `STAT_OFF` minus that width (3 to 12 words across `bench/runtime`, 242 in the wide test). The width is taken once over the live device segments, after `c_header` checks their arity. When the frame doesn't fit, the call sets `rn = F | 1 << 16` (no call site reads `rn`) and jumps to `work_loop`'s `default:`, which spills and dispatches `F`; any other unknown fid still posts `ERR_FIDS`. Metal has no `goto`, so the jump goes through the switch.
- A self call compiles to a loop, so its check comes after the loop's parameters are set and copies them back to `r0..` only on the spill path; otherwise the loop would keep `r0..` live on every iteration.
- `lane_spill` and `lane_unspill` are out-of-line device functions. `FID_EXIT` handles a spill frame before it reads `FID_T`.

## Why a lane never writes past its stack

Between two checks a lane pushes at most one frame: a check passes only while the widest frame still fits, and after a call returns its continuation pushes one frame before the next check. A restore resumes the lane at about half a stack plus one def's words. A def has at most 493 words on the stack (a continuation takes at most 247 parameters, and every word a fork keeps to its end counts against its last continuation's), 443 in the wide test, so a lane resumes at about 1,520 words at most, below every threshold. Each def's words on the stack when a continuation's fid is on top (`FID_DEEP`, emitted only in device code) come from `emit_fork`.

## Limits

- Past 2^12 nested spills a lane posts the deep-stack error, so runaway recursion under `!` stops in 1 to 2 s. That is 64 MB of blocks a lane: about 25 lanes running away at once fill a 2 GB span and get the out-of-memory error first. A million-deep recursion takes about 1,000 spills.
- When a spill cannot get its block, the lane stops with the out-of-memory error before it copies anything.
- A loop that keeps crossing the threshold from well below still spills on each crossing: `sawtooth_over`, a loop whose callee recurses 1,100 deep, takes 1.82 s on the M4 for 3,000 iterations, where main faults.

## Effects on shared code

- Host: `WL_ROOM` and `WL_FULL` expand to nothing and 0, and `FID_DEEP` is device-only. `objdump -d` shows the same host machine code as main for symreg, merkle, queens, raytrace and tree-matmul, apart from addresses.
- Device: every return through `FID_EXIT` tests `wf == FID_EXIT` first.
- Device: `ERR_DEEP` now means 2^12 spills, not a full stack. `tests/io/stack_fault_trap.bend`'s comment says so; its output is unchanged.
- `FID_DEEP` joins `FID_T` among the reserved names.

comp.ts goes from 66,000 to 66,799 ttok (+799), so the repo gate stays red until the cap in `gates/repo.ts` goes up.

## Tests

`tests/compile/bang_lane_spill.bend` covers a 5,000-deep `List.append` (#1393), `two!(365n)` (#1394), a fork whose spills come at its second call while it holds words from its first, the review's loop a few words under the top (its first call spills once here; giving back the whole stack spilled 6,000 times), and a split-then-append recursion over 4,096 elements. `tests/compile/bang_lane_spill_wide.bend` covers a def with 443 words on the stack. Both pass on Metal, on CUDA, natively, interpreted and as JS. All 44 runnable tests with a `!` pass on an M4 mini and on an RTX 3090; main fails only the two spill tests, and the same two other tests don't build to a runnable program on either. [bend-bench](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench) `compiler-check` builds and runs every test natively on both: 863 pass on main and 862 here, the same 19 print something else and the same 920 do not build to a runnable program on either; the one difference, `tests/io/tcp_send_slow_peer.bend`, timed out once while the machine's load average passed 100 and passes 3 of 3 runs alone. Checking and emitting C take the same time in total (0.991x and 0.975x).

## Metal (Mac mini M4)

Measured with bend-bench's [`metal/compare.sh`](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/blob/41840f6bda8cf4207f8446fc5fbfbc971add852d/metal/compare.sh) and summarized by `bend-bench metal-report` ([how to run it](https://github.com/wakamex/bend-bench/blob/41840f6bda8cf4207f8446fc5fbfbc971add852d/RUNNING.md#metal-on-apple-silicon)), on a Mac mini M4 (10-core GPU, macOS 26.7.2), main 00d29f44 against this PR:

- The review's program: 0.136 s on main and 0.133 s here at depth 2,040, 0.137 and 0.128 s at 2,000. A million-deep recursion takes 0.77 s, the 100,000-element split-append 0.19 s, and a loop calling across the threshold 0.10 s, where main faults; `deep!(1000000000n)` stops with the deep-stack error after 1.3 s.

The largest increase is gameoflife (0.137 to 0.143 s, +4.4%); the largest decreases are tree-matmul (-20.0%) and histogram (-16.1%).
- Runtime of the same 17 programs in 4 blocks of A B B A / B A A B. A block's ratio is main's time over this PR's, so above 1x means this PR is faster; with 4 blocks, the interval is the lowest and highest block, so a verdict means all 4 agree:

| Program | Main (s) | This PR (s) | Median block ratio | Lowest to highest block | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| bfs | 0.772 | 0.770 | 0.997x | 0.982x to 1.002x | no detected change |
| editdist | 0.467 | 0.476 | 0.994x | 0.982x to 1.002x | no detected change |

Every form of that check I tried costs histogram the same 2%, including the earlier one before the parameter copy, which makes queens slower than this form does. tree-radix is 0.2% slower. I haven't found why queens, symreg and lexer get faster.

## CUDA (RTX 3090, CUDA 13.1)

title: A native spin polls the error word every 4096 steps, not every step (#1776)
body:
The error poll in a flat loop put a counter and a branch in the hot path. On
CUDA, ptxas then stopped unrolling the loop and yielded on every step
(#1776). It is one of the two costs a bang pays on its main pass (#1781).

This moves the poll out of the step: the device's native spin runs its body
in an inner loop of 4096 steps and reads the error word once, after them.

**The period does not change.** `err_spun` read the word every 4096 steps
too, so an error is caught after the same number of steps as before; only
the branch leaves the hot path. Both numbers have to move together, so the
second one is a parameter of the first now (`WL_NSPIN`'s comment says so).

The program measured (#1776's file, five rounds of 16,384 leaves at 2M steps
each, the three builds alternated, the best of each):

```
import Base

def flat_l(k: Nat, +x: F32, acc: F32) -> F32:
  match k:
    case 0n: acc
    case 1n+q: flat_l(q, x, ((acc * 0.999 : F32) + x : F32))

def flat_tree(d: Nat, +k: Nat, +i: U32) -> F32:
  match d:
    case 0n: flat_l(k, U32.to_f32(U32.and(i, 7)), 0.0)
    case 1n++q:
      a b = flat_tree(q, k, (i * 2 : U32)) flat_tree(q, k, ((i * 2 : U32) + 1 : U32))
      (a + b : F32)

def rounds(n: Nat) -> F32:
  match n:
    case 0n: 0.0
    case 1n+q: F32.add(flat_tree!(14n, 2000000n, 0), rounds(q))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(F32.show(rounds(5n)))
```

On an RTX 5060 (driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4):

| | ms |
| --- | --- |
| upstream/main | 648 |
| this branch | 332 (1.95x) |
| with the poll removed | 324 |

So this branch is 2.5% off a spin that never polls. (On a hot GPU the ratio
is larger — 1233 ms against 533 ms when the card was at 85 C — so the
numbers above come from an idle card, and the alternation shares the drift.)

A memory-bound loop is not affected, as expected: `tests/run/stencil3d.bend`
takes 175 ms against 172 ms. The poll is not what makes those loops slow.

## What this does not touch, and why

The spin **segments** and the dispatcher (`work_loop`) keep the plain poll.
`wpoll` there is one variable shared by the dispatcher and every segment, so
giving both the split would have one loop reset the other's count; it needs a
counter per segment. It also matters less: a segment loop only iterates for a
def with a tail self-call that is not flat, and such a def does its non-flat
work (a fork, a bang, a closure apply) on every step, so the poll is a much
smaller share of it than it was of a flat loop of arithmetic, which is where
the 20x was measured. If a program shows otherwise, the same shape applies
there with a counter of its own.

Only CUDA is measured. The change is on the device path, so Metal gets it
too, and I could not time an M4 here: the pins on `apple_m4` are the ones
that would say whether Metal gains like CUDA or something else.

## Verification

- Every test builds and runs the same: 1197 / 1707 pass with the CUDA lane,
  the same 55 that already fail on `main` (mostly tests that need a network).
- The host's C is the same: `clang -S` gives byte-identical assembly.
- The `INLINE`/`DFAR` choice is made from a spin body's length, and this adds
  two lines to every spin, so a spin near the 8192-character threshold could
  have flipped to a call. It does not: 830 test files, all 17
  `bench/runtime` programs and 18 demo files emit the same choice as `main`,
  0 flips.
- `tests/run/spin_poll.bend` is a spin that runs past the poll's period.

`bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 54 / 54`; `comp.ts` is at 65,967 ttok locally
(the CI tokenizer counts a few more of the same bytes, so there is margin).
The branch is rebased on current `main`.

The review fix is on top of `f95f2bc4`: the `#if BEND_RTC` split moved out of
`#if DEVICE`, so the host and Metal alias `WL_SPIN` and only CUDA gets the
`do/while` pair. That fixes the host build failure (`WL_NSPIN`/`WL_NSPUN`
undeclared on CPU-only builds) and both `spin_poll.bend` (160000) and
`spin_fault.bend` (message, exit 1) pass on the host here.

Separate follow-up: #1880 adds `Array.get_unchecked` for the CPU mask
discussion in #1781.

title: File.open: a "x" mode that creates a file and fails if it exists
body:
### What Bend should do

`File.open` could accept `"x"`: create a new file for writing, and fail if the path already exists. In POSIX terms this is `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL`.

```python
c : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File> <- File.open(path, "x")
match c:
  case Done{value}:  # the file is new, and this writer made it
    ...
  case Fail{error}:  # the message is "File exists": another writer made it first
    (code, message) = error
    IO.print(message)
```

### Why

At de26a917, `File.open` accepts `"r"`, `"w"`, and `"a"`, and any other mode fails with `EINVAL` (`bend2/effs/file_open.c`, `bend2/effs/file_open.js`). No mode refuses a path that exists. So a program that must not overwrite another writer's file has to check first and then open, and two writers can both pass the check. With `"x"`, the kernel decides in one step.

`O_CREAT | O_EXCL` also refuses a symbolic link at the last path component, which a durable writer wants too.

### Is this Base or a hub package?

WONTFIX.txt says Base holds only the effects no library can build (#1106, #1117), and a library can build an exclusive create as a foreign effect. I am asking anyway because `"x"` completes the POSIX modes of an effect Base already has, without adding a new effect. If it belongs on the hub, that answers it, and we will ship it there.

### What we checked

We applied an 8-line change to `bend2/effs/file_open.c` and `bend2/effs/file_open.js` on `main` (de26a917) and ran one test on the interpreter, the JS lane, and the C lane. All three print the same lines:
1. `"x"` on a new path opens it, and we write `keep`.
2. `"x"` on the same path returns `Fail`, with message `File exists`.
3. Reading the file back gives `keep`, so the refused open changed nothing.
4. `"wx"` still returns `Invalid argument`.

With the patch, `tests/io/file_open_mode.bend` still passes, with `"r+"` and `"w+"` refused (interpreter and JS lane at de26a917; all three lanes at v2.0.38). If you want the change, we would extend that test rather than add a file. Its header lists the modes, so it changes with the patch anyway.

Two details for a reviewer:
- Node's `"wx"` adds `O_TRUNC`. On a file that the call just created, truncation does nothing.
- The test needs a random path, because Bend has no `unlink` to delete the file afterwards.

<details><summary>The patch (8 lines) and the test</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/bend2/effs/file_open.c b/bend2/effs/file_open.c
index f46383140..fbef8f07a 100644
--- a/bend2/effs/file_open.c
+++ b/bend2/effs/file_open.c
@@ -11,6 +11,11 @@ static int file_open_mode(const char* mode) {
   if (strcmp(mode, "a") == 0) {
     return O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND;
   }
+  // "x": create, and FAIL if the path already exists. This is the one primitive a durable writer needs to make
+  // overwriting impossible (the carrier's L-C3); every other mode here truncates or appends.
+  if (strcmp(mode, "x") == 0) {
+    return O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL;
+  }
   return -1;
 }
 
diff --git a/bend2/effs/file_open.js b/bend2/effs/file_open.js
index 2b98f8fb4..710c191f7 100644
--- a/bend2/effs/file_open.js
+++ b/bend2/effs/file_open.js
@@ -6,12 +6,13 @@ function file_open(path, mode) {
   if (name.includes(0)) {
     return io_fail(process.platform === "darwin" ? 92 : 84);
   }
-  if (!["r", "w", "a"].includes(mode)) {
+  if (!["r", "w", "a", "x"].includes(mode)) {
     return io_fail(22);
   }
   try {
+    // "x" is Node's "wx": create exclusively, failing with EEXIST when the path exists.
     const fd = require("fs")
-      .openSync(name.length > 0 ? Buffer.from(name) : "", mode, 0o644);
+      .openSync(name.length > 0 ? Buffer.from(name) : "", mode === "x" ? "wx" : mode, 0o644);
     return io_done(fd);
   } catch (e) {
     return io_fail(-e.errno);
```

```python
# Review test (Genga): "x" creates a fresh path, refuses an existing one with EEXIST (matched, not tried), the refused
# open leaves the file's bytes alone, and Node's own "wx" spelling stays EINVAL in every lane.
import Base

law answer:
  for r: Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File>
  IO(Unit)

def answer(r):
  match r:
    case Done{value}:
      do IO<Unit>:
        u : Unit <- File.close(value)
        IO.print("opened")
    case Fail{error}:
      (code, message) = error
      IO.print(message)

law write_go:
  for w: File & Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), Unit>
  IO(Unit)

def write_go(w):
  (f, r) = w
  do IO<Unit>:
    u : Unit <- IO.pass(Unit, r)
    File.close(f)

law read_go:
  for m: File & Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), String>
  IO(Unit)

def read_go(m):
  (f, r) = m
  do IO<Unit>:
    data : String <- IO.pass(String, r)
    p    : Unit <- IO.print(data)
    File.close(f)

law first:
  for r: Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File>
  IO(Unit)

def first(r):
  match r:
    case Done{value}:
      do IO<Unit>:
        w : File & Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), Unit> <- File.write(value, "keep")
        x : Unit <- write_go(w)
        IO.print("created")
    case Fail{error}:
      (code, message) = error
      IO.print(message)

def at(n: U32) -> String:
  String.append("/tmp/bend_genga_excl_", U32.show(n))

def run(+n: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    a : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File> <- File.open(at(n), "x")
    b : Unit <- first(a)
    c : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File> <- File.open(at(n), "x")
    d : Unit <- answer(c)
    f : File <- IO.try(File, File.open(at(n), "r"))
    m : File & Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), String> <- File.read(f, 64)
    e : Unit <- read_go(m)
    g : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), File> <- File.open(at(n), "wx")
    answer(g)

law main:
  IO(U32)

def main():
  do IO<U32>:
    r : Result<&1, &1, (U32 & String), U32> <- IO.random_u32()
    n : U32 <- IO.pass(U32, r)
    u : Unit <- run(n)
    return 0

#|created
#|File exists
#|keep
#|Invalid argument
```
</details>

title: BendRT paper: the CPU corpus size and the JS request path differ from comp.ts; a question about the CUDA cube
body:
Three passages in the BendRT paper (`bend2/docs/BendRT/main.typ`) disagree with `bend2/comp.ts` on `main` (de26a917). I'm filing this as an issue rather than a PR, since the papers are yours to word. Each item has a suggested sentence in case it helps.

**1. The CPU corpus size (main.typ:297).** The paper says the host "reserves 8 TB". `corpus_setup` maps `1ull << 33` (8 GiB) on the CPU (comp.ts:5405), and `corpus_grow` doubles it in place while it is under `1ull << 43` (comp.ts:5393). So 8 TiB is the cap, not the start. On macOS arm64 (at e5527d5), `vmmap` of a running binary showed one 8 GiB reservation, with 128 KiB resident.
Suggested: "the host maps 8 GiB at start and doubles it in place as the heap fills, up to 8 TiB, with pages faulting in on touch".

**2. How a JS request reaches the loop (main.typ:528).** The paper says a request "unwinds to the loop as a thrown value". The JS emitter returns `{ $: <name>, args: [...], kont: (x) => ... }` (comp.ts:3236), and the loop continues with `op = op.kont(x)` (comp.ts:6552). At de26a917, `tests/run/js_loop_capture.bend -o loop.js` emits that object, and `bun loop.js` exits 0.
Suggested: "a request is returned to the loop as a tagged object carrying its continuation".

**3. A question: the cube on CUDA (main.typ:114, 296, 407-411).** The paper says the rings form "a 128 by 128 square, one ring per lane, the same on every target". On CUDA, `gpu_probe` sizes the cube from the L2 cache (comp.ts:5145): `CUBE_LOG = 31 - CLZ(clamp(l2 >> 16, 16, 128))`, and `RING_LEN` is `1 << (17 - CUBE_LOG)` (comp.ts:3543). On an NVIDIA TITAN RTX (6 MiB L2, Linux, at e5527d5), the probe printed `CUBE_LOG=6`, so a 128 by 64 cube of 8192 rings with 2048 slots each. A Mac printed 128 by 128, with 16384 rings of 1024 slots. The total slot count is the same.
Which one is intended? If the code is right, the passage and its neighbours (":114 a fixed 128 by 128 grid", ":296 the 2^14 task rings", ":411 1024 slots") could say that the CUDA cube is sized from L2. If "the same on every target" is the design, then the probe is what changes.

The cited `comp.ts` lines and paper lines were re-read at de26a917. Items 1 and 3 were measured at e5527d5.

**AI disclosure:** a person asked for this check. Claude (an AI) compared the paper with the code, ran the macOS checks, and wrote this issue. Another Claude session ran the CUDA probe on the person's Linux machine. The person reviewed it and asked for it to be filed.

title: BendRT: the corpus grows from 8 GB, JS requests return, CUDA sizes the cube (#1822)
body:
#1822 found three BendRT passages that disagree with `comp.ts`. The code is the intended behaviour in each case, so this PR changes the paper.

- **Corpus (§4):** the host maps 8 GB and doubles it in place up to 8 TB (`corpus_setup` maps `1ull << 33`, `corpus_grow` stops at `1ull << 43`). The paper said it reserves a flat 8 TB.
- **JS requests (§GPU/JS):** the emitter returns `{ $, args, kont }`, and the loop continues with `op.kont(x)`. The paper said requests unwind as a thrown value; nothing is thrown.
- **The cube (§1, §cube, §limits):** the paper said it is 128 by 128 "the same on every target". That holds on the CPU and Metal. On CUDA, `gpu_probe` sizes it to the L2: one 128-lane group per 64 KB, from 128 by 16 up to 128 by 128. `RING_LEN = 2^(17 - CUBE_LOG)`, so rings are up to 8192 slots deep and a cube always holds 2^21 slots. This is deliberate, per d8dba9e2 (sizing the bag to the chip) and a7e5e5c2 (Metal pinned back to 128). The corpus layout stays 128 by 128 everywhere, so "the $2^14$ task rings" in §4 is unchanged.

The PDF is rebuilt with typst 0.15.1 and is still 6 pages.

Closes #1822.

title: File.open takes "x": create a new file, fail if the path exists (#1821)
body:
Closes #1821.

`File.open(path, "x")` creates `path` for writing and returns `Fail` with `EEXIST` ("File exists") if the path already exists. Today the only way to avoid overwriting another writer's file is to check first and then open, and two writers can both pass that check. With `"x"` the kernel decides in one step. `O_EXCL` also refuses a symbolic link at the last path component.

This adds no new effect or name. It's one more value for the mode argument `File.open` and `File.open_bytes` already take. It completes their POSIX modes, and we stop there: no `"r+"`, `"w+"`, flags or permission argument.

- `bend2/effs/file_open.c`: `file_open_mode` maps `"x"` to `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL`.
- `bend2/effs/file_open.js`: `file_open_with` accepts `"x"` and passes Node's `"wx"` to `fs.openSync`. Node also sets `O_TRUNC` for `"wx"`, which does nothing on a file the same call just created. Node's own `"wx"` spelling still gets `EINVAL`.
- `tests/io/file_open_mode.bend`: `"wx"` is refused. `"x"` creates a random path and writes `keep`, a second `"x"` on that path is refused with `File exists`, and reading the file back gives `keep`. The path is random because Bend has no `unlink`, so each run leaves one `/tmp/bend_io_excl_*` file behind.

The patch and test follow the ones in #1821 by @animegolem.

Checked: the test gives the same output on the interpreter, JS and C lanes, and fails without the change. `gates/repo.ts` PASS 54 / 54, `gates/test.ts` PASS 1707 / 1707 on main 96c068f5.

title: A JS effect gets and answers Bend's own text and converts it itself; an export converts all of its text
body:
A C effect gets a `String` as a Bend term and turns it into bytes itself: `io_cstr` validates and writes U+FFFD for a Char that is no Unicode scalar, `io_cbuf` copies raw bytes, and `io_str` builds a text answer. The JS side now follows the same rule: an effect converts its own text, in both directions. Before this, the compiler's foreign-effect wrapper also ran `str_out` on top-level text arguments and `str_in` on text answers. That converted text twice on most paths (the wrapper, then `io_bytes`, and a third time in `get_env.js`), and it left nested text, such as `Process.run`'s `List(String)` args, to the effect anyway.

## Change
- **`comp.ts`:** an effect's wrapper no longer converts text: an effect gets and answers Bend's own text, at any depth, and converts it itself. A module export converts all of its text, at any depth.
  - `host()` becomes `host_in(A, x)`: `nat_in` for a `Nat`, `Math.fround` for an `F32`, applied to an effect's answer and to an export's arguments.
  - `run_lib` runs an export's arguments through `host_text(·, str_in, str_out)` and its answer through `host_text(·, str_out, str_in)`. The walk goes by value, not type: in the JS runtime only `Char` and `String` are strings, so every string it meets is Bend text. It therefore covers what a type-directed conversion can't: a polymorphic def (`poly(-A, x: A) -> A`), text in a ctor, list or array, and a function in either direction, which gets wrapped with the directions swapped for its arguments. On `main` only a top-level `String` or `Char` was converted.
  - A value with no text to change comes back as itself (`===`), so GUIDE.md's "an `Array` argument is the caller's own array, updated in place" still holds. A shared value is walked once (memoized by identity), so sharing can't make the walk exponential. Cost: a 1M-element `Array<U32>` takes 25 ms on Bun and 32 ms on Node per crossing.
- **Base effects:** each converts its own text.
  - `args.js` needs no `str_in`, and says why: Node and Bun decode argv as UTF-8, a bad byte as U+FFFD, so it can't hold a lone surrogate (checked with CESU-8 `ED A0 80` and `ED B0 80`, on Bun 1.3.14 and Node 26.3.1).
  - `get_env.js` answers through `str_in`, because `process.env` can be set from JS, and Bun keeps a lone surrogate set there.
  - `window_open.js` checks for a NUL in `str_out(title)`, as `window.c` runs `io_cstr` then `io_nul`. Bend's text for a non-scalar Char holds zeros (`Chr{55296}` is `"\udc00\^@\^[\^@"`), so a check on the raw title would read a NUL that isn't there.
  - A conversion that cannot change its text is left out: hosts go to `io_addr`, which already rejects whatever `str_out` would change; `Process.run`'s output is decoded UTF-8; a UDP peer's host is a dotted quad; `Window.open`'s message is ASCII.
  - `UDP.send_to` hands its unsent text back in `Fail` (and the `try_` twin in `Wait`) exactly, on both lanes. In C, `udp_send_to.c` reads the datagram without consuming it (`udp_send_buf`, `io_cbuf`'s walk done with `term_peek`) and keeps the value in `w->item`, which hands it back on Fail or Wait and drops it after a send. Before, the C lane rebuilt the value from the UTF-8 copy, so `Chr{55296}` came back as U+FFFD while JS gave 55296.
- **bend-lint (`tools/bend-lint/src/bend/effects.js`):** every String crossing the lint channel goes in with `str_in` and out with `str_out`, nested text included. That includes a source's text, which can be an editor's unsaved buffer.
- **`guide/EFFECTS.md`:** the JS section's text guidance, nested text included:
  - Text arrives Bend-encoded. Text leaving Bend goes through `io_bytes`/`str_out`; text coming in goes through `str_in`/`io_text`.
  - Bend's text is not a host string. A non-scalar Char is `\uDC00` and three 11-bit parts, which may be 0, so a check for a NUL, a length or a pattern tests the converted text, as `window_open.js` does.
  - A `Char` answer is `char_new(code)`, not `io_text`, which can give `""` or several characters.
  - Host text that may hold a lone surrogate (`JSON.parse`, text built from code units, `process.env`) needs `str_in`, because a lone `\uDC00` would read as a packed Char with no error. Text that cannot hold one (a literal of valid text, `io_text`, argv) goes in as it is.
  - A module export converts text itself, at any depth: its caller gives and gets host strings, and a lone surrogate going in or a non-scalar `Char` coming out reads as U+FFFD. A function that crosses converts its own arguments and answer. `GUIDE.md` says text crosses as a host string, and that a value with no text to change crosses without a copy.
- **Tests:**
  - `marshal_char_scalar` has `echo` (returns the Char, which reads back as 55296) and `seen` (returns `str_in(str_out(c))`, which reads back as 65533).
  - `marshal_string_scalar`'s valid answers stay raw host strings, which need no `str_in`; `torn` (a lone surrogate) calls `str_in` itself.
  - `window_open_args` adds a title holding `Chr{55296}`: `accepted` on every lane. Without the `window_open.js` fix, the JS lane and the interpreter answered EILSEQ.
  - `marshal_string_scalar` adds `torn_low` (`str_in("a\uDC00bcd")`), which counts 5. It counts 2 without `str_in`, the packed-Char misread. `torn` now prints its codes, `97;65533;`, so a missing `str_in` shows as `97;55296;`; its old count was 2 either way.
  - `udp_bad_address` sends `SCon{Chr{55296}, "x"}` to a bad host and reads the kept text's first code: 55296 on every lane (65533 on C before). It then sends the same datagram successfully.
  - `marshal_char_scalar` adds `echo_list`: a `List<String>` holding `Chr{55296}` crosses an effect and back as it is, 55296.
  - New `text_host_export` builds a `.mjs` and calls its exports:
    - Valid and astral text round-trips.
    - The packed form passed in (`"\uDC00\0\^[\0"`) is just host text with a lone surrogate: it becomes `"\uFFFD\0\^[\0"`, counts 5 Chars plus 1 for `"x"`, and a lone `"\uDC00"` Char reads 65533.
    - `Chr{55296}` reaches the caller as U+FFFD in a String, a Char, a list, an array, a tuple through a polymorphic def, a returned closure's answer, and a host callback's argument. The callback's lone-surrogate answer comes back cleaned.
    - An `Array` with no text comes back `===` and updated in place, and so does a ctor with no text to change.
    - Removing the walk fails it, and so does always copying.

**Breaking for third-party `.js` effects and for JS callers of exports.** An effect that passed a top-level `String` straight to a host API now calls `str_out` or `io_bytes`, and one that answers a host string that may hold a lone surrogate calls `str_in`. A caller of an export now gets nested text converted too (on `main` only a top-level `String`/`Char` was), and a function it gets or passes converts on each call. Valid text behaves the same either way; only non-scalar Chars and lone surrogates differ.

This replaces most of #1549, which moves the extra `str_out` calls the other way (out of the effects, kept in the wrapper).

## Checks
- **repo:** merged with current main, **`comp.ts` is 66,118 ttok, 118 over its 66,000 cap**, so `gates/repo.ts` passes 53 / 54. `GUIDE.md` is 7,999 of 8,000. The export walk costs about 200 ttok, and it needs a simplification elsewhere in `comp.ts` before merging.
- **Export walk:** the 13 tests that build a module pass from the repo root. `run_lib` is only used by exports, so other programs' output is unchanged. The suite-wide numbers below predate the walk.
- **Local, after the latest commit:** every test, C and JS lanes, on main and on main + this PR, with a 5 s alarm. The results are the same apart from the new and changed tests, which pass (876 C, 916 JS). `tools/bend-lint`'s `bun test`: 134 / 134. The tests that build a module run their JS lane from the repo root; all 13 pass on both trees. The 3 C failures are this machine's: `gfx/window` and `gfx/clicks` expect "no display", and `io/stack_fault_trap` exits 138 under the runner.
- **Local (macOS, after the rebase onto main):** the 50 io and gfx tests that use the changed effects, interpreted, as JS and native, windows opened on a desktop. The only failures also fail on main on the same machine: `clicks` and `window` expect "no display", `tcp_recv_max_huge` differs by a trailing space, and `process_run_node_module`'s JS lane.
- The cluster gates (test, ping, perf) have not run since the rebase. Before it: test 1707/1707, ping 72/72, perf 123/124 (histogram PAR-CPU at 1.25x the pin, which also missed on #1814, whose C is byte-identical to main's).

title: fix(cli): prevent GPU archives from overwriting inputs
body:
Native GPU builds also write `<binary>.gpu`. Previously, when a loaded Bend or foreign source occupied that path, the CLI accepted the requested binary output and then overwrote the source with the GPU archive.

The CLI now checks the archive destination against the existing input set before starting a GPU build, reusing the resolved-path and inode checks for explicit outputs. This follows the precedent set in [1364d73e](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/commit/1364d73e85f1722f490685eb050a39f7e8713ea2), which rejects outputs that would overwrite files the program reads.

The existing output-input test now requires rejection, preserved source bytes, and no binary for this collision.

Validation: the regression fails unchanged code and passes the fix; source and freshly compiled CLI path matrices pass on macOS, including normal CPU/Metal execution and CPU-only builds. Repository gate 54/54; strict TypeScript retains the baseline's 11 diagnostics.

title: Python target: a first pass, preliminary results, and the comp.ts cap
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# A Python target beside C and JS: a program, and an importable module.
$ bend main.bend -o main.py && python3 main.py
$ bend lib.bend  -o lib.pym          # writes lib.py

>>> import lib                       # plain Python, no FFI, no marshalling
>>> lib.greet("world")
'hello, world'
>>> lib.inc(41)
42
```

### Why

**This is a first pass, and every number below is preliminary.** We are
asking for feedback on the approach before we open a PR, because the work
cannot pass the repo gate as it stands (see "Conflicts with the repo gate").

The README lists Python as a planned target. We want to write the pure core
of a Python application in Bend, with its laws, and import it from the rest
of the Python code as ordinary functions. A C library behind an FFI would need
hand-written glue for every value that crosses the boundary, and that glue is
the part no law covers. A Python target has no boundary.

#### What exists

Branch: https://github.com/AFDudley/bend/tree/python-target (22 commits on
`de26a9170`, 2 behind `main`). Diff:
https://github.com/bendlang/bend/compare/main...AFDudley:bend:python-target

- A `py` backend in `bend2/comp.ts`, built as a close mirror of the JS
  backend: tagged values, tag-test matches, self tail calls as loops, other
  tail calls through a trampoline. Every edit to shared code is gated on a
  new `FL.py` flag.
- A Python runtime string and Python twins for the effects in `bend2/effs/`.
  Window and audio copy the JS twins exactly (no display, a silent
  clock-drained device).
- `-o x.pym` writes an importable `x.py`.
- `U32` masked on `int`, `Nat` as `int`, `Char` as an `int` (any 21-bit
  word round-trips), exact decimal-to-`F32` rounding with
  `fractions.Fraction`, and NaN bits kept as integers.
- A recursion prelude: `sys.setrecursionlimit` plus `main` in a thread with a
  large stack (512 MB, falling back to 256 and 64).
- A local two-lane runner, `gates/test_py_local.ts`, because `gates/test.ts`
  needs the cluster. It builds `-o t.js` and `-o t.py` for every test and
  compares each run to the `#|` lines with a 5 s limit.

LLM agents wrote the code under our review; we checked the results below
ourselves where marked.

#### Preliminary results (one Linux host, load average 13–70)

| lane | pass | fail | dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| JS | 872 | 3 | 845 |
| Python (CPython 3.12) | 863 | 3 | 854 |
| Python (PyPy 7.3.21 / 3.11) | 863 | 3 | 854 |

- The JS output is unchanged: every test compiled to JS on `de26a9170` and
  on the branch is byte-for-byte identical (875 same, 0 different, 845 not
  built on either side). We checked this ourselves.
- Python's 3 failures are the same 3 the JS lane fails on this host
  (`proof_app_main`, `io_stderr_failure`, `io_chan_reclaim_limit`). Under
  PyPy, `io_chan_reclaim_limit` passes and `io_tcp_send_slow_peer` times out
  instead.
- The 9 extra Python drops are tests with a `.js` twin and no `.c` twin that
  probe a JS-host property (`js_closure_host`, `marshal_char_strict`,
  `module_export_keys`, the three bundle/HTML tests, two audio-clock probes,
  `random_u32_js_fail`). The C lane drops them by the same rule.
- Deep non-tail recursion (`List.foldr`, `String.length`): both lanes pass
  at 10k; at 100k JS overflows and Python passes; at 200k both overflow.
- The corpus run found real Python-lane bugs that are now fixed: a
  null-versus-parked ambiguity in the IO loop, `select` failing past fd 1024,
  effect sources sharing one scope, `File.read` asking for 1 byte on a
  zero-length read, an O(n) run-queue pop, and string literals rebuilt one
  character at a time (173M calls in `io_tcp_send_slow_peer`).

Speed, the slowest tests, run alone (we timed these ourselves):

| test | CPython 3.12 | PyPy | JS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io/within_busy` | 3.00 s | 0.79 s | 0.25 s |
| `reg/closure_value_owns` | 3.35 s | 0.63 s | 0.19 s |
| `io/tcp_text_residue` | 3.03 s | 1.59 s | 0.36 s |
| `io/chan_reclaim_limit` | 38.34 s | 2.48 s | 2.94 s |
| `io/tcp_send_slow_peer` | 2.68 s | 4.13 s | 0.61 s |

PyPy closes most of the CPython gap with no code change. The remaining
CPython cost is per-call overhead (closures, the trampoline, immutable string
prepends), not one hot spot.

#### Conflicts with the repo gate

We ran `main`'s `gates/repo.ts` over the branch. It fails, and we do not
think we can fix it alone:

1. **`bend2/comp.ts` is 80,248 tokens against the 66,000 cap.** `main` is
   already at the cap; the backend adds about 14,000. The gate says the caps
   are permanent and code is never moved out to meet them.
2. **102 `.py` files are not in the allow list:** 35 in `bend2/effs/` and 67
   test twins in `tests/`. The list allows `.c` and `.js` only.
3. `PYTHON_TARGET_RESULTS.md` and `gates/test_py_local.ts` are not in the
   allow list. These are for this review and would leave the branch before a
   PR.

#### Possible next steps

- **Type the emitted Python as strongly as Python allows.** The emitter
  already knows every type. One path: `U32`, `Nat` and `Char` as `NewType`s
  over `int`; one `@dataclass(slots=True)` per constructor, a union alias per
  ADT, and `match`/`case` in place of `"$"`-tagged dicts; `TypeVar` and
  `Generic` for type parameters; `Callable` for closures; dependent types
  erased to the nearest simple type, with `object` (not `Any`) where Python
  cannot express them. The acceptance would be: every Python file emitted for
  the corpus, with the runtime and the effects, passes `mypy --strict`, and
  the corpus results do not change. The class representation should also cut
  CPython's per-access cost, and typed output can be compiled with mypyc.
  The hard part is the runtime itself (the trampoline, the IO loop's
  continuations, `run_clo`) and the effect files.
- **Use the compiler's ownership facts.** `brw_of`, `FL.own`, `val_own` and
  `val_brw` know when a value has exactly one owner. In Python that allows a
  safe in-place append for an owned string or list, which removes the O(n)
  prepend copies.
- **Profile `io_tcp_send_slow_peer` under PyPy**, the one test PyPy makes
  slower.

#### Questions

1. Is a Python target something you want upstream?
2. If yes, how should a third backend fit the `comp.ts` cap: a
   simplification you have in mind, an authorization, or a different
   structure?
3. Should Python effects and test twins be `.py` files in the allow list, as
   `.c` and `.js` are?
4. Do you want the Python lane in `gates/test.ts`, and is PyPy acceptable as
   the reference interpreter?

title: Run Process.run through one worker on Bun and Node
body:
Fixes #1468. Picks up the shared-worker direction from #1469, which was closed as stale.

Bun and Node use one `node:worker_threads` worker with `child_process.spawn`. There is no separate Node fallback. A child can leave stdin unread; its descendants cannot keep the input pipe hanging after it exits. The combined output cap kills the child as the bytes arrive.

Added the three stdin regressions from that review. Also checked the delayed `touch` case: cap 5 blocks the side effect, while the same script with a higher cap really creates the marker.
