title: fix(io): clear prior errors before native file reads
body:
After a write fails on a read-only file, a successful native read can consume bytes but return the previous `EBADF` error. This is a regression in #1845: `IoWork` is reused, and the new read loop does not clear its error on a full read, a newline, or a partial read before EOF.

Clear the error at the start of the shared read function. Errors before any bytes are read still return `Fail`. The regression test covers `File.read`, `File.read_line`, `File.read_bytes`, and `File.read_at`, plus EOF, zero-length reads, and file position.

Validation:
- The new test fails on unpatched native code with `Bad file descriptor` (exit 9). It passes on unpatched JavaScript and patched native code.
- All 10 file IO tests pass locally on their supported backends: source execution and Bun JavaScript, plus native C for the 9 tests with C support.
- Rebased onto `8d6cdb85`; checked the new `r+` tests and the regression again.
- Repository gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`. Diff checks pass. Independent review found no required changes.
- Full cluster tests were not run locally.

title: perf(io): drain the JS channel's parked waiters from a head index
body:
The JS channel removed its first parked waiter with `Array.shift()`, which moves every remaining waiter on V8, so draining N senders (or receivers) parked on one channel was O(N²) on Node. #1851 fixed the same pattern for the buffer only.

**Change** (`bend2/effs/chan.js` only; the C lane keeps its own list and is untouched):

- **One queue for the buffer and the waiters.** `q_new`, `q_size`, `q_push` and `q_pull` are a head index that compacts in place (`copyWithin` + `length`) once more than live+64 have been pulled. #1851's buffer code and the waiters both use it, so the compaction lives once.
- **A `try_` waiter whose timer comes first is marked `gone` and left for `chan_head` to drop,** the way it already drops waiters whose IO has returned. Before, it was found by `indexOf` and spliced out. A wake sets the same flag, which `late` checks for "already woken". A timeout is now O(1), and nothing searches the queue.

FIFO, close and the `try_` timers behave as before. The first commit added the head index; 1b8b71b0 moved it into the shared queue and added the `gone` flag (see the comment thread).

**Drain** (from the first commit; 1b8b71b0 matches it, see the comment for a three-way run):

`N` senders park on `Chan.new(U32, 0)`, then `N` receives. Before → after, median of 20 runs (each a fresh process, before/after interleaved, macOS arm64, Node 25.9, Bun 1.4.2):

| N parked | Node time | Node CPU | Node peak RSS | Bun time | Bun peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k | 0.03 → 0.03 s | 0.02 → 0.02 s | 61.8 → 61.3 MB | | |
| 25k | 0.24 → 0.06 s | 0.28 → 0.11 s | 128.5 → 128.8 MB | | |
| 100k | **3.35 → 0.11 s** | 3.40 → 0.20 s | 263.9 → 264.6 MB | 0.09 → 0.09 s | 190.8 → 186.8 MB |
| 200k | **13.2 → 0.20 s** | 13.3 → 0.51 s | 348.7 → 348.0 MB | 0.16 → 0.16 s | 294.5 → 292.9 MB |

<details><summary>p80 / p95 (change, %)</summary>

| | wall | CPU | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node, 1k | 0 / +75 (0.031 → 0.054 s, one run of 20) | 0 / +46 | 0 / +0.2 |
| Node, 25k | -72 / -66 | -61 / -62 | +1.3 / +8.4 |
| Node, 100k | -97 / -96 | -94 / -94 | +0.4 / +0.4 |
| Node, 200k | -98.4 / -98.3 | -96 / -96 | +0.1 / -0.3 |
| Bun, 100k | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | -3 / -10 |
| Bun, 200k | -6 / -10 | -1 / -5 | -1 / -2 |

</details>

On Node at 25k–100k, peak RSS is ~0.5 MB higher (of ~264 MB); at 200k it is level. I have not pinned down why (my guess is fewer GC cycles before the peak in a run that is now 30x shorter).

**Timeouts** (1b8b71b0): 100k `try_send` waiters on a rendezvous channel, all timing out, on Bun 1.3.14: main 2.23 s, first commit 2.20 s, 1b8b71b0 1.60 s. 1.5 s of each is the timer itself. This benchmark doesn't run on Node, because the JS poller needs `bun:ffi`.

**Still O(N²):** waking a `try_` waiter searches `io.waits` to cut its timer (`chan_wake`). That's in the scheduler in `comp.ts` and out of scope here.

New test: `tests/io/chan_wait_drain.bend`. 20000 senders park on a rendezvous channel; receiving 15000 must see them in send order (the queue compacts 8 times with live waiters behind; an off-by-one in the compaction fails it), then a close fails the rest and a receive answers None. It passes on Bun, Node and the C binary, and `gates/repo.ts` passes.

On 1b8b71b0: cluster gates test 1717/1717 and repo 54/54. Every test that uses `Chan.`, run under Bun and Node, prints the same output and exits the same way as with main's `chan.js`.

title: fix(io): Process.run of an empty program answers ENOENT on JS, as on C
body:
`Process.run("", ...)` failed with a different error on each lane:

| lane | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| C | `Fail` 2 (ENOENT) | `Fail` 2 (ENOENT) |
| Bun | `Fail` 5 (EIO) | `Fail` 2 (ENOENT) |
| Node | `Fail` 5 (EIO) | `Fail` 2 (ENOENT) |

Node and Bun's `spawn("")` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`, which carries no errno, so the worker fell back to EIO. C's `posix_spawnp("")` answers ENOENT, the same as a missing executable. The JS lane now answers ENOENT before spawning, after the EINVAL checks (a zero limit or timeout, a NUL in an argument), which is the order C uses: `""` with a zero limit is still 22 on both.

Test: `tests/io/process_run.bend` gets an `empty program` case next to `missing`. Before the fix it prints `empty program: False` on Bun and Node and `True` on C; after, `True` on all three. The other `process_run*` tests and `gates/repo.ts` pass.

title: fix(io): TCP.recv past INT32_MAX caps the read as C does on JS
body:
`TCP.recv`, `recv_bytes`, `try_recv` and `try_recv_bytes` with a `max` of 2^31 or more failed with `22 Invalid argument` on Bun, while the C runtime reads the data:

| lane | `TCP.recv(s, 4294967295)` before | after |
|---|---|---|
| C | `Done` "hello" | `Done` "hello" |
| Bun | `Fail` 22 (EINVAL) | `Done` "hello" |

recv(2) past INT32_MAX bytes answers EINVAL on macOS. C's `tcp_recv_start` already caps the read at INT32_MAX (`tcp_recv.c`, and WONTFIX.txt: "the runtime only caps it at INT32_MAX"); the JS lane now caps the same way, as `file_read.js` does. `max = 0` is still EINVAL on both, checked before the cap. This is the TCP half of #783; UDP is already bounded at 65507.

Test: `tests/io/tcp_recv_max_huge.bend` (from `tcp_recv_max_zero.bend`, ports 23117+) runs `recv` with 2^32-1, `recv_bytes` with 2^31 and `try_recv` with 2^32-1 over loopback. Before the fix Bun prints `recv 4294967295: 22 Invalid argument`; after, Bun and C print the expected lines. `tcp_recv_max_zero`, `tcp_loopback` and `gates/repo.ts` pass. Node does not run TCP (`bun:ffi`), as on main.

title: fix(io): retry interrupted native file writes
body:
A signal can interrupt native `File.write` or `File.write_bytes` after a short write. The current loop returns `Fail` with `EINTR` and loses its byte offset. Retrying the full value from Bend can duplicate the bytes already written.

Retry only the interrupted `write()` call. The offset advances only after a positive result. Zero progress still returns `EIO`, and other errors still return `Fail`.

The native regression test injects `EINTR`, writes two bytes, injects `EINTR` again, then writes the remainder. It checks that every stage ran and that the file contains the exact text or binary payload once. The short text write splits a UTF-8 character. The JavaScript fixture uses ordinary host writes.

Validation:
- The new test fails on unpatched native code with `Interrupted system call` (exit 4), and passes after the fix.
- All 11 file IO tests pass locally: source execution and Bun JavaScript, plus native C for the 10 tests with C support. This includes zero-progress and permanent-error tests.
- A separate macOS probe with real `SIGUSR1` signals and a pipe reproduced the failure: the original loop stopped after 65,536 bytes of a 1 MiB payload. The retry loop wrote all 1 MiB with exact contents.
- Repository gate: `PASS: 54 / 54`. Diff checks pass. Independent review found no required changes.
- Full cluster tests were not run locally.

title: Docs: the GPU build recipe (CUDA search order, nvrtc.h as the marker, lib64 vs lib, +RTS --gpu-build, the silent CPU fallback) exists only in cli_build's comment
body:
### What is missing

The guide documents what bangs `(\!)` *mean*` (GUIDE.md: "\`!\` runs on GPU", and "A machine without a GPU runs \`!\` on the CPU (still in parallel)"), and README says \`!\` needs clang 19+ / Metal or CUDA 12 — but **how a build actually reaches the GPU lane is written down only in a source comment** (`bend2/main.ts`, `cli_build`):

- the search order: `$CUDA_HOME`, `$CUDA_PATH`, `/usr/local/cuda`, `/opt/cuda` (Arch's), first one **that holds `include/nvrtc.h`**;
- the library layout: `lib64` first, `lib` as nix lays them (`-L $cuda/lib64 -L $cuda/lib -lcuda -lnvrtc`);
- the build runs the binary once with `+RTS --gpu-build` to write the GPU program — so **the loader needs `libnvrtc.so.13` at build time**, from `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` when it is not a system library;
- and the line the comment ends with: **`else the ! runs on the cores`** — silently. A `! `` program with no toolkit found builds as CPU, links no CUDA library, and nothing in the output says which lane ran.

### Why it matters (what it cost us)

Reverse-engineering this produced two filed bugs on the consuming side: [nuxyel/BendTorch#10](https://github.com/nuxyel/BendTorch/issues/10) — its `make gpu` hardcoded `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(CUDA_HOME)/lib` (broken for every `lib64` toolkit, the exact layout `cli_build` links first), and with no toolkit its gate printed **"on the GPU"** for a run that had linked zero CUDA libraries. Nothing in our docs or theirs could tell the user: (1) which paths to set, (2) that `nvrtc.h` is the marker file, (3) that the *runtime* loader also needs the NVRTC library, (4) how to verify which lane a binary was built for (today: `ldd` and hope).

### Repro of the silent fallback (this machine, no toolkit anywhere)

```
$ unset CUDA_HOME CUDA_PATH
$ bend demo/anything_with_bangs.bend -o prog   # exit 0, no message
$ ldd prog | grep -c -E 'nvrtc|libcuda'
0
```

### Proposal

A short **"Building for the GPU"** section (guide, or README's compilation bullets) stating:

1. the search order and the `nvrtc.h` marker (`cli_build` already comments it);
2. `lib64`/`lib` layouts and that a user-unpacked toolkit works if `CUDA_HOME` names it;
3. the runtime loader: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$cuda/lib64` (or an installed driver + `libnvrtc`) or the binary dies with `libnvrtc.so.13: cannot open shared object file`;
4. **which lane ran**: either document `\ldd x | grep nvrtc` as the check, or have the build print one line (`gpu: CUDA at /path` vs `gpu: no toolkit, building CPU`) — the comment already knows; the user never sees it.

The comment at `cli_build` is accurate and good; this is about promoting it to user-facing docs and making the fallback visible.

title: Two stuck calls of distinct defs compare by their bodies, unfolded once
body:
A stuck call still compares by its head def's name. Now, when two calls of distinct defs on as many arguments differ by name, each def's body is unfolded once on its arguments, and the two compare with every def rigid. A call inside either body, a recursive one included, stays a call.

```python
def not1(b: Bool) -> Bool:            # not2: the same body
  match b:
    case True{}:
      False{}
    case False{}:
      True{}

def stuck(b: Bool) -> {not1(b) == not2(b) : Bool}:     # now checks
  {==}
def partial() -> {snd1(1) == snd2(1) : U32 -> U32}:    # now checks
  {==}
```

Lean accepts both of these by `rfl`. Two recursive defs with the same body, such as `r(n) == s(n)` stuck on `Nat`, still don't convert. Each body calls itself by its own name, so they'd need coinduction, not one unfolding. Lean's `rfl` rejects that case too.

## Changes
- **`bend2/bend.ts`, `compare_go`'s `App` case:** if the heads match, compare the arguments as before. If they don't and both heads are defs with bodies on the same number of arguments, compare the two bodies applied to their arguments under `RIGID`.
- **`bend2/bend.ts`, `term_spine`:** a new helper that applies a term to a list of arguments, firing a λ head. The new comparison, `compare_go`'s bare-def η loop and `def_inst`'s template instantiation each folded `term_apply` by hand, and now all three use it. `bend.ts` goes from 43,767 to 43,961 ttok.
- **`bend2/bendtt.lean`:** the same fallback in `Term.conv`. `Term.unfold` returns the two bodies on their arguments, and they're compared with the empty book. `Term.conv` now takes its book after the colon, so the recursive call can switch books. `conv_sound` covers the fallback by δ, which the declarative theory already has (`Par.delta`), so no claim changes. `consistent` and `book_check` still depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The kernel goes from 62.7k to 63.4k ttok, under its 64k cap.

## Tests
- **`tests/check/stuck_call_unfold.bend`:** a stuck call on an open variable, a partial call, and a stuck call inside a constructor now convert.
- **`tests/check/stuck_call_unfold_recursive.bend`:** two recursive defs with the same body still don't convert.
- **`tests/check/stuck_call_unfold_differ.bend`:** defs whose bodies differ don't convert.
- **`tests/check/canonical_ref_conversion.bend`:** this test pinned bend3's refusal of exactly this case. It now expects `0`, and its comment explains why.

Local results:
- **`--check-only` on all of `tests/`:** the only verdict change is `canonical_ref_conversion`.
- **Local `--verdict` gate (`gates/safe_node.ts`):** 0 false rejects, the same as `main`. `canonical_ref_conversion` and `stuck_call_unfold` agree, and the other two are rejected by bend2 before reaching the kernel.
- **`gates/repo.ts`:** PASS 54/54.
- **Not run:** `gates/test.ts` and `gates/perf.ts` need the cluster.

## Check time
Measured locally on an M-series Mac with `--check-only`. Base is `main`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `compute_1600` | 530 ± 7 ms | 535 ± 5 ms |
| `defs_12800` | 313 ± 2 ms | 319 ± 5 ms |
| `generics_3200` | 401 ± 3 ms | 402 ± 2 ms |
| `proofs_3200` | 865 ± 24 ms | 866 ± 10 ms |
| `trees_400` | 646 ± 4 ms | 647 ± 6 ms |
| 25 demo files (best of 5, summed) | 1.6 s | 1.6 s |
| 1,725 tests (best of 2, summed) | 207.0 s | 207.0 s |
| `--verdict` gate, 1,728 files (summed) | 539.4 s | 538.1 s |

The benchmarks are hyperfine with 2 warmups and 10–15 runs. Every difference is inside one standard deviation. An unchanged copy of bend2 in the same scratch location timed the same as the repo copy, so the copy's location adds no bias.

The fallback runs only after an application comparison has already failed. Across the benchmarks, demos and tests it ran 32,875 times. Five times it got past its first check and actually unfolded: `canonical_ref_conversion` and four `tests/state/*_goal.bend` files. Those four are the recursive case and still fail as before.

Note: AGENTS.md lists `bend2/bend.ts` as human-written, so that part needs a human review.

title: fix(check): say a def given <...> is a def, and how a do block opens
body:
Two easy slips gave errors that didn't point at the fix:

```python
def main() -> IO<Unit>:     # a def written with a datatype's <...>
  do IO(Unit):              # a do block's effect written with (...)
```

The first reported `a declared datatype (unknown: IO)`, although `IO` is defined. The second reported only `expected '<'`.

Neither problem is specific to IO. Any def written as `X<...>` hits the first, and any `do M` without its `<` hits the second. So instead of a special case for IO (as in #1835), both errors now come from what the name is and what was written:

- **`book_adt`.** A name in type position is either a datatype or a def. A def keeps `a declared datatype` and adds `Note: X is a def: write its arguments as ()`, the mirror of the existing `Note: X is a datatype: write its arguments as <>`. The name comes through `name_show`, so an imported def reads as the file spells it (`L.Twice`, not `lib.Twice`). A def with no parameters notes `Note: X is a def with no arguments: write it as X` instead, since the slip is the `<...>` itself. An unknown name keeps `(unknown: X)`.
- **The `do` parser.** A missing `<` now reports `'<' (a do block is written do M<...>:)`, with the effect the user wrote, whatever follows the name. The header checks nothing about the name.
- **A missing `.bind` / `.pure`.** A `do` block on `M` desugars to `M.bind` and `M.pure`. When one is undefined, the `a defined name` error now notes `a do block on M calls M.bind and M.pure`, so the error no longer names only a call the user never wrote.

## Tests
- `tests/check/def_type_args.bend` (new): `Twice<U32>` for a user-defined `def Twice(A: Type) -> Type`.
- `tests/parse/do_effect_parens.bend` (new): `do IO(Unit):`, from #1835.
- `tests/check/def_type_args_none.bend` (new): `Num<U32>` for `def Num() -> Type`.
- `tests/parse/do_missing_param.bend`: `do Result:` now pins the new message.
- `tests/check/do_missing_bind.bend`: `do Box<>:` with no `Box.bind` now pins the note.

## What I ran
- Test gate: 1723/1723. Repo gate: 54/54.
- `IO<Unit>` as a return type reports `a declared datatype` with `Note: IO is a def: write its arguments as ()`.
- A def from a file imported `as L`, written `L.Twice<U32>`, gets `Note: L.Twice is a def: ...` (before this, it showed the internal `lib.Twice`).

Supersedes #1835 (thanks @adeerkhan, who is co-author on the commit).

title: Calls passing a source lambda to a non-recursive def inline the callee, through a leading one-arm match
body:
**`comp.ts` is 66,846 ttok, 846 over the 66,000 cap, so `repo-gate` fails until that is settled.** Replaces #1356. It does the same job by inlining instead of minting specialized defs: +886 ttok against `main`, where #1356 cost +1,136, with the same speed.

## What it does

When a call passes a lambda written in the source in a live parameter position, and the callee isn't recursive, the callee is inlined at the call site. The lambda is then applied in place, and no closure is built.
- **Through a leading match:** inlining passes through a callee's leading `match` when the matched type has one constructor (tuples, records). A small helper, `def_at`, puts the callback into the match arm.
- **Beta:** a lambda applied directly to its arguments is reduced in `anf`.
- **Emitter:** when a `let` binds the result of a one-arm match, the rest of the code moves into that arm. A match in tail position is emitted directly. This also applies to one-arm matches written in source.

There are no new defs, keys, markers or fuel. Termination comes from the callee being non-recursive.

## Results

The fixtures from #1288 (by @mizchi) are included unchanged, and all 5 print their expected output.

**Speed** (M4, 10⁸ steps, 7 runs each, measured before the rebase onto #1968; after it, a re-measured helper-with-a-capturing-lambda loop went from about 0.26 s on `main` to about 0.01 s):

| program | main | #1356 | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| helper called each step with a fresh capturing lambda | 241 ms | 51.4 ms | 51.4 ms |
| bind-style callback | 841 ms | 102.6 ms | 102.7 ms |
| destructures a tuple literal | 866 ms | 26.3 ms | 26.5 ms |
| destructures a call result (`get`-style) | 911 ms | 51.7 ms | 51.5 ms |

**Closures built** in the fixtures (main / #1356 / this, measured before the rebase):

| fixture | main | #1356 | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| `known_callback` | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| `known_callback_array` | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| `known_callback_layouts` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `known_callback_shapes` | 11 | 3 | 3 |
| `known_callback_edges` | 21 | 18 | 19 |

**Checks:**
- `test.ts` passes 1803/1803 and `perf.ts` 124/124, on `main` at #1968.
- Everything under `bench/` compiles to the same C as main, and JS output is unchanged across the corpus. The C changes in 42 of the 1,383 programs that load, including the demos `app_slash_boss_3d` and `io_tcp_echos`.
- `tsc` shows no new errors in `comp.ts`.
- `repo.ts` fails only on the ttok cap.

## Not covered

- **Matches with more than one arm** (Bool, Nat, List helpers): the rest of the caller would have to be copied into every arm.
- **Recursive callees.**
- **Callees with more than one non-callback argument left** when the match is reached.

None of the fixtures need these.

## Cost

+886 ttok. Getting under the cap needs about 846 tokens cut elsewhere in `comp.ts`, or a raise.

Not run: CUDA, Linux and the JS benches.

title: Pointer events: one Press for the mouse, a finger or a pen
body:
The web added input one device at a time: mouse events, then Touch Events
(Apple, 2008), then Pointer Events (Microsoft, 2012), which Safari took up
in 2019. Browsers still ship all three, and fire mouse events after each
touch for pages that only know the mouse. Bend is at the first step:
`Mouse{x, y, button, down}` knows one pointer, never says it left, and a
key or button held as the window loses focus never comes up.

This takes the last step directly. A mouse, a finger and a pen are one
`Press`, `Move`, `Leave` and `Lost`, carrying what W3C Pointer Events measures: one
primitive for every device, now and later, for the price of one breaking
change while few apps match on `Mouse`.

```python
type Event is Data:
  Press{id, tool, x, y, time, button, down}  # a pointer: the mouse (id 0), a finger or a pen
  Move{id, tool, x, y, time}                 # with no button down, a hover
  Leave{id}                                  # no button down, off the window (pointerleave)
  Lost{id}                                   # pressed, taken away: what it held ends with no release (pointercancel)
  Focus{on}
```

Only what W3C defines is here. Gestures (tap, drag, pinch), a trackpad's
pinch and swipe, and drops from other apps are no standard's pointer
events, and each wants its own design: they are left for later PRs.

**Breaking.** `Mouse` is gone. Buttons are W3C's: right is 2, was 1.
Coordinates are `F32`, past the window's edge while a button holds the
pointer. Base now owns `Tool`, `Press`, `Leave`, `Lost` and `Focus`, so a
program declaring one of these fails; `Tool`'s constructors are dotted
(`Tool.Mouse`, ...), so they take no names from programs.

## Rules

- A `Tool` (`Tool.Mouse{}`, `Tool.Finger{..}`, `Tool.Pen{..}`) carries W3C Pointer Events'
  force, size, tilt and twist; a force is 0 unless pressed, and a value the
  device doesn't report is W3C's default.
- `Press` and `Move` carry the system's time in ms (W3C's `timeStamp`), a
  `U32` that wraps: only differences count.
- A pointer with no button down that goes off the window, or a pen out of
  range, is a `Leave`; the mouse comes back as id 0. A pointer pressed and
  taken away (a grab elsewhere, a pen out of range while pressed, a lost
  focus) is a `Lost`. Both free the id; while a button holds a pointer, it
  stays past the window's edge.
- One queue per window keeps events whole: every release has its press,
  and a pointer leaves or is lost once. A lost focus sends `Lost` for each held
  pointer and a key-up for each held key, then `Focus{False}`.
- X11 loads libXi (XInput 2.2) at run time, as it already loads
  libXrandr, so a build needs no `libxi-dev`. Without libXi, core events
  give the mouse alone.

## Tested

In WSL (WSLg, X11), one file at a time:
- `gfx_app_play`, `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window_events` in the checker and
  native C (built CPU only, with clang), headless as on the minis; the
  triangle demo's main under `--check-only`.
- `gfx_window_events` on WSLg's display: XInput2 events of a made-up touch
  screen, pen and evdev touchpad through window.c's own handlers.
- c798c399 (`Leave` apart from `Lost`, `Tool.*` dotted): all four gates
  green on the minis (repo 54/54, test 1733/1733, perf 124/124, ping
  81/81), and `gfx_window_events` built with clang and run under Xvfb on
  Debian: `True`.
- Before the cut, at a68cba74: real input through XTest on both X11 paths
  (XInput2, and the core fallback forced by failing the libXi load): moves,
  buttons, scroll, `Lost`, focus releases and `Window.grab`'s `Look`.

Not tested:
- The Mac on a display: it builds and runs headless in the test gate on
  the minis, and its half of `gfx_window_events` moves and clicks the
  mouse only.
- Real touch screens and pens (WSLg has none).

Known gaps: on X11 a pen leaves only when it leaves the window (XInput2
has no proximity events), and a single-touch evdev touchpad or screen,
which declares no touch class, reads as a pen.

Numbers: window.c 1,120 → 1,613 lines, base.bend +29.

title: Diagnostics: a pure let inside a do block is refused with "expected: a pattern (a binder or a constructor)" pointing at the previous statement
body:
### What happened

A definition cannot sit inside a `do` block — fine, if that is the rule — but the refusal names neither the rule nor the line at fault. The error points at the **statement before** the let, with a message about patterns:

```
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)
- observed : IO.bind(Unit, Unit, IO.print("a"), _ => {x : IO(Unit)})
Location:
7 |   do IO<Unit>:
8>|     IO.print("a")
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
9 |     x = pure_of()
```

The offender is line 9; the caret sits on line 8, and neither the message nor the location suggests that the problem is the `x = ...` at all (I first suspected the `IO.print` call). Hoisting the binding before the `do` works — that is the shape MLBend's examples use — but nothing says so.

### How to reproduce

```bend
import Base

def pure_of() -> Nat:
  5n

def bad() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print("a")
    x = pure_of()
    IO.print(U32.show(x))
    return Unit{}

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  bad()
```

```
$ bend repro.bend        # 2.0.38 (and the same on 2.0.39)
```

All four spellings are refused the same way (bend 2.0.38):

| variant | refusal |
|---|---|
| pure let after an effect | `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` |
| pure let first in the block | `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` |
| typed pure let (`x : Nat = ...`) | `expected : U32` (equally opaque) |
| effect statement with `;` before the let | `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` |

### Why it matters

Writing a new ML program, this cost a debugging round: the first suspect was the `IO.print`/bind desugaring (the message shows an `IO.bind`), not the let. A program author hitting this has no way to learn "a let may not sit inside a do block; hoist it or use `x <- eff`" from the compiler's words.

### Proposal

- The message names the rule: `a definition cannot appear inside a do block (a let is a def-body form): bind the value before the block, or use `x <- eff` for an effect`, and
- the Location points at the **let line**, not the previous statement.

(Allowing the let there would of course also fix it — but if the grammar stays as is, the diagnostics should say so.)

title: fix(runtime): share large freed blocks across host lanes
body:
Fixes #1856.

Each host lane currently keeps its last freed large block in COLD. Other lanes cannot reuse that block until the lane frees another block of the same class. Large temporary arrays can therefore increase peak memory with the worker count.

Send host blocks of at least `CAP_WORDS` (256 KiB) directly to the shared bank in `heap_hand`. Smaller blocks keep the existing HOT/COLD policy. The decision stays in the generation handoff, with no new branch in the inline `heap_free` path. Device frees still use `dev_cut`.

The cutoff uses `CAP_WORDS` because GPU mode sets `KEEP_WORDS` to 256 words. A normal Bend host loop that fills and drops 2 KiB arrays showed heavy lock contention when those blocks also went directly to the bank. With the fixed cutoff, its paired median time ratios are 1.016 at one thread and 0.930 at 16 threads.

The regression checks immediate reuse by another lane at 256 KiB and 1 MiB, no heap growth during reuse, live payload integrity, and smaller cached generations in both CPU and GPU modes. It fails on main. It also rejects the lower GPU cutoff.

A local Bend workload produces 32 arrays of 524,288 U32 cells on one lane, reads their endpoints on parallel lanes, and repeats this for 12 rounds. All runs return `2726963360`. Medians of three runs on an Apple M5 Max:

| CPU threads | Peak RSS before (MiB) | Peak RSS after (MiB) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 65.59 | 65.59 |
| 4 | 72.02 | 65.95 |
| 16 | 96.73 | 66.92 |

At 16 threads, this workload uses about 31% less peak RSS. Large-block retention in lane caches is zero in all final runs.

Validation against `dd7d74db` with Bun 1.3.14 and Apple clang 21:

- New regression: CPU at 1/16 threads, Metal, and `BEND_POISON`. Bun and interpreted IO also pass.
- 55 existing fixtures: 110 native checks; 16 fixtures: 32 poison checks; nine Metal fixtures pass with the final compiler.
- Concurrent allocation, payload, and heap growth checks pass with 16 threads under normal execution, poison, and UBSan, for the host cache sizes in CPU and GPU modes.
- All 17 runtime benchmarks at 1/16 CPU threads, plus five Metal benchmarks: 384 output checks pass. Three-run median time ratios are 0.921–1.061. Five-run repeats of the largest increases are 0.964–1.030. Peak RSS ratios are 0.986–1.021. All ratios are after/before.
- Repository gate: 54/54. TypeScript diagnostics match main exactly; the existing diagnostics remain in `bend.ts`, `safe.ts`, and documentation tools.

The cluster test/performance gates, CUDA, and BendTorch training were not run locally.

title: fix(parser): a do-block let without its type names the working form, at the let's line
body:
Closes #1868

## What

`x = pure_of()` inside a `do` block is refused with `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` and the caret on the **previous** statement (the leftover `= v` was being re-parsed as the next statement). The typed form the grammar's `DoLet` takes — `x : T = v` — works; the refusal now says exactly that, located on the let itself:

```
- expected : a do-block let with its type (write "x : T = ...", or bind the value before the block)
- observed : 'x '
Location:
15 |     IO.print("a")
16>|     x = pure_of()
   |     ^^
17 |     IO.print("ok")
```

The guard is four conditions in `parse_term_do_stmt`, right where a statement term has been parsed: a `Var` head, no `:` to follow (that is the typed path), no `==` (keep the equality statement as it was), and an `=` waiting — then `parse_fail` with the message above. Nothing else in the statement parse moved.

## Why

The message named neither the rule nor the line: the caret sat on `IO.print("a")` and the observation showed an `IO.bind`, so the first suspect was the desugaring, not the let. Full characterization (four spellings) in #1868 with the correction comment: typed lets were always fine.

## Checks

- `tests/spec/comp_do_let.bend` — new spec pin: the refusal above, the location, `exit 1`. Run with `bun bend2/main.ts tests/spec/comp_do_let.bend`: output matches the pin.
- `tests/spec/comp_let_split.bend` — still refuses identically (its pin unchanged).
- The typed-let control (`x : Nat = pure_of()` then `IO.print("ok")`) still runs and prints `ok`.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: `bend2/bend.ts` under its 48k cap; the one red file (`bendtt.lean` 64885 > 64000) is **pre-existing on `main`** and untouched here.
- The full `gates/test.ts` shards need the mini cluster — not run locally; the change is a parse-time refusal on a form that never parsed.

title: docs(guide): `guide/GPU.md` — the build recipe `cli_build` already knows
body:
Closes #1863

## What

A new **`guide/GPU.md`** (readable as `bend guide gpu`, the same way `bend guide shaders` works) that spells out, in user-facing words, what until now lived only in `cli_build`'s comment in `bend2/main.ts`:

1. **Finding a toolkit** — the search order (`$CUDA_HOME`, `$CUDA_PATH`, `/usr/local/cuda`, `/opt/cuda`) and `include/nvrtc.h` as the marker file; a user-unpacked toolkit works.
2. **What the build does** — `-DBEND_CUDA=1`, `-I`/`-L`/`-lcuda -lnvrtc` (`lib64` first, `lib` as nix lays them), and the `+RTS --gpu-build` run that writes `file.gpu` beside the binary.
3. **Running it** — the loader needs `libcuda.so.1` and `libnvrtc.so.13`; with an unpacked toolkit, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64` or the binary dies with `libnvrtc.so.13: cannot open shared object file`; `--gpu off` / `--gpu 4GB`.
4. **Which lane ran** — the part that was fully invisible: with no toolkit the build **succeeds silently** on the CPU lane, and `ldd file | grep -E 'cuda|nvrtc'` is how you tell.

`guide/GUIDE.md`'s Tooling sentence now points at `bend guide gpu` (net smaller than before, so GUIDE.md stays under its permanent 8k cap), and `GPU.md` joins `EFFECTS.md`/`SHADERS.md` on `gates/repo.ts`'s allow list, uncapped like them.

## Checks

- `bun gates/repo.ts`: **54/55** — GUIDE.md back under 8000, GPU.md allowed; the one red file (`bendtt.lean` 64885 > 64000) is **pre-existing on `main`** and untouched here.
- `bend guide gpu` prints the new page.
- Every claim in the page is taken from `cli_build` itself (the search list, the marker file, the link flags, the `+RTS --gpu-build` step, the silent fallback) — nothing invented; the failure mode (`libnvrtc.so.13: cannot open shared object file`) is reproduced in nuxyel/BendTorch#10 with exact outputs.

The optional half of #1863 — having the *build itself* print one line when it falls back to the CPU — is deliberately **not** in this PR (it changes compiler output); happy to send it separately if wanted.

title: perf(io): find a woken try_ waiter's timer by binary search on JS
body:
## What

On the JS backends, waking a parked `try_send` / `try_recv` waiter cuts its timer from `io.waits` with a linear `findIndex`. When waiters are woken out of deadline order, for example draining channel `b` while channel `a` holds older timers, each wake scans past every older timer, so a drain of N waiters is O(N²).

`io_park_on` keeps `io.waits` sorted by `at`, and now returns the timer it parks. The waiter keeps that entry (`w.timer`), and `chan_timer` binary-searches to its deadline, then walks the timers that share it until it reaches that entry. The `splice` that removes the timer is still linear, but it is a native move rather than a callback per entry, which is where the time went. The C runtime is unchanged.

In `io_park_on`, an absent deadline now defaults to `Infinity`, so the sort compares `at` directly; `comp.ts` stays at the same ttok count.

## Benchmarks

N `try_send` senders (600 s bound) park on `a`, then N on `b`; main drains `b`, then `a`. `bun bend2/main.ts`, 15 runs per side, main and this branch interleaved, Apple M4, `/usr/bin/time -l` (10 ms resolution). Same output on both sides.

| N | drain of b, p50/p80/p95 | wall p50/p80/p95 | CPU p50/p80/p95 | max RSS p50/p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10k | 186/189/191 → 10/10/11 ms | 260/260/270 → 80/90/90 ms | 450/460/480 → 280/290/320 ms | 122/128 → 122/126 MB |
| 40k | 2934/3033/3483 → 121/125/140 ms | 3150/3250/3700 → 340/350/380 ms | 3440/3580/3930 → 640/670/700 ms | 307/320 → 266/272 MB |

Draining in park order (`a`, then `b`), where `findIndex` already hit index 0, is unchanged within the 10 ms timer resolution: at 40k, drain 335 → 338 ms p50, wall 550 → 550 ms p50, CPU 860 → 850 ms p50, RSS 268 → 265 MB p50.

Matching the timer by identity keeps the 40k wall at 0.35 s. A plain `indexOf` on the entry, without the binary search, takes 0.52 s.

## Test

`tests/io/chan_try_wake_timers.bend` parks 300 senders on `a` (60 s), then 300 on `b` (30 s) and 300 on `b` (60 s), so `b`'s timers sit before and after `a`'s. On JS it first stops the clock (`Clock.stop`, in `chan_try_wake_timers.js`; a no-op in the `.c`), so `b`'s 60 s timers are due at exactly the same time as `a`'s and a woken waiter must walk past equal deadlines to find its own. It drains `b`, then `a`, then receives on `b` with no sender left. With every woken timer cut, `io.waits` is empty and the runtime reports the deadlock at once. If a lookup misses, a stale timer keeps the loop alive until the bound: with the walk over equal deadlines removed, the run waits out the bound and the gate's alarm reports it as a timeout (without the stopped clock, that broken walk still passes).

It passes on main and on this branch, on Bun and C. Merged onto main 378be5fd: `repo` 54 / 54, `test` 1727 / 1727, `ping` 81 / 81, `perf` 123 / 124 (the merkle compile cell, which fails on main too).

title: Shorter syntax for laws
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# Shorter laws. Every construct is sugar over today's syntax; nothing changes in the checker
# or the kernel.
#
#   law f(+x, y):          one `for` per parameter, in order, types inferred from the signatures
#                          and constructor fields the law uses; quantities stay explicit and
#                          `x: T` is still allowed
#   when b                 premise {b == True{} : Bool}
#   when not b             premise {b == False{} : Bool}
#   a == b, a != b         {a == b : T}, {a != b : T}, with T inferred
#   b as a proposition     {b == True{} : Bool}, or {b == False{} : Bool} for `not b`
#   a + b, a < b, ...      T.add(a, b), T.is_lt(a, b), ... for the operands' type T
#   r.field                field of a single-constructor record
#   List.length(xs)        leading erased arguments filled in: List.length(&2, String, xs)
#
# Nothing is reordered or simplified, and a type that can't be inferred is an error.

# demos/app_win_is_bug_2d, today:
law you_cant_win:
  for moves: List<Game.Move>
  board = Game.replay(Game.start(), moves)
  {Game.is_won(board) == False{} : Bool}

# proposed:
law you_cant_win(moves):
  not Game.is_won(Game.replay(Game.start, moves))

# demos/app_triangle_2d, today:
law click_inside:
  for +x: U32
  for +y: U32
  for button: U32
  for +n: U32
  for hit: {True{} == App.Tri.inside(x, y) : Bool}
  {App.Tri.event(Mouse{x, y, button, True{}}, n) == Some{(n + 1 : U32)}
    : Maybe<U32>}

# proposed:
law click_inside(+x, +y, button, +n):
  when True{} == App.Tri.inside(x, y)
  App.Tri.event(Mouse{x, y, button, True{}}, n) == Some{n + 1}

# from our code, a wrong answer to a puzzle starts a 3 second cooldown. Today:
law C2:
  for +entries: List<&2, S.Entry>
  for +digits: Maybe<&2, List<&2, Nat>>
  for +c: Nat
  for +now: Nat
  for ready: {Nat.is_lt(now, c) == False{} : Bool}
  for different: {P.exact(entries, digits) == False{} : Bool}
  {S.attempt(entries, digits, False{}, c, now) == S.Attempt{"invalid_attempt", False{}, 0n, Nat.add(now, 3000n)} : S.Attempt}

# proposed:
law C2(+entries, +digits, +c, +now):
  when not (now < c)
  when not P.exact(entries, digits)
  S.attempt(entries, digits, False{}, c, now) ==
    S.Attempt{"invalid_attempt", False{}, 0n, now + 3000n}

# and a turn is never cut short. Today:
law S8:
  for head: S.Entry
  for tail: List<&2, S.Entry>
  for +turn: S.Turn
  for examinations: List<&2, S.Watching>
  for +now: Nat
  for early: {Nat.is_lt(now, P.deadline(turn)) == True{} : Bool}
  {S.advance(head <> tail, Some{turn}, examinations, now) == Some{turn} : Maybe<&2, S.Turn>}

# proposed:
law S8(head, tail, +turn, examinations, +now):
  when now < turn.next_ms
  S.advance(head <> tail, Some{turn}, examinations, now) == Some{turn}
```

### Why

Laws are what a human reads to trust AI-written code, so they need to be short. We ported two small modules of our game server from TypeScript (51 and 56 lines) and had Codex write the Bend code and the proofs. The proofs were fine. The laws and their helpers came to 230 and 252 lines, and part of that is syntax: a typed `for` per binder, `: T` on every equality, `{b == True{} : Bool}` to use aBool as a condition, `Nat.add` for `+`, and no field access.

We wrote a desugarer for the syntax above and translated all 20 of our laws, and the 43 laws in the 2.0.38 demos, back into current Bend. Every translation is the same term as the original under Bend's own term comparison, and the original proofs give the same result on them, plain and with`--verdict`. It cuts what a human reads by 21% and 32% in tokens on our two modules, and the demo laws go from 399 lines to 175. Inferred parameters and bare `==` do most of it.

The rest of the length on our code is helpers that spell out exact behaviour, which no syntax removes. Happy to share the desugarer and the audit.

title: fix(verdict): use checked definitions as model fallbacks
body:
An uninstantiated higher-order template can fail `--verdict` with `no model for use~F`, even when the book contains a checked proof with the required type. This fixes the original example in #1182 by using that proof as the model after the existing model construction passes fail. It follows the [maintainer's proposed direction](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1263#issuecomment-6045064743).

The fallback selects a checked definition with no template parameters, no `@unsafe` flag, and an equal type in the model book. Normal emission sends its body and dependencies to the unchanged kernel. The template constant remains opaque. Each root constant records its model or `null`, so emission does not repeat a failed search. Existing model choices stay the same. The additional #1182 cases that need coordinated model choices remain out of scope.

Two regression fixtures cover the original `def` form and the `law` + `def` form with a helper declared later. The comments retain the rules for type propagation, model variables, empty types, and qualifying checked definitions. `safe.ts` is 23,996 ttok under its unchanged 24,000 cap.

Validation:

- Both new fixtures reproduce the failure on main `378be5fd`, print `Z{}`, and pass `--verdict` with Lean 4.34.0 and the unchanged BendTT kernel.
- The kernel rejects both exports when the proof body is replaced with `{==}`. Missing helpers, unsafe helpers, and an uninhabited dependent result remain rejected.
- All 1,741 fixture outcomes match the previous PR commit `f3ef5d3e`. All 1,254 emitted BendTT files are byte-identical, including 41 exports with unchanged out-of-scope entries. The other 487 fixtures fail the unchanged Bend checker. All 70 complete proof exports pass the kernel in both versions (140 checks). The original comparison against main also found no changed existing exports.
- A call-count check covers missing models, shared constants, model hits, instance models, and a real export retry. Each root constant now searches once per pass; text and diagnostics remain unchanged in all 11 cases.
- Repository gate: 54/54. TypeScript reports the same 11 existing diagnostics as `main`.
- The synthetic case with 3,000 unrelated definitions and 200 distinct missing models falls from 733 ms on the previous PR commit to 314 ms after caching misses (eight warmed, alternating rounds). The fallback still scans the checked definitions once per failed model request; main without this fallback took about 37 ms in the earlier comparison.

The distributed gates were not run because this environment has no cluster access.

Optional review suggestions tested:

- **Checked definitions below an extra binder:** I tested a third model pass seeded with checked definitions and a variant that traverses only lambdas. Both pass the original, later-helper, and extra-binder examples in the unchanged kernel. Missing-helper and unsafe-helper controls remain rejected. Both exceed the current file cap and repeat definition comparisons at each binder. In the 3,000-definition / 200-missing-model stress case, the seeded pass changes the median from 260 ms to 939 ms. The lambda-only variant changes it from 393 ms to 1,391 ms (five paired runs). These are separate runs, each compared with its paired baseline containing only the required fixes. Both are about 3.5 times slower. I left this extension out; it needs a more efficient type lookup.
- **Skip a matching definition that cannot be emitted:** I reproduced the selection problem with an `@unsafe` proof named `poison`, a checked wrapper named `first` that calls it, and a later valid `inj` proof of the same type. The export selects `first`, so `use` goes out of scope through `poison`. Skipping `first` helps the partial export, but the full verdict still fails because `poison` and `first` are roots. A guard on known failures handles only definitions already emitted; a general solution needs speculative emission and correct state recovery across group retries. I found no case where this change would make the full verdict pass, so I left it out of this PR.

title: fix(io): Process.run on macOS refuses a file with no #! line, as on Linux
body:
## What

`Process.run` is documented as running a program "without a shell", but on the C lane on macOS a file with no `#!` line ran through `/bin/sh`. macOS's `posix_spawnp`, like `execvp`, retries a file the kernel refuses with ENOEXEC as a shell script. glibc's `posix_spawnp` does not, and Bun answers ENOEXEC on both systems.

A file `/tmp/x` with mode 755 holding `echo through a shell`:

| lane | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| C, macOS | runs, prints `through a shell` | `Fail` with 8 (ENOEXEC) |
| C, Linux (glibc 2.41, Docker) | 8 | unchanged |
| Bun, macOS and Linux | 8 | unchanged |

On macOS the PATH search now happens in `process_spawn`, which calls `posix_spawn` on each candidate and follows the rest of [Libc's `posix_spawnp`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/Libc/blob/main/sys/posix_spawn.c): a name with a slash is not searched, an empty entry is `.`, a candidate too long for the buffer is ENAMETOOLONG, ENOENT/ENOTDIR/ELOOP/ENAMETOOLONG move on, E2BIG/ENOMEM/ETXTBSY stop, and any other error moves on when `stat` can't see the candidate, with EACCES kept for the end. Other systems still call `posix_spawnp`.

## Test

`tests/io/process_run_no_shell.bend` writes a script with no `#!` line to `/tmp`, makes it executable with `/bin/chmod` and runs it. It prints `refused: 8`. Before this change the C lane on macOS printed `ran: through a shell`; Bun passes before and after.

To check that nothing else moved, a small C harness calls `posix_spawnp` and a verbatim copy of `process_spawn` with the same PATH. They agree on every case but the `#!`-less file (0 before, 8 now): a symlink loop then a good entry (0), a loop alone (2), a 300-character component then a good entry (0), a candidate longer than `PATH_MAX` (63), a mode-000 directory then a missing one (2) or a good one (0), a mode-644 file then an executable one (0), a mode-644 file alone (13), a missing name (2), a trailing `:` (2), a name longer than `PATH_MAX` (63). A Bend probe built on main and on this branch also agrees on the C lane for: found in PATH, an empty entry running from the working directory, a `#!` script, a relative name with a slash, and PATH unset.

`tests/io/process_run*.bend` pass on Bun and C. `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54.

## Left as they were

Differences I saw while testing that this does not touch:
- Node on Linux runs the `#!`-less file through sh (libuv's child uses `execvp`); Node on macOS answers 8.
- With PATH holding only a non-executable match, Bun answers 2 and C answers 13; Bun also does not search an empty PATH entry. The C answers are the same as before this change.

title: Stop ignoring .agents folder + personal-preference skills
body:
I initially PR'd that .agents md should also be ignored, alongside then-also-ignored .claude folder. In hindsight: not the best idea. Claude now reads from .agents as well, and it only makes sense to establish common skills so that all mantainers are in sync.

title: CUDA: the dispatches' entry check reads the frontier from device memory, not from the managed H
body:
Fixes #1854.

#1447's entry check, `if (!turn_groups(H[H_FRONT], at)) return;`, makes every block of every CUDA dispatch wait on a load from the managed allocation, and that costs ~3.5% on programs made of many small bangs (#1854). A load from plain device memory costs nothing there, so this keeps a copy of the frontier in a `__device__ u64 bend_front`:

- `turn_set` writes it on the device too (pass 2, behind `BEND_RTC`, so Metal and the host are unchanged);
- the host writes it with one 8-byte `cuMemcpyHtoD` at the start of `gpu_pass`, after its own `turn_set`, and fails loudly if that copy fails;
- `gpu_load` takes its address with `cuModuleGetGlobal` (checked against `CUDA_SUCCESS`);
- the entry check reads it instead of `H[H_FRONT]`.

Every round keeps the check, the chained rounds included, the kernel keeps its three arguments, and Metal's code is unchanged.

RTX 4050 Laptop, driver 615.78.08, toolkit 12.9, alternated runs on an idle machine, the same output on both (the first two rows timed again on the rebased commit, 5 rounds; the benches before the rebase):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #1854's reproduction (10,000 one-round bangs, median of 5) | 13.58 s (13.52-13.72) | 13.05 s (13.04-13.06) |
| a two-layer Llama, 200 AdamW steps on the GPU (median of 5) | 16.71 s (16.66-16.79) | 16.21 s (16.19-16.27) |
| the 17 runtime benches on the GPU, `+RTS --gpu` (median of 3 each) | | geomean 1.00x (0.99-1.03x) |

After the rebase on 4f99f4c1, the tests with a bang and a `main` (45 files), built with both compilers and run on the GPU: 43 print their `#|` lines on both; the other two, `tests/printer/offload_bang_g` and `_h`, refuse to build on both, as they should.

`bend2/comp.ts` is at 66,059 ttok against the 66,000 cap (main is at 65,956), so the PR adds 103. I kept the change as small as I could (13 lines added, 2 changed) rather than trim unrelated code to fit. I have no Metal machine; the Metal path doesn't change, since every addition is behind `BEND_RTC` or in the CUDA host section.

title: fix(io): retry interrupted TCP sends without losing progress
body:
A signal interrupting `send(2)` makes `TCP.send`, `TCP.send_bytes` and their `try_` twins return `Fail(EINTR)`, including after an earlier short send. Both C and JS now retry the unsent bytes on EINTR. Successful short sends still advance the offset; EAGAIN and deadline handling are unchanged.

The regression uses a real socketpair with controlled syscall interception: EINTR before progress, a two-byte short send, EINTR again, then completion. It checks all four public APIs and verifies the exact UTF-8 bytes, including a short send inside a character. Unchanged upstream emitted JS and native C both exit 4 with `Interrupted system call`; the fixed interpreter, emitted JS and native C each print all four expected lines.

Validation on Linux x86_64, Bun 1.3.12:
- 27/27 program/backend checks: the new test plus tcp_bytes, tcp_loopback, tcp_try, tcp_try_bytes, tcp_try_recv, tcp_short_recv, tcp_recv_max_zero and tcp_send_slow_peer, each through interpreter, emitted JS and native C.
- Repository gate: PASS 54/54. `git diff --check` passes.
- Independent read-only review using review-agent: no findings; reviewer also checked repeated interpreter execution and a following TCP test in the same process.

Existing `tcp_text_residue` fails with `send stopped on a character boundary` on this Linux machine, identically on unchanged main d30d7ddd and this branch. It is not included in the passing count. No macOS, GPU or mini-cluster gate run is claimed. EINTR followed by EAGAIN/deadline expiry or a terminal error is not specifically injected by the new test; existing deadline tests pass.

AI-assisted implementation with an independent agent review.

title: fix(io): release timed-out JS channel payloads
body:
A timed-out JS channel waiter could retain its discarded payload through its timer while it remained behind a live waiter. `chan_late` now clears that timer reference alongside its other retained fields, preserving lazy queue cleanup and live timer lookup.

The new JS-only test exercises a real timed send and verifies that its discarded array is collected. It fails on unchanged main and passes with the fix.

title: Add Array.get_unchecked, an @unsafe read without the wrap mask
body:
Implements the first step Renan asked for in #1781: an `@unsafe` read whose index the caller promises is below the block's capacity. It skips the wrap mask; writes are unchanged.

**Spelling and safety**

- `Array.get_unchecked(-T: Data, a: Array<T>, +i: U32) -> Array<T> & T`, `@unsafe` like `Array.fork`.
- The interpreter runs its body, which is `Array.get` (so it stays masked there).
- The C lane emits the index without `blk_at`'s `and`; the JS lane reads `$0[$1]`.
- This is a proposal for the spelling/safety story; `bend2/bend.ts` is untouched, and I would not land it without your call on the name and the contract.

**Why only reads**

The writes in the tensor-array kernels are not the hot instruction here, and an unchecked write would need the same promise plus a story for the array's single owner. Keeping this read-only makes the surface smaller.

**Change**

- `bend2/base.bend`: the `@unsafe` definition.
- `bend2/comp.ts`: `array_get_unchecked` in `OPERATIONS`; `arr_op` uses `(u32)i << lgs` instead of `blk_at(...)` for it, and treats it as a get (no write).
- `tests/run/array_get_unchecked.bend`: reads an in-bounds cell and checks the returned array and value on the interpreter, C and JS lanes.

`bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 54 / 54`; `comp.ts` is at 65,981 ttok. The test prints `4.5`.

A local check on the #1781 dot loop (i7-14700HX, clang 22.1.8, Bend 2.0.39, one thread, three runs): 0.19-0.21 s with the mask, 0.12-0.16 s with `Array.get_unchecked`, same output. That is only a quick check, not the full tables Renan offered to run.

This does not address (2), the proof-bound read for tensor-array: as Renan said, tensor-array carries laws and cannot use `@unsafe`, and its copies in tensor-fork/tensor-gpu can take this read today. The checked version can replace it when the array carries its capacity.

title: fix(io): File.read and its twins read through fs on Node, where bun:ffi is missing
body:
`File.read`, `read_line`, `read_bytes` and `read_at` end the run on Node, because `file_read.js` asks `io_sys()` for libc's `read`/`pread`, and that needs `bun:ffi`:

```
$ node r.js     # File.open + File.read(f, 100) on a 5-byte file
Error: Cannot find module 'bun:ffi'
```

This is the same kind of bug as #1468, but for reads. When `io_sys()` throws, the reads now go through `fs.readvSync`, and the errno comes from the thrown error. On Bun nothing changes: the FFI path is the same code. I used `readvSync` and not `readSync` because `readSync` skips the syscall for a 0-byte read, so `File.read(h, 0)` on a write-only handle would answer `""` instead of EBADF. A failed `require("bun:ffi")` costs about 10 µs on Node (`readSync` costs about 0.4 µs), so the first failure is cached. Without the cache, 200k small reads took 3.2 s on Node. With it they take about 0.3 s.

`tests/io/file_read_no_ffi.{bend,js}` follows `file_size_no_ffi`: the twin makes `io_sys()` throw, the test reads `"hello\nbye"` through all four effects, then reads 64 bytes and 0 bytes from an append-only handle (both `fail 9`). On main it prints `Error: no ffi table on this host` (exit 1). With the fix it passes on interp and JS. The same `.bend` without the twin also prints the expected lines under real Node 25.9.

- The 20 file IO tests that use the read effects, plus `file_size_no_ffi` and `tcp_connect_no_ffi`, pass on interp, JS and C: 57/57. I ran them locally, not on the minis.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 54/54.
- Perf on Bun, 20 interleaved fresh-process runs each, main vs this branch, all within noise:
  - one 50 MB `File.read`: p50 going from 22.2 to 21.8 ms, p95 from 25.4 to 22.9 ms, peak RSS 122.8 MB on both
  - 200k `File.read(f, 16)`: p50 going from 201.9 to 201.0 ms, p95 from 203.7 to 205.1 ms, CPU 0.29 s and RSS 51.2 MB on both
  - Node, new: 43.9 ms and 316.8 ms p50 for the same two

The TCP/UDP effects still need `bun:ffi` on Node, as on main. I left them alone.

title: docs(io): each lane's clock zero, and File.read_line with max 0
body:
Two small doc fixes, both found by reading the code.

The complete example in `guide/EFFECTS.md` prints "ms since boot" on every lane, but only the C side counts from anything close to boot. `clock.c` reads `io_tick()`, which is `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (`comp.ts`, `io_tick`), and `clock.js` reads `performance.now()`, which starts with the process. So the two lanes print very different numbers for the same program. I changed the label to "ms" and added two sentences after the example saying where each side counts from, and that only the difference between two reads compares across lanes.

The comment on `File.read_line` in `base.bend` says it answers `""` only at the end of the file. With `max` 0 it also answers `""`: `file_read_fill` asks `read` for 0 bytes, gets 0, and `io_sys_end` leaves no error (`file_read.c`); `file_read.js` breaks out on `n <= 0` the same way. The comment now says both.

Docs only, so nothing to run. `base.bend` and `EFFECTS.md` have no ttok cap in `gates/repo.ts`.

title: fix(comp): an effect source's CIDs pull in their families, so Window.open without Window.frame builds natively
body:
A native build of a program that calls `Window.open` and never `Window.frame` failed to compile:

```
error: use of undeclared identifier 'CID_Text'
error: use of undeclared identifier 'CID_Key'
... (20 errors on macOS, one per Event constructor use)
```

The compiler defines `CID_*` only for the datatypes in `FL.srcs`. `Event` reaches a Bend program only through `Window.frame`'s return type, but `window.c`'s `Window.open` block builds events (`window_chunk`, the Mac view's `push:` calls), so a program that only opens a window names ids that were never defined.

`effect_src` already adds the defs a C source names by `FID(k)` to `FL.srcs`. Now, in the same `c_ids` callback, a constructor named by `CID(k)` adds its family too, so every id a hand-written effect uses is defined. One line in `bend2/comp.ts`; `window.c` is unchanged. This replaces an earlier version of this PR that defined the seven Event ids as 0 in `window.c`, a hand-kept list that #1867 broke within a day.

A side effect: `tcp_recv.c`, `udp_recv_from.c` and `udp_send_to.c` guard their bytes helpers with `#ifdef CID(Con)`, so loading one of those files now always pulls in `List` and compiles the helpers. They agree with the runtime's own `#ifdef CID(Con)`, and every TCP and UDP test still builds natively.

`comp.ts` stays under its cap (65,996 / 66,000) by dropping three comment phrases the code already says: the `(240 + log2 in CID_T)` formula, which `cid()` spells out; "adt_of and js_expr call it only for that check"; and the wording of the splice note in front of `c_ids`.

`tests/gfx/window_open_only.bend` opens a 0-wide window (it fails before looking for a display) and never calls `Window.frame`. Its C lane fails on main with the errors above and passes here.

Gates on `origin/main` 5396ca449: repo 54/54, test 1735/1735, perf 124/124, ping 81/81, safe 1124 agree / 0 false reject. Not run: the Linux X11 build.

title: fix(io): Window.open rejects a bad size or a NUL title on JS, as on C
body:
`Window.open("Bend", 0, 48)` answers EINVAL 22 natively but ENOTSUP (45 on macOS, 95 on Linux) on Bun and Node. A NUL in the title is the same story: EILSEQ on C, ENOTSUP on JS.

`window.c` checks the title for a NUL first (EILSEQ), then each side against 1..16384 (EINVAL), and only then looks for a display. `window_open.js` skipped straight to "no display". It now runs the same two checks in the same order, with the per-platform EILSEQ that `file_open.js` already uses.

Test: `tests/gfx/window_open_args.bend` opens with a zero or too-large side and with a NUL title. On main the JS lane prints `45` for all six cases while C prints the expected codes; with this change Bun, Node and C all print the same. `gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54. This is a cold error path, so no perf numbers.

The test calls `Window.frame` in its (never taken) `Done` branch because a C build that uses `Window.open` without `Window.frame` fails on `CID_Text`; that one is fixed in #1883. #1108 also edits `window_open.js`, so one of the two may need a small rebase.

title: test: chan_try_wake_timers freezes performance.now for the whole checkup process, so later sleeping tests in its shard hang the test gate
body:
### What happens

`tests/io/chan_try_wake_timers.js` (added in #1872) implements `Clock.stop()` on JS by replacing `performance.now` with a constant, and never restores it:

```js
function clock_stop() {
  const at = performance.now();
  performance.now = () => at;
  return { $: CID(Unit) };
}
```

`gates/test.ts` interprets every module of a shard in one process (`bend main.bend --checkup`). When a test that sleeps or waits on a bound runs after `chan_try_wake_timers` in the same shard, its timer never comes due, so bun never exits. The shard's ssh session then waits out its 20 minute timeout, and the gate (or `gates/_run.ts`, at its 30 s cap) fails with no verdict.

Whether this happens depends only on how `shard_split` packs tests by source size, so an unrelated PR that adds or resizes a test can trigger it. That is what happened on #1881: adding `tests/io/file_read_no_ffi.bend` put `chan_try_wake_timers` and `spawn_sleep` in the same shard (37 of 48), and the test gate hung. A later push moved them apart again and the gate passed.

### Repro (main at 5396ca449)

```text
$ printf 'import ./tests/io/chan_try_wake_timers.bend as a\nimport ./tests/io/spawn_sleep.bend as b\n' > agg.bend
$ timeout 15 bun bend2/main.ts agg.bend --checkup
--- ./tests/io/chan_try_wake_timers.bend ---
b 179700, a 44850
bend: deadlock: every computation waits on a channel
exit 1
--- ./tests/io/spawn_sleep.bend ---
main
                       # hangs; timeout exits 124
```

- Each test alone exits normally, and so does the reverse order (spawn_sleep first).
- `tests/io/chan_try_gone_bound.bend` after `chan_try_wake_timers` hangs the same way, so any test that waits on a timer is affected.

### Suggested fix

Restore the clock once the timers that need it are gone, as `tests/io/audio_monotonic_clock.js` does for `Date.now` with its reset call. For example, a `Clock.start()` twin that puts back the saved `performance.now`, called after the two drains and before the final `Chan.recv`. At that point no timer is left, so the deadlock is still reported at once and the expected lines stay the same.

title: test(io): chan_try_wake_timers starts the clock again once its timers are gone
body:
Fixes #1885.

`Clock.stop` on JS replaced `performance.now` with a constant and never put it back. `gates/test.ts` interprets every test of a shard in one process (`--checkup`), so any later test in the same shard that waits on a timer never sees it come due: the shard hangs until the gate's 20 minute ssh timeout, and the remote `bun` is left running on the mini (14 such orphans were found on the CI nodes today, the oldest 17 h old).

This adds a `Clock.start()` twin that restores the saved `performance.now`, called after the two drains, when no timer is left. The final `Chan.recv` still reports the deadlock at once, so the expected lines are unchanged. On C both effects are no-ops, as `Clock.stop` already was.

### Verified
`--checkup` of `chan_try_wake_timers` followed by another test (20 s cap):

| second test | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `spawn_sleep` | hangs (142) | `main / b / a / done`, 0 s |
| `chan_try_gone_bound` | hangs (142) | `bounded / ok`, 1 s |
| `tcp_connect_black_hole` | hangs (142) | `tick ×3 / ticks done`, 0 s |

- C and JS lanes of `chan_try_wake_timers` print the same three expected lines.
- `gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54.

title: feat(io): add positioned byte writes
body:
## Problem and fix

`r+` permits sequential overwrites, but Base has no positioned write that preserves the sequential cursor. Add `File.write_at(file, offset, bytes)` using C `pwrite` and an explicit JS `fs.writeSync` position. Related to #1843.

Append handles now return EINVAL before writing, including empty data, avoiding Linux silently appending at the wrong position. C checks descriptor flags; JS records append opens and clears them on close. The Base comment documents that a later failure can leave a written prefix.

## Blast radius

One additive Base definition, the existing C/JS file-write effects, JS open/close tracking, and one shared JS-runtime Set in `comp.ts` so separately scoped effect sources can share flags. Four regression files; ten files overall. No parser, emitter logic, dependency, gate, or cap changes. Existing sequential writes and #1817's shipped stdout flush remain intact.

Starting offsets remain `U32`; this does not complete #1843's 64-bit offsets/sizes or sync proposal. No atomicity, rollback, or durability guarantee is added.

## Regression evidence

The ordinary fixture covers binary bytes, unchanged neighbors, cursor preservation, EOF growth, holes, empty writes, byte validation, and handle reuse after failure. Its append extension rejects nonempty and empty positioned writes, verifies unchanged content after an allowed sequential append, and reopens for a successful positioned write. This extension fails against the previous PR head `5d90248` on source CLI, native C, Bun, and Node.

The controlled fixture exercises short writes, C EINTR retries, zero progress, and errors after partial progress. Independent mutations detect missing JS append registration, missing close cleanup, and misclassifying a failed C flags query as append.

## Checks

- Repository gate **54/54** with CI-pinned `ttok 0.3`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Both fixtures and existing binary, interrupted/zero-write, `r+`, byte-path, and stdout-order regressions pass source CLI, native C, emitted Bun, and emitted Node on macOS arm64.
- 96 deterministic random writes and a sparse write crossing 4 GiB match independent Python byte/size checks on all four paths.
- Linux arm64 Docker: **8/8** native C/Node runs pass, including append rejection and independent complete-file/sparse-region checks.
- Independent runtime controls pass for `open_bytes`, empty append writes, exact descriptor reuse, foreign handles without an open effect, and closed-descriptor errors. The gate-style `--checkup` aggregate also passes with both new fixtures, interrupted writes, and stdout ordering.

## Validation limits

Local macOS uses Bun 1.3.11, Node 26.8.2, and clang 23.1.4; Linux uses Node 26.12.1 and clang 14.0.6. Full mini-cluster test/performance/ping gates, GPU, Windows, x86-64 Linux, and Linux Bun were not run for this revision. Short/EINTR/zero-progress controls use fault injection; ordinary file operations and append rejection were observed through the OS. JS tracks append flags for handles opened through Bend; flags changed by foreign code are outside this check.

Existing `file_open_mode` passes three macOS paths; its Node error-message mismatch reproduces unchanged on the baseline. The foreign control fixture's `--check-only` reports foreign-dependent definitions; its executable paths pass. #1817 is now merged and included in the tested branch. Older #1601's complete integration remains unverified.

title: fix(cli): say when a ! program builds for the CPU because no CUDA toolkit was found
body:
Fixes #1863

On Linux, a program with `!` and no CUDA toolkit (no `include/nvrtc.h` under `$CUDA_HOME`, `$CUDA_PATH`, `/usr/local/cuda` or `/opt/cuda`) built with exit 0 for the CPU lane, and nothing said so. `cli_build` now prints one line to stderr and builds as before:

```
bend: no CUDA toolkit (include/nvrtc.h under $CUDA_HOME, $CUDA_PATH, /usr/local/cuda or /opt/cuda), so ! runs on the CPU
```

The change is a notice only, so existing CPU-only builds keep working. macOS always builds the Metal lane and never prints it.

- Linux (docker, arm64, clang 19, no CUDA): a `!` program prints the line, builds with exit 0 and runs (`1024`); the same program without `!` prints nothing.
- macOS: the `!` program builds with no notice.

title: fix(parser): refuse a stray = after a do block's last statement
body:
Closes #1868. Supersedes #1870, whose commit is kept here as the first commit (by @adeerkhan).

## What

Inside a `do` block, a statement the parser can't continue is taken as the block's last term, and the parser returns without checking what follows. With `x = v`, the leftover `= v` leaked to the term around the block, which then failed with `expected : a pattern (a binder or a constructor)` on the statement *before* the let.

#1870 caught this for a plain-name head only. A destructure (`(a, b) = v`, `Pair{a, b} = v`), a dotted name (`m.k = v`) or `return e = v` still leaked. This PR replaces that guard with `parse_do_end`, which runs where the block ends (after `return e` and after a plain last term) and refuses any `=` that isn't `==` or `=>`:

```
- expected : a do-block let with its type (write "x : T = ...")
- observed : '='
Location:
12 |     IO.print("a")
13>|     x = pure_of()
   |       ^
14 |     IO.print("ok")
```

Untyped do-lets are still not accepted; the message points to the typed form.

## Why only `=`

A broader check ("nothing but a dedent or a closer may follow the last statement") refuses valid code: a `)` on its own deeper line, `x : T = do M: return v;` (the outer let takes the `;`), and `{do M: a == b : T}`. The only places the parser accepts a bare `=` after a term are a let's pattern and a typed let's type, and a `do` block in either is already broken. So refusing `=` can't misfire.

## Checks

- Every `.bend` file using `do` (254) run with `--check-only` before and after: only the pins below changed (re-run after merging main).
- `tests/parse/do_let_untyped_after_step.bend` (moved from #1870's `tests/spec/comp_do_let.bend`, which isn't a comp-splice pin): the refusal above.
- `tests/parse/do_let_untyped.bend` (from #1807): its pin now takes the new refusal. #1807's note in `err_lost_type` only fired when the let was a plain name and the error span started at it, which is not the #1868 case; its `<-` note is unaffected.
- `tests/check/monad_do_destructure.bend`: its pin now takes the new refusal on `(a, b) = p`, not the old error on the line before.
- The three cases above still parse as before.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54.
- The full `gates/test.ts` shards (cluster) were not run.

title: Fast Array Initialization
body:
### What Bend should do

Bend should initialize arrays faster, or enable users to discharge to a proof of initialization before access.

### Why

I'm currently modeling a language runtime in Bend, using arrays to model stacks/continuations. Array initialization and resizing (to double size) is currently running about 8 instructions per word, or about 15% of my current benchmark loads.

Array initialization should not be the performance bottleneck.

title: refactor(comp): simplify comp.ts with the same behavior (-137 ttok)
body:
Structural simplifications to `bend2/comp.ts`, taking it from 65,982 to 65,845 ttok on main 757180e3 so #1880 can restore the comments it removed and still fit under the 66k cap. No names are shortened, no comments removed, nothing golfed; each change removes a concept or a duplicate of an existing helper.

| Change | ttok |
|---|---:|
| `emit_put` drops the bindings left at a body's end, since every `emit_put` ends a body: `emit_spin` loses its `tail` mode, and `emit_body` / `emit_match` their own `bind_dead` before `emit_put`. |  −27 |
| `val_new` is the one place that decides which words keep a root; four callers stop filtering by `box` themselves. | −35 |
| `js_match` sends Nat rows through the literal rows, as `emit_match` does for C. | −24 |
| CUDA's `gpu_map` zeroes the managed memory it maps, instead of `corpus_setup` doing it under `#if BEND_CUDA`. | −23 |
| JS closures build their wrapper with `block()`, as `js_def` does. | −18 |
| `unit_emit` resets `FL.unit` to null after the unit emits, instead of saving and restoring it: units never nest and it starts out null, so a use outside a unit still fails. | −10 |

## Output

All 1,762 tests, and the 72 `.bend` files under `demos/` and `bench/`, built to C and JS with main and with this branch:

- C differs only by the CUDA zeroing moving from `corpus_setup` into `gpu_map` (compiled out on Metal and CPU).
- JS differs only where a Nat test was `x === N` and is now `x == N`, the same as word literals. A Nat in JS is always a number, so the two are equivalent.
- Build logs (including expected refusals) are identical.
- The 771 JS outputs that changed print the same under both builds.

title: BendTT: a comparison is done when both sides are already the same, and first runs with every def rigid
body:
Part of #1164 (the kernel half; the elaborator half is a separate PR). Alternative to #1815's kernel change.

## What

`Term.fits` unfolded both sides to their weak heads before comparing, with no equality check. A type def whose unfolding names itself, like `F = ∀-x:F -> <>`, therefore never finished comparing to itself: `F` against `F` unfolds to the same `∀`, compares the domains, `F` against `F` again, until the stack overflows. Even `id : ∀x0 : F -> F = λx0 => x0` overflows on `main`. `Term.conv` doesn't have this problem because it checks `a = b` first; `fits` didn't.

This brings the kernel's comparison closer to bend2's `term_compare`:

- **`fits`** checks `U = T` before unfolding, as `conv` already did with `a = b`. When both sides unfold to the same term, the comparison one level down starts with the same check, so there is no second check after unfolding.
- **`Term.rigid f`** runs a comparison first against `Book.nil` (the empty book, where no def unfolds), then against the real book, each pass from the same fuel (so a comparison can now spend up to 2 × `FUEL`). It's used where the checker starts a comparison (`Ctx.fit`, and the `Rfl` check of an equation), as bend2 runs its rigid pass at the top of `term_compare`.

The new check only turns a failure into a success, and the full pass starts from the same fuel, so `--verdict` can't reject anything `main` accepted.

Compared with #1815's `sameRef` shortcut, the `U = T` check also covers applied recursive types with identical arguments: for `H(A) = ∀-x:H(A) -> A`, `λx => x : H(x0) -> H(x0)` still overflows #1815's kernel and checks here. Arguments that differ only by unfolding (`H(U1)` vs `H(U2)` with `U2 = U1`) still overflow; that needs comparing arguments before unfolding, left for a follow-up.

## Proofs

- The new equality branch in `fits_sound` is `crefl`.
- `sees_nil`: `Book.nil` is seen by any book.
- `rigid_sound` reuses `fits_sound` and `conv_sound` unchanged for both passes.

`lean bend2/bendtt.lean`: no errors, no `sorry`, the same 62 warnings as `main`.

## Checks

Hand-written `.bendtt` files on the built kernel (`main` overflows on all the accepted ones):

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `om : ∀x0 : ∀-x0:F -> <> -> <> = λx0 => (x0 -x0)`, and its η-long form | checks |
| `keep`, `run` from #1164, η-long and not | checks |
| `id : F -> F`, `id : F -> ∀-x0:F -> <>` | checks |
| `id : ∀-x0:*1 -> ∀x1:(H x0) -> (H x0) = λ-x0 => λx1 => x1` | checks |
| `boom : <> = (om om)` | rejected (quantity) |
| `bad2 : ∀x0:F -> ∀x1:F -> <> = λx0 => x0` | rejected (quantity) |
| `F` against a separate but identical-looking `G = ∀-x0:G -> <>` | still overflows (needs comparing infinite unfoldings; out of scope) |

`--verdict` over all 1763 files in `tests/`, `main`'s kernel vs this one (both with `main`'s elaborator): identical output on every file (1134 check, 629 fail), total time 465 s vs 461 s, no file more than 2 s slower. On the cluster, merged onto `main` fad0bb9da (87f93dd3): repo 54/54, test 1771/1771, ping 81/81, perf passes (it doesn't run the kernel), safe 1143 agree / 0 false reject. The hub corpus wasn't run.

No `.bend` test here: on `main`, every `.bend` file with a recursive function type overflows in `safe.ts`'s η-long elaboration before reaching the kernel. The #1164 examples become `--verdict` tests in the elaborator PR, which needs this one to pass them.

title: fix(io): write held stdout before a JS File read
body:
**Bug:** on JS, `IO.print` holds stdout when it is a pipe. `File.read*` blocks in `readvSync` without writing it out first, so a program that prints and then waits for a reply deadlocks. C writes it out before it waits (`io_sync` before `select`).

**Repro:** `{ printf 'a\n'; sleep 3; printf 'b\n'; } | node prog.js`, where `prog.js` echoes each `File.read_line` of `/dev/stdin`. JS prints `a` after 3 s; native prints it at once.

**Fix:** `io_sync()` at the top of `file_read_with`, as `file_write.js` does. Only `bend2/effs/file_read.js` (+2 lines) and one test in `tests/io/` change.

**Cost:** a loop that prints between reads now writes on each read, as C does.

**Tested:** new `tests/io/file_read_stdout_order`: on `main`, the interpreter, Bun and Node print `two one three`, and native passes; with the fix, all four pass. Nearby `tests/io` file and stdout tests pass. Linux (WSL2), Bun + Node. Not tested: macOS, the cluster gates.
