title: The run path (`bend file.bend`) overflows its stack on a 32k-element list, while `--check-only` and `-o` are fine
body:
The plain run path dies with `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)` and exit 1 — no file, no line — on a twelve-line program that the checker accepts and that compiles and runs natively without trouble.

## Repro

```bend
import Base
import mlbend-generative@0.1.1.0/main.bend as G

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  xs = G.noise_of(7n, 32768n)
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(Nat.show(List.length(&2, F32, xs)))
    return Unit{}
```

```
$ bend repro.bend
bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)        # exit 1
$ bend repro.bend -o prog && ./prog
32768                                               # fine
```

## Where the line is

| list length | `bend file.bend` | `-o` then run |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 | prints 4096 | fine |
| 8192 | prints 8192 | fine |
| 16384 | prints 16384 | fine |
| **32768** | **faults** | prints 32768 |
| 65536 | faults | prints 65536 |

Same on **2.0.38** and **2.0.39** (both checked on the same machine).

## Why I think it is the run path, not the program

- `--check-only` passes.
- `bend … -o prog` then running `prog` does the same work (65536 elements) in both versions.
- It is frame size, not recursion depth: a 65536-element **Nat** list summed by a recursive `match` on the same run path is fine, so the run path tolerates 65536 frames when each frame is small. Each element here is a Box–Muller call (`G.noise_of` → `gauss_at`), and ~32k of those frames do not fit.

## Why it matters

`bend <file>.bend` is the documented way to run a program ("check the file, then run main"). A program of this size is ordinary for data and ML work; the failure mode gives no location and looks like a fault in the program, so the first move is to rewrite code that is fine. It cost me an afternoon before I noticed `-o` was unaffected.

A larger stack for the run path, or a diagnostic that names the limit (`stack limit reached: N frames; build with -o for the compiled path`), would both resolve it.

I can minimise further or test a patch if that helps.

title: fix(io): flush stdout before JS file reads
body:
When stdout is piped, a prompt written with `IO.write` can stay buffered while `File.read_line` waits for input. The shared JS file-read helper now flushes stdout before reading, so a client waiting for the prompt can respond.

The new regression checks stdout/read ordering. It fails on the previous code and passes across the tested runtimes. Focused file-read/output-order tests, Linux container checks and the repository gate (54/54) pass.

title: safe.ts: a term at a type with no finite η-long form goes out whole (#1164)
body:
Fixes #1164 together with #1892 (the kernel half, merged). Alternative to #1815.

Rebased onto `main` after #1930 and #1945, the simplification passes that make room for it under `safe.ts`'s cap.

## What

`safe.ts` writes every term of a function type η-long, because bend2 converts up to η and the kernel doesn't. Some types have no finite η-long form. One kind names itself again in its unfolding: `F = @-x: F -> Empty`, `H(A) = @-x: H(A) -> A`. The other keeps growing: `K(n) = @-x: K(1n+n) -> U32`. Before this PR, `-o` and `--verdict` overflowed the stack on terms like `om(f) = f(f)`, `keep(f) = f` and `run(g, k) = g(k)`.

`eta_finite` decides this per call (a type not headed by a ∀):

- **The rule:** a call goes whole if it embeds a call of the same def that it was unfolded from (homeomorphic embedding). A repeat embeds itself.
- **What "embeds" compares:** a variable matches any variable, a nat matches any no smaller nat, and any other literal matches a literal of its kind. It remembers each pair of nodes it has compared, so a comparison costs at most the product of the two terms' sizes.
- **Computed arguments:** a call is compared at its arguments' data: constructors computed down, a nat as its literal, a datatype at its head. bend2 checks a type position dead, with no descent check, so `Dn(Nat.sub(n, 1n))` is accepted; compared as written, `Dn(Nat.sub(3n, 1n))` would look like it grew out of `Dn(3n)`. If computing an argument never ends, `-o` hangs, as bend2 would.
- **Why the walk ends:** every path that never repeats eventually reaches such a call.
- **Every other call goes η-long,** but only after the calls it unfolds to are decided. So an η-long call never leads back to itself.
- **Each call is walked once:** `e.fin` keeps each verdict, a ∀'s too, so the walk is linear in the number of distinct calls. `e.keys` keeps each type object's key by depth, so a repeated question skips the lowering.
- **Keys:** a call is keyed by the variables it binds, with every other variable written the same way. So when the emitter later asks about a type under its own binders, it lands on the same calls.

At a type that goes whole, two things now go out whole instead of η-long: a tree leaf outside a Σ chain with no column left to take, and a call's argument.

Exported now:

```
keep : ∀x0 : ∀-x0 : F -> Empty -> ∀-x1 : F -> Empty =
  λx0 => λ-x1 => (x0 -x1)
keep_k : ∀x0 : (K (.Zero, ())) -> (K (.Zero, ())) =
  λx0 => λ-x1 => (x0 -x1)
```

The first call of a recurring or growing def still gets one η level (`keep`, `keep_k`, `keep_h3`), and the call it unfolds to goes whole. In a cycle through two defs (`MA` ↔ `MB`), the one asked about first goes whole.

## Cost

Two kinds of equation now fail `--verdict` because the kernel converts without η:

- **An η equation at a type that recurs**, like `{f == (x => f(x)) : F}`. Before this PR it overflowed. #1815 rejects it too.
- **An η equation that needs an η level past a finite count-up**, like `D(0n) → D(1n) → D(2n) → U32`. Any rule that always stops must cut some count-ups that happen to be finite.

At other finite types, η equations still check. That includes `V(A, 1n+p) = A -> V(Two(A), p)` and `C(i, 1n+p) = U32 -> C(1n+i, p)`, where one argument grows while another shrinks.

## Checks

- `tests/check/eta_recursive_type.bend` covers:
  - `om`, `keep`, `run`, `keep_h`, `keep_h3` and `keep_k`
  - `id : F -> F` and `id : H(A) -> H(A)`
  - η equations at `Endo(Endo(U32))`, `Fun(2n)`, a finite alias, `W(z, z => z)`, `P = (U32 -> U32) -> F`, the written-out `@-x: F -> Empty`, `V` and `C`
  - the mutual growth `MA`/`MB`
  - `keep_r` over `Dbl(24n)` (`Dbl(1n+p) = Dbl(p) -> Dbl(p)`), which takes 0.5 s; a walk that repeats shared subtrees takes over 60 s and would hit the gate's 30 s limit

  `gates/test.ts` only runs `--checkup`, so `gates/safe.ts` is what exercises this.
- `--verdict` on all 1792 files of `tests/` against the previous head (a9c5177d), run locally with the same kernel: the same verdict on every file.
- Timing with `-o` (`main` in parentheses): `Fun(4000n)` 0.6 s, `Dbl(20n)` 0.06 s, `C(0n, 300n)` 0.18 s (0.07 s), `V(U32, 16n)` 2.1 s (0.58 s), `V(U32, 18n)` 8.6 s (2.2 s). `V`'s η-long output grows 4× per two levels, on `main` too. Before memoising `embeds`, `C(0n, 22n)` took 16.7 s and `V(U32, 16n)` 17 s.
- The test also covers `Dn(3n)`, a count-down through `Nat.sub`, and `C(0n, 60n)`, which the version before memoising did not finish in 120 s.
- `bun gates/safe.ts tests`: 1796 files, agree 1144, unsafe 142, bend2 rejects 507, out of scope 3, false reject 0, timeout 0, infrastructure 0.
- `bun gates/_run.ts`: repo 54 / 54, test 1783 / 1783, perf 123 / 124 (pass), ping 80 / 81 (pass). `safe.ts` is at 23900 / 24000 ttok (23991 with #1949).
- Not run: the hub corpus.

Not fixed here: `Sink = U32 -> Sink` still hangs bend2's own `--check-only` (#1164).

title: --verdict: a law instantiated with lambdas for a ~ function and a ~ proof about it is out of scope ("an application with no known head type"), though bend2 accepts it
body:
### What you did

bend hyp.bend --verdict

### What happened

```text
Human note: My AI is confident I should submit this, I'm learning bend and don't understand it myself tbh, but from what I do understand it seems real.

Bend 2.0.39 (the latest release; the same code path is on `main` at 9a4dfe3c), Linux x86_64, kernel built with Lean 4.34.0.

### Reproducer


import Base

law via:
  for ~f: U32 -> U32
  for ~ok: (@x: U32 -> {f(x) == f(x) : U32})
  for x: U32
  {f(x) == f(x) : U32}

def via(f, ok, x):
  ok(x)

law use:
  for x: U32
  {(x + 1 : U32) == (x + 1 : U32) : U32}

def use(x):
  via(~(y => (y + 1 : U32)), ~(z => {==}), x)


### What happens

- `bend hyp.bend --check-only` prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- `bend hyp.bend --verdict` prints `SOME PROOFS FAIL`, then `BendTT: out of scope: - use: an application with no known head type`, then the TypeScript/kernel mismatch banner.
- `bend hyp.bend -o hyp.bendtt` prints `BendTT: out of scope, so not in hyp.bendtt: - use: an application with no known head type`.

### When it happens

It takes both: the template function and the template proof about it must each be something other than a plain name. Swapping either one for a named def makes `--verdict` pass.

| `~f` | `~ok` | `--verdict` |
|---|---|---|
| named def | named def | passes |
| lambda | named def with a declared type | passes |
| named def | lambda | passes |
| lambda | lambda | out of scope |
| def applied to a template, `app_h(~h)` | def applied to a template, `h_ok(~h)` | out of scope |
| lambda | def applied to a template | out of scope |

A lambda for `~f` alone, with no hypothesis about it, passes. So does a curried lambda for a two-argument `~f`.

The second reproducer has no lambda among the arguments, only applied defs:


import Base

def app(~g: U32 -> U32, x: U32) -> U32:
  g(x)

law via:
  for ~f: U32 -> U32
  for ~ok: (@x: U32 -> {f(x) == f(x) : U32})
  for x: U32
  {f(x) == f(x) : U32}

def via(f, ok, x):
  ok(x)

def app_h(~h: U32 -> U32) -> U32 -> U32:
  y => app(~h, y)

def h_ok(~h: U32 -> U32) -> (@z: U32 -> {app_h(~h)(z) == app_h(~h)(z) : U32}):
  z => {==}

law use:
  for ~h: U32 -> U32
  for x: U32
  {app_h(~h)(x) == app_h(~h)(x) : U32}

def use(h, x):
  via(~app_h(~h), ~h_ok(~h), x)


### Where it seems to come from

The message is raised in `spine` in `bend2/safe.ts` (line 1091 on `main`). When an application's head is neither a def nor a variable, the translator takes the head's type from an annotation, and otherwise gives up. Substituting the argument for `~f` into `~ok`'s type `@x: U32 -> {f(x) == f(x) : U32}` leaves `(y => y + 1)(x)`, whose head has no annotation. A named proof avoids this because its type comes from its own declaration.

`~f`'s declared type (`U32 -> U32`) is available at that point. So the translator could annotate the substituted argument with it, or beta-reduce a lambda head.

### Expected

Either `--verdict` translates this (bend2 already accepts it), or bend2 rejects it for the same reason, so that the check and `--verdict` agree.

### Workaround

Give the proof a name with a declared type. That works when `~f` is a lambda. It doesn't work when the proof itself needs template arguments, as in the second reproducer. There I proved the instance directly by the same induction, instead of instantiating the general law.

### Impact

I hit this while instantiating a generic law with list functions. The law says that a derivative lifted from correct single-edit derivatives is correct. The instantiation is out of scope, so each instance needs its own copy of the induction.

### Related

- #1175 (closed): a spliced inline lambda emitted an un-annotated beta-redex. It's a similar shape, on a different path.
- #1483: a template lambda capturing a run-time value. The reason given differs: "a template argument that depends on a run-time value".
- #1182: how `--verdict` chooses models for `~` constants.

---
```

title: fix(io): retry interrupted native file opens
body:
Native `File.open` and `File.open_bytes` returned `Fail(EINTR)` when a signal interrupted `open`. Retry only interrupted opens, then return the final descriptor or error.

The native regression test injects two interruptions for each path type. It checks successful opens and `EEXIST`, and rejects any retry after the final result. The JS test uses ordinary file opens.

Validation on macOS:

- The new native regression fails before the fix and passes after it.
- A separate test sends a real signal during a blocked FIFO open. It fails before the fix and passes after it.
- All 43 executions across 15 related file tests pass, using the default run, generated JS, and native C where supported.
- The new generated JS test also passes under Node.
- The repository gate passes: 54 / 54.

Linux was not tested. The full cluster gate was not run.

title: fix(io): park the JS File and Process effects so io_wait flushes stdout
body:
**Bug:** on JS, `IO.print` holds stdout when it is not a terminal. `File.open`, `File.read*`, `File.size`, `File.write*` and `Process.run` run synchronously inside the effect (`openSync`, `readvSync`, `Atomics.wait`), so the loop never reaches `io_wait` and never writes the held text before blocking. A program that prints and then reads from a peer waiting for that output deadlocks. C runs these effects through `io_work`, parks the fiber, and flushes in `io_wait` before `select`.

**Fix:** each of these effects parks itself with `io_park_on(undefined, 0, k, () => …, 0)`, due at once, so it runs at the next `io_wait`, after its `io_sync`, as in C. This follows the rule `io_eff` already enforces ("an effect that waits parks itself"), so nothing new goes into the loop:
- `io_run`: unchanged.
- `io_wait`: skips `select` (and `io_sys`, which needs `bun:ffi`) when it waits on no fd with a zero timeout, so parked files still work on Node.
- `file_write.js`: its own `io_sync` is gone; the wait flushes first.
- `comp.ts`: +11 ttok (65,985 / 66,000).

As in C, the fiber now parks, and other fibers run before its result comes back. The remaining difference is inherent to JS: the syscall runs on the main thread, so it blocks every fiber while it runs.

Supersedes #1893 (by @MattCozendey), which added an `io_sync` to `File.read` only. Its test `tests/io/file_read_stdout_order` is kept.

**Tested (macOS):**
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 54 / 54.
- All 30 `tests/io` tests that use File, `Process.run` or `random_u32`, plus `file_read_stdout_order`, pass on Bun.
- `file_read_stdout_order` and `stdout_file_order` pass on Node.
- Repro (`IO.print("ready")`, then `File.read_line` on `/dev/stdin`, fed by `(sleep 3; echo hi) |`): "ready" arrives at 0 s on Bun and Node.
- New `tests/io/file_open_fifo_peer`: stdout is moved onto a pipe read by a shell that opens a FIFO for writing only after it sees "ready", so a flush that comes after the effect blocks hangs the run. With this PR it passes on native, Bun and through `--checkup` (stdout is put back for the next test). On `main`, the Bun lane hangs (killed at 10 s) and native passes.

- `tests/io/file_read_prompt`, from #1895 (by @toprameen): `IO.write("prompt> ")` with no newline, then `File.read_line`. Passes on Bun, Node and through `--checkup`; on `main` the read runs before the prompt is written.

Not run: native, the cluster gates.

title: fix(io): UDP sends continue after interruptions
body:
UDP text and byte sends currently return a failure when a system call is interrupted before transmission. The C and JS implementations now make another send attempt with the same datagram and destination, following the TCP behavior in #1878. Other errors, existing deadline handling, and empty datagrams keep their existing behavior.

The regression exercises all four send APIs with two controlled interruptions followed by a real loopback send. It checks the received bytes and that one successful send occurred. The exact test fails on unchanged main and passes with this change in the default run, emitted Bun JS, and native C.

Local macOS arm64 validation passed 30 focused executions across 10 fixtures and the repository gate passed 54/54. Independent Astra/high review found no actionable issues and exercised the waiting and error paths. Interruptions were injected; real-signal and Linux behavior have not been exercised.

title: fix(verdict): preserve dependent template argument types
body:
Passing a lambda as a `~` function together with its dependent proof made `--verdict` report `an application with no known head type`. Match lambdas and template applications that normalize to lambdas had the same failure. Bend accepted the source, but the elaborator could not export the proof.

Fixes #1897.

## How

`tele_open` (used by `def_emit`) gives each specialized `~` column its checked domain:

- `arm` receives the column annotated at its domain, so a call to a `~` parameter in the body has a known head type.
- In the def's type, a λ column goes into later domains bare, so it β-reduces where a domain applies it, but with its body typed at the codomain (`lam_typed`, from a lowered copy, so applying it does not re-normalize its argument). An annotated λ there leaves `App(Ann(λ), x)` redexes that `kind()` cannot see through (a `~` λ returning a Type-kind datatype went out as a kernel mismatch). A fully bare λ loses the type of a match it returns or receives.
- Other columns (match lambdas, applications) go into later domains annotated.

Specialization cache keys keep the original normalized columns. Datatype columns are never specialized and a template never leads a group, so `adt_emit` and `group_emit` are unaffected in practice.

A second commit simplifies `safe.ts` with the same output (one-line switch cases in `term`, inferred return types on local arrows, `MARK` for `mark()`, inlined one-use locals, shorter comments), to fit the change under the 24,000-token cap.

## Tests

Twelve fixtures in `tests/proof/template_proof_*.bend`: direct lambdas, template applications, nested templates, dependent domains, shared and erased parameters, reuse of an involution proof, a match lambda as a theorem result, in a later proof parameter's domain and returning a type, a curried λ returning a match, a match passed to a λ in a later domain, and a λ returning a Type-kind datatype.

## Validation (merged onto main 00d29f448)

- Gates: repo 54/54, test 1815/1815, perf 124/124, ping 81/81. safe: 1158 agree vs main's 1146 (the 12 fixtures), 0 false rejects, 3 out of scope as on main.
- `--verdict` over all 1,815 tests: identical to main except the 12 fixtures, out of scope on main, `ALL PROOFS CHECK` here.
- `-o` over all tests: byte-identical to main except the fixtures and `template_inst_model.bend`, whose `qvvv_1`/`qvvv_2` types now read `(pred (.S, (x0, ()))) == x0` instead of `x0 == x0`. The kernel accepts both.
- The simplification commit alone: every `.bendtt` export of `tests/` is byte-identical.
- `safe.ts`: 23,953 / 24,000 tokens.

## Not fixed here

A λ column whose body applies a match lambda, e.g. `~(y => ({\{True: False{}; False: True{}} : Bool -> Bool})(y))`, is still out of scope, as on main: the column is normalized with `term_snf`, which drops the inner match's annotation.

title: `Process.open`: a child's stdin and stdout as `File` handles
body:
**Need.** I run a program that answers my lines, one at a time. I send a line. It answers with lines. I send the next line. The program must stay alive between turns.

**Problem.** `Process.run` cannot do this. It takes all input at the start and gives all output at the end. Base has no `File` for a child's stdin or stdout. It has no `stdin` handle for the program itself.

**My workaround.** Two foreign effects. They return Base's `File` type, so I add no handle type (#825).
- `open(program, args)` gives the pid, the child's stdin and the child's stdout. The child's stderr is the parent's. Closing stdin gives the child EOF.
- `stdin()` gives the program's own stdin.

It is about 300 lines of C and JS. The JS lane uses Bun's FFI only (`pipe(2)` and `Bun.spawn`), never Node. It works on Linux and macOS.

**Ask.** Will you add `Process.open` and `stdin` to Base? I would then delete my code. Open points: stderr, wait and kill, and the JS lane.

I found no issue, PR or WONTFIX entry about this.

title: fix(io): File.write_at rejects an O_APPEND fd on Bun, as on C
body:
`File.write_at` on a file descriptor that has O_APPEND, but didn't come from `File.open(path, "a")`, answered differently per lane:

| lane (macOS) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| C | `Fail` 22 (EINVAL), file unchanged | same |
| Bun | `Done`, byte 0 overwritten | `Fail` 22, file unchanged |
| Node | `Done`, byte 0 overwritten | same as before (no `bun:ffi`) |

`base.bend` says an append handle fails with EINVAL before any byte is written. `file_write.c` reads that off the fd (`fcntl(F_GETFL) & O_APPEND`). `file_write.js` only checked `io_file_append`, which `file_open.js` fills for mode "a", so an append fd opened any other way went through to the write. A shell's `>>` on stdout, reopened as `/dev/stdout`, is one way to get such an fd.

`file_write.js` now asks the fd with `fcntl` through `io_sys()`, the way `tcp_connect.js` reads flags, and falls back to `io_file_append` where `bun:ffi` is missing. So Node behaves as before: it refuses the "a" handles from `File.open` and can't see the rest.

Test: `tests/io/file_write_at_append_fd.bend` opens the file with O_APPEND in a C/JS twin, outside `File.open`. On `main`, the interpreted and Bun runs print `unexpected success: write_at on an O_APPEND fd rejected`, and C passes. With this change, every lane prints the three `#|` lines. A second case takes the FFI table away with the helpers from `file_read_no_ffi.js` (no-ops on C) to pin the Node fallback. It fails if the fallback returns `false`.

Checked on macOS arm64: the new test, `file_write_at`, `file_write_at_control`, and `file_binary` on every lane, `file_read_no_ffi` on Bun, the built `file_write_at.js` under Node 24, and `gates/repo.ts` (54 / 54). Not run: the cluster gates, and Linux, where pwrite(2) on an O_APPEND fd appends whatever the offset, so the stray byte would land at the end instead.

title: app_win_is_bug_2d: PROOF.bend passes after an edit that lets the player reach the flag
body:
### What you did

`bend PROOF.bend` in `demos/app_win_is_bug_2d`, after the edit below

### What happened

```text
$ bend PROOF.bend
ALL PROOFS CHECK
Use --verdict for mathematical validity.
$ bend REACH.bend
won field: True (the player stood on the flag)
```

`LAWS.bend` is the same as on `main`. Even so, seven `Left{}` and four `Up{}` from `start()` put the player on the flag. On the unedited demo, the same moves leave `won` at `False{}`.

The README says the AI "could have moved the flag, made the room kill you, or whatever. The only thing it can't do is commit a bug". Here the player takes the flag, which is the bug the demo is built to block.

### The file

The edit replaces three bodies in `main.bend`:

```python
def wall(+x: Nat, +y: Nat) -> Bool:
  False{}

def is_won(g: Game) -> Bool:
  False{}

def at_flag(g: Game) -> Bool:
  False{}
```

and rewrites `PROOF.bend`:

```python
import Base
import ./main.bend as Game
import ./LAWS.bend as Laws

def Laws.you_cant_win(moves):
  {==}

def Laws.never_on_flag(moves):
  {==}
```

`REACH.bend` replays the moves:

```python
import Base
import ./main.bend as Game

def say(g: Game.Game) -> IO(Unit):
  Game.Game{x, y, w} = g
  match w:
    case True{}: IO.print("won field: True (the player stood on the flag)")
    case False{}: IO.print("won field: False")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  say(Game.replay(Game.start(), [Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Left{}, Game.Up{}, Game.Up{}, Game.Up{}, Game.Up{}]))
```

### bend version

Bend 2.0.39 (`main` at 7a7e6505)

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)

### Why it happens

In 0ea9d0f3 ("the flag law is the page's own"), `LAWS.bend` defined `drawn`, `flag_at`, and `at_flag` itself, so `never_on_flag` was about the board the page draws. 573002f0 moved them into `main.bend` for #1119 ("LAWS files hold laws only"). `main.bend` describes itself as "AI-written and may be rewritten at will", so the law now rests on a definition the AI is free to change. The comment above the law still promises "an 'F' cell of the board the page draws", which is the same kind of gap #1119 fixed in `io_http_fetch`.

The lab on bend-lang.com still ships the 0ea9d0f3 `LAWS.bend`. With that file, the same edit fails at `Laws.never_on_flag`.

This isn't #1002. Every name here resolves as written.

### Possible fixes

All three keep LAWS files to laws only.

1. Write `never_on_flag` against `Game.grid` with Base alone (`String.lines`, `List.get`, `String.get`), so no AI-owned helper sits between the law and the page. The flag certificate in `PROOF.bend` would have to be redone.
2. Move the page-reading helpers to a human-owned file that `LAWS.bend` imports, and say in GUIDE that a law's helpers belong there.
3. Narrow the comment to what the law states, as in #1119, and pin the helpers with laws on concrete boards, for example `{Game.at_flag(Game.Game{1n, 1n, False{}}) == True{} : Bool}` and `{Game.is_won(Game.step(Game.Left{}, Game.Game{2n, 1n, False{}})) == True{} : Bool}`. Both hold on the demo today and fail after the edit above, but they only rule out this particular edit.

I'm happy to open a PR for whichever you prefer. I couldn't run `--verdict` here (no Lean), but the proofs use no `@unsafe` or foreign code, so I'd expect it to accept them too.

title: feat(base): add U32.popcount and U32.ctz

Bit counting is the core loop of bitboards (chess, Go), bitsets and sparse sets. This gives it an obvious name that is always the fast version.

- `U32.ctz`: `popcount(~n & (n - 1))`, so 32 at 0 with no branch.

title: fix(io): TCP receives retry after an interruption instead of failing
body:
A `recv(2)` interrupted by a signal returns -1 with `EINTR`. `TCP.recv` and its three twins (`recv_bytes`, `try_recv`, `try_recv_bytes`) answered that as `Fail(4)` ("Interrupted system call") on both lanes: C's `io_again` retries only `EAGAIN`, and the JS lane only `35/11`. Nothing was read, so the call should simply be retried, as #1878 did for TCP sends and #1900 for UDP sends.

**Change**
- `bend2/effs/tcp_recv.c`: retry `recv` while it fails with `EINTR`, before `io_sys_end`.
- `bend2/effs/tcp_recv.js`: same retry on `errno` 4; `EAGAIN` still parks and `try_` deadlines are untouched.

**Test**: `tests/io/tcp_recv_interrupted.{bend,c,js}` wraps `recv` (C via `RTLD_NEXT`, JS via `sys.recv`/`sys.errno`, like `tcp_send_interrupted`) so the first call on the armed socket fails with `EINTR`, then checks that each of the four effects still reads the data and that the retry happened.

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| interp | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 4/4 lines, exit 0 |
| C (clang) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 4/4 lines, exit 0 |
| JS (Bun) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 4/4 lines, exit 0 |

The other 17 `tests/io/tcp_*` tests give the same output on interp and C; `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. Run on macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; not run on Linux or Node.

title: fix(io): UDP receives retry after an interruption instead of failing

title: fix(io): TCP accepts retry after an interruption instead of failing
body:
An `accept(2)` interrupted by a signal returns -1 with `EINTR`. `TCP.accept` and `TCP.try_accept` answered that as `Fail(4)` ("Interrupted system call") on both lanes: C's `io_again` retries only `EAGAIN`, and the JS lane only `35/11`. No connection was taken off the backlog, so a server loop lost an accept for nothing; the call should simply be retried, as #1878 and #1900 did for sends.

**Change**
- `bend2/effs/tcp_accept.c`: retry `accept` while it fails with `EINTR`, before the `O_NONBLOCK` step.
- `bend2/effs/tcp_accept.js`: same retry on `errno` 4; `EAGAIN` still parks and the `try_` deadline is untouched.

**Test**: `tests/io/tcp_accept_interrupted.{bend,c,js}` listens on a loopback port, connects to it, and wraps `accept` (C via `RTLD_NEXT`, JS via `sys.accept`/`sys.errno`) so the first call on the listener fails with `EINTR`. It checks that both `TCP.accept` and `TCP.try_accept` still hand back the connection and that the retry happened.

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| interp | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 2/2 lines, exit 0 |
| C (clang) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 2/2 lines, exit 0 |
| JS (Bun) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | 2/2 lines, exit 0 |

The other `tests/io/{tcp,http,server}_*` tests and `port_bound` give the same output with and without the change on interp and C; `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. Run on macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; not run on Linux or Node.

title: fix(io): an interrupted TCP connect is waited on instead of failing
body:
A non-blocking `connect(2)` interrupted by a signal returns -1 with `EINTR`, but POSIX keeps the connection going in the background: it completes as an `EINPROGRESS` one would, and calling `connect` again answers `EALREADY`. `TCP.connect` closed the socket and answered `Fail(4)` ("Interrupted system call") on both lanes, dropping a connection that was about to succeed.

**Change**
- `bend2/effs/tcp_connect.c`: when `connect` itself answers `EINTR` (the socket exists), treat it as `EINPROGRESS`: park until writable, then read `SO_ERROR`.
- `bend2/effs/tcp_connect.js`: same, for `errno` 4 once `fcntl` has made the socket non-blocking.

Unlike #1878 and #1900, this does not retry the call: a second `connect` on the same socket would fail with `EALREADY`.

**Test**: `tests/io/tcp_connect_interrupted.{bend,c,js}` wraps `connect` (C via `RTLD_NEXT`, JS via `sys.connect`/`sys.errno`) so it starts the real connect and then answers `EINTR`, as an interrupted call does. It accepts on the listener, sends "hi" over the new socket, reads it back, and checks that `connect` was issued only once.

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| interp | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | `connected once`, exit 0 |
| C (clang) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | `connected once`, exit 0 |
| JS (Bun) | `Interrupted system call`, exit 4 | `connected once`, exit 0 |

The 27 other `tests/io/{tcp,http,server}_*` and `port_bound` tests give the same output with and without the change on interp and C; `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. Run on macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; not run on Linux or Node.

Note: #1825 also edits `tcp_connect.js`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: 2.0.38 added `Event.Text` to Base; a program with its own `Text` constructor is refused with "duplicate declaration: Text", and the notes do not say so
body:
### What you did ``` bend text_ctor.bend -o text_ctor ``` ### What happened On 2.0.37 the program builds and prints `text:hi

`. On 2.0.38, 2.0.39 and main (bf35ec3, 2026-10-28, run with `bun bend2/main.ts`) the same file is refused before any of its code is checked: ```text Error: - expected : a fresh constructor name (duplicate declaration: Text) - observed : 'Text' Location: 4 | type Node is Data: 5>| Text{s: String} | ^^^^ 6 | Elem{tag: String} ``` The other declaration is Base's: 2.0.38 gave `type Event` a `Text{text: String}` constructor ("Native windows emit `Text` events", #1019, PR #1441). A constructor name is one namespace with Base, so a Base addition can refuse an existing program that never imports windows. Three things made this cost more than the rename itself: 1. The 2.0.38 notes mark `+RTS`, the JS tags and `TCP.send` as **Breaking** and say nothing about `Text`. A new bare constructor name in Base is a breaking change for every program that already uses the name (bend-lint hit the same one: PR #1565). 2. The error points only at the user's line. It does not say that the other `Text` is Base's `Event.Text`, so the first reading is "I declared Text twice", and the search starts in the wrong place. 3. The guide does not list the bare constructor names Base reserves. Today there are 23 (`Chr Close EQ F32 False GT Key LT Look Mouse Move Pix Qua SCon SNil Scroll Succ Text True U32 Unit WNil Zero` in 2.0.39's base.bend); `Text`, `Key`, `Move`, `Close`, `Look` are ordinary words a DOM, a game or an editor would pick. What would have avoided the afternoon: a **Breaking** line in the notes when Base gains a bare constructor name; the error naming the other declaration (`Base: Event.Text`); and a line in the guide saying Base's constructor names are reserved, with the list or the `grep` that produces it. Whether a user constructor should be able to shadow Base's, or Base's event constructors should carry a prefix as #1565 did for bend-lint, is your call; the report is about the silence. The same pattern in 2.0.36: `Chan.send` answering `Result` instead of `Bool`, `TCP.recv` answering `Maybe`, and `io_eff` losing its third argument shipped without a Breaking line (PR #1259). Programs that compiled on 2.0.35 stopped, and for the C effect only `clang` said so. ### The file ```python import Base # A program with its own `Text` constructor: 2.0.37 builds it, 2.0.38+ refuses it. type Node is Data: Text{s: String} Elem{tag: String} def show(n: Node) -> String: match n: case Text{s}: "text:" ++ s case Elem{tag}: "<" ++ tag ++ ">" def main() -> IO(Unit): IO.print(show(Text{"hi"}) ++ " " ++ show(Elem{"p"})) ``` ### bend version bend 2.0.39 (also 2.0.38, and main at bf35ec3 run with `bun bend2/main.ts`); builds on 2.0.37 ### uname -sm Darwin arm64 ### clang --version (the first line) Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)

title: 2.0.38 and 2.0.39 emit C that Apple clang 21 cannot compile ("live register clobbered by inserted prologue instructions"); 2.0.37 and main from #1817 build
body:
### What you did

```
bend main_c2.bend -o element-c2
```

A ~1400-line program (a CDP server) built natively with the clang Xcode ships. Its source is private; the emitted C is 89-102 MB.

### What happened

```text
fatal error: error in backend: live register clobbered by inserted prologue instructions
clang: error: clang frontend command failed with exit code 70 (use -v to see invocation)
```

This is the Apple clang 21 diagnostic reported second-hand in #1233 (closed by its author). Here it is reproduced, with a version range:

- The same program builds natively on 2.0.37 with Apple clang. On 2.0.38 and 2.0.39 the emitted C fails as above at `-O3`, `-O2` and `-O0` (`-O0` dies after 190 s on the 2.0.39 C, 102 MB).
- Homebrew LLVM clang 22.1.8 compiles the same C at `-O3` and the binary runs. That is my workaround: `CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang`, which 2.0.39 honors.
- main at 52637f7 (2026-10-28, run with `bun bend2/main.ts`) emits C that Apple clang 21 compiles at `-O3`, and the binary serves. `git bisect` over c2ed404e..52637f7 with the same program (emit, then Apple clang `-O3`): c2ed404e, 7e59bfb and 34c7abb crash, 3ed8746 compiles. **3ed8746 (#1817, 2026-10-27) is the first commit whose C Apple clang 21 accepts.** The emitted C is 63 KB larger from that commit on (88,889,623 to 88,952,728 bytes). #1817 describes its change to the C as the spin prototypes and the order of spins, so what Apple clang trips on seems to depend on where a function sits in the file, not only on its body; the shape may still be latent.

So the emission that trips Apple clang entered between 2.0.37 and 2.0.38 and left with #1817. 2.0.38 and 2.0.39 are the released versions where a program that checks does not build with the clang Xcode ships, and nothing in their notes says so. The release that carries #1817 closes this for me; I am filing the range so its notes can say so, and so anyone on Xcode's clang knows which versions to skip or to set `$CC` on.

### The file

Not small, and private. I can attach the emitted C gzipped (9.7 MB) if it helps reduce it.

### bend version

bend 2.0.38 and bend 2.0.39 (fail); bend 2.0.37 and main at 52637f7 (`bun bend2/main.ts`) build

### uname -sm

Darwin arm64

### clang --version (the first line)

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)

title: perf(io): dequeue the JS run queue without Array.shift
body:
`io_run` took each runnable computation with `io.runs.shift()`, which moves every remaining entry on V8, so draining N runs that became runnable together was O(N²) on Node. #1859 fixed the same pattern for the channel's waiters; this is the scheduler's own queue, which those waiters wake into.

**Change** (`bend2/comp.ts`, `io_run` only, +4/−3): new runs still go to `io.runs`; the loop pops from a local `next`, and when `next` is empty it takes `io.runs` reversed as the next batch. Order stays FIFO, each dequeue is O(1) amortized, and a dequeued run is released at once. `io_push` and the C runtime are untouched. comp.ts stays under its cap (65998 / 66000 ttok).

**Drain**: `N` spawned tasks park on `Chan.recv` of one rendezvous channel; `main` closes it, so all N become runnable at once. Before → after, median of 10 runs per arm (each a fresh process, before/after interleaved, macOS arm64, Node 25.9, Bun 1.4.2):

| N woken | Node wall | Node CPU | Bun wall | Bun CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25k | 0.23 → 0.06 s | 0.27 → 0.10 s | 0.03 → 0.03 s | 0.09 → 0.09 s |
| 100k | 0.83 → 0.10 s | 0.91 → 0.19 s | 0.08 → 0.08 s | 0.24 → 0.22 s |
| 200k | **14.39 → 0.18 s** | 14.65 → 0.45 s | 0.12 → 0.11 s | 0.30 → 0.28 s |

Bun's `shift` is already O(1), so Bun is level. On Node the queue only gets deep through channels: `IO.sleep` and the `try_` timers need `bun:ffi`.

**New test**: `tests/io/run_queue_fifo.bend`. 20000 spawned waiters park on a channel; a closer spawned after them wakes all 20000 at once, and each reports its index on a second channel, which `main` must read as 0, 1, 2, ... It passes on interp, Bun, Node and the C binary before and after the change; with the `reverse()` dropped it fails with `woken out of order at 0`. The other `tests/io` tests give the same results with and without the change on interp, and `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54.

title: fix(tests): the FIFO peer gives up when its run dies first
body:
`tests/io/file_open_fifo_peer` (from #1899) starts a peer shell that echoes the run's first line to the real stdout, then writes "hi" into a FIFO the run opens. The peer inherits the shard's stdout, so if the run dies before opening the FIFO, the peer blocks forever on `printf hi > fifo`, orphaned, holding the node's ssh session open. The test gate then waits out the 20 min shard timeout instead of reporting the failure, which looks like a hung cluster node.

Seen with #1906, whose JS runtime throws `ReferenceError: str_in is not defined` at `peer_arm`'s return: every test gate run hung on the node holding this test's shard and left two orphaned peers there (checkup lane and JS lane).

The fix, in both the C and JS peers:
- `IFS= read -r l || { rm -f "$1"; exit 1; }`: a run that dies before its first line closes the pipe, and the peer exits.
- `(sleep 10; [ -p "$1" ] && rm -f "$1" && kill $$) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`: in the checkup lane the error text itself becomes the first line, so the peer also needs a bound on the FIFO wait. The watchdog only acts if the FIFO is still there (the normal path removes it within milliseconds), so it never kills the `cat` the peer execs into, and it holds no stdout.

Checked:
- main + this: test gate `PASS: 1781 / 1781`; repo `PASS: 54 / 54`. The test prints exactly `ready`, `hi` on the C, JS and checkup lanes, with no peer, watchdog or FIFO left after.
- #1906 + this: the gate finishes in 15 s with `FAIL io_file_open_fifo_peer [interp]` / `[js]` (`PASS: 1746 / 1781`, the rest of that shard's checkup lane fails with it) instead of hanging, and no peer is left on the node.

title: fix(io): an interrupted File.read_line no longer reads a byte before its buffer
body:
`file_read_fill` retried an `EINTR` with `continue` inside a `do { } while`, so the retry first evaluated the loop condition. In line mode with nothing read yet (`got == 0`), that condition reads `w->data[got - 1]`, one byte before the buffer. If that byte happened to be `'\n'`, the loop stopped and `File.read_line` answered `""`, which callers take as end of file, instead of retrying.

**Change** (`bend2/effs/file_read.c` only): retry the `read`/`pread` in its own `do { } while (n < 0 && errno == EINTR)`, the loop `tcp_recv.c` and `file_write.c` already use. The JS twin reads `b[-1]` as `undefined` and was already right.

**Test**: `tests/io/file_read_line_interrupted.{bend,c,js}` wraps `read` (C via `RTLD_NEXT`) so the first read of the file answers `EINTR`, then checks that `File.read_line` answers `ab\n` and that the read was retried.

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| C with `-fsanitize=address` | `heap-buffer-overflow` in `file_read_line_call` | `[ab\n]`, exit 0 |
| C (clang -O3) | `[ab\n]` (the stray byte was not `'\n'` this time) | `[ab\n]` |
| interp | `[ab\n]` | `[ab\n]` |

Without ASan the old code only misbehaves when the byte before the allocation is `'\n'`, so the test is deterministic only under ASan. `file_read_line`, `file_read_after_error`, `file_binary`, `file_open_interrupted` and `file_write_interrupted` give the same output; `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. Run on macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; not run on Linux.

title: perf(cli): the .bend loader reads and checks Base once per process
body:
`load_js`, which backs the Bun plugin, the node hook and the page bundler, called `book_read(path)` with no base, so every `.bend` module a process imported parsed and validated Base again. `cli_checkup` already avoids this by reading Base once and seeding each file's book from it when the file's header imports Base.

**Change** (`bend2/main.ts` only):
- `imports_base(file)`: the header check `cli_checkup` used inline, now a function both callers share.
- `load_js` keeps one `load_base` promise per process and passes it to `book_read` when `imports_base` holds; a file whose header does not import Base reads as before.

**Imports** (`N` modules, each `import Base` and one def, imported from a Bun script through the plugin). Before → after, median of 15 runs per arm, before/after interleaved, each a fresh process, macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2:

| modules | imports | whole process |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 38 → 38 ms | 54 → 54 ms |
| 4 | 102 → 40 ms | 118 → 56 ms |
| 16 | 338 → 47 ms | 356 → 62 ms |

The first module still pays for Base; each later one now costs ~1 ms instead of ~20 ms.

**Same output:** the exported `load` gives byte-identical JS before and after for all 109 `tests/run/*.bend` (103 load, 6 fail with the same error on both), loaded in one process so the after side reuses Base across all of them. `module_export_keys`, `bundle_inline`, `bundle_page_input`, `html_script_types`, `output_input_links`, `nat_host_export`, `f32_host_export`, `process_run_node_module`, `random_u32_js_fail` and `chan_try_release` give the same output and exit status. `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. Not run on Linux or under node's `--import` hook.

title: Explain JS run-stack exhaustion and give the native command

title: comp.ts: shed tokens with no output change

title: Add hi/lo positioned file IO and size64
body:
This picks up the remaining 64-bit file IO part of #1843. The `r+` mode and U32 `write_at` already landed in #1853 and #1887.

Adds `File.read_at64(file, hi, lo, max)`, `File.write_at64(file, hi, lo, bytes)` and `File.size64(file)`. Offsets are `hi * 2^32 + lo`, below `2^63`; sizes come back as `(hi, lo)`. Positioned operations leave the sequential cursor alone, and the existing U32 `size` still reports overflow rather than truncating.

One JS trap worth calling out: Node 22 silently ignores a BigInt position in `writeSync` and `readvSync`. Wide reads use `readSync` instead; Bun uses typed `pread`/`pwrite`. Node returns `EOVERFLOW` before a write crossing its safe-integer position range, rather than writing at a rounded or ignored offset. C and Bun support the full signed offset range.

Checked 14 file cases on Bun and 12 on native C, including the new sparse-file regression up to 8 GiB; that regression also passes as standalone Node JS. Separately used real files of size `2^53 + 5` to check odd read/write offsets and size halves against Python's OS calls: exact bytes and unchanged cursor on all three backends, with Node's unsupported write leaving the file untouched. Those sparse files used 4 KiB each and were closed/unlinked. Repo gate: 54/54.

title: Device: a lane runs up to 4096 steps on HEAP_OFF after a failed allocation (page faults on AMD)
body:
When `heap_alloc_miss` cannot bump a page, it posts `ERR_HEAP` and returns `HEAP_OFF`, the reserved first heap page, which every failing lane then shares. A lane reads the error word only through `err_spun`, every 4096 steps: the main loop has polled at 4096 since c7276c38, and 85ecb69e8 made 4095 the one mask. Until then the lane keeps stepping on nodes that other failing lanes overwrite, reads one shape as another, and can follow a word that was never a location.

- **HIP** (the `hip` branch; RX 6600M, ROCm 7.2.4): `bench/runtime/tree-radix` at the default 1 GB span ends in `Memory access fault by GPU node-1 ... Page not present`, at an address about 34 GB past the corpus, instead of `bend: out of memory`. Polling on every step makes it report out of memory on every run, so the window is the cause.
- **CUDA**: same path. A stray load outside the managed corpus is an illegal address, so the run would end in `bend: device fault`. It is rarer, since the span is the whole card. Untested.
- **Metal**: same window. `tree-radix` at `--gpu 1GB` on an M-series reports out of memory cleanly, so either the GPU tolerated the loads or that run did not take the path. Untested beyond that one run.

Fix on the `hip` branch (1878aaec): `err_post` sets a plain `__shared__` flag (`BEND_RTC` only) that `err_spun` reads every step, so a lane stops at its next step after it posts. On HIP it costs nothing measurable (gameoflife 105 vs 109 ms). A per-step read of the global error word cost 24x, and a volatile shared flag 10x. Metal would need the flag passed down as threadgroup memory, since MSL has no file-scope threadgroup variables.

#1820's `WL_NSPIN` does not go through `err_spun`, so with both, its inner loop needs the flag too.

title: fix(lint): changed imports fail the declaration guard
body:
The declaration guard now compares import paths and aliases, including Base, before reusing loaded dependencies. Previously, a rule could receive approval for an import change that altered the program’s result. Whitespace and comment formatting remain accepted.

All 136 bend-lint tests pass; both new regressions fail before the fix. The repository gate passes 54/54. Type checking retains the same three existing bend.ts errors.

title: Add interactive child pipes and stdin Files
body:
A child can now stay alive between requests: `Process.open` gives its pid and stdin/stdout Files, `Process.wait` reaps it, and `File.stdin` duplicates the program’s own stdin. There’s no shell, and child stderr stays with the parent.

The JS side is Bun-only, as requested. It follows the existing effect-local `Process.run` worker approach; `io_run` stays synchronous, and captured runs still work on Node.

Checked with native Clang and Bun: repeated exchanges with one child, EOF, a wait started before the exchanges, exit/signal status, and handle ownership. Existing process/reentrant IO cases, real piped stdin, inherited stderr, Node compatibility, the trusted-kernel Base import, and repo gates also passed. The Bun/native cases also passed on macOS arm64: https://github.com/oxura/bend/actions/runs/40772796513/job/123114157667.

Closes #1902.

title: safe: preserve affine quantities for single-use live captures (depends on #1489)
body:
## Scope and dependency

**Draft, partial fix. Depends on #1489.** This branch preserves oxura's commits through 3d56955222017f07b5416d377efbbb6ee6da239a unchanged. Their typed capture lifting is not my work. The additional commit is f0e720d255919f89b06199c10fa2df5a19070c66. Please review that delta until #1489 lands, then this can be rebased. This is not a replacement or duplicate of its type-only support.

Allow a single-use live template capture to be passed through the existing explicit capture environment without declaring an arbitrary closure reusable. Capture quantities are carried consistently on lifted binders and call arguments: known Data gets quantity 2, otherwise quantity 1. The native BendTT kernel remains the final gate. No change to bend.ts, Base, the kernel, theorem statements or unsafe handling.

## Regressions and local results

Official Bun 1.4.4, macOS arm64, official Lean 4.34.0, native BendTT built from this dependency's exact kernel source. Tests ran with sanitized environment and isolated HOME.

- New tests/check/template_live_capture.bend: --check-only and actual --verdict pass. Its generic caller passes a runtime A -> A closure once. Before this delta, #1489 rejects it as a runtime-dependent template argument.
- New tests/check/template_live_capture_affine.bend: --check-only passes, but actual --verdict **must reject** the duplicated affine closure. It rejects in twice.qvv_1, expected *2, observed *1. This intentionally records the remaining frontend/kernel discrepancy, not a passing kernel law. Its check-only expected output follows the existing fixture convention.
- Existing tests/check/template_type_capture.bend: --check-only and --verdict pass.
- Separate False == True negative proof: still rejected by frontend.
- Actual bend-collections intrusive edits proof at 60b73aa0899c81687604b9626ade1a12afac04de: passes kernel under the dependency. No changes to that proof.
- Actual bend-collections hash_table/proof.bend: **still fails**, now in the native kernel at set_post.qvvvvvv_1 with expected *2, observed *((.Q1 <&> .Q1)). This confirms we do not make its affine higher-order witness duplicable merely to manufacture success.

## Explicit non-goals and remaining work

This does **not** fix the six bend-collections definitions sc_from, pc_from, dc_from, set_contract, pop_contract, del_contract. The source passes a runtime witness containing an affine function to a template that reuses it. A general live-capture translation cannot just give that witness Data kind. A sound broader design is still needed. No proof was dropped, specialized to a trivial example, or reported verified from partial emitted output.

This draft intentionally changes such cases from blanket out-of-scope to kernel rejection. It is not merge-ready until the desired diagnostic/classification, capture cache/quantity interactions, and full regression gates are reviewed. The existing #1489 cap/mutual-group concerns are inherited, not claimed resolved.

## Commands and gate limits

For each fixture: bun bend2/main.ts tests/check/FILE.bend --check-only and --verdict, with Lean 4.34.0 on PATH and no BENDTT override so the matching kernel is built. git diff --check passes.

bun gates/repo.ts was attempted locally but could not complete because ttok is unavailable. No cap was changed. The permanent 24k safe.ts budget remains applicable. Private mini-cluster test/ping/perf/safe gates were not run and no cluster access is claimed. Broad soundness/compatibility is not inferred from this small targeted set.

The initial motivation was #1483, but #1489 already addresses the type-only reproducer. This PR only proposes the additional quantity-preserving single-use live-capture slice. Automated assistant implementation and local testing, with the dependent work explicitly attributed above.

title: perf(c): let clang vectorize blk_new's fill at a runtime depth
body:
Part of #1890. Growing an array by doubling it (`ANode{a, Array.new(T, k, v)}`) could fill each new half one cell at a time in the C backend. When the depth is a runtime value, clang can fail to count the iterations of `blk_new`'s fill loop, depending on what it inlines around it. This one-line change gives it a count it can read, and the `U32` fill is vectorized in every probe below.

It does not speed up array initialization in general. A fresh `Array.new` with a constant depth was already vectorized, and so was the doubling loop in some inlining shapes (see below). The gain is in the runtime-depth cases where clang failed to count the loop.

## Cause

`blk_new` fills its block with

```c
for (u64 i = 0; i < (1ull << c); i += 1) {
```

When `c` is a constant (a fresh `Array.new(U32, 24n, v)`), clang vectorizes this loop. When `c` comes from a runtime depth (an array grown in a recursive loop), `-Rpass-analysis=loop-vectorize` reports "loop not vectorized: could not determine number of loop iterations", and the loop's exit test compiles to `lsr x16, x8, x9; cbz x16`, which tests `(i >> c) == 0`. Computing the bound once and testing `i != w` gives clang a trip count it can read.

## Change

```diff
-  for (u64 i = 0; i < (1ull << c); i += 1) {
+  for (u64 i = 0, w = 1ull << c; i != w; i += 1) {
```

`c` is at most 31 (the `d + lgs > 31` check above), so `w` cannot overflow, and `w >= 1`, so the loop runs the same iterations as before. The refcount loop above it is untouched.

## Benches

Apple M1, Bend 2.0.39, main at 65a521fe (this branch is on 4f99f4c1, which leaves `comp.ts` unchanged), built with the CLI's `clang -std=c11 -O3`. Each probe makes 100 arrays and reads one cell of each into a checksum. Instructions come from `/usr/bin/time -l` (medians of three runs), minus the same probe at depth 0, divided by 100 × 2^d. Every probe prints the same checksum before and after.

| probe | main, instr / element | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Array<U32>` doubled from one leaf to 2^24 | 5.81 | 1.24 | −79% |
| `Array<Pt>` (two `U32` fields) doubled to 2^23 | 15.62 | 13.60 | −13% |
| `Array<String>` doubled to 2^20 | 64.64 | 60.52 | −6% |
| fresh `Array.new(U32, 24n, v)` | 0.27 | 0.27 | none |
| fresh `Array.new(Pt, 23n, v)` | 14.04 | 14.04 | none |
| fresh `Array.new(String, 20n, v)` | 58.57 | 58.56 | none |

Wall clock for the `U32` doubling probe, 7 interleaved runs: main 1.03–1.07 s (median 1.05), this PR 0.60–0.64 s (median 0.60). A run the day before gave medians of 1.14 and 0.69.

The doubling probe (`u32-grow-24`):

<details>

```python
import Base

def fill(+i: U32) -> U32:
  i

def key(x: U32) -> U32:
  x

def at(r: Array<U32> & U32) -> U32:
  (a, x) = r
  key(x)

def grow(+d: Nat, +k: Nat, +v: U32, a: Array<U32>) -> Array<U32>:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      a
    case 1n+p:
      grow(p, 1n+k, v, ANode{a, Array.new(U32, k, v)})

def one(+i: U32) -> Array<U32>:
  grow(24n, 0n, fill(i), ALeaf{fill(i)})

def loop(+n: Nat, +acc: U32) -> U32:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      loop(p, U32.add(U32.mul(acc, 3), at(Array.get(U32, one(U32.add(acc, 1)), acc))))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(U32.show(loop(100n, 1)))
```

</details>

Whether clang vectorizes the old loop depends on what it inlines around it. With `one`, `fill` and `key` removed (`grow(24n, 0n, U32.add(acc, 1), ALeaf{U32.add(acc, 1)})` inline in `loop`), main already vectorizes the fill, at 1.05 instructions per element, and so does this PR. With `i != w`, both shapes vectorize.

## Assembly

The inlined fill in the `U32` doubling probe, before (one 32-bit store per 5 instructions):

```
sub  w16, w8, #1
str  w10, [x14, w16, uxtw #2]
lsr  x16, x8, x9
add  x8, x8, #1
cbz  x16, loop
```

After (16 cells per 7 instructions, then a scalar tail):

```
and  x16, x14, #0xfffffff0
add  x16, x8, x16, lsl #2
stp  q4, q4, [x16]
stp  q4, q4, [x16, #32]
add  x14, x14, #16
cmp  x9, x14
b.ne loop
```

## Checks

- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54. `comp.ts` goes from 65,956 to 65,960 ttok (`gpt-3.5-turbo` encoding).
- The C lane of `gates/test.ts`, run locally with the gate's rules: 877 / 879, including the 80 array tests that build to C (8 more have mains the gate does not print, and it skips them on this lane, as here). The two failures, `gfx_clicks` and `gfx_window`, expect "no display". This Mac has a desktop session, so they fail the same way on main here. `tests/run/stencil3d.bend` builds with `BANGS 1`, so the Metal compiler accepted the changed runtime source, and the test passes. That is a compile check. I did not confirm that any test runs `blk_new` on the GPU (stencil3d's `Array.new` calls are arguments to its bang).
- Arrays at depths 0 to 9, made fresh with a runtime depth and doubled from one leaf, of `U32` (fills 0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 2654435761), two- and three-field structs, `String`, and a `U32` and `String` struct. The C output is the same as the JS lane's and the interpreter's on every line, on main and here.
- I did not run `tsc`. The change is inside the C runtime's text.

## Not covered

- GPU execution of the new loop is untested, on Metal and on CUDA. CUDA was not built at all. There is no toolkit on this machine.
- The cluster gates (`gates/test.ts` on the minis, `gates/perf.ts` against the pins) were not run.
- Two-field elements stay scalar. The fill reloads `v[i & 1]` every cell (6 instructions a cell). `__restrict` on `v` does not change that, so it is not aliasing. A fix needs a different loop shape and belongs in its own change.
- `String` elements cost about 60 instructions each, and this change takes 4 off the doubling probe, so most of the cost is elsewhere (probably reference counting). Not measured further.
- #1778 (the fill running on one GPU lane) is not addressed.

title: fix(native): run effect cleanup before fatal exit
body:
Closes #1624.

This fills the cleanup gap left after #1655 and #1828: native effect constructors can set `err_cleanup`, and the first fatal claimant runs it before exiting. The hook must be async-signal-safe. It doesn’t recover the program or swallow its original signal.

I checked this with real PTYs on Linux and macOS arm64. Before the change, failstop/SIGSEGV/SIGBUS left the terminal raw; afterwards, its configuration is restored and the exit/signal stays the same. Normal exit is a separate control. [macOS before/after and stack-fault run](https://github.com/oxura/bend/actions/runs/40775148841/job/123122403391).

The native consumer also covers one-shot cleanup and a fault inside the hook; it passed through native, Bun and Node on Linux. The existing stack-fault case still terminates by signal on both OSes.

Repo gate: 54/54. Compiler: 65,992/66,000 tokens, with no budget or gate changes.

title: safe.ts: simplify; three small fixes
body:
Split out of #1896, to merge before it: the parts of that PR that only simplify `safe.ts`, with nothing about η, a further cleanup pass, and three small fixes the reviews of it found (see Behaviour changes). Meant for a squash merge, so #1896 rebases cleanly after it.

## What

New helpers, beside the existing `alls`, `lams` and `mats`:

- `Of<K>` for `Extract<HTerm, { $: K }>`.
- `vr(l)`, `ref(k)` and `lab(k)` for the kernel's `Var`, `Ref` and `Lab`.
- `apps(f, xs)` for a head applied to its arguments, each at its quantity. It replaces eight hand-written `reduce`s:
  - `root_emit`'s annotation
  - `adt_emit`'s `at`
  - `tree`'s convoy and dry match
  - `args`
  - `group_call`
  - `group_emit`
  - `arm`
- `ann(e, s, o, T, why)` for a kernel term annotated at `T` unless the kernel infers it. `spine`, `let_term` and `rwt_term` each spelled this out, with their own handling of a missing `T`. With no `T`, `why` is the out-of-scope reason.
- `tup(xs)` for the tuple `(x, y, .., ())`. `ctr_term` builds constructors with it, and `group_call` builds selectors.
- `wnf(b, T)` for `B.term_wnf(b, T)` (27 uses).
- `fill(b, T, xs)` for `B.tele_fill(b, T, xs, B.ctx_nil())` (7 uses).
  - Both take the book, so the Model section uses them at `e.mb` and the rest at `e.book`.
- `tkey(t)` for `B.term_key(B.term_lower(t))` (3 uses).
- `node(x)`: a type guard for whether `x` is a λ, a match or a refutation, which `tree` and `arg_term` each tested by hand.
- `pass(e, s, n, ps, live, qs)` for a call's non-specialized arguments, each at its quantity. `args` and `group_call` share it.
- `pair_lams(e, q, l, b)` for a default arm's λs over its tag and fields.
- `copies(e, q, b, ls)`: `q`, or 2 when `q` is 1 and `b` uses one of the levels `ls` twice. This rule is now written once, for `lams`, `pair_lams` and `let_term`.
- `scope_var(s, T, q)` binds the next bend2 variable to a new kernel binder. It replaces `scope_bind`'s `kb` flag and `scope_kq`. `scope_hide(s, q)` takes the binder's quantity directly.

- `group_emit` builds its selector types with `alls` and `apps`, instead of nesting the Σ and ∀ by hand.
- `convoy_bind` always ends in a function `f(s)`, which every caller already built, instead of taking a tree and its chain too.
- A tree's λ goes through `lams`, which handles the copy, instead of reassigning `q`.
- `o_show` and `o_uses` walk with an inner closure. `o_uses` no longer threads its accumulator through its own signature.
- A binder's refutation and tag go into its scope as it is built, in `tree`'s λ and `swi`'s default.

Reuse and consistency:

- `B.term_strip(t)` replaces `open(t)[0]` (9 uses). `safe.ts`'s `open` stays for the uses that need the annotation too.
- A missing entry is `x ?? oos(..)`, as `spine` already did: `item_emit`, `swi`, `term`'s variables and `ctr_term`.
- `mark` is a lookup table, as `bend.ts`'s `quant_show` is.
- Locals no longer shadow module functions:
  - `safe_pass`'s `oos` is now `gone`;
  - `root_emit`'s `pick` is now `chosen`;
  - `tree`'s and `rebuild`'s `arm` are now `h` and `branch`;
  - `group_call`'s `args` is now `pass`;
  - `arg_term`'s `tree` is now `bare`;
  - `let_term`'s `put` is now `inl`.

Other changes:

- `safe_pass` keeps the out-of-scope lines as it prints them (`string[]`), so `safe_book`'s two callers stop formatting `[name, why]` pairs.
- `group_of` is inlined (`e.groups.get`).
- `args` checks once whether `k` is a name, instead of three times.
- `model` finds its fallback def with `find`.
- `kernel_check` trims the kernel's output once.
- `def_emit` builds its no-model reason apart from the term, and only when no model is found.
- `tree`'s λ normalises its domain only when it might rebuild the λ, and only once.
- `closed_val` reads a variable's level once, instead of casting it four times.
- `safe_book` runs one pass per loop round, with no repeated call in the loop header.
- `def_emit`'s comment points to the header for how a def with no body goes out, instead of repeating it.
- Duplicate cases merged: `o_show`'s `∀` and `Σ`; `ctr_term` starts its fields with the label; `arm` calls `scope_bind` once.

title: Three more demos: PROOF.bend passes after an edit to main.bend alone, as in #1904
body:
_Edited: narrowed to the three demos #1932 fixes. `app_triangle_2d` will get its own issue._

### What you did

`bend PROOF.bend` in three demos, after editing only `main.bend`, the file GUIDE.md:319-322 gives to the AI. `LAWS.bend` is unchanged. `PROOF.bend` is rewritten, which the AI may also do.

### What happened

Each prints ALL PROOFS CHECK, and each program then breaks what its law's comment says. Checked on `main` at 4f99f4c1.

| demo | the law rests on (in `main.bend`) | the edit | what breaks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proof_insertion_sort` | `Sorted`, `count` | `sort` returns `xs`, `Sorted` is `Unit`, `count` is `0n` | `bend main.bend` prints `[3n, 1n, 2n]`; its header says `[1n, 2n, 3n]` |
| `pure_par_sum` | `seq` ("spec for LAWS.bend only") | `sum` and `seq` return `0n` | main prints `0`, not `2147450880` |
| `pure_par_sort` | `sum` ("spec for LAWS.bend only") | `mix` returns `x`, `sum` returns `0n` | the leaves of `sort(4n, True{}, gen(4n, 0n))` add up to 240, not 120 |

`bend PROOF.bend --verdict` (Lean 4.34.0) prints ALL PROOFS CHECK for all three edits too.

### Why it happens

#1915 fixed this shape in `app_win_is_bug_2d`: the flag law now reads the board through `BOARD.bend`, kept with `LAWS.bend`, and the demo's README says "a claim must not rely on an editable helper to say what it means". The three demos above still define what their laws mean in `main.bend`.

None of them is a regression. Each definition has been in `main.bend` since the law that uses it was written (b55e5322, e95a3c34, b5602d19). No `LAWS.bend` other than `app_win_is_bug_2d`'s ever held a `def`, and 573002f0 moved those out ("LAWS files hold laws only", #1119). GUIDE.md:319-322 names two files, the human's and the AI's, and a law's spec has no place in the human's.

Narrowing the comments, as 2.0.32 did for `io_http_fetch` (#1119), doesn't fit here: `proof_insertion_sort` would then only claim that `sort`'s output is whatever `main.bend` calls sorted.

This is the family of #1002 and #1236, where a file the AI writes changes what a law means. Those go through name resolution. This one needs only the file the AI is told to edit.

### Moving only the named helper is not enough

Two of the specs stand on other definitions in `main.bend`:

- With only `seq` moved to a spec file, `pure_par_sum`'s law reads `Spec.seq(Par.pow2(d), i)`. Setting `pow2` and `sum` to `0n` still checks, and main prints `0`.
- With only `Sorted` and `count` moved, `Sorted` still reads `main.bend`'s `LE`. `LE` as `Unit` and `sort` returning `xs` still check, and main prints `[3n, 1n, 2n]`.

Both pass `--verdict` as well.

`BOARD.bend` doesn't have this problem: it reads `Game.grid(map_h() - 1)`, the same call the page makes (`web/main.js:12`). So a spec file needs every definition its meaning stands on, except what the user sees, or a type whose shape the spec's own definitions pin (such as `pure_par_sort`'s `Sort.Tree`).

### Possible fixes

1. Do what #1915 did, per demo: a `SPEC.bend` beside `LAWS.bend` with every definition the laws' meaning needs, and the program imports the ones it also uses (`LE`, `pow2`). #1932 does this.
2. GUIDE.md:319-322 could name a spec file beside `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend`. I've left GUIDE alone, since it's yours to edit.

`app_triangle_2d` has a related gap that needs a design choice, and `pure_hvm5_mini` and `app_slash_boss_3d` keep similar definitions under a `# Spec` heading in `main.bend` ("What LAWS.bend measures"). I'll file those on their own once #1932 is in, so this issue covers what #1932 fixes.

### The file

<details>
<summary>The three edits</summary>

`proof_insertion_sort/main.bend`, three bodies:

```python

  xs

def Sorted(xs: List<&2, Nat>) -> Type:
  Unit

def count(+x: Nat, xs: List<&2, Nat>) -> Nat:
  0n
```

`proof_insertion_sort/PROOF.bend`:

```python

import ./LAWS.bend as Laws

def Laws.sort_sorted(xs):

def Laws.sort_perm(x, xs):
  {==}
```

`pure_par_sum/main.bend`, two bodies, and `PROOF.bend`:

```python

  0n
```

title: fix(demos): keep the sort and sum specs outside the editable programs
body:
Fixes #1931.

As in #1915, each demo gets a `SPEC.bend` beside `LAWS.bend`, with `BOARD.bend`'s header. It holds every definition the laws' meaning needs, and `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend` read them from there.

I named all three `SPEC.bend` since they play the same part in each demo, so the name says what the file is for. `BOARD.bend` keeps its name here.

| demo | moved to `SPEC.bend` | `main.bend` |
|---|---|---|
| `proof_insertion_sort` | `LE`, `Sorted.from`, `Sorted`, `bump`, `count` | `le_case` and `dec` use `Spec.LE` |
| `pure_par_sum` | `pow2`, `seq` | `sum` uses `Spec.pow2` |
| `pure_par_sort` | `sum` | loses `sum`, nothing else |

`LE` and `pow2` move too: moving only `Sorted`, `count` and `seq` leaves the laws standing on definitions in `main.bend`, and an edit there still passes (the issue has both). The programs import them, so `le_case` now returns evidence of `SPEC.bend`'s order, and `sum` splits its range with `SPEC.bend`'s `pow2`. Those two `SPEC.bend` files say so in their header.

One choice is yours: `pow2` is both part of what the law means (2^d numbers) and how `sum` splits its range. The other way is a copy of `pow2` in `SPEC.bend` and a lemma `Par.pow2(d) == Spec.pow2(d)` in `PROOF.bend`, so the split stays the program's and only `SPEC.bend` reads the program, as in #1915, for one more induction. I'm happy to switch to that.

`pure_par_sort`'s `SPEC.bend` reads `Sort.Tree`, the type the program sorts. `Spec.sum` checks only if a leaf is a `Nat` and a node a pair of trees, so a different `Tree` fails in `SPEC.bend` rather than changing what the sum means.

The proofs change only in names (`Sort.LE` to `Spec.LE`, `Par.seq` to `Spec.seq`, and so on). No checker, kernel, gate or other demo changes.

### What I checked

On 4f99f4c1, macOS arm64:

- `bend PROOF.bend` and `bend PROOF.bend --verdict` (Lean 4.34.0) print ALL PROOFS CHECK in each demo, and `bend SPEC.bend` checks.
- The programs print what they printed before: `[1n, 2n, 3n]` (interpreted and C), `2147450880` (C, on Metal and with `+RTS --gpu off`), `sorted` (C, on Metal and with `+RTS --gpu off`).
- The issue's edits now fail, each at its law. I ran them in throwaway copies, as #1915 did, rather than adding attack demos to the tree:
  - `pure_par_sort`, `mix` returning `x`: expected `Nat.add(Spec.sum(d, x), Spec.sum(d, y))`, observed `Nat.add(Spec.sum(d, x), Spec.sum(d, x))`.
  - `pure_par_sum`, `sum` returning `0n`, with or without its own `pow2` returning `0n`: expected `0n`, observed `Spec.seq(Spec.pow2(d), i)`.
  - `proof_insertion_sort`, `sort` returning `xs`, with or without its own `LE` as `Unit`: expected `Spec.LE(lo, h)`, observed `Unit`.
- A `def Spec.seq` in `main.bend` or `PROOF.bend` is refused ("Spec is an import's alias"). A `def SPEC.seq` there is accepted, but the law still reads `SPEC.bend`'s: with `sum` returning `0n` it fails as above, and it checks only when `SPEC.bend`'s own `seq` returns `0n`.
- The changed and new files are in `gates/repo.ts`'s allow list, and demos have no token cap. I couldn't run the gate itself here (no `ttok`).

Not run: the cluster gates, Linux.

title: Base: should Array state its own laws (set keeps the size, get after set, set leaves other cells alone)?
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
# Base would state these next to Array.set, so packages don't each carry a copy.
# sz(T, a) = Pair.snd(Array<T>, U32, Array.size(T, a))
# J(i, n) = U32.and(i, U32.sub(n, 1)) and Z(i, n) = U32.is_lt(J(i, n), U32.shr(n)): the masked index and
# the first branch, as Array.swap.at and Array.get.at compute them
law size_set:
  for -T: Data
  for a: Array<T>
  for +i: U32
  for +v: T
  {sz(T, Array.set(T, a, i, v)) == sz(T, a) : U32}

law get_after_set:
  for -T: Data
  for a: Array<T>
  for +i: U32
  for +v: T
  {Pair.snd(Array<T>, T, Array.get(T, Array.set(T, a, i, v), i)) == v : T}

law get_other_set:
  for -T: Data
  for a: Array<T>
  for +i: U32
  for +k: U32
  for +v: T
  for h: Apart(T, a, sz(T, a), J(i, sz(T, a)), Z(i, sz(T, a)), J(k, sz(T, a)), Z(k, sz(T, a)))
  {Pair.snd(Array<T>, T, Array.get(T, Array.set(T, a, i, v), k)) == Pair.snd(Array<T>, T, Array.get(T, a, k)) : T}
```

### Why

Base defines `Array.get`, `Array.set` and `Array.size` but states no law about them, so every package that reasons about an array's contents has to prove them from the tree. I needed these three for bend-ml's tensor-array and proved them outside Base, on Bend 2.0.39, with `--verdict`, no `@unsafe` and no axioms, for any `T: Data`: [`docs/upstream/array_set_laws.bend`](https://github.com/nuxyel/bend-ml/blob/devel/docs/upstream/array_set_laws.bend) (462 lines; `bend array_set_laws.bend --verdict` prints ALL PROOFS CHECK, and running it prints `(1.5, 2.5, 9.0)`). The first two hold for every i, because the two descents mask it the same way, and for every tree, balanced or not (#808).

The third needs a hypothesis, and "i and k differ after the mask" is not enough: `Array.size` follows the leftmost path, so in `ANode{ANode{ALeaf{0.0}, ALeaf{1.0}}, ALeaf{2.0}}` (size 4) a write at 2 changes the read at 3 (the 9.0 above). `Apart` is defined by recursion on the tree with the branch tests `Array.swap.go` and `Array.get.go` use: `Empty` when both descents reach the same leaf, `Unit` at the node where they part. On a concrete tree it computes, so `Unit{}` proves it. On a perfect tree it holds exactly when the masked indices differ, but I have not proved that in Bend; it needs lemmas about U32 bits.

It is longer than it looks because an array is affine inside a proof too: the lemma that `Array.size` returns the array it measured, the induction step and the lemma that opens the pair `Array.swap.go` returns each need the same subtree. The file proves them all in one pass over the tree, and works around #1077 with a trailing `Unit`.

Three questions:
1. Would you like these in Base, so packages don't each carry a copy? I can send a PR.
2. Is a tree predicate like `Apart` an acceptable hypothesis for the third, or would you rather state it for perfect trees with "the masked indices differ", next to a predicate for perfect trees? The second reads better but needs the U32 bit lemmas, which I'd have to write first.
3. If not in Base, is a package the intended home for laws about Base's types?

title: fix(io): initialize wake pipe before setting nonblocking mode
body:
`io_loop` combines `pipe` and `fcntl` with bitwise OR, which does not sequence their calls. A compiler may run `fcntl` first, changing the flags on the initial descriptor (stdin) and leaving the newly created wake pipe blocking. Draining that pipe can then hang the event loop.

Use short-circuit OR to create the pipe before configuring its read end, and stop if creation fails. Add a native regression test that checks the actual wake pipe's flags.

Validation:
- Native `wake_pipe` regression and `hello_print` smoke test pass on macOS.
- Forced `fcntl` before `pipe` in the generated C: the regression fails with the expected error.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54/54 pass.
- The full cluster test gate was not run locally.

title: A read without the wrap mask for code that must pass --verdict: in an F32 4x4 tile, the mask is the whole 2.2x gap to C
Add wide U32 arithmetic primitives
body:
Multi-precision arithmetic needs the upper half of a product and its carries. This adds `U32.mul_hi`, `U32.add_hi`, `U32.mac_hi`, and `U32.mac64` so workloads such as cryptographic field arithmetic can express these operations in Bend.

The Base definitions give the operations their mathematical meaning; compiler intrinsics provide C and JavaScript implementations, including device-specific wide multiplication. `U32.mac64` returns a selected 32-bit word of a 128-bit multiply-accumulate result, and returns zero for indices outside 0–3.

This branch also includes a compiler simplification intended to make room for the additions. It is based on an older upstream revision and needs its merge conflicts resolved and its size brought within the repository gate before submission.

**Validation on this branch**
- The existing `U32.mac64` test and the new out-of-range index regression pass on native CPU and JavaScript. Reinstating the old out-of-range behavior makes the regression fail.
- GPU execution and the full cluster test gate have not been run in this environment.
- The repository gate fails because `bend2/comp.ts` exceeds its 66,000-token cap; this needs to be addressed.

title: perf(c): fill blk_new by element stride, not per-cell modulo
body:
**Draft** — coordinating with @raramos9 on #1890 / #1928. Happy to adjust or stand down if that follow-on is already theirs.

Part of #1890. Related to #1928 (trip-count fix for runtime-depth `U32` fills). This PR targets the multi-word case #1928 left open, and keeps the `w = 1ull << c; i != w` trip-count form in the new loop.

## Cause

`blk_new` filled with

```c
for (u64 i = 0; i < (1ull << c); i += 1) {
  blk_write(..., i % (1u << lgs) < n ? v[i % (1u << lgs)] : 0);
}
```

For `U32` (`lgs == 0`) that is one invariant store. For a two-field struct (`lgs == 1`, `n == 2`) it reloads `v[i % 2]` every cell, so multi-word growth stays heavier than the per-word `U32` rate even after #1928's trip-count fix.

## Change

Walk the block by element stride instead of by cell with modulo:

```diff
-  for (u64 i = 0; i < (1ull << c); i += 1) {
-    blk_write(H, arr, l, (u32)i, i % (1u << lgs) < n ? v[i % (1u << lgs)] : 0);
+  for (u64 i = 0, w = 1ull << c; i != w; ) {
+    for (u32 j = 0; j < (1u << lgs); j += 1, i += 1) {
+      blk_write(H, arr, l, (u32)i, j < n ? v[j] : 0);
+    }
   }
```

`w` is a multiple of `1 << lgs` (`c = d + lgs`), so the loops cover exactly the block. Padding when `n < stride` stays a zero write. The common `Array<Pt>` shape unrolls to two loop-invariant stores. The outer `i != w` form keeps #1928's clang-readable trip count.

## Benches

Linux x86_64, Bend built with the CLI's `clang -std=c11 -O3`, compared against `main` plus the #1928 one-line trip-count fix as the baseline for fairness on multi-field (that fix alone does not close the `Pt` gap). Each probe makes 100 arrays and folds one cell of each into a checksum. Instructions from `perf stat -e instructions:u` (medians of three), minus the same probe at depth 0, divided by `100 × 2^d`. Checksums match before/after, and match the JS lane.

| probe | baseline (#1928 trip-count), instr / element | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Array<Pt>` (two `U32` fields) doubled to 2^23 | 8.00 | 5.25 | −34% |
| `Array<U32>` doubled to 2^24 | 2.63 | 2.63 | none |

`5.25` instr/element for `Pt` is `2.625` instr/word — the same per-word rate as `U32` on this host. Wall clock here is noisy (memory-bound); instructions are the stable signal.

## Checks

- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54. `comp.ts` is 65,973 ttok (`gpt-3.5-turbo`), under the 66,000 cap.
- C-lane `#|` match on: `array_fill_fold`, `array_boxed_get`, `array_size`, `array_poly_elem`, `array_map_loop`, `array_fork`, `array_copy_pair`, `array_nested`, `array_clone_boxed`, `array_static_default`, `array_equality`.
- Probe checksum identical on C and JS.
- Cluster gates not run (no mini access). GPU / #1778 not addressed. Proof-backed init not addressed.

title: comp.ts says the same in 26 fewer tokens on the word and intrinsic paths
body:
comp.ts goes from 65,956 to 65,930 ttok (-26, `ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo` as `gates/repo.ts` pins it), with the same output.

## What changes
