title: [complexity, checker] O(2^n) — Checking a returned type checks the same lambda again
Base is re-parsed and re-checked for every book; the header-regex workarounds make --checkup and bend-lint accept programs bend rejects
body:
## Problem

`Bend.book_load` can't reuse a module it has already loaded and checked. Every new book parses `base.bend` from scratch, and `book_valid` checks it again (about 20 ms each time). Inside one process, that cost repeats once per book.

Three callers work around this on their own, each with a copy of the same header regex and its own cache of a checked Base:

| Caller | Workaround |
|---|---|
| `cli_checkup` (`bend2/main.ts`) | header regex, then starts the book from a Base checked once |
| `tools/bend-lint/src/seam.ts` | a copy of the regex, plus a Base cache keyed on `base.bend`'s contents |
| `load_js` (#1920, closed) | would have added a third copy, with a cache that never retries or refreshes |

`gates/test.ts` and the plain CLI don't work around it at all.

## The workaround changes results

Starting from a checked Base only gives the same result when Base would have loaded first anyway. The regex `/^(?:[\t\r ]*(?:(?:#|import )[^\n]*)?\n)*[\t ]*import Base\s/` also accepts other imports *before* `import Base`. Those modules then get parsed with Base's names already in the book, so their names resolve differently than in a normal run.

Repro on `main` (2cbabca0):

```
# lib.bend (no import Base)
def xs() -> List<Nat>:
  []

# main.bend
import ./lib.bend as L
import Base

def main() -> List<Nat>:
  L.xs()

# top.bend
import ./main.bend as M
```

```
$ bend main.bend
SOME PROOFS FAIL
- message  : a declared datatype (unknown: lib.List)

$ bend top.bend --checkup
--- ./main.bend ---
[]
exit 0
```

`--checkup` runs a program that `bend` rejects. bend-lint has the same flaw. `book.order`, and so the JS emit order, can also differ from a normal run. The regex only looks at the file's own header, so a module that gets Base through another import gets no speedup either.

## Proposed fix

Fix it once, in `book_load`:

- Where `import Base` is handled, insert a cached, already-checked Base instead of parsing `base.bend`. Key the cache on `base.bend`'s contents, and don't cache failures. Base's names then enter the book at the same moment parsing would add them, so name resolution and order match a normal run wherever the import appears, directly or through another import.
- Have `book_valid` skip those entries. #1846 changes `done` from "skip the first N entries" to a test over entries, which removes the need for Base to come first. Base entries are already marked with `b`.
- The cached entries keep their checked bodies (`Def.e`), so the compiler and `safe.ts` keep working. That's why this has to be a cache: `--trust` from #1846 only skips checking, and only works with `--check-only`.
- Then delete the regex in `cli_checkup`, the regex and cache in `seam.ts`, and anything #1920 would have added. Every caller gets the speedup with no changes: the CLI, `--checkup`, the JS loader, the linter and the gates.

Before relying on this, confirm that Base's checked result doesn't depend on anything loaded before it. That should hold, since Base only refers to Base and only Base fills Base's laws.

Tests:
- the repro above: `--checkup`, the JS loader and `bend-lint` should give the same result as `bend main.bend`;
- a module that gets Base only through another import;
- an edited `base.bend` in a long-running process.

## Priority

Low for speed: nothing in the repo imports more than two `.bend` modules from JS in one process. Higher for correctness, because `--checkup` and bend-lint already disagree with `bend` on the repro above.

Related: #1920 (closed, the loader-only version), #1846 (the `book_valid` change this builds on), #1234 (re-checking imports across separate runs, which a persistent cache would address; this issue is about reuse inside one process).

title: [complexity, checker] O(n^3) — Quantity comparison keeps searching after it has an answer
body:
Consider these programs:

```bend
def test(q: Quant, r: Quant, X: Kind(q <&> r)) -> Kind(r <&> q):
  X
```

```bend
def test(q: Quant, r: Quant, X: Kind(q <&> r <&> q <&> r)) -> Kind(r <&> q <&> r <&> q):
  X
```

Let `n` count quantity variables in each `<&>` expression, including repeats:
2 and 4 above. Main makes `3n² + 4n + 4` comparisons and `n³ + 12n² + 3n + 30` evaluator
steps: O(n²) and O(n³), respectively.

**Cause.** `<&>` takes the smaller quantity, so reordering its operands leaves the
`Kind(...)` type unchanged. For each quantity on the left, Bend searches the right
expression, computing both recursive answers before combining them with `&&` or `||`.
Even a successful match does not stop the search. Repeatedly reducing the remaining
lists adds another factor to the evaluator work.

**Searching after the answer is known may not be necessary.** For `||`, the second
recursive search could run only if the first returned false; for `&&`, only if it
returned true. Each search here could then stop within the first two entries, `r, q`,
giving O(n) comparisons instead of O(n²). Repeated list reduction could still take
O(n²) evaluator steps, instead of O(n³).

To reproduce on main `7a7e6505a`, save either program as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

Source: [the two eager branches][source1].

[source1]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7a7e6505aeff2101a139a8419e16098ed2a89110/bend2/bend.ts#L3157-L3168

title: Model template field equalities from constructor hypotheses
Compile dense native U32 matches with guarded switches
body:
A flat U32 match with exact hits interleaved with low-bit defaults emits an if/else ladder. This promotes safe dense exact hits into a C switch and retains the remaining ordered chain in its default arm.

An exact hit `x == n` moves only when every earlier row's predicate is false at `n`. Thus its switch case is the original first match. In the switch default, none of the promoted equalities can hold, so removing those rows preserves the remaining first-match order. The planner uses structured match rows, not parsed C conditions.

Bodies are emitted once in their original order before the dispatch is rearranged. The existing common-allocation hoist is retained. The optimization applies to native flat U32 matches; the JavaScript path and other match types retain their emitted output.

### Measurements

Apple M5 Pro / 64 GiB, Apple clang 21, Bun 1.4.4, source base `4982c105`, one CPU thread, GPU off. Both compilers build identical application sources with `clang -std=c11 -O3`; the SAT replications include proof construction/output.

The separately planned primary standalone confirmation passed: 48.112 → 12.342 ms (3.90×).

The first standalone captures were refused (worst CV 5.39%, 5.95%, 5.46%). The confirmation was declared separately, after a 60-second cooldown, with 80 invocations per group instead of 16. Both captures use 20 groups per arm, old/new A/A controls, balanced order, CV ≤5% and A/A within 5%. No outlier removal, gate relaxation or retry of the other refused conditions. The earlier refusals remain part of the result.

The known FPGA complete solve passed at 5.617 → 4.243 ms (24.5% lower); a PHP12 replication passed at 6.832 → 5.572 ms (18.4% lower). These reused local SAT workloads support a scoped result; they do not establish a general SAT or language speedup. Their full solver source is outside this patch. The standalone reproducer is included below.

<details><summary>Every original timing condition, including refusals</summary>

| Condition | Base ms | Patch ms | Gates |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| dispatch-0 | 48.959 | 12.930 | REFUSED |
| dispatch-7 | 48.259 | 12.568 | REFUSED |
| dispatch-4294967295 | 48.193 | 12.821 | REFUSED |
| lexer | 5.285 | 5.278 | PASS |
| hashmap | 2.181 | 2.184 | REFUSED |
| raytrace | 5.139 | 5.143 | PASS |
| original-public-FPGA | 5.617 | 4.243 | PASS |
| signed-sparse-php12-unsat | 6.832 | 5.572 | PASS |
| signed-sparse-php14-unsat | 10.340 | 8.400 | REFUSED |
| signed-sparse-php12-balanced | 3.958 | 3.044 | REFUSED |
| planted-260-1040 | 3.514 | 3.495 | REFUSED |
| planted-coloring-250-880 | 8.463 | 4.750 | REFUSED |
| chain577-unsat | 2.736 | 2.732 | REFUSED |

Only 4/13 original conditions qualified. Refused medians are descriptive, not accepted speedups or regressions. Lexer, hashmap and raytrace wrappers emitted byte-identical C across both compilers. The entire original profile is not qualified.

</details>

### Checks

- All 1,862 existing tests/runtime-benchmark/demo inputs emitted identical C/JS or identical diagnostics across both compilers; no compile caps. Two added fixtures were included in the 1,864-input sweep and were the only C changes. All JS was identical. The third added fixture was separately checked.
- Three regression fixtures pass interpreter/JS/native execution with both compilers. They cover masked defaults/high bits, owned arrays/tail loops and one shared constructor-allocation site before the switch.
- The actual branch emitter agrees with an independent first-match reference on 5,439,240 selections from 72 structured-row plans, including overlaps, duplicate keys, sparse keys and high bits. This is finite testing, not a compiler proof.
- Both native SAT replicas pass 409 original formulas: 612 SAT models and 206 original-file refutation executions checked, with identical archived proof bytes; 64 trivial-checker paths additionally confirmed by RUP. 22 malformed rejections and 14 further replication executions pass.
- Both compilers' CPU/Metal executions of a small forked fixture agree with an independent Python checksum. Both Metal archives build. CUDA and the maintainer cluster gates were not run.
- `gates/repo.ts`: 54/54. `comp.ts`: 65,962 tokens with the gate's tokenizer, under the unchanged 66,000 cap (base: 65,935). Existing emitter comments are condensed to offset the new code.

### Standalone reproduction

```sh

git worktree add --detach ../bend-dispatch-base 4982c105b9e8e06cc1d1e2d0d63c546dac4aa377

These are whole-process measurements. Other CPUs/clang versions and the broader upstream gates still need validation before merge.

title: safe.ts: simplify again, same output
body:
A second simplification pass over `safe.ts`, with the same output. It makes room for #1896 under `safe.ts`'s 24000-token cap. `safe.ts` goes from 23289 to 22875 ttok. #1896's η commits, picked onto this branch, apply cleanly and land at 23952.

## What

Helpers:

- `lams2(q, l, b)` builds `λt => λf => b` at `q`, a default arm's binders. `swi`'s empty default wrote these λs out by hand; now both of `swi`'s cases build them. The default arm passes `copies(e, q, b, [l, l + 1])` as `q`. It replaces `pair_lams`.
- `uses` had one caller left, `tree`'s rebuild check, which now reads `o_uses` itself.
- `spec_val` had one caller, `args`, and is inlined.
- The out-of-scope fixed point in `safe_pass` finds each def's names the first time it asks, then reuses them, instead of walking the def again on every pass. As before, it walks nothing when no def is out of scope.
- `safe_book` and `safe_pass` share an `Out` type.

Shorter forms:

- `term`'s ∀ case builds its node in one literal, `A` before `B` as before. Switch cases keep their braces.
- `let_term`, `rwt_term` and `adt_emit` use their one-use locals in place, in the same order.
- `tele_open`'s return type is inferred from the record it builds.
- `adt_emit` applies `D.arms` to the tag with `apps`, as everywhere else.
- `def_emit`'s no-model reason goes straight into `?? oos(..)`, which builds it only when no model is found; the else branch it covers is parenthesized. Its type goes into `e.out` without a local.
- `kernel_bin` reads `$BENDTT` directly, and its comment names `LEAN_VERSION` instead of repeating it.

Comments:

- As in `bend.ts` and `comp.ts`, which comment 3% and 5% of their functions, a comment that only restates its code goes. That covers 19 one-liners, including those over `vr`, `tkey`, `node`, `fill`, `wnf`, `all_of`, `ctr_term`, `o_refs`, `apps` and `alls`. Comments that give a reason, a contract or an encoding stay, or move into the code:
  - `mentions` takes a `B.LTerm`, so passing an unlowered term (whose binders hide their variables in closures) is a type error;
  - `no_ctr` is `no_ctr_left`: every constructor matched away, not a datatype declared with none;
  - `mats` says `h` runs from the last label to the first, and that what `h` names goes out in that order.
- `safe_book`'s comment points to the header for the out-of-scope rule instead of repeating it; `kind`'s and `run_read`'s say the same in fewer words.

## Checks

- `-o` on all 1795 files of `tests/`, `main` (0a41eea3) against this branch: the same BendTT and the same messages on every file.
- `bunx tsc -p bend2/pack`: no errors in `safe.ts`.
- `bun gates/_run.ts`: repo 54 / 54, test 1782 / 1782, perf 124 / 124, ping 80 / 81 (pass).
- `bun gates/safe.ts tests`: the same verdict as `main` on every file: agree 1143, unsafe 142, bend2 rejects 507, out of scope 3, false reject 0, timeout 0, infrastructure 0.

title: perf(c): blk_new fills whole elements, clones keep runs; JS shares the cell depth wall
body:
Follow-up to #1928. That PR gave clang a trip count for `blk_new`'s fill, which vectorized `U32` fills; elements of two or more cells stayed scalar. This PR fills element by element so they vectorize too, fixes two `blk_new` error paths, keeps a clone's runs of equal cells with one refcount bump each, and makes the JS lanes refuse the same array depths as C.

`comp.ts` is 65,982 ttok, under its 66,000 cap (main is 65,905).

## Fill

```c
for (u32 i = 0, w = 1u << c; i != w; i += 1u << lgs) {
  for (u32 j = 0; j != 1u << lgs; j += 1) {
    blk_write(H, arr, l, i + j, j < n ? v[j] : 0);
  }
}
```

The inner count is the constant `2^lgs` at every inlined call, so clang unrolls it and stores whole elements in vectors. The per-cell `i % (1u << lgs)` and `< n` test are gone. The index is `u32`: `c <= 31`, so `w <= 2^31`.

Telling clang `c <= 31` (`__builtin_assume`, or `c & 31`) does not vectorize the old `i < (1ull << c)` loop. Only the `!=` form does.

## Clone

A copy that keeps its cells (`Array.clone` of boxed elements, and `blk_node`/`blk_half` on a shared block) made one atomic count add per cell through `blk_keep`. `blk_fill` now copies the block in one plain pass, which vectorizes. It then walks the copy and keeps each run of `k` equal cells with one `term_keep(e, w, k)`, the way `blk_new` keeps each field once by `2^d - 1`. `k` cells hold `k` counts, so `k` stays under `RFC_CNT` and `rfc_bump` still sees an overflow: a 2^23-cell `String` clone still fails with "more than 2^24-1 live copies", and a 2^22 one still runs.

The keep pass reads the copy, not the source. A first version kept from the source after the copy, so a cell that another thread wrapped in place in between would keep the wrapped term while the copy held the raw one. Reading the copy keeps exactly the term each cell was copied as, as the old per-cell `blk_keep` did. A wrap (`k = 1`, an unshared term) is still written back to the source as before.

## Error paths (in effect only on the device, where `err_post` does not exit)

- The depth check is `d > 31 - lgs` (`lgs <= 31`), so it cannot wrap. Runtime Nats stop at 2^48-1, so the old `d + lgs > 31` could not wrap either; the new form does not depend on that cap.
- Once `ERR_CNTS` is posted, the element is no longer kept with `k = 2^d - 1`. That bump carried out of the 24-bit count into the loc bits of the redirect cell.

## JS depth wall

`array_new` in JS checked only `d > 31`, so `[p : Pt^31n]` set out to build 2^31 elements (still running after 5 minutes) while C refuses class 32 with "an array past the deepest block class 31". The JS emitter now passes the element's cell class (`lay_arr(lay_el(T)).lgs`, the value C gets) to `array_new`, which refuses `d > 31 - lgs`. C, JS and the interpreter now refuse `Pt^31n`, `P3^30n` and `U32^32n` alike. `tests/io/array_depth_bound_wide.bend` pins the `Pt` case. It passes on both lanes here and times out on main's JS lane.

The cell class reaches `array_new` as one more literal argument of the array ops, so `js_call` keeps its signature. To pay for the JS change, every tuple the JS runtime builds (the array templates, `array_rmw`, `nat_divmod` and `io_tup`) goes through one `tup_new(a, b)` helper, `nat_divmod` builds one tuple, and `lay_arr`/`arr_new` say `n || 1` for `Math.max(1, n)`.

## Benches

Apple Silicon, Apple clang 17, `clang -std=c11 -O3` as the CLI builds. Each probe makes 100 arrays (fresh, or grown by doubling from one leaf as in #1928) and reads one cell of each into a checksum. Cycles are from `/usr/bin/time -l`, medians of three. Every probe prints the same checksum before and after. Most of what is left in the clone probes is dropping the clone (`term_drop` walks every cell), which this does not change.

These numbers are from before the rebases (on f1273d30, then 0ba4e5ec) and weren't run again.

| probe | main (after #1928) | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Array<U32>` doubled to 2^24 | 1.83G | 1.85G | flat |
| `Array<Pt>` (2 × `U32`) doubled to 2^23 | 3.11G | 1.82G | −41% |
| `Array<P3>` (3 × `U32`) doubled to 2^22 | 3.10G | 2.04G | −34% |
| `Array<String>` doubled to 2^20 | 1.00G | 1.00G | flat (7 interleaved runs) |
| fresh `Array.new(Pt, 23n, v)` | 1.71G | 0.42G | −76% |
| fresh `Array.new(P3, 22n, v)` | 1.76G | 0.65G | −63% |
| fresh `Array.new(String, 20n, v)` | 0.88G | 0.88G | flat |
| 100 clones of `Array.new(String, 20n, v)` | 1.60G | 1.07G | −33% |
| 100 clones of 2^18 distinct strings | 474M | 424M | −10% |

## Checks

- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 54 / 54 after the rebase on 0ba4e5ec.
- `bun gates/test.ts` on the minis, rebased on 0ba4e5ec: 1825 / 1828 and 1823 / 1828 before the simplification commits, and 1826 / 1828 after each of them, and 1828 / 1828 after the `ERR_CNTS` fill fix. Every failure is a `[js]` timeout of an `io/` test with a foreign `.js` file, and the set differs between runs. Main failed the same way in the same session (1824 / 1826: `io_exit_status [js]`, `io_bundle_inline [js]`). The five failing tests behave the same on main and here when run locally.
- The simplification commit changes only runtime lines: every test's emitted C and JS differs from the previous commit only in `blk_fill`, `blk_new`'s fill bound and `nat_divmod`. A fresh `Array<Pt>` fill probe and a `String` clone probe compile to the same vector loads and stores, and run in the same time. `Nat.divmod`, including by 0 and 1, prints the same on C, JS and the interpreter as on main.
- The `COPY` macro commit changes only the three copy loops it replaces (`ctr_take`, `blk_fill`, `root_take`) in the emitted C. The fill and clone probes keep the same vector load and store counts (436 and 33).
- The `ERR_CNTS` fill fix: on the device `err_post` does not exit, so `blk_new` used to write a value it had not kept into every cell. It now fills the block with the 0 the padding cells hold. `Array.new` at depth 24 and `Array.clone` of a depth-23 array, both called through `tree!(...)` so they compile for the device, report the copy limit with exit 1 on host and Metal. Depths 23 and 22 run correctly.
- Checks with no code change: a run bump of k reports the copy limit at the same count as k single bumps, since `a32_add` returns the old count. A temporary check that no run of k > 1 cells holds an unwrapped boxed term never fired across the cluster suite (1826 / 1828, the usual JS `io/` timeouts).
- Every test, C and JS lanes, run locally with the gate's rules (5 s alarm), on main and on this branch. The results are the same apart from the two new tests: 878 C and 881 JS pass here. The 3 C failures happen on main too and come from this machine: `gfx/window` and `gfx/clicks` expect "no display", and `io/stack_fault_trap` exits 138 under the runner where the test expects 1. `io/chan_reclaim_limit` failed once on main's JS lane and passed on rerun (timing).
- A readback test sums every cell at runtime depths 0–9 for `U32`, `Pt`, `P3`, `String`, `{String, U32}` and `{U32, String, U32}`, made fresh and by doubling. C, JS and the interpreter print the same value.
- `ERR_CNTS` (`Array.new(String, 24n, s)`) and `ERR_ARRS` still fire on the host.
- `tests/reg/array_clone_runs.bend` clones `String` and `{String, U32}` arrays with one long run and with runs broken up by `Array.set`, writes one copy, and sums every cell of both, depths 0–11. C, JS and the interpreter agree, and so does main's C. With the run bump forced to 1 it ends in a memory fault. An overcount only leaks, which it cannot see.

## Not covered

- GPU execution, on Metal and on CUDA. `stencil3d` builds with Metal and passes, which only shows that the runtime compiles there.
- `gates/perf.ts`. No bench pins the multi-cell fill.
- JS speed of `tup_new` (one small call per get, size, clone and divmod, which the JIT should inline). Not measured.
- `ANode` of two class-31 blocks: C refuses class 32, while JS concatenates. It needs more than 2^31 cells to reach.
- Structs with a boxed field, such as `{String, U32}`, interleave their cells, so their clones have runs of one and gain only from the plain copy pass.
- `blk_node`/`blk_half` on a shared block take the new keep path too. Only the suite and the readback test cover them, not a bench.

title: perf(check): short-circuit quantity comparisons (#1942)
body:
Closes #1942.

## Problem

Checking that `Kind(q <&> r)` fits `Kind(r <&> q)` takes O(n²) quantity comparisons and O(n³) evaluator steps, where n counts the quantity variables in each meet. At n = 1024 the check takes 16.5 s.

## Root cause

In `compare_go`'s `Typ` case, a meet on the left splits into "both sides fit" and a meet on the right splits into "either side fits". Both recursive comparisons were computed into `const`s before being combined, so the search kept going after the answer was known. Each extra comparison also walks the remaining right-hand meet chain in `term_wnf`, which adds the third factor of n.

The eager form came from the `term_equal` → `term_compare` rename in `0e56d956`. The code before it short-circuited.

## Solution

The recursive comparisons are now returned directly through JavaScript's `&&` and `||`. The right operand is evaluated only when the left one hasn't already decided the result. That means a `false` stops a "both sides fit" check, and a `true` stops an "either side fits" search. This is 4 insertions and 6 deletions in `bend2/bend.ts`, with no other change.

## Correctness

- `compare_go` and `term_wnf` never throw or report. Errors come from their callers (`term_check`), based on the final boolean, so a skipped branch can't hide a diagnostic.
- The checker solves no unknowns during comparison. Holes compare by name, so no constraint is lost.
- Their only writes are caches: a cell's evaluated value, and the merge of two share cells already proven equal. Either one can only reproduce a result already reached, so a skipped branch just leaves less cached.
- Usage counting reads source syntax, not cached values.
- The left operand still runs first, and the right one runs only when it can change the answer.
- The one behavior change is that a skipped branch that would have looped forever no longer runs. Nothing in `tests/` reaches that case.

## Measurements

Counts are `compare_go` calls and `term_wnf` loop iterations, taken on an instrumented copy for the issue's family (`q <&> r <&> …` against `r <&> q <&> …`):

| n | Comparisons before | Comparisons after | Evaluator steps before | Evaluator steps after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 24 | 22 | 92 | 86 |
| 4 | 68 | 42 | 298 | 198 |
| 8 | 228 | 80 | 1,334 | 558 |
| 16 | 836 | 156 | 7,246 | 1,854 |
| 32 | 3,204 | 308 | 45,182 | 6,750 |
| 64 | 12,548 | 612 | 311,518 | 25,758 |

- **Before.** The counts match the issue's formulas exactly: 3n² + 4n + 4 comparisons and n³ + 12n² + 3n + 30 steps.
- **After, for the issue's family.** The counts fit about 9.5n + 4 comparisons and exactly 6n² + 18n + 30 steps for n ≥ 4. That is O(n) comparisons and O(n²) steps. Every leaf now matches within the first two leaves of the other side. The leftover factor of n in steps comes from re-walking the right-hand chain in `term_wnf`.
- **Wall clock.** n = 512 drops from 2.42 s to 0.06 s, and n = 1024 from 16.5 s to 0.12 s.

## Worst case (unchanged complexity)

The issue's family is the best case for short-circuiting. When matches sit at the far end, for example n distinct variables in reverse order, the search still visits most of the other side. That case stays O(n²) comparisons and O(n³) steps and only does less work:

| n (distinct, reversed) | Comparisons before | after | Steps before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 12,672 | 6,687 | 312,138 | 208,902 |

Removing the remaining re-walk of the meet chain would need a different representation of meets and is out of scope here.

## Tests

- **`tests/check/meet_order_fits.bend`** covers:
  - reordered operands
  - repeated variables
  - a match on the first leaf
  - a match only on the last leaf (the second branch must run)
  - a full reversal
  - regrouping with parentheses
  - `&2` as the meet's identity
- **`tests/check/meet_order_rejects.bend`** checks that `Kind(q <&> r)` is still refused as `Kind(q)`, with the exact error.
- **Run locally:**
  - Both new tests pass alone and through `--checkup` the way the test gate aggregates them.
  - All 1784 files under `tests/` give byte-identical `--check-only` output before and after: 1142 pass and 642 fail as expected. No file does more comparison work.
  - `gates/repo.ts` passes 54/54. `bend.ts` drops from 44,493 to 44,473 tokens.
- **Not run locally:**
  - `gates/test.ts` needs the mini cluster.
  - `gates/perf.ts` needs the bench minis.
  - `--verdict` and `gates/safe.ts` need Lean v4.34.0, which isn't installed here.

title: --verdict: runs that build the kernel at the same time can break each other's build
body:
`--verdict` builds the BendTT kernel the first time it runs (`kernel_bin` in `bend2/safe.ts`), into `~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/`. Every run builds in that same directory, writing `bendtt.lean`, `bendtt.c` and `bendtt` there. So runs that start together on an empty cache write over each other's files, and one of them can fail to build.

## Reproduce

With `$BENDTT` unset and `HOME` pointed at an empty directory that links to the real `~/.elan` (so the cache is empty), start four `bend tests/check/alpha_equivalence.bend --verdict` runs at once. On `main`, 3 of 5 tries had one run fail:

```
Error: BendTT infrastructure: the kernel did not build (…/leanc: ld64.lld: error: undefined symbol: main | >>> referenced by the entry point | clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation) | ); --verdict needs Lean v4.34.0 (elan toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0), or $BENDTT set to a built kernel
```

That run's `leanc` read a `bendtt.c` that another run's `lean -c` was rewriting.

The cache also takes `bendtt`'s existence as "built", and `leanc` writes `bendtt` in place. So a run could also pick up a half-written kernel, or a build cut short could leave one. I could not catch either on macOS, where `bendtt` appears at full size at once, but nothing guarantees that.

## Scope

It only happens on the first build for a given `bendtt.lean` and Lean version. `gates/safe.ts` passes a prebuilt kernel, so the gates do not go through this path.

title: fix(safe): each kernel build goes in a dir of its own, renamed into place whole
body:
Fixes #1948.

`kernel_bin` built the BendTT kernel in `~/.bend/bendtt/<hash>/` itself. So `--verdict` runs that started together on an empty cache wrote over each other's `bendtt.c`, and one could fail to link. The cache also took `bendtt`'s existence as "built", while `leanc` wrote it in place.

## What

- Each build runs in a fresh `build-XXXXXX` directory under the cache directory.
- The finished `bendtt` is renamed into place. The rename is atomic, so `bin`, once there, is a finished kernel. When two builds finish, the later rename replaces an identical file, and a run already executing the earlier one keeps its inode.
- The build directory is removed when the build ends, whether it succeeds or fails. A build stopped by a signal (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGKILL; the `finally` does not run then) leaves its `build-XXXXXX` directory behind, but no `bendtt`, so the next run builds normally. Leftover directories are not cleaned up: one could belong to a build still running.
- `run`'s tool parameter is `exe`, so it no longer shadows `bin`, the kernel path the rename writes.

## Checks

The tests point `HOME` at an empty directory that links to the real `~/.elan`, so each one starts from an empty cache.

- Four `--verdict` runs at once on an empty cache:

  | Branch | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `main` | a failed run in 3 of 5 tries (`leanc: … undefined symbol: main`) |
  | this branch | every run checks in 6 of 6 tries; only `bendtt` is left in the cache directory |

- A build stopped 5 s in, by SIGKILL, SIGINT or SIGTERM: the next run builds and checks; the stopped build's directory stays.
- No Lean on the PATH: the same "the kernel did not build" error as before, and the build directory is gone.
- `bun gates/_run.ts`: repo 54 / 54, test 1782 / 1782, perf 124 / 124, ping 80 / 81 (pass). The gates use a prebuilt kernel, so they do not reach this code.
- `safe.ts` goes from 23900 to 23993 ttok, under its 24000 cap.

title: Pick host-FAR loops by the F32 math in their body (follow-up to #1814)
body:
Follow-up to #1814, which merged before this review point was addressed.

## The change

#1814 made a long loop (`SPIN_FAR` chars, `seg.spin`) a `FAR` call on the host when one of its live parameters has top-level type F32 (`ty_adt(A)?.k === "F32"`). The reason is clang's SLP vectorizer. That type test misses:

- F32 inside a record or tuple (`pos: Vec3`), which still reaches the loop as separate 32-bit words;
- a generic parameter (`x: T`) used at F32, since `ty_adt` of a type variable is null.

SLP packs float arithmetic, not parameter types. This PR checks the loop's emitted C body for F32 ops instead (`f32_unbox(` / `f32_rewrap(`, which every F32 op emits). That catches both cases above, because the body is fully concrete, and it skips a loop that only passes an F32 along without doing math on it. I also updated the comment on `SPIN_FAR` and the runtime comment above `DFAR`, which still said "The host lets clang decide".

## Checks

- **Emitted C:** all 1,867 `.bend` files under `bench/runtime`, `demos` and `tests`, compiled with `-o x.c` on main and on this branch. Exit codes match (916 build, 951 fail, as on main). Every emitted file is byte-identical except the runtime comment line. The host-`FAR` loops are still nbody's, raytrace's and one in `app_slash_boss_3d`, so #1814's numbers still hold.
- **Gates:** repo 54/54, test 1783/1783. Ping is 80/81, and main fails the same case (a BendHub publish of `lic_bom--name.bend`, which the local hub refuses). Perf is 123/124, and main shows the same: merkle's COMPILER cell sits at 1.14–1.16x on both, and main also went 123/124 in one run.
- **Perf, alternating main and this branch (2 runs each):**

  | cell | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | nbody SEQ-CPU | 4.819 / 4.817 s | 4.818 / 4.822 s |
  | nbody PAR-CPU | 0.712 / 0.710 s | 0.711 / 0.711 s |
  | raytrace SEQ-CPU | 4.160 / 4.162 s | 4.160 / 4.163 s |
  | raytrace PAR-CPU | 0.700 / 0.703 s | 0.701 / 0.700 s |

  No cell moves beyond run-to-run noise.
- **Size:** `comp.ts` is 65,917 ttok (main 65,907, cap 66,000).

title: fix(js): exported text closures stay callable
body:
Exported Bend functions that return another function could crash when called from JavaScript if their eventual result was a String or Char. The generated wrapper tried to convert the returned function to text before the caller could use it.

For example, `pre("hello ")` should return a function that accepts `"world"`, but instead threw a TypeError.

The wrapper now uses the current call’s return type to select conversion. Returned functions remain callable, and actual text results keep their existing conversion.

The new regression tests String/Char closures, erased arguments and arity-raised lambdas. Local macOS checks: the regression fails on the base and passes through source and compiled CLIs and emitted Bun/Node; neighboring host-boundary fixtures and the repository gate pass. Strict TypeScript reports the same seven baseline errors.

Previously reported in #1549. #1825 now proposes removing export text conversion as part of a broader breaking change. That would also remove this failure if merged; this PR preserves the current text-conversion contract.

title: perf(check): avoid redundant kind checks for let bindings
body:
Closes #1940

## Cause

check-let checks every binder's inferred type against `Kind(qj)`. infer-app returns `B(a)` with the surface argument substituted, so `x = tag(q => ..)` has type `Tag<q => ..>`. Checking that type infers the ADT, and `tele_check` checks the lambda again. A lambda whose body holds another such let repeats the inner pair, so n nested lets cost 11·2ⁿ − 9 checker calls.

For an ordinary or erased binder that check is redundant. `Kind(g)` fits `Kind(h)` for every `h` other than `+`, so it can only confirm that the inferred type is a type, and inference already guarantees that: book types are checked when defined, context types come from checked goals and earlier lets, and `B(a)` is a type because `B` was checked under `x : A` in the signature and `a` checks against `A`. Only an unrestricted `+` binder adds an obligation, that its type is Data.

## Change

check-let calls `term_check_kind` only when the binder's kind is Data, and the rule comment says so. That is a `+` binder outside an `@unsafe` def: in one, `lhs_kind` only asks a `+` binder to be a type.

This is BendTT's let rule. `Typed.lett` in `bendtt.lean` requires `V : T2` only when `q = Q2`, and `Term.check` checks `V` against `T2` only `if q == Q2`.

## Measurements

Checker calls (`term_check` + `term_infer`) for the issue's family with n nested lets:

| n | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 13 | 8 |
| 10 | 11,255 | 62 |
| 16 | 720,887 | 98 |
| 24 | 184,549,367 (formula) | 146 |

Before is exactly 11·2ⁿ − 9 and after is exactly 6n + 2, through n = 32. At n = 24, `--check-only` takes 35.87 s before and 0.03 s after. The five checker benches are unchanged within noise.

## Tests

- `let_dependent_type`: the issue's family 30 deep, a shadowed binder and an erased binder; accepted.
- `let_unsafe_dependent_type`: `+` binders of an `@unsafe` def, 30 deep; accepted.
- `let_dependent_domain`: a domain `T: Data` that fits the ADT's `-T: Type`; accepted.
- `let_dependent_domain_bad`: a domain `T: Type` that does not fit `-T: Data`; refused at the signature.
- `let_plus_dependent_type`: `+x` at a dependent type that is Type; refused.
- `let_forward_refused`: a malformed type from a signature below the let; refused at that signature's own event, which is what the skipped check relies on.

Depth 30 is 2^30 checks if the doubling returns, past the gates' 30 s cap, so a regression fails the run. A depth-10 test still passed on the exponential build.

On the rebased branch, against its base `db64cf76`:

- `--check-only` over all 1837 tests: identical verdicts and output, except the two 30-deep tests, which time out at 25 s on the base.
- `-o .bendtt` over the accepted tests: byte-identical.
- `bun gates/_run.ts`: test 1824 / 1824, repo 54 / 54, perf 124 / 124; ping skipped (no site repo).
- `--verdict` on the five tests above: the same verdicts as `--check-only`.

Merged onto `main` at `d0949580`: test 1825 / 1825; perf 123 / 124, the one miss being the `merkle` compile cell at 1.16x, which `main` also misses.

Not run: `gates/safe.ts`, which needs a kernel binary built on a Lean node.

## Limitations

Only let binders are fixed. infer-app still substitutes the surface argument into `B(a)`, so other checks of that type double the same way, and these stay exponential, to be handled in a follow-up PR:

- nested `+` lets outside `@unsafe`, which still check their type's kind. The kernel does the same at `Q2`.
- nested `+` lambdas, in and outside `@unsafe`.

An inferred type is not yet known to be a type when it comes from a signature below the let. A dead region or an `@unsafe` def can name one, and so can a live call to a foreign def. Every such program I probed is still refused, at that signature's event at the latest, but a let can now bind the malformed type first, with two effects:

- The error can blame later code. With `def g() -> 0n` below it, `-x = g(); -y = h(x);` reports `expected Nat, observed 0n` at `h(x)`, not `expected Kind(&0), observed Nat` at the let. With a foreign `def bad(a: Nat) -> 0n` below it, `x = bad(0n); -y = h(x); 0n` in a live def does the same.
- The checker can hang instead of refusing. With `def g() -> {(x => x(x)) : Nat}((x => x(x)))` below it, `-x = g(); -y = h(x);` loops where the base refuses at the let. This is a new route to an existing hang, not a new kind: `-y = h(g())` already hangs on the base.

title: Metal: standalone renderer fails with “a function the device does not hold”; CPU and interpreter agree
body:
### What you did

On an M1 Mac, save the file below as `metal_fids_repro.bend`:

```sh
bend metal_fids_repro.bend -o mfr
./mfr
./mfr +RTS --gpu 1GB
./mfr +RTS --gpu off
bend metal_fids_repro.bend
```
### What happened

```text
Original Metal investigation:


$ ./mfr
bend: a function the device does not hold

$ ./mfr +RTS --gpu off
57798656

$ bend metal_fids_repro.bend
57798656

```

The standalone Metal reproducer failed in 5/5 recorded runs, with exit status 1 in under a second. A 1 GB GPU memory cap also failed. Expected: `57798656`, matching the CPU and interpreter. Fresh Linux checks with Bend 2.0.39 confirmed that both controls still print `57798656`.

The program builds cells on the host, performs an `IO.now()` step, then calls `Frame.node!`. Thus the bang is at a fresh IO step, not inside earlier CPU-parallel work.

The original reduction found that replacing the constant `Seg{67588, Seg{100532, SegEnd{}}}` in `Font.pick` with a heap-built `Seg{c, SegEnd{}}`, or returning `SegEnd{}` from both arms, made the GPU run pass. In this reproducer the glyph code is always 32, so the arm for code 33 is not taken. Changes to that unexecuted arm nonetheless changed GPU success/failure.

Instrumentation during the original investigation observed invalid task words at device task entry and changing invalid function IDs. This suggests memory corruption or a Metal toolchain issue, rather than an ordinary missing function, but the root cause is unverified. No compiler fix is claimed.

Related reports checked: #1128 (F32.show on the device), #1513 (type-family closure discovery), and #1433 (Metal compiler flow-state limit). This file does not call F32.show or use the type-family/closure pattern in #1513. No matching open report was found.

### The file

```python

import Base

type Segs is Data:
  SegEnd{}
  Seg{+s: U32, next: Segs}

def Font.pick(b: Bool, +c: U32) -> Segs:
  match b:
    case True{}:
      Seg{67588, Seg{100532, SegEnd{}}}
    case False{}:
      SegEnd{}

def Font.glyph(+c: U32) -> Segs:
  Font.pick(U32.is_eq(c, 33), c)

type Item is Data:
  IGlyph{+x: U32, +y: U32, +code: U32}

type Items is Data:
  INil{}
  ICons{+it: Item, next: Items}

type Cells is Data:
  CNil{}
  CLeaf{ts: Items}
  CQua{tl: Cells, tr: Cells, bl: Cells, br: Cells}

def pick(c: Bool, a: F32, b: F32) -> F32:
  match c:
    case True{}:
      a
    case False{}:
      b

def fmin(+a: F32, +b: F32) -> F32:
  pick((a < b : F32), a, b)

def fmax(+a: F32, +b: F32) -> F32:
  pick((a < b : F32), b, a)

def clamp01(+x: F32) -> F32:
  fmin(1.0, fmax(0.0, x))

# n glyphs in rows of 40, 18 x 40 px apart, codes 32..126.
def Text.grid(n: Nat, +i: U32, acc: Items) -> Items:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+p:
      Text.grid(p, (i + 1 : U32), ICons{IGlyph{(i % 40 * 18 : U32), (i / 40 * 40 : U32), (i % 95 + 32 : U32)}, acc})

def Item.meets(+it: Item, +x0: U32, +y0: U32, +x1: U32, +y1: U32) -> Bool:
  match it:
    case IGlyph{gx, gy, _}:
      ((gx < x1 + 2) && (gx + 16 > x0) && (gy < y1 + 2) && (gy + 30 > y0) : U32)

def Items.keep(meets: Bool, +it: Item, acc: Items) -> Items:
  match meets:
    case True{}:
      ICons{it, acc}
    case False{}:
      acc

def Items.clip(xs: Items, +x0: U32, +y0: U32, +x1: U32, +y1: U32, acc: Items) -> Items:
  match xs:
    case INil{}:
      acc
    case ICons{+it, t}:
      Items.clip(t, x0, y0, x1, y1, Items.keep(Item.meets(it, x0, y0, x1, y1), it, acc))

def Cells.build(+k: Nat, xs: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Cells:
  match k xs:
    case _ INil{}:
      CNil{}
    case 0n ICons{h, t}:
      CLeaf{ICons{h, t}}
    case 1n+e ICons{h, t}:
      +xs = {ICons{h, t} : Items}
      +s = U32.shln(64, e)
      +x1 = (x + s : U32)
      +y1 = (y + s : U32)
      q0 : Items = Items.clip(xs, x, y, x1, y1, INil{})
      q1 : Items = Items.clip(xs, x1, y, (x1 + s : U32), y1, INil{})
      q2 : Items = Items.clip(xs, x, y1, x1, (y1 + s : U32), INil{})
      q3 : Items = Items.clip(xs, x1, y1, (x1 + s : U32), (y1 + s : U32), INil{})
      a b c d = Cells.build(e, q0, x, y) Cells.build(e, q1, x1, y) Cells.build(e, q2, x, y1) Cells.build(e, q3, x1, y1)
      CQua{a, b, c, d}

def Glyph.d2(segs: Segs, +u: F32, +v: F32, +best: F32) -> F32:
  match segs:
    case SegEnd{}:
      best
    case Seg{s, next}:
      +x0 = U32.to_f32((s .&. 15 : U32))
      +y0 = U32.to_f32(((s >> 4n) .&. 31 : U32))
      +dx = (U32.to_f32(((s >> 9n) .&. 15 : U32)) - x0 : F32)
      +dy = (U32.to_f32(((s >> 13n) .&. 31 : U32)) - y0 : F32)
      +l2 = fmax((dx * dx + dy * dy : F32), 0.0001)
      +t = clamp01((((u - x0) * dx + (v - y0) * dy) / l2 : F32))
      +qx = (x0 + t * dx - u : F32)
      +qy = (y0 + t * dy - v : F32)
      Glyph.d2(next, u, v, fmin(best, (qx * qx + qy * qy : F32)))

def Glyph.cov(near: Bool, +k: U32, +gx: U32, +gy: U32, +px: F32, +py: F32) -> F32:
  match near:
    case False{}:
      0.0
    case True{}:
      +u = ((px - U32.to_f32(gx)) / 1.75 : F32)
      +v = ((py - U32.to_f32(gy)) / 1.75 : F32)
      +d = (F32.sqrt(Glyph.d2(Font.glyph(k), u, v, 1000.0)) * 1.75 : F32)
      d

def Px.go(ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32, +px: F32, +py: F32, +ink: F32) -> U32:
  match ts:
    case INil{}:
      F32.to_u32((ink * 255.0 : F32))
    case ICons{IGlyph{gx, gy, k}, t}:
      Px.go(t, x, y, px, py, fmax(ink, Glyph.cov(True{}, k, gx, gy, px, py)))

def Px.at(+ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Pix{Px.go(ts, x, y, (U32.to_f32(x) + 0.5 : F32), (U32.to_f32(y) + 0.5 : F32), 0.0)}

def Tile.b2(+ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Qua{Px.at(ts, x, y), Px.at(ts, (x + 1 : U32), y), Px.at(ts, x, (y + 1 : U32)), Px.at(ts, (x + 1 : U32), (y + 1 : U32))}

def Tile.b4(+ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Qua{Tile.b2(ts, x, y), Tile.b2(ts, (x + 2 : U32), y), Tile.b2(ts, x, (y + 2 : U32)), Tile.b2(ts, (x + 2 : U32), (y + 2 : U32))}

def Tile.b8(+ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Qua{Tile.b4(ts, x, y), Tile.b4(ts, (x + 4 : U32), y), Tile.b4(ts, x, (y + 4 : U32)), Tile.b4(ts, (x + 4 : U32), (y + 4 : U32))}

def Tile.b16(+ts: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Qua{Tile.b8(ts, x, y), Tile.b8(ts, (x + 8 : U32), y), Tile.b8(ts, x, (y + 8 : U32)), Tile.b8(ts, (x + 8 : U32), (y + 8 : U32))}

def Tile.go(+cs: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  Tile.b16(cs, x, y)

def Cell.fork(+k: Nat, +cs: Items, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  match k:
    case 0n:
      Tile.go(cs, x, y)
    case 1n+e:
      +h = U32.shln(16, e)
      a b c d = Cell.fork(e, cs, x, y) Cell.fork(e, cs, (x + h : U32), y)
        Cell.fork(e, cs, x, (y + h : U32)) Cell.fork(e, cs, (x + h : U32), (y + h : U32))
      Qua{a, b, c, d}

def Frame.node(c: Cells, +k: Nat, +x: U32, +y: U32) -> Image:
  match c:
    case CNil{}:
      Pix{0}
    case CLeaf{ts}:
      Cell.fork(2n, ts, x, y)
    case CQua{tl, tr, bl, br}:
      match k:
        case 0n:
          Pix{0}
        case 1n+e:
          +s = U32.shln(64, e)
          a b cc d = Frame.node(tl, e, x, y) Frame.node(tr, e, (x + s : U32), y)
            Frame.node(bl, e, x, (y + s : U32)) Frame.node(br, e, (x + s : U32), (y + s : U32))
          Qua{a, b, cc, d}

def Frame.show(+cells: Cells) -> Image & Cells:
  (Frame.node!(cells, 5n, 0, 0), cells)

def Img.sum(img: Image) -> U32:
  match img:
    case Pix{c}:
      c
    case Qua{a, b, c, d}:
      (Img.sum(a) + Img.sum(b) + Img.sum(c) + Img.sum(d) : U32)

def Frame.sum(p: Image & Cells) -> U32:
  (img, _) = p
  Img.sum(img)

def go(n: Nat, +text: Items, +acc: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      IO.print(U32.show(acc))
    case 1n+p:
      do IO<Unit>:
        cells : Cells = Cells.build(5n, text, 0, 0)
        now : Nat <- IO.now()
        t : U32 = Frame.sum(Frame.show(cells))
        go(p, text, (acc + t : U32))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    cells : Cells = Cells.build(5n, ICons{IGlyph{0, 0, 32}, INil{}}, 0, 0)
    now : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(U32.show(Img.sum(Frame.node!(cells, 5n, 0, 0))))
```

bend 2.0.39

Darwin arm64

Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.6.4.2)

title: [complexity, checker] O(n^2 log n) — An empty match copies all variables before inspecting the first
body:
Define `Empty` and `Unit`:

```bend
type Empty is Type:
type Unit is Data:
  U{}
```

Consider these terms:

```bend
def test(e: Empty) -> Unit:
  x = {\{} : Unit -> Unit};
  U{}
```

```bend
def test(e: Empty) -> Unit:
  x = {\{} : Unit -> Unit};
  y = {\{} : Unit -> Unit};
  U{}
```

Let `n` be the number of local empty matches: 1 and 2 above. Main copies
O(n² log n) array entries during checking.

**Cause.** Each `\{}` has no cases, although its input type `Unit` has a constructor.
The outer parameter `e: Empty` justifies this because `Empty` has none. To find it,
`ctx_dead` searches for an available variable with an empty type. First,
`pmap_to_array` copies the entire variable tree into an array. Repeated array joins
copy O(k log k) entries for k variables in scope. Only then does the search inspect
`e`, the first entry, and return. Repeating this as the scope grows copies
O(n² log n) entries.

**Copying the whole scope before searching may not be necessary.** Searching the
variable tree directly could stop at the first eligible empty type. Here `e` is at
the first node, so n matches could need O(n) search visits without the array copies.

To reproduce on main `7a7e6505a`, save the setup and either term as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

Source: [tree-to-array copying][source1], [empty-type search][source2].

[source1]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7a7e6505aeff2101a139a8419e16098ed2a89110/bend2/bend.ts#L562-L574
[source2]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/7a7e6505aeff2101a139a8419e16098ed2a89110/bend2/bend.ts#L842-L854

title: [complexity, flattening, checker] O(n^2) — Checking a call copies its growing argument list each time
body:
Consider these programs:

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}

def discard(x1: Unit, x2: Unit) -> Unit:
  U{}
def example() -> Unit:
  discard(U{}, U{})
```

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}

def discard(x1: Unit, x2: Unit, x3: Unit) -> Unit:
  U{}
def example() -> Unit:
  discard(U{}, U{}, U{})
```

`discard` ignores its arguments and returns `U{}`. Let `n` be the number of arguments
passed to `discard`: 2 and 3 above. Checking `example` copies
`0 + 1 + ... + (n-1) = n(n-1)/2` existing argument-list entries:
1 and 3, respectively. Checking `discard` is separate.

**Cause.** Bend represents a call as nested applications. On each step towards the
called function, `term_infer` builds `[tm.x, ...sp]`, where `sp` holds pending
arguments. Adding one argument copies every argument already collected.

**This quadratic list work may not be necessary.** A linked list could add each
argument with one node pointing to the existing list. Building it and converting
it to an array once would take O(n) work.

The same copying occurs when `body_flatten` loads ordinary parameters with repeated
`vars.slice(1)` calls: n parameters copy `n(n-1)/2` entries to emit n lambdas.
Keeping the original array and advancing an index could make this list work O(n).

Constructor matching also copies growing field arrays for the recursion check and
the branch's type. With n fields, each loop copies `n(n-1)/2` entries. Each generated
function could keep a linked prefix and build the ordered array once all fields
are present, giving O(n) list work including conversion.

To reproduce on main `7a7e6505a`, save either program as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

[binder-tail copies][source3], [recursion fields][source4], [branch-type fields][source5].

title: [complexity, checker] O(n^2) — Comparing calls reduces the same remaining expression again
body:
Consider these programs:

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}

def test(f: Unit -> Unit -> Unit) -> {f(U{}, U{}) == f(U{}, U{}) : Unit}:
  {==}
```

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}

def test(f: Unit -> Unit -> Unit -> Unit) -> {f(U{}, U{}, U{}) == f(U{}, U{}, U{}) : Unit}:
  {==}
```

Let `n` count arguments in each call to `f`: 2 and 3 above. Main makes
`n(n+1)` evaluator visits to applications: 6 and 12, respectively. This is O(n²),
although each call has only n applications.

**Cause.** `{==}` checks that the two calls are equal. Before comparing them,
`compare_go` asks `term_wnf` to evaluate them. The evaluator walks all n applications
to find `f`, but cannot run an unknown function parameter. Comparison then enters
the shorter function prefix and asks the evaluator to walk it again: for example,
`f(U{}, U{}, U{})`, then `f(U{}, U{})`, then `f(U{})`. Each side takes
`n + (n-1) + ... + 1` application visits.

**Reducing the same remaining expression again may not be necessary.** After the
first walk, comparison could retain that the prefixes end at the same unknown
variable. None can evaluate further while `f` is unknown. Reusing that fact could
reduce the application visits to `2n`: one walk for each call. This concerns
repeated evaluation; collecting the calls' arguments is the separate list-copying
cost in [#1956][argument-copying].

[Issue #984][github-current] is open as of 29 October 2026. It gives an exponential
form of repeated evaluation: each quantity definition refers to its predecessor
twice. The quadratic bound above describes the repeated-call-prefix example, not that chain.

To reproduce on main `7a7e6505a`, save either program as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

Source: [comparison entry][source1], [application evaluation][source2].

title: C builds a segment of any width: continuations take wide frames, joins and closures pack the words past WIDE (#1069)
body:
Fixes #1069.

A program the interpreter and JS run could fail `bend -o` with `an arity over 247` whenever a segment kept more than 247 words live: a record built field by field with calls, a list literal of calls, values live across a fork, a closure's captures. Since 2.0.39 a real program hits it too (hapsland, reported on #1069): #1806 lets `command_selected` borrow `command` instead of moving it, so `NativeRun.command_selected$k1063` keeps it live and goes from 243 to 254 words. #1806 is right; the limit is the problem, and that program has 27 segments between 200 and 247 words.

The 247 limit is the register bank's, but only some segments enter through it:

- A continuation reads its live words from the stack (`seg_take`, `WL_ARGS`); only its results ride registers, and the bank is already sized without it. It only needed a wider arity: `Fid` takes u16 fields when some arity passes 255, u8 otherwise, so other builds keep their table. On Metal all four fields must share one width: a u16 `ar` beside u8 fields leaves the device lane with "frontier drained" even in small programs.
- A fork join and a closure enter through registers (`FID_ENTER`'s `WL_LOAD`, `Clo~apply`). `seg_pack` moves their live words past WIDE into one `~pack` node of 2^c words, a constructor with its own CID, so a dropped closure's `term_drop` frees it and its fields. `seg_open` reads it back into locals at the segment's entry and frees it. Both join paths, parallel and sequential, pack the same tail. Words of any width pack, which covers the multiword captures #1788 boxed.
- `term_drop` reads `64 | (n - 240)` only for constructors: a wide task or closure now exists.

Programs under the limit emit the same C as before, apart from the `Fid` typedef's position and that `term_drop` line (checked on 73 tests in tests/run and tests/reg).

Tests (tests/reg), each failing to build on main and passing on interpreter, JS and C at 1 and 4 threads:
- wide_frame: a 300-String record built by calls (continuations).
- wide_fork_join, wide_fork_join_gpu: 300 U32 live across a fork, on the host and under `!`.
- wide_closure_pack: closures over 300 Strings, applied and dropped.
- wide_capture_calls, wide_capture_closure: from #1788 (multiword captures).

What stays:
- A def whose own parameters pass WIDE in one-word values still fails; multiword parameters keep their boxing rule.
- Apple clang 21 crashes when a `preserve_none` function's frame passes 4 KB (#1233). A segment with about 500 live words reaches it; `-fno-stack-check` builds it, and 600 live words then run correctly.
- Under `!`, very large programs (10+ MB of C) are slow or crash in Metal's compiler on main too.

Related: #1788 (multiword captures, superseded by this), #1494 (an earlier spill through the evaluator stack, closed).

title: safe.ts: a ~ argument's run-time Data variables are its instance's captures (#1483)
body:
Fixes #1483.

A template argument that names a run-time variable, as in `List.all(~&2, ~Nat, ~(y => Nat.is_le(lo, y)), xs)` inside a type, sent the def out of scope ("a template argument that depends on a run-time value"), so every lemma over such a type was unverifiable.

`closed_val` now lifts those variables: each run-time variable of a Data type (or an enclosing capture) that the argument's normal form names becomes `\0cap<j>`, numbered by first place. The instance takes the captures first, at q=2 (`def_emit`), its key includes their types (`item_key`), and the call passes the caller's variables (`args`). Function captures stay out of scope, since the kernel's q=2 binders need a Data type. root_emit's G keeps the old Open_Error fallback (`cap: undefined`), and a group call with captures is Open_Error.

- tests/check/template_type_capture.bend: the issue's repro, an inductive proof over it, colliding captures, a dependent capture type, a datatype field, a law over its own `~b`, a capture the normal form drops, captures passed on between nested instances. Out of scope on main, ALL PROOFS CHECK under `--verdict` here.
- `-o` is byte-identical to main on every existing test.
- bend-mathlib's sort.bend, with `internal_least` back in its `List.all` form: 16 defs out of scope on main, ALL PROOFS CHECK here.

title: [complexity, checker] O(n^2) — Every recursive call proves the same argument is smaller again
body:
Define `Unit` and `N`:

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}

type N is Data:
  Z{}
  S{p: N}
```

Consider these terms:

```bend
def test(t: N) -> Unit:
  match t:
    case S{S{+p}}:
      x = test(p);
      y = test(p);
      U{}
    case _:
      U{}
```

```bend
def test(t: N) -> Unit:
  match t:
    case S{S{S{+p}}}:
      x = test(p);
      y = test(p);
      z = test(p);
      U{}
    case _:
      U{}
```

Let `n` count nested `S` constructors and `m` count calls to `test(p)`.
Bend makes `m(n+1)` visits through the pattern to check that these calls decrease.
In these examples, `m=n`: 2 in the first and 3 in the second. The pattern is
written once, so the source grows like `n+m`, while these visits grow like `n*m`.
Growing both together therefore gives quadratic work in the amount of syntax.

**Cause.** `+p` allows more than one use of `p`, but each recursive call must pass a
smaller argument. `term_descend` searches from the outermost `S` to establish that
`p` is inside `t`. Every call uses the same `p` under the same pattern, but repeats
the search. There are m calls and n layers.

**Repeating these searches may not be necessary.** Neither `p` nor the pattern
changes between these calls. Establishing once that `p` is smaller, then using
that fact at each call, could give O(n+m) work for this family.

The closed [issue #1543][github-current] reports exponential work to establish
that the argument of a **single recursive call in the source** is smaller.
Here, each `test(p)` requires only a linear walk through the pattern, but Bend
repeats that same walk for every `test(p)` written in the arm.

To reproduce on main `4f99f4c19`, save the setup and either term as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

Source: [descent search][source1], [recursive call check][source2].

title: import: a segment starting with a digit is refused, but the error says digits are allowed
body:
**Bend 2.0.38** (also observed with the 2.0.39 notice).

### Reproduction

```sh
mkdir -p sub/2d sub/d2
printf "def value() -> F32:\n  1.0\n" > sub/2d/main.bend
cp sub/2d/main.bend sub/d2/main.bend

printf "import Base\nimport sub/2d/main.bend as M\n\ndef main() -> IO(Unit):\n  do IO<Unit>:\n    IO.print(F32.show(M.value()))\n    return Unit{}\n" > probe_2d.bend
printf "import Base\nimport sub/d2/main.bend as M\n\ndef main() -> IO(Unit):\n  do IO<Unit>:\n    IO.print(F32.show(M.value()))\n    return Unit{}\n" > probe_d2.bend
```

### Observed

`bend probe_2d.bend`:

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : an import path of plain names (letters, digits, _ and -; the hub*s files import the hub*s)
- observed : (sub/2d/main.bend)
```

`bend probe_d2.bend` prints `1`.

### What the rule appears to be

A path segment must **start with a letter or `_`**. `d2` passes, `2d` does not. The message lists digits as valid in a name, which sends the reader looking for a path or permission problem instead of renaming the directory.

### Proposed

Either accept `2d` (it is letters and digits), or change the message to say that each segment must start with a letter or `_`, and add a Note pointing at the segment and the first character. The restriction itself is fine; the diagnostic is the issue.

This is a diagnostics defect, not a capability gap: renaming `2d` to `two_moons` fixed it.

title: Array.new: the depth argument is undocumented, and a length gives "an array past the deepest block class 31"
body:
**Bend 2.0.38.**

### Reproduction

```bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    a = Array.new(U32, 12288n, 0)
    return Unit{}
```

```text
SOME PROOFS FAIL
bend: an array past the deepest block class 31
```

Changing only `12288n` to `14n` builds and runs. The intent was a 12,288-element array; `d` is a **binary-tree depth**, so the correct value is 14 (2^14 = 16,384 leaves), or `T.depth(n)` where that helper is available.

### Observed

`bend base Array.new` shows the definition but nothing says `d` is a depth:

```text
def Array.new(-T: Data, +d: Nat, +v: T) -> Array<T>:
  match d:
    case 0n:
      ALeaf{v}
    case 1n+p:
      ANode{[v : T^p], [v : T^p]}
```

The error names the block class but not the argument, and a reader who passes a length has no way to know that 31 is a depth bound rather than a size bound.

### Relation to existing issues

This is not #1267 (the closed depth-24 boxed-value split between JS and native), and not `tests/io/array_depth_bound.bend` (depth 31). It is the public signature and its diagnostic.

### Proposed

- Document `d` as the tree depth, `2^d` leaves, and that the largest legal depth is 31.
- Make the error say so, for example: `depth 12288 exceeds the deepest block class (31); pass the depth, for example 14 for 12288 elements`.
- If useful, add `Array.of_length(n, v)` or point at `T.depth(n)`, so the common case does not require knowing the representation.

The workaround is proven: depth 23 loads a 6.3 MB byte array in 45 ms.

title: fix(array): the depth-wall error and Array.new say d is a depth
body:
Fixes #1962 (the first two points; no new helper).

`Array.new(T, d, v)` takes a depth: it builds `2^d` cells. Passing a length, as in `Array.new(U32, 12288n, 0)`, hits the depth wall with "an array past the deepest block class 31", which names neither the argument nor that 31 is a depth. The fix is 14n (16384 cells).

**Change**

- `bend2/base.bend`: a comment above `Array.new`: d is a depth, not a length (14n for 12288 cells), at most 31.
- `tests/io/array_depth_bound.bend`: its `#|` line carries the new text.

| `Array.get(U32, Array.new(U32, d, 7), 5)` | Before | After |

| d = 12288n, interp / JS / C | "…block class 31", exit 1 | "…block class 31 (a depth d holds 2^d cells)", exit 1 |
| d = 14n, interp / JS / C | `7` | `7` |

title: fix(import): the path error says each name starts with a letter or _
body:
Fixes #1961.

An import is refused at two points, and both used one message: "an import path of plain names (letters, digits, _ and -; the hub's files import the hub's)". It named neither of the two rules behind it.

- **The path as written** must be plain names, each starting with a letter or `_` (`[A-Za-z_][\w-]*`), so no name segment starts with a digit and every key has one spelling (#1042). `import sub/2d/main.bend` failed here with a message that listed the digit as allowed.
- **The file it resolves to** must keep that shape too, and it must stay on its side of the hub: a hub file imports only hub files, and a local path does not land in the hub's store. Here every segment can be a plain name, so the name message sent the reader looking for a bad name that isn't there. And `observed` showed the path as written, even when the resolved path was the problem, as with a link to `2d/`.

**Change**: the rules don't change, and neither does what they refuse. The new hub check takes two cases out of the old condition: a file in the store without a `0x` head, and a hub file that reaches outside the store. Everything else the old condition refused keeps the name message.
- `bend2/bend.ts`: a shape failure says "an import path of plain names (each starts with a letter or _, then letters, digits, _ and -)". When the resolved file fails it, `observed` is the resolved path. A hub crossing says "an import on its side of the hub (a hub file imports only hub files, and a local path stays out of the hub's store)", with the path as written.
- `guide/GUIDE.md`: the imports paragraph states the name rule (7976 → 7980 ttok, cap 8000).
- `tests/import/digit_segment.bend` (new): `./2d/x.bend` gets the name message.
- `gates/ping.ts`: two checks for the hub message. A file in the store imports `../stray.bend` (the store's root) or `../../out.bend` (outside it). A test under `tests/` can't place files in the store, and ping already runs bend with its own `HOME`.
- `tests/import/{dotted_path,hub_head_path,hub_head_local,tilde_path}.bend`: their `#|` lines carry the name message.

| Import | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `./2d/x.bend` | plain names (letters, digits, _ and -; the hub's …) | plain names (each starts with a letter or _, …), observed `'./2d/x.bend'` |
| `./good/x.bend`, `good` a link to `2d` | same, observed `'./good/x.bend'` | plain names, observed `'2d/x.bend'` |
| a store file importing `../stray.bend` | plain names (…) | its side of the hub, observed `'../stray.bend'` |
| a store file importing `../../out.bend` | plain names (…) | its side of the hub, observed `'../../out.bend'` |
| `./d2/x.bend`; a store file importing `./inner.bend` | runs | runs |

**Verification** (macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2, Apple clang 21; Linux arm64 in Docker, Debian 13, Bun 1.4.2, clang 19 with X11 and ALSA headers)

- [x] The table above on macOS and Linux, with a temp `BEND_LIB` for the store cases.
- [x] The new ping block, run on its own (a copy of it, byte for byte, with `bun bend2/main.ts` in place of the installed bend and the same temp `HOME`): 0/2 on main, 2/2 with the change, on macOS and Linux.

The only lanes that change are the four updated tests' message line, plus the new test. Against the `#|` lines: macOS interp 1782/1782, JS 927/927, C 875/878; Linux interp 1779/1782, JS 923/927, C 874/878. The misses are the same on the base: windows with no display, and `stack_fault_trap`'s exit code on macOS.

title: perf(check): ctx_dead searches the scope in place instead of copying it first
body:
Fixes #1955.

`ctx_dead` copied the whole scope into an array with `pmap_to_array` before it looked at the first variable. A scope with n local empty matches (`\{}`) calls it n times, so the copies grew as O(n² log n) while the search itself stopped at the first variable.

**Change** (`bend2/bend.ts` only): `pmap_any` walks the tree in place, next to `pmap_to_array`, and `ctx_dead` uses it. It visits the same nodes in the same order (value, then left, then right) and stops at the same first empty type, so `term_wnf` and `book_adt` run on the same variables in the same order. No cache and no memo: the search only skips the copy (#993, #1075).

**Measured** on the issue's program with n `x = {\{} : Unit -> Quant}` lines, `--check-only`:

| n | entries copied in `ctx_dead`, before | after | wall time, before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 393 | 0 | 20 ms | 20 ms |
| 1024 | 4,383,927 | 0 | 66 ms | 36 ms |
| 4096 | not counted | 0 | 820 ms | 160 ms |
| 8192 | not counted | 0 | 3,124 ms | 530 ms |

Copies were counted with a temporary counter, since removed. Times are medians of 7 runs, before and after alternated.

None of the checker benches calls `ctx_dead`, and their medians of 5 alternated runs stay within noise: compute_1600 508 → 505 ms, defs_12800 297 → 297, generics_3200 382 → 384, proofs_3200 823 → 833, trees_400 803 → 798. So this only matters for scopes with many empty matches.

On Linux, medians of 7: n = 1024 77 → 43 ms, 4096 982 → 199 ms, 8192 4,042 → 609 ms; checker benches compute_1600 609 → 613, defs_12800 361 → 368, generics_3200 458 → 455, proofs_3200 922 → 929, trees_400 1142 → 1140.

**Verification** (macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; Linux arm64 (Docker, Debian 13, Bun 1.4.2, clang 19))

- [x] Wall time, issue program n = 16 to 8192, and the 5 checker benches, macOS and Linux: above

title: fix(check): a constructor's fields grow as a list, without copying
body:
Fixes #1956. #1967 did the call spine and `body_flatten`, and this does the constructor fields, the last copies #1956 names.

## What

`lhs_ext` and `term_check_mat_goal` built a constructor's fields with `[...xs, x]` and `xs.concat([x])`, so a constructor with n fields copied n(n-1)/2 entries. They now cons onto the existing `List` and build the array once with `list_to_array`. The list is persistent because these closures can be entered more than once.

The `Ref` case from #1967 now reads a call's pending arguments with the same helper, instead of its own loop.

Output is unchanged: the fields come out in source order, and `tests/check/list_order.bend` pins that.

## Numbers

`--check-only` on a match over one constructor with 4,000 fields, best of 9, macOS: 257 ms on `main`, 220 ms here. `bend.ts` goes from 45,100 to 45,150 ttok (cap 48,000).

The gain only shows on very large constructors. The point of this PR is finishing #1956.

## Dropped from the earlier version

This PR was +151/-54. It no longer has:

- **Level-order `ctx_dead`:** it changed which `@unsafe` binder type a program hangs on, to save 0.4-0.6 s at 8,000 empty matches when `Empty` isn't first. #1965 fixes #1955 with main's order.
- **Batched var columns in `match_flatten`:** about 0.02 s saved, and it removed the "a variable pattern" error that guarded the path. That code is back as it is on `main`.
- **`patt_lams`, the `pmap_to_array` change and the list spine in `term_infer`:** #1965 and #1967 cover those cases, except `patt_lams`' later-binder branch, which saved about 0.03 s at 4,000 binders.

A review suggested recording dead binders in `ctx_bind` instead. I didn't do that: it would have to reduce every binder's type when it's bound, and main only does that when an empty match needs it. `def f(x: loop(0n)) -> Nat` finishes on `main` today, so that would add hangs.

## Testing

- This PR on `main` `e73e9f98`, `gates/_run.ts`: `repo` 54/54, `perf` 124/124, `test` 1817/1817.

title: perf(check): a call's pending arguments are a cons list, and parameters flatten in one loop
body:
Part of #1956: the call spine and `body_flatten`. Constructor fields are left for later (see the end).

Checking a call `f(a1, …, an)` walks its nested `App`s toward `f`, and each step built the pending arguments as a new array, `[tm.x, ...sp]`, so a call with n arguments copied n(n-1)/2 entries. Flattening a def's n parameters did the same with `body_flatten(b, vars.slice(1), fr)`.

**Change** (`bend2/bend.ts` only)
- `term_infer`: the spine is a `List<HTerm>`, the file's existing cons list, and `App` passes `list_set(sp, 0, tm.x)` (a cons; the key is unused). The `Ref` case reads it into an array once, only when `qt` is not None, and `def_inst`, the `slice(x)` and the decreasing-call loop use that array as they used `sp`. No other caller passes a spine.
- `body_flatten`, default arm: a loop from the last parameter to the first wraps the same `Lam`s. The recursion always landed in this arm again, since `b` does not change.

No cache and no memo: it only drops copies (#993, #1075).

**Measured** on the issue's `discard` with n parameters and a call with n arguments, `--check-only`:

| n | spine entries copied, before | after | `body_flatten` entries copied, before | after | wall time, before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 18 ms | 19 ms |
| 8 | 28 | 8 | 28 | 0 | 19 ms | 19 ms |
| 32 | 496 | 32 | 496 | 0 | 20 ms | 20 ms |
| 512 | 130,816 | 512 | 130,816 | 0 | 25 ms | 23 ms |
| 2048 | 2,096,128 | 2,048 | 2,096,128 | 0 | 45 ms | 32 ms |
| 8192 | 33,550,336 | 8,192 | 33,550,336 | 0 | 262 ms | 67 ms |

Before is n(n-1)/2 in both places; after, the spine is read once (n entries) and `body_flatten` copies nothing. For n = 2 the spine read costs one entry more than before. Copies were counted with temporary counters, since removed; times are medians of 7 runs, before and after alternated.

Checker benches, medians of 5 alternated runs: compute_1600 501 → 503 ms, defs_12800 285 → 289, generics_3200 380 → 374, proofs_3200 817 → 777 (ranges 814–840 and 763–824 overlap; Linux below shows no change), trees_400 810 → 809. So this only matters for calls with many arguments.

On Linux, medians of 7: n = 512 27 → 23 ms, 2048 59 → 42 ms, 8192 381 → 104 ms; checker benches compute_1600 609 → 601, defs_12800 378 → 380, generics_3200 457 → 445, proofs_3200 931 → 926, trees_400 1159 → 1145.

**Verification** (macOS arm64, Bun 1.4.2; Linux arm64 (Docker, Debian 13, Bun 1.4.2, clang 19))

- [x] Copies in the spine and `body_flatten`, n = 2 to 8192, macOS: the table above
- [x] Wall time, issue program n = 2 to 8192, and the 5 checker benches, macOS and Linux: above
- [x] All 1796 tests under `tests/`, interpreter, before vs after, macOS and Linux: no difference (on macOS `proof/app/main`, which greets until killed, is not comparable; on Linux its output is capped at 1 MB and matches)
- [x] `gates/repo.ts`: 54/54 (bend.ts 44,532 / 48,000 ttok)
- [x] Strict `tsc` of bend.ts alone: the same 19 errors before and after, all missing types
- [ ] `gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`: run on the minis
- [ ] The constructor-field copies the issue also names (below)
- [ ] Metal, CUDA: not run; the change is in the checker

**Left out**: the constructor-field copies the issue also names (`[...xs, x]` in `lhs_ext`, `xs.concat([x])` in `term_check_mat_goal`) sit inside term bodies built as functions that can run more than once, so they need a different change. Hence "part of".

Note: #1734 reads `sp[j]` and `sp.length` in the `Ref` case; there the array is now `xs`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: refactor(comp): shed tokens and compile large programs faster
body:
comp.ts drops 40 ttok (`ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo`, as `gates/repo.ts` pins it), and large programs compile faster. It merges cleanly with `main`, taking comp.ts from 66,000 to 65,960, which leaves room under the 66,000 cap.

Compile time (C and JS together, median of 7 alternating runs):

| Program | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `demos/app_slash_boss_3d` | 746 ms | 614 ms |
| `demos/pure_hvm5_mini` | 270 ms | 235 ms |

## What changes

**Compile time**
- **`c_ids` scans only the runtime.** The emitted C names no ids, and it was most of the text being scanned.
- **JS builds skip `ty_srcs`.** It only adds ADT names to `FL.srcs`, and JS reads only the defs from that map.
- **`term_const` is memoized.** It re-walked the same constructor trees.
- **`js_lib` drops `FL` after building a module**, so the loader's host doesn't keep the book alive. After a module build and a GC, the heap goes from 87 MB to 5.4 MB on boss and from 33 MB to 5 MB on hvm5.

**Simplification**
- `NATIVE` is inlined where it is read, and `IO_EMIT` where it is used.
- `term_aux` returns `u32`, which removes the `(u32)term_aux` casts. `io_hand_v` is the one place that needs the width, and it now casts itself.
- `turn_take` and `tld_of` name repeated expressions.
- `ty_holds` takes its predicate as data, where its cache was keyed on a closure's source text.
- `lay_arr` returns `arr` as a number, and a few one-use locals and inferred annotations go.

## Behavior

- **One partial fix:** `js_lib(book, true)` overflowed the stack in `ty_srcs` on `tests/check/eta_recursive_type`, and that module now builds. Only JS is fixed: `ty_srcs` still overflows on a recursive type in a C build, as it does on `main`.
- **C:** the emitted program code is unchanged across the corpus. Only the runtime text differs, from the `term_aux` and `turn_take` edits.
- **JS:** output is byte-identical apart from the fix above.

## Verification

- `tests/run/array_lent` is new. It covers Array parameters that are shared and passed to defs that ignore them, on every lane. It passes on `main` too, so it guards behaviour and is not a test of this PR's changes.
- `gates/_run.ts` on a clean checkout: repo 54/54, test 1786/1786, perf 124/124. Ping was skipped because that checkout has no site repo next to it.
- I compared C, JS and module output against `main` for all 1,875 `.bend` files under `tests`, `demos` and `bench`; 1,378 of them load, and the rest fail before reaching the compiler.
- **Not tested:** the CUDA device path was not built, so the `term_aux` change is untested there. Metal is covered by the test gate.

title: fix(parse): point spaced successor patterns and glued x+y at the right spelling
body:
Addresses #1510.

The parsing stays as it is (see the reply on the issue). This only fixes errors that pointed the wrong way, and the GUIDE.

- **Spaced successor in a pattern.** `case 1n + p` and `case (1n + p : Nat)` now say `a pattern (a successor takes no spaces: 1n+p)`. `case 1n +p` adds the same hint to its pattern-count error.
- **Other operators in a pattern.** `case p + 1n` and `case 2n * p` say `a pattern (a binder or a constructor)`, without the annotation hint or the "we broke this after launch" note.
- **A `+` that reads as a binder.** `x+y`, `x +y`, `x y+z` and `x+y == 3` used to fail at the next `def` or at the second `=`. They now point at the `+`:
  ```
  - expected : '=' (an operator takes spaces on both sides and a type: (a + b : T))
  - observed : '+'
  ```
  `x+g(y)` and `x+y.z` get the same hint and location, from the `+` case of the term parser. `(1+x : U32)`, `(x+y, 1)` and `x+y` in a do block also move to the `+`. `1n +n 2n` changes too, so `tests/parse/chain_old_spellings_000.bend` is updated.
- **GUIDE.** The Terms list now has `3n+e`, and says `e` runs to the end.

Not covered: `x+1` parses as the operator and keeps its existing error, and `x-y` / `5n-x` stay as they are, per the reply on the issue.

Tests 1797/1797, including 12 tests for these errors. The repo gate is 54/54.

@AbarnaaSree, you asked to take #1510. This covers the error messages.
