title: A fit weakens a quantity its datatype only passes along, so List<&2, A> fits List<&1, A>
body:
A reusable `List<&2, A>` now fits where a `List<&1, A>` is expected, and not the other way round. `{List<&1, A> == List<&2, A>}` still doesn't check.

Related to #1994 and #2004: with this, a reusable list can be passed to a function that takes an affine one. This is the minimal alternative to #2043, which computes full variance for every datatype parameter.

## The rule

In LE mode, a fit compares a datatype's quantity argument by the quantity order (inside `Kind(_)`) when the datatype may weaken that slot. Every other argument is compared by conversion, as before.

A quantity slot may weaken when every use of it in the datatype's fields satisfies all three conditions:
- it is the bare parameter,
- it is passed to a quantity slot that may weaken too (the datatype's own included),
- it is outside any function domain.

Any other use rules weakening out: under an arrow's domain, inside a larger argument, or anywhere else in a field's type. For example, a `Use<&2>{f: List<&2, Nat> -> Nat}` may copy the list it is given, so it can't stand in for a `Use<&1>`, which may be given an affine list.

`adt_weakens` checks this in one walk of the fields. A slot still being asked is assumed to weaken. That is sound because the only use the walk accepts is passing the quantity along positively.

## What it doesn't do

Type parameters are still compared by conversion. So `List<&2, List<&2, Nat>>` fits `List<&1, List<&2, Nat>>`, but not `List<&1, List<&1, Nat>>`. Covariance through type parameters (rose trees, mutual families, nested lists) needs the full variance of #2043.

## Kernel

This PR changes only bend2. BendTT on `main` has no matching rule, so `--verdict` gives `SOME PROOFS FAIL` on `accept_weaken`, and `gates/safe.ts` will flag the disagreement. The kernel side will follow separately.

## Tests

- **`tests/grade/accept_weaken.bend`:** a reusable list fits an affine one, a list of reusable lists fits an affine list of them, and a `Bag<&2, Nat>` fits a `Bag<&1, Nat>` where `Bag` passes its quantity to `List`.
- **`tests/grade/accept_weaken_quant.bend`:** a quantity whose type only evaluates to `Quant` (`-q: Q()`) still weakens: a reusable `Box<&2>` fits an affine `Box<&1>`.
- **`tests/grade/reject_weaken.bend`:** a quantity under a function's domain doesn't weaken.
- **`tests/grade/reject_weaken_loop.bend`:** a quantity passed back to its own slot under an arrow doesn't weaken.
- **`tests/grade/reject_weaken_deep.bend`:** a quantity under two domains doesn't weaken either. Only uses outside every domain count, as in the kernel's rule.
- **`tests/grade/reject_upcast.bend`** (existing): `List<&1, Nat>` still doesn't fit `List<&2, Nat>`.

## Checked

- **Local test suite:** every test under `tests/` was run on this Mac with Bun, on this branch and on `main` (4024f04d). Every test on `main` gives the same output and exit code on both, and the five new tests pass here. `accept_weaken` fails without the change. The C and JS lanes and the minis were not run.
- **By hand:** `Bag<&1, Nat>` doesn't fit `Bag<&2, Nat>`, `List<&2, List<&2, Nat>>` doesn't fit `List<&1, List<&1, Nat>>`, and `{List<&1, Nat> == List<&2, Nat>}` doesn't check.
- **Size:** `bend.ts` is 45,955 tokens, against 45,429 on `main` and a 48k cap.

## Not run

The cluster gates (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`, `gates/safe.ts`, `gates/repo.ts`), GPU.

title: feat(tools): bend-cache, a proof cache for --check-only outside bend
body:
`bend --check-only` re-checks every def of the book on every run, Base included (#1234). `tools/bend-cache` is that check with a proof cache, outside bend, as #1631's close asked: bend stores nothing, and bend.ts and main.ts are unchanged.

```sh
bun tools/bend-cache/src/cache.ts PROOF.bend
```

A def whose check read nothing that changed since a run where it passed is skipped. The output is the CLI's, byte for byte, exit code included.

## How

While a def is checked, proxies on `book.tlds`, `book.ctrs` and `book.tmps` record the first read of each name and what it found. Those tables are the only state the checker reads (bend.ts holds no other mutable state). The trace keeps a hash of each read, and the names the def's elaborated body refers to. On a later run, `book_valid` asks at each def's own event whether every read hashes the same now. If so the def is skipped, and the verdict gets the names it kept.

Whether a law is opaque or filled when a def reads it is part of what the read finds. So the order of events needs no rule: a file that sees a fill it does not import, through the load order, is just another read. That is what #1846 had to model by hand, and why a key on a file's text and its imports (the `.olean` way) is wrong in Bend. That scheme gave 6 false passes on the probes.

It patches bend2 as Bun loads it, like bend-lint (each edit matches once, else exit 2, drift):
- `bend.ts`: `book_valid` also takes a skip predicate, and counts TODOs for skipped entries. A law whose fill was dropped is a TODO at the law, which may be skipped: without this, a dropped fill passes.
- `main.ts`: `book_read` validates through a hook; `book_promises` reads the names kept for skipped defs. It reads `t.e`, which a skipped check does not make: without this, a skipped def that calls Base's `Array.fork` passes.

It also stops if `Book` gains a field.

Only a check slower than `--min-ms` (0.2) keeps a trace: on books of thousands of cheap defs, hashing every trace cost more than checking.

## Tested

- `bun test` in `tools/bend-cache` (7 cases): library reuse, edits, a fill seen through load order, a dropped fill, Base `@unsafe` and an `@unsafe` template instance, and drift.
- Edit-then-check, against `bend --check-only`, byte for byte: 125 books (the #1846 probes, demos, tests/import, a sample of tests/proof and tests/check). 1,044 single edits (a literal +1, two imports swapped, a def or fill deleted), each run then reverted, with the cache kept across edits: 0 differences.
- Replay of all 1,933 tests, demos, evals and runtime benches, cold and warm: 0 differences.

## Numbers

End to end, ms, median of 5, M4:

| | `bend --check-only` | bend-cache, warm |
|---|---|---|
| #1234 client after another client | 726 | 67 |
| #1234 library edited, client | 665 | 66 |
| slash_boss PROOF.bend, rerun | 2,698 | 158 |
| slash_boss, a proof added to PROOF.bend | 2,738 | 160 |
| a file that only imports Base | 59 | 57 |

Base's defs are each too cheap to keep a trace, so Base is checked every run (~20 ms).

On the checker benches (no Base, thousands of cheap defs), a cold run costs +15–30% (the proxies) and a warm run gains only where some def is slow (trees_400 754 → 201 ms).

Supersedes #1846. The full comparison (prefix keys, file and import keys, `--trust`, a long-lived process, and scoping fills by imports) is in the comment there.

title: [complexity, parser, flattening, checker] O(n^2) — Each use of an outer variable searches past every local
body:
Consider these programs:

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}
type Units is Data:
  Nil{}
  Cons{head: Unit, tail: Units}
def example(+x: Unit) -> Units:
  a1: Unit = U{}
  Cons{x, Nil{}}
```

```bend
type Unit is Data:
  U{}
type Units is Data:
  Nil{}
  Cons{head: Unit, tail: Units}
def example(+x: Unit) -> Units:
  a1: Unit = U{}
  a2: Unit = U{}
  Cons{x, Cons{x, Nil{}}}
```

Let `n` count both the local bindings and the list cells containing `x`: 1 and 2 above.
`+x` permits the list cells to reuse this value. Finding these `x` references alone
makes `n(n+1)` list-entry visits per term conversion: 2 and 6 above, or O(n²).

**Cause.** `parse_var` searches names from the newest binding backwards. During term
conversion, `term_higher` searches its list of bindings in the same order using
`list_get`. Each use of `x` passes all `n` unrelated locals. Resolving one use does not
help the next. This conversion lookup runs during both loading and checking.

**These repeated scope searches may not be necessary.** While parsing, a name index
could point to the current binding, restoring the old entry when its scope closes.
During conversion, the existing number-indexed tree could provide logarithmic lookups.
New versions could share the unchanged parts of earlier trees, while saved function
bodies retain their original bindings. Expected constant-time name lookups and
logarithmic numeric lookups and updates could reduce ordinary loading and checking
for this family to O(n log n), including construction of the lookup structures.

The numeric tree trades cheaper deep lookups for more expensive updates: adding a
binding changes from O(1) to O(log n), as does finding the newest binding. It is not
an improvement for every scope shape.

Match lowering also searches repeatedly when matching the last of n parameters:
it finds the parameter, skips the first parameter and searches again. Finding it once
and skipping the whole preceding group would make those searches linear, while
producing the same lambdas in the same order.

To reproduce on main `4024f04dc`, save either program as `example.bend`;
run `bun bend2/main.ts example.bend --check-only`.

Source: [name search][source1], [binding-list search][source2],
[conversion lookup][source3], [match lookup][source4].

[source1]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/4024f04dc65527d9783481ba0672b818039c80d1/bend2/bend.ts#L1694-L1705
[source2]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/4024f04dc65527d9783481ba0672b818039c80d1/bend2/bend.ts#L585-L592
[source3]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/4024f04dc65527d9783481ba0672b818039c80d1/bend2/bend.ts#L707-L721
[source4]: https://github.com/bendlang/bend/blob/4024f04dc65527d9783481ba0672b818039c80d1/bend2/bend.ts#L2741-L2794

title: A law names its module's own def even when a Base constructor shares the name (#1236)
body:
Fixes #1236.

`parse_reso` looked every name up in `tlds` and `ctrs` together, but `parse_fresh` refuses a declaration by one table only. In a module whose law uses its own def above the def's declaration, `LAWS:Done` didn't exist yet, Base's constructor `Done` did, so the law resolved to the bare key `Done`. `LAWS.bend`'s `def Done` was still accepted (at `LAWS:Done`, since the constructor is in `ctrs`), and the entry's own `def Done` filled the bare key the law now named. `--verdict` certified a different law than `LAWS.bend` states.

Defs and constructors already live in separate tables, and the syntax always says which one a name means, so the fix is to resolve in that table only. `parse_reso` takes the table like `parse_own` does, defaulting to `tlds`. The three constructor sites pass `ctrs`: an `X{..}` literal, a `\{X: ..}` arm, and the check that a bare pattern binder isn't a constructor. Resolution and `parse_fresh` now agree. A forward use can only fall back to a bare name in the same table, and declaring that name afterwards is refused as a duplicate. No def named like a constructor is refused; the issue suggested refusing them, which wasn't needed.

### Other behavior changes

All of these come from the same rule, and all only affect imported modules (the entry has no namespace, so its own and bare names coincide):

- **Fixed:** a module with its own `def Done` can write `Done{b}` and `\{Done: ..}`. Before, both resolved to the def, and the module failed with `a declared constructor (Result declares Fail, Done)`.
- **Now refused, as in the entry:** that module binding a bare `Done` in a pattern or let. It gets `a braced constructor pattern (Done is a constructor: write Done{}, or rename the binder)`. The entry already refused this; the module's own def only hid the constructor before.
- **No longer refused:** `A.x(..)` where alias `A`'s module has a *constructor* `x` and Base has a def `A.x`. A call can only mean a def, so it resolves to Base's `A.x`, as it already did when the module had no `x` at all. The guard still fires when both candidates are in the same table.
- **Kept:** `Maybe{..}` in a module now resolves to `M:Maybe`. The checker's `Maybe is a datatype: write its arguments as <>` note also tries the name without its module, so the note still fires there.

### Tests

- `tests/import/law_def_named_ctr.bend` (+ `_lib`): the issue's repro on Base's `Bool`.
- `tests/import/ctr_named_def.bend` (+ `_lib`): `Done{..}`, `\{Done: ..}` and `Done(..)` side by side in a module.
- `tests/import/ctr_of_datatype.bend` (+ `_lib`): the datatype note from an imported module.

### What I checked

On 4024f04d, macOS arm64:

- `law_def_named_ctr` prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK` before and fails at `L.thm` (`expected : b / observed : True{}`) after, with and without `--verdict`. Its lib alone still reports `1 TODO found.`
- `ctr_named_def` fails before (`a declared constructor`) and prints `True{}` after. `ctr_of_datatype` matches `origin/main`, and loses the note without the checker change.
- `bend <f> --check-only` over all 1902 `.bend` files in `tests/` and `demos/`, old against new: identical output except `law_def_named_ctr` and `ctr_named_def`.
- `gates/_run.ts` on the cluster, rebased on 3c1f0d3a, against a clean `origin/main` the same way: repo 54 / 54, test 1835 / 1835 (main 1829 / 1829), perf 122-124 / 124 on both, ping 81 / 83 on both (the same two publish cases fail on main). The 30 s cap was hit on both sides under cluster load; two of the branch's ~20 test runs came back two short while all four gates ran at once, which didn't reproduce in eight verbose runs, alone or alongside the other gates.

Not run: Linux.

Note: AGENTS.md marks `bend2/bend.ts` as human-written; this change is made with Claude at my request, so please review it as such.

title: perf(check): a free name skips the env walk, and check-ctr never builds its result type
body:
Closes #1997. Supersedes #2037 and does the same job without a cache.

**Cause.** `parse_var` gives each free name (`Unit` in the issue) a fresh index and stores its `Ref` in `v`. Nothing ever binds that index, but `term_higher` still walked the whole env with `list_get` before falling back to `v`. Filling `k` parameters per value then costs `k` names × `k` steps, and each value also rebuilt the result type `N<A0, .., Ak>` (another `k²` lookups) that check-ctr threw away. Over `d + 1` values that is O(n³) when `k = d = n`.

**What.**
1. `term_higher` returns `tm.v` for a free name before looking it up in the env.
2. `tele_check` returns the rest of the telescope as a thunk, `ret`, instead of building it. check-ctr never calls it, so the last field's `B`, which only builds the result type, never runs. infer-adt and def_inst call `ret()`.

There is no cache, so nothing depends on object identity or on `ctr.T` being a plain spine. Fix 1 also speeds up every other telescope fill, check-mat included.

**Numbers.** `bun bend2/main.ts ex.bend --check-only` on the issue's chain (`k = d = n`), on a slower machine than #2037's (main took 363 s at n = 2400 there vs 91.5 s in #2037):

| n | main | fix 1 only | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 800 | 4.3 s | 2.0 s | 0.16 s |
| 2400 | 363 s | 26 s | 0.93 s |

Each value still fills its `k` parameters, so the work is O(k·d). The issue's addendum explains why that part stays.

**Checks.**
- Fix 1 is only valid if a free name's index is never bound. With an exit-on-violation probe in `term_higher`, `--check-only` over all 1,839 `tests/**/*.bend` never triggered it.
- `bun bend2/main.ts <file>` over 1,840 `tests/**/*.bend` gives identical stdout, stderr and exit code on main (4024f04d) and on this branch. `tests/proof/app/main.bend` is left out: it prints forever, so a timeout cuts it off at a different point each run.
- `tsc` reports the same 7 errors as on main, so no new ones.
- `gates/repo.ts` passes 54 / 54.

**Not fixed.** A bound variable is still looked up by walking the env, an association list. A constructor whose field uses the parameters, `S{p: N<A0, .., Ak>}`, still costs k lookups through a k-deep env per value: n = 1600 checks in 3.6 s here (6.9 s on main). Making the env a `PMap` brings that to 0.74 s, but it is 1–6% slower on every checker bench (and 0.92 s → 1.57 s on the issue's chain), so the env stays a `List`.

`tests/check/ctr_param_chain.bend` (600 parameters, 600 levels, taken from #2037 with its comment corrected) checks the output. It prints `600` on main too, so it guards correctness, not speed.

title: fix(verdict): name the definition on translation stack errors
body:
The 16-line example in #1984 passes source checking, then overflows during BendTT translation. The CLI reports a stack error without a definition name. This change adds the active definition name while retaining the host error message. The example now reports:

```text
Error: BendTT: while translating p: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
```

This addresses the diagnostic request in #1984. It does not fix the translation cycle or close that issue. Root and item emission add context to `RangeError`; an inner error keeps its original definition name. Proof checking, out-of-scope handling, and survey classification stay unchanged. One header paragraph is shorter, with its technical facts retained, to keep `safe.ts` at 23,986 / 24,000 tokens.

The regression uses the real source CLI. It checks source acceptance, `--verdict`, failed export without changing an existing output, an imported definition, and a successful inline-type control. It fails on main and passes with the change.

Validation on main `3c1f0d3a`:

- Regression passes through the source CLI, emitted JavaScript, and a freshly compiled CLI.
- All 252 existing proof, template, and import fixtures keep their export outcomes and diagnostics after output-path normalization. All 159 emitted files are byte-identical.
- Repository gate: 54/54. `git diff --check` passes.
- TypeScript reports the same nine existing diagnostics as main.
- Cluster test, performance, ping, and safe gates were not run.

title: [Usability] Unify import syntax by double-quoting and adhering to URI schemes
body:
### What Bend should do

Besides from importing like:
```python
import ../foo.bend
```
you can also import like:
```python
import "../foo.bend" // defaults to "file" schema
```
OR
```python
import "file:../foo.bend" // functionally identical
```

which should stay for compatibility reasons. Aliases stay identical.

### Why

1 - There's already a precedent to double-quote-imports: that is exactly how effects works right now.
2 - Assuming file-system paths is myopic and gives room to a silent assumption that the file exists or is accessible. With schemas it becomes clear that paths are promises of bytes(whichever way you get them).
3 - Its a more natural way to reference bendhub.
4 - It's EXTREMELY useful to adhere to battle-tested standards. Consider Javascript:: [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/URI/Reference/Schemes). They have (to name a few): data, http(s), ftp, blob, data, ws(s). Prefixing some useful subset of these can give room to, say: allowing the compiler to compile bend strings(instead of a .bend file that necessarily exists on the system), or allowing an import to be provided at compile time(esbuild, bun allows this). This could also enable future "eval" work if that's ever planned.

title: perf(comp): an unfold builds the callee's body once
body:
Constant folding spent half its time on a body it threw away. To unfold a call, `emit_unfold` substituted the folded arguments into the callee's body and walked it only to check that the unfold was allowed, then built the body again inside lets for the arguments the body copies. Both copies are fresh terms, so every node visit missed the memos (`term_spine`, `term_open`, `term_uses`). In `bench/runtime/merkle` the throwaway check was 18,700 node visits, about 15 ms of the 33 ms the fold takes per emit.

## The change

- **The body is built once.** The lets' variables are made first, and the body is built and checked over them. The old check saw each let-bound argument inside the body; the new one looks into a let's value where it meets the let's variable, so it rejects the same arguments (one holding a lambda or a match).
  - Where the two checks can differ, an argument applied as a function in the body, the new check sees that application's arguments as live (a variable has no type to erase them by), so it can only reject more. Rejecting an unfold folds less and is never wrong. No test or bench hits it.
  - The new lets keep the `Many` quantity the old ones had (`let_open` takes it).
- **`term_kids` no longer forces its term.** Its three callers pass a forced one, and `term_force` of a forced term returns it (a forced term is never a bound variable or a literal).
- **The fuel is unchanged:** each unfold is charged its node count before its calls fold, as before.

## Numbers (M4, best of 5–9)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| merkle: time under `emit_fold` (CPU profile, 40 runs) | 32.7 ms | 22.5 ms |
| merkle: emit (`-o main.c`) | 0.120 s | 0.110 s |
| editdist: emit | 0.120 s | 0.109 s |

The other 15 benches move within ±4 ms (noise). merkle and editdist are the ones that fold most, and the two closest to the perf gate's COMPILER limit (1.14x and 1.12x).

## Checks

- Every test's and bench's C and JS is byte-identical to main's (1874 files).
- repo 56/56; `comp.ts` is 65,996 ttok (cap 66,000), with 3 fewer lines.

title: fix(check): an LE compare meets a share cell's class too, and tests for #1984
body:
Fixes #1984.

88a7dfda (on main since 2.0.40) fixed #1984's cycle the same way this PR did: compare writes no value, and two cells found equal join a class through root-to-root links. This PR is now a small follow-up to it, plus tests for the cases this PR's review found.

## The change

`compare_go` checked a pair's class only inside the branch for two filled cells in EQ mode. So when an EQ compare had already linked two cells, a later LE compare of the same cells walked their shared graph as a tree.

Repro (`conversion_shared_cells_le`): `{A == B : Type} & (A -> B)` proved by `({==}, x => x)`, where `A` and `B` are shared graphs, each level `t -> t` of the level below. The `{==}` links the cells in EQ, then `x => x` compares `A` against `B` in LE.

| levels | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.34 s | 0.06 s |
| 26 | 4.20 s | 0.05 s |
| 40 | killed at 30 s | 0.06 s |

Now the class check is `compare_go`'s first test, in either mode. A class only records equalities found in EQ, and EQ implies LE, so using it in LE is sound. At 16 levels, the test makes 9,902 LE compares instead of 140,973.

`cell_class` now also halves the path it walks: each step relinks a cell to its grandparent, so a class's chain stays short even though a union has no rank. `bend.ts` grows by 41 tokens (45,714 of its 48k cap), and tsc reports the same errors as on main. bend.ts is human-written, so this needs a maintainer's review.

## Tests

All pass on main except where noted:

- `conversion_shared_cells_no_cycle`: #1984's program. Before 88a7dfda it overflowed the stack under `--verdict`.
- `conversion_shared_cells_no_cycle_check`: #1984's program plus `{c == A{}}`. The checker used to hang.
- `conversion_shared_cells_self_value`: `{S{pr(c)} == c} & {c == S{Z{}}}`. Copying the evaluated value instead of `lhs.v` would still make a cycle.
- `conversion_shared_cells_three_way`: three equal let-chains compared pairwise, so the last pair is two links from its root. A one-hop lookup went exponential here.
- `conversion_shared_cells_le`: the LE case above. Main walks it as a tree.
- `conversion_shared_cells_once`'s header now says cells join a class instead of becoming one.

**Limit:** none of these tests can catch a slowdown by timing out. BendTT doesn't share cells yet (#1555): `--verdict` takes 20.7 s at 20 levels of the LE test and runs out of fuel at 20 levels of the three-way one. But a tree walk only passes the test gate's 5 s alarm past about 28 levels. So the tests use 16 and 18 levels. They check correctness and that the kernel agrees, not speed.

**Not covered, and older than both fixes:** a shared type compared only in LE, with no EQ compare first, is still walked as a tree, because only EQ creates links. Trying EQ first for two filled cells in LE fixed it, but a failed attempt isn't remembered, so the LE walk retried it at every level: a type built by passing a growing `Nat -> t` through an argument, compared against one ending in `Type` instead of `Data`, went from 0.06 s to 1.04 s at 4,000 levels. That was reverted. A real fix needs a memo of failed attempts, which is out of scope here.

## Gates

- repo 56/56, test 1844/1844, ping 83/83.
- perf 124/124. Checker benches are within noise of main.
- safe (`tests`): 1176 agree, 148 u, 530 bend2 rejects, 3 out of scope, 0 false rejects, 0 timeouts. That's main's 1171 plus the 5 new tests.

title: perf(safe): a constructor records its datatype, and ctr_term skips its last field's rest
body:
Split out of #2048. That PR fixes the checker on #1997's chain; this one fixes the `--verdict` translation (`safe.ts`) on the same shape.

**Cause.** On a constructor chain `S{S{..Z{}}}` against `N<Unit, ..>` with `k` parameters, `ctr_term` built the result type `N<A0, .., Ak>` twice per value. Building it costs `k` parameter lookups through the env (a `List`), so `k²` per value:
1. `book_fam` unbound the constructor's whole telescope only to read the datatype's name off that result type.
2. The field loop applied the last field's `B`, which only rebuilds the result type, and dropped it.

**What.**
1. The parser stores the datatype's name on the constructor (`Ctr.f`, set in `parse_book`, the only place a `Ctr` is made), and `book_fam` returns it.
2. `ctr_term` stops before the last field's `B`, as check-ctr does in #2048.
3. With the name stored, `book_fam` only did a second lookup and an unchecked cast, so it is gone: check-ctr's error paths, `ctr_term`, `ctr_build` and `c_ids` read `.f` from the lookup they already do, and `row_val` and `ctr_adt` read it instead of unbinding the constructor's type when there is no expected type.

**Numbers.** `bun bend2/main.ts ex.bend -o ex.bendtt`, minus the `--check-only` time, on the issue's chain (`k = d = n`):

| n | main | this PR | with #2048 too |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 800 | 1.5 s | 0.5 s | |
| 2400 | 154 s | 52 s | 0.3 s |

title: fix(comp): a fold reads an argument's liveness by its position
body:
Follow-up to #2051 (its review's finding 3). Folding asked whether a call's argument is live by looking its term up among the spine's live arguments, which matches by object identity:

- `emit_fold_args` and `emit_unfold`'s lets used `m.args.includes(m.all[i])`, so one term object at an erased position and at a live one counted as live at both: the erased one would be folded and let-bound too.
- `emit_unfold`'s `hit` used `fs[m.all.indexOf(a)]`, which reads the first position holding that object, so it could judge a live argument by an erased one's value. It was also quadratic in the arity.

`term_spine` already computes `live` per position; the `Spine` now keeps it, and the three read it by position.

**Reach:** no test or bench reaches the difference, and I couldn't build one. After substitution a repeated argument is a constant, a variable or an unfold's let variable (#2051), which fold to themselves and are never let-bound, so the old and new code agree. It would take the checker putting one non-constant term object at an erased and a live position. So this is a correctness fix for a case nothing hits today, plus one way to ask liveness instead of three.

`anf`'s spine walk (`const on = m.args.includes(f.x)`) has the same identity test; it's left as is, since reading it by position there costs about 20 tokens.

`probe_of` no longer forces its term, which pays for the new field: its three callers pass forced ones (`emit_args` strips its arguments, `emit_expr` peels with `ty_peel`, `emit_clo` passes unbound probes), and forcing a forced term returns it.

## Checks

- Every test's and bench's C and JS is byte-identical to main's (1874 files).
- repo 56/56; `comp.ts` is 66,000 ttok (cap 66,000).

title: Persistent module-level compilation artifacts
body:
### What Bend should do

Bend should support emitting reusable, module-scoped, intermediate representations before whole-program optimization and C emission.

Unchanged modules should be loaded from these artifacts rather than checked and lowered again. Artifacts should include the interfaces and implementation information needed for cross-module checking, template expansion, etc.

The final build would combine the reachable module artifacts, perform whole-program optimization, and emit a single C file.


### Why

Bend’s C backend currently emits a single whole-program C file. In on of my projects, an application imports hundreds of modules across 6–7 repositories. Even with my fork’s partial type-checking support, an end-to-end build takes over an hour. 

This obviously will not reduce the time it takes to do whole-program optimization but I wager that is not the cause of the current performance bottleneck.

title: Two terms written alike convert before either unfolds
body:
Addresses the problem in #1232. It replaces #1832, which is now closed. This is a fresh, smaller change, built from main.

### The problem

A conversion whose sides become equal only after a def unfolds evaluates both copies of a closed call:

```
def big() -> Nat: Nat.pow(2n, 30n)
def boxed() -> Box: Box{big()}
def boxed_eq() -> {Box{big()} == boxed() : Box}: {==}
```

The rigid pass fails on the whole goal, because `boxed()` does not unfold there. The full pass then unfolds `boxed()` to `Box{big()}` and evaluates `big()` on both sides. That is 2^30 `Succ` cells each, and it overflows the stack. The cheap question, "are these two written alike?", is never asked again after the first unfold.

### The change

Before the full pass steps a pair whose left side may be a call (an `App`, a `Ref` or a cell), `compare_go` compares the two sides as written with `term_compare_raw`.

- **What `term_compare_raw` is:** a walk through cells and annotations over vars, refs, literals, applications and constructors. It never unfolds and never steps, so it costs at most the size of the terms. Two share cells it finds alike become one, as in #1151. A walk without steps cannot build a cycle.
- **Soundness:** equal as written implies definitionally equal. Anything else falls through to the unchanged comparison. Two calls of one def with different numbers of arguments are not written alike (`_arity.bend`).
- **Bounded cost:** a walk that fails spends one unit of fuel, and only for that pair's own walk. The fuel comes back when the pair returns. So a path asks at most 10 times, and its siblings keep their fuel.
  - This is Agda's `--syntactic-equality=FUEL`, scoped per path like smalltt's approximate conversion ("rigid N shots").
  - The answer did not depend on the bound: 3 and 30 gave the same results as 10 on the repros and on the adversarial cases.

### Measurements

Main is d869d086. `bend.ts` goes from 45,452 to 45,974 ttok (+522).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| repros (`tests/check/conversion_call_after_unfold*.bend`, 8 files) | 3 overflow, 1 timeout | all check |
| 2,486 files (`tests/`, `demos/`, `bench/checker`, a hub store) | | identical output |
| 112 bend-collections roots at 512b7364 (`prove.py --list`) | 1,241 s | identical output, 1,031 s (0.83x) |
| smallest stack where `f64ofnat` checks | 4,918 KB | 3,028 KB |
| `compute_1600`, CPU, min of 9, local | 0.893 s | 0.895 s |
| cluster perf gate, `compute_1600` | 0.499 s | 0.498 s |
| other checker benches | | within noise |

- **The four f64 roots** that overflowed on #1832 pass here. Their smallest stack is the same as main's within measurement noise (±10% from JIT tiering), except `f64ofnat`, which needs less.
- **The pathological cases from #1832's first version** match main: `add(a, b) == add(b, a)` at n = 3000 takes 0.11 s, and the 22-deep `z(n) + z(n)` chain takes 8.3 s against 8.5 s.
- **Gates:**
  - repo 56/56, ping 83/83, test 1845/1845.
  - perf 123/124, the same as main in the same session.
  - safe on `tests/`: agree 1175, false reject 0, timeout 0.

### What else I measured, and why not that

- **Comparing the arguments with the rigid pass (#1832's route) has no bound.** The rigid pass does not unfold defs, but it still runs betas and matches. Five secp256k1 roots went from 15–24 s to over 300 s, even when each path asked only once.
- **Lean's choice, every call pair with a failure memo:** `compute_1600` at 1.10–1.16x.
- **Fuel shared by the whole conversion:** twelve sibling fields that are equal only after a step use it up (`_wide.bend`).
- **Turning a def off on a path after it fails:** one extra frame per def, and the f64 roots overflowed.
- **Plain smalltt (once per path, then fully):** costs nothing, but misses `_near` and `_type`.
- **Known limit:** 20 call pairs nested on one path that differ as written, with the copy below all of them, still evaluate the copy. A credit that grows with the conversion's own work handled that case, at 1.05x on `compute_1600`.

Lean's kernel, Rocq's `conversion.ml`, smalltt and Agda's `SyntacticEquality` were the references for these options.

### Not in this PR

- **Two copies of a very deep value** (`nat(100000n) == nat2(100000n)`) still overflow, as on main. That is the depth of the recursion, not this problem.
- **#1151's cell merge** `rhs.v = lhs.v` loops when the left cell's value mentions the right one, as main does on a short existential example. A union-find on cells fixes it, and I can send it separately.

title: perf(check): a + binder reads its type's kind off the head
body:
Alternative to #2020, for #1940's family: the same cases, plus the ones #2020's fast path leaves exponential (families whose kind reads a quantity, `List<&2, ..>`, `Either<&2, &2, ..>`, aliases).

## Cause

infer-app substitutes the surface argument into `B(a)`, so `tag(q => ..)` has type `Tag<q => ..>`, lambda included. A `+` let, and a `+` lambda binder, show that type is Data with `term_check_kind`, which checks the whole type, and so the lambda, again. Its result is discarded: the check only answers "is it Data". Nested, that is 2ⁿ.

## Change

The type at both sites is one bend2 already built and checked (a value's inferred type, a goal's domain). So `term_check_bound` reads its kind through its head's declared type, without checking any argument:

- a family `D<xs>`: D's declared kind, through its telescope
- a def application `F(xs)` (an alias): F's declared type, through its telescope
- an equation: Data

An argument enters a telescope only when it is a quantity literal (`&2` in `List<&2, A>`); any other argument is a fresh variable. So nothing unchecked is ever normalized, and a malformed argument from a signature below the use can't loop. A kind that reads a non-literal argument comes out open, and misses.

The reading is compared against `Kind(q)` (with `@unsafe`'s `+` → `&1`). A miss, or any other head, takes `main`'s `term_check_kind`, so every refusal keeps its message, and `@unsafe` `+` lambdas keep `main`'s domain check. The other heads hold no substituted lambda, so the full check costs what it does on `main`.

+24 / −2 in `bend.ts`.

## Measurements

`--check-only`, nested `+` lets:

| type | depth | `main` | #2020 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Tag<f>` (Data) | 30 | timeout | 0.03 s | 0.02 s |
| `Tag<&2, f>`, kind `Kind(a)` | 20 | 0.91 s | 1.25 s | 0.02 s |
| `List<&2, Tag<f>>` | 20 | 1.57 s | 2.09 s | 0.06 s |
| alias `TagD(f)` (`-> Data`) | 22 | — | 3.68 s | 0.02 s (30 deep) |

`Either<&2, &2, Tag<f>, Nat>` and `Sigma<Nat, n => Tag<f>>`: 0.06 s at depth 30.

## Tests

#2020's 13 tests, unchanged, plus:

- `lam_plus_grade_nested_type`: 30-deep `+` lambdas at `List<&2, Tag<f>>`.
- `let_plus_grade_affine_refused`: a `+` let at `List<&1, ..>`, refused with `main`'s message.

`bun gates/test.ts` 1852 / 1852, `repo.ts` 56 / 56.

Not run: `gates/safe.ts`, which needs a built `.tmp/bendtt` and the gate nodes. The kernel is unchanged.

## Limitations

- **`--verdict` is still exponential on nested `+` lets.** The time is the kernel's, not `safe.ts`'s: emitting the BendTT is 0.06 s at every depth, while `bendtt` alone takes 0.22 s / 0.89 s / 3.69 s at depths 16 / 18 / 20. Its let rule has the same cause, and skipping the check there needs a regularity lemma in `bendtt.lean` (63.0k / 64k). `let_plus_nested_type` stays at 20 deep for that.
- **Same trust as #1952.** A `+` binder no longer checks its type's arguments, so a malformed type reaching it from a def signature below a dead use enters the context unchecked, as for ordinary binders since #1952.

title: fix(demos): pure_hvm5_mini's laws import a pure core, so its proofs check
body:
Fixes #1989 (the last of its four demos; #1990 and #2039 fixed the other three).

## Problem

On `main`, `bend PROOF.bend` in `demos/pure_hvm5_mini` prints SOME PROOFS FAIL with `35 defs rely on unsafe or foreign code`. `LAWS.bend` imports `main.bend`, and `main.bend` holds six `@unsafe` defs: the parser (`term`, `defs`), the collector (`free_run`), the copier (`inst`), the loop (`run`) and its driver (`drive`). The other 29 call them. No law uses any of them.

## Fix

This is the split from the issue, not fuel. `run`/`drive` normalize an arbitrary program, which need not halt, so the `@unsafe` marks there are accurate. Fuel would change what the demo computes.

- **`core.bend`** (new): the transitive closure of what `LAWS.bend`/`PROOF.bend` name: `Term`, `Ws`, the lexer and cursor (`chr_*`, `str_*`, `name_code`, `word_cat`, `opens`), the run words (`run_word`, `run_push`, `run_pop`, `bit0`), the printer (`nam*`, `bits_*`, `run_len`, `term_show`), `pick`, `alphabet`, `lam`, `book_depth`. Defs and comments moved verbatim, in their original order and sections.
- **`main.bend`**: `import ./core.bend as C`, and the parser, evaluator and `main` name those through `C.` (212 lines, mostly `C.Term` and `Term` constructors). Apart from that and a note in the header, nothing changed.
- **`LAWS.bend`, `PROOF.bend`**: `import ./core.bend as Hvm`. The laws and proofs themselves are unchanged.

## Checked

- `bend PROOF.bend`: ALL PROOFS CHECK, and also with `--verdict`.
- `bend main.bend`: `&S{#0{()},#1{()}}` and `- Itrs: 79 interactions`, the same as on `main`.
- `bend main.bend --check-only` still lists the six `@unsafe` defs and their dependents, which is expected for an evaluator.
- `gates/repo.ts`: PASS 56 / 56. `core.bend` fits the demos allow rule. No other gate reads `demos/`.

title: Base: the U32 bit facts an Array law on perfect trees needs
body:
# Base: the U32 bit facts an Array law on perfect trees needs

`tensor-array` proves `get_after_set` and `get_other_set` outside Base (bendlang/bend#1934), and the last one takes
`ASet.Apart` as its hypothesis: the write's descent and the read's descent part at some node. On a perfect tree of
`2^d` leaves, `Apart` holds exactly when the two masked indices differ, and supplying that needs four facts about
`U32`: masked index, `shr(2^d)`, the branch bit, and the subtraction bound. Base states only `U32.add_comm`.

The lemmas that do not need the missing pieces are proved outside Base, verified by the Lean kernel
(`lean 4.34.0`), in `u32_bits.bend` (local draft):
- `shr_shl`
- `ctop_eq`
- `top_shl`
- `shl_p2`
plus the helper defs they rest on (`ctop`, `top`, `init`, `zeros`, `p2`, `shl_put_zeros`, `shl_put`, `top_put`,
`top_cons`, `init_put_eq`). The canonical `2^d` is `p2(d, n)`: `d` zeros, a one, then zeros, with
`shl(p2(d,n)) == p2(d+1,n)`.

Reproduce:

    PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH bend u32_bits.bend --verdict

## What is still missing, and why it belongs here

1. **`Nat.add(d, Nat.sub(32, d)) == 32`** for `d <= 32`. `top(p2(d,32)) == False` for `d <= 30` closes as
   `Q(K,d) = top(p2(d, d+K)) == False` by induction on `d` (the step is `p2(d+1,n) == F :: p2(d,n-1)` and the top of a
   cons is the top of its tail), but instantiating at the 32-bit width needs `K = 32-d`. Base states no `Nat.sub` law.
2. **`Word.and`, `Word.sub`, `Word.cmp`.** The mask fact (`and(j, 2^d - 1) == j` for `j < 2^d`) needs
   `sub(2^d, 1) == ones(d)` with borrow, a mask law, and `cmp` as unsigned comparison; the subtraction bound needs
   subtraction without borrow. Base proves `Word.adc` and `Word.add_comm` only.

The six lemmas above are offered as they stand: they are the part of the library that does not need the missing
pieces, and they make the remaining work a matter of `Nat` and word arithmetic rather than tree induction.

## The program

```bend
# DRAFT, local only (never committed): the four U32 bit facts bend-ml#26 needs, as a library.
#
#   PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH bend .local/u32_bits.bend --verdict
#
# ASet.Apart on a perfect tree of 2^d leaves needs, from ASet/get_other_set:
#   1. J(j, 2^d) == j                     when j < 2^d        (the mask keeps the low d bits)
#   2. shr(2^(d+1)) == 2^d
#   3. Z(j, 2^d) == bit d-1 of j
#   4. j with bit d-1 set: sub(j, 2^(d-1)) < 2^(d-1)
#
# Base has only U32.add_comm, so each needs Word (little-endian bit list) lemmas first.
#
# Proved: A and B.
#   A. shr(shl(w)) == ctop(w)      shifting up and back down clears the top bit
#   B. ctop(w) == w when top(w) == False
# Still to prove:
#   C. top(2^d) == False for d <= 30. It is the SAME statement as fact 2: A gives
#      ctop(w) == shr(shl(w)), so "ctop(pow2 d) == pow2 d" is "shr(pow2(d+1)) == pow2 d".
#      Neither is a shortcut for the other; both need the canonical pattern of shln(1, d),
#      because shl moves the single set bit. Done toward it: init/init_shl (dropping the top
#      bit commutes with shifting up) and shl_put. Note init_p and shl.put are the same
#      recursion; they differ only at length 0.
#      Also done: top_shl (top(shl(w)) == top(init(w))), via top_put/init_put_eq/top_cons.
#      Also done: the canonical word p2(d, n) = d zeros, one, then zeros (matching d first,
#      then n, avoids the match-order trap that blocks the natural two-way recursion), and
#      shl_p2: shl(p2(d,n)) == p2(d+1,n), which is what makes 2^d structural.
#      Also done: top_zeros and top_p2 — top(p2(d, d+2+j)) == False, i.e. the fact for every
#      word whose length exceeds the one's position by at least 2, by induction on d.
#      What remains of C is only the instantiation at the 32-bit width: top(32, p2(d,32)) needs
#      d + (2+j) == 32, i.e. the size bound d <= 30 that belongs to the array law (a U32 holds
#      2^d, so d <= 31; the top bit is the d = 31 edge). No standalone bit lemma can supply it.
#   D. the mask fact, E. Z is bit d-1, F. the subtraction bound, after C.
#
# The measured oracle these unlock is tensor-array/tests/apart.bend: 21,590 pairs through
# depth 7, 0 failures (2026-11-05).
import Base

import Base

def ctop_p(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> Word(1n+p):
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          WCon{False{}, WNil{}}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          WCon{b, ctop_p(q, b0, tq)}

def ctop(n: Nat, w: Word(n)) -> Word(n):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      WNil{}
    case 1n+p:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          ctop_p(p, b, t)

def top_p(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> Bool:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      b
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          top_p(q, b0, tq)

def top(n: Nat, w: Word(n)) -> Bool:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      False{}
    case 1n+p:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          top_p(p, b, t)

# LEMMA A: shifting a word up and back down clears its top bit
def pad_put(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> {Word.shr.pad(p, Word.shl.put(p, b, t)) == ctop_p(p, b, t) : Word(1n+p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          %pad_put(q, b0, tq) : {WCon{b, Word.shr.pad(q, Word.shl.put(q, b0, tq))} == WCon{b, _} : Word(1n+p)}
          {==}

law shr_shl:
  for +n: Nat
  for w: Word(n)
  {Word.shr(n, Word.shl(n, w)) == ctop(n, w) : Word(n)}

def shr_shl(n, w):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      {==}
    case 1n+p:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          %pad_put(p, b, t) : {Word.shr.pad(p, Word.shl.put(p, b, t)) == _ : Word(1n+p)}
          {==}

# LEMMA B: a word whose top bit is False is its own top-cleared copy
def ctop_p_eq(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p), h: {False{} == top_p(p, b, t) : Bool}) -> {ctop_p(p, b, t) == WCon{b, t} : Word(1n+p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          Equal.sym(Word(1n), WCon{b, WNil{}}, WCon{False{}, WNil{}},
            Equal.cong(Bool, Word(1n), x => WCon{x, WNil{}}, b, False{}, Equal.sym(Bool, False{}, b, h)))
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          Equal.cong(Word(1n+q), Word(1n+(1n+q)), x => WCon{b, x},
            ctop_p(q, b0, tq), WCon{b0, tq}, ctop_p_eq(q, b0, tq, h))

law ctop_eq:
  for +n: Nat
  for w: Word(n)
  for h: {False{} == top(n, w) : Bool}
  {ctop(n, w) == w : Word(n)}

def ctop_eq(n, w, h):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      match w:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+p:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          ctop_p_eq(p, b, t, h)

# drop the most significant bit
def init_p(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> Word(p):
  match p:
    case 0n:
      WNil{}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          WCon{b, init_p(q, b0, tq)}

def init(+p: Nat, w: Word(1n+p)) -> Word(p):
  match w:
    case WCon{b, t}:
      init_p(p, b, t)

# the p-shape: init_p(p, b, shl.put(p, b0, t)) == shl.put(p, b, init_p(p, b0, t))
def init_put(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +b0: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> {init_p(p, b, Word.shl.put(p, b0, t)) == Word.shl.put(p, b, init_p(p, b0, t)) : Word(p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b1, tq}:
          %init_put(q, b0, b1, tq) : {WCon{b, init_p(q, b0, Word.shl.put(q, b1, tq))} == WCon{b, _} : Word(1n+q)}
          {==}

# shl(p, w) is shl.put(p, False, w): both are False at the head and the bits shifted in
def shl_put(+p: Nat, w: Word(p)) -> {Word.shl(p, w) == Word.shl.put(p, False{}, w) : Word(p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match w:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          {==}

# LEMMA C1: dropping the top bit commutes with shifting up (in shl.put form, which is
# what init_put gives; shl_put converts when shl itself is needed)
def init_shl(+p: Nat, w: Word(1n+p)) -> {init(p, Word.shl(1n+p, w)) == Word.shl.put(p, False{}, init(p, w)) : Word(p)}:
  match w:
    case WCon{b, t}:
      init_put(p, False{}, b, t)

# init_p and shl.put are the same recursion; only length 0 differs in the operands
def init_put_eq(+p: Nat, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> {init_p(p, b, t) == Word.shl.put(p, b, t) : Word(p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b0, tq}:
          %init_put_eq(q, b0, tq) : {WCon{b, init_p(q, b0, tq)} == WCon{b, _} : Word(1n+q)}
          {==}

# top of a word is top_p with an ignored head
def top_cons(+p: Nat, w: Word(p)) -> {top(p, w) == top_p(p, False{}, w) : Bool}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match w:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          {==}

# the top bit of shl.put and of init_p agree: they are the same recursion
def top_put(+p: Nat, +c: Bool, +b: Bool, +t: Word(p)) -> {top_p(p, c, Word.shl.put(p, b, t)) == top_p(p, c, init_p(p, b, t)) : Bool}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match t:
        case WNil{}:
          {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match t:
        case WCon{b1, tq}:
          %top_put(q, b, b1, tq) : {top_p(q, b, Word.shl.put(q, b1, tq)) == _ : Bool}
          {==}

law top_shl:
  for +p: Nat
  for w: Word(1n+p)
  {top(1n+p, Word.shl(1n+p, w)) == top(p, init(p, w)) : Bool}

def top_shl(p, w):
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          match t:
            case WNil{}:
              {==}
    case 1n+q:
      match w:
        case WCon{b, t}:
          match t:
            case WCon{b0, tq}:
              %top_put(q, b, b0, tq) : {top_p(q, b, Word.shl.put(q, b0, tq)) == _ : Bool}
              {==}


def zeros(+n: Nat) -> Word(n):
  match n:
    case 0n:
      WNil{}
    case 1n+p:
      WCon{False{}, zeros(p)}

# 2^d as a word of length n: d zeros, a one, then zeros
def p2(+d: Nat, +n: Nat) -> Word(n):
  match d:
    case 0n:
      match n:
        case 0n:
          WNil{}
        case 1n+q:
          WCon{True{}, zeros(q)}
    case 1n+p:
      match n:
        case 0n:
          WNil{}
        case 1n+q:
          WCon{False{}, p2(p, q)}

# shl.put(p, b, zeros(p)) is b followed by zeros
def shl_put_zeros(+p: Nat, +b: Bool) -> {Word.shl.put(1n+p, b, zeros(1n+p)) == WCon{b, zeros(p)} : Word(1n+p)}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      {==}
    case 1n+q:
      %shl_put_zeros(q, False{}) : {WCon{b, Word.shl.put(1n+q, False{}, zeros(1n+q))} == WCon{b, _} : Word(1n+(1n+q))}
      {==}

law shl_p2:
  for +p: Nat
  for +n: Nat
  {Word.shl(n, p2(p, n)) == p2(1n+p, n) : Word(n)}

def shl_p2(p, n):
  match p:
    case 0n:
      match n:
        case 0n:
          {==}
        case 1n+q:
          match q:
            case 0n:
              {==}
            case 1n+r:
              Equal.cong(Word(1n+r), Word(1n+(1n+r)), x => WCon{False{}, x},
                Word.shl.put(1n+r, True{}, zeros(1n+r)), WCon{True{}, zeros(r)},
                shl_put_zeros(r, True{}))
    case 1n+r:
      match n:
        case 0n:
          {==}
        case 1n+q:
          Equal.cong(Word(q), Word(1n+q), x => WCon{False{}, x},
            Word.shl.put(q, False{}, p2(r, q)), p2(1n+r, q),
            Equal.trans(Word(q), Word.shl.put(q, False{}, p2(r, q)), Word.shl(q, p2(r, q)), p2(1n+r, q),
              Equal.sym(Word(q), Word.shl(q, p2(r, q)), Word.shl.put(q, False{}, p2(r, q)), shl_put(q, p2(r, q))),
              shl_p2(r, q)))

# the top of a nonempty all-zero word is False
def top_zeros(+p: Nat) -> {top(1n+p, zeros(1n+p)) == False{} : Bool}:
  match p:
    case 0n:
      {==}
    case 1n+q:
      top_zeros(q)

# C, in the form that needs no width: d zeros, a one, then 2+k zeros, so the top is False
law top_p2:
  for +j: Nat
  for +d: Nat
  {top(Nat.add(d, Nat.add(2n, j)), p2(d, Nat.add(d, Nat.add(2n, j)))) == False{} : Bool}

def top_p2(j, d):
  match d:
    case 0n:
      %top_zeros(1n+j) : {top(Nat.add(0n, Nat.add(2n, j)), p2(0n, Nat.add(0n, Nat.add(2n, j)))) == _ : Bool}
      {==}
    case 1n+r:
      Equal.trans(Bool,
        top_p(Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)), False{}, p2(r, Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)))),
        top(Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)), p2(r, Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)))),
        False{},
        Equal.sym(Bool, top(Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)), p2(r, Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)))),
          top_p(Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)), False{}, p2(r, Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)))),
          top_cons(Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j)), p2(r, Nat.add(r, Nat.add(2n, j))))),
        top_p2(j, r))
```

title: perf(main): the verdict skips its walk set on a book with no promise
body:
`book_promises` (the `--verdict`/default check verdict) built `own`, the deduplicated `book.order` outside Base, before its early return. So every book with no `@unsafe` or foreign def paid for a `Set` over all its defs and then threw it away. This PR collects the two root lists (`@unsafe`, foreign effects) in one pass over the tlds and builds `own` only after the early return.

Found while profiling why `generics_3200`'s checker cell sits at 1.12–1.21× its pin. Most of that growth is the parser; this is the part in `main.ts`.

**Measurements (local, min of 9 runs)**

| bench | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| generics_3200 | 0.399 s | 0.393 s |
| compute_1600 | 0.513 s | 0.503 s |
| defs_12800 | 0.315 s | 0.313 s |
| proofs_3200 | 0.819 s | 0.817 s |
| trees_400 | 0.623 s | 0.622 s |

`book_promises` itself drops from 6.5 ms to about 2 ms on generics_3200.

**Checks**

title: perf(parse): an operator is looked up by its first character, and a dotted name is checked by its dots
body:
> **This PR edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which AGENTS.md marks as human-written.** It was opened at Nicolas's request, as a proposal for the file's owner to review, rewrite or close.

Two hot spots in the parser, found while profiling why the `generics_3200` checker cell sits at 1.12–1.21× its pin. Base plays no part: none of the checker benches imports Base, and swapping `base.bend` for the pin's version or an empty file leaves the time unchanged.

1. **Operator lookup (`parse_term_ops`).** After every term the parser sliced the next three characters and shortened the slice until `INFIX` knew it. At most positions no operator starts, so that was three slices and three missed lookups each time: about 29 ms of generics_3200, the parser's hottest lines (the pin's operator search took about 13 ms). `INFIX_BY_HEAD` now lists the `INFIX` keys by first character, longest first: the parser reads the next character, tries only the keys it heads with `startsWith` (no slices), and a term ends at once when it heads none, end of input included. A new operator must be added there too.
2. **Name check (`parse_lexeme`).** Every name was tested against the whole-name regex `^[A-Za-z_]\w*(\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*$`. The loop before it only consumes letters, digits, `_` and `.` after a head character, so a name breaks the words-joined-by-dots rule exactly when a dot is not followed by a letter or `_` (`foo.`, `a..b`, `Vec.2d`). The check is now `k.includes(".") && /\.(?![A-Za-z_])/.test(k)`: names without a dot never reach a regex, and the regex says the rule directly. It agrees with the old regex on every name the loop can produce up to 4 characters (14.1M names).

Both changes keep the parser's behaviour: the first picks the longest key that matches, as the old loop did, and returns exactly where it would have shrunk to `""`; the second rejects exactly the names the old regex rejected.

**Checker benches (local, min of 9 runs)**

| bench | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| generics_3200 | 0.397 s | 0.380 s |
| defs_12800 | 0.316 s | 0.288 s |
| proofs_3200 | 0.820 s | 0.772 s |
| compute_1600 | 0.515 s | 0.513 s |
| trees_400 | 0.631 s | 0.625 s |

On the cluster, generics_3200 read 1.09× in a verbose perf run under full gate load (it read 1.12–1.21× on main). Together with #2060 it should land about 1.03×.

**Checks**
- `tests/parse` and `tests/check` (458 files) print identical output, error messages included.
- `INFIX_BY_HEAD` holds exactly the 23 `INFIX` keys, each under its first character, longest first.
- `bend.ts` 45425 → 45539 ttok (cap 48000).
- Gates (`_run.ts`, 3 runs): repo 56/56; ping 81/83, failing 2 BendHub publish checks, as on main; test 1831/1838, failing 7 io/gfx tests with `Permission denied`, as on main: stale `/tmp/bend_io_*` files owned by another user on cluster nodes 58 and 72–78; perf 117–119/124, and main gives 118/124 on the same cluster at the same time: merkle and nbody's compile and GPU cells (1.23–1.54× on both) and noisy SEQ-CPU cells. title: perf(parse): field names, array updates, namespaces and later match parameters are found without rescans
body:
> **This PR edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which AGENTS.md marks as human-written.** It was opened at Nicolas's request, as a proposal for the file's owner to review, rewrite or close.

Three small fixes from the complexity issues, each a few lines, none changing what the parser builds.

- **#2005: field names.** `parse_tele` rejected a duplicate field by comparing it with every earlier field (`tele.some`). A `Set` of the names seen now answers it: O(n) for n fields instead of O(n²).
- **#2022: array updates and operator namespaces.**
  - `term_write` collected every argument of a group's call to test whether it is a four-argument `Array.set`, once in each enclosing group. It now follows at most five links: a fifth already rules the form out.
  - `parse_term_ns` read the namespace type's head again at every operator it renamed. Its callers now read the head once and pass it in.
- **#2046 (the match-lowering part only): matching a later parameter.** When the matched variable was the k-th parameter, `match_flatten` wrapped one parameter at a time, searching and copying the parameter list again at each step. It now finds the parameter once and wraps the k parameters before it in one pass. The lambdas come out the same and in the same order, and the skipped steps could never take another branch: the only test before them does not depend on which parameter is first.

The rest of #2022 and #2046, and the other complexity issues, need larger changes. The `parse_var` scope scan from #2046 comes in a separate PR.

**Load times (in-process `book_load`, best of 12, machine under load)**

| program | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| a call of 2000 arguments inside 2000 groups (#2022) | 91–100 ms | 12–22 ms |
| a constructor with 4000 fields (#2005) | 142–237 ms | 23–39 ms |
| a match on the last of 2000 parameters (#2046) | 28–30 ms | 10–11 ms |

**Checks**
- Every `.bend` file under `tests/` (1851 files) prints the same output with `--check-only` as on main, error messages included. Among them, 19 tests use `x[i] <- v`, 234 use namespaced operators, and 16 hit the match-lowering errors.
- `bend.ts` 45508 → 45590 ttok (cap 48000).
- Gates (`_run.ts`): repo 56/56, ping 83/83. Test 1833/1838 fails only io/gfx tests with `Permission denied` from stale `/tmp/bend_io_*` files on cluster nodes, as on main. Perf 119–121/124 fails the same cluster cells as main does today: merkle and nbody, compile and GPU time. Two earlier runs hit the 30 s cap while the local machine sat at load 20–28; ping passed 83/83 on its own in 8 s.

title: comp.ts: drop a dead pread binding, an unused ALC row and a redundant park case
body:
Three runtime simplifications in `bend2/comp.ts` (65,994 → 65,977 ttok). Each removes something nothing uses or a case the general path already covers.

- **JS `io_sys` no longer binds `pread`.** Its only user was the old `effs/file_read.js`, which moved to `fs.readvSync` in #1881. No effect, test, demo or the CLI calls it. `read` stays: `guide/EFFECTS.md` documents it as part of `io_sys()` for user effects. `file_read_no_ffi.bend`'s comment now says io_sys binds `read` and once bound `pread`.
- **`ALC[CUBE_T + 1]` becomes `ALC[CUBE_T]`.** The extra row was for the old `ALC[1 + arg]` indexing. Since #1269 the main thread uses `ALC[0]` and the pool workers use `ALC[1 .. pool_size - 1]`, and `pool_size <= CUBE_T`. The unused 768-byte row goes.
- **`io_park_add` sets `w->prev = w->next->prev`.** The `w->next == w ? w : …` case is redundant: when `w` is the only parked node, the next line, `w->next->prev = w`, writes the same field.

## Verified (on main b5e6b2ef)

- **Emitted output:** stdout, stderr and exit codes match main for every `.bend` under `tests/`, `demos/` and `bench/runtime/` (1,923 files, C and JS). The only differences in the emitted text are these three lines.
- **Clang:** all 930 emitted C programs compile cleanly under clang's unused-function and unused-macro warnings, and the 67 `!` programs under Metal. No runtime function or macro goes unused, apart from CUDA-, Linux- and ObjC-only code, which I checked by hand.
- **tsc:** `comp.ts` type-checks with the same errors as main.
- **Gates:** repo 56/56, test 1838/1838, perf level with main run back to back (121 vs 120 / 124; the machine is noisy).

title: perf(parse): a name finds its binder through an index, not a scan of every local
body:
> **This PR edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which AGENTS.md marks as human-written.** It was opened at Nicolas's request, as a proposal for the file's owner to review, rewrite or close.

The parser part of #2046. `parse_var` looked up a name by walking the scope stack `stk` from the newest binder down. Every use of an outer variable passed all the locals bound after it, and every global name (`Unit`, `U32.add`, …), which is never on the stack, passed all of them. n locals and n uses cost O(n²).

`Parse` now also keeps `idx`: each name's binders on `stk`, newest last. `parse_push` adds to both (`parse_open` and the rewrite binder's hidden `_` go through it), `parse_close` pops both back to the mark, and `parse_var` reads the newest binder of its name directly. `stk` and its length marks stay as they were. The parser has no try/catch backtracking: every binder it opens is closed by `parse_close` before its scope's mark is reused, so `idx` always matches `stk`.

The conversion part of #2046 (`term_higher`'s `list_get`) and its match-lowering part (in #2062) are not in this PR.

**Load times (in-process `book_load`, best of 12)**

| program | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 locals, then 2000 uses of a parameter bound before them (#2046's family) | 36–37 ms | 14 ms |
| 2000 locals, then 2000 uses of a global constructor | 13 ms | 2.6 ms |

On the checker benches the scope lookup (`parse_var`, `parse_open`, `parse_close`) falls from about 8.4 ms to 6.4 ms of parse time per run (CPU profile, 9 runs over generics_3200, defs_12800 and proofs_3200): their defs bind few locals, so the gain there is small.

**Checks** (rebased on #2062, `e75ccac0`)
- Every `.bend` file under `tests/` (1852 files) prints the same output with `--check-only` as on main, error messages included.
- Every runtime bench compiles to byte-identical C on main and on this PR.
- `bend.ts` 45755 → 45826 ttok (cap 48000).
- Gates: repo 56/56. Perf 124/124 in 12 of 15 runs on each side; in the other 3 runs, cold-compiler spikes (1.5–3 s on random benches) hit main and this PR alike.

**Perf gate, 15 paired runs** (main and this PR back to back in each round, alternating which went first; effect = geometric mean of per-round PR/main ratios, bootstrap 95% CI, exact sign-flip test)

| total per run | all 15 rounds | 12 rounds without the spikes |
|---|---|---|
| checker benches (5) | +0.1% [−0.2%, +0.3%], p=0.59 | −0.0% [−0.3%, +0.2%], p=0.74 |
| compiler column (17) | +1.3% [−4.5%, +7.8%], p=0.65 | −0.1% [−1.1%, +0.9%], p=0.80 |
| runtime cells (control: same C) | +0.1% [0.0%, +0.2%], p=0.06 | +0.1% [0.0%, +0.2%], p=0.03 |

No cell differs after a Holm correction. The control's +0.1% is cluster drift, since the binaries are identical, so differences under ~0.2% are below what the gate resolves. The profiled gain on the checker benches (~0.1% of their total) is under that floor. The PR's gain shows in the large-local programs above.

title: fix(formatter): preserve prefix quantities after semicolons
body:
The formatter changes valid `(x = &0; &1)` to `(x = &0; & 1)`, which Bend rejects. A semicolon starts a new body, but the formatter did not include it in `PREFIX_CONTEXT`. Add the missing marker so the existing prefix rule preserves the quantity literal.

Add six cases for `&0`, `&1`, and `&2`, with adjacent and spaced semicolons and trailing comments. The existing test harness checks exact formatting, idempotence, and equal Bend output with default spaces, four spaces, and tabs.

Validation:

- `npm test`: TypeScript build and all 35 formatter/LSP tests pass; none skipped.
- The same tests with the old formatter fail on both exact formatting and actual Bend execution.
- Both affected repository fixtures, `let_dependent_type.bend` and `let_unsafe_dependent_type.bend`, check after formatting.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 56/56 pass. `git diff --check` passes.

title: app_slash_boss_3d: PROOF.bend passes after an edit that lets a paused game's clock run
body:
### What you did

`bend PROOF.bend` in `demos/app_slash_boss_3d`, after editing only `main.bend` and `PROOF.bend`. `LAWS.bend` is unchanged. This is the same gap as #1931 and #1981; it shows now because #2039 made this demo's proofs check.

In `main.bend`, `Game.rest` lets the clock run in a pause, and `Game.steps` fades the flash without stepping the game (it moves below `Sim.fade`, which it now calls). In `PROOF.bend`, the helper `pause_tick` goes, since it no longer holds, and `Laws.pause_freezes` becomes `{==}`.

<details>
<summary>The edit</summary>

```diff
--- a/demos/app_slash_boss_3d/main.bend
+++ b/demos/app_slash_boss_3d/main.bend
@@ -1062,7 +1062,7 @@
 def Game.rest(+g: Game) -> Game:
   Game{time, held, taps, mode, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast} = g
   +paused = U32.is_eq(mode, 4)
-  Game{R.word(paused, time, (time + 1 : U32)), held, 0, mode,
+  Game{(time + 1 : U32), held, 0, mode,
     Fighter.rest((U32.is_eq(mode, 2) || U32.is_eq(mode, 3)), hero), boss, Sim.dec(flash),
     Game.cape(paused, False{}, cloth, hero, time), Game.garb(paused, garb, boss, time), lens,
     blast}
@@ -1114,19 +1114,16 @@
 # Live.steps runs them), n fades of a countdown, and a frame's events
 # joined.
 
-def Game.steps(n: Nat, +g: Game) -> Game:
-  match n:
-    case 0n:
-      g
-    case 1n+k:
-      Game.steps(k, Game.step(g))
-
 def Sim.fade(n: Nat, +x: U32) -> U32:
   match n:
     case 0n:
       x
     case 1n+k:
       Sim.fade(k, Sim.dec(x))
+
+def Game.steps(n: Nat, +g: Game) -> Game:
+  Game{time, held, taps, mode, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast} = g
+  Game{time, held, taps, mode, hero, boss, Sim.fade(n, flash), cloth, garb, lens, blast}
 
 def Game.cat(a: List<Event>, b: List<Event>) -> List<Event>:
   match a:
--- a/demos/app_slash_boss_3d/PROOF.bend
+++ b/demos/app_slash_boss_3d/PROOF.bend
@@ -20,35 +20,9 @@
 # A pause freezes the world
 # -------------------------
 
-# one tick of a paused game with no key tapped: only the flash fades
-law pause_tick:
-  for +time: U32
-  for +held: U32
-  for +hero: Slash.Fighter
-  for +boss: Slash.Boss
-  for +flash: U32
-  for +cloth: R.Cloth
-  for +garb: Slash.Garb
-  for +lens: Slash.Lens
-  for +blast: Maybe<&2, Slash.Blast>
-  {Slash.Game{time, held, 0, 4, hero, boss, Slash.Sim.dec(flash), cloth, garb, lens, blast}
-    == Slash.Game.step(Slash.Game{time, held, 0, 4, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast})
-    : Slash.Game}
-
-def pause_tick(time, held, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast):
+def Laws.pause_freezes(n, time, held, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast):
   {==}
 
-def Laws.pause_freezes(n, time, held, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast):
-  match n:
-    case 0n:
-      {==}
-    case 1n+k:
-      %pause_tick(time, held, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast)
-        : {Slash.Game.steps(k, _)
-           == Slash.Game{time, held, 0, 4, hero, boss, Slash.Sim.fade(k, Slash.Sim.dec(flash)),
-                cloth, garb, lens, blast} : Slash.Game}
-      Laws.pause_freezes(k, time, held, hero, boss, Slash.Sim.dec(flash), cloth, garb, lens, blast)
-
 # P twice restores the pause state
 # --------------------------------
 
```

</details>

### What happened

On `main` at ae7341dd:

```text
$ bend PROOF.bend
ALL PROOFS import Base
import ./main.bend as Slash

def time_of(g: Slash.Game) -> U32:
  Slash.Game{time, held, taps, mode, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast} = g
  time

def mode_of(g: Slash.Game) -> U32:
  Slash.Game{time, held, taps, mode, hero, boss, flash, cloth, garb, lens, blast} = g
  mode

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  +g0 = Slash.Game.pause(Slash.Game.fresh(0, 1))
  +g3 = Slash.Game.step(Slash.Game.step(Slash.Game.step(g0)))
  IO.print("paused (mode " ++ U32.show(mode_of(g0)) ++ "): time " ++ U32.show(time_of(g0)) ++ ", after 3 ticks: time " ++ U32.show(time_of(g3)))
$ bend PROOF.bend --verdict
ALL PROOFS CHECK
$ bend CHECK.bend
paused (mode 4): time 0, after 3 ticks: time 3
```

On the unedited demo, `CHECK.bend` prints `paused (mode 4): time 0, after 3 ticks: time 0`.

### Why it happens

`pause_freezes` and `esc_quits` measure the game with `Game.steps`, `Sim.fade` and `Game.cat`, which sit in the `# Spec` section of `main.bend` ("What LAWS.bend measures"). Nothing in the game calls them; only `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend` do. So an edit to `main.bend` can change the measure along with the game, and the law still holds. Until #2039, this demo's `PROOF.bend` failed on its `@unsafe` loop, which hid the gap.

### The file

<details>
<summary>CHECK.bend</summary>

```python
CHECK
```

</details>

### A fix, and what it leaves

#2067 moves the three into a `SPEC.bend` with the header the other demos' spec files use, as #1932 did for the sort and sum demos. `steps` still goes through the game's own `Game.step`, which is what `pause_freezes` is about, so `SPEC.bend` imports `main.bend`, as the `SPEC.bend` of `pure_par_sort` and the `BOARD.bend` of `app_win_is_bug_2d` do. `fade` counts down with a `dec` of its own, so an edit to `Sim.dec` can't move it either, and `cat` needs nothing from the game. The edit above then fails at `Laws.pause_freezes`.

What it leaves: the laws pin `Game.step`, not the loop that runs it. If `Live.steps` calls another stepper that runs the clock in a pause, `PROOF.bend` still checks. Pinning that would take a law over `Live.steps`.

### bend version
