title: Defs that tail-call each other in a cycle run as one loop: a head's spin holds the other defs' bodies
body:
**`comp.ts` is 66,233 ttok, 233 over the 66,000 cap** (main 65,981, +252), so `repo-gate` fails until that is settled. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run.

## What it does

Bend has no `if` and cannot match on a local, so a test of a computed value is a helper def that matches it and tail-calls back. Base's `String.contains` is one:

```python
def String.contains.if(t: String, p: String, here: Bool) -> Bool:
  match here:
    case False{}:
      String.contains(t, p)
    case True{}:
      True{}

def String.contains(s, p):
  match s:
    case SNil{}:
      String.is_empty(p)
    case SCon{h, t}:
      String.contains.if(t, p, String.starts_with(SCon{h, t}, p))
```

A def whose only calls to itself are tail calls is flat: the C lane emits it as a spin (a C function with a loop), and a call to it is a C call. A tail-call cycle across two or more defs was never flat, so every def of the cycle was a segment, every call into it from an expression was a frame and a return through the segment table, and every def that called it stopped being flat too (`U32.show`, `Nat.show`, `String.starts_with`, `Map.get.leaf`, ..). The JS lane already runs such a cycle as one loop over its defs' bodies (`$pc`).

Now a cycle is flat too, and runs as one spin, when one of its defs is a **head**: every other def of the cycle is named from one place in the cycle. The head's spin holds each other def's body in place of the one call to it, and a call back to the head is the spin's own jump. `String.contains` is emitted as

```c
INLINE Term spin_String_contains(Env e, THR Term* o, Term r0, Term r1) {
  Term _s_0 = r0;
  Term _p_0 = r1;
  WL_SPIN
    if (term_aux(_s_0) == CID_SNil) {
      ..
    } else {
      ..
      if (spin_String_starts_with(e, _o_1, term_ctr(CID_SCon, _nd_0), _p_0) == 0) {
        return 0;
      }
      if ((u32)_o_1[0] == 0) {          // String.contains.if, in place of its call
        r0 = _f_1;
        r1 = _p_0;
        _s_0 = r0;
        _p_0 = r1;
        WL_AGAIN(spin_String_contains);
      } else {
        term_sink(e, _f_1);
        term_sink(e, _p_0);
        o[0] = 1;
      }
    }
  break;
  }
  return 1;
}
```

where main emitted four segments (`String.contains`, its continuation after `String.starts_with`, `String.starts_with` and `String.starts_with.go`), with a frame pushed, three jumps and a return through the segment table each turn. There is no selector and no new C construct: it is the body a def with a tail call to itself already gets, with the helper's test where its call was.

## The rule

- `loop_of(d)` (already there, for the JS lane) is d's strongly connected component in the graph of tail calls.
- **A head** of a cycle (`loop_head`) is a def such that every other def of the cycle is named exactly once inside the cycle (a count of `Ref`s per pair of defs, kept by `file_book` beside the site counts it already keeps). Then every turn goes through the head, each other def hangs from it by its one call, and the head's spin holds each body once: the spin is as long as the defs together, never longer.
- **A cycle is flat** (`flat_of`) when it has a head, no def of it forks, bangs or calls a def of the cycle in an argument, and every def they call outside the cycle is flat. A cycle that is not flat is compiled exactly as on main.
- **In the spin of a head** (`emit_body`), a tail call to another def of the cycle emits that def's body with the arguments as its parameters, through the path a tail call to a def with one call site already takes in a segment (`emit_args` as for a jump, then `emit_body`). A tail call to the head is the self-jump.
- **A def of the cycle that is no head** (`hop`, below, since `loop` also calls itself) gets a spin that calls the spins of the defs it tail-calls: one C call per entry, the turns run in the head's spin. The chain of such calls follows the one-call tree down from a def to a head, so it is no deeper than the cycle has defs, and no spin of a cycle calls itself.
- A segment (a def of the cycle run as a task, under a fork or a `!`) calls the spin, as it does for any flat def.

```python
@unsafe
def hop(n: Nat) -> Nat:        # no head: loop is named twice in the cycle
  loop(n, False{})             # spin_hop calls spin_loop

@unsafe
def loop(n: Nat, b: Bool) -> Nat:   # the head: hop is named once
  match n:
    case 0n:
      0n
    case 1n+p:
      match b:
        case True{}:
          hop(p)               # hop's body here, its call to loop a jump
        case False{}:
          loop(p, True{})      # a jump
```

## How a cycle can arise, and the count before building

Mutual recursion is refused by the checker (a def may only call one above it), with two ways round: a def may call an unfilled `law` before the def that fills it, which only Base's own defs and `@unsafe` defs may do; and an `@unsafe` def may call a def below it. So every cycle is in Base, through a law, or has an `@unsafe` def in it.

A counting pass over the checked terms (a hook in a scratch copy of the compiler): every def of Base, the 909 tests that build, 18 demo programs, the 17 `bench/runtime` programs and the 22 koru kernels (`korulang/koru-benchmarks`, `suites/osprey-compute-kernels/bend`). A cycle is a strongly connected component of the tail-call graph with two or more defs.

| | cycles | of two defs | of three | with a call to a def of the cycle in an argument | flat as built |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| tests (all `@unsafe`) | 9 | 8 | 1 | 4 | 5 |
| demos, benches, kernels (their own defs) | 0 | | | | |

- **Entered from outside** at one def in 18 of the 19, at each of its three defs in one (a ring in `tests/run/js_group_args`). **No helper has a caller outside its cycle.**
- **Named from one place in the cycle**: every def but one (`loop` in `tests/run/unsafe_tail_cycle`, which calls itself as well). So every cycle without a call in an argument has a head, and all 15 become loops.
- The 4 with a call in an argument (`wnf` / `wnf_app` in three tests, `count` / `back` in one) are left alone.

Base's ten, and what reaches them: `U32.show.go` / `.fin` (all 17 benches, for the one number they print; 5 demo programs; 520 tests), `Nat.show.fin` / `.go` (all 22 kernels, for their one number; 7 demo programs; 222 tests), `String.eq` / `.go` (under `Map.get`, `Map.has`, `Map.pop`; 4 demo programs, 29 tests), `Map.diff` / `.fin` (2 demo programs), `U32.read.go` / `.if` (4), `Nat.read.go` / `.if` (3), `String.contains` / `.if` and `String.starts_with.go` / `.if` (the `textstats` kernel, 7 tests), `U32.hex.go` / `.fin` (11 tests), `String.trim_start` / `.if` (1 test).

**On a hot path: one program.** `textstats` spends 75% of its instructions in `String.contains`. Everywhere else the cycle runs once per printed number or per parsed argument.

## Bounds by hand, before the compiler work

The cycle's own cost, separated from borrowing: the same algorithm with the same ownership, the helper folded into its caller in the source as a flag parameter (the one way Bend can spell it), built with main. Instructions retired, one thread.

| program | cycle spelling, main | one def, by hand, main | | cycle spelling, this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `textstats` (Base's `String.contains` and `String.starts_with` copied into the file, verbatim and merged) | 205.3M | 192.4M | -6.3% | 193.2M |
| `isqrt` with a helper def (`iter` / `iter.if`), against its flag spelling doing the same work | 234.4M | 187.8M | -19.9% | 187.8M |
| `primes` with helper defs (a ring of three, and `go` / `go.if`), against the kernel's flag spelling | 165.1M | 112.7M | -31.7% | 134.5M |

- `textstats`: a verbatim copy of Base's four defs in the kernel's file emits the same C as Base's (205.27M both). So of the 5.4x between main and the hand-written flat twin over the same lists (38.0M, measured before this work), **the cycle is 6%**; the rest is ownership: `String.contains` owns both strings, so every position keeps a count on the tail and on the pattern, rebuilds the node it matched and hands it to `String.starts_with`, which frees it node by node. That is unchanged here (the merged def's parameters are owned exactly as the two defs' were).
- `isqrt`: the kernel's own flag spelling computes the next iterate twice; both columns compute it once (`+y = ..` in the helper spelling, a `let` under the flag's arm in the other). With this PR the helper spelling emits the flag spelling's loop statement for statement, less the flag.
- `primes`: the helper spelling does one division less per number (it tests `d * d > n` before `n % d`), yet after this PR it still runs more instructions than the flag spelling on main. That is clang, not the cycle: `Nat.mod` is `Pair.snd` of the native divmod, whose test for a boxed half clang compiles to a compare chain in one loop and an early branch in the other (17 instructions a turn against 13, read off the assembly). With that test gone (#2173 + #2174 applied to both sides) the helper spelling is ahead: see below.

## Results

One M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`, `/usr/bin/time -l`. Each build is swept over 16 placements (0 to 15 `nop`s at the head of the text, 4 bytes each), 3 rounds, the least per placement; cycles are least / median / most over the placements, and the last column is the range of this / main over the same placement.

| program | instructions, main | this | | cycles, main | this | this / main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| `textstats` (koru kernel, unchanged source) | 205.0M | 193.0M | **-5.9%** | 31.1M / 31.5M / 32.8M | 28.7M / 29.5M / 30.1M | 0.907 to 0.961 |
| `isqrt`, helper spelling (helper also called from outside) | 234.2M | 187.5M | -19.9% | 68.6M / 68.7M / 68.9M | 59.7M / 59.8M / 60.1M | 0.869 to 0.875 |
| `isqrt`, helper spelling (entered at the head) | 226.5M | 198.5M | -12.4% | 71.1M / 71.2M / 72.3M | 65.5M / 65.7M / 66.3M | 0.908 to 0.931 |
| `primes`, helper spelling | 164.8M | 134.3M | -18.6% | 35.8M / 36.3M / 36.9M | 35.2M / 35.4M / 35.7M | 0.959 to 0.990 |
| `isqrt`, helper spelling, on #2173 + #2174 | 170.7M | 129.1M | -24.4% | 63.2M / 63.3M / 63.5M | 47.3M / 47.5M / 47.7M | 0.745 to 0.754 |
| `primes`, helper spelling, on #2173 + #2174 | 113.4M | 77.3M | -31.8% | 25.0M / 25.2M / 25.4M | 22.8M / 23.1M / 23.4M | 0.898 to 0.928 |

The flag spellings on the same sweeps: `isqrt` 187.5M and 59.7M / 59.8M / 60.1M on main, 129.0M and 47.2M / 47.5M / 47.8M on #2173 + #2174 (the helper spelling is now level with it); `primes` 112.5M and 34.1M / 34.6M / 34.7M on main, 84.2M and 23.2M / 23.5M / 23.7M on #2173 + #2174 (the helper spelling is now ahead in both). So the natural spelling of a computed test no longer costs anything against flag parameters.

**The 22 koru kernels** all emit different C, because each prints its one number with `Nat.show`. The least of 5 interleaved runs: `textstats` 205.15M to 193.14M instructions (-5.9%); 19 others within 0.2% (the worst `primes`, -0.19%, and `wordfreq`, +0.12%). Two run more instructions at the same cycles: **`josephus` 92.1M to 112.1M (+21.7%; cycles 127.2M and 127.0M) and `nestedloop` 231.4M to 247.1M (+6.8%; cycles 147.8M and 147.7M)**. Their loops are textually identical C in the two builds; what changed is that `Nat.show`, now a spin, is inlined by clang into the C function that holds the loop, and clang then compiles the same loop with more instructions a turn (two more in `josephus`). With `spin_Nat_show` kept out of line by hand both are back at main's count (92.1M, 231.5M). Over 16 placements their cycles are 0.985 to 1.013 and 0.975 to 1.081 of main's (medians +0.2% and -0.05%). The same two kernels move the same way under #2173 (`josephus`, +10.8% instructions, no cycles) and #2174 (`nestedloop`).

**Base's functions**, in loops over values made at run time (`micro/` in the scratch files; same sweep, 2 rounds):

| program | instructions, main | this | | cycles, main (median) | this | this / main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `U32.show` of 1M numbers | 468.1M | 432.9M | -7.5% | 86.7M | 86.7M | 0.992 to 1.016 |
| `Nat.show` of 1M numbers | 547.4M | 497.4M | -9.1% | 130.7M | 130.5M | 0.992 to 1.006 |
| `String.contains`, `starts_with`, `eq` on 200-character strings | 1,842.7M | 1,682.4M | -8.7% | 338.2M | 321.9M | 0.928 to 0.987 |
| `U32.read`, `Nat.read`, `String.trim_start` of one shared string | 859.7M | 844.7M | -1.8% | 136.1M | 143.8M | **1.032 to 1.068** |
| `U32.show` and `Nat.show` in one statement | 1,035.5M | 967.9M | -6.5% | 155.4M | 192.9M | **1.235 to 1.248** |

The last two rows run fewer instructions and more cycles at every placement. See "Not covered": a call to a def that is now flat runs where it is written in its statement, where main ran it first.

**Bend's suite.** All 17 `bench/runtime` programs emit different C, because each prints its one number with `U32.show`, which is now a spin. Instructions retired, one thread, the least of 2 interleaved runs:

| bench | main | this | | bench | main | this | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `bfs` | 28.746G | 28.746G | +0.002% | `nbody` | 39.787G | 39.788G | +0.002% |
| `editdist` | 49.777G | 49.777G | -0.000% | `queens` | 89.815G | 89.815G | +0.000% |
| `gameoflife` | 172.350G | 172.350G | +0.000% | `raytrace` | 82.952G | 82.953G | +0.000% |
| `hashmap` | 18.496G | 18.496G | -0.001% | `symreg` | 50.766G | 50.767G | +0.001% |
| `histogram` | 44.362G | 44.362G | -0.000% | `terrain` | 44.569G | 44.568G | -0.001% |
| `kmeans` | 41.577G | 41.577G | +0.000% | `tree-bitonic` | 148.701G | 148.702G | +0.000% |
| `lexer` | 53.407G | 53.407G | -0.000% | `tree-matmul` | 62.582G | 62.582G | -0.001% |
| `mandelbrot` | 43.446G | 43.446G | -0.000% | `tree-radix` | 13.789G | 13.774G | -0.110% |
| `merkle` | 47.320G | 47.314G | -0.013% |  | | | |

The worst is +0.002% (`bfs`, `nbody`), the best -0.11% (`tree-radix`); every output is equal. In cycles the single runs of that table moved `editdist` by -20% and `nbody` by +5.7%, which is placement: over 16 placements `editdist` is 8,449.7M / 8,452.0M / 10,621.0M on main and 8,450.2M / 8,451.7M / 10,624.3M here (one placement in 16 costs 25% in either build, as before), and `nbody` 21,330.7M / 22,051.8M / 22,694.4M and 21,323.6M / 22,114.4M / 22,722.1M. The other 15 were within 0.9% in the single runs and were not swept.

**Compile time and code size.** Of the 966 programs that build (909 tests, 18 demo programs, 17 benches, 22 kernels), 791 emit different C: 743 tests, 9 demo programs, all 17 benches and all 22 kernels, nearly all through `U32.show` and `Nat.show`. 81 defs are new spins, and the programs that change have 22,147 segments where they had 25,607.

- Emitted C, the programs that change: tests -1.37% in bytes (71.77 MB to 70.79 MB), demos -3.25%, benches -0.41%, kernels -1.21%. The most a program shrinks is -13.4% (`tests/base/u32_divmod`), the most one grows +0.27% (`tests/io/channel_fork_join`). `app_slash_boss_3d`: 2,928,604 to 2,887,214 bytes.
- No spin changes its size class in any program: every new spin is `INLINE` (under `SPIN_FAR` characters), none is `FAR` or `DFAR`.
- Compile time: emitting the C of all 966 programs takes 271.4 s on main and 271.8 s here (five at a time, on a loaded machine). `app_slash_boss_3d`, the largest (2.9 MB of C), emits in 0.69 s with either (the least of 5), and clang's user time on its C is 6.15 s and 5.95 s (the quietest of 3 pairs).

## Cost

+252 ttok, measured by removing each part from the final file: `flat_of` (the cycle's defs checked together, the head asked for, no call in an argument) 96, `loop_head` 64, the comment 50, the held call in `emit_body` 26, the count of names per pair of defs in `file_book` 16. No new emitter path: the held body goes through the path a tail call to a def with one call site takes on main.

## The other design: one spin with several entries

The alternative is what the JS lane does: the bodies of the cycle's defs in one C loop under a selector, a tail call inside the cycle sets the selector and the parameters and goes round. I built it in a scratch copy to compare (not in this PR):

| | this PR (bodies held by a head) | one spin with entries |
|---|---|---|
| `comp.ts` | +252 ttok | +624 ttok, with no comment, no cached Array location in a cycle's spin and an untyped field on `Seg` |
| reaches, of the 15 cycles found | 15 | 15 |
| reaches beyond them | cycles with a head | every cycle without a call in an argument (also one where two defs each call themselves; none found) |
| emitted C | the helper's body where its call was; no selector | `if (pc == 0) { .. } else if (pc == 1) { .. }` in the loop, `pc = 1; continue;` at each call |
| `primes`, helper spelling | 134.6M instructions | 172.2M (main: 165.1M) |
| `isqrt`, helper spelling | 187.8M | 187.9M |
| `textstats` | 193.3M | 187.4M |
| emitted C bytes, the three programs | 254,387 | 256,042 |

The selector costs nothing only where clang threads every `pc = k; continue` to its arm. It does on `isqrt` and `textstats` and does not on `primes` (a ring of three called from a cycle of two), which comes out slower than main's segments. A loop whose speed rests on clang's jump threading is not something to emit, and the selector version costs 2.5 times the tokens, so the head version is the one here. What it gives up is the cycle with no head, which nothing in Base, the tests, the demos, the benches or the kernels has. (`textstats` running 3% fewer instructions under the selector version is clang too: the two builds differ only in those two spins, which do the same work.)

## What merging changes besides the loop

- **Ownership.** Borrow facts stay per def and per parameter; nothing is merged in them. A body held in the head's spin takes each argument as it is (owned, or rooted in one of the head's borrowed parameters), and the held call hands ownership over exactly as main's jump into the helper's segment did, so a value the cycle hands a helper to own is still the helper's to free (`tail_cycle_owners` has a helper that a caller outside lends a string and the cycle hands one it made; with the held call lending like a plain call instead, that test frees twice). One step out, a tail call into the cycle from a flat def is now a call to a spin, which lends where main's jump handed the value over; no parameter in the corpus changes because of that. A hook that prints every boxed parameter's ownership once the facts settle finds 962 of the 966 programs with every parameter owned or lent as on main, and four that differ, in six parameters:
  - `demos/io_rollback_netcode/walkers_demo` and `walkers_test`: `String.eq`'s second parameter is owned where main lent it. `Post.drop` reads `name` in `String.eq(.., name)` and passes it to its own recursion. On main `String.eq` was not flat, ran first and was lent `name`; now the recursion runs first, with a kept copy, and `String.eq` is the last reader, so it is handed the string to free. This is the order change of "Not covered" showing in ownership: which use of a `+` value is the last one can move.
  - `tests/base/string_contains`: `String.starts_with`'s pattern is owned where main lent it. The test's literal calls are now unfolded, down to `String.starts_with.go.if("..", "..", ..)`, and a literal argument makes its parameter owned, as it does on main for any call.
  - `tests/gfx/fullscreen_input`: `want`'s parameter is lent where main owned it (not traced).
- **A helper with other callers.** None exists in Base, the tests, the demos, the benches or the kernels. When one does (`tail_cycle_shapes`' `col.if`, `tail_cycle_owners`' `wk.if` and `gt.if`), it gets a spin of its own: a loop of its own if it is a head too (a cycle of two with one call each way has two heads, and each def's spin holds the other), a call to the head's spin if not. The emitter's unfolding of a call with a literal argument can also name a helper from outside (`rev(U32, n, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [])` becomes a call to `rev.if` at the call site).
- **The size class of the merged spin.** A spin under `SPIN_FAR` (8,192) characters is `INLINE`, a longer one is a call on the device (`DFAR`) and, if it loops over F32 math, on the host too (`FAR`). The head's spin is as long as the cycle's defs together. In the 966 programs no spin changes class: all 81 new spins are `INLINE`.
- **Defs that fork or use `!`.** A def with a fork or a `!` call is not flat, so a cycle with one is compiled as on main (`fk.a` / `fk.b` in `tail_cycle_callers`). A cycle called from a fork's branches or with `!` runs through its defs' segments, which call the spin: same output on the CPU and on Metal (`tail_cycle_callers`: `tree!`, `ev!`, `ev.if!`). The 62 programs with a `!` call whose C changes (44 tests, the 17 benches, one demo) were built whole by both compilers, each with its GPU program, and run with `--gpu on`: the same result from both on all 62.
- **Closures over a def of the cycle.** A def passed as a function, a partial application of either def, a closure that calls the cycle and a def of the cycle that answers a closure calling the other all go through the closure's own segment, which calls the spin (`tail_cycle_callers`).
- **`@unsafe` cycles with a call in an argument.** Left alone (4 in the tests). Merging one is sound for the values it computes but would move the recursion to the C stack: the deliberately wrong version that merges them prints the right lines until the recursion is deep (`tail_cycle_callers` runs 20,000 frames in sixteen forked leaves, and that version dies on a pool thread's 512 KB stack).
- **Compile time and code size.** Above: no measurable difference in emit time, 1.2% less C.

## Checked

Against main (8c329c1b), on one M4:

- **The native lane** (every `tests/**/*.bend` with `#|` lines: build with `-o bin`, run with `--gpu off` at the default thread count, compare stdout): 886 pass on main, 889 here (the three new tests), 953 do not build (they expect an error), 21 differ and 1 times out on both, and **no status differs** over the 1,874 files they share.
- **Memory.** For every program whose C differs, both C files are patched to count live heap words at exit, built with `-DBEND_POISON` (a freed word is poisoned) and run: the 743 tests, 16 of the benches and 5 demo programs print the same lines, exit with the same code and leave the same count of live words, and so do the three new tests and six scratch programs. Not decided by it: `tree-bitonic` (over a minute at `-O1` with either compiler; its `-O3` output is equal), the relay `server.bend` (it never ends), `app_slash_boss_3d` and `walkers_demo` (both builds exit at once with the same code, 45, in a session with no window to open), and `walkers_test`, which needs a relay: run by hand on a fresh local relay, two bots in one room print the same three lines with either compiler, as the demo promises (the hashes change from run to run on main too).
- **The JS lane.** `-o x.js` emits byte-identical JS with both compilers for all 909 tests and all 35 demo and bench programs, alone and after a C emit in the same process. The rule is reached from the JS lane only through `flat_of` in a match table's rows, and `file_book` opens every term in main's order, so the probes and the order of a cycle's defs under `$pc` are main's.
- **The gate's in-process checks**, run by hand with both compilers: the comptime twins emit the same C, and the four state fixtures compile to the same bytes and leave the same probes over the gate's eleven steps.
- **`tsc`** over `bend2` and `gates`: the same 10 errors on main and here, none in the changed lines.
- **New tests**, each on four lanes with both compilers (C at `-O1` with poisoned frees, C at `-O3` on every core, JS, `bend file.bend`), all eight runs equal:
  - `tests/run/tail_cycle_shapes.bend`: a ring of three entered at each def, a helper with a caller outside, a self call beside a cross call, a def named from two places, a cycle with no head; 3,000,000 turns each.
  - `tests/run/tail_cycle_owners.bend`: a matched node the helper rebuilds, reusable lists, a value one def builds and the other answers, a string lent to the whole cycle, parameters that swap, a helper lent a string from outside and handed one to own, a record of words, an erased type parameter, parameters that differ in count and kind, a Nat rebuilt as matched, an Array written and read in place, and Base's own cycles on text made at run time.
  - `tests/run/tail_cycle_callers.bend`: the cycle under a fork, under `!`, as a function value, behind a partial application and a closure, answering a closure, in a literal call; and the four kinds of cycle that must stay as they were.
  - How each def came out was read off the emitted C (the counts come from `IO.now`, so nothing is folded away). One loop each: `r0`, `r1`, `r2`, `col`, `loop`, `two.b`, `keep`, `look`, `mk`, `cnt`, `swp.if`, `inc`, `fibp`, `rev`, `rev.if`, `mix.a`, `mix.c`, `dn`, `fill`, `asum`, `wk`, `wk.if`, `gt`, `ev`, `cl.a`, `cl.b`, `even`, `odd`, `out`, `kp`. A spin that calls a head's: `col.if`, `hop`, `two`, `two.a`, `swp`, `gt.if`, `ev.if`, `ev.end`. Segments, as on main: `pa`, `pb`, `nt.a`, `nt.b`, `fk.a`, `fk.b`, `hv`, `oc.a`, `oc.b`, `dp.a`, `dp.b`, `oq.a`, `oq.b`.
- **Deliberately wrong versions** of the rule, each run against the three new tests, five older tests with cycles and six scratch programs, with live words counted. Twelve are caught by the new tests:

  | wrong version | caught by | how |
  |---|---|---|
  | a cycle with a call in an argument is merged | `callers` | dies on a pool thread's stack |
  | the other defs of the cycle may fork or call in an argument | `callers` | the same |
  | a def being asked about counts as flat (a def outside calls back into the cycle) | `callers` | the same |
  | only the asked def's callees must be flat | `callers` | the C does not compile |
  | no head needed | `shapes` | overflows the C stack at 3,000,000 turns |
  | flat, but each def calls the other's spin instead of holding its body | all three | the same |
  | every def is a head | `shapes`, `owners` | the compiler overflows its own stack (it holds a body inside itself) |
  | a def named twice in the cycle is still held | `shapes`, `owners` | the same |
  | a spin that is no head holds the others too | `shapes`, `owners` | the same |
  | the self-jump is told by the held def, not the spin's | all three | the same |
  | the held call lends as a plain call does | `owners` | a string is freed twice |
  | two arguments swap on the way into the held body | all three | wrong lines, or no end |

  Two are not wrong and no `#|` line can see them: a segment that holds the bodies too (the same loop, in the segment), and sites counted over the whole program instead of inside the cycle (fewer cycles become loops).

Not run: the cluster gates (`test`, `perf`), CUDA, Linux, x86, clang other than Apple clang 17.

Not measured together with the other open drafts on this ground. #2162 (statements unfold into defs that are not flat) is independent of this: nothing here unfolds a helper into a def that is not flat, a body is held only in the spin of a head. #2175 leaves a def in a tail cycle alone and still does. What is left of `textstats` is ownership (#2148's ground): `String.contains` and `String.starts_with` own their strings before and after.

## Not covered

Every way the behaviour can differ from main:

- **Order inside a statement.** A call to a def that is not flat is cut out of its statement and runs first; a call to a flat def runs where it is written. The defs that become flat here (the cycles, and every def that was not flat only because it called one: `U32.show`, `Nat.show`, `String.starts_with`, `Map.get.leaf`, ..) therefore move from the first group to the second. Values do not depend on it. Two things can:
  - *Which failure is met first*, in a statement where two calls both fail-stop (a Nat past 2^48-1, an absurd match) or one of them never returns (`@unsafe`): the outcome can be the other one's.
  - *Cycles*, through the allocator. `Nat.add(len(U32.show(x)), len(Nat.show(y)))` built both strings and then walked both on main; here it builds and walks the first, then the second: 6.5% fewer instructions and 23.5% to 24.8% more cycles at every placement. Spelled with two `let`s (main's order) the same program is at 153.5M cycles against main's 155.5M. Each call alone is level (0.992 to 1.016 and 0.992 to 1.006). The reading that the walks' frees and the next build's allocations become one chain through the free list is inferred, not traced. A second micro-program (a `+` string read by `U32.read` and by `Nat.read`) runs 1.8% fewer instructions and 3.2% to 6.8% more cycles; its three parts alone are each faster (-1.2% to -1.7% cycles), every parameter's ownership is the same in both builds, and spelling the order out with `let`s recovers half of it (+3.0%). Not traced further.
- **Unfolding reaches the cycles.** The emitter unfolds a call to a flat def when a literal argument decides a match (up to `FOLD_FUEL`), so it now does for a cycle's defs: `even(10n)` in an argument is computed by the compiler, and `rev(U32, n, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [])` loses its first turn (the call site names `rev.if` with the rest of the list). An unfolded call does not evaluate an argument its arm never reads, where the JS lane and `bend file.bend` do (#2181, on main for every flat def): a program that relied on such an argument failing behaves as #2181 describes for more defs than before.
- **Frames held.** A call into a cycle from an expression pushed a frame on the heap stack and the cycle's turns were jumps between segments; now the call is a C call (inlined or not by clang) and the turns are a C loop. The C stack grows by one frame per call into a spin that clang leaves out of line, and by at most one more per def of the cycle for an entry at a def that is no head; no spin of a cycle calls itself, and a cycle with any call to its own defs in an argument is left on the heap stack.
- **Tasks.** With `seq` clear, a jump into a segment that cannot fork is handed back to the scheduler as a task, which main did for a jump into a cycle's def from another segment; a call to a spin is not, and the spin runs to its end where it was called, as every flat loop does. On the device a spin polls for a failure every 4,096 turns (`WL_SPIN`), as before.
- **Other spellings of the same thing stay as they were**: a cycle where no def is a head. That is one where two defs are each named twice (`f` calls `f.if` from two arms and `f.if` calls `f` from two), or two defs each call themselves. Holding a body twice would take the first; the selector design would take both. Nothing in the corpus has either.
- **clang.** Two kernels run more instructions at equal cycles because clang inlines the print into the function that holds their loop (above). The suite's 17 are within 0.11%.

title: fix(lint): preserve raw apostrophe character literals
body:
Bend accepts `'''` as an apostrophe character. In a list such as `[''', 'a']`, the lint formatter reads the middle apostrophe as the end of the literal. It then reads the closing bracket as part of another literal and exits with `format/layout: unbalanced delimiters`.

Consume the middle apostrophe before looking for the closing quote. The editor formatter uses the same rule. [PR #1971](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1971)

The regression test formats a list that also contains a literal `'#'` and has a trailing comment. It checks the output, compares the Bend definitions before and after formatting, and runs the linter a second time.

- All 136 bend-lint tests passed. The new test failed on `main`.
- Six programs kept their output after `--fix` and were unchanged on a second pass. They cover raw and escaped apostrophes, adjacent literals, and apostrophes inside a string.
- The repository gate passed all 56 checks. TypeScript reported the same six errors in `bend.ts` and `comp.ts` on both revisions.

title: fix(gates): detect the startup marker anywhere in a stderr chunk
perf(base): skip rebuilding maps in empty-left unions
body:
When the left map is empty, `Map.union` used to turn the right trie into a list and reinsert every entry through `Map.set`. It now returns an existing branching right trie directly. This relies on the Base Map API invariant that each internal node has two nonempty children. Unions of two nonempty maps retain insertion order and right-side precedence.

On macOS arm64, I timed batches of 220 unions with 1,024 entries in the right map. Times include result-size checks and are medians of three alternating baseline and patched runs after warmup.

| Workload | Native C | Bun | Node |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty left | 85 → 6 ms | 1,111 → 1 ms | 425 → 2 ms |
| Two disjoint 1,024-entry maps | 192 → 194 ms | 3,890 → 3,375 ms | 1,202 → 1,213 ms |

The patched empty-left JavaScript runs are near the timer’s resolution. Independent whole-process measurements, including startup, also showed a speedup.

The extended fixture checks prefix-key ordering and preserves the empty-right and singleton-right proof reductions. An equality with a known multi-entry right map and an abstract left map can now require a case split on the left. The case-split proof passes Lean.

title: Linux: binaries using Window link libX11, so they do not start on headless machines
body:
On Linux, `bend file.bend -o out` links every binary that uses the Window effects with `-lX11` (the compile is `clang -std=c11 -O3 file.c -lpthread -lm -lX11 -ldl -o out`, Bend 2.0.40). Such a binary then fails at load time on a machine without libX11, even when it never opens a window:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libX11.so.6: cannot open shared object file
```

This hits programs where a window is optional. For example, a VMM with an optional `--display` flag cannot run on a headless server (Debian without X), although it never calls `Window.open` there.

`effs/window.c` already loads libXrender, libXrandr and libXi with `dlopen` at run time. The suggestion is to load Xlib the same way:

- `dlopen("libX11.so.6")` on the first `Window.open`.
- If that fails, make `Window.open` return its existing "no display" error.
- Drop `-lX11` from the link line.

Only the Xlib headers would be needed at build time.

What we do in the meantime (bend-vmm, `scripts/x11-lazy.sh`):

- Emit C with `-o x.c`.
- After `#include <X11/keysym.h>`, add a static function pointer for each Xlib function the C calls, plus a `#define XFoo (*bx11_XFoo)`.
- Make `XOpenDisplay` go through a loader that dlopens libX11 and fills those pointers. If it can't, it returns NULL.
- Compile without `-lX11`.

Tested on arm64 Linux: a window opens under Xvfb, and `Window.open` returns its "no display" error with no DISPLAY and with libX11 absent. Doing this in the runtime would make it unnecessary.

title: perf(flatten): a match's rows are grouped by constructor once, not rescanned per constructor
body:
> **This PR edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which AGENTS.md marks as human-written.** It was opened at Nicolas's request, as a proposal for the file's owner to review, rewrite or close.

Refs #2040 (the loading half; the checking half is a separate PR).

**What.** `match_flatten` took the first constructor in the column and scanned every row to build its branch (`patt_mark`, `flatMap`) and the rows left for the default (`filter`). It then recursed on the leftover rows. With n constructors that is n(n+1)/2 row visits per pass, and the recursion is n deep.

The rows are now grouped by constructor in one pass, in the order each first appears. Each branch merges its own rows with the variable rows in source order, and the variable rows alone make the default after the last constructor. This is what the recursion produced:
- each level's constructor was the first one left among the rows;
- variable rows were never removed;
- `patt_mark` only reads variable rows, so `xq` was the same at every level.

The branches are built in the same order as before, so `fr()` hands out the same fresh variables.

**Load time** (in-process `parse_book`, best of 21; a `Token` with n constructors and a match with one arm each, as in the issue)

| n | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 80 ms | 1.2 ms |
| 2000 | 280 ms | 2.1 ms |
| 4000 | 968 ms | 4.7 ms |

At n = 4000, `--check-only` takes 3.15 s on main and 1.19 s with this PR. What remains is mostly `book_adt` in the checker, which is the checking half.

**Scope.** This only helps a column with many distinct constructors. Nat and String literal patterns expand into two-way decisions (`Zero`/`Succ`, `SNil`/`SCon`, and 32 `True`/`False` bits per character), so their columns never have more than two constructors. On 100–400 literal arms, load times are unchanged within noise. Their costs come from the encoding (#1403, #1266).

**Checks**
- **Same terms:** every flattened term (the three `body_flatten` calls in the parser) was dumped on main and on this PR for all 1874 `.bend` files under `tests/`: 986,141 terms, about 418k of them with a `Mat`. The dumps are byte-identical, fresh variable numbers included.
- **Same outputs:** every test prints the same output and exit code with `--check-only` as on main, error messages included.
- `base.bend` parse time is unchanged (main 4.6–5.0 ms, this PR 4.4–5.3 ms, best of 60).
- `bend.ts` 45949 → 46179 ttok (cap 48000).
- The cluster gates (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`) were not run.

title: perf(check): a match arm finds its constructor by name, not by filtering the datatype's
body:
> **This PR edits `bend2/bend.ts`, which AGENTS.md marks as human-written.** It was opened at Nicolas's request, as a proposal for the file's owner to review, rewrite or close.

Refs #2040 (the checking half; the loading half is #2193).

**What.** At every arm, check-mat called `book_adt`, which built a `Set` of the matched constructors (`r`) and filtered the datatype's whole constructor list. It used the result only to find the arm's constructor and to test whether exactly one was left. That is O(n) per arm and O(n²) per match.

`r` only grows at check-mat, by a constructor of `a_wnf.k` that was not yet in it. The parser never sets it, and everywhere else it is copied unchanged. So `r` has no duplicates and only holds constructors of its own datatype. Two things follow:
- The arm's constructor is `book_ctr(book, tm.k)` when its family `f` is `a_wnf.k` and `r` does not hold it. Each constructor is registered once, as the same object in `book.ctrs` and in its datatype's `c`.
- The datatype has `c.length - r.length` constructors left.

The validation half of `book_adt` is now `book_adt_tld`, so both cases still raise the same errors in the same order. check-efq still uses `book_adt` to list the missing constructors.

**Not changed.** `r.includes` and `r.concat` stay linear per arm, so this is still O(n²), with a much smaller constant. Removing them means storing `r` as a shared set with a count, which touches the `ADT` term, type comparison, `term_higher`/`term_lower` and the three `F.r.includes` in `safe.ts`.

**Check time** (`bend file.bend --check-only` wall time, best of 3; a `Token` with n constructors and a match with one arm each, as in the issue)

| n | main | this PR | #2193 | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 0.07 s | 0.05 s | 0.05 s | 0.03 s |
| 2000 | 0.17 s | 0.11 s | 0.10 s | 0.04 s |
| 4000 | 0.50 s | 0.34 s | 0.29 s | 0.07 s |
| 8000 | 1.85 s | 0.95 s | 1.08 s | 0.16 s |
| 16000 | 7.34 s | | | 0.45 s |

With both PRs at n = 16000, `includes` and `concat` take about 72% of what remains.

**Checks**
- **Same answers:** a copy of this PR that also computed the old `rem` at every check-mat, and threw if the constructor or the "one left" test differed, ran all 1874 `.bend` files under `tests/` with no mismatch. A forced failure confirmed the assertion ran.
- **Same outputs:** every test prints the same output and exit code with `--check-only` as on main, error messages included.
- `bend.ts` 45949 → 46137 ttok (cap 48000).

title: Guide: how to build the C that -o file.c emits
body:
`bend file.bend -o file.c` emits the C source (GUIDE.md:550), but nothing says how to build it. You need that to link foreign code against external libraries, to make portable macOS binaries, or to pass any compiler flag, since `bend -o bin` takes none. Today the only reference is `cli_build` in `bend2/main.ts`.

**What the explanation should cover**

- **The base command** that `bend -o bin` runs:
  ```
  cc -std=c11 -O3 file.c -lpthread -lm -o bin
  ```
  with clang 14+ (19+, or Apple clang 17+, for `!`).
- **Platform additions:**
  - Linux: `-lX11 -ldl` when the C includes `<X11/...>` (Window), and `-lasound` for `<alsa/...>` (Audio).
  - macOS, for a program that uses `!` or contains `#import` (Window): `-x objective-c -fobjc-arc -fmodules`.
  - A program that uses `!` adds `-DBEND_METAL=1` on macOS, or on Linux `-DBEND_CUDA=1 -I$CUDA/include -L$CUDA/lib64 -L$CUDA/lib ... -lcuda -lnvrtc`. After `cc`, it runs `./bin +RTS --gpu-build`.
- **Foreign code that uses an external library:** the emitted C contains the foreign `.c` verbatim, so the library goes on the `cc` line (`-lfoo`, or `/path/libfoo.a` to link it statically, plus that library's own dependencies). `bend -o bin` has no way to add it.
- **macOS:**
  - A fully static binary is impossible: Apple ships no static libc, so `-static` fails with `ld: library 'crt0.o' not found`. Static archives for everything else, with `libSystem` linked dynamically, work fine, and that's all a Bend binary needs: `otool -L` shows only `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib`.
  - By default a binary targets the build machine's macOS version and CPU (built on macOS 26/arm64, it has `minos 26.0`, arm64 only), so it won't start on older macOS or on Intel Macs. `-mmacosx-version-min=11.0 -arch arm64 -arch x86_64` builds a universal binary for 11.0+. `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0 bend file.bend -o bin` also works, since `bend` passes its environment through to `cc`.

**Where it can go.** GUIDE.md is at its cap (8000 / 8000 ttok, `gates/repo.ts`), so adding it there needs a trim elsewhere in the GUIDE. README.md has room (3071 / 4000), or it can be a page of its own (e.g. under `bend2/docs/`) with a pointer from the GUIDE's `-o file.c` line.

**Related, not part of this issue.** `bend -o bin` reads `$CC` but not `$CFLAGS`/`$LDFLAGS`, and a foreign import cannot name the libraries it needs. Passing those two variables through to `cc` would let `bend -o bin` cover foreign code with external libraries as well.

title: String.contains tests a position from the node's fields and walks with a prefix def of its own, so a search takes neither string apart
body:
A Base change only: `comp.ts` is untouched (65,981 ttok). `base.bend` goes from 33,694 to 33,847 ttok; it has no cap in `gates/repo.ts`, and `repo.ts` passes 56 / 56. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster. Two commits: the first kept a second copy of `String.starts_with`'s walk (two defs and a law); the second replaces it with one def, described here.

## The problem

```python
def String.contains(s, p):
  match s:
    case SNil{}:
      String.is_empty(p)
    case SCon{h, t}:
      String.contains.if(t, p, String.starts_with(SCon{h, t}, p))
```

The arm rebuilds the node it has just matched to hand it to `String.starts_with`. A rebuilt node is a new value, so on the C lane `String.contains` owns its text. At every position it takes the node apart, counts the tail (`term_keep`) and the pattern, allocates a node (when the text is a literal, which has no spare to reuse) and a count cell for its tail (`rfc_seal`), and `String.starts_with.go` takes that copy apart again and drops it. A text the caller keeps is first shared, so every cell of it ends up behind a count cell.

On `textstats` (a koru kernel: 200,000 words scored with `String.length`, `String.contains(w, "o")` and `String.starts_with(w, "t")`), `String.contains` is 75% of the instructions.

## What changes

```python
def String.contains.pre(p: String, s: String, same: Bool) -> Bool:
  match p s same:
    case _ _ False{}:
      False{}
    case SNil{} _ True{}:
      True{}
    case SCon{y, yt} SNil{} True{}:
      False{}
    case SCon{y, yt} SCon{x, xt} True{}:
      String.contains.pre(yt, xt, Char.is_eq(x, y))

def String.contains.at(p: String, h: Char, t: String) -> Bool:
  match p:
    case SNil{}:
      True{}
    case SCon{y, yt}:
      String.contains.pre(yt, t, Char.is_eq(h, y))

def String.contains(s, p):
  match s:
    case SNil{}:
      String.is_empty(p)
    case SCon{h, t}:
      String.contains.if(t, p, String.contains.at(p, h, t))
```

- **`String.contains.at`** tests a position from the node's two fields, so nothing is rebuilt.
- **`String.contains.pre`** is the prefix walk, carrying whether every char so far was the same. It is one def whose only call to itself is a tail call, so it needs no law and the C lane runs it as a loop on main. Only `String.contains` reaches it, and `String.contains` lends it both strings at every position (it reads them again afterwards), so it borrows them in every program.

With that, the walk in `String.contains` only peeks: no allocation, no count, no free. When the caller does not keep the text, `String.contains` still owns it and frees each node as it passes.

The JS lane keeps its intrinsic (`string_contains`), so its output is unchanged.

**Why not `String.starts_with` itself.** The compiler gives a def one ownership per parameter for the whole program. `String.starts_with(s, p)` is a tail call into `String.starts_with.go`, so as soon as one caller hands `String.starts_with` a string it owns, `.go` owns its strings everywhere, and a search sharing that walk has to count each tail before lending it. Three simpler spellings, measured below, do not keep the gain: passing `s` itself to `String.starts_with` (both parameters are already `+`), calling `String.starts_with.go.if` from `.at`, and matching the pattern in `String.contains` itself.

## Measured

One M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`, `/usr/bin/time -l`, against main `9c586f09`. Instructions retired:

| program | main | first commit | this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `textstats` (koru kernel, literal words) | 205.6M | 97.6M | 73.6M | -64.2% |
| 200 searches for an absent 3-char pattern in a 24,576-char heap string the caller keeps | 3,419.3M | 696.1M | 384.7M | -88.7% |
| the same, in a program where another call hands `String.starts_with` a built string | 5,596.4M | 714.0M | 402.5M | -92.8% |
| 200 searches, each in a 3,072-char string built for it | 441.4M | 243.4M | 210.3M | -52.4% |

Cycles for `textstats`, the least of 15 interleaved runs at one placement, on a loaded machine (load average about 8): 35.6M on main, 20.9M for the first commit, 17.4M here. The first commit was swept over 16 placements (30.52M / 31.38M / 32.36M on main, 17.90M / 18.55M / 19.77M); this one was not.

The simpler spellings that do not keep the gain (instructions; `textstats` / kept string / kept string with `String.starts_with` owning elsewhere / built string):

| spelling | | | | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 205.6M | 3,419.3M | 5,596.4M | 441.4M |
| `String.starts_with(s, p)` on `s` itself | 205.6M | 3,419.2M | 5,596.4M | 441.4M |
| `.at` calling `String.starts_with.go.if` (the walk shared) | 124.1M | 696.1M | 5,206.4M | 243.4M |
| the pattern matched in `String.contains`, no `.at` | 109.4M | 2,331.2M | 2,349.1M | 451.1M |
| `.pre` called on `s` itself, no `.at` | 179.3M | 3,769.7M | 3,787.4M | 485.0M |
| this PR | 73.6M | 384.7M | 402.5M | 210.3M |

**With #2188.** On a branch that merges the open optimisation drafts (`opt/integration`, where #2188 runs a tail cycle of two defs as one loop), the first commit's pair of defs is a loop too, and it is level or better than the flag: `textstats` 44.6M for the pair and 45.0M for this, the kept string 282.6M and 384.2M, the built string 187.4M and 196.9M (without either, 172.7M, 2,988.8M and 372.5M). The flag costs a step on a mismatch: `.pre` peeks at both strings before it reads the flag, where the pair's `.if` read the flag first. Parameters are matched in order and the first that changes must shrink, so the flag cannot come first.

#2148 and #2134, the compiler-side drafts on borrowing, leave these programs unchanged on their own bases.

## Reach

A text and a pattern searched twice and read whole afterwards; a tail that shares its cells with a kept text, searched both ways; a text built for the search; a search as a tail call; the strings of a kept list; empty texts and patterns; a pattern longer than the text; a match at the very end; an overlapping near-match (`aaab` in `aaaa…`); chars past U+FFFF and past Unicode; and one call that hands `String.starts_with` a built string. title: fix(window): load Xlib at run time so Window binaries start without libX11
body:
Fixes #2192.

`bend -o out` added `-lX11` for every program whose emitted C included the X11 headers, so a Window binary carried `libX11.so.6` in `DT_NEEDED` and failed at load on a headless machine even when it never called `Window.open`. `window.c` now loads libX11 at run time and resolves every Xlib function it calls through a `dlsym` table; `cli_build` drops `-lX11` and keeps `-ldl`.

## What changed

- `bend2/effs/window.c`: Linux-only `bx11_*` table plus `pthread_once` / `dlopen("libX11.so.6", RTLD_LAZY | RTLD_GLOBAL)`. A missing library or symbol makes `XOpenDisplay` return `NULL`, so `Window.open` keeps returning its existing `ENOTSUP` "no display" error. `XDestroyImage` and `NextRequest` stay direct because they are header macros over struct fields.
- `bend2/main.ts`: `["X11", "X11", "dl"]` -> `["X11", "dl"]`; comment updated.
- `tests/gfx/window_no_x11.bend/.c/.js`: `x11.absent` uses `dl_iterate_phdr` on Linux to assert no `libX11.so*` is loaded before any display work; the width-0 `Window.open` is the nearby control. Expected `True` then `failed`; macOS and the JS lane report absent.

## Checks run

- `bun gates/repo.ts` -> `PASS: 56 / 56`.
- macOS (Apple clang 21, arm64): `bun bend2/main.ts tests/gfx/window_no_x11.bend` -> `True` / `failed`; native `-o` and `-o .js` + node also `True` / `failed`.
- Debian 13 arm64 container, clang 19.1.7, `libx11-dev`:
  - `bun bend2/main.ts tests/gfx/window_no_x11.bend -o /tmp/wnx` -> `True` / `failed`.
  - `readelf -d /tmp/wnx` -> only `libm.so.6` and `libc.so.6`; no `libX11.so.6`.
  - The same test built with the old `-lX11` link line -> `False` / `failed`, so the regression test catches the old behavior.
  - Fixed binary with a deliberately broken `libX11.so.6` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` -> still `True` / `failed`; the old-link-line binary fails at load (`file too short`).
  - With the system `libX11.so.6` moved away, a valid-size `Window.open` returns `failed` (the existing no-display error), no crash.
  - Under `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 640x480x24"`, a valid-size `Window.open` prints `opened`, so the lazy symbols resolve.
  - Every `tests/gfx/*.bend` builds in the container (10/10).
  - `tests/gfx/window_title.bend` under Xvfb prints `True` three times; `window_open_only` prints `failed`.

## Not run

- `bun gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`, `gates/ping.ts`, and Metal/CUDA qualification: the cluster is unreachable from this checkout (`ssh cluster` refused) and GPU paths are untouched. No cluster qualification is claimed.
- The Linux checks above are local container results, not cluster results.

## Note

Dropping `-lX11` means third-party foreign C that calls Xlib directly must either appear after `window.c` in the emitted translation unit (the aliases then cover it) or load/link Xlib itself. In-repo foreign C that does this (`window_title.c`, `fullscreen_input.c`) builds and runs through the aliases.

title: fix(runtime): count nested array fields in shared records
body:
The native runtime stops when both handles from `Array.fork` match a record that contains nested arrays. This also fails with one CPU worker. The added regression stops with `bend: runtime fail-stop` on `main`. With this fix it prints `4`, `4`, and `8`, as the JS runtime does.

`rfc_seal` gives constructor fields reference counts before a record can be shared. It skips array and buffer handles, so `span_fade` rejects those fields when it opens the shared record. Include `TAG_ARR` and `TAG_BUF` when `BLK_SHR` is enabled. This follows the stated `Array.fork` contract for affine elements. [Maintainer comment](https://github.com/bendlang/bend/pull/1566#issuecomment-6290514970)

The regression covers nested `Array<U32>` and `Array<String>`, a recursive record, and replacement through `Array.set`.

Validation on macOS with Apple clang 21

- The regression passed with AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, and `BEND_POISON`.
- A copy of the regression with `twice!` passed with `+RTS --gpu on` on Metal.

title: fix(comp): a folded call evaluates an argument its chosen arm drops
body:
Fixes #2181.

`emit_unfold` folds a call whose constant arguments decide its matches. A live, non-constant argument becomes a probe, and the chosen arm body is wrapped in a `let` for it. When the arm did not use that argument, the binding was dead, the emitter dropped it, and the argument was never evaluated: the C lane printed `100` for `pick(boom(k), 0n, 100n)` where the interpreter and JS evaluate `boom` and stop at the Nat wall.

`emit_unfold` now refuses a fold whose body does not use one of its probes, so the call is emitted normally and evaluates its arguments like the other lanes.

## What changed

- `bend2/comp.ts`, `emit_unfold` (+7/-7 lines): the `bad` predicate that already rejects a fold now also reports a probe the folded body does not use. Four behavior-neutral tightenings in the same function (merged declarations, a `while` loop over the probe list, `&&` in place of a ternary) keep `comp.ts` at **65,996 / 66,000 ttok** (main is 65,995).
- `tests/reg/unfold_drop_arg.bend`: the issue's file; expects `bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1` and `exit 1` on all three lanes.
- `tests/reg/unfold_drop_arg_run.bend`: control; the same call with `Nat.sub(k, k)` as the selector, so no fold happens. It already stopped on every lane before the fix, which isolates the literal selector as the trigger.

## Checks run (local, macOS arm64)

- **Before the patch:** `bun bend2/main.ts` and `-o .js && bun .js` print the Nat wall (exit 1); `-o drop && ./drop` printed `100` (exit 0). The emitted C had no `boom` call and only `100ull` reached `Nat.show`.
- **After:** all three lanes print `bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1` (exit 1); the emitted C now calls `spin_boom` before `spin_pick`.
- `bun gates/repo.ts` -> `PASS: 56 / 56`.
- **Blast radius:** emitted C before/after for every `tests/**/*.bend`, `bench/runtime/*/main.bend` and `demos/*/main.bend` that compiles: 927 identical, 14 differ, plus the 2 new tests. The 14 are `tests/check/{convoy_dependent,kind_domain_self_call,kind_generic_none,kind_none_is_type,kind_self_call_eta,meet_uses_in_arms}`, `tests/compile/loop_peel_countdown`, `tests/cost/accumulator_loop`, `tests/io/bool_bridge`, `tests/proof/fold_assoc`, `tests/run/{bit_walking,graph_bfs,word_wrap_chains}` and `bench/runtime/raytrace`. Each was built and run on the interpreted, JS and C lanes in both trees: byte-identical output, and their `#|` lines still match.
- `tests/reg/unfold_arg_type.bend` (prints `0`) and `tests/run/nat_overflow.bend` (wall, exit 1) still pass on all three lanes.

The change is in the C emitter only; the interpreter and the JS emitter do not use `emit_unfold`.

## Rebase onto current `main` (`0e2f38f7`)

`main` grew from 65,981 to 65,995 ttok after this PR was opened, so the patch was 66,011 / 66,000. The tightenings above bring it back to **65,996**, and the branch is rebased on `0e2f38f7`. Re-checked on Linux x86_64:

- `ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo < bend2/comp.ts` -> `65996`
- `bun gates/repo.ts` -> `PASS: 56 / 56`
- `tests/reg/unfold_drop_arg.bend` and `tests/reg/unfold_drop_arg_run.bend`: interpreted, JS and C lanes all print the Nat wall and exit `1`
- `tests/reg/unfold_arg_type.bend`, `tests/run/{nat_overflow,bit_walking,graph_bfs}.bend`, `tests/compile/loop_peel_countdown.bend`: expected output on the interpreted lane

## Not run

title: perf(io): read directly into JavaScript file buffers
body:
JavaScript file reads allocated a temporary view and a one-element array for each host call. Positive reads now fill the existing buffer directly. Zero-byte reads still use `readvSync` so Bun reports OS errors such as `EBADF` on a write-only handle.

For 40,000 50-byte lines on macOS ARM64, the median of seven paired runs went from 979 to 770 ms on Bun and from 1,089 to 1,022 ms on Node. A single 16 MiB read and EOF check stayed within 1 ms of baseline. Repeated zero-byte Bun reads were slower in some stress runs.

title: fix(cli): preserve Base import order in checkup
body:
Refs #1941.

When a module imports a dependency before Base, `--checkup` can preload Base and accept a dependency that a normal run rejects. It now reuses checked Base only when `import Base` comes first, preserving normal import order.

Fully addressing #1941 requires shared Base caching in `book_load` and support in `book_valid`, both in `bend2/bend.ts`, followed by integration into the standalone linter. Those parts remain outstanding.

The regression fails before the fix and passes afterward through source and compiled CLIs. Repository checks pass 56/56. Independent review found no actionable issues. The full ping gate skips because the site checkout is absent.

title: fix(base): classify F32.hypot overflow at the rounding boundary
body:
`F32.hypot` can return infinity for a result that rounds to the largest finite F32. It can also return the largest finite F32 for a result that rounds to infinity. Both occur on `9c586f09` in the default CLI, native C, Bun, and Node. This follows #1515.

| Inputs | Current bits | Correct bits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2.22e38, 2.578916e38` | `7f800000` | `7f7fffff` |
| `3.4028235e38, 1.0e35` | `7f7fffff` | `7f800000` |

**Draft because of a performance regression.** The numerical checks pass. A focused loop of ordinary calls is 2.71 times slower on Node. The measurements below make that cost explicit for review.

The scaled squares lose information near the overflow boundary. For inputs whose maximum magnitude reaches 2^127, the fix checks the original significands with existing 48-bit `Nat` operations. The exact check selects infinity or a finite result from the scaled formula.

For the relevant finite inputs, write `hi = A*2^104` and `lo = B*2^(104-d)`. The overflow midpoint is `(2^24 - 1/2)*2^104`. Set `D = (2^24-A)*(2^24+A) - 2^24` and `P = 4^d`. Overflow occurs when `floor((B^2 + floor(3P/4))/P) > D`. This also handles an exact midpoint. For `d >= 12`, overflow is impossible, and clamping d to 12 gives the same decision. All integer intermediates fit below 2^48.

The regressions cover both reported cases, signs, argument order, an exact midpoint and its adjacent inputs, large exponent gaps, zero, infinity, and NaN. The GPU test adds parallel checks at the boundary.

Validation

- An independent integer oracle checked 45,264 input pairs. The default CLI, native C, Bun, and Node pass all cases. Main fails 1,614. The oracle checks classification exactly and finite accuracy within two ULP.
- Forced Metal passes all 45,264 classification checks. The two-ULP check retains 21 tiny-value failures. Each exact input/output pair also fails on main.
- The new regression passes the default CLI, native C, Bun, and Node. The extended GPU regression also passes on forced Metal.
- 34 related math programs passed 169 of 170 local run checks. The Node NaN-payload test is the sole failure and emits identical JS on main and this branch. Its payload behavior is listed in `WONTFIX.txt`.
- The repository gate passes 56/56.

Performance on Apple M5 Max, macOS 26.6.2, Apple clang 21, Bun 1.3.14, and Node 24.15.0. These are median process times from nine alternating pairs after one warmup.

| Workload | Native, one worker | Bun | Node |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 30 million ordinary calls | 37.34 → 41.68 ms | 880.95 → 890.65 ms | 146.02 → 395.45 ms |
| 300,000 boundary calls | Startup dominates at about 3 ms | 172.09 → 228.28 ms | 232.83 → 360.85 ms |

The ordinary loop uses runtime-generated coordinates and returns the same checksum. On Node, the new cold branch prevents loop peeling in this benchmark. The generated loop then boxes its accumulator and seed on each iteration. With loop peeling disabled for diagnosis, both versions take about 374–380 ms. Several helper arrangements retained this cost. The existing runtime benchmarks contain no `F32.hypot` calls.

The full cluster suite and CUDA were not run.

title: perf(base): Map.set updates an existing key in one walk down the trie
body:
`Map.set` on a key that is already in the map now walks the trie once instead of twice. Updates get 34-44% faster and use 22-29% less peak memory. A word-frequency count over 16 MB of text gets 19-21% faster.

## What

Before, `Map.set` always ran `Map.seek` to find the nearest leaf. If that leaf held the same key, it ran `Map.put`, a second walk from the root, to store the value.

Now the first walk stores the value itself when the leaf's key matches. When the key is new, the walk hands the value back with the first bit where the two keys differ, and `Map.ins` takes it from there as before.

`Map.seek`, `Map.put`, `Map.set.go` and the old `Map.set.fin` are removed. `Map.set` was their only caller. `git grep` finds no other use in tests, the guide, `comp.ts` or `bendtt.lean`. The tree shape does not change: an update rebuilds each node on the path with the same position and sibling, and only the leaf's value changes.

## Why

Counting words is the usual `Map.get` + `Map.set` loop, and most `Map.set` calls hit a key that is already there. A `sample` profile of that loop over 16 MB of text puts `Map.seek` and `Map.put` at about 500 samples together, next to about 270 for `Map.get`.

## Results

Whole-process wall-time medians (p50) of 10 alternating pairs after 1 warm-up. Every run printed the same output digest on both sides. Peak RSS is the process high-water mark.

| Case | macOS arm64, base → branch | Docker Linux arm64 (4 CPUs, 2 GB), base → branch |
|---|---|---|
| word frequency, 16 MB | 2.29 → 1.80 s (-21%) | 4.00 → 3.24 s (-19%) |
| word frequency, 4 MB | 0.589 → 0.475 s (-19%) | 1.04 → 0.819 s (-21%) |
| word frequency, 1 MB | 0.162 → 0.133 s (-18%) | 0.253 → 0.205 s (-19%) |
| 320k updates | 1.29 → 0.789 s (-39%), RSS 124 → 88 MiB | 1.39 → 0.916 s (-34%), RSS 134 → 96 MiB |
| 80k updates | 0.233 → 0.144 s (-38%), RSS 32 → 23 MiB | 0.288 → 0.178 s (-38%), RSS 42 → 30 MiB |
| 20k updates | 0.0549 → 0.0338 s (-38%) | 0.0613 → 0.0346 s (-44%) |
| 320k new keys | 0.606 → 0.482 s (-20%), RSS 124 → 88 MiB | 0.736 → 0.610 s (-17%), RSS 134 → 96 MiB |

New keys still take two walks (find the nearest leaf, then `Map.ins`), yet they also got faster and lighter. I measured that but did not dig into why. Word frequency RSS is unchanged; there the input string dominates memory.

<details>
<summary>Workloads</summary>

- Word frequency: read a file, and for each line `String.trim`, `String.split(' ')`, then `Map.get` and `Map.set` with the count + 1. Print the whole `Map.to_list`. The input is the repo's own text (GUIDE, README, WONTFIX, base.bend) repeated to 1, 4 and 16 MB.
- Updates: `Map.set` over n keys `"item/" ++ U32.show(i * 2654435761)`, then the same n keys again. Print the size and the sum of values.
- New keys: the first half of the above only.

C output of `bun bend2/main.ts <file> -o x.c`, built with `clang -std=c11 -O3 x.c -lpthread -lm` (Apple clang on macOS, Debian clang 19 in Docker).

</details>

## How to test

- `bun gates/repo.ts`
- The 13 tests that use `Map.` or `Set.` (`git grep -l -E 'Map\.|Set\.' -- 'tests/*.bend'`) match their expected `#|` output on the interpreter, `-o x.js` under bun, and `-o x.c` natively, before and after.
- A differential check: `Map.set` of 5000 random keys over `{\0, a, b, U+10FFFF}` with lengths 0 to 6, so many repeat, then print the whole `Map.to_list`. The output is identical before and after on the interpreter, bun, node and C.

## Risk

The change is limited to `Map.set` and its private helpers in `base.bend`. `comp.ts` and `bend.ts` are untouched. Reverting this one commit restores the old path.

title: perf(base): retire completed IO.within deadlines
body:
A successful `IO.within` call can leave its deadline sleep running after the program has finished its work, so the program cannot exit until the deadline passes.

A positive deadline now waits on its own `cancel` channel with `Chan.try_recv(Unit, cancel, ms)`. If that wait times out, the deadline sends `None{}` on the action's result channel; when the caller has its answer it closes `cancel`, which retires the pending timer. The action's result channel is untouched, so the race keeps its order: an action that comes due before its deadline still wins when the event loop resumes after both are overdue. A timed-out action still runs to completion, and a zero deadline keeps the existing race.

On macOS arm64 with Apple Clang 21, a winner against an eight-second deadline took **8.05 s on upstream and 0.17 s with the patch** (single end-to-end runs, including process startup).

Tests:
- `tests/io/within_shutdown.bend`: a zero deadline lets the action's own zero sleep win, and a winner with an 8-second deadline exits within the gate's 5-second alarm (upstream times out).
- `tests/io/within_overdue.bend`: a 10 ms action against a 50 ms deadline, with a blocking effect holding the loop until both are overdue; the action wins.
- `tests/io/within.bend` is unchanged.

`guide/GUIDE.md`: the `IO.within` sentence now says the action keeps running after a timeout, since a deadline that loses is retired.

title: Datatype nodes: an arm that re-forms its node keeps it whole, the counted take and wrap inline, a recursive drop, and flat defs lent a box
body:

Checked `rbtree` on main loses nearly a factor of two to cache aliasing between 64-byte cells carved 8 words apart (the odd-stride row is the control: nothing else changes). With this PR it no longer does, so of its 3.1x, 1.6x to 1.7x is the change and the rest is that effect going away.

Peak memory: `rbtree-ck` 3,677 MB to 2,033 MB, `rbtree-ck-unsafe` 2,581 MB to 2,033 MB; the others unchanged.

## 1. An arm that re-forms its node keeps the node whole

```python
def is_red(t: Tree) -> Tree & Bool:
  match t:
    case Node{Red{}, l, k, v, r}:
      (Node{Red{}, l, k, v, r}, True{})
    case t0:
      (t0, False{})
```

On main the first arm takes the node apart and builds it again, and so does the second (its default replays the pattern). A unique node is rebuilt in its own cell; a shared one is copied: five loads, a count added to each child, the old node dropped, a new node and later a new count cell, and the copy no longer shares with the tree it came from. Nested patterns do the same to every node they look into: `balance1` opens both grandchildren to test their colour and rebuilds the ones that are not red, and checked `rbtree`'s `ins` opens both children of every node on the path to read one key.

Now, in `emit_match`, a constructor arm of a boxed scrutinee is rewritten first (`arm_self`, the rewrite Nat and word matches already use): a `K{f0, .., fn}` that holds exactly the fields the arm bound, in their places, is the scrutinee. If after that **every path** of the arm uses the scrutinee, and no path uses a field that holds a box for anything else, the arm does not take the node: its word fields are read through the reference and the node is handed on as it came. An arm that opens with a match on a first field that is an enumeration (the colour) is split by that field, read through the reference, so that each colour is decided on its own: `is_red` becomes two reads, and `balance1` takes a grandchild only when it is red.

Sound by construction: the rewrite replaces a node by an equal node, and the scrutinee is bound as an ordinary affine value (used twice, it is kept, like any other). Nothing is read after the scrutinee is handed on except word fields, which are locals by then. The rule needs every path to use the scrutinee because a path that only dropped it would trade main's inline free for a generic drop (`kmeans` showed it: +21% instructions before the rule had that clause).

Counts on `rbtree-ck` (main to this step): shared nodes copied 49.1M to 25.2M (the number of nodes on the insert paths, which is what a hand-written version copies), node allocations 246.5M to 126.8M, count cells 331.7M to 134.4M, count increments 93.7M to 49.1M. Checked `rbtree`, whose type is never shared: node allocations 245.7M to 126.0M, frame words 913M to 514M.

## 2. The take and the wrap of a counted node are inline on the host

`span_fade` (the take of a counted node) and `rfc_wrap` (a new count cell) are `INLINE` on the host and unchanged on the devices. The take is #2114's change (by Lorenzobattistela), included here rather than depended on, because by itself it costs `lexer` +2.9% instructions on this machine. `lexer`'s 834M takes are of a constructor that has static nodes but is never shared; `ctr_take` is emitted for those too, and the inlined counted path, never run, makes each take two instructions longer. So `node_fields` now reads a constructor that is static but not hot in place, as it reads any other uncounted node (`lexer` -0.6%). That relies on the invariant the uncounted path already relies on: only a hot constructor's node is ever counted. `ctr_take` keeps its signature (the effect sources call it).

## 3. The host frees constructor nodes by recursion

`term_sink` goes to `term_fall` on the host: a constructor node is freed at once, its spine field (the one `CID_T` already names) loops, the other fields recurse, and a count is dropped inline for each child, so a child that is still shared costs no call. Past 64 levels, and for anything that is not a constructor node of at most 247 fields, it is `term_drop`'s walk, unchanged; the devices only have the walk. Same decrements, same frees, in another order.

`hashmap` -20% instructions (its final drop; its counts do not change), `deriv` -10%, `nqueens` -24% (59.8M drops of a list that is still shared), `rbtree-ck` -7%.

## 4. A flat def is lent a box its caller still uses

```python
def push(ok: Bool, queen: U32, xs: List<&2, U32>, xss: ..) -> ..:
  match ok:
    case True{}:
      (queen <> xs) <> xss
    case False{}:
      xss
```

`append_safe` uses `xs` again after the call, so on main it adds a count before every `push` and `push` drops it in the arm that does not cons: 59.8M atomic adds and 59.8M drops in `nqueens` where 4.67M lists are consed. Now a call to a flat def that does not loop, with an owned box the caller uses afterwards in a parameter the def owns, calls a second copy of the def (`spin_push_2`) in which that parameter is lent: where the def owns it, it adds the count (`term_keep`); where it only drops it, nothing happens; where it matches it, it reads through the reference. The caller seals the value first (`rfc_seal`: a count cell if it has none), so the def's `term_keep` never has to hand a new reference back.

Never more count operations than main: one add where main added one, none where main added one and dropped it. The caller holds its own reference across the call, which runs on the caller's thread.

`nqueens`: count increments 59.8M to 4.67M, decrements 64.5M to 9.35M.

## Found on the way

- **A leak, by the memory check on an existing test** (`tests/io/chan_shared_node`, 9 live words): a closure made inside the lent copy of a def captured the lent box as if it were still lent, so it added a second count and never dropped its own. The adversarial programs had no closure in a lent def; `lend_flat` has one now, and the wrong version is caught. Sibling looked for: every other place a value crosses into a scope that owns it (frames, tasks, the inlined once-called def); none can hold a lent word, since a lent copy is flat.
- **A leak, by review, before any test showed it**: an operation whose C names its operand twice (`Map.bit`) added the count of a lent word twice. `lend_flat_twice` covers it. Sibling: every template of the C lane goes through the same alias now.
- **A build break**: `ctr_take` is called by the effect sources (`effs/audio.c`, `effs/process_run.c`), so its signature stays as it was (a first version gave it a parameter and 30 `io` tests stopped building).
- **Three regressions on Bend's suite, each fixed before this was opened**: `kmeans` +21% (step 1 without its every-path clause), `histogram` +116% (step 3 with the decrement inline in `term_sink`: clang stopped inlining four spins), `lexer` +2.9% (step 2 as #2114 has it; see there).
- **Main**: ThreadSanitizer reports a race in the scheduler (`monk_step`'s atomic write against a plain read in `row_grow`) on main as on this branch: seen on `lend_flat` at 8 threads, in 4 runs of 5 on main. Not looked into.

## Fixed after review: a use-after-free with an erased field (commit 5)

Found by another agent's program, reproduced here (`tests/rfc/erased_lookahead.bend`): a node type with an erased field among its boxed ones, `EN{-n: Nat, l: E, b: Bool, k: U32, r: E}`, and a lookahead insert. On dd56b9ec it dies with a memory fault at -O3 and under `-DBEND_POISON`; main, the interpreter and the JS lane print `467313141`.

**Cause.** Step 1 rewrites an arm that re-forms its node (`arm_self`): it opens the arm's field binders and replaces a constructor of exactly those binders by the scrutinee. The rewritten arm's binders are lambdas whose bodies are computed again when they are entered. A live binder is entered through `term_open`, which hands back the rewritten body; an erased binder is entered by `emit_body` with a fresh variable (`x.f(Var)`), and the body computed again from that variable no longer matches the constructor, so the arm came back unrewritten. The scrutinee's uses had been counted on the rewritten arm, so its fields were read through the reference (the node kept whole), and on the path that used the fields instead the node was dropped first: in the reproducer, `term_sink` of the left child, then its peeked fields stored. With the erased field later in the node the same mismatch crashed the compiler instead (`b.n` of an unbound use).

It was not slot arithmetic: node slots, peeked fields, the box test and the split all count live fields only, and are right with erased fields (checked below).

**Fix.** A field binder of a rewritten arm answers the rewritten body whatever variable enters it (+42 ttok, `comp.ts` 67,588). Only arms the rule rewrites are touched: the C of all 913 earlier tests, the 7 Perceus ports, the 17 benches and the 22 kernels is byte-identical to before the fix, so every number above stands.

**Siblings tried**, each now a test in `tests/rfc/` (a tree type whose node holds the fields in the order given; same, swap, a peek of the key, a lookahead that re-forms the child, the lookahead insert, a flat def lent the tree with an erased parameter first, unique, shared and forked, and dropped):

| test | fields | on dd56b9ec | fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `erased_first` | `-e1, l, k, r` | memory fault | ok |
| `erased_middle` | `l, -e1, k, r` | compiler crash | ok |
| `erased_last` | `l, k, r, -e1` | compiler crash | ok |
| `erased_two` | `-e1, l, -e2, k, r` | memory fault | ok |
| `erased_two_adjacent` | `l, -e1, -e2, r, k` | compiler crash | ok |
| `erased_after_split` | `c, -e1, l, k, r` (colour split, then erased) | compiler crash | ok |
| `erased_before_split` | `-e1, c, l, k, r` | memory fault | ok |
| `erased_record_sum` | a record with two erased fields among boxes, and a three-armed sum with erased fields, nested | memory fault | ok |
| `erased_lookahead` | the reproducer | memory fault | ok |

Each fixed one agrees on the interpreter, the JS lane and C at 1 and 8 threads with poisoned frees, with main's live count (0), and is clean under ASan and TSan (but for main's scheduler report). The fix reverted is caught by all nine. The rule still fires on them (`same`, the key peek and the lookahead read the node through the reference); a rebuild with a different erased value (`renum`) is not taken for the original, which is conservative. Step 4's lent copies take the right parameter past an erased one (`spin_push_1`), and step 3's table counts slots only (`EXN` has arity 3 for 5 fields).

Why the earlier tests missed it: no program had an erased field in a node the rule reaches.

Rerun on the fixed tree: the native lane against main, the same status on every earlier test; the 9 new tests pass. Four statuses flipped in this run (`string_contains` and `string_ends_with` timed out, `gfx/clicks` and `gfx/window` passed where main's baseline run had failed them): the machine was at a load of about 30, and the four pass on main and on the fix when run alone. The memory check at 1 and at 8 threads: 913 earlier tests, all the same as main (their C is byte-identical to before the fix); the 17 new tests run through the same check one by one (same output, live count 0). Metal: the 46 tests with a `!` call (now with `arm_reform_bang`) pass with the GPU on, as main's 45 do. JS: the emitted JS of the 913 earlier tests is byte-identical to main's (the JS lane never takes the rewrite).

## Checked

- **Native test lane** (every `tests/**/*.bend` with `#|` lines, built and run with the GPU off, compared with those lines): 890 ok, 22 that differ and 1 that times out on main; the same status on every one of them here, plus the 8 new tests.
