- **Metal**: the 45 tests with a `!` call, run with the GPU on, main against this branch: 45 pass on both. The new `arm_reform_bang` test runs steps 1 and 4 on the device.
- **JS**: the emitted JS of 913 tests is byte-identical to main's.
- **Adversarial programs** (now `tests/rfc/arm_reform*.bend`, `lend_flat*.bend`, `drop_fall.bend`): a node unique on one path and shared on another through the same def; a tree two holders share, one rebuilding a path and the other reading the old tree afterwards; a shared node inspected and then dropped by its other holder, on other threads; rebuilds with two fields swapped, with one field changed, and twice; constants; deep recursion both ways; a spine that is not the last field; the same def called by a caller that keeps its tree and by one that gives it away; the same tree twice in one call; a type shared only in a branch that never runs. Each agrees on the direct run, the JS lane and C at 1 and 8 threads, with main's live count (0), and is clean under `-fsanitize=address` and `-fsanitize=thread`, but for a report in main's own scheduler (`monk_step` against `row_grow`) that main gives too.
- **Wrong versions**, each built and run against those programs: the box-field test off; fields compared out of order; the colour split off by one; the peeked fields owned; the split keeping its first field; a lent box not kept, kept twice, not sealed, or owned; a kept word named twice by an operation; a closure capturing a lent box as lent; a shared node freed by the drop; a count cell not freed; a static node freed; a child skipped; no depth bound; a count dropped twice; a node with two holders taken in place. All 18 are caught; four more only change speed.

## Not covered

- **The node is still freed before the call and allocated after it**, and so is its count cell: after this PR `rbtree-ck` does the count operations of a hand-written version (25.2M copies, 49.1M increments, 74.3M decrements) but 126.8M node allocations against 29.4M and 134.4M count cells against 29.4M. By hand edit, keeping the node and its cell across the call is a further -7% instructions on `rbtree-ck-unsafe` and -19% to -25% on `rbtree-unsafe`, with no change in cycles that I could measure at this load. That is #1810's ground (it builds the constructor before the call, and leaves hot constructors and arms whose result feeds another def alone); this PR does not touch it and the two should compose.
- **An outer node whose fallback row hands it back after a nested pattern failed** (`case Node{c, Node{Red{}, ..}, k, r}: ..` then `case t0: t0`) is still taken and rebuilt: the rewrite sees a field consumed by the nested match.
- **A split only on the first field**, and only when it is an enumeration.
- **A lent parameter only for flat defs that do not loop**, and only a single box of a datatype (not an Array, not a pair).
- **The devices keep the walk** for drops, and the out-of-line take and wrap.
- **A drop that knows the node's shape** (code per datatype): by hand a further -6% instructions on `rbtree-ck-unsafe`.
- **The count cell as a separate cell** (against a count inside the node): a design question, not touched.
- Not run: the cluster gates (so not `gates/test.ts`' repeated in-process compiles either), CUDA, Linux, x86, E-cores.

title: Show the source file, line and column in CLI errors
body:
When an imported module has an error, the CLI shows the definition and underlines the token. A developer reading the build log still has to find the file. For example, a typo in `lib/price.bend` previously gave only `Location: total` and the excerpt.

The CLI now appends the canonical source path and one-based line and column. The example produces this location.

```text
--> /project/lib/price.bend:4:12
```

The CLI uses the files the loader already tracked. An error in an import statement points to the statement in the importing file. The batch `--checkup` format stays compatible with existing test fixtures.

## Verification

- The new regression covers an entry-file error, an imported definition, and a missing dependency. It failed on the base commit and passed with this change through the source CLI, the compiled CLI, and emitted JavaScript.
- All 518 existing error snapshots with a source location matched through `--checkup`.
- All 136 `bend-lint` tests passed. The repository gate passed all 56 checks.
- TypeScript 7.0.2 reported the same 10 diagnostics on this branch and the base commit.

title: perf(base): bound the Nat.read length check
body:
`Nat.read` now short-circuits its length check when it sees a 16th character after trimming leading zeros. Inputs with exactly 15 characters still compare against the maximum `Nat`.

In a local benchmark of 100,000 reads of a 128-digit field, native C went from **43 ms to 3 ms**, Bun from **36 ms to 31 ms**, and Node from **68 ms to 21 ms**. Near the cutoff, Bun took **32 ms instead of 17 ms** for 100,000 reads of a 16-digit field.

Existing parser fixtures pass, and BendTT verifies that the old and new readers return the same result for every `String`.

title: perf(base): avoid rescanning key prefixes in Map.has
body:
`Map.has` reuses the key cursor from `Map.get` so deeper splits can resume from the previous character. `Set.has` uses the same path. The extended fixture checks hits through both recursive branches and misses with long and short queries.

Median times from alternating local runs with prebuilt queries and 50% hits:

| Set | Lookups | Native C | Bun | Node |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 short identifiers | 480,000 | 16 → 19 ms | 145 → 93 ms | 71 → 69 ms |
| 16 namespaced identifiers | 112,000 | 106 → 88 ms | 1,006 → 126 ms | 625 → 70 ms |
| Two long keys with one late split | 128,000 | 66 → 97 ms | 266 → 127 ms | 164 → 65 ms |

The two-key case pays to initialize a suffix and reaches a leaf immediately. I kept the cursor implementation for the gains on deeper tries and included the shallow native cost above.

title: A match tests a later enumeration first and does not open a node every arm re-forms
body:
**`comp.ts` is 68,120 ttok, 2,120 over the 66,000 cap** (main 65,995), so `repo-gate` fails until that is settled. Measured on one Mac (M4) under heavy load from other jobs (load average 7 to 25 throughout), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run. Instruction counts are the measure here; cycle figures are marked where they come from a placement sweep.

## What it does

Bend has no `if` and cannot match on a local, so checked code that compares a key and then descends a tree passes the comparison as a parameter and matches it together with the tree, with one level of lookahead (Base's `Map` does this; so does the checked `rbtree` port of the Perceus set):

```python
def ins(t: Tree, o: Cmp, +k: U32, +v: Bool) -> Tree:
  match t o:
    case Node{Red{}, Node{c, a, +ky, vy, b}, kx, vx, r} LT{}:
      Node{Red{}, ins(Node{c, a, ky, vy, b}, U32.cmp(k, ky), k, v), kx, vx, r}
    case Node{Red{}, l, kx, vx, Node{c, a, +ky, vy, b}} GT{}:
      Node{Red{}, l, kx, vx, ins(Node{c, a, ky, vy, b}, U32.cmp(k, ky), k, v)}
    ...
```

`bend.ts`' `match_flatten` compiles the rows into a tree of lambda-matches in binder order: a constructor column decides at its binder's position, its fields take the binder's place, and "a ctr row makes its column strict even under an earlier catch-all". The termination rule wants the shrinking parameter first, so the source cannot put `o` first. The tree the emitter receives therefore opens `t`, then `t.l` (five loads, and the node taken), then `t.r` (the same), and only then tests `o`; on the `LT` path the opened right child is re-formed, on `GT` the left one, on `EQ` both. On main every such open of an owned node frees its cell before the recursive call and allocates a new one after it.

The emitter is free to do otherwise without touching `bend.ts`: at every match it holds all the pending arguments as already-evaluated values (`emit_body`'s `args`), so it can test a later word argument first, and it can decline to open a box whose arms all re-form it. Two rules in `emit_match`, nothing else changed:

1. **A match whose every arm re-forms the node is no match** (`mat_eta`). If each constructor arm uses its fields only to rebuild that same node (`arm_self`), the rebuilt node is used at most once on every path (exactly once if the node is owned), and the arms are then the same term (`term_same`; a field-less arm compared with the others' body at that constructor, a default arm applied to the node), the node is bound whole and the body emitted once. An arm that opens with a match on its first field, an enumeration (a node's colour), counts as one arm per value. 
2. **A later enumeration is tested first** (`mat_cols`, `mat_pick`) when the match is on a box and, for some value of a later argument that is an enumeration (a `Bool`, a `Cmp`, any type of field-less constructors) or an enumeration field of a one-constructor record argument (`Map`'s `String & Bool`), the match would then be no match by rule 1. The emitter tests that word first and emits, per value, the tree with that value's arm taken at every test of it (`mat_pick`: positions follow the arguments each arm consumes, erased binders consume none, a word / `Array` / `IO.OP` match ends the walk, a test of another type is left alone). Inside each copy rule 1 then removes the opens no row of that value reads.

`ins` above becomes: test `t`, its colour, `o`; on `LT` open only `l`, on `GT` only `r`, on `EQ` neither. The decision per match is memoised per match, lent-ness and argument layout.

## Ownership and frees, before and after

For a removed open of node `x`, on each path:

- **owned, unique, uncounted** (checked `rbtree` on main): before, `x`'s fields are loaded, its cell becomes the arm's spare (or is freed), and the re-form allocates (taking the spare) and stores the same fields. After, `x` is passed on; nothing is loaded, freed or allocated.
- **owned, counted** (a hot type): before, `ctr_take` frees the count cell (count 1) or copies the node and drops one count (shared), and the re-form allocates and seals a node holding the same fields. After, the node and its count cell are passed on unchanged.
- **lent**: before, the fields are peeked and the re-form builds a new owned node from lent fields (so the def owns its parameter, as `val_own` records). After, the lent node is passed where the rebuilt one was: a lend to a borrowing callee, or an own fact at an owning position, by the same `val_own` rules as any lent variable. A lent node may also be used on no path (a read-only lookup that ignores the child), which costs nothing; an owned node must be used on every path, so no generic `term_sink` replaces an inline free.

In every case the values reachable from the result are the same; what goes away is a take and a rebuild of the same node (and, for a shared node, a copy). No value is dropped on a path where it was not dropped before, which is why the rule requires the node used on every path when owned. The live heap word count at exit matches main on every program whose C changes (below).

## Reach

Over every program that builds among the tests, the demos, `bench/runtime`, the 22 koru kernels and the Perceus ports (979 programs, 991 more do not build an executable): **35 emit different C**, through 32 defs:

- Base (8): `Map.ins.go`, `Map.get.go`, `Map.has.go`, `Map.pop.go`, `Map.upd.go` (both rules), `String.contains.pre`, `String.order.go` (both), `List.merge.go` (its lent copies; rule 1 only).
- Benches: `hashmap` (`has`), `tree-bitonic` (`flow`, `warp_zip`), `tree-radix` (`merge`), all rule 1.
- Kernels: `textstats` (through `String.contains.pre`).
- Demos: `pure_hvm5_mini` (Map, `str_find`, `str_skip`, `str_word`), `io_rollback_netcode/server` (Map).
- Perceus ports: `rbtree`, `rbtree-ck` (`ins` both rules, the balance defs rule 1), the `@unsafe` spellings (balance defs), `deriv` (`add`, `mul`).

One thread, GPU off, instructions retired (least of 3 interleaved runs; the noise is about 0.1%):

`rbtree-ck`'s counts include kernel work that grows under memory pressure (main read 74.1G to 81.1G across sessions on the same binary); the figures above are from the quietest session for each.

Cycles, checked `rbtree`, 16 placements of the segments (4-byte steps), 2 interleaved rounds, least / median / most (load average 9 to 10, so wide):

| build | instructions | cycles |
|---|---:|---|
| main | 21.85G | 8.68 / 8.90 / 9.73G |
| this | 12.12G | 6.23 / 6.44 / 6.94G |
| hand bound (selector-first `ins` transplanted) | 13.06G | 5.49 / 5.68 / 6.09G |

| #2207 | 14.64G | 2.89 / 3.10 / 3.57G |

On main the change's cycles sit above the hand bound's at the normal stride and level with it at the odd one: main's checked `rbtree` is the one program with the L1D set conflicts described in section 25's cause 4, and moving allocations changes how hard they hit. With them out of the way (odd stride) the change takes main from 5.14G to 3.64G median (1.41x); on #2207, which has no such conflicts, 3.10G to 2.61G (1.19x).

## Checks

- **Memory**: the 35 programs and the new test, emitted with main and with this, built with `-DBEND_POISON` and a count of live heap words at exit (`heap_alloc` / `heap_free` patched): same output, exit code and live count (0) on every one, at one thread and at eight.
- The same memory check for `#2207 + this` against #2207: same on all 36, at one thread and at eight (the new test faults the same way on both: see the end).
- **Native and JS lanes** on the 22 changed tests and the new one: no status differs from main (`io/args` and `io/args_bytes` fail the same way on main and here: they want arguments).
- **Interpreter, JS and C** (1 and 8 threads, poisoned, live count) on five adversarial programs (an owned, a lent and a shared tree; a selector computed from the tree; arms reading a child on one value and keeping it on another; default rows; the node's colour matched first; three-deep patterns; an erased field before the children; a record of two enumerations; a tuple selector; lists; arms that re-form the node but answer differently; a node re-formed twice or dropped): equal everywhere.
- **Metal**: `tests/base/map_leaf_eq` (the one changed test with a `!` call) prints its `#|` lines with the GPU on.
- **Wrong versions**: 18 edits of the rule, each run against the adversarial programs and the new test (C at 1 and 8 threads with poisoned frees and the live count, and JS). Caught (8): a pick that takes the first arm, a record field one off, no arm comparison, field-less arms not compared, the default arm not compared, the colour split re-forming the wrong colour, the hoisted test's values reversed, the hoisted copies not pruned (the emitter recurses until the stack overflows). Sound and only slower or larger (4): a node used twice let through (`term_keep`), an owned node dropped whole (`term_sink`), every node treated as lent, a default arm left unpruned. Not caught (6): position errors in `mat_pick` (fields not counted, erased binders counted, a default shifted, a binder treated as a test), the record field index one off, and the type guard removed; in every test program these make the rule fire less, never wrongly, since a wrong position meets no test of the selector's type. The field-index error would be unsound on a record whose two fields are enumerations of one type when pruning one field's test by the other's values leaves the match with nothing to open; no program here has that shape and the test does not catch it.
- `tsc` (strict, on `comp.ts` alone): no new errors.
- New test `tests/run/match_columns.bend` (interpreter 14 s): every shape above, on owned, lent and shared trees, met at run time on leaves and nodes.
- Five small Perceus ports (`rbtree`, `rbtree-ck` and their `@unsafe` spellings at 3,000 inserts, `deriv` at 6): interpreter, JS and C (1 and 8 threads, poisoned, live count 0) equal, on main and on #2207.

## Costs

- `comp.ts` +2,125 ttok.
- Emit time: unchanged on the 17 benches (2.97 s against 3.07 s in total, noise); +0.1 to +0.2 s (1.4x to 2.1x) on programs that use `Map` (`tests/base/map_ops` 0.25 s to 0.40 s, `pure_hvm5_mini` 0.50 s to 0.60 s). The cost is the arm comparisons (`term_same`) repeated at each level of a deep match; memoising per match and building the picked trees eagerly took it from about 2x to about 1.5x.

## Not covered

- A match that tests the selector only after a match on another argument that is not a box (a word, an `Array`) is left as it is past that match.
- Rule 1 compares arms structurally: an arm with a match on another argument that the other arms bind as a plain variable (a default row `t0 _` beside rows that open a record) is not the same term, so such a match is kept.
- An enumeration nested two records deep (`Bool & Bool & U32` as a tuple of a tuple) is not a candidate; a flat record is.
- Dependent types: arms are compared with their type annotations ignored, as `term_same` does; an argument whose type depends on the scrutinee's constructor would take the first arm's annotations.
- Measured on an M4 under load; x86, Linux, CUDA, the cluster gates not run.

Stacks cleanly on #2207 (branch `opt/match-columns-stacked` on nicolas-abril/bend: this diff on #2207's tip, the duplicate `path_use` removed; 69,551 ttok). Found on the way, in #2207 itself (not this change): a type with an erased field before its children (`EN{-n: Nat, l: E, b: Bool, k: U32, r: E}`) with the lookahead insert above faults on #2207 (`memory fault`, also with `-DBEND_POISON`) and runs on main; the arm that keeps `l` whole sinks it with `term_sink` and then stores its fields. Reproducer (38 lines):

```python
import Base

type E is Data:
  EL{}
  EN{-n: Nat, l: E, b: Bool, k: U32, r: E}

def edig(t: E, acc: U32) -> U32:
  match t:
    case EL{}:
      U32.add(U32.mul(acc, 29), 5)
    case EN{n, l, b, k, r}:
      edig(r, U32.add(U32.mul(edig(l, U32.add(U32.mul(acc, 29), Bool.to_u32(b))), 137), k))

def eins(t: E, o: Cmp, +k: U32) -> E:
  match t o:
    case EL{} _:
      EN{0n, EL{}, True{}, k, EL{}}
    case EN{n, EN{m, a, b2, +ky, c}, b, kx, r} LT{}:
      EN{n, eins(EN{m, a, b2, ky, c}, U32.cmp(k, ky), k), b, kx, r}
    case EN{n, EL{}, b, kx, r} LT{}:
      EN{n, EN{0n, EL{}, False{}, k, EL{}}, b, kx, r}
    case EN{n, l, b, kx, EN{m, a, b2, +ky, c}} GT{}:
      EN{n, l, b, kx, eins(EN{m, a, b2, ky, c}, U32.cmp(k, ky), k)}
    case EN{n, l, b, kx, EL{}} GT{}:
      EN{n, l, b, kx, EN{0n, EL{}, True{}, k, EL{}}}
    case EN{n, l, b, kx, r} EQ{}:
      EN{n, l, Bool.not(b), kx, r}

def ebuild(+n: Nat, t: E) -> E:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      t
    case 1n+m:
      +x = U32.mod(U32.mul(U32.from_nat(n), 2654435761), 1000)
      ebuild(m, eins(t, U32.cmp(x, 500), x))

def main() -> U32:
  edig(ebuild(5n, EL{}), 2)
```

title: test(proof): Array.get and Array.set on perfect trees, with the U32 facts they need (#2059)
body:
Closes the gap #2059 describes: the U32 facts behind Array's descent, and with them Array laws that hold on any perfect tree.

## What it proves (`tests/proof/array_perfect_tree.bend`, Base only)

The U32 facts, phrased the way Array computes them. `shln(1, d)` is what `Array.size` returns for a tree of depth d.

| law | statement |
|---|---|
| `u32_shln_one` | `to_nat(shln(1, d)) == 2^d`, for d < 32 |
| `u32_shr_shln_one` | `shr(shln(1, e+1)) == shln(1, e)` (the half size in `get.go` / `swap.go`) |
| `u32_and_low_mask` | `and(x, sub(shln(1, d), 1)) == x` when `to_nat(x) < 2^d` (the mask in `get.at` / `swap.at`) |
| `u32_is_lt_shln_one` | `is_lt(x, shln(1, e)) == Nat.is_lt(to_nat(x), 2^e)` (the branch bit) |
| `u32_sub_shln_one` | `to_nat(sub(x, shln(1, e))) == to_nat(x) - 2^e` for `to_nat(x)` in `[2^e, 2^(e+1))` (the right half's index) |

The Array laws, on `build(d, l)`, the perfect tree of depth d over the first 2^d entries of a list:

| law | statement |
|---|---|
| `array_get_perfect` | `Array.get(Nat, build(d, l), x) == (build(d, l), nth(l, to_nat(x)))` |
| `array_set_perfect` | `Array.set(Nat, build(d, l), x, v) == build(d, upd(l, to_nat(x), v))`, given 2^d ≤ len(l) |

Both hold for every d < 32 and every index below 2^d.

## Why the laws are stated on `build(d, l)`

A proof about a program that threads an array usually holds the array erased: Arrays are `Type`, so they can't be copied into several lemma calls. Lemmas whose proof matches on a live array can't be applied to such an array. `build(d, l)` describes the array by a live list, so these laws apply wherever the list is known. I used them to prove an in-place array algorithm correct (a Taylor shift, by simulation against the same template run on a list), with nothing assumed.

## How the U32 facts are proved

Each goes through the bits of a Word, with no extra word laws beyond Base:

- **Borrow chain.** `sub(2^d, 1)` is d ones (`borrow`, `sub_one`).
- **Set bit.** Subtracting 2^e from a value with bit e set clears that bit (`sub_set`).
- **Comparison.** `Word.cmp` agrees with `Nat.cmp` one bit at a time (`cmp_to_nat`).
- **Mask.** Masking a word below 2^d with a word worth 2^d - 1 keeps it (`wmask`).
- **Shifts.** `shl`/`shr` move 2^d structurally.

## Checks

- `bun bend2/main.ts tests/proof/array_perfect_tree.bend` prints `{==}` in about 0.9 s.
- `--verdict` prints `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.

## Notes

- **Self-contained.** Every lemma is proved in the file, including the Nat order and arithmetic kit, so it doesn't depend on #2142 or any package. It overlaps #2142's goal (the `2^d` word and `shl` lemmas) but not its text. I'm happy to rebase onto #2142's lemmas if you'd rather keep one copy.
- **Size.** At about 1,100 lines it is much larger than the other proof tests. If Base wants these laws, the U32 section could move there and the test would shrink to the Array part.
- **Element type.** `build` and the laws are written for Nat elements. A generic version needs a default value for `nth` on short lists.

title: Bend is not a prove-able language
body:
### What Bend should do

```python
I love your project and you're and I don't mean to be disrespectful. So please forgive the harsh title.
But:
You are repeating the age old error every programming language ever invented has made. A language without a obligatory unit system for ALL values is not provable.
```

### Why

This is what mathematicians often overlook: **There are no pure numbers / values in real life.** Every value has an implicit (sic!) meaning / unit. If it is only implicit and not explicit the whole program becomes not prove-able.

If you think a unit system should be optional, think again, or ask Nasa how they lost some of their Mars missions.

To prove that a parameter or return value conforms to expectations it's unit MUST be made explicit. There is no way around that.
This does not only apply to conversion errors and confusions of scale but also to logic erros resulting of drifting implicit units between functions or libraries.

I understand that this is much to ask of a programming language, but if your goal is a prove-able programming language for AI agents then it needs to be done.

Just me two cents. Keep up your good work.

title: Re-checking Bend proofs in Lean's kernel: all 86 positive proof tests re-check
body:
I've been translating Bend definitions and proofs into Lean 4 so that Lean's kernel re-checks them: https://github.com/alstrup/bend2lean. It loads files with Bend's own loader (`bend2/bend.ts`) and translates the core terms one-to-one, Base included. Lean never sees Bend's checker, only the terms.

**On `tests/proof`** (main at `0e2f38f7`, Lean 4.35), scored against each test's own expected output:

- **Positive tests:** all 86 that Bend accepts re-check completely in Lean.
- **Negative tests:** 32 of the 35 that Bend rejects are rejected by Lean too. None is accepted with an invalid proof. Of the other three, two are rejected by Bend only for `@unsafe` IO code or an open law, and one doesn't translate.
- **Coverage:** this includes lexicographic recursion (compiled to nested `Nat.rec`), non-uniform nested types, and `Type`-valued type arguments.

**How the core maps:**

| Bend | Lean |
|---|---|
| a λ-match | `match` |
| `{a == b : T}` | a Type-valued equality, since Bend's equalities are data |
| `%e : P` | its J eliminator, which is exactly Bend's rewrite rule |
| `Word(n)` | an indexed `BWord n` |
| user types | `inductive` |

`IO` code is skipped as effect code.

**A larger example.** A fast in-place Taylor shift on `Array` comes with a Bend proof that it computes `p(x+1)`. The proof uses the `Array.get`/`Array.set` laws of #2213. The whole chain is 266 definitions, and the result is a Lean theorem about `ashift` itself, using only Lean's standard axioms. The compiled Bend code runs about 7× faster than the same in-place algorithm written in Lean.

Bend is cool. The checker is fast, and its error messages are precise enough that the ~1,500 lines of proofs behind this came together quickly, even without tactics. Being able to prove code and run it at C speed in the same language is a great combination.

**Questions:**

1. Is a second, independent check of `tests/proof` useful to you, for example as an optional gate?
2. If so, should it stay an outside tool, or live in the repo? It reads `bend.ts`'s term shapes, so it breaks when they change.
3. Is there anything in `tests/proof` you would expect a second checker to disagree on?

title: fix(comp): avoid JavaScript stack overflows when counting lines
body:
Counting the lines in this repository's README overflows the default Node stack. Counting the lines in the changelog also overflows the default Bun stack. Both failures occur in an ordinary call to `List.length(&2, String, String.lines(text))`.

| Input file | Node on main | Bun on main | Node and Bun with this fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Stack overflow | 281 | 281 |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Stack overflow | Stack overflow | 984 |

Both files end with a newline. The counts include the final empty field, as specified by `String.lines`.

The JavaScript backend now splits strings and counts list elements with loops. The splitter advances one Bend character at a time. This preserves separators next to empty fields and prevents matches inside a packed character. The regression test also checks partial application and the Base reduction for `String.split` on `SCon`.

I ran the new regression and six related fixtures on the Bend CLI, generated JavaScript under Node and Bun, and native CPU. All seven passed on each path. The repository gate passed 56/56.

Related to #798.

title: A let of U32 operations moves below a non-tail call that does not read it
body:
**`comp.ts` is 66,427 ttok, 427 over the 66,000 cap** (main 65,995), so `repo-gate` fails until that is settled. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run. One commit (`90509f4d`).

## What it does

A `let` whose value is U32 operations moves below the next call that pushes a frame, when the call does not read it and every variable it reads is read after the call anyway. The frame keeps those operands instead of the result, and the continuation computes it again.

`queens`' `solve` binds the next sibling's bit and columns before its child call and reads them only in the sibling call after it:

```python
case 1n+g False{} False{} Stat0{}:
  +cc = U32.and(full, U32.not(U32.or(nc, U32.or(nl, nr))))   # the child call reads cc, cb, cn
  +cb = U32.and(cc, U32.sub(0, cc))
  +cn = U32.or(nc, cb)
  +b2 = U32.and(sib, U32.sub(0, sib))                        # only the sibling call reads b2, n2
  +n2 = U32.or(cols, b2)
  solve(g, U32.is_zero(sib), U32.is_eq(n2, full), U32.sub(sib, b2), n2, .., cols, ld, rd, full,
    solve(g, U32.is_zero(cc), U32.is_eq(cn, full), .., nc, nl, nr, full, Stat0{}, sols, U32.inc(nodes)), 0, 0)
```

On main every child call stores `g, sib, cols, ld, rd, full, b2, n2` and the continuation's id (9 words) and reads 8 back; `sib` and `cols` are in the frame anyway, so `b2` and `n2` are two stores and two loads that three ALU operations replace. Here the frame is 7 words.

## The rule

`let_sink(x, ty)`, called by `emit_body` before `anf`, so the C, Metal and JS lanes all take it:

- x binds one name to a tree of U32 operations (`U32.*` with a C template; all are total, division and modulo by zero included) over variables and constants;
- the lets after x, if any, are such lets too, and what follows them is a call that pushes a frame (not flat; one binding, so a parallel `let` is left alone);
- the call does not read x, and every variable x reads is read after the call.

x then moves to just after the call. In a chain each let moves as far as it can: above, `cc`, `cb`, `cn` stay and `b2`, `n2` move.

Why it is sound: a U32 operation cannot stop the program, and values do not change, so computing it after the call gives the same word; the call does not read it; its operands are the same variables, still bound after the call since they are read there. A let that calls a def or does `Nat` arithmetic (which can stop at 2^48) never moves: `tests/run/let_sink_abort.bend` has a let that must stop the program before a call that never returns.

## Reach

Of 1,940 programs (17 benches, 18 demos, the tests, 22 koru kernels, 7 Perceus ports), 975 emit C on both; 3 emit different C: `queens`, `tests/reg/wnf_memo_bound_key`, `tests/run/expr_interpreter`. No demo, kernel or Perceus port changes. A variant that also moves a let past later independent lets reaches nothing more among the benches, demos, kernels and ports, so it is not in.

## Measured

`queens`, one thread, GPU off, M4, quiet machine; cycles over 16 placements x 2 rounds, least / median / most:

| build | instructions | cycles |
|---|---:|---|
| main | 89.82G | 21.81 / 22.12 / 22.29G |
| this PR | 87.57G (-2.5%) | 22.12 / 22.28 / 22.37G |
| `opt/integration` (the 14 drafts) | 71.33G | 18.50 / 18.56 / 18.71G |
| `opt/integration` + this change | 66.81G (-6.3%) | 18.10 / 18.21 / 18.39G (-1.9%) |

**On main this saves instructions and no cycles** (the median is 0.7% higher, the ranges overlap): main's `solve` still sets up a C frame and tests `seq` on every entry, and the two words do not show. On `opt/integration`, where #2176 and #2177 have removed that, it is -1.9% at every placement. The 16 other benches emit the same C as main, so their instructions are unchanged.

## Checks

- the 3 programs whose C changes and the two new tests: C at default threads, JS and the interpreter print the same as main; the memory check (`-DBEND_POISON`, live heap words counted at exit) gives 0 live words at 1 and at 8 threads, as main; `queens` at full size on C at 1 and 8 threads and on Metal (full and small sizes);
- every other test emits main's C, so its native-lane status is main's;
- 7 wrong versions of the pass: the 4 that change results (moving a let the call reads, dropping the let, putting it inside the call's argument, moving a let that calls a def) are each caught by the new tests; the other 3 only change which lets move (past a parallel let, any intrinsic, without the liveness test).

Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86, `tsc`.

## Context

From a study of `queens`' gap to its C twin (1.46x in cycles on main, 1.22x on `opt/integration`): a ladder of C twins taking Bend's constraints one at a time, frame counters, hand edits and a profile-guided bound. Of the causes the compiler can remove by itself, recomputing these frame words is the one over 5% of instructions on `opt/integration` that applies to main; the other, an answered call that pushes no frame (-13% instructions, -3.3% cycles on #2177), needs #2177 and is on `opt/queens-early` of nicolas-abril/bend. Tools and numbers: `bench/pgo-queens` there.

title: A heap node's U32 and tag fields share a word when that drops its size class (rbtree ports -9% to -31% cycles)
body:
**`comp.ts` is 66,856 ttok, 856 over the 66,000 cap** (main 65,995, +861), so `repo-gate` fails until that is settled; every other `repo` check passes locally (55 / 56). Measured on one Mac (M4) under load from other sessions, not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run.

## What it does

A heap node keeps each field in its own 64-bit word, so a `Bool` or an enumeration tag takes a whole word, and the node's block is the next power of two. The Perceus `rbtree`'s

```python
type Tree is Data:
  Leaf{}
  Node{color: Color, lchild: Tree, key: U32, value: Bool, rchild: Tree}
```

is 5 words in an 8-word block, 3 of them for 34 bits. This PR lays `color`, `key` and `value` in one word, `key | color << 32 | value << 33`, so `Node` is 3 words in a 4-word block. The program cannot tell: the layout is per constructor and every build and read goes through the same two functions.

- `node_pack(k)` (`lay_bits` gives each word's bits: a tag's `ceil(log2 arms)`, 32 for a `w32`, 64 for a box or `w64`): the `w32` and tag words are packed first-fit, widest first, into words of at most 56 bits (so at most one `U32` per word), the shared words first, then the boxes in order. It is used only when that lowers the node's size class.
- `ctr_build` writes each shared word as `(u64)((u32)(x) & mask) << shift | ...` (the static image too); `node_fields` reads a field back as `(u32)(w >> shift) & mask`; `c_header` gives the runtime the new arity and spine.
- Not for Base's runtime types (`OWNED`), nor for a type that foreign C names (`CID(..)` in an effect source) or takes (in a foreign def's signature), nor anything those hold (`ty_fix`): such C writes the words itself.

## The condition, and why it suffices

The layout is a function of the constructor alone, the same in every def, closure, fork task, `!` call and polymorphic caller of one binary, so a node built anywhere is read correctly everywhere. Where a node's words are observed:

- **Emitted code** (host and device, one source): only `ctr_build` writes them and only `node_fields` reads them (fresh, shared through `ctr_take`, or peeked through a lent root), and both use `node_pack`. A generic field is a box (64 bits) and is never packed, so instances agree.
- **The runtime's generic walks** (`term_drop`, `span_fade` under `ctr_take`, `rfc_seal`): they read each word as a term. A shared word is below 2^56 (masks on write keep it there even if a tag were out of range), so its tag byte is 0 and its RFC bit clear: a trivial term, skipped like any `U32` field today. `CID_T` carries the new arity (the block's class) and the spine at its new slot.
- **Foreign and IO C**: excluded types keep their layout. The runtime itself names only constructors of Base's runtime types (`OWNED`) and `List`'s `Con` and `Nil`, whose fields are boxes.
- **The JS lane and the interpreter**: untouched; the JS of all 985 test and demo programs that emit JS is byte-identical.
- **The value**: a tag word is its constructor's index (built by `emit_ctr`, `val_arms`, `emit_zero` or a comparison), below 2^bits; a `w32` is a `u32`.

## Reach, counted before building

A hook over the checked terms (Base, the tests, the demos, the 17 benches, the 22 koru kernels and their 17 forked ports, the 7 Perceus ports; 862 files that check) and a run-time count of every node built, per constructor, in the 63 runnable programs. Branch `bench/representation` (nicolas-abril/bend) has both, the scripts, the other candidates and their counts, and every measurement below.

| | count |
|---|---:|
| heap-node constructors | 838 |
| ... with a tag word | 20 |
| ... where sharing a word lowers the size class (this PR) | 5: the 4 rbtree ports' `Node`, `tests/reg/show_shared_layout`'s `Other` (25 words to 1) |
| ... where it would not (left alone) | 15 |
| records (non-recursive) that are boxed into nodes at run time | at most 10 boxes per run anywhere |

On a hot path: only the rbtree ports, 340M to 504M `Node`s per run. No bench or kernel builds a node this changes: their hot nodes are boxes only (`tree-bitonic`'s `Node`, 4.26G per run; `tree-radix`, `tree-matmul`), a word and boxes (`merkle`'s `Mn`, `hashmap`'s `CCons`), or three `U32` (`kmeans`' `Sl`, 168M per run, which two shared words cannot hold under 2^56).

As built, the C changes in 4 Perceus ports, raytrace (a `CID_T` entry only: `Hit` is never boxed at run time), 4 demos (pong's `Pong`, slash boss's `Cue`, `Sound`, `Voice`, the netcode walkers test's `Key`, pure_hvm5_mini's `Bind`), 9 tests and the 2 new tests. Every other bench, kernel, forked port, Perceus port, test and demo emits byte-identical C.

## Results

M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`. Instructions (median), and P-core cycles least / median / most over 16 placements (0 to 15 `nop`s before the first segment), 3 rounds in all, the least per placement; load average 6 to 18 from other sessions.

| Perceus port | instructions, main | this | | cycles, main | this | this / main |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| `rbtree` | 22.21G | 19.21G | -13.5% | 8.32G / 8.51G / 8.81G | 7.41G / 7.81G / 7.93G | 0.846 to 0.936 |
| `rbtree-ck` | 81.81G | 69.71G | -14.8% | 15.50G / 20.52G / 23.76G | 11.98G / 14.10G / 15.89G | 0.614 to 0.778 |
| `rbtree-unsafe` | 11.30G | 10.08G | -10.8% | 2.75G / 2.83G / 2.91G | 2.61G / 2.68G / 2.79G | 0.917 to 0.978 |
| `rbtree-ck-unsafe` | 54.49G | 45.70G | -16.1% | 11.35G / 13.88G / 15.51G | 9.14G / 9.88G / 12.64G | 0.638 to 0.893 |

Every placement is faster on all four. The `-ck` ports keep every fifth tree alive, so they are bound by memory and their ranges are wide under load; the median gain there is about 30%.

Maximum resident set: rbtree 270 MB to 132 MB (one run each).

Where the gain comes from, `rbtree` and `rbtree-ck` (a variant that shares the words but pads the node back to 5 words, so the block stays at 8):

| port | build | instructions | cycles | over main, per placement |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `rbtree` | main | 22.07G | 8.36G / 8.59G / 8.86G | |
| | words shared, block kept | 19.97G | 8.37G / 8.45G / 8.74G | 0.969 to 1.019 |
| | this PR | 19.18G | 7.70G / 7.85G / 8.06G | 0.891 to 0.937 |
| `rbtree-ck` | main | 81.68G | 15.34G / 21.32G / 25.84G | |
| | words shared, block kept | 78.33G | 15.02G / 19.69G / 22.96G | 0.692 to 1.147 |
| | this PR | 68.17G | 11.79G / 13.80G / 16.26G | 0.546 to 0.818 |

Sharing the words alone saves instructions (one load for three fields) and no cycles; the cycles come with the smaller block. That is why the rule asks for a lower size class, and leaves the 15 constructors where it would not drop alone.

The rest of the suite: the 16 other benches, the 22 kernels, the 17 forked ports and the other 3 Perceus ports emit byte-identical C, so they are not rerun. raytrace (its `CID_T` differs in one entry): 83.02G / 83.24G instructions on main, 83.20G / 83.16G here, two runs each.

## Checks

- **The native lane on every program whose C changes** (13 tests and demos, the 2 new tests), main against this branch: C lane, JS lane and interpreter, and the C with `-DBEND_POISON` and a live-word count at exit (`heap_alloc` / `heap_free` patched) at 1 and 8 threads. All the same on both, every test's `#|` lines met, 0 live words at exit everywhere. The other 919 tests and demos that build emit byte-identical C, so their status cannot differ.
- **New tests**: `tests/run/node_pack.bend` (three packed types built, matched, rebuilt in place, shared, captured by a closure and a partial application, held in a `List` and a `Maybe`, dropped, handed to a fork and to a `!` call, read down a deep spine, and laid out in the static image; keys with the top bit set), `tests/io/node_pack_foreign.bend` (foreign C writes a type that would pack). Interpreter, JS and C agree; also with a 1,000,000-node spine (C only, the interpreter overflows), and on Metal (`--gpu on`) for `node_pack`.
- **Wrong versions**, each caught by the new tests (C, poisoned frees, 1 and 8 threads):

| wrong version | new tests | the repo's 9 tests whose C changes |
|---|---|---|
| pack a type foreign C writes | caught (faults) | not caught |
| a tag read without its mask | caught (hashes) | not caught |
| a field one bit short of its width | caught (hashes) | caught (`bst_insert`) |
| `CID_T` keeps the old word count | caught (faults) | not caught |
| the spine's slot not remapped | caught (102,260 live words at exit) | not caught |
| two `U32` in one word (the top byte then holds data) | caught (faults) | not caught |
| no mask on write | not caught: a tag is in range by construction, the mask is a guard | not caught |
| a reused node's class from the old word count | caught (faults) | caught (`bst_insert`) |

The spine and two-`U32` versions passed the first spellings of `node_pack.bend`; the test now shares and drops nodes and drops a big tree next to a live one.

- `tsc`: no new errors in `comp.ts` (the same 3 as main).
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: 55 / 56, the ttok cap.

## Not covered

- Not run: the cluster gates (`test`, `perf`, `ping`, `safe`); CUDA; Linux.
- Records in registers and frames are untouched: packing their words would add shifts where nothing is loaded or stored (101 of 704 records could lose a word; queens' `Stats`, lexer's `Mode`, raytrace's `Hit`, tree-radix's `Chk` are on hot paths, none bounded by hand).
- A node whose shared words do not lower its size class is left alone (15 constructors, none hot): fewer stores against more shifts, not measured.
- Two `U32` cannot share a word: the word would no longer look like a trivial term to `term_drop` and `span_fade`. Allowing it (and so `kmeans`' `Sl`) needs the runtime to know a node's raw words.
- A type that foreign C takes or names keeps its layout even where that C only passes it through.

title: Benchmark movement proof checking on a 120 × 80 board
body:
**TL;DR** — Adds one command to benchmark 38,400 moves on a 120 × 80 board. The companion checker optimization in #2220 cuts the time for this proof from **9.88 s to 1.54 s**.

### Reproduce

From the repository root, run:

```sh
demos/app_win_is_bug_2d/bench_movement.sh bun bend2/main.ts
```

The script enlarges a temporary copy of the game and times the no-win movement proof. It checks four directions from every cell. The separate rendered-board law is omitted from the timing.

### Why add this benchmark?

Larger maps require checking more cells, and comparing larger coordinates takes more recursive steps. The five existing checker benchmarks never triggered the shortcut in #2220. This workload makes its performance impact measurable.

The figures above are median wall times from three runs per version on an Apple M4 Pro with Bun 1.2.17, including CLI startup.

title: Speed up proof checking for concrete Nat pairs that count down together
body:
**TL;DR** — Skip repeated countdowns on known numbers during proof checking. The same game proof checks in **1.54 s instead of 9.88 s (6.4× faster)** on the benchmark in #2219.

### How it works

When a function reduces `f(a + 1, b + 1)` directly to `f(a, b)`, the checker can remove the shared count in one step. For example, `f(119, 121)` reduces to `f(0, 2)`. The original function handles the base case and determines the result. The shortcut requires concrete operands and matches the recursive call by structure.

### Evidence

- The regression proof covers equal and unequal inputs, a symbolic case, and a similar function that must perform work after recursion. It passed locally. The checker also rejected the game proof when a wall was removed to open a path to the flag.
- Timings are medians of three runs per version on an Apple M4 Pro with Bun 1.2.17. The shortcut fired zero times across the five existing checker benchmarks.
- This changes proof evaluation. Review should focus on the recursion matcher and its handling of symbolic terms. The full upstream validation gates are still pending.

title: An e-graph over each arm, and three rules that reshape defs: a default constructor dropped, one call site, fusion
body:
**`comp.ts` is 80,977 ttok** (main 65,995: +14,982); the cap was set aside for this draft by the owner. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run. Numbers are against the integration branch (`opt/integration` at bae64757 on nicolas-abril/bend, which merges #2153, #2161, #2162, #2175, #2177, #2180, #2188, #2207, #2211, #2217, #2218 and others onto main 0e2f38f7) with this branch merged onto a copy of it, unless a line says main. Scripts, raw results and the debug build: https://github.com/nicolas-abril/bend-eqsat (private).

## What it does

A pass on the checked terms, in `file_book`, before emission, C lane only (like #2175's `acc_def` and #2180's `def_fix`). Two parts:

- **An e-graph over each arm.** A def's case tree (its lambdas, its matches, a fork's `let`) stays as it is. Each arm's expression below it (calls, constructors, literals; a `let`'s name is its value's class; a closure is a leaf whose own arms go through the pass in turn) goes into an e-graph: hash-consed nodes, union-find, congruence rebuilding. The rules below add equal terms for up to 8 rounds or 2,000 nodes, then the cheapest term comes back out by a static cost model, and a class read twice whose type is all words is bound once by a `let` (common subexpressions). An arm changes only if that saves at least 1 in the model, so an arm no rule improves is left exactly as it was.
- **Three rules that make new defs or change a type.** Where a rule builds a def it writes it as an unannotated core term and has bend.ts' own `def_check` elaborate it: types, quantities and termination are checked again, and a refusal leaves the program as it was.

```python
# isqrt (koru): the Newton iterate is computed twice, as an argument and in the flag
iter(n, y, Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n),
     Nat.is_lt(Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n), y))
# compiled as if written
+x = Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n)
iter(n, y, x, Nat.is_lt(x, y))
```

## The rules

Term rules, in the e-graph; each is an equation of pure terms:

| rule | holds because |
|---|---|
| fold: a U32 operation on literals is its value; `Nat.add` / `Nat.mul` too when the value is at most 2^32 - 1 | evaluation (a larger Nat literal is not a word) |
| units: `x + 0`, `x - 0`, `x * 1`, `x \| 0`, `x ^ 0`, `x & ~0` (U32), `x + 0n`, `x * 1n` (Nat) | U32 wraps; a Nat operand is already under 2^48 - 1 |
| `U32.inc(x)` is `x + 1` | its definition |
| `Nat.add` commutes and reassociates; `Nat.mul` commutes | no partial sum of Nats exceeds the whole, so both orders pass 2^48 - 1 together (#2175's argument); the same product. `Nat.mul` does not reassociate: a later 0 hides an earlier overflow |
| unfold: a call to a def that does not recurse is its body at its arguments; a match in it on an argument whose class holds a constructor or a Nat literal takes that arm (case of a known constructor); a def that recurses unfolds only through a match on a constructor | evaluation; each unfolding of a recursion consumes a constructor, so it stops |
| fusion: `f(g(ys))` is `f~g(ys)` | by construction of `f~g` (below) |

U32 and F32 reordering hold too (U32 wraps; Base proves `U32.add_comm`) but are left out: they never lowered a cost and made every arm's e-graph grow each round. None of Base's other laws is an equation between runtime terms this pass meets (they are about `Word`, `Equal`, `Nat.max` and foreign signatures).

Rules that change defs or types:

- **A default constructor dropped** (type level, whole program). A datatype `D{} | P{f..}` with no parameters and `U32` / `Nat` fields, whose `D{}` acts as `P{0, ..}` at every match the program runs: each match on it has an arm for both, and `D`'s arm equals `P`'s arm at zero fields in the e-graph under the hypothesis `D{} = P{0, ..}`. That makes "replace every `D{}` by `P{0, ..}`" a simulation (values related by it go to related results at every match), so `D{}` is built as `P{0, ..}`, every `D` arm is dropped, and the type keeps one constructor: no tag word, one arm where there were two. Checked over every def the program reaches; refused if a foreign def, `main` or a def's type names the type or `D`. This is `queens`' `Stat0{}` as `Stats{0, 0}` (section 30's step 1 of the optimisation log).
- **One call site.** A def `d` whose case tree ends, in every arm, in an expression with exactly one call to the same def `g` (one argument, a frame or more in the model, not `d`, not `@unsafe`) becomes `d(ps) = d~k(g(d~s(qs)), ps)`: `d~s` is `d`'s case tree answering each arm's argument (over the parameters it matches or reads), `d~k` the same tree with the call replaced by its value. For every input `d~s` takes the arm `d` takes, so `d~k` answers what `d` did; `g` now runs before the rest of its arm. A version that would read an affine parameter twice is refused by the checker. This is `listops`' `runOne`.
- **Fusion (deforestation).** `f(g(ys))`, with `g` a recursion that builds what `f`, a one-parameter recursion, takes apart, is `f~g(ys)`: `g`'s case tree with `f` applied at each leaf (`f` is strict, so `f` of a match is the match of `f`'s), elaborated and checked to terminate by `def_check`. Its arms go through the e-graph like any def's: `f` unfolds on the constructor the leaf builds, and `f(g(y))` folds back into `f~g(y)` (the induction step). `f~g` is kept only if no call to `g` is left in it, and only call sites the model prefers take it. With the shared-word rule, `check(make(d))` (binarytrees) becomes `d` steps: `make(p)` twice in an arm builds equal trees, so `check~make(p)` twice is one call.

**What can differ from main**, as with #2175 and #2180: every rule is an equation of pure terms, so a program that runs to its end prints the same. What moves is when a value is computed: a shared value once, at the head of its arm; `d~s` selects before the arm's other work; a fused recursion never builds its tree. So a program that stops (the Nat limit, an `@unsafe` recursion) can stop at another point of the same run, or not at all where a fused recursion no longer computes a part of a tree that overflowed and was never read. No rule copies a value of a boxed type: sharing a box would turn its type into counted nodes program-wide (what #2180 measured), so only words are shared.

## The cost model, and where measurement disagreed

Static, in rough instructions: a `Nat.add` / `Nat.mul` 2 (its limit test, which clang cannot share), a division 4, a heap node 6, a call to a def that recurses 20 (a frame), a call to a def that does not what its body costs (the emitter unfolds it; a match 3 and 1 an arm). U32 and F32 operations, word-sized constructors, unchecked Nat operations, operations or calls on literals, and defs with no parameters cost 0. That last line is the calibration; the first version priced word arithmetic and constants and was wrong in both directions:

| program | the model said | measured | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| koru nestedloop | folding `MD()` into `1000000007n` saves 4 an iteration | +5.0% instructions, -8% cycles: clang turns a literal divisor into a multiply sequence | constants cost 0: no change |
| nbody | sharing U32/F32 subterms of `sim` saves about 3 | +5.4% instructions: `sim`'s C fell under `SPIN_FAR`, became `INLINE` and was inlined into its callers | word arithmetic costs 0: no change |
| gameoflife | sharing four U32 indices saves 2 | 0.0%: clang already shares them | no change |
| koru listops | one call site: nothing visible | 0 at the kernel's 7 iterations, -21% instructions at 700 (clang inlines `runOne` at its one site once `go` is not unrolled; mechanism inferred from the iteration count alone deciding it) | taken, measured |
| koru binarytrees | fusion: one call of 20 for two of 40 | 2^13 nodes built and walked become 13 steps (main: 1,639M to 12M instructions) | taken |
| koru digitsum, on main only | sharing `Nat.div(n, 10n)` saves 4 a call | +2.7% instructions on main (cycles inside the range); unchanged on the integration branch; the spins' order in the C changes too, cause not traced | open |
| coins, forked factorial | (first version) sharing word work | -3.2% and -6.3% instructions | lost with the calibration: traded for no regression |

The default drop is not cost-driven (one word and one test fewer per value is assumed to pay): measured, below.

## Results

One M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`. Cycles are P-core cycles over 16 placements (`nop`s before the first segment, 2 rounds, least / median / most).

Targets, against the integration branch:

| target | what the pass does | instructions | cycles, median (range) | new over the baseline? |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `queens` `solve` | drops `Stat0{}` | 58.47G to 55.05G (-5.9%) | 17.61G (17.55 / 17.68) to 16.54G (16.42 / 16.70): -6.1% | yes (`r1`, the hand pair accumulator: -4.8%) |
| koru `isqrt` | binds the iterate once | 163.4M to 128.3M (-21.5%) | 59M to 48M (-19%) | yes |
| koru `isqrt`, forked port | same | 168.4M to 133.4M (-20.8%) | 64M to 50M (-22%) | yes |
| koru `binarytrees` | fuses `check(make(d))` and shares its two equal calls | 11.96M to 11.03M (-7.5%): start-up only, #2180 already computes it once | inside the range | yes (#2031 is not in the baseline) |
| koru `listops` | one call site for `runOne` | 13.43M to 13.45M median (noise) | inside the range | no gain on the kernel as shipped; -21% / -26% at 700 iterations |
| koru `fib` | nothing | | | #2175 has it; no accumulator rule here |
| koru `pascal` | nothing | | | needs `binom(n, k) = 0` for `k > n` and a change of variables: a lemma about the def's own values, not an equation the rules can reach |
| koru `powmod`, `factorial` | two shares of `Nat.div(b, 2n)` | -0.2% | inside the range | the doubling loop is a product mod `m`; replacing it needs a closed form for a recursion and modular laws Base does not state |
| Base `String.contains` (before #2196) | nothing | | | needs `String.starts_with.go` specialised on a constructor in the argument it matches second (constructor specialisation, not a rule here); on main since #2196 |

On main: `queens` 89.87G to 85.01G instructions and 22.13G to 18.88G cycles (-14.7%, ranges apart, section 30's figure for step 1), `isqrt` -21.5% / -19%, `binarytrees` 1,639M to 12M instructions and 279M to 5M cycles.

The suite, against the integration branch: 19 of the 63 programs (17 benches, 22 kernels, 17 forked kernels, 7 Perceus ports) change their C (`kmeans`, `queens`; `binarytrees`, `coins`, `digitsum`, `exprtree`, `factorial`, `isqrt`, `listops`, `powmod`, `primes`, `wordfreq`; seven forked ports); no Perceus port changes. No program is worse than +0.15% in instructions (`listops`' start-up noise), and every cycle median is inside its base's placement range except the gains above. What it found beyond the targets in the suite (all inside noise): `kmeans` computes `b2u(U32.is_zero(n))` once, `primes` `d + 1` once, `digitsum` `n / 10` once, `coins` `coin(k)` once, `wordfreq` drops a `1n * c`. Over every test and program the default drop fires twice (`queens` and its test), one call site twice (`listops` and its test), fusion 31 times in 21 programs (both `binarytrees` ports, the rest tests, e.g. `String.length(String.append(..))`), and arms are rewritten in 306 programs, mostly compile-time evaluation of calls on literal lists in test `main`s.

## Search cost and compile time

Per target, the pass takes under 30 ms; the largest arm's e-graph has 2,006 nodes (`binarytrees`, at the budget), most under 50. Budgets: 8 rounds and 2,000 nodes an arm, 400,000 nodes a build, closures 32 deep; gates skip the rounds on an arm of word arithmetic alone or with nothing shared, foldable or unfoldable.

`compile_book`, the least of 3 runs, one process per program: +7.9% over the 17 benches and 15 demos together; `app_slash_boss_3d` 1,787 to 1,937 ms (+8.4%); small programs +10% to +25% of a few tens of ms (the perf gate's COMPILER cell also counts the check and clang, about 0.6 s on bfs). Perceus `deriv` (a 3.7 GB compile on main): times swing from 15 to 34 s on both builds under load, inconclusive; peak memory 5.17 to 5.93 GB.

## Checks

Against main:
- The 162 tests whose C changes (every other test emits byte-identical C): the C lane prints the same as main on all 162 (3 differ from their `#|` lines on main too: two network tests, and one whose output is longer than the harness keeps); the memory check (poisoned frees, live heap words at exit) is the same at 1 and 8 threads, 0 live words on 158, the same counts on the rest.
- JS: the pass is C only; the 162 tests' emitted JS is byte-identical.
- Metal: the 4 changed tests with `!` calls build their GPU program and print their `#|` lines.
- `tsc`: the same errors as main.
- Four new tests, `tests/run/eqsat_{cse,drop,sites,fuse}.bend`: each rule's shapes and its refusals (a default that one match does not treat as zeros, one matched by a catch-all arm, a call-site candidate reading an affine parameter twice, a capture of a let-bound value), and programs that stop on the Nat limit on every lane, fused or not.
- Ten wrong versions (a wrong unit, a wrong fold, `Nat.sub` / `Nat.mul` reordered, a default dropped unchecked or built at the wrong fields, a wrong call-site selector, a fusion found by its producer alone, a literal taking the other arm, a shared word bound affine, a captured variable moved): 9 caught by the new tests; the affine binding emits the same C (the emitter counts reads itself). The repo's own tests whose C changes catch 5 of them and miss the reordering, both drop versions and the selector.

Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86.

## Not covered

- No accumulator rule (#2175 does it) and no loop-invariant hoisting (#2180 does it).
- Not built from the brief's list: case of case, eta, currying, an ADT as sums of products, `Unit × A ≅ A` (section 31 found the wrappers already erased and no closures in the benches). Let floating is subsumed: lets are read through and re-bound by extraction.
- The e-graph does not reach across a match: each arm is its own graph, so nothing is shared between arms or hoisted out of one.
- The default drop takes two-constructor, parameterless types with word fields and zero as the default; it reaches only `queens`' `Stats` in the suites (as section 30 counted).
- The cost model cannot see clang (inlining, a constant divisor, a spin's size), which is where it was wrong.

title: An arm computes a checked Nat operation or a division once, where clang could not merge its copies (from #2221)
body:
**`comp.ts` is 67,545 ttok** (main 65,995: **+1,550**); the cap is set aside for now. One rule extracted from #2221 (the e-graph draft, left open), as a small pass without the e-graph. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run. Measured on main and merged onto a copy of the integration branch (`opt/integration` at bae64757 on nicolas-abril/bend).

## What it does

An arm of a def (its expression below the lambdas and matches) that computes the same checked Nat operation or division twice computes it once, bound by a `let` at the arm's head, when clang could not merge the two copies itself. C lane only; a pass on the checked terms in `file_book`, before emission, like #2175's `acc_def`.

```python
# isqrt (koru): the Newton iterate is computed as an argument and again in the flag
iter(n, y, Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n),
     Nat.is_lt(Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n), y))
# compiled as if written
+x = Nat.div(Nat.add(y, Nat.div(n, y)), 2n)
iter(n, y, x, Nat.is_lt(x, y))
```

## The rule

A term is a candidate when its head is `Nat.add`, `Nat.mul`, `Nat.double` (checked: they test the 2^48 - 1 limit), `Nat.div`, `Nat.mod`, `U32.div` or `U32.mod`, applied to two arguments, and it appears at least twice in the arm (equal by `term_same`). It is bound once when:

- **clang could not merge the copies**: the term contains a checked operation, or a checked operation runs between two of its copies (in the order the arm runs: arguments left to right, each before its call). A checked operation posts an error past the limit (`nat_chk` calls `err_post`), and clang does not move or merge across that. Two divisions with nothing checked between them clang already merges;
- **it can move to the arm's head**: none of its variables is bound by one of the arm's own `let`s, and no copy is inside a closure;
- it is not inside another bound candidate.

**`digitsum`, the case that set the first condition.** #2221 shared any division read twice. In `digitsum` the two `Nat.div(n, 10n)` are adjacent in the emitted C, and clang had already merged them: both builds run one `umulh` a step. Removing the duplicate in the source only changed the shape of clang's loop, +2.7% instructions on main (removing the second call by hand from main's C, keeping everything else, reproduces it exactly; the spins' order, which also changed in #2221's C, is not the cause). In `isqrt` a checked add runs between the two `Nat.div(n, y)`, clang keeps both, and sharing the division alone already gives the whole gain (164.0M to 128.6M instructions by hand). With the condition, `digitsum` is not touched (its C is byte-identical to main's) and `isqrt` is.

**Soundness.** The copies are equal pure terms, so the arm answers the same. What moves is when the term is computed: once, at the head of the arm, before the arm's other work. A program that stops on the Nat limit can stop at another point of the same run (as with #2175 and #2180). The bound term is a `Nat` or a `U32` (a word), so no box becomes shared.

## Reach

Of the 63 programs measured (17 benches, 22 koru kernels, 17 forked ports, 7 Perceus ports) 16 change their C, the same 16 on main and on the integration branch: `exprtree`, `factorial`, `isqrt`, `mutual`, `powmod`, `primes` and the forked `collatz`, `digitsum`, `factorial`, `gcdsum`, `isqrt`, `mutual`, `powmod`, `primes`, `textstats`, `wordfreq`. No bench of Bend's suite and no Perceus port changes. Of the tests, 2 change (`run/nat_mul_wide`, `run/nat_div_native`) besides the new one. Only `isqrt` (both ports) is hot.

## Results

One M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`. Cycles are P-core cycles over 16 placements (least / median / most), 2 rounds.

| program | base | instructions | cycles, median (least / most) |
|---|---|---|---|
| koru `isqrt` | main | 165.0M to 129.6M (-21.5%) | 60.0M (59.4 / 62.2) to 48.7M (48.0 / 52.0): -18.9%, ranges apart |
| koru `isqrt` | integration | 164.9M to 130.1M (-21.1%) | 60.2M (58.8 / 61.1) to 48.8M (47.2 / 50.7): -19.0%, ranges apart |
| koru `isqrt`, forked port | main | 169.9M to 135.1M (-20.5%) | 64.5M to 51.3M (-20.4%), ranges apart |
| koru `isqrt`, forked port | integration | 170.3M to 135.1M (-20.7%) | 64.3M to 51.3M (-20.2%), ranges apart |
| the other 14 that change | both | -1.07% to +0.96% (median instructions over the sweep; the largest moves are on kernels of 17M to 75M instructions, mostly start-up, and change sign between the two bases) | every median inside the base's range |

`digitsum` (the kernel) is byte-identical to main on both bases; its forked port changes (another arm) and is level: 338.1M to 337.8M instructions on main, cycles inside the range.

Instructions here are medians over the sweep's runs: on this machine a binary's count moves by up to a few percent between sessions (start-up), so single runs do not settle sub-1% questions.

## Compile time

The pass itself, timed inside `compile_book` (3 runs): 14 to 16 ms on `app_slash_boss_3d` (about 1.6% of its `compile_book`), 1 to 5 ms on each of the 17 benches. End-to-end `compile_book` against main over the 17 benches and `app_slash_boss_3d`: +3.2% (least of 3; per-bench numbers move ±30% with the machine's load, both ways).

## Checks

Against main:
- Every test whose C changes (`run/nat_mul_wide`, `run/nat_div_native`, `run/share_checked_ops`) and every one of the 16 programs above: the C lane prints the same as main, and the memory check (poisoned frees, live heap words at exit) is the same at 1 and 8 threads, 0 live words everywhere (the new test ends on the Nat limit, so it prints no count, on main too). All other tests emit byte-identical C.
- JS: the pass is C only; the changed tests' JS is byte-identical. Metal: no test or program with `!` calls changes. `tsc`: the same errors as main.
- A new test, `tests/run/share_checked_ops.bend`, its arguments read at run time from `IO.args` (literal arguments are evaluated by the compiler and would hide the pass): the isqrt shape, two divisions with nothing checked between (left alone), copies naming an arm's `let` (left alone), copies inside a closure (left alone), a shared `Nat` past 2^32, `U32` divisions with a checked add between, and a shared product past the Nat limit (stops on every lane).
- Wrong versions: binding by head instead of the whole term (`swap`), binding a `Nat` as a `U32` (`type`), binding a `U32` as a `Nat` (`u32`): all caught by the new test; the repo's tests that change catch `swap` and `type` and miss `u32`. Two more change nothing observable by construction: a copy that names an arm's `let`, or that sits in a closure, cannot be found under its binder (the body is opened again with fresh variables), so moving one leaves a dead `let` the emitter never runs.

Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86.

## Not covered

- Copies inside a closure, and copies that name one of the arm's `let`s, stay where they are.
- Nothing is shared between two arms of a match, or hoisted out of one.
- The condition is about clang's behaviour (what it merges), measured on these programs, not derived.
