title: Merge what no consumer can tell apart: a default constructor that matches treat as zeros, and per flow, values nobody reads (from #2221)
body:
**`comp.ts` is 74,749 ttok** (main 65,995: **+8,754**; this PR's first version, the zero-default rule alone, was +3,270); the cap is set aside for now. One rule extracted from #2221 (the e-graph draft, left open), then generalised: merge what no consumer can tell apart. Measured on one Mac (M4), not on the cluster: the `test` and `perf` gates have not been run. Measured on main and merged onto a copy of the integration branch (`opt/integration` at bae64757 on nicolas-abril/bend).

## What it does

Two rewrites before any def is opened, C lane only, once a file:

1. **A default constructor dropped** (the first version of this PR, unchanged): a datatype `D{} | P{f..}` whose `D{}` acts as `P{0, ..}` at every match the program runs keeps `P` alone. This is `queens`' `Stat0{}` as `Stats{0, 0}`.
2. **Per flow, what nobody reads is erased** (new). A flow is a set of values that can meet: a def's parameter or result, a pattern or let variable, a field of the constructors of another flow, joined by unification over the checked terms of every def main reaches, field by field (a list's elements and its tails are flows of their own). On a flow that does not escape:
   - a **dead flow**, whose values nobody matches, reads or passes on to what is not analysed, is erased: each parameter of it goes from its def and from every call;
   - a **live flow that builds one constructor**, whose other fields are dead flows (or never set) and whose other constructors it never builds, **carries that field alone**: `K{.., x, ..}` is `x`, the match on it is a lambda, and the flow's positions take the field's type (bend2 already erases a one-field wrapper, so no copy of the type is needed).

```python
# rbtree-ck (Perceus): trees holds every fifth tree, but main reads its head only
def make_tree_aux(+n: Nat, +freq: U32, t: Tree, acc: List<&2, Tree>) -> List<&2, Tree>:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      t <> acc
    case 1n+p:
      ..
      make_tree_aux(p, freq, t1, keep(U32.is_eq(U32.mod(k, freq), 0), t1, acc))
def head(ts: List<&2, Tree>) -> Tree: ..     # Nil{} -> Leaf{}, t <> rest -> t
# compiled as if written: the list's tails are a dead flow (acc goes, and every keep),
# Nil is never built where the list is matched, so the list is its head
def make_tree_aux(+n: Nat, +freq: U32, t: Tree) -> Tree:
  match n:
    case 0n:
      t
    case 1n+p:
      ..
      make_tree_aux(p, freq, t1)
def head(ts: Tree) -> Tree: ts
```

## The rules and their conditions

**Default constructor** (as before): no parameters, two constructors, `D` nullary and `P` of `U32` / `Nat`; at every match on the type, both arms present and `D`'s equal to `P`'s at zero fields once normalised (literals folded, units dropped, `D{}` read as `P{0, ..}`); the type not in a foreign def's or `main`'s type, `D` in no def's type.

**Flows.** A flow escapes, and is left alone, when a value of it reaches: a foreign def or `main`'s result; a closure, or a def used as a value (a partial application, a template argument), whose parameters then take anything; a `!` call (device code); an intrinsic that takes more than words (Arrays); a field or parameter of generic type (polymorphic code). A dead flow is one with no match on it, no read (an intrinsic operand) and no escape. A one-field flow also has: no catch-all arm in its matches; values not stored in another constructor's field; a field not of the type itself; a type the compiler does not encode itself.

**Re-check.** Every def these touch (the defs that build, match, take or return the flow, and every caller of a def whose signature changes) is written again unannotated, with its new signature built over the old one's binders, and elaborated by bend.ts' `def_check`. A dropped binder still read (checked in its own scope) or any refusal leaves the whole program as it was.

**Why it is sound.** A dead value has no reader: nothing the program prints depends on it, so not computing it changes nothing observable but time, memory and one thing below. A one-field flow's values are built only by `K` and every match on them takes `K`'s arm and reads the kept field alone (the others are dead), so passing the field instead is the same computation. The flow analysis is a sound over-approximation (unification merges flows, never splits them), and what it cannot follow it marks as an escape. Its claims are also checked against the types: a value whose type changes where something unanalysed would see it makes `def_check` refuse.

**Behaviour, as the repo owner ruled:** a value nobody reads is dead and is not computed. A program that stopped while computing one (the Nat limit, an `@unsafe` recursion) no longer stops there; what a program prints when it runs to its end is the same. The C and JS lanes already disagree on this (#2181); that is to be fixed later, not here. In `rbtree-ck` the gain is the benchmark's kept trees disappearing (it keeps every fifth tree alive and never reads them), so its numbers overstate the gain for a real program.

## Count

A hook over the checked terms (the flow analysis plus each generalisation's condition, globally and per flow) over Base, the tests, the demos, the 17 benches, the 22 koru kernels and their 17 forked ports, the 7 Perceus ports (1,264 (file, type) records, 3,377 flows), with run-time counters (entries into every segment and native function, by def) over the 63 runnable programs. "Hot": the defs that build or match the candidate entered 10^5 times or more.

| candidate | qualifying (file, type) | holds | hot |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| this PR's first rule: `D{}` = `P{0, ..}` at every match | 30 (27 types) | 5 (5 types) | `queens`' `Stats` |
| 1. a constructor merged into another under a substitution, every match | 938 (177 types) | 26 (18 types) | `queens`' `Stats`, `exprtree`'s `Expr` |
| 1a. the substitution literals alone (Option with a default) | | 9 (9 types) | `queens`' `Stats` |
| 1b. the merged constructor's fields | | 4 (4 types) | none |
| 1c. with a call (evaluated when built) | | 13 (5 types) | `exprtree`'s `Expr` (`Add{l, r}` as `Lit{addM(eval l, eval r)}`) |
| 2. a field no consumer reads | 1,139 (333 types) | 123 (82 types) | `cfold`'s `Var{name}` |
| 3. a constructor never built | 938 (177 types) | 43 (36 types) | none |
| 1 to 3, per type | 1,264 (373 types) | 166 (112 types) | the three above |
| 4. per flow (built and matched, no escape, not generic): 1 to 3 | 973 flows (280 types) | 250 (96 types) | the above, and `rbtree-ck`'s and `rbtree-ck-unsafe`'s result list |
| 4. ... where the type as a whole fails | | 144 (34 types) | `rbtree-ck`, `rbtree-ck-unsafe` |

Two analysis defects found on the way and fixed in the hook (each over-claimed): a `!` call's result was not joined to its callee's (a false hit in merkle), and a def used as a value did not mark its parameters escaping. One defect was in this PR itself and is fixed here: the reach scan skipped every key named `v` (a variable's type), and with it the values of `let`s, so a def called only from a `let`'s value was not checked; it kept its `D` arm against a type without `D`, a compile crash (now a test: `pt.bad` in `tests/run/drop_default_ctor.bend`). #2221's `eq_reach` has the same defect.

## Bounds (by hand, respelled source, main; then built)

| hit | bound | built? |
|---|---|---|
| `rbtree-ck`'s list as its head | 74.1G to 21.5G instructions, 14.4G to 8.3G cycles | yes: the measured build is exactly the bound |
| `rbtree-ck-unsafe`, the same | 49.0G to 11.2G, 10.3G to 2.8G | yes, the same |
| `exprtree`'s `Expr` merged into `Lit{eval ..}` (a word) | 74.6M to 59.0M instructions (-21%) | no: the substitution evaluates `eval` when the node is built, and `eval` can stop on the Nat limit, so a program that builds a tree and never reads it could stop where it did not; a rule that allows only terms that cannot stop does not reach it |
| `cfold`'s dead `Var{name}` | 764.2M to 763.2M (-0.1%): `Var{1}` is already packed into the term word | no |

Left out: merging under a substitution (1, 1a, 1b: no hot reach beyond the default this PR already drops; 1c not sound as stated); dead fields and dead constructors over a whole type (2, 3: no hot reach that the per-flow form does not take); a flow that keeps more than one field or constructor would need a copy of the type (no hot reach).

## Results

One M4, one thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`. Cycles are P-core cycles over 16 placements (least / median / most); `queens` 2 rounds, the rbtree ports 1 (their ranges are far apart).

| program | base | instructions | cycles, median (least / most) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `queens` | main | 90.32G to 85.37G (-5.5%) | 22.43G (22.09 / 22.69) to 19.07G (18.99 / 19.21): -15.0% |
| `queens` | integration | 58.72G to 55.24G (-5.9%) | 17.76G (17.63 / 17.98) to 16.71G (16.57 / 16.77): -5.9% |
| `rbtree-ck` | main | 73.91G to 21.48G (-70.9%) | 14.28G (14.13 / 17.27) to 8.45G (8.27 / 8.59): -40.9% |
| `rbtree-ck` | integration | 22.91G to 9.34G (-59.2%) | 5.48G (5.43 / 5.65) to 2.13G (2.09 / 2.17): -61.1% |
| `rbtree-ck-unsafe` | main | 48.92G to 11.25G (-77.0%) | 10.40G (10.35 / 10.81) to 2.79G (2.77 / 2.84): -73.2% |
| `rbtree-ck-unsafe` | integration | 21.87G to 9.00G (-58.8%) | 5.31G (5.27 / 5.41) to 2.19G (2.15 / 2.24): -58.9% |

Every range is apart. No other program of the 63 changes its C, on main or on the integration branch (`deriv` compared alone, for memory). Of the tests, 27 change besides the two new ones.

## Compile time

The two passes, timed inside `compile_book` (3 runs): 34 to 40 ms on `app_slash_boss_3d` (about 6% of its `compile_book`), of which the flow pass 27 to 32 and the default rule 7 to 8; 3 to 17 ms on each of the 17 benches (`queens` the most: the default rule re-checks its defs). The perf gate's COMPILER cell also counts the check and clang (about 0.6 s on bfs), where this is 1% to 3%.

## Checks

Against main:
- Every test whose C changes (27, and the two new ones) and the three programs: the C lane prints the same as main, and the memory check (poisoned frees, live heap words at exit) is the same at 1 and 8 threads, 0 live words everywhere. All other tests emit byte-identical C.
- JS: the passes are C only; the changed tests' JS is byte-identical. Metal: `queens` (`run!`) and `compile/vector_boxed_default` (the one changed test with `!`) built with `--gpu on` print their answers on main and here. `tsc`: the same errors as main.
- New test `tests/run/drop_dead_flow.bend` (arguments read at run time from `IO.args`): a list read by its head alone (it becomes its head, its `keep` calls go), and the same list read through a count of its tail, a closure, generic code, a `!` call and a catch-all arm (each stays a list); `tests/run/drop_default_ctor.bend` gains the `let` reach case.
- Wrong versions of the default rule (skipping the arm check, building `D{}` at ones, a wrong fold, a wrong unit): caught by the new tests, none by the repo's own tests. Of the flow rule: a match that does not read and a one-field flow keeping the wrong field are refused (`def_check` or the binder check: the program compiles as on main); ignoring escapes, allowing a flow stored in another constructor and allowing a catch-all arm change the C of 10 tests, all of which still print their `#|` lines: in each instance either nothing unanalysed saw the value or the type check refused the rewrite.

Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86.

## Follow-up count (after the ruling)

Counted with the same hook, extended with the exclusion that stops each flow, which arms of each def read each parameter, and which call sites compute its argument (results in nicolas-abril/bend-eqsat, `results/general/`). Hot: the defs involved entered 10^5 times or more in the 63 runnable programs.

| candidate | holds | hot |
|---|---:|---|
| one-field flows as built here | 85 flows | `rbtree-ck`, `rbtree-ck-unsafe` |
| ... with only "stored in another constructor" in the way | 44 | none |
| ... with only a catch-all arm in the way | 1 | none |
| ... with only a closure in the way | 10 | none |
| ... with only a generic position in the way | 0 | none |
| more than one field or constructor kept, something dead (a cloned type) | 75 | none |
| ... with those exclusions allowed too | 149 | `cfold`'s `Var{name}` (bounded: -0.1%, already packed) |
| dead parameters whose callers compute the argument | 68 | `rbtree-ck`'s `acc` (taken here) |
| parameters read in some arms only, the argument a call, a checked operation or a division | 960 | all hot ones are loops whose exit arm alone does not read it: the waste is once a loop (lexer's `gen`, hashmap's `look`, `josephus`, `collatz`, `powmod` / `factorial`'s `mm`) |
| a merge evaluated when built, every value read anyway (`exprtree`'s `Expr` as its value) | 1 | bound by hand: -21% / -18% instructions, -7% cycles on main / on the integration branch; built on `opt/observe-general` (below), not here |

So nothing beyond what this PR does has hot reach with a gain except `exprtree`, left out above and built on its own branch (next section).

## The general version (branch `opt/observe-general` on nicolas-abril/bend, not this PR)

Built after the ruling, as asked: the most general form of the idea that the count and the bounds supported. It keeps this PR's two rules unchanged and adds a third on the same flows:

- **Stored folds.** A flow read by one fold alone carries the fold's result. The fold `f` is a total def of one parameter, the structure, with no catch-all arm, whose every arm passes each recursive field to `f` exactly once, on every path of the arm. The flow is stored in no other flow, matched by `f` alone, and every parameter and `let` of it is read on every path (a lambda is not a path; a match is all of its arms). Each constructor site becomes `f`'s arm for it (fields bound by `let`s, a recursive field's `f(r)` the field itself), and each `f(x)` becomes `x`. `f`'s work moves from read time to build time; every path reads it, so only where a program stops can move. A non-recursive type is a fold too (an enumeration read by its code: `gameoflife`'s `Cls`).
- **Copy fact.** Two recursive fields given the same word-typed term are computed once (`Node{make(p), make(p)}`).
- A flow both this PR's one-field rule and the fold rule take keeps the one-field rule. If the whole rewrite fails `def_check`, the one-field rules and then each fold are tried alone and what checks is kept.

**Count first** (the same hook, extended to folds and producer facts; recursive flows that are built and matched: 720; hot as above):

| candidate (per flow) | holds | hot | bound by hand |
|---|---:|---|---|
| one fold consumes it, nothing escapes | 277 | `binarytrees` (both ports), `exprtree` | |
| ... the fold's only parameter the structure (storable) | 130 | the same three | `exprtree` -21% instr / -7% cycles; `binarytrees` on main -99% |
| several folds of it, nothing escapes | 25 | `nqueens`' `List`, `symreg`'s `Expr` (each fold takes other changing arguments: not storable) | not built |
| ... several storable folds (a tuple of results) | 3 | none | not built |
| a fold and something else | 368 | the rbtree ports, `cfold`, `deriv`, `kmeans`, `merkle`, the tree benches | not eligible |
| folds, escaping | 50 | `nqueens`, `hashmap`, `tree-radix` | not eligible |
| producer fact: a field the same literal at every build | 547 | `cfold`'s and `deriv`'s `Expr` | `deriv` `Var{"x"}` as a constant: -0.7% instr / -2% cycles (and its flow escapes through a closure); `cfold` -0.1%: not built |
| producer fact: a field a copy of another | 24 | `binarytrees`' `Node{t, t}` | built (with the folds) |
| producer fact: a constructor never built in the flow | 161 | `rbtree-ck`'s lists | already taken by this PR's one-field rule |
| this PR's rules | 254 | `queens`, `cfold`, the rbtree-ck lists | |
| storable folds, producer facts or this PR's rules, together | 401 | the above | |

**Soundness.** The fold's work is computed when a node is built, which is earlier than the program did, so it is allowed only where every path consumes it anyway: each recursive call in each arm is on every path of the arm (not under a lambda or a nested match), each parameter of the flow is read on every path of its def, each `let` of it is read, the flow is matched by the fold alone and stored in no other flow. Every rewritten def goes through `def_check`; a refusal leaves the program as it was (the rules that check are kept).

**Measured** (one M4, 1 thread, GPU off, `cc -O3`, 16 placements x 2 rounds; P-core cycles least / median / most). Only four programs of the 63 change their C against this PR, on main and on the integration copy:

| program | base | instructions | cycles, median (least / most) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exprtree` | main | 74.90M to 59.26M (-20.9%) | 28.81M (28.29 / 30.76) to 26.63M (26.13 / 28.16): -7.6% |
| `exprtree` | integration | 71.38M to 58.56M (-18.0%) | 28.53M (28.02 / 29.81) to 26.69M (26.29 / 27.09): -6.4% |
| `binarytrees` | main | 1638.3M to 11.5M (-99.3%) | 280.9M to 3.76M |
| `binarytrees` | integration | 12.21M to 11.31M (-7.4%, start-up: integration already does not build the trees) | 3.72M to 3.48M, ranges overlap |
| `binarytrees` (forked port) | main / integration | 1638.7M to 14.7M / 12.21M to 11.34M | 279.1M to 4.15M / 3.73M to 3.61M, overlap |
| `gameoflife` (`Cls` read by its code) | main / integration | unchanged (172.35G, 79.85G) | 31.805G to 31.801G / 18.234G to 18.231G, overlap |

**Cost against this PR:** `comp.ts` 78,675 ttok (+3,926 over this PR, +12,680 over main). The flow pass on `app_slash_boss_3d`: 21 to 35 ms here, 26 to 60 ms there; benches about 1 ms either way.

**Checks:** 46 tests change C against this PR on main (50 on the integration copy, plus the four programs and the new test): C, JS and interpreter print the same as the base, memory check 0 live words at 1 and 8 threads. JS identical (C-only pass). Metal: `gameoflife` (`batch!`) prints the same with `--gpu on` and off. New test `tests/run/fold_stored.bend`: two trees that become their fold, six that must stay trees (a fold on a path not taken, behind a match in the fold's arm, behind a lambda the arm passes on, from an unread let, through generic code, matched by two defs), each of which would overflow a Nat if its fold ran early. Wrong versions: dropping the every-path check of the arm, of the parameters, the copy fact on unequal terms, the fields bound in the wrong order, and letting a fold take a flow this PR's rule takes are each caught (the last by the repo's own `check/cop_field_match` and `parse/plus_binder_nested`, a bug found and fixed on the way); dropping the "matched by one def" or "stored in no other flow" checks is refused by `def_check` (same C); dropping the `let` check changes nothing (an unread `let` is already dead).

**Which goes in.** This PR stays as it is. The general version's one gain over it on the integration branch is `exprtree` (-18% instructions, -6% cycles, one kernel); its `binarytrees` gain on main is already on the integration branch. That is +3,926 ttok and a slower flow pass for one kernel, so it lives on `opt/observe-general` (from main, this PR's commit as its base, pushed) for the owner to take or leave.

## Not covered

- A flow that keeps two fields or two constructors needs a copy of its type (renamed, cloned); not built (no hot reach).
- A substitution that evaluates when built (`exprtree`): on `opt/observe-general`. A default other than zero; a type with parameters for the default rule.
- A flow through a closure, a `!` call, generic code or an Array is left alone.

title: fix(comp): a module exports its own defs, so a page ships what it uses
body:
## Problem

In module mode (the bun plugin in `bend2/main.ts`, and `bend file.bend -o f.mjs`), `js_lib` exports every live, non-IO def of the **whole book**, the defs of imported files included (keys like `"lib:unused"`). Then `file_book` compiles everything reachable from all of them, and the module exports one `export default { ... }` object, which bundlers cannot shake.

So a page that uses one def of a large imported file ships all of that file. The guide also says `-o f.mjs` emits "an ES module of **its** non-IO defs", but the command exports the imported file's defs too.

We hit this in a game engine written in Bend (opengameworld/engine). A module that uses one clip of a generated 42-clip animation library:

| | today | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| bundle, minified | 9,071 KB / 1,893 KB gzip | 167 KB / 33.5 KB gzip |
| loader compile (what `bun --hot`/dev pays per change) | 3.1 s | 0.76 s |
| headless Chromium, emulated phone (CPU 4x, 1.6 Mbit/s, 150 ms), until ready | 10.2 s | 0.52 s |

## Change

```diff
-    return done_live(t) && !t.b && t.x === 0 && io_base(FL.book, t.T) === null;
+    return done_live(t) && !t.b && t.x === 0 && io_base(FL.book, t.T) === null
+      && !k.includes(":");
```

A module exports only its own defs. This uses the existing convention: `bend.ts` says `ns:name` is internal, and `cli_verdict` already reads `!k.includes(":")` as "a def of this file". The reachability pass that already exists then keeps only what those exports reach. The whole-program build (`-o x.js`, rooted at `main`) is unchanged.

`comp.ts` must stay under its 66k cap. On current main it is at 65,995 tokens (cl100k_base, the encoding `ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo` uses, counted with js-tiktoken). The new condition costs 7 tokens, so `if (mod) { FL = null!; }` in the same function becomes `if (mod) FL = null!;`, a form `comp.ts` already uses. The result is 65,998.

## Test

`tests/io/bundle_own_exports` follows `bundle_inline`. Its effect builds a page whose module imports a file with an unused def, then checks three things:
- the build succeeds;
- the unused def's string is not in the bundle;
- the bundle runs and the module exports only `pick`.

It prints `2` on current main and `0` with this change. I ran it interpreted and compiled to JS (`-o t.js`, then bun). `bundle_inline` and `bundle_page_input` still print `0` in both lanes.

## Behavior that changes

1. **JS can no longer reach an imported def through the default object.** For example, `R["lib:used"]()`. Those keys contain `:`, so dot access never reached them. A module that wants to expose an imported def re-exports it with one line: `def used() -> U32: L.used()`. A GitHub code search found 5 public files that import `.bend` modules, and none of them read such a key.
2. **An imported file's JS effect is no longer pulled in by an unused export.** Today a def such as `def later() -> Unit -> IO(U32)` is exported, because `io_base` does not see it as IO. It drags its effect file into the page, and that file's top-level code runs at load. With this change, an effect file that nothing reachable uses is not loaded. Base's `effs/*.js` only call `io_eff(...)` at load time, so they are unaffected.

## Evidence

The full evidence, with reproducible harnesses, is at https://github.com/caiodomingues/poc-bend-treeshake. It was gathered on v2.0.40.

- **Bend's own `tests/` corpus, differential in module mode.** 1,852 files, 1,237 of them compiled and loaded, 4,605 zero-argument values compared: **0 mismatches**. The patch drops 288 imported-def exports.
- **Scenarios.** Chains, diamonds, imported types, closures and currying, names such as `Place.word`, `new`, `__proto__`, `default`, `then`, `__esModule`, and effects: same output, except the two cases above.
- **Other environments.** The same modules under Node (direct, and through this loader), esbuild, Rollup (ESM and CJS), Vite and webpack all print what released Bend prints. Every one of these bundlers then drops the unused code.
- **The engine above.** Its 99 tests pass, and the clip's value is identical (same JSON hash).

## An alternative, not in this PR

Keeping the default object as it is and adding a pure named export per own def (under its exact Bend name, as an ES2022 string export name; `default` and `then` excluded) breaks nothing for existing importers. It lets `import { x }` drop even a file's own unused defs. But it costs about 206 tokens, which puts `comp.ts` over the cap, and it does not speed up compiling. The patch and its tests are in the repo linked above, if that direction is preferred.

## Not tested here

- The C and GPU lanes. This test has no C twin, like `bundle_inline`.
- The cluster gates (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`).
- `ttok` itself. The count above uses the same encoding through js-tiktoken. With 2 tokens of room, the repo gate on this PR is the real check.

title: test(io): process_run's late stdin reader keeps its stdin under dash
body:
On Linux with dash as `/bin/sh` (Debian, Ubuntu and their derivatives), `tests/io/process_run.bend` prints `late stdin reader: False` on every lane: C, JS and the interpreter.

The case runs `/bin/sh -c "(sleep 0.05; cat) <&0 & exit 0"`. POSIX gives an asynchronous list a standard input like `/dev/null` before its explicit redirections, so under dash `<&0` duplicates `/dev/null` and `cat` reads nothing. bash, which is macOS's `/bin/sh`, keeps the real stdin when the list redirects it. Without Bend:

```
$ head -c 128000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' z | dash -c "(sleep 0.05; cat) <&0 & exit 0" | wc -c
0
$ head -c 128000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' z | bash -c "(sleep 0.05; cat) <&0 & exit 0" | wc -c
128000
```

This saves stdin in fd 3 before the list starts, and the late reader reads fd 3:

```diff
-      Process.run("/bin/sh", ["-c", "(sleep 0.05; cat) <&0 & exit 0"],
+      Process.run("/bin/sh", ["-c", "exec 3<&0; (sleep 0.05; cat <&3) & exit 0"],
```

The descendant still holds the stdin pipe after the shell exits, so the case tests the same thing. Both shells print 128000 for the new command. On Linux x86_64 (dash 0.5.12) the test passes on C, JS and the interpreter, 3 runs each, where before it failed every run. I have no Mac to run it on. The new command is plain POSIX sh, and it gives 128000 under bash here as well.

title: fix(io): Process.run's worker loads its modules on Node before 20.16 too
body:
Since #1842 the `Process.run` worker loads its modules with
`process.getBuiltinModule`, which Node added in v22.3.0 and v20.16.0. On an older
Node the worker throws at its first line. The caller then waits out the run's
timeout plus a second, and gets `Fail(5)`. This happens for every `Process.run` in a
program run by that Node, whether as `node p.cjs` or in module mode. Bun is not
affected. Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 package Node 18.19 as `nodejs`.

```python
import Base

def show(r: Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32 & (String & String)>) -> String:
  match r:
    case Fail{(code, msg)}: "fail " ++ U32.show(code) ++ ": " ++ msg
    case Done{(code, (out, err))}: "done " ++ U32.show(code) ++ " " ++ out

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    r : Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, U32 & (String & String)> <-
      Process.run("/bin/echo", ["hello"], "", 128, 1000)
    IO.print(show(r))
```

```
$ bun bend2/main.ts p.bend -o p.cjs && node p.cjs        # Node 18.19.1
fail 5: errno 5                                          # after about 2.1 s
```

The worker now uses `getBuiltinModule` when Node has it and `require` otherwise:

```js
const load = process.getBuiltinModule ?? require;
```

Where `getBuiltinModule` exists, `??` never reads `require`, so a module-mode worker
on a current Node runs as before.

Results with this change, for `node p.cjs`, and for
`node --input-type=module -e 'await import("./p.cjs")'` and
`node --input-type module -e '...'`:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Node 18.19.1 | `fail 5: errno 5` (about 2.1 s) on all three | `done 0 hello` (about 0.1 s) on all three |
| Node 24.22.3 | `done 0 hello` | `done 0 hello` |
| `bun p.cjs` | `done 0 hello` | `done 0 hello` |

The new test `tests/io/process_run_old_node` builds that program and runs it with
`node --require <preload>`, where the preload does `delete process.getBuiltinModule`.
A `--require` preload also runs in worker threads, so this simulates an older Node on
any Node. It prints `1` on main and `0` with this change, under both Node 24.22.3 and
Node 18.19.1. Like `process_run_node_module`, it skips when no `node` is on PATH.

The five existing `tests/io/process_run*` tests on the JS lane and the interpreter:

- With Node 18 on PATH, `process_run_node_module` returns 1 on main and passes here.
- With Node 24, it passes on both.
- `process_run` fails on both builds, at its late stdin reader. That is unrelated:
  the case relies on bash as `/bin/sh`, and this machine has dash (#2225).
- The other three pass everywhere.

With Node 24 on PATH, all 245 `tests/io` tests give the same results on main and with
this change, on the JS lane and on the interpreter. The C lane does not use this file.

title: Tail recursion modulo context: a constructor's field filled by the call (shared constructors too), and any associative op carried
body:
**Stacked on `opt/integration`** (nicolas-abril/bend bae64757, main 0e2f38f7 plus the open drafts merged). This PR's own changes are the last three commits (`bae64757..6d4c03e8`). The constructor half builds on #1810's mechanism. The operator half generalises #2175's `acc_def`, which is in the stack.

## What

Tail recursion modulo context: a non-tail call whose result only goes into a context the caller then returns runs in constant stack. Two kinds of context are handled.

- **A constructor (destination passing).** When a constructor boxes a call's result once, the node is built before the call, and the call fills that field. Lists, strings and trees then build in constant stack, and the node reuses the cell it consumes.
  - This is #1810's `Dst~put` frame, ported onto the stack and extended to shared (counted) constructors, which #1810 refused.
  - A hole carries bit 63 when its node is shared, and a store into it seals what it stores (`rfc_seal`).
  - When the frame on top is already a `Dst~put`, the new node goes into its hole and its own field becomes the hole, so a chain of any length uses one frame.
  - The hole's slot follows #2218's packed words.
  - #2177's `//base` copy is left off calls that take a hole.
- **An associative and commutative operator (accumulator).** `acc_def` (#2175) took only `Nat.add` and `U32.add`. It now takes whichever operator appears first on a tail: U32 `add` (also spelled `U32.inc`), `mul`, `xor`, `and`, `or`, and Bool `or`, `xor`. Each self call takes the result so far in turn, starting from the operator's unit.
  - A def that mixes operators keeps its frames.
  - Left out: `Nat.mul`, whose overflow order differs, and `F32`, which is not associative.

The C lane only; JS is byte-identical (spot-checked on 40 changed tests). `comp.ts` is 88,949 ttok, +1,574 over `opt/integration`; the token cap is left aside.

## Bounds measured before building (instructions, one thread)

- #1810 against its base (4f99f4c1): rbtree -11.8%, json -4.8%, lexer -2.4%; nothing on pidigits, k-nucleotide or havlak. It does nothing on msort and qsort, whose lists are shared.
- An affine context `a*x + c` carried through symreg's `eval` (+, -, * mixed), respelled by hand: **+13%** (41.2G against 36.4G on integration). #2177 already takes that recursion, so mixed-operator contexts were not built.

## Measured against `opt/integration` (all 230 bend-benchmarks programs)

- Every program prints its `expected.txt` on every run: 5 interleaved runs at one thread, plus 10 threads for the parallel ports.
- A hole now fires in 36 programs, besides Base's `String.append`, which every program that prints reaches.

Set apart, as in the integration measurement: the 28 programs with a `*_fix` harness hoist, rbtree-ck(-unsafe), and awfy/storage. On the other 200, the geometric mean is **0.993 instructions, 0.994 cycles**.

Placement sweeps (16 positions, 2 rounds, P-core cycles least / median / most, G):

| program | instructions | cycles, integration | cycles, this |
|---|---:|---|---|
| perceus/cfold | -27.1% | 0.184 / 0.188 / 0.190 | 0.100 / 0.102 / 0.104 |
| clbg/pidigits | -3.6% | 3.370 / 3.489 / 3.678 | 2.413 / 2.462 / 2.502 |
| perceus/rbtree | -16.4% | 2.114 / 2.146 / 2.153 | 1.901 / 1.916 / 1.920 |
| perceus/rbtree-unsafe | -17.0% | (median of 5: -11.5%) | |
| kostya/primes | -10.6% | 3.522 / 3.716 / 3.933 | 2.972 / 3.157 / 3.339 |
| koka-extra/finger-tree | -11.2% | 1.629 / 1.637 / 1.704 | 1.381 / 1.390 / 1.461 |
| koka-extra/finger-tree-fip | -13.4% | (median of 5: -16.3%) | |
| koka-extra/rbtree-del | -12.3% | 2.732 / 2.786 / 2.830 | 2.403 / 2.421 / 2.437 |
| clbg/n-body | -7.6% | 2.386 / 2.390 / 2.399 | 2.182 / 2.186 / 2.197 |
| respelled/listops | -7.8% | level | |
| clbg/regex-redux, kostya/json, osprey/textstats | -1.5% each | | |

Set-apart programs with a real hole (their harness loop already runs once): koka-extra/msort -14.4% instructions and -15.2% cycles (shared lists); msort-fip -15.4% and -18.9%; lookup -5.5% and -19%.

Losses:
- No program outside the set-apart group loses more than **1.5%** instructions. The worst are osprey/primes +1.5%, exprtree +1.2%, digitsum +1.2% and isqrt +1.0%, all a few-ms kernels.
- Cycle moves at equal instructions overlap under sweeps: digitsum (both ports), isqrt-par, wordfreq, textstats, polybench syr2k (+1.3% median) and covariance (+1.1% median).
- Set apart: awfy/permute +9.8% instructions. Its C differs from integration only by the `Dst~put` entry in the segment table. parallel-ml/ocaml-binarytrees5 +3.9% instructions and +11% cycles (median of 5, not swept).

## Checks

- **Native lane and memory check.** The 977 of 1,103 tests whose C changes, built with `-DBEND_POISON` and live-word counting, at 1 and 8 threads, give the same output, exit code and live words as integration. The 27 expected FAILs are unchanged. 7 IO and reg tests end with the same non-zero live count as integration.
- **Metal.** The 52 changed `!` tests and `ctor_tail_dest_bang` pass on Metal.
- **New tests.**
  - `tests/run/tmc_dest.bend`, `tmc_dest_shared.bend`, `acc_monoids.bend`, checked on C, JS and the interpreter.
  - #1810's three `ctor_tail_dest*` tests, now under `tests/run/`.
- **Wrong versions.** 8 of 10 are caught: no seal, the unpacked slot, the hole not moved, a wrong `mul` or `and` unit, the spare kept, a hole for a value used twice, the shared bit off. Two guards are caught by no test:
  - the check that no owned value is shared between the call and another field;
  - `bind_dead` before the jump.

  Both are kept from #1810 as defensive. The checker and the emitter's moves seem to make them unreachable; this is not proven.
- Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86.

## What it would replace

- **#2175**: replaced. This generalises its accumulator.
- **#1810**: replaced. Same mechanism, extended to shared constructors.
- Not ported: #1810's fork form (`l r = f(a) g(b); Node{l, r}`, built before both calls).

title: perf(comp): a lambda passed to a def runs in a copy of the def, its captures passed as parameters
body:
**Stacked on `opt/integration`** (nicolas-abril/bend bae64757: main 0e2f38f7 plus the open drafts merged), as #2227 is. This PR's own changes are the last four commits (`bae64757..91f2ce71`). It subsumes #2030 (its six fixtures are included and pass). Measured on one M4, not on the cluster.

## What

A call that passes a source lambda to a def `k` calls `k~cN` instead. `k~cN` is a copy of `k`:

- It takes the variables the lambda captures as its first parameters, then `k`'s other parameters.
- It holds the lambda where `k` held its parameter. Where `k` applied the parameter, the lambda is reduced in place: a variable or constant argument is substituted, any other argument is bound by a `let`. So no closure is built and none is applied.

More precisely:

- **Recursion.** A copy that reaches `k` again with the same lambda calls itself, so a recursion that passes its lambda on unchanged becomes one loop. This covers `k` passing it on, and a def `k` calls passing it back. Copies are keyed by the lambda's lowered term, binders and captures counted relative to the call.
- **Nesting.** A copy is walked like any def. A lambda inside a lambda, or one handed through two defs, gets its own copy where it lands.
- **Type arguments.** The copy also takes the call's erased (type) arguments. So a generic `pair.go(A, B, R, p, k)` copied for a `U32` pair reads its fields as words, not boxes.
- **Captures.** Variables the lambda names only in types are captured as erased parameters.
- **Cells.** `k`'s body and type are lowered and raised again before copying. A cell holds a type whose levels are its def's own, and a copy moves the levels: without this step a `U32` was read as a box (caught by delaunay-animation's LZW loop, now `tests/run/clo_elim_generic.bend`).
- **Bounds.** One copy per def and lambda, at most 64 per def. The copies of a def total at most 16,384 terms. No def over 4,096 terms is copied.
- **Termination.** A copy of `k` that passes `k` a lambda no smaller than its own leaves that one a closure. A continuation that grows each step (`go(p, x => k(x + 1))`) therefore stops after one copy.
- **Scope.** Only parameters of function type, below the declared arity (so `IO.bind`'s raised continuation is left alone), and no bang calls. C only: the pass runs before `file_book`, and JS is unchanged.
- **Cost.** A body with no lambda in a call is not walked. The pass takes about 70 ms on delaunay-animation.

One fix outside the pass: `emit_args` lent a flat def a box whenever the parameter was laid as a box. With the closure gone, a wide record the caller held open reached that path and was passed as 65 words (`tests/compile/record_wide_boxed_params.bend` stopped building). It now lends only a box.

## Why not #2162's unfolder or #2030's inlining

#2162's unfolder works at emit time, inside a segment, under fuel, and refuses a residue that forks. Most lambdas in the benchmarks are fork-join continuations (`pair.go(split(s), a => b => (l r = f(a) g(b); join(l, r)))`). A copy is a def, so it can recurse, is emitted once, and keeps forking where it forked. #2162 stays as it is (constants); this covers the lambda arguments it refuses.

#2030 inlined non-recursive callees at the source level. It stalled on the `comp.ts` cap, and then conflicted with the integrated drafts (`term_any`'s tail rule, `file_book`, the removed `term_map`). Its fixtures (`known_callback*`, `known_fn_inline`) pass here.

## Results

`closures/` is a new suite in nicolas-abril/bend-benchmarks (8056c4b): the closure spellings of parallel-ml's palindrome, wc and delaunay-animation, and six programs written for the suite, each with a helper-def spelling. Instructions and cycles are medians of 5 runs at one thread; "helpers" means the helper-def spelling on `opt/integration`.

| program | instructions, integration | this | helpers | cycles, integration | this | helpers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| palindrome (closures) | 81.60G | 2.31G | 3.53G | 15.49G | 0.95G | 1.17G |
| wc (closures) | 60.77G | 3.60G | 3.25G | 11.37G | 0.54G\* | 0.56G\* |
| delaunay-animation (closures) | 113.97G | 19.95G | 21.40G | 19.80G | 4.96G | 5.12G |
| pipeline (3 nested `Result.bind`) | 10.24G | 0.68G | 0.68G | 1.48G | 0.22G | 0.22G |
| twolevel (lambda through 2 defs, 3 captures) | 11.48G | 1.19G | 1.18G | 1.74G | 0.31G | 0.31G |
| cps (recursion passes its continuation on) | 5.56G | 4.80G | 4.35G | 1.52G | 1.49G | 1.40G |
| search (Base `List.any/all/find`) | 8.84G | 1.80G | 1.83G | 1.53G | 0.44G | 0.44G |
| pfor (parallel loop, lambda body) | 22.44G | 1.24G | 1.20G | 3.54G | 0.23G\* | 0.23G\* |
| mapfold (template lambdas, control) | same C | | | | | |

\* P-core cycles, the median of a 16-position placement sweep. The plain medians of 5 did not repeat under the sweep.

- The closure spellings now run as their helper-def spellings do, and palindrome and delaunay-animation run faster, from the filled type arguments.
- `cps` keeps about 10%: its copy carries the captured start through each step of the walk, while the helper spelling applies it once at the end.

**The 230 programs.** The C changes in 44, all in parallel-ml: the fork-join kit's `pair.go` continuations and other lambdas. These are the survey's 44 programs with closures. None of the set-apart programs changes (the 28 #2180 hoists, perceus/rbtree-ck(-unsafe), awfy/storage). Every program prints its `expected.txt` on all 5 runs, and at 10 threads.

- On the 44, the geometric mean is **0.973 instructions and 0.980 cycles** (medians of 5).
- Gains:

| program | instructions | cycles (median of 5) |
|---|---:|---:|
| parallel-ml/palindrome | -34.8% | -19.8% |
| parallel-ml/delaunay | -27.2% | -13.0% |

| parallel-ml/delaunay-animation | -6.8% | -4.8% |
| parallel-ml/flatten | -3.5% | -8.3% (sweep: -0.9%) |

- **No loss.** Every cycle change over 5% at near-equal instructions was swept (16 positions, 2 rounds), and all overlap. The table lists the sweep medians.

| program | instructions (median of sweep) | P-core cycles least / median / most, integration | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| bfs-tree-entangled-fixed (+24.5% in the 5 runs) | 5.283G / 5.258G | 4.086 / 4.432 / 5.230 | 3.976 / 4.304 / 5.081 |
| bignum-add-opt (+26.0%) | 6.120G / 6.090G | 1.238 / 1.254 / 1.288 | 1.253 / 1.274 / 1.294 |
| bfs (+7.3%) | 6.089G / 6.058G | 3.917 / 4.065 / 4.259 | 3.873 / 4.072 / 4.255 |

| centrality (-15.6%) | 6.676G / 6.645G | 4.379 / 4.456 / 4.625 | 4.320 / 4.451 / 4.596 |
| bfs-delayed (+22.6% instructions in one run) | 5.461G / 5.444G | 3.739 / 3.825 / 3.932 | 3.685 / 3.793 / 3.898 |

- Instruction counts of these runtime-heavy ports vary by several percent from run to run, so the instruction columns above are medians.

**Code size and compile time.**

- The C shrinks in every changed program: -12.5% in total over the 44, up to -36% for closures/palindrome.
- Every user closure is gone; the 8 left are the runtime's IO closures.
- Emit time over the 53 changed programs is +19% (21.4 s to 25.6 s, one run each). Most of it is in emission, not the pass: delaunay-animation `c_units` goes from 0.82 s to 1.1 s, and the pass itself takes 70 ms.
- With best of 3: parallel-ml/delaunay-animation 1.11 s to 1.45 s, `app_slash_boss_3d` 1.51 s to 1.59 s (+5%).
- `comp.ts` is 91,192 ttok, +3,817 over `opt/integration`. The token cap is left aside.

## Checks

- **Native lane, 1,107 tests** (the repo's, plus #2030's six fixtures and `clo_elim`): every status is equal to `opt/integration`'s (957 pass, 27 FAIL whose expected lines hold stderr or exit codes, 123 compile-error tests). The C changes in 66 tests, plus `clo_elim_generic`.
- **Memory**, `-DBEND_POISON` with live heap words counted at exit, at 1 and 8 threads, on the 67 changed tests: the same output as integration. There are 0 live words on 65. The other two behave identically on both: `gfx__clicks` reports no count; `io__tcp_send_slow_peer` has 420 live words.
- **JS and the interpreter** go through `js_lib`, which this does not touch. The JS of the six closure tests is byte-identical to integration's.
- **Metal** (`--gpu on`) passes on the three changed `!` tests: `gpu_reach_plain`, `fork_leaf_result_loop`, `sum_loop_shapes`.
- **The final head emits the same C** as the measured one on all 985 emitted tests and 244 programs.
- **New tests:**
  - `tests/run/clo_elim.bend`: a capture shared with the caller (a list and a tree read after the call); captures of four layouts; a lambda handed through two defs; one def copied for two lambdas; a lambda the def returns; a lambda the def stores in a node; a recursion that passes its lambda on unchanged; a recursion through the lambda's own body; a continuation that grows each step.
  - `tests/run/clo_elim_generic.bend`: delaunay-animation's LZW loop in its closure spelling.
- **Wrong versions** (`bench/closure-elim/results/wrong_versions.txt`). Caught:
  - copies keyed without the lambda;
  - captures passed in reverse;
  - beta binding the wrong argument;
  - the lend without its box test;
  - erased arguments not filled.

  Not caught by any test:
  - copying the body with its cells. With the type arguments filled, a stale level only names an open type. This held on every program, delaunay-animation included, so the lowering is kept as a guard.
  - passing type-only captures as live. This needs a variable that the lambda names only in a type and the caller also consumes; no test has one.

## Not covered

- A function chosen by a value (`choose(U32 -> U32, c, f, g)`): its parameter's type is a type variable, so it is left a closure.
- Named defs passed as values, and partial applications.
- JS.
- Cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86.

Raw results, scripts and sweeps: nicolas-abril/bend branch `bench/closure-elim` (9fde286b).

title: fix(lint): format a glued < that no > closes instead of throwing
body:
`format/layout` throws on a file that checks when a `<` glued to a name is not a type argument. `bend-lint` then exits 2 and writes nothing, although the fix is marked safe:

```python
import Base
def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    Unit<- IO.print("x")
    IO.print("y")
```

```
$ bun tools/bend-lint/src/lint.ts t.bend --rules tools/bend-lint/rules/format.ts --fix
bend-lint: format/layout: unbalanced delimiters
$ echo $?
2
```

`(a<4 : U32)` in a def body does the same. Removing the one space before `<-` in a repository file, such as line 92 of `tests/base/read_bounds.bend`, is enough to reach it.

## Why

`tokens()` splits a `<-` glued after a name into `<` and `-`, so that `Box<-T` opens type arguments. `tree()` then opens a group at every `<` glued after a name. In `Unit<- m` and `a<4` no `>` closes that group, so `tree()` throws at the end of the file.

## What changes

- `tokens()` splits `<-` only when no space follows it, as in `Box<-T`. `Unit<- m` stays a bind and formats as `Unit <- m`.
- `tree()` gives a `<` group's tokens back to its enclosing group when a `)`, `]`, `}` or the end of the file comes before its `>`. `(a<4 : U32)` formats as `(a < 4: U32)`, as `(a < 4 : U32)` already does.
- A fully glued `Unit<-m` still splits. The rule's parse check now reports it without a fix instead of throwing.

## Verified

title: With stdin closed, the C lane's wake pipe takes fd 0, and reading /dev/stdin blocks forever
body:
### What you did

`si.bend` reads 4 bytes from `/dev/stdin`:

```python
import Base

def show(p: File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, String>) -> IO(Unit):
  (f, r) = p
  match r:
    case Done{s}:
      do IO<Unit>:
        u : Unit <- IO.print("Done(" ++ String.quote(s) ++ ")")
        File.close(f)
    case Fail{(code, msg)}:
      do IO<Unit>:
        u : Unit <- IO.print("Fail(" ++ U32.show(code) ++ ")")
        File.close(f)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    f : File <- IO.try(File, File.open("/dev/stdin", "r"))
    p : File & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, String> <- File.read(f, 4)
    show(p)
```

Each lane runs it with stdin closed (`<&-`):

```
bun bend2/main.ts si.bend -o si && timeout 5 ./si <&-
bun bend2/main.ts si.bend -o si.js && bun si.js <&-
node si.js <&-
bun bend2/main.ts si.bend <&-
```

### What happened

```
C:            (nothing, killed by timeout: exit 124)
JS, Bun:      Done("")
JS, Node 24:  Done("")
interpreter:  Done("")
```

With `</dev/null` instead of `<&-`, the C lane prints `Done("")` too.

`io_loop` opens its wake pipe with `pipe(io_wake_fd)`. With fd 0 closed, the pipe's read end becomes fd 0:

```
$ strace -f -e trace=pipe2,openat ./si <&-
pipe2([0, 3], 0)                        = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/dev/stdin", O_RDONLY) = 4
```

`/dev/stdin` then opens the wake pipe, and `File.read` blocks on it. The program's read and the event loop also share that pipe.

Reopening a closed fd 0, 1 or 2 on `/dev/null` before `pipe(io_wake_fd)` would give the C lane the other lanes' answer. I have not opened a PR, as the fix goes in `comp.ts`, which is at its cap.

### bend version

main 0dfcb81c (`bun bend2/main.ts`), Bun 1.4.0, Node 24.22.3

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 23.1.6

title: perf(comp): strided and downward counters get index bounds; a loop's next turns read a fixed array side by side
body:
Closes most of what is left between Bend and C on PolyBench's array kernels after `opt/integration`, and roughly halves the cycles of the dot-per-cell kernels, with no program slower. Stacked on `opt/integration` (1bae0165, which merges the earlier drafts #2137, #2149 with 3d772230 and 72ce6fbb, #2154, #2135 and the rest; none of those is part of this PR, and this PR replaces none of them: it extends #2149 and #2154). **This PR's own commits are `1bae0165..1d4901b2`:**

- f49c0791 **A counter stepped by a fixed word, or down, gets a bound.** #2149 bounds a counter stepped by a constant. A counter stepped by a word fixed for the loop (a column walk, `p + step`), down by a constant (`p - 1`) or down by a fixed word (`p - s`) now gets one too (`at + step * (n - 1)` up, `at - step * (n - 1)` down, none if it wraps), so its accesses lose their masks in the mask-free copy. A step taken through a `let` keeps its form. Test `tests/run/array_index_stride.bend`.
- f79888c0, a1918aa9 **A loop's next turns read a fixed array side by side.** #2154 runs the next 16 turns' calls of a countdown loop together when the inner loop is over words. In the mask-free copy it now also takes an inner loop that reads one array the turns hand it: a dot per output cell (lu's, ludcmp's and cholesky's Gram product, correlation, covariance). The array, and every word all lanes enter with that the lane step hands on unchanged, is passed once for all lanes; a counter of the outer loop stepped by a constant or a fixed word is that much further on in each lane. The lanes run only when (1) the loop's copy writes that array nowhere and hands it to nothing else (checked on its text), (2) b and its lane step only read arrays and compute words (checked on their text once every spin is emitted), (3) no array is shared anywhere in the program (`BLK_SHR 0`), and (4) the turn still holds the array the lanes read (a runtime check). A lane variant now emits its helpers in place. Lanes over two arrays are left out (clang keeps that step scalar: doitgen 1.9x the cycles). Test `tests/run/lanes_array.bend`.
- 70588988 takes out a part of f49c0791 that handed a flat cycle's (#2188) in-place steps the bounds of their arguments: ocaml-lu-decomp 0.33x and parallel-ml lu 0.92x the cycles, but ocaml-nbody-imm 2.25x, linearrec-opt 1.59x, to-gif 1.30x, linearrec 1.20x, ocaml-nbody 1.14x (in linearrec the unmasked loop moves its F32 accumulator between integer and float registers every turn).
- 2c011931, 1d4901b2 **In a loop that writes, an access along a word's stride stays masked.** Bare, syrk ran 1.22x the cycles at every placement and deriche 1.10x the instructions (below). syr2k's 0.79x goes with them. Two more read-only cases in the stride test.

Out-of-range indexes keep Bend's semantics exactly: an access without a proven bound is masked as before, and the lanes read through masked accesses.

## Where the gap was (one M4 P-core thread, cycles median of 5, C = PolyBench's own kernel at `-O3 -ffp-contract=off`)

On main the stencils and gemm were 2.9x-3.9x behind C; that was the index masks (`blk_at`), which keep clang from vectorising, and `opt/integration` (#2137/#2149) already removes it. A C twin per kernel (the PolyBench kernel taking on Bend's constraints one at a time: run-time sizes, Bend's loop form, wrapping u32 indexes, arrays as u32 cells of one u64 heap, masks) puts the whole main-to-C gap on the masks for jacobi-2d (twin 1.14G -> 4.45G cycles with masks; C 1.30G, main 4.73G, integration 1.18G), heat-3d, gemm, floyd-warshall and lu; seidel-2d is latency-bound and level everywhere. What integration left:

- **lu, ludcmp, cholesky (1.14x-1.17x):** the ports build the matrix with a dot per cell (`B[r][s] = sum_t A[r][t] * A[s][t]`), a chain of dependent adds, where PolyBench runs `t` outermost and accumulates in memory, independent per cell. C's loop order in the twin: 2.52G -> 1.87G. Running 16 cells' dots side by side (twin): 1.22G; the init alone 1.83G -> 0.53G. That is commit 2.
- **durbin (1.48x), gemver (1.12x):** loops down an array (`p - 1`) or along a column stayed masked. Commit 1.
- **heat-3d (1.19x):** Bend's loop form on 118-cell rows (+11% in the twin) and wrapping u32 indexes (+5%); not addressed.
- **atax:** `(i + j) % n` in the init with a run-time `n` (C's is a constant). Not the compiler.
- floyd-warshall runs at 0.26x of C (the port reads `path[i][k]` once per row, so clang vectorises; the C does not); correlation and covariance are memory-bound in C.

## syrk, and why word strides stay masked in loops that write

Unmasking syrk's column read (`C[i][j] += x * A[j][k]`, `j` along the row, `A` down a column) made it 1.20x-1.25x the cycles at every one of 16 placements, for 10% fewer instructions; the loop is the same nine instructions minus the read's two `and`s. A C twin of that loop reproduces it (3.72G against 3.08G), at any offset between the two arrays (not 4K aliasing), and one extra op on the read's address, even an `and` with an opaque all-ones word, gives the masked speed back (3.16G); without the row update (the read alone) unmasking is faster. So it takes the strided miss-prone read beside the read-modify-write of the row; the exact mechanism in the core is not identified. deriche's filters, unmasked, ran 1.10x the instructions at level cycles: with two copies of the loop, clang keeps its F32 coefficients in integer registers and moves each to a float register every turn. Rather than a rule for syrk's shape alone, every word-stride access in a loop that writes stays masked; reads in loops that only read (dots, column sums) still lose their masks. This costs syr2k's 0.79x and symm's small gain; everything else is unchanged.

## Effect (this PR against `opt/integration`, same session, interleaved)

| program | cycles | instructions | Bend / C before -> after |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| correlation | 0.306x | 0.437x | 0.90 -> 0.33 |
| covariance | 0.319x | 0.431x | 0.95 -> 0.32 |
| cholesky | 0.416x | 1.438x | 0.97 -> 0.40 |
| lu | 0.496x | 1.295x | 1.14 -> 0.57 |
| ludcmp | 0.496x | 1.295x | 1.17 -> 0.59 |
| durbin | 0.717x | 0.303x | 1.48 -> 0.95 |
| trmm | 0.957x | 0.804x | |
| mvt | 0.959x | 0.720x | |
| gramschmidt | 0.969x | 0.914x | |
| gemver | 0.973x | 0.775x | 1.12 -> 1.04 |
| 2mm, 3mm, doitgen, adi | 0.977x-0.997x | 0.89x-0.90x | |
| syrk, syr2k, symm, deriche | 0.998x-1.000x | 1.000x-1.003x | |
| nussinov | 1.041x (16-placement sweep: median 0.997x) | 0.947x | |
| graphio (parallel-ml) | 1.053x (sweep: median 1.010x) | 1.019x | |

16-position placement sweeps (median cycles, ratio to integration per placement): lu 2.553G -> 1.264G (0.488x-0.517x), correlation 3.243G -> 1.025G (0.283x-0.411x), cholesky 2.187G -> 0.919G (0.416x-0.429x), durbin 3.039G -> 2.222G (0.717x-0.737x), syrk 3.098G -> 3.082G (0.988x-1.025x).

**The lane kernels run more instructions in fewer cycles.** cholesky runs 1.44x the instructions, lu and ludcmp 1.30x, in 0.42x-0.50x the cycles. Without lanes each cell's dot is one chain of dependent float adds, so the core waits on the add latency every step. With lanes, 16 independent chains run side by side and the core overlaps them. The bookkeeping that makes this possible costs instructions: each lane's words are loaded from and stored back to small per-lane arrays every step, and every lane computes its own index. (correlation and covariance also run fewer instructions, because their unmasked strided reads save more than the lanes add.)

Of the 244 benchmark programs, 39 emit C that differs from `opt/integration`'s (most PolyBench kernels; some bend-runtime, clbg and kostya programs whose #2154 lane variants now emit helpers in place; graphio); the other 205 emit the same C. Over the 39: geometric mean of cycles 0.878x of integration; 13 faster by more than 2%, none slower by more than 2% once swept (nussinov and graphio, 4-5% in 5-run medians, are level under placement sweeps).

## Checks

- The native test lane, all 1,102 tests on this head: 952 pass, 27 FAIL (the tests whose expected lines hold stderr or exit codes; the same 27 on `opt/integration`), 123 do not emit C (the same 123). The two new tests pass on C, JS and the interpreter alike.
- Memory check (`-DBEND_POISON`, live-word count) on every test whose C changes on the way (`array_index_stride`, `lanes_array`, `countdown_lanes`, `loop_call_inline`, `loop_fixed_call`, `mix_lanes`, `sieve_eratosthenes`): right output and 0 live words at 1 and 8 threads.
- No changed test calls the GPU (`!`), and GPU lane selection is untouched (the lanes are `#if !DEVICE`, the mask-free copy is host-only), so Metal was not rerun.
- Adversarial tests. `array_index_stride`: counters stepped by a word in range, past the end, by 0 and wrapping past 2^32; down by 2 and by a word, in range and under zero; a growing step; a step bound through a `let`; read-only loops along a word, down by a word and with a growing step. `lanes_array`: rows summed in lanes in range, two apart, past the array's end (the reads wrap), fewer than 16 rows, short rows; and the shapes that must not run in lanes: a sum that writes the cells it reads, a turn that writes the array it sums, turns that sum two arrays in turn (the runtime check), turns that swap the arrays.
- Deliberately wrong versions, each caught by the new tests: a down counter with no wrap check, a word step taken as 1, a word step whose word is not fixed, a down-by-word step taken as 1; lanes without the runtime array check, without the loop's write check, with a counter's lane offset taken as 1, and without b's purity check (8 of 8).
- All 244 benchmark programs: the 39 whose C changes print `expected.txt` (5 runs at one thread; the parallel ports also at 10 threads); the other 205 emit the same C as `opt/integration`.

Not run: the cluster gates, CUDA, Linux, x86. `comp.ts` 90,799 ttok (integration 87,824; +2,975).

title: Keep the native wake pipe off standard descriptors
body:
Fixes #2232. If stdin was closed before a native program started, the wake pipe could become fd 0. Opening `/dev/stdin` would then read the event loop's own pipe and hang. Fill any closed standard descriptors with `/dev/null` before creating that pipe; inherited descriptors stay as they are.

On Linux the reported program went from timing out to reading EOF. The new gate case also passed with a normal input pipe, and with stdin closed alongside stdout, stderr, or both. Repo gate: 56/56. The ping script bundles; the full installer/mini gates and macOS/GPU checks weren't run, so I'm leaving this in draft.

title: Fold known match arms in JS expressions
body:
Fixes #2181 on the JS side. `pick(boom(k), 0n, 100n)` now prints `100` instead of evaluating `boom(k)` and hitting the Nat limit. JS expression calls reuse the C emitter's fold, so the chosen arm keeps the arguments it needs. This doesn't change the tail-call path or settle general strictness.

The original case now prints `100` through the CLI too. The new regression checks both the dropped argument and a live argument on Node, Bun and native C. Four existing JS call/closure cases and the repo gate (56/56) passed. Keeping it draft: mini test/perf, macOS and Metal/CUDA weren't run.

title: Parallel bend-cache writers can lose each other’s traces
body:

title: fix(rt): a task's heap continuation runs in turns, not in the finished task's sequence
body:
**Stacked on `opt/integration` (1bae0165): this PR's own commit is `0ce9272b`; the rest of the diff against main is integration's.** `comp.ts` +53 ttok (87,824 to 87,877 on integration). Measured on one Mac (M4, 4 P + 6 E cores), GPU off, every timed run under the shared lock; other processes held at most 3.6 cores during the scaling runs. The cluster gates have not been run.

## The bug

A drain runs each task in sequence (`seq`: a fork's calls run inline, its frames on the stack). When such a task finished, `FID_EXIT` entered the task's heap continuation directly and kept the sequence bit (`seq = (seq & 1) | …`). That continuation, and every continuation after it, then ran with its forks inline: the rest of the program on one thread. A heap continuation is made by code running in turns; `monk_step` already runs a continuation it is handed in turns (`seq = false`), and now `FID_EXIT` does the same on the host (the device keeps its bit).

The path is reached when a grow turn hands a fork-free task to the drain because its continuation is fork-free (or a join): that continuation's own continuation can fork. Traces (a per-thread event log patched into the emitted C) on `opt/integration`, 10 threads:
- `parallel-ml/delaunay`: one drain task ran 4,017 ms in sequence, from `pfor_go_0_j3`; for 100% of the run one worker was busy. With the fix: 965 ms.
- `parallel-ml/bfs`: one 437 ms task from `pfor_go_6_j8`, 70% of the run with one worker busy; with the fix 61% of the run has all 10 busy.

This is the "rounds that do not speed up" in the parallel-ml README (the BFS family, `delaunay` with `Split.split`'s loops forked, `primes-blocked`'s evaluation order).

## Effect

Wall ms at 1 / 2 / 4 / 10 threads, median of 5 (min-max in `bench/par-split`'s `results/curves.jsonl` on nicolas-abril/bend):

| program | main | integration | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| bfs | 1297 / 1009 / 894 / 834 | 987 / 757 / 660 / 610 | 985 / 574 / 407 / **319** |
| bfs-delayed | 1181 / 910 / 804 / 733 | 952 / 724 / 619 / 575 | 961 / 558 / 399 / **308** |
| bfs-det-dedup | 1545 / 1262 / 1155 / 1116 | 1192 / 969 / 892 / 818 | 1196 / 701 / 515 / **408** |
| bfs-det-priority | 2019 / 1695 / 1574 / 1536 | 1168 / 935 / 848 / 782 | 1178 / 668 / 464 / **356** |
| bfs-tree-entangled-fixed | 1221 / 1063 / 1048 / 960 | 1004 / 840 / 815 / 796 | 977 / 547 / 462 / **474** |
| centrality | 1543 / 1255 / 1138 / 1083 | 1133 / 894 / 793 / 748 | 1132 / 644 / 470 / **379** |
| low-d-decomp | 961 / 557 / 415 / 321 | 738 / 504 / 405 / 341 | 740 / 455 / 337 / **271** |
| delaunay | 3883 / 2044 / 1540 / 1025 | 3190 / 3236 / 3184 / 3180 | 3237 / 1752 / 1342 / **935** |
| delaunay, Split.split forked | 3856 / 3893 / 3749 / 3714 | 3156 / 3233 / 3175 / 3117 | 3205 / 1679 / 1294 / **856** |
| max-indep-set | 1250 / 709 / 512 / 404 | 957 / 558 / 404 / 308 | 949 / 557 / 400 / 306 |
| msort (control) | 1906 / 982 / 583 / 347 | 1202 / 622 / 370 / 206 | 1201 / 625 / 368 / 207 |
| quickhull (control) | 822 / 458 / 294 / 199 | 685 / 386 / 247 / 164 | 686 / 389 / 244 / 166 |

The other programs measured (primes, primes-simple-bool, primes-blocked, triangle-count, mcss, tokens, seam-carve, suffix-array, nearest-nbrs) are within ±5% at every thread count.

All 244 bend-benchmarks programs print `expected.txt` at 1 and 10 threads. One thread never takes the path, so the code run there is the same: instructions over the 215 programs outside the set apart (the harness-hoisted 28, rbtree-ck) have a geomean of 1.0016 (the run-to-run noise of `/usr/bin/time`'s count here, up to 2.7%). At 10 threads, over the 155 programs above 0.1 s (one run each), wall geomean 0.978. Re-measured with 5 runs: `closures/delaunay-animation` 1300 to 1389 ms (+6.8%) and `bend-runtime/tree-bitonic` 1223 to 1266 ms (+3.4%) are slower: there the sequential continuation was cheaper than its turns.

## Checks

- Native lane, 1,100 tests: no status differs (952 pass, 25 FAIL as on integration, 123 that do not emit).
- Memory check (`-DBEND_POISON`, live words) at 1 and 8 threads on the 117 tests that fork: 0 live words but `io/heap_large_reuse` (65,536, as on integration); `io/stack_fault_trap` and `gfx/clicks` exit as on integration.
- Metal: the 53 `!` tests built with `bend -o` and run with `--gpu on` print the same as on integration (52 run; `gfx/clicks` waits for a window on both). The device path is unchanged.
- New test `tests/run/fork_exit_turns.bend`: fork-free halves whose join is followed by a forking caller, 60 rounds; same result at every thread count.

title: perf(rt): a hungry drain splits the oldest fork a sequential task has open
body:
**Stacked on #2253, which is stacked on `opt/integration` (1bae0165): this PR's own commit is `6938a7d6`.** `comp.ts` +3,465 ttok over #2253 (87,877 to 91,342). Measured on one Mac (M4, 4 P + 6 E cores), GPU off, under the shared lock; other processes held at most 2.0 cores during the A/B below. The cluster gates have not been run.

## What

A drain runs each of its tasks in sequence on the thread that claimed it, and a task never moves. When one task holds most of a drain's work (one corner of an unbalanced fork tree), it runs on one thread while the others wait for the next turn. This is lazy task creation for the drain:

- A two-call fork run in sequence notes its first call's frame on the thread's fork list (only threads of a pool with more than one; the test is a bit of `seq`, a register, so one thread pays a test and a branch per fork and its first continuation).
- Threads past their claims hunt. While more hunt than tasks wait, a note turns the thread's **oldest** unsplit frame into a task, at most once per 20 µs of a thread: the fork's `s` segment reads the second call's arguments off that frame (as its first continuation would) into a task whose answer goes to a future, in a slot of the thread's box, and writes the fork's `w` segment into the frame's id word.
- Returning there, `w` takes the task back and runs it, or waits for the thread that took it, running others' tasks meanwhile; then it continues as the first continuation would.
- A drain still ends when its claims do: a claim waits for every task split off it. A hunter that finds nothing for a while sleeps until a task is boxed or the drain ends.

Without the 20 µs limit, `bend-runtime/tree-bitonic` split 3.3 million small frames at 10 threads and took 2,682 ms against 1,292; with it, 1,315.

## Effect

Wall ms, median of 5, #2253 and this PR interleaved:

| program | 1 thr #2253 | 1 thr this PR | 10 thr #2253 | 10 thr this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| unbalanced fork tree (micro, item i holds 1/(i+1)) | 2979 | 2983 | 1031 | **358** | 0.35x |
| bfs | 957 | 953 | 307 | 298 | 0.97 |
| delaunay | 2972 | 2961 | 854 | 830 | 0.97 |
| msort | 1188 | 1186 | 202 | 198 | 0.98 |
| bfs-tree-entangled-fixed | 945 | 903 | 427 | 426 | 1.00 |
| mcss / nearest-nbrs / triangle-count / primes / 1000 rounds of 64 leaves | | | | | 0.99 to 1.00 |
| seam-carve | 965 | 966 | 284 | 297 | **1.05** |
| one array forked per element (micro) | 74 | 85 | 1242 | 1323 | **1.07** |
| fib with a fork at every level (micro) | 42 | 54 | 8 | 12 | **1.39** |

The unbalanced micro now scales 8.3x on 10 threads (2.9x before). The parallel-ml programs these were found in (primes, primes-simple-bool) do not gain: they run the same instructions at 10 threads as at 1 but 2.7x the user time, memory traffic (lanes of different primes unmark the same lines of a 400 MB array), not the scheduler.

**Cost.** Fine-grained forks pay the note and its drop: the fib micro (a fork every ~38 instructions) +31% at one thread (+4.7% instructions; the rest is the drop test in the first continuation, measured by removing it by hand), +39% at 10. Over the 244 bend-benchmarks programs at one thread, instructions against #2253: geomean 1.0016 over the 215 outside the set apart (the harness-hoisted 28, rbtree-ck), within this machine's run-to-run noise of up to 2.7%; above it: `osprey/fib` (bend-par) +6.5%, `polybench/atax` +5.1%, `osprey/pascal` (bend-par) +4.3%, `polybench/bicg` +3.9%. At 10 threads, wall geomean 0.980 over 157 programs above 0.1 s (one run each).

## Checks

- All 244 programs print `expected.txt` at 1 and 10 threads.
- Native lane, 1,100 tests: no status differs from integration (952 pass, 25 FAIL, 123 that do not emit).
- Memory check (`-DBEND_POISON`, live words) at 1 and 8 threads on the 117 tests that fork and the new tests: 0 live words but `io/heap_large_reuse` (65,536, as on integration).
- Metal: the 53 `!` tests built with `bend -o`, run with `--gpu on`, print the same as on integration; the notes are empty on the device.
- New tests in `tests/run/`: `lazy_split_deep` (a fork chain 20,000 frames deep beside a filler tree, both sides), `lazy_split_unbal` (item 0 holds half the work), `lazy_split_results` (second calls returning a tree, a list and a pair), `lazy_split_shared` (one array forked to every leaf). Right at 1, 2, 4 and 10 threads, 3 runs each.
- Wrong versions: splitting the newest frame (whose frame is not written yet), not waiting for a split task, reading the wrong answer word, a steal without its compare-and-swap: each gives wrong answers in the new tests. Not dropping notes exhausts memory (killed by the 4 GB cap). Never taking a task back, no 20 µs limit, and hunters that never hunt only change the speed.
