title: Do not consume flags as bend-cache option values
body:
Fixes #2275. `--cache --stats` used to create a file named `--stats`. Value-taking options now report the missing value instead of swallowing the next flag. `--cache ./--stats` still means an explicit file.

I reproduced the stray file, then checked the real CLI with all three value-taking options and an explicit dash-prefixed path. Two focused cache tests and the Linux repo gate passed (56/56). Mini gates not run.

title: Preserve Base import order in bend-lint
body:
Refs #1941. `bend-lint` accepted the issue's repro even though `bend --check-only` refused it. This uses the same Base-first rule that #2201 added to `--checkup`. The cached Base is reused only when it's the first import. This doesn't change the checker or try to solve shared Base caching.

The original repro now exits 1 in both commands. The tests also cover Base first and a file whose unsaved text puts the dependency first. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. Mini gates not run.

title: bend-lint silently ignores arrays in rule configuration
body:
### What you did

Set `rules.json` to `{"rules": []}` and ran:

```sh
bun tools/bend-lint/src/lint.ts main.bend --config rules.json --json
```

### What happened

The command exits 0 and prints `{"ok":true,"findings":[]}`. The config itself is an object, but its `rules` value is not the documented map keyed by rule id. Bad overrides should fail with exit 2 instead of being ignored. This is distinct from #2256, where the JSON document itself is an array or null.

### The file

```python
import Base
def main() -> U32:
  42
```

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: The effects guide makes both backend imports sound mandatory
body:
### What you did

I took the clock example from `guide/EFFECTS.md` and tried it with just the source needed by each backend: `clock.js` for `bend main.bend` and `bend main.bend -o out.cjs`, and `clock.c` for `bend main.bend -o out`.

### What happened

All three runs printed `ms: <number>`. The guide says an effect's body *is two imports*, which reads like both source files are required even when a package targets only one backend. It should say that an effect can import only the implementation for the lane it targets.

### The file

The clock example in `guide/EFFECTS.md`, with the other lane's import removed.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version

clang version 22.1.8 (Fedora 22.1.8-4.fc44)

title: Validate per-rule lint configuration
body:
An object like `{"rules": []}` used to pass and silently use the rules' defaults. `rules` now needs to be a map, and an override for a loaded rule must be an object or `"off"`.

Fixes #2279.

The original CLI command now exits 2. The focused tests check a few bad shapes, valid overrides, and turning a rule off. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. Mini gates not run.

title: Explain single-backend foreign effects
body:
Fixes #2280. The guide made it sound like even a JS-only or native-only effect needs both files. This says which import each lane uses and keeps the example that targets both.

I ran the clock with just the JS import (interpreter and compiled JS on Bun/Node), just the C import (Linux native), and both imports. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56.

title: Validating a single bend-lint fix compares every pair of edits
Validate large lint fixes in range order
body:
A rule that returned one large fix paid for every pair of edits before the linter displayed it, even without `--fix`. This checks ranges in order, per file, and only compares neighbors. The rule still gets the same result and keeps its original edit order.

Fixes #2283.

On the same 16,000 edits, three-run median validation time went from 1,232 ms to 6 ms. That includes a warm lint run with the rule; the result stayed the same. A 200,000-edit check passed too, as did three focused tests and the Linux repo gate (56/56). Mini gates not run.

title: perf(base): Array.show walks from the last element, so it copies each element's text once
body:
`Array.show` was quadratic on the C lane. Each step passed the text shown so far to `f` and appended `", "` to the result, and `String.append` copies its first argument, so the step at element k copied the whole prefix. It now walks from the last element to the first, as `Array.write` takes its elements, and puts each element's text in front of the rest. Every step copies only one element's text.

`f` is still called with `"["` for the first element and `", "` for the others, as `Array.write` calls it. Under the contract in the comment above `Array.write`, "f(s, x) being s followed by x's text", the output is the same string.

## Timings

`Array.show(~U32, ~sh, Array.new(U32, dn, 7))` with `sh(s, x) = s ++ U32.show(x)`, printing the length. C lane, one thread, pinned to one core, best of 3 runs (one run for main at 65,536 cells):

| cells | main | this |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 11 ms | 3 ms |
| 4,096 | 183 ms | 2 ms |
| 16,384 | 999 ms | 4 ms |
| 65,536 | 57.5 s | 5 ms |
| 262,144 | | 16 ms |
| 1,048,576 | | 58 ms |

Bun, Node 24 and the interpreter take the same time before and after (Bun 33 ms, Node 32–44 ms, interpreter about 300 ms at 16,384 and 65,536 cells). The JS lane prints a pure `main`'s arrays through `Array.show`, and the walk stays a tail loop, so it does not deepen the stack.

## Verified

Linux x86_64, Bun 1.4.0, clang 23.1.6:

- I compared the old definition, kept under another name, with the new one on arrays of 1 to 1,024 distinct `U32`s, with two `f`s, and on arrays of `String`s that hold quotes. Every case printed the same string on the C lane, Bun, Node 24 and the interpreter.
- The same program under `-fsanitize=address,undefined -DBEND_POISON`, at 1 and 4 threads, reported no errors.
- I ran all 1,079 tests under `tests/` on the JS lane with and without this change, and every test gets the same verdict. `tests/show/array_elements.bend` passes on the C lane, the JS lane and the interpreter.

title: fix(cli): an error in a def with a ~ parameter names its own file, not base.bend
body:
Since #2208, a CLI error ends with `--> file:line:col`. For an error in a def with a `~` parameter, that line names `bend2/base.bend` instead of the file the error is in:

```python
import Base

def f(~x: U32) -> U32:
  True{}
```

```
$ bend f.bend --check-only
SOME PROOFS FAIL
Error:
- expected : U32
- observed : Bool
Location: f
3 | def f(~x: U32) -> U32:
4>|   True{}
  |   ^^^^^^
5 |
--> /…/bend2/base.bend:4:3
```

The excerpt and the caret are right. Without the `~`, the last line is `--> f.bend:4:3`. The line and column are the user file's, so the `base.bend` location is often a blank line or a column past the end of its line. In a file that doesn't import Base, the `-->` line is missing entirely.

## Why

`book_location` decides a span is Base's when some tld marked `b` has a type in the span's file. `def_check` checks a def with `~` parameters in a book of its own: each parameter becomes a tld `f~x` marked `b: true`, typed in the def's own file. That book's tlds inherit the others through the prototype, so `Object.values` sees only those parameter tlds, and they match.

## What changes

`book_location` walks the inherited tlds too (`for … in`) and skips names with a `~`. The other locations are unchanged: an error in an imported file, in the entry, at a missing import, at a template call site like `List.map(~U32, ~U32, ~(x => True{}), xs)`, and in Base itself. For the last one, I appended a broken plain def and a broken template def to a copy of base.bend, and both still print `base.bend:<line>:<col>`.

`tests/io/cli_source_location` gains the case above: it returns 3 on main and 0 with this change, on the interpreter and on Bun.

## Verified

Linux x86_64, Bun 1.4.0:

- I ran `--check-only` on all 1,882 `.bend` files under `tests/` with and without this change. 1,880 print the same output. The other two are existing tests that hit this bug, `tests/comptime/err_generic.bend` (`--> bend2/base.bend:8:3`) and `tests/page/comp_param_match.bend` (`--> bend2/base.bend:13:10`). With the change, each names its own file at the same line and column. Their `#|` lines don't include the `-->` line, so their expected output is unchanged.
- `main.ts` grows by 226 characters. I could not run `ttok` here. By characters, `main.ts` is about 13k tokens against its 16k cap.

title: perf(base): a bench for String.join's cost, and it is not the cost
body:
`String.join` is right-nested and `String.append` copies its first argument, so the string copied at every level is the head piece, and the copies are the sum of the head pieces' lengths: **O(n) in characters, not the O(n^2) the prefix sums would give.** The count that says otherwise counts the other nesting, the one that copies the tail.

This bench joins `n` lines with a separator and folds the joined text into a checksum, so the answer depends on every character and on the order. The C twin joins into one buffer with a plain loop and the TS twin joins with `Array.prototype.join`; all three print the same checksum at every size (140807 at 100 lines, 286908 at 200, 579410 at 400, 1165614 at 800, 2366261 at 1600, 4789659 at 3200).

Measured on the JS lane under bun, **the join alone is under a millisecond at every size the millisecond clock can resolve**, and the C twin is flat at 2.2-2.4 ms and the TS twin at 10.8-11.9 ms (both dominated by their start-up). So the join is not the bottleneck, and the cost of copying it was measured by counting rather than by timing.

A count needs a clock: this bench is the instrument that settles it, and the lines of the count it replaces are gone.

The three files are covered by the existing `gates/repo.ts` allow line for `bench/runtime/[a-z-]+/main.(bend|c|lean|ts)`, so no allow-list change is needed. There is no Lean twin: the perf gate runs the bend, C and TS lanes, and a Lean twin would be a third reference rather than a second measurement.

title: Substitute call arguments into emit_unfold let type annotations
body:
### User-visible failure

Pure, safe Bend programs (passing `bend --verdict`) can crash with `SIGSEGV` (`bend: memory fault`) when compiled to native C if a function with an erased type parameter (e.g. `def caller(-A: Type, ...)`) calls a flat polymorphic function whose erased type parameter shares the same name and index (e.g. `def dup(-A: Data, b: Bool, +x: A)`).

Even without a colliding caller parameter name, unfolding a polymorphic flat function leaks raw callee type variables into caller `Ann` nodes, causing `facts_hot` to fall back to `fact_add("open")` and degrading unboxed layouts.

### Root cause

In `bend2/comp.ts`, `emit_unfold` previously annotated unfolded `let`-bound arguments using `tele_unbind(m.tld!.T).doms`:

```ts
const doms = tele_unbind(m.tld!.T).doms;
const lets = fs.map((a, i) => !m.live[i] || term_const(a)
  || term_strip(a).$ === "Var" ? null
  : { p: probe("a"), v: Bend.Ann(a, doms[i][2]) });
```

`tele_unbind` leaves the callee's telescope variables unsubstituted (e.g. `Var("A", 0)`). When the caller binds the resulting `let` and later shares it (`bind_pop`), `facts_hot(sc.def, b.A, true)` looks up `Var("A", 0)` in the **caller's** telescope (`tele_unbind(tld_of(def).T).doms[w.i]`). If the caller also has an erased `-A` at index `0` (e.g. `Unit`), `facts_hot` marks the caller's `-A` argument hot instead of the actual instantiated type (`Node`):

- `Node`'s constructors (`Leaf`, `Bin`) remain cold (`CID_T[CID_Bin].hot == 0`), skipping `rfc_seal` on constructor children and emitting `term_loc(...)` instead of `ctr_take(...)` when matching.
- When the unfolded body shares the bound `Node` (`term_keep`), it becomes RFC-wrapped, so subsequent matching reads the RFC redirect word + adjacent heap memory as constructor fields and faults (`SIGSEGV`).

### Minimal change

- `bend2/comp.ts` (`emit_unfold`): walk `m.tld!.T` step-by-step via `ty_all(T)` and substitute each folded argument `T = f.B(a)` before annotating `Bend.Ann(a, f.A)`.
- `tests/reg/unfold_poly_hot.bend`: regression test (passing `--verdict`) covering colliding caller `-A` at index `0`, forwarding a caller's own erased type parameter at index `1` with a non-`Var` expression, and a dependent parameter type instantiated by a folded argument.

### Before / after evidence

On `tests/reg/unfold_poly_hot.bend` (`main` at `966bbb74`):

- **Before fix**:
  - Generated C has `CID_Unit` hot (`{ 0, 1, 0 }`), `CID_Leaf`/`CID_Bin` cold (`{ 1, 0, 0 }`, `{ 2, 0, 0 }`), and unsealed `Bin` children.
  - Native C binary crashes with `bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)` / `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` (exit code `139`).
- **After fix**:
  - Generated C has `CID_Unit` cold (`{ 0, 0, 0 }`), `CID_Leaf`/`CID_Bin` hot (`{ 1, 1, 0 }`, `{ 2, 1, 0 }`), and `rfc_seal` on `Bin` children.
  - `bun bend2/main.ts tests/reg/unfold_poly_hot.bend --verdict` -> `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
  - Bun JS, Node JS, native C (`-O3` and `-O3 -DBEND_POISON`, `--threads 1` and `--threads 4`) all output `94` (exit `0`).

### Validation & limits

- Verified on Linux x86_64 (`bun 1.3.12`, `node v24.14.1`, `clang 23.1.5`, Lean `v4.34.0`):
  - `bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 56 / 56` (`bend2/comp.ts`: `65,989 / 66,000` ttok, +9 tokens).
  - `tests/reg/unfold_poly_hot.bend`: `--verdict`, JS (Bun & Node), C (`-O3` and `-DBEND_POISON`, `--threads 1` & `--threads 4`).
  - `tests/reg/*.bend` and `tests/rfc/*.bend` sweep (JS + native C): `126` passed, `0` failed (`7` skipped for platform/foreign requirements).
- Not verified: macOS / Mac-mini cluster (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`), Metal, and CUDA device lanes.

title: Disable arr_loc redirect caching in spins that may free RFC cells
body:
### User-visible failure

When compiled to native C, programs that drop or split an RFC-wrapped `Array` inside a flat (`spin_*`) function and then allocate/wrap a new `Array` of the same size class can silently read the wrong array's elements (`Array.get`) and silently corrupt another live array's backing storage (`Array.set`).

This reproduces both in **100% pure, safe Bend** (passing `bend --verdict`, via `rfc_seal` when `BLK_SHR == 1`) and in `Array.fork` + `Array.join` code.

### Root cause

Commit `ef66a7cc` (`#1155`) caches the resolved data location `q{i}` for each `box` parameter `r{i}` of a `spin_*` function at entry (`Term h{i} = r{i};`) and rewrites `blk_loc(e.mem, a)` in `arr_loc` to:

```c
a == h0 ? q0 : blk_loc(e.mem, a)
```

This assumes that any later `Array` handle `a` with the same 64-bit `Term` bits as `h{i}` still points to `q{i}`. When `h{i}` is an RFC-wrapped `Array` (`term_rfc(h{i}) == true`), that invariant breaks if the `spin_*` function (or a `spin_*` callee) frees `r{i}`:

1. Dropping/splitting `r{i}` (`term_sink`, `blk_free`, `blk_half`, `blk_node`, or a freeing `spin_*` callee) returns its class-0 RFC redirect cell `r` to the lane's LIFO free list and its backing block `old_loc` to its size-class free list.
2. Subsequent allocations place another array `pad` at `old_loc`, a new array `b` at `new_loc`, and wrap `b` in an RFC cell (`rfc_seal` or `Array.fork`), which pops the **same** class-0 cell `r`.
3. The new handle `b1` now has identical 64-bit `Term` bits to `h0`, yet points to `new_loc != q0 (old_loc)`.
4. `arr_loc` matches `b1 == h0` and returns stale `q0` (`pad`'s backing storage), causing `Array.get` to read `pad` and `Array.set` to overwrite `pad`.

This also occurs across self-tail-loops (`WL_AGAIN`) when a `spin_*` drops its `Array` parameter and loops with a recycled RFC-wrapped handle (so merely restricting `arr_loc` to `p === i` is insufficient).

### Minimal change

- `bend2/comp.ts` (`term_same`, commit 1): remove the redundant hand-written recursion over `Lam`, `App`, `Ctr`, and `Mat` that duplicated `Bend.term_lower`, keeping the fast short-circuit on `x === y || x.$ !== y.$ || (x.$ === "Ctr" && x.k !== y.k)`. Saves 156 tokens (`65,989 -> 65,833`) so the fix lands in the file's normal style with 87 tokens of headroom (`65,913 / 66,000`).
- `bend2/comp.ts` (`arr_q`, `arr_loc`, `emit_spin`, `emit_native`, commit 2):
  - Track a `"free"` fact per `spin_*` in `c_units()`'s existing fixed-point loop whenever a `spin_*` takes at least one `"box"` parameter (`seg.ks.includes("box")`) and either emits an array-RFC-freeing helper (`/term_sink|blk_(free|half|node)/`) or calls another `spin_*` in `seg.refs` with `fact("free", r)`.
  - Pass the spin's `fid` to `arr_q(k, f)` so spins with `fact("free", f)` omit `Term h{i} = r{i};` / `, u64 q${i}` and always resolve `blk_loc(e.mem, a)` freshly (including when passing `q` into a non-freeing leaf `spin_*`).
  - Requiring `seg.ks.includes("box")` is sound (a spin with no boxed parameters cannot decrement a caller's RFC refcount) and preserves `#1155` caching on hot non-freeing loops such as `spin_array_hold` and `bench/runtime/histogram`.
  - Generated C is byte-for-byte identical to `main` everywhere except the spins that lose their `h`/`q` cache.
- `tests/reg/spin_array_reuse.bend` (100% safe Bend, passes `--verdict`): covers direct drop (`term_sink`), self-tail-loop (`WL_AGAIN`), transitive freeing `spin_*` callee + non-freeing leaf callee, `ANode` match (`blk_half`), and `ALeaf` match (`blk_free`), checking both `Array.get` reads and `Array.set` non-corruption of `pad`.
- `tests/reg/spin_array_fork_reuse.bend`: covers the `Array.fork` + `Array.join` reuse path.

### Before / after evidence

On `tests/reg/spin_array_reuse.bend` (`main` at `3d5bf43d`):

- **Before fix** (native C silently reads `pad` and overwrites `pad` on all 5 cases):
  ```text
  2
  111333 333
  444333 333
  666666 666
  901903 903
  801803 803
  ```
- **After fix** (`--verdict`: `ALL PROOFS CHECK`; Bun JS, Node JS, native C `-O3` & `-DBEND_POISON`, `--threads 1` & `--threads 4` all match):
  ```text
  2
  222333 111
  555333 444
  777777 666
  902903 901
  802803 801
  ```

On `tests/reg/spin_array_fork_reuse.bend`:
- **Before fix** (native C): `111333 333`
- **After fix** (Bun JS, Node JS, native C `-O3` & `-DBEND_POISON`, `--threads 1` & `--threads 4`): `222333 111`

Hot-loop caching & output preservation:
- `tests/reg/spin_array_hold.bend` and `bench/runtime/histogram/main.bend`: emitted C only changes on the freeing spins; all hot non-freeing loops (`spin_bump`, `spin_tot_go`, `spin_swap`, `spin_col_go`, `spin_grp_go`, `spin_cols_go`, `spin_count_go`, `spin_zero_go`, `spin_fill_go`, `spin_sum_go`) are byte-for-byte identical to `main`.
- `bench/runtime/lexer/main.bend`: emitted C and JS are byte-for-byte identical to `main` (and JS is byte-for-byte identical across all 36 `bench/runtime/*` + `match`/`u32`/`f32`/`nat`/`char` tests).

### Validation & limits

- Verified on Linux x86_64 (`bun 1.3.12`, `node v24.14.1`, `clang 23.1.5`, Lean `v4.34.0`):
  - `bun gates/repo.ts`: `PASS: 56 / 56` (`bend2/comp.ts`: `65,913 / 66,000` ttok, `-76` net from `main`).
  - `tests/reg/spin_array_reuse.bend` (`--verdict`, Bun, Node, C `-O3` & `-DBEND_POISON`, `--threads 1` & `--threads 4`), `tests/reg/spin_array_fork_reuse.bend`, `tests/reg/spin_array_hold.bend`, and all 20 runnable `tests/run/*array*.bend` tests on native C.
- Not verified: macOS / Mac-mini cluster (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`), Metal, and CUDA device lanes.

title: Multiple build outputs can resolve to the same file through links
body:
### What you did

In a scratch directory, create `output.js`, set `output.c` as a symlink to it, and run:

```sh
printf 'original\n' > output.js
ln -s output.js output.c
bend main.bend -o output.js -o output.c
```

### What happened

Bend exits 0, but `output.js` holds C source, not JS. The second output overwrites the first because the two spellings resolve to one file. Direct duplicate outputs already fail before writing. The same check should cover linked output destinations.

### The file

```python
import Base
def main() -> U32:
  42
```

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Bend help does not show the separator for program flags
body:
### What you did

Ran `bend argv.bend --verbose`, then followed its suggestion to read `bend --help`.

### What happened

`bend argv.bend --verbose` reports `unknown option --verbose`. Help shows `bend <file.bend> [args]` but doesn't show the `--` separator that lets the flag reach `IO.args()`. `bend argv.bend -- --verbose` already works. The existing command should be visible in `--help`.

### The file

```python
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    xs : List<String> <- IO.args()
    IO.print(List.show(~&1, ~String, ~(s => "<" ++ s ++ ">"), xs))
```

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: A multi-file bend-lint fix preview rescans every edit for every file
body:
### What you did

Called the public `render(diag)` with one diagnostic that has one safe fix spanning generated modules. Each module has `# original` as its first line. The rule returns four adjacent one-character replacements per file, interleaving the files by offset.

### What happened

The preview scans the full edit list once per source. With 1,024 files (4,096 edits), render took 19 ms median over three runs; with 4,096 files (16,384 edits), it took 168 ms. Output order and patch hunks should stay the same if edits are grouped once, by first occurrence of their source. This happens in preview rendering, not in fix validation (#2283) or in `--fix` selection (#2258).

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Show the program argument separator in bend --help
body:
Fixes #2291. `bend file.bend --verbose` says to see `--help`, but help didn't show the `--` separator. It now lists `bend <file.bend> -- [args]`.

I ran an `IO.args()` program with `-- --verbose 'two words'`. It printed the same argument list before and after. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56.

title: bend-cache treats --help as an unknown argument
body:
### What you did

Ran `bun tools/bend-cache/src/cache.ts --help` without a Bend file.

### What happened

It prints `bend-cache: unknown argument --help`, then the usage text on stderr, and exits 1. The tool already has a usage text. `--help` and `-h` should be able to print it successfully without a project, compiler checkout or cache.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Group lint preview edits by source
body:
Fixes #2292. Rendering a fix preview used to filter every edit once for every file. This groups edits in one pass, in the order the files first appear.

A preview with 4,096 files and 16,384 edits dropped from 168 ms to 9 ms median over three runs. The full preview had the same bytes and hash. Two focused tests and the Linux repo gate passed (56/56). Mini gates not run.

title: Reject build outputs linked to the same file
body:
Fixes #2290. `-o out.js -o linked.c` could succeed and leave C source at both names when they pointed to the same file. Bend now rejects linked destinations before it writes anything. This also covers hard links and a symlink to an output that doesn't exist yet.

The original command now exits 1 and leaves the existing file alone. The Linux CLI fixture passed with existing, dangling and directory links, hard links, and the existing input/sidecar cases. The repo gate passed 56/56. Mini gates not run.

title: Print bend-cache help without loading Bend
body:
Fixes #2294. `bend-cache --help` used to call the flag unknown and exit 1. Both `--help` and `-h` now print the existing usage to stdout and exit 0, before opening a Bend file or loading the checker.

I ran them with no checker available and confirmed no cache file was created. Two focused tests and the Linux repo gate passed 56/56. Mini gates not run.

title: Compiler discovery hides bend-lint argument errors
body:
### What you did

Ran `BEND_DIR=/not-a-checkout bun tools/bend-lint/src/lint.ts --unknown`. Then tried it with no arguments and with a bare `--config`.

### What happened

All three commands exit 2, but report that the compiler directory is missing. None identifies the invalid flag, missing file, or missing option value. Help already works without loading Bend. Invalid invocations should also stop before compiler discovery, and valid invocations should still report compiler load errors.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Package preparation rescans each module directory for LICENSE
body:
### What you did

Published a scratch package to a loopback test hub. The entry imported 640 files in one folder and one nested module. The root and nested folders each had a `LICENSE`; the root also had `README.md`.

### What happened

Before contacting the hub, `pkg_files` reads and scans the same directory for an exact `LICENSE` entry for every imported file. Preparing one directory with many modules repeatedly enumerates all its entries, though the answer only depends on the directory. The scan can run once per source directory without changing any published bytes or package hash.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Validate bend-lint arguments before loading Bend
body:
With a missing Bend checkout, `bend-lint --unknown` used to report the compiler path instead of the bad option. It now parses the command line first, once. Help still works without a compiler; a valid invocation still reports a real compiler load error.

Fixes #2298.

I checked an unknown option, missing input, missing `--config` value, help, and a valid run. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. Mini gates not run.

title: The formatter serializes both full token streams to compare their shape
body:
### What you did

Formatted a synthetic large document with 25,000 declarations, each shaped like `def value0(a:U32,b:U32)->U32:` followed by an indented `(a  +  b : U32) # value`.

### What happened

After constructing the formatted document, the formatter joins all token strings into a second full-size serialization of each version and recalculates the original indentation levels. The safety check can compare tokens, `%` spacing and indentation directly without allocating the two large strings. Median time with the current formatter was 381 ms across five warm runs.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Scan each package directory once for licenses
body:
Fixes #2299. When lots of modules sit together, `--publish` used to scan their directory again for each file to find `LICENSE`. It now remembers whether each directory has that exact entry. The root scan also finds `README.md`.

I ran real `bend --publish` against a loopback-only hub with 645 manifest files. The package hash, both licenses, and README were unchanged. Local timings were noisy, so I'm not claiming a fixed speedup. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56; the full site-backed ping gate was not run.

title: Compare formatter token shapes without serializing them
body:
Fixes #2301. The formatter now checks token text, `%` spacing and indentation directly instead of joining two full fingerprints. It reuses the original indentation depths and skips the check if nothing changed.

On a 25,000-declaration document, the formatted output had the same size and hash. Median time over five warm runs went from 381 ms to 335 ms; peak RSS went from 283,064 to 271,684 KiB. Five focused formatter tests and the Linux repo gate passed (56/56). Mini gates not run.

title: A leading end-of-options separator does not accept the Bend filename
body:
### What you did

Ran `bend -- -program.bend --sample`, using `--` to separate options from a file whose name begins with a dash.

From source, the equivalent is `bun bend2/main.ts -- -- -program.bend --sample` because the Bun launcher consumes the first separator.

### What happened

Bend exits 1 and prints its usage. `bend ./-program.bend -- --sample` works; `IO.args()` gets `--sample`. A separator before the file should consume the next token as the file, and pass the remaining tokens to the program, rather than treating every token as a program argument without a file.

### The file

Any valid file named `-program.bend`; the example prints `IO.args()`.

### bend --version

Bend 2.0.40, upstream `966bbb7435`, Bun 1.4.4.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

title: Allow the option separator before a Bend file
body:
`bend -- -program.bend --sample` used to show usage because every token after `--` became a program argument. The first token is now the file if Bend hasn't seen one yet. Later tokens still belong to the program, and options before `--` still apply.

Fixes #2304.

I exercised both separator positions through the source CLI, checked `--check-only` before the separator, and ran a JS file built from the dash-prefixed source. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. The site-backed ping gate wasn't run.

title: bend-lint previews drop CRLF from changed lines
body:
### What you did

Rendered a `bend-lint` fix that replaces a value on a CRLF line (without touching the line ending). Then I saved the unified diff and ran `git apply --check --unidiff-zero -p0` against the same file.

### What happened

The diff contains LF on both the `-` and `+` lines, even though the corresponding source and replacement lines both have CRLF. Git cannot match the removed line (`patch does not apply`). The same omission makes an LF-only conversion look like an identical removed and added line.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8. Bun 1.4.4 ran bend-lint; the native compiler wasn't involved.

title: Keep CRLF in bend-lint fix previews
body:
The preview used to strip `\r` along with `\n`. That made an ordinary edit to a CRLF file impossible to apply from the diff, and hid CRLF-to-LF changes. The preview now keeps `\r` in the line body.

Fixes #2306.

I checked both kinds of edits in bend-lint, then applied the generated diff with `git apply --unidiff-zero` and compared the result byte for byte. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. The mini gates weren't run.

title: bend --publish mistakes paths containing @ for package names
body:

Ran `bend --publish './work@branch/prog.bend'` on a valid entry. The `@` is in the checkout directory, not in the package name.

### What happened

Bend refused the file before it read it: `a package is named <name>@<version>`. The optional publish operand takes the path just because it contains `@`. Passing the file before `--publish` works around this.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

Linux x86_64.

title: Accept at-signs in Bend publish paths
body:
`bend --publish work@branch/prog.bend` was trying to parse the path as a release name. A `.bend` path now stays a file; the optional `name@version` is still validated separately.

Fixes #2308.

I compared both argument orders against a loopback hub. The new order sends the same file and gets the same hash, and malformed package names still fail before any request. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. The site-backed ping gate wasn't run.

title: bend-lint copies the formatter stack for each width check
body:
### What you did

Called `format` from `tools/bend-lint/rules/format.ts` with width 80 on a definition returning a `List<List<U32>>`: one source line containing `[[0], [1], ...]`. Repeated each size five times under Bun 1.4.4.

### What happened

At 1,024 singleton lists the median was 19.6 ms; 4,096 took 96.2 ms; 16,384 took 1,139.0 ms. Each fit check copies the remaining print stack, even when it only looks at a couple of frames before seeing a break. The measurement is of `format` itself, not the type checker.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8; not used in the repro.

title: Avoid copying the bend-lint formatter lookahead stack
body:
You don't need to copy all the pending siblings to see whether a group fits. The printer now reads them in place and uses a small local stack for the part it probes.

Fixes #2310.

With 16,384 singleton lists on one source line, median `format` time dropped from 1,139 to 120 ms (five interleaved runs per tree, width 80, Bun 1.4.4 on Linux). Output was byte-identical. All 40 formatter tests and the Linux repo gate passed. The mini gates weren't run.

title: String.quote builds a temporary string for each printable ASCII character
body:
### What you did

Ran `String.quote` 192 times on a 122,880-character printable ASCII string, consuming the result each time. Native Linux build with clang `-O3`, one process at a time.

### What happened

Median 0.43 s across five runs. The ordinary characters make a one-character string via `Char.quote` and then consume that string to put the same character onto the reversed result. Escapes need that path; an ordinary ASCII character doesn't.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8.

title: Quote plain ASCII directly in Base strings
body:
Plain ASCII can go straight onto the reversed result. Quotes, backslashes, controls and non-ASCII still use the existing escaping path.

Fixes #2312.

The 192 × 122,880-character native run went from 0.43 to 0.38 s median. A deliberately escape-heavy mixed string went from 0.31 to 0.32 s. Both had identical output (five interleaved runs on Linux, clang 22.1.8). `string_kit`, `string_escape` and `char_any_code` passed in JS and native C; `string_kit` passed in the interpreter too. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56; the mini gates weren't run.

title: bend-cache accepts blank and non-finite --min-ms durations
body:
### What you did

Ran `bend-cache m.bend --min-ms ' ' --stats` with a new cache file, then tried `--min-ms Infinity` with another new cache file.

### What happened

Both runs exit 0. The blank string is coerced to zero and keeps all 544 traces for this tiny file; `Infinity` keeps none. Neither is a millisecond duration. An accidentally blank shell variable should not switch caching to a different policy.

title: Require a finite bend-cache threshold
body:
A blank `--min-ms` acted like zero, and `Infinity` meant no traces. Neither is a duration, so bend-cache now reports both as usage errors. Zero and fractional durations still work.

Fixes #2314.

title: bend --checkup drops the source location from compiler errors

title: Keep source locations in Bend checkup diagnostics

title: Inline HTML diagnostics count CR-only source lines as one line

header

`, `

second line

title: Reject malformed Bend checkup header imports

A bare `import` or an import path without an alias used to disappear from `--checkup` and leave it exiting zero. These now get an error; `import Base`, trailing comments, and text after the header still work as before.

Fixes #2318.

title: Bend bundles inert inline scripts inside HTML templates
body:
### What you did

Bundled a page containing `<template><script type="module">const x = ;</script></template>` with `bend page.html -o dist`. The script is an inert example in the template, not a module entry point.

### What happened

Bend tries to compile the script as a normal inline module and refuses to bundle the page. Even valid template text gets moved into the page's JavaScript bundle. Only active scripts outside the template should be compiled.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

Linux x86_64.

title: Keep inline template scripts out of Bend bundles
body:
Inline module scripts inside HTML templates are inert. Bend now leaves them in the page instead of adding them to the JS bundle.

Fixes #2322.

I bundled a page with nested templates between two active scripts. Both inert script bodies stayed byte-for-byte in the HTML, while both active scripts made it into the JS. The old bundler refused that page. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56; the site-backed ping gate wasn't run.

title: Aborting a queued bend-lint check waits for an unrelated import
body:
### What you did

Called `lint()` on a file importing a package, then called `lint()` on a second file while that import request was still in flight. Aborted only the second run through its `AbortController`. The package request was held by a loopback server.

### What happened

The second call does not reject with the abort reason until the first import finishes, even though it never needs to start. An editor can be left waiting for a cancelled check behind an unrelated slow network request.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8. The repro uses Bun 1.4.4, not clang.

title: Reject aborted queued bend-lint checks promptly
body:
An aborted lint call shouldn't wait behind another file's package download. It now rejects with the original abort reason right away. The checker still finishes and cleans up its own turn before anything else runs.

Fixes #2324.

A loopback import held the first check open: the second rejected before release, then a third check ran normally. Three focused tests and the Linux repo gate passed. The mini gates weren't run.

title: bend --checkup resolves relative imports beside a symlink
body:
### What you did

`src/list.bend` imports `./program.bend as P`. `alias/list.bend` is a symlink to `../src/list.bend`. Ran `bend alias/list.bend --checkup`.

### What happened

`--checkup` looks for `alias/program.bend` and exits 1. `bend alias/list.bend --check-only` succeeds, and `bend src/list.bend --checkup` runs `src/program.bend`. The batch command should use the entry's real directory, like the loader.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8; the repro only uses Bun.

title: Resolve Bend checkup imports from the real entry
body:
`--checkup` now resolves relative imports from the actual entry file, not from the directory where a symlink points to it. That matches the normal loader.

Fixes #2326.

I compared symlinked and direct runs byte for byte, and confirmed that an absolute import still runs. The Linux repo gate passed 56/56. The site-backed ping gate wasn't run.

title: bend-lint recopies all earlier findings for rules that emit none
body:
### What you did

Used the public `lint()` API with a generated stress pack: one rule emits 15,000 findings, 4,096 rules emit nothing, and the last rule reports how many earlier findings it sees. Timed `lint()` with warmed compiler state under Bun 1.4.4.

### What happened

The baseline median was 247.0 ms over five runs. Every empty rule copies the entire findings list even though the next rule sees the same contents. This stress case deliberately puts a lot of quiet rules after a large finding group.

### bend --version

2.0.40, main at `966bbb74`.

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64.

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8 (not involved in the measurement).

title: Leave bend-lint findings unchanged after empty rules
body:
If a rule reports nothing, there is no reason to copy all the findings that came before it. The next rule sees the same findings in the same order.

Fixes #2328.

On a stress pack with 15,000 findings followed by 4,096 quiet rules, the median went from 247.0 to 9.7 ms over five interleaved runs per tree. All 15,001 final diagnostics matched. Four focused tests and the Linux repo gate passed. The mini gates weren't run.

title: bend-fmt-lsp allocates a pin list for each unanchored line
body:
### What Bend should do

`bend2-fmt-lsp` only needs the last inline body whose column is at or before the current line. It can look backward and stop at the first match instead of filtering the entire pin list and creating an array just to take its last item.

### Why

Every nonblank, unanchored line pays for that intermediate array, including files without any active pin. I formatted a checked 300-declaration module with inline `do` bodies and mixed indentation on `966bbb7`: 2,703 temporary arrays at this lookup, versus zero with a backward search. The formatted text was byte-for-byte identical, and both source and formatted files printed `t`, `uv`, `w` with the Bend CLI. This is an allocation count, not a wall-clock benchmark.

title: Find the active formatting pin without allocating
body:
Look backward for the last usable layout pin. No temporary array, and the selection order stays the same.

On a 300-declaration module, the lookup went from 2,703 arrays to zero. The formatted output was identical, and both files ran with the same output through the Bend CLI. The formatter's 37 tests (including the stdio LSP session) and the repo gate (56/56) pass on Linux. Draft because I couldn't run the mini gates.

Fixes #2330

title: Extra arguments to bend guide and bend base get the wrong error
body:
### What you did

`bend guide effects extra`, then `bend base --types extra`.

### What happened

Both exit 1, but neither points at the extra argument. `guide` gets treated like a Bend source file (`no such file: guide`), and `base --types extra` reports `unknown option --types` even though `bend base --types` works. Each command should keep its own usage message. `bend --help` should also show that `guide` can take a topic; `bend guide effects` already works.

### bend version

2.0.40 (`966bbb7`)

### uname -sm

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8 (Fedora 22.1.8-4.fc44)

title: Report extra arguments to bend guide and bend base
body:
Keep guide and Base in their own command paths when there are too many arguments. The help now shows that a guide can take a topic.

I ran both bad invocations and compared five valid invocations against main; their output stayed byte-for-byte the same. The repo gate passed 56/56 on Linux. I could not run the mini gates.

Fixes #2332

title: Bend-written lint rules scan every source for each span
body:
### What Bend should do

Resolve source paths once per Bend-written lint rule, rather than linearly scanning the book's files for every diagnostic span, edit and `Lint.text` call. A rule that doesn't resolve any spans doesn't need an index.

### Why

On `966bbb7`, I ran a Bend-written rule over an entry importing 64 modules. The 528 warnings each carry a source span and an edit. The old lookup examined 35,376 path candidates; the indexed version made no linear searches and produced byte-for-byte identical diagnostics. That's a count of path comparisons, not a timing result.

title: Index book source paths for Bend-written lint rules
body:
Build a path index on the first span lookup in a rule. Rules that never look up a span still skip that work.

A rule over 64 imports produced the same 528 diagnostics before and after. The old path scans made 35,376 comparisons. The repo gate passed 56/56; 136 lint tests passed, and one unrelated test could not create a filename containing a backslash on this mount. Mini gates were unavailable.

Fixes #2334

title: Formatting strips a valid UTF-8 byte-order mark
body:
### What you did

Format a valid UTF-8 `.bend` file saved with a byte-order mark in `bend2-fmt-lsp`. I also ran `bend main.bend --check-only` before formatting; it passed.

### What happened

The formatted replacement starts with `import Base` instead of the original `U+FEFF` followed by `import Base`. Formatting spacing shouldn't change how the file was saved. The opening bytes should still be `ef bb bf`.

### bend version

2.0.40 (`966bbb7`), formatter 0.1.0

Linux x86_64

### clang --version (the first line)

clang version 22.1.8 (Fedora 22.1.8-4.fc44)

title: Honor editor final-newline preferences in bend2-fmt-lsp
body:
### What Bend should do

Honor `insertFinalNewline` and `trimFinalNewlines` when the editor explicitly sends them with `textDocument/formatting`. Keep the existing final-newline behavior when neither option is set. If the file uses CRLF, use it for a newline the editor asks us to add.

### Why

An editor can request a final newline in the same format call that fixes the indentation. The server currently formats names and spacing but ignores that request, leaving clients to make a second edit or ignore their own save preferences. Both settings are standard LSP `FormattingOptions`.

title: Honor explicit final-newline options in bend2-fmt-lsp
body:
Keep EOF newlines as they are unless the editor asks to add or trim them. An added newline follows the file’s line endings.

I sent both options through the stdio LSP server, including a CRLF-only file and extra mixed newlines at EOF. The formatter’s 38 tests and the repo gate (56/56) pass on Linux. The mini gates weren’t available.

Fixes #2337

title: Keep the UTF-8 BOM when formatting Bend files
body:
Keep the BOM separate from the text being formatted so changing indentation doesn’t erase it.

I sent a BOM-bearing document through the real stdio LSP server and checked that the edit still starts with `ef bb bf`. The formatted file checks in `bend --check-only`. On Linux, the formatter’s 38 tests and the repo gate (56/56) pass. The mini gates weren’t available.

Fixes #2336

title: Explain importing Bend modules into JS hosts
body:
The guide now says what the emitted `.mjs` exports, where to put a handwritten `.d.mts`, and how to state ordering laws over a pure replay. This covers the docs part of #1988, not generated declarations or Hermes support.

I checked the replay law with BendTT, ran both event orders on Node 22, and used the handwritten declaration from a strict TypeScript consumer. Repo gate: 56/56. The mini cluster was unreachable; Hermes was not tested.

title: Split CRLF as one separator in String.lines
body:
`String.lines` split on `\n` but left `\r` at the end of each Windows line. It now consumes CRLF together, without removing standalone `\r` or changing the trailing empty line. `String.split` is unchanged.

The new fixture gave the expected output in the interpreter, Node 22 and the Linux native build. I could not reach the mini cluster.

title: Look only for config files during bend-lint discovery
body:
A directory called `bend-lint.json` used to stop the search and fail with `EISDIR`, even when a parent folder had a real config. The search now skips anything that isn’t a file and keeps the same precedence. An explicit `--config` still reports an invalid path.

Verified the real CLI and the lint suite on Linux: 126 passed, 12 skipped. I could not reach the mini cluster.

title: List --checkup in the Bend CLI help
body:
`--checkup` already works, but it wasn’t in `bend --help`. The usage text now explains that it checks and runs direct imports separately, unlike `--check-only`.

Checked the actual help output and ran the displayed command with a small imported file; it printed `7`. `main.ts` is 13,365/16,000 tokens. The mini cluster was unavailable.

title: Format compact do binds in bend2-fmt-lsp
body:
The editor formatter left `Unit<-IO.print("x")` glued and could space an erased datatype binder like a do bind. It now formats `Unit <- IO.print("x")` but keeps `type Box<-T: Type>` together. This is the language server, not the bend-lint change in #2237.

All 38 LSP and formatter tests passed on Linux across two runs. A real stdio request returned the edit, and both example programs printed the same result before and after formatting. The mini cluster was unavailable.

title: refactor(comp): drop dead code in comp.ts (44 tokens)
body:
This PR removes dead code in `comp.ts`: 65,989 → 65,945 ttok, 44 tokens freed. It started as room for #2289, which has since found its own. What's left is headroom.

Each change removes code that can't run, or calls an existing helper. The emitted C, JS and MJS are byte-identical for every `.bend` file under `tests/`, `bench/` and `demos/`.

## What changes

- **`facts_hot` never gets a null type** (13 tokens). Every caller passes an `HTerm`: `b.A`, `A` in `bind_uses`, `Spine.all` elements in `emit_args` and `emit_intr`, and the recursive calls on `w.f(DUMMY)`, `term_kids`, `fam`, and ADT field types. `ty_wnf` returns a term for a term, so the `B &&`, the five `w?.` and the `"no type"` fallback are dead. `const w = ty_wnf(B)!` is the same idiom as in `piece`.
- **`row_val` never sees a `Bool` constant** (13 tokens). `emit_row` only asks for `WORDS` cells (`U32`, `F32`, `Nat`). The recursion only goes into the arguments of an operation with JS text, and no such operation that returns a word takes a `Bool`. `Map.msb.u` has C text only, and `Bool.to_u32` is not an operation. So `k === "Bool"` never holds. `Cell` keeps `boolean`, since the comparison operations still return one from `ROWS`.
- **`js_def` never gets an intrinsic** (13 tokens). Its names come from `FL.srcs`. On the JS lane, `src_add` gets:
  - the roots, which are `"main"` or non-Base defs, while `intr_of` needs `tld.b`;
  - refs that `file_book` already checked with `!intr_of(s.k)`, against the same `FL`;
  - ADT names from `ctr_build`, while `intr_of` needs a `Def`.

  The `effect_src` and `ty_srcs` paths run only on the C lane.
- **`anf` calls `ty_all`** (5 tokens). `ty_all` is `Bend.tele_open(FL.book, ty!)!`, the same call, as `emit_body` and `js_func` already use it.

## Verified

Linux x86_64, Bun 1.4.0, main 6180be5b.

- **Emitted output:** I emitted every one of the 1,963 `.bend` files under `tests/`, `bench/` and `demos/` to C (`-o x.c`), JS (`-o x.js`) and MJS (`-o x.mjs`), with and without this change. For each file and lane I hashed the exit code, the emitted file and the messages. All 5,889 results are identical.
- **Types:** `tsc --noEmit` on `comp.ts` (TypeScript 5.9.3) reports the same diagnostics before and after. This change adds none.
- **Tokens:** `ttok -m gpt-3.5-turbo` gives 65,989 → 65,945.

title: perf(io): bound initial sequential read buffers
body:
Sequential JavaScript reads can allocate a buffer based on the full file size even after the cursor reaches EOF. Large estimates now start with a smaller buffer and grow to the saved estimate only after that first buffer fills.

With a 1 MiB cap at EOF, the initial buffer drops to 64 KiB. In paired macOS runs, repeated EOF reads took 84% less time on Bun and 53% less time on Node. Existing file-read fixtures passed.

title: A U32 argument from a JS caller reaches the program unmasked
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend host_u32.bend -o host_u32.mjs
node host_u32.call.mjs      # 17 lines, it only calls the exports
```

### What happened

```
U32 7 show -> "7"  add(x,1) -> 8  is_zero -> false
U32 4294967296 show -> "4294967296"  add(x,1) -> 1  is_zero -> false
U32 -1 show -> "/"  add(x,1) -> 0  is_zero -> false

Nat 281474976710655 show -> 281474976710655  add(x,1) -> FAIL-STOP: bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1
Nat 281474976710656 show -> 281474976710656  add(x,1) -> FAIL-STOP: bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1
Nat 9007199254740992 show -> 9007199254740992  add(x,1) -> FAIL-STOP: bend: a Nat past the largest immediate 2^48-1
```

The first U32 line is fine. The two below it pass a host number to a def whose argument is a `U32`, and a JS number is not a `U32`.

`U32.add` masks it and answers right. `U32.show` and `U32.is_zero` do not, so the three columns give three different readings of one argument. `4294967296` comes back as text for a number the type cannot hold, and `is_zero` says `false` about a value `U32.add` has already treated as `0`. `-1` prints as `/`, one character, because the decimal loop is subtracting from a negative.

Masking at the edge gives these, and this is what Bend itself prints for the same calls once the checker holds the value in range (`expected.bend`):

```
0
1
True
4294967295
0
False
```

So `U32.show(4294967296)` should be `0` and `U32.is_zero(4294967296)` should be `true`. One program, one argument, contradicting itself inside one lane, no C involved.

### Where

`host()` at `bend2/comp.ts:3080` wraps arguments as they cross a `.mjs` edge.

```ts
const k = ty_adt(A)?.k;
return k === "Char" || k === "String" ? `str_${out ? "out" : "in"}(${x})`
  : k === "Nat" && !out ? `nat_in(${x})`
  : k === "F32" && !out ? `Math.fround(${x})` : x;
```

Char, String, Nat and F32 each get a coercion on the way in. `U32` is the one word type that falls through to the bare `x`. Two exports from `host_u32.mjs`:

```js
"show":     run_lib((a0) => str_out(run_loop($show(a0))), 1),
"nat_show": run_lib((a0) => str_out(run_loop($nat_show(nat_in(a0)))), 1),
```

The mask exists downstream in the arithmetic builtins, which is why the columns disagree with each other instead of all being wrong the same way. One row fixes it, mirroring the `Math.fround` case:

```ts
: k === "U32" && !out ? `${x} >>> 0`
```

A `u32_in(x)` that throws the way `nat_in` throws is probably the behaviour you want, since a caller who passes `-1` where a `U32` belongs would rather hear about it than get `/`.

### Same edge, Nat, smaller

`nat_in` bounds at `2^53`, the largest exact JS integer, while the immediate wall is `2^48-1`, so a host caller gets a past-the-wall Nat into a def and `Nat.show` prints it. `#779` covers a Nat past the wall fail-stopping, and it does, one step after the boundary instead of at it, which is why the last two lines above print a value before failing. Same two lines of code and same shape of fix, so mentioning it while you are in there.

For context, this is the only JS against C divergence I found. I ran both lanes over the 1670 test files that have a `main` and compared stdout. 754 of them are fixtures the checker rejects, so 916 reached both lanes, and all 916 matched byte for byte.

### The file

```bend
# host_u32.bend
import Base

def show(x: U32) -> String:
  U32.show(x)

def succ(x: U32) -> U32:
  U32.add(x, 1)

def zero(x: U32) -> Bool:
  U32.is_zero(x)

# the same question about the other word type that crosses an edge
def nat_show(x: Nat) -> String:
  Nat.show(x)

def nat_succ(x: Nat) -> Nat:
  Nat.add(x, 1n)
```

```js
// host_u32.call.mjs
import lib from "./host_u32.mjs";

const t = (f) => { try { return String(f()); } catch (e) { return "FAIL-STOP: " + e; } };

for (const v of [7, 4294967296, -1]) {
  console.log(`U32 ${v}`,
    "show ->", JSON.stringify(lib.show(v)),
    " add(x,1) ->", lib.succ(v),
    " is_zero ->", lib.zero(v));
}
console.log("");
for (const v of [281474976710655, 281474976710656, 9007199254740992]) {
  console.log(`Nat ${v}`,
    "show ->", t(() => lib.nat_show(v)),
    " add(x,1) ->", t(() => lib.nat_succ(v)));
}
```

```bend
# expected.bend, the masked answers
import Base

def row(+x: U32) -> IO (Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print(U32.show(x))
    IO.print(U32.show(U32.add(x, 1)))
    IO.print(Bool.show(U32.is_zero(x)))

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    row(0)            # 2^32 masked to a U32
    row(4294967295)   # -1 masked to a U32
```

### bend version

`bend 2.0.40`, commit `3d5bf43`

### uname -sm

`Darwin arm64`, Apple clang 21. The `.mjs` caller ran under bun 1.4.5 here because node is not installed on this machine.

title: A --gpu size past the 64 bit range is cast out of range and accepted
body:
### What you did

```sh
bend gpu_mark.bend -o mark        # the CLI builds this one with GPU support
./mark +RTS --gpu 999999999999GB
```

`gpu_mark.bend` is `tests/run/gpu_mark.bend` unchanged, pasted at the bottom.

### What happened

```
$ ./mark
1212
$ ./mark +RTS --gpu 4GB
1212
$ ./mark +RTS --gpu 999999999999GB
bend: reservation failed
```

`999999999999GB` is about 0.9 zebibytes, which does not fit a `u64` byte count. The `--gpu` parser multiplies it as a `double` and casts to `u64` before it checks whether the argument was well formed, and that cast is the C UB UBSan is for. No GPU is needed to see it, so I used a two line program:

```
$ bend tiny.bend -o tiny.c
$ cc -O1 -fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow -o tiny_u tiny.c
$ ./tiny_u +RTS --gpu 999999999999GB
tiny.c:2897:13: runtime error: 1.07374e+21 is outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned long long'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior tiny.c:2897:13
ok
$ ./tiny_u +RTS --gpu 1e400GB
tiny.c:2897:13: runtime error: inf is outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned long long'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior tiny.c:2897:13
bend: expected on, off or a size like 4GB after --gpu
```

`1e400GB` is the case the syntax check does catch, one line after the cast already happened. `999999999999GB` is the case it does not catch, because every character is a digit. The size reaches `mem` and nothing looks at the magnitude. I printed it from a copy of the emitted C:

```
4GB              -> mem = 4294967296
999999999999GB   -> mem = 18446744073709551615
17179869184GB    -> mem = 18446744073709551615
```

On arm64 an out-of-range `double` to `u64` saturates, so a bad argument quietly becomes a request for a 16 EiB corpus, and the program dies with `bend: reservation failed`. That reads like the machine ran out of address space rather than like the flag was wrong, and there is no hint about what size was asked for. Fail-stopping on a failed reservation is fine by me, `#792`. The complaint is the order: validate the number, then reserve.

The same cast on the GPU program, `mark.c` numbers its lines differently:

```
$ cc -O1 -w -fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow -o mark_u mark.c
$ ./mark_u +RTS --gpu 999999999999GB
mark.c:3140:13: runtime error: 1.07374e+21 is outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned long long'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior mark.c:3140:13
bend: this binary has no CUDA or Metal GPU support
```

That last line is only because I built `mark.c` by hand without `-DBEND_METAL=1`. The CLI build has GPU support and gets as far as the reservation, which is the first block above.

One thing I could not test here. The x86-64 sequence for an out-of-range `double` to `u64` wraps instead of saturating, so the same flag on Linux could land on a far smaller corpus than the one asked for and run on it silently, instead of failing loudly. That is reading only, I have no x86 box.

### Where

`bend2/comp.ts:5929`, the `--gpu` arm of the runtime option loop.

```c
double n   = strtod(v, &end);
u64    mul = !strcmp(end, "GB") ? 1ull << 30
  : !strcmp(end, "MB") ? 1ull << 20 : 0;
mem = (u64)(n * (double)mul);
if (!strcmp(v, "off")) {
  gpu = 0;
} else if (!strcmp(v, "on")
  || (mem >= 16384 && end == v + strspn(v, "0123456789."))) {
```

The cast at `5933` runs before the check at `5937`, and that check only looks at the lower bound and at the shape of the text, never at whether the product fits. A bound before the cast is all it needs:

```c
if (!(n >= 0) || n > 1.8446744073709552e19 / (double)mul) {
  err_fail("expected a GPU size that fits 64 bits after --gpu");
}
```

which also clears `inf` and `nan`, since neither compares as a valid size.

### The file

```bend
# gpu_mark.bend, tests/run/gpu_mark.bend unchanged
# the GPU mark f!(x) has zero semantic content: interpreter and CPU-only
# compiled code treat it exactly as f(x)
# ported from bend3: depth becomes Nat, the fork a parallel let
import Base

law gmark:
  for +d: Nat
  U32

def gmark(d):
  match d:
    case 0n:
      3
    case 1n+p:
      a b = gmark(p) gmark(p)
      U32.add(a, b)

law main.out:
  U32

def main.out():
  x = gmark!(2n)
  y = gmark(2n)
  U32.add(U32.mul(x, 100), y)

law main:
  IO(Unit)

def main():
  IO.print(U32.show(main.out()))

#|1212
```

```bend
# tiny.bend
import Base

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    IO.print("ok")
```

### bend version

`bend 2.0.40`, commit `3d5bf43`

### uname -sm

`Darwin arm64`, Apple clang 21.

title: fix: bound --gpu sizes before the cast, mask U32 host arguments (#2348, #2347)
body:
Fixes #2348 and #2347, one commit each.

## #2348: `--gpu` size past 2^64 bytes

Repro on main (6180be5b), `tiny.bend` from the issue, built with `-fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow`:

```
$ ./tiny_u +RTS --gpu 999999999999GB
tiny.c:2897:13: runtime error: 1.07374e+21 is outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned long long'
ok
$ ./tiny_u +RTS --gpu 17179869184GB
tiny.c:2897:13: runtime error: 1.84467e+19 is outside the range of representable values of type 'unsigned long long'
ok
```

Fix: the C `--gpu` arm keeps the size as a double and sets `mem` only for a well formed size in [16384, 2^64), so no out-of-range cast happens and an oversize size gets the usual "expected on, off or a size like 4GB after --gpu". The JS runtime takes the same upper bound, so both lanes accept and reject the same sizes (checked on 19 edge inputs, including `17179869183GB` accepted, `17179869184GB`, `1e400GB`, `nanGB`, `-4GB`, `.GB` rejected). Its regex reads the number as `[\d.]*`, the same language as before, and `runtime_gpu_invalid` still passes.

The arm is restructured (`gpu = strcmp(v, "off") != 0`, one error branch) so comp.ts stays under its 66k ttok cap: 65997 after both commits, 65989 before.

After: no UBSan report, exit 1 with the flag error, and a real GPU build of `tests/run/gpu_mark.bend` now rejects `999999999999GB` instead of dying with "reservation failed".

## #2347: U32 argument from a JS caller

Repro on main, `host_u32.bend` and its caller from the issue:

```
U32 4294967296 show -> "4294967296"  add(x,1) -> 1  is_zero -> false
U32 -1 show -> "/"  add(x,1) -> 0  is_zero -> false
```

Fix: `host()` masks a U32 coming in with `x >>> 0`, like it rounds an F32 with `Math.fround`. After:

```
U32 4294967296 show -> "0"  add(x,1) -> 1  is_zero -> true
U32 -1 show -> "4294967295"  add(x,1) -> 0  is_zero -> false
```

which matches the issue's `expected.bend`. I went with masking rather than a throwing `u32_in`: it is what the U32 ops already do, it matches the F32 edge, and it needs no new error text under the cap. Happy to switch if you'd rather fail-stop.

The Nat remark in #2347 (`nat_in` bounds at 2^53, not 2^48-1) is left alone: #1656, `nat_host_export` and `nat_host_bounds` pin 2^53 as the host range on purpose.

## Tests

- `tests/io/runtime_gpu_huge`: builds a program as C and JS, checks both reject `999999999999GB`, `17179869184GB`, `1e400GB` and accept `17179869183GB`, `4GB`.
- `tests/io/u32_host_export`: 2^32, -1, 2^32+5 through `show`, `is_zero` and `add`, one call and curried.

Both fail on main (exit codes 1 and 2) and pass here. These also still pass: `runtime_gpu_invalid`, `f32_host_export`, `nat_host_export`, `nat_host_bounds`, `nat_host_neg`, `u32_to_f32_host_zero`. I could not run the cluster gates from here. I ran these locally under bun 1.4.5 on Darwin arm64.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: The C backend builds and runs on a 32-bit host (ARMv7)
body:
TLDR: I well know that this change has little chance being included, yet it might serve others in need of an off the shelf 32 bit version.

The rest has been made by Claude Fable 5.2.

A binary built by `bend main.bend -o main` for a 32-bit Linux target stops at
`bend: reservation failed`: the runtime reserves an 8 GiB corpus and 2 GiB per
worker stack. These three commits make it run there. A 64-bit host takes the
same paths as before.
 
### What changes
 
- **Runtime** (`comp.ts`): on a 32-bit host the corpus is 1 GiB and a stack
  64 MiB.
- **Effects** (`effs/`): `read_at` and `write_at` zero-extend their U32
  offset, which an `intptr_t` sign-extended past 2^31. `File.read` grows its
  buffer from 64 KiB instead of allocating `max` bytes up front, and
  `TCP.recv` fills 16 MiB at most.
- **CLI** (`main.ts`): `-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_TIME_BITS=64`, and
  `-Wno-ignored-attributes` for `preserve_none` on a target without it.
35 lines added, 12 removed. No new file, no change to `bend.ts`.
 
### Why
 
A Raspberry Pi 2 experiment with a Bend program. Through the JS target it takes
11.05 ms of processor per frame and 68 MiB; through the C target, with this change,
5.34 ms and 2 MiB.
 
### Tested
 
On a Raspberry Pi 2 Model B (ARMv7, 902 MiB, glibc 2.44), cross-compiled with
clang 22, the commits applied on 0e2f38f:
 
- The tree of 2^20 leaves of the BendRT paper: right sum on 1 and 4 threads.
- The C lane of every directory of `tests/` (compile to C, build, run, compare
  with the `#|` lines): 1 866 files, 897 pass, 953 not run by the C lane,
  12 need X11 or ALSA, 4 fail. The four are below.
- The experiment program: outputs are byte for byte the same as the JS
  target's, for three sets of options (one does FFTs in F32).
On x86-64 (clang 18), the commits rebased on 6180be5, same script: 904 pass,
1 fails (`io_tcp_text_residue`).
 
### Not tested, and limits
 
- Four tests of `tests/io` fail on the Pi and were not investigated:
  `io_process_run` (it also runs `/usr/bin/perl`, absent there),
  `io_tcp_text_residue` (fails on x86-64 too), `io_tcp_send_slow_peer`
  (out of time) and `io_file_write_at_control` (it interposes `pwrite`; with
  64-bit file offsets the runtime calls `pwrite64`, which is probably why).
- Rebased on 6180be5, the commits build for ARMv7 but were not run there: the
  runs on the Pi are on 0e2f38f.
- One 32-bit target only: ARMv7 with glibc and clang. Not musl, not gcc.
  32-bit x86 does not build: clang 22 crashes on it.
- The gates were not run. `gates/repo.ts` needs ttok, which I could not run:
  the change adds a few lines to `comp.ts` and `main.ts`, and I do not know
  how close they are to their caps.
- On a 32-bit host a program has 1 GiB of corpus at most, and a deep
  recursion faults at 64 MiB of stack instead of 2 GiB.
